Sevinc Turkkan is a great and passionate teacher. Also, she makes the best baklava I have ever had.

Good teacher! Take her class if you want to learn something.

He uses iclicker for attendance (it's partially that you are there and that you answer the question correctly), he encourages everyone to talk during the iclicker questions. Lectures are pretty boring. First test was easy the other two were so-so. No homework is graded. Weekly quizzes

Awful, avoid at all costs. He has potential to be a good teacher, but he is so lazy and so hard to meet up with to ask questions. He never grades anything until week 10 and takes points off for stupid things.

This professor is extremely passionate about what he is teaching. This class was disorganized, the professor cancelled class multiple times, assigned way too much work for a 200 level course, and they were extremely defensive of their teaching style. Very knowledgeable and passionate. However, usually cancels class and assigns excessive extra homework instead. Very defensive and difficult to approach. Assigned work we never discussed in class then midterm and final included information never covered. I don't recommend.

Dr. Nicosia cancels class all the time as well as assigns work that is very confusing to understand. Goes on tangents during boring lectures or watch a movie that we can watch at home and we don't talk about the movies we do watch.

Dr. Nicosia seems like a really cool person but I think that they have much more passion for film and theater than they do for teaching. We were assigned way too much work last minute, and I didn't really enjoy what could have been a very fun class

I took VISL-120. I dropped the class due to missing the online midterm deadline because of a personal issue, which Dr. Nicosia was not understanding of at all. Dr. Nicosia is an amazing professor, and his classes are thoroughly interesting. I've taken 3 classes with him so far and hopefully will continue to in the future. There is a lot of reading, there is a fair amount of writing, so be prepared for that.

performing identity: wordy articles to read, a movie or two to watch every week, & a short easy paper due each week based of the reading & viewing. can easily get an A by just trying & showing up, dont even need to be active in discussion. 1 group project & final 10 pg paper. overall the prof is great, easy to talk to , knowlegable & open minded

Awesome class about science fiction film and television. The theory can be difficult at times but he always takes time in class to explain and answer questions.
Feels like a lot of work initially but it's an easy class. Professor is always available if needed to meet outside of class.

I really really enjoyed Intro to Theatre with Nicosia. For sure there was quite a bit of reading and writing, but the prompts are very straight forward and it is really not hard to put out the two page paper if you actually did the reading.

Going in I didn't know what to expect.  There was a lot more work than expected.  There was at least one two-page paper due almost every week.  However, the prompts were not that difficult.  Nicosia took students feedback to heart and changed somethings along the way, even the time of our final exam.  He truly cares about his students + the course.

This coarse had more work than my Computer Science class. While that should say it all I will expand on that. comment: While the lectures are boring and drawn-out, he is good at explaining difficult concepts. I never felt completely lost even when learning new topics because he explained it thoroughly and clearly. As long as you go the the lectures, take notes, and pay attention, you'll do fine.

Only grades are hw/quiz/exams.

Had for Graphical Math. Lecture consisted of notes for 3/4's of the class and an attendance question that very minimal with 5% of your total grade. Worst was tests, no matter how much I studied I never seemed to get over a 50% grade and no TA's present in the class, get ready for lots of note taking and 3 midterms and every topic final for 35%

If you're taking this teacher, please understand that this isn't the math teacher you can skip class until exam day. You will inevitably fail. Do this, and you'll pass (with the VERY lenient curve).

comment: His lectures are completely written by him during the class and are accessible outside of class. He teaches a lot of in-depth info in each class. During lecture if you ask him a question he just answers with where to find it in the textbook. However, one on one he explains the topics well. Professor Raj is an all around good professor.  He is clear and you will understand the material.  His tests are not easy but they are not overly difficult if you pay attention.  I would recommend him for DBC.

Professor Carle is not one to give fair grades. Simply get on her bad side and she will lower your grades with strict interpretation of wording on her assignments. You are better off teaching yourself because if you try to learn from her in class you will fail. Don't make the same mistake I did AVOID HER!!!!!!

This is one of the most frustrating classes I have taken. In the beginning of the term, it was made clear that minimal help will be given to us, in order to prepare us for the real world. She is so confusing, very hard to understand, assignments thrown around and not even mentioned due date. She needs to get her act together. She makes me want to change majors so I do not have to deal wit her again.

She is the worst professor in the entire RIT! She is simply pathetic at teaching and she clearly doesn't realize her methods of teaching is so horrendous that it drives every student crazy. She is a very smart person, but terrible at teaching. She gives way too much work that doesn't make any sense. knows the material but doesn't know exactly how to say it to the 1st year students who have no idea

She is an absolutely terrible teacher.  She was so dry in her lesson and her jokes.  The work is hard and there is not much guidance.  She is also anti-social.  She didn't even say what her name was on the first day of class until I asked her.
Horrible teacher.  She goes really fast when teaching the computer part so you cant follow and does not slow down or answer questions.  She also gives insane amount of work at the end of the quarter
This teacher if very nice and understanding although she is a hard grader you will learn the material.  I recomend her to castro.
Great teacher, knows the material really well. makes you actually work for your grade unlike castro. highly recommend this teacher.

Had her for Solid Modeling.  Took it online over the summer.  It was outside of my major, but I wanted to learn another CAD program.  While it was mainly self taught, it wasn't bad, and she answered questions well through email.

This was her first Quarter teaching Dynamics and i must say that she did an exelent job. I have had her for other classes and i disliked her but this class she was very personable and did a great job teaching dynamics. I WOULD RECOMEND HER OVER LUI!!!

Terrible teacher for both solid modeling AND Intro to materials tech. Teaches poorly, and grades extremely harshly. Tests are nightmares, and you won't get a damn thing out of the class except a lot of stress. Castro is worse, but grades much easier
Horrible, horrible teacher, go for castro, he may not be a great teacher but even he is better than carle, so annoying and harsh, she loves shutting down students

Worse Class and Teacher I have ever had. Doesn't know how to teach. She just uses other peoples powerpoint and prezis along with videos to teach. Learned little to nothing the entire semester. Had her for Introduction to Theatre and enjoyed the class but took little away from it. She's an enjoyable person to casually converse with- but she can really talk... Most classes become rambling lectures... There's a lot of little assignments as well- easy, yet time consuming. Overall, she's an easy professor that takes up a lot of your time.

She's a really nice lady and fun to talk to but I can't even. She gives you a 10-15 page paper (she expects 20) for the final and pretty much all of the "mini-homeworks" are projects. If you take her, prepare to work and put up with extremely vague prompts.

For off, Prof. Peace has a ton of experience with theatre, so if you have questions chances are you will get an answer.  As for grading, she doesn't has an exact rubric for projects.  This does allow room for creativity, just remember to include what she says to include.  It really isn't a bad class, just do the work and take notes.

If you don't live, breath, and sleep theatRE, you're SOL with this class. I had to take it as a perspectives class and by week 3 I wanted to rip my hair out. She gives oodles of assignments, rarely updates her grade book, and expects you to magically understand the assignment with a minute amount of explanation. URGH!

Where to begin? How about the fact that this woman is out of her mind. She is an awful teacher. She will prattle on for an entire hour and you won't have learned a single thing. She is crazy, and her homework amount is ridiculous for a non-core class.
Worst professor ever. No need to explain.
DO NOT take this class with her. Worst teacher ever. Tons of homework; has no idea how to teach. She is easy to talk though.

Do not take intro to theatre with her. Professor is a time waster just to fill class time, assigns more homework than my core classes, does not get grades back in a timely manner. My most stressful class and has made caused me many mental breakdowns because of harsh grades.
Tons of homework

Do NOT take Intro to Theatre with her if you are expecting a blow off. She is one of those professors that thinks their class is the center of our education. Gives a lot of homework. Doesn't know how to teach. Finds ways to waste time class throughout. Grades the paper extremely late. Got most of my papers 1-2 months after I submitted them.

I love Amy so much! I had her my freshman year for Drawing 1, and decided to take Intro to Painting with her, and she's just as amazing! I've never painted before, and Amy really makes me feel comfortable and able to paint to the best of my ability! She is also always willing to help me out whenever I need it!

I loved Amy's way of teaching; it was very fun, and she's super nice. Her help and descriptions on how to do or fix something can sometimes be a little stressful, as she does it in a very hyperactive way. But she will definitely help you if you're struggling, as she fixed one of my eyes for me in my portrait. She also isn't harsh with grades.

Very funny, but if you're not a super great painter, she doesn't talk to you for more than a few minutes. Doesn't post guidelines for projects, gives confusing advice for what to fix. Generally frustrating class, also creatively restrictive. Doesn't like anything that isn't slightly stylized realism.

Amy is by far one of my favorite professors. I took her 8 am class (which she starts at 8:30) and I loved it. She is a great professor for any class, as she is such a funny and creative person. She could (verbally) tear your art to pieces, but she is so good at critique that you finish with a smile on your face and a good idea of what to fix.

I absolutely adore Amy, she is such a positive energy and wonderful instructor, I've taken her 8 am classes (which she starts at 8:30) twice and have enjoyed every minute of it. Her critique style is so well done, no matter how problematic your piece is you come out of it not only knowing what needs to change but also feeling confident.

Prof. McLaren is an honest grader, and she'll point out flaws in a piece with a very no-nonsense attitude. She looks for students who go above and beyond: staying late, asking questions, coming to the studio outside of class. Her teaching style is a lot to get used to, but all of her insights are worth it. Not a lot of projects, but a lot of work!
She has lot of energy at 8am somehow. She's very flexible, the class needed extra time on one of our assignments and she gave an extra two weeks. I also learned more in this class.

Amy was wonderful!  I had her for an 8AM class, and her energy made it worth waking up early for it.  She genuinely cares about her students, and is very understanding that some of the people who take the drawing foundation course may be photo majors that have less drawing skill.

Amy is amazing! I had no drawing experience before drawing 1, and she has been so helpful and good to me! I had Amy at 8am and she let us come in at 8:30. She also had an extra night drawing class just for anyone to finish up their final! As long as you do all of your drawings, Amy's class is an easy A!

As a first-year I was nervous about what to expect from drawing but Amy was amazing! She is extremely warm and welcoming and always wants to help her students improve. There aren't crazy amounts of homework if you use your time well in class, and you can always contact her outside of class even if you need help on anything.

Amy is amazing and I'm not exaggerating when I say she kept me going throughout my first semester. Class was always fun and my drawing skills improved significantly in her class. She started at 8:30 instead of 8, and we regularly got coffee breaks. I built my whole semester 2 schedule around getting her again.

Amy is hilarious and a great prof. Made class start at 8:30 instead of 8am. She is full of energy and makes class enjoyable. Kinda tough grader but gives you multiple grades throughout the project to improve. Super encouraging and gives helpful feedback. Don't buy everything on the supply list at once, I did and ended up not using 90% of it

I knew it was going to be a good year as soon as I walked into this class at 8am on a Monday. Amy has a lot of energy. She allows coffee breaks. She gives more than one grade per project. She doesnt give much homework, although she does give you her phone number in case you want to text her for feedback on anything. Be ready for constant feedback!

As a freshman who didn't have a lot of drawing experience, I was scared. The first day of class with Amy, I knew it was gonna be just fine. She is one of my favorite teachers I've ever had and is really passionate about what she does. She brings the class together and everybody's drawing significantly demonstrated improvement.

She is a hilarious professor and loves to get the class participating in a fun way during class. She is easy to talk to and is very helpful and providing suggestion to better your work. She even encourages you to text her at any time and she is willing to give feedback on your work when outside of the classroom.

By far, Amy is one of the greatest professors and teachers I've ever had.  Her advice, teaching, and honesty is unparalleled, and only surpassed by her personality.  She will push you out of your comfort zone and is not afraid to tell the truth plus, shes pretty funny.  I only wish she taught my illustration classes :(

Amy is the best drawing professor at RIT. She is energetic and passionate about drawing and helps each student fulfill their potential. She grades you on your ability  and not in comparison to others. If you show up and turn in work you will not fail her class. She gives out her number so you can her outside of class.  If you can, take her class!

Amy is probably one of my favorite drawing professors! As long as you manage your time in class theres a ton of freedom to leave the class to grab a coffee or anything. Would love to take a class with her again since she's so fun and funny! She's there to help you and show you how to draw better. HIGHLY RECOMMEND HER.
She's my most favorite teacher in my whole life. If I have a chance, I would take any classes with her no matter what! I had a class with her at 8 in the morning, she has a plenty of energy!

Amy was nice, although I didn't really care for most of her projects.  I did well in her class even though I'm into computer arts and not drawing.  If you had a question on your work outside of class you could takture and send it to you and she would help.  Overall a pretty easy class.

An amazing teacher, probably the best I have ever had. Classes are casual and she always listens to student feedback. Be prepared to learn about "happy accidents" and bricks that "make you want to cry". The big project of each quarter is usually finished by week 9 to help ease the burden of finals week. Would absolutely take her class again.
great teacher. super enthusiastic and knows what she is talking about. she expects a lot from you though. take her class if you want to GET BETTER at drawing, not just to get an easy A.

I thank her for my improvement in drawing... and art in general. Great teacher. She is a TRUE artist! She pushes her students to get better.. and they sure do! Fun and friendly lady!! Even though I was frustrated throughout her class (lack of drawing skills), she made me want to come to class and do better.

Great teacher! Really knows what she's doing but sometimes it's hard to understand the point she's trying to get across. Helped me get into drawing and improve amazingly. If you want an easy class don't take her: She's hard as hell, but she'll make you an amazing drawer.
Amy was my favorite teacher this year. She pushes you to your limits. Not clear on things- speaks in sounds rather than words. Take her, she's fun :)

Amy is a wonderful professor, willing to help you whenever you need it, and she genuinely cares about your growth as a student and individual, unlike most of the foundations teachers here. She's really hard to understand sometimes, but is very challenging and pushes you out of your shell to be better. She's adorable and full of energy. Take her.
She is sometimes hard to understand, and she can ask a lot of you, but if you push through and do the work, she definitely rewards you.

Great teacher, I absolutely hated drawing, design etc. before this course, but she really tried hard to make it fun and relevant. She gives a lot of freedom with assignments, so that was great for a foundation class, because I could still work in whatever medium I wanted. She was absolutely nuts, but I would take her again if I could.

She took over for Cliff Wun when he went on sabbatical, and I have to tell you- she was tougher than him in a lot of respects. Getting an A from Amy is nearly impossible, but you will learn a LOT. She is wacky, crazy, and a ton of fun. You'll love her.

Amazing teacher! I wouldnt replace her with anyone! She's tough but I've learned an incredible amount.  She likes to customize projects to what students want to do, and tries to keep people motivated.  She always has things to challenge people on, but gives enough compliments to boost confidence as well. Take her if you want to learn something.

Incredible teacher, I have learned a ton from her this in my drawing foundation classes. My class with her has improved much more than most other foundation classes.  She works you long and hard, but she'll take into account what students want to do and will try to make things fun.  Take classes with her if you want to learn something.
Soft spoken and very straightforward. He will assign homework and then proceed to do the problems in class. Everything is open notes, so as long as you take good note you should not have a problem.

It was his first time teaching the class, but he did pretty good! He kept handing out extra credit so that everyone could get to at least a B and therefore no one would need to take the final. He's also beyond chill about the course structure, so if you don't like something, just tell him.

comment: Class was really easy if you took electronics in high school. His voice is raspy and kinda hard to understand sometimes. His motions are really awkward and its really funny. But he is a nice and understanding guy if you forgot to do the homework or left it back at the dorms. Don't slack off when he teaches binary it is essential throughout the clas

The class I took with him was pretty much show up to class and work on that weeks project. Every now and then he would give a 20-40 minute lecture, which was always thorough and explained the concepts. There however was little guidance with setting up the technology unless you specifically asked for help. I really enjoyed the class.

Great debates was a really great class overall. Relatively easy assignments that are mostly graded for completion with one major assignment for the whole semester. Lectures were relatively interesting and she's clearly very passionate about a lot of the subject matter.

Dr. Edwards really made this class worth it. She teaches this class with a real passion, and as a result her lectures are quite engrossing. There's almost no homework, only three one-page papers and a three-page final. She's quite approachable if you enjoy talking about baseball, and she's obviously really informed about the sport and its history.

Edwards is very knowledgeable about baseball and history, so her lectures are good if you're interested in the course material. She also frequently opens the floor to discussion. The only grades in the class were participation and "letters" in which we summarized what we learned throughout the course, which were very open-ended.

I have taken classes by Professor Edwards before and I would take even more if I could. She is hilarious and extremely passionate about what she teaches, and it shows in her lectures and after-class conversations. Highly recommend her for any class she's teaching.

You can tell she really cares about what she lectures about. Attendance was a sign in sheet and your grade consists of participation (which was just attendance and submitting 3 or 4 discussion posts in the entire semester) as well as 3 essays that she grades leniently. Take her for a gen ed.

I absolutely adored every lecture by Professor Edwards, as she was passionate, engaged, and hilarious. Class discussions were important to this class, but there was no participation grade. She even cancelled a paper because she could tell we were all burnt out. I highly recommend her to anyone passionate about history and ready to laugh.

I absolutely adore this woman and recommend her History of Baseball class to anyone who wants to fill a perspective or have a chill time with an interesting class. I do not care about baseball at all but this woman's lectures had me emotionally invested. She is super engaging, banters with the class, does YOPS interviews, and has easy assignments.

History of baseball was super easy and I was typically engaged even though I'm not a baseball fan. You don't really have to do the readings and I think there were like 6 short papers you had to write for 100% of your grade. Easy A if you pay attention

I loved Dr. Edwards' History of Baseball class. She's very funny and makes the class super entertaining. While she doesn't take attendance, it can sometimes be a struggle to figure out what's going on if you've missed a class or two, but she's very good at keeping MyCourses updated and all around a great personality.

She really likes sports and the class was on the history of baseball, so she was knowledgeable about the material. It was very easy, mostly asynchronous and easy to forget about, but it didn't really matter. Literally BS your way through every essay and you'll be fine.

comment: History of Baseball was super easy. Outside readings, a couple 3 page papers, and a final report. Lectures were very interesting, you can tell she loves teaching this course.

Dr. Edwards is an absolutely phenomenal professor. Although the class is mostly lecture, it very much is an open forum for discussion. There is not much homework and the homework that is assigned is fairly short readings that are talked about in class the next day. She also tells hilarious but relevant stories in class, which are simply fantastic.

You have to show up to classes, she passes around a sign in sheet. This class has no tests or quizzes, there are only 3 short essays throughout the semester. Other than that there were a few short readings for homework but you could get by without reading them if you ever took a history class before.
Dumb class, all we did was look at her family tree and write papers about it. She tried to make it interesting, but eh.

History of baseball, great class. I had no interest in baseball. Passed the class with ease. Never spoke, the entire class is basically lecture but it doesn't put you to sleep.  She is very passionate about this class and loves to teach about baseball.

She is very opinionated, and if you don't agree with her, you're wrong.  She gave me an opinion C- on a paper because she didn't agree with me on my opinion.  Also, there are next to no guidelines for any of the papers.  On the plus side you can show up late for class because she is always around 10 minutes late herself.

She doesn't believe in giving exams because not all people are test takers.  She wanted very much for people to be involved in class.  You don't have to buy a book which is nice, but you do have to do all of the reading online (which really hurts my eyes). But get ready to read for every class

All she do is talk too much during the class and no tests, quizzes and exams except only 2 papers and projects. It wouldn't be helpful for you to get A for this course since i thought it is easy to pass but NOT. She is very harsh on the grading system and flexible on attendance, and optional assignment. It is hurting on your grade to fail this.

She talks way too much, goes off on tangents.  She grades really harshly because she thinks that all students should have the same writing abilities that she does.  She did give out two extra credit assignments though.  Wouldn't take her again.
Was so excited to take this class. She just talked the whole time and went on tangents. Wasn't helpful at all and winded up hating the class. Don't suggest a class with her.

She is very passionate about baseball, so it makes the class more fun. The textbook is useless, so I'm glad it's cheap. The only problem I had is that she talks the entire time, and if you miss a point or a name, you're screwed on the notes. Hopefully she gets a study guide. We always got out early, which was awesome!
Awesome Teacher, have her for Hist of Baseball, really energetic and really into the material, class requires little work, but goes over a ton of information, great teacher for a great class.

She knows what she's talking about but goes off on tangents and can get quite boring with the lectures - she just speaks with no visualizations - as much as I am a die-hard baseball fan. Women teaching baseball - don't know how I feel about that.

I loved her as a teacher, I took two of her classes, American History in Disabilities and Deaf history in the US. She was very interesting when she spoke and knowledgeable and always available for help.
She graded us based on our writing ability, not on our understanding of the material. This is History, not writing.

She's pretty biased in her essays. She only offered two essays, all were worth 30%, the remaining 10% was participation. First two essays, my opinion conflicted with hers and I got a C. The last essay, I changed my opinion to conform with hers and I got a B. It kind of says something.

Had her for American History:History of Baseball.  She knows her stuff well, obvious red sox fan(though i didn't mind as i hate the yankees anyways).  Grades pretty easy, oppertunites for extra credit, class doesn't usually last the full time, decent professor
I'm taking her again next year!
classes are discussion-oriented, very involved with interesting readings and field trips. interesting and intellectually challenging but it's not difficult to stay on top of material.
Very knowledgable in history. Her classes tend to be long, and most times boring, but she has a wealth of information to share. Grading is pretty easy.
She is awesome.  I loved going to class.
Hated this class.  She is totally type A.

Professor Clark is a great guy. Funny personality (very dry sense of humor), not a lot of work, lenient grading and will talk about things that matter, not just the curriculum. I'd take him again if I didn't have a scheduling conflict. He's a great option for comm.

For a communication teacher he was very bad at communicating to the class which made the work confusing and infuriating at times. He was also rather rude to the class and students making condescending jokes and put down. He also had little respect for boundaries and would look through my notebook or ask too personal of questions.

Public Speaking course. Attendance was taken daily but only really counted on days when speeches were occurring. Speeches were frequently assigned but usually not to challenging. He likes to make silly jokes and you are a shoe-in for an A if you are on his good side. Textbook not necessary and only used for two online quizzes.

He jokes around a lot in class but as long as you get on his good side he's a really good professor. I had him for Public Speaking where he counted attendance on days that we had speeches so that we could support our classmates but the rest of the days attendance is not mandatory. You only need the textbook for the 2 online quizzes.
very approachable person. Willing to talk about anything and gives great advice. Even though some of the activities are broken he's there helping everyone to make sure they can be completed.

Great professor-He not just is unhappy about how the course structure isn't great, but he wants to improve the outdated labs, and started doing mini lectures/a few fun facts. All work is online, doesn't really take attendance ig but 2 lowest quizzes changed to 100 if you attend every class. Very reasonable, nice/helpful prof! "This is true" indeed.

Professor Martin is new to RIT, but he is caring and very accessible outside of class. He came from the industry, so he has insights to share. The course is fairly easy, and the vibe was great. He try to have minimal homeworks assigned for students. And encourages group work. Overall, I highly recommend Professor Martin!
Dude fell asleep during my presentation. I'm sure once upon a time he was great but the class itself I gained nothing from.

Awful! LITERALLY falls asleep EVERY WEEK during class presentations. Changed main class project AFTER add/drop period to be more difficult. REQUIRES us to watch dozens of pre-recorded videos, even though its an in-person class and lecture covers the SAME topics at a tenth the pace of videos. Quizzes have questions we've never covered. Never again

unorganized. no need to show up to class he just asks weird open ended questions. He grades the semester long 3 part project very very leniently (easy 100 for doing it), not difficult at all. His tests are full of unfair bogus trick questions... despite this, this class is the easiest A you'll get with very very little time put in (skip class)

His lectures aren't great, the tests are meh. But he is extremely flexible and all aspects of the projects were negotiable if you wanted to do something else, does his best to help students, and is very friendly and sweet. What his lectures lack he makes up for by being kind and open to feedback. Also the class was not that hard.

Seems like a nice guy but not a fan of his class. He would record video lectures and made you teach yourself. comment: Honestly surprised there aren't more reviews for Dr. Hittinger. I took his decision analysis class as part of my PUBL immersion and he was great. Would highly recommend, awesome Professor

Dr. Hittinger is amazing. He is obviously very enthusiastic about the topic of energy and makes it very fun to learn. There are a lot of essays (like one/two page) so if the class is in your immersion instead of your main curriculum its seems harder to find the motivation to do them. Had for Climate Change. His section was the best: fun, interesting, and very practical discussions. A great sense of humor. Did a great job teaching us Climate Policy without needing an economics background. Had a fun class game for us, too. Papers require some serious research work.

a lot of your grade in this class comes from one paper and one group project. Make sure you get a good group or it will be difficult. Also, he has a dog that he brings to class if everyone wants him to. Overall, great professor and you'll learn a lot

Prof Lee did not want to be in class, maybe this was because the material was so basic, maybe he just hates teaching this class. Oh dear. You can tell this man is brilliant and loves the subject, but he does not teach anything at all. This course was my biggest cause of stress this semester, and I was surprised not to fail. He will answer your questions, but often you're too confused for that to help you.
Bad professor, gives out homeworks and expects students to inherently know how to do them.

Smart man, but a horrible teacher. He talks extremely fast, and no one at my table could keep up. He is confusing and somewhat unhelpful at explaining things. Fortunately we had an awesome TA (John). I was very good at physics before I took him, and I had a horrible time in his class.

Talks too fast and doesn't cover material clearly. He is useless at answering questions, as he just talks in circles and leaves you wondering why he said anything at all. Very intelligent man. tests are BRUTAL. class average is around a 65 and curves it to a 75 however. show as much work as possible. vaguely goes over stuff and relies on the TA a lot.
He is a good professor. Lectures may go a bit fast at times but if you don't understand everything you should definitely go and see him during office hours, he is extremely helpful.
Professor Andersen is by far the best professor I came across at RIT. Although I did not get an A in his class. He always tried to make the subject interesting and challenging at the same time

The best physics professors I have interacted with. always ready to help and challenges the student to think on his/her own. Always ready to give advise and extremely active when teaching. Knows the course really well but wants the student to dig in more . In his books efforts count a lot.

He is a very intelligent man however he is very vague when solving problems and assumes that everyone is on the same level, but I will admit that this office hour is the golden key to passing the class even though he doesn't leave much open so he's kind of hard to talk to if the time exceeds more than 30 minutes.

Prof Anderson is a very smart man, but he is unable to recognize that students in physics 311 don't know as much as he does.  When you ask him a question, he makes you feel very stupid and then hardly answers the question.  Would not recomend unless you already know everything covered in the course.

Are you a genius? Then this is your professor. Unfortunately I'm not. If you can catch concepts at the speed of light and want to learn a new way of doing things(he really changed my way of doing problems, for instance, now i do everything algebraicly and then i plug in numbers), then chose him. But if you are not the best**** then go to another.
One of the best professor I ever have

Horrible teacher.  Talks WAY too fast and will make you feel stupid for asking him a question.  Impossible grader and his tests are never like any of the work done for the class.  Claims to grade labs one way but will take points off for ridiculous things.  Nit picks.  DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY IF YOU WANT TO PASS.

Anderson teaches WAY too fast.  If you take him, don't be surprised if you have to do most learning from the book.  He is very helpful though, outside of class hours, and tends to be able to teach things more slowly one-on-one.  Also, his test questions are unlike anything he covers in class.
Doc Andersen is a premium professor.  he is helpful both in and out of class and is mad cool to boot.
Hard professor, but makes it up in the end with huge curve.  Expect to learn a LOT!!!
Moves super fast, ask a question and he'll make you feel stupid.  Such a bed prof that a 70 is an A and a 45 is a C.

Unclear instructions, discussions are due before the due date, when? no clue. How many of my peers am I supposed to respond to? No clue. Discussions are 2 points, so you get 1/2 credit if you miss one of these criteria. No actual teaching, just chapters in a textbook, no personal feedback. She is just a grader collecting a check, not a teacher.

Pretty lame/lazy prof. Deadlines? Incredibly blurry. Get ready to respond to 5 classmates' discussion posts on a Saturday night. Only ended up posting 4 responses or were late and had to post them Sunday? 1/2 credit. Sounds insignificant but it tanks your grade. The only good part is that the weekly quizzes are unlimited tries.

This class could be easy, but Dr. K's rudeness ruins the experience. She's condescending, unhelpful, and quick to shut students down. Instructions are unclear, yet she grades like everything was perfectly explained. If you can tolerate being treated poorly when you have a question, you will pass—but it won't be enjoyable.

If you reach out to her and email her she is super nice! However, when something is due on a Monday it really means it is due on Friday. So if you take her class make sure you do things a few days before they are due. You can retake quizzes as many times as you want/need until you get a 100. Overall, it is a great asynchronous class!

I stupidly submitted my rough draft/notes for my final paper and received a horrible grade. I emailed Kmiecinski immediately and she was very understanding. Please do not make a foolish mistake because her assignments are clear if you simply pay attention,

She is a lovely person and lectures are interesting. My only feedback would be that sometimes, there are little details that she says won't be on the test (like the DRI for calcium, tiny numbers like that) and then they WILL be on the test. So make sure you memorize as many of the detail numbers if you can. Some information outdated. Overall great!
Had her for Sports Nutrition. Terrible class, would not recommend. Doesn't understand what a deadline means, and is no help at all when it comes to the material. Don't take a class with her.

3 credit class with roughly 26 hours of work outside of class each week. Powerpoints and handouts are confusing and difficult to follow even if you were in lecture taking notes. Exam "review" includes her handing you a simple list of the powerpoints, case studies and handouts that could possibly be on it.  Very intimidating.

Elizabeth L. is quite strict with online discussion because if you post from friday-monday and then you will receive either 0 or one point out of two. This class only has one easy way and that is to receive C or below if you want to hurt your GPA.

She is very strict, provides little assistance, and has grades due on mondays but if you turn it in on monday or on sunday you get half credit. 48 question quiz with two short answers you only get an hour. questions were obscure. she will not let you complete the course ahead of schedule.

Online Sports Nutrition class-grading was mostly from weekly discussion (must reply to 8 other students). Is strict grader,grading what you didn't do vs. what you did. Final was online with 62 Q's in an hour. The Q's were too specific, needing exact numbers,and short answers.Barely got to complete the test with a minute left. I don't recommend.
He keeps you busy throughout the week, like three submissions in a week. Ideal to take his course in summer rather than taking it with other subjects in Fall/Spring.

Started this class with an aim to LEARN. Completed it, and I was NOT disappointed. The amount of take-away was huge. Grades well. Knows A LOT! Very helpful

Nice guy. Online class was pretty relaxed with a moderate workload. Responsive to emails and was generally very helpful if you had questions. Tests were a bit difficult however and he relies on his students to provide test questions which I find to be a bit odd.
He's very helpful. The midterm and the final were easy; we were able to use cheat sheet in both of them. His grading is fair. His way of teaching is very interesting and very easy to understand.

Definitely a good professor to take this course with. Clifton had some fun with the class, but I genuinely also felt that I learned quite a bit. The class consisted of some online quizzes, writing assignments, group discussions, and a final group project.
Great teacher. He made his own textbook so we dont have to buy one, each lecture was very interesting and funny, and homework assignments are actually fun to do.

Professor Clifton was my best professor this semester. He truly cares about all of his students and gives amazing feedback on every paper. Clifton is a super chill dude and his lectures are super interesting. All quizzes are online and can be taken as many times as needed, which is nice. Clifton wrote his own textbook over quarantine, so the book is free. loved this class!! interesting discussions and lenient grader, described the material extremely well and honestly made me consider doing my immersion in ethics

Clifton is a great professor! Textbook is his own so you don't need to buy one. He's a pretty caring guy and knows what he's talking about. I looked forward to Professor Clifton's class as a nice break during my week. The atmosphere is relaxed and the topics are interesting. Make sure to remember discussion posts.

David Sanchez was the professor who re-sparked my interest in 3D. I'm so happy to have had him. he sits down with you and helps answer your questions, makes you feel appreciated in the class, and respects the work you put into the class! overall, amazing professor

A huge advocate for blended learning (in classroom and online)...if you don't like online classes, don't take this one. A good portion of your grade depends on the online aspect! Very understanding of people with disabilities

I personally hated Jenkins. He is full of himself and full of his area of study (intercultural communication, of course) I am a straight A honors student at RIT and did not get an A in his class. And I found it really boring. Don't take it if you can manage...
Extremely hard teacher! WAAAAYYY too much work for the unimportant classes he teaches! Expect lots of busy work and hardly any actual teaching or lecturing! Poor teacher and way to strict on grades!

A lot of busy work.. You have to do five interviews with people of different cultures and have to read and respond to each and every persons journals (about ten in your group). Gets old after a while. Class is mandatory! If you don't go to class you will most likely get a lower letter grade. Taking notes is a MUST.
Jenkins is a good professor. He knows a lot and is willing to help students. I just felt like his tests were impossible to pass. The class is a lot of work but if you're willing to do it, then do it.
Jenkins draws for attention.  He is awesome.

Well spoken & entertaining...never boring.  Lots of work but if you do it, you will do well.  Fair grading, # of assignments/test.  Tests do have book reading info so read book.  Focus on PPs though & attend class bc it is on test too.  Test are tough but he prepares you well if you pay attention in class & study 1 hr a day starting a week b4 test.
Very straight-forward with assignments and expectations. Stuck to the syllabus. Not difficult, but not easy.
Best guy ever!!!! Interesting, understanding, funny...
The greatest professor ever. So interesting...  You have to do the work but if you have at least some interest in the class, you'll do just fine.
tests are quite hard but lectures are interesting. If you're looking for an easy A, look elsewhere
Great professor overall, goes out of his way to get to know you.  his tests are not easy, but you will learn alot.  his grading methods are consistent.

She is super helpful, caring, and genuinely seems to care about her students. Course is very lecture heavy but its also just a lot of material to get through so it makes sense. She teaches directly from the textbook for the most part, so if you read the book you will be fine.

She is a very difficult and picky grader, her instructions and rubrics are very vague and she never explains more than the bare minimum. Most of her assignments or instructions are taken from different colleges; she did not seem to have any original assignments, potentially being the reason for vague expectations.
Online textbook is worth the money, fun and engaging lectures. Written assignment feedback is good but grading is fair, not easy - spend a week on each of the two. Relevant class! Take Psyc 101!

It can be annoying how she responds to you in that child-like way but the atmosphere is chill. She has very little tolerance for late work or being interrupted while lecturing. Outside of class though, she's helpful with questions and likes having conversations about stuff. Just look like you're paying attention to the lecture and get ahead on work

comment:
Dr. Chand-Matzke really brings energy to the classroom. Overall very interesting survey of psychology with lots of selected case studies and section readings that add body to the material. 

Grading wise, the exams are open textbook and notes, and all of the other assignments are completion based except 2 research reports and infographic projects.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Good professor but mostly boring lectures. Decent amount of coursework but not too difficult overall. She is strict on grading your 2 papers but gives good feedback.

All quizzes & exams are online. There are weekly in-class assignments that are just participation points. Her lectures were so interesting-- she explains things well & makes sure students understand key concepts. She cares a lot about participation & encourages it, but it is not mandatory. She is one of my favorite professors here! Highly recommend

If you have her you must go to class, each day there is graded assignments that ended up bringing my grade from an A to a B only because I missed class. If you go to every class you will be fine, but the classes are somewhat boring.

Her classes all around were okay, she is a decent professor. Work was pretty average leaning towards hard. But while I was in the hospital due to a kidney stone, I was unable to submit my paper on time. She refused to accommodate and accept my paper. And for that I can't give her more than a two.

If you read/take notes on the textbook, you'll do great. Tests and quizzes are open note. Go to class because there's in-class assignments. Lectures are boring and cover what you read in the textbooks but she gives research examples and is passionate. There are 2 papers and 2 infographics. The class is easy if you just do the work as you go.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Chand-Matzke was one of my least favorite professors I've had at RIT. Her class is not hard, just exceedingly boring and will put you to sleep every class (which would not slide and you'd have a fun meeting with her). She only knows how to read slides made from the textbook (which you have to read anyways), and talks to you as if you're a child.
She has a nice personality but is a very harsh grader and assigns a lot of homework. I do not recommend taking her at all.
For giving hard to follow presentations, she is a harsh grader. Not very flexible. Don't recommend.

An able and intelligent person, but not very well suited to teaching. I learned a lot from her class, mostly from the textbook that we were required to read. Trivial group assignments enforced attendance and textbook-oriented homework enforced reading. Good class overall, but be prepared to rework your learning style to fit exactly what she wants.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Do not take her! she gives an unnecessary amount of homework and papers to complete. She made us do 4-pages of lab each week, conduct research and write a sample paper that was about 20-30 pages, and complete two homework assignments per week. AVOID her at all costs, specifically for PSYC-251.

This professor's lecture is lengthy, & she frequently provides confusing feedback. She assigned so many assignments other course fell sideway. At the halfway point of the semester, the class average on the first draft of a research paper was 59%, it was later curved to 65%, allowing some of us to pass the course.  Dont take her class if you can.

Dr. Chand-Matzke is very caring and does her best to support everyone. When we answered questions, she did her best to acknowledge what everyone said and encouraged everyone, regardless of if the answer was wrong. She does not take late work but did allow me to resubmit a large assignment because of a dropbox mix-up. Focuses only on psych research.

Matzke is always willing to help you out. Her homework, quizzes and tests are textbook heavy but if you are interested in the material the textbook should be just fine. She can be a boring lecturer but makes it easy to pass and review on your own. Doesn't allow tech for notes so have paper and pencil. Syllabus is clear on what happens each week.

She is a great professor and really loves when people participate. However, it is not mandatory. Assignments are usually pretty simple and just check that you are keeping up with the class material. The tests and quizzes are pretty easy if you pay attention in class and read the textbook chapters. Really nice professor, do take a chance on her!

Chand-Matzke is a good professor. She cares about her students and is very accommodating. Homework is manageable and tests were never too difficult. Attendance was only required on one day for in class activities (you would just get an A on them for showing up and trying). Lectures were kind of boring but that's more the material instead of her.

I dont understand her bad reviews? Lectures are easy to follow and are posted online. She gives many examples of class material for whole class understanding. Attendance only matters on one class day and she tells you when. Only Hw is easy 10 question quizzes once a week and a short paper every few weeks. Tests are MC and 2 very short answer.

Chand-Matzke was one of the worst professors I've ever had. She did not have a very interesting teaching style, and all her tests are based on the textbook readings. There was never a time that I wanted to go to her class. I would not recommend her, especially if you like psychology. She will ruin it for you.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: I have taken this professor for a few classes and I think that she does a good job explaining the material for the tests. There is barely any homework and there is usually a paper that is due by the end of the semester. Her tests are not bad at all as long as you know your notes. She is so sweet and always willing to help out!

Professor Chand-Matzke seems nice and caring. However, despite working really hard in her class, it was almost impossible to get an A in her class. Class average on her exams were in the C's. She has a very monotone voice and expected so much work put in for a 200 level psych course. I would not recommend taking a psych class with her.

Professor Chand-Matzke seems to be a good person at heart, but her teaching style is very difficult to follow along with. Her lectures are hard to follow and really don't help with the tests, which are 72% of your overall grade and they are abstract and very difficult to do good on. There is no HW which makes it harder to follow along in class.

Rambling lectures, but good class structure, if you make sure to do the reading you should be good to go. Some people get really whiny about her classes but if you put in a medium amount of effort it's not hard to get a good grade. Material ok, not amazing.

Mediocre professor. Lectures are very boring and hard to pay attention to. Lecture slides are unorganized and confusing. Relies on a lot of class participation. Tests are poorly worded and does not grade on a curve if class average is low, which significantly impacts your grade.

Well organized, lectures were methodical and repetitive at times, but informative. Gives good study guides! Very easy to talk to outside of class and very friendly. My favorite class the semester I took it.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Would take again']

comment: Okay professor, not great but also not horrible. Her lectures mostly go off the book with a few studies and TEDx talks that are important to pay attention to, as they will come up as exam questions. Exams were difficult mostly due to the wording of each question, and some questions seemed more subjective but only had one correct answer.

She is very professional and good at teaching. She makes the material and her expectations very clear. You will have to read a chapter from the textbook each week and you'll have a few research articles to read and write about. There is an average amount of homework, but the assignments and exams are easy if you put in a little effort.m

Definitely not the easiest professor, her lectures basically went over what was in the book and weren't too exciting. The tests were fairly hard if you haven't fully understood the material or remembered a lot of it.

I was super excited to take personality because I thought it would be interesting, but do yourself a favor and take it with a different professor! Her exam questions are not fair, and it's VERY opinionated. She has a very monotone voice, so lectures are difficult to pay attention to and she likes to focus on theories that are not well supported.
Be prepare to write. Grades pretty harshly and lectures are pretty boring. Expect to do a lot of reading on your own and has high expectations for students.
She teaches well and pushes for classroom interaction. As long as you're ready to be there and learn, the class is a nice A to add.

SO MUCH WRITING. I took her psychology of gender class. The material was super interesting to me, but her class quickly became the most dreadful activity I had to do  every week. Endless amounts of writing for a 200 level class. I would never take her again. There were no tests either. Literally everything was another writing assignment.

I took Personality with Dr. Chand-Matzke and enjoyed it. Only thing is that sometimes you had no idea what to study for the exams (there's so much material), but once we gave her that feedback she started doing review sheets which helped a ton on narrowing it down. You'll definitely work but I found her reasonable and you knew what was expected.

She is really good at clarifying things up and making sure we are in a normal pace of getting through everything to make sure we have understood the material/ goals in this course. We had conducted an informal experiment and worked on our final APA paper for the whole semester. There is only one midterm exam.

You have to read every chapter of the book and come to class ready to discuss. This was a Tue-Thur class, so Tue was "Lecture" (which was basically non-graded discussion) and Thur was "Discussion" (where you are expected to participate at least once for a grade). The class completely turned me away from personality psychology and was very boring.

1. Where is the humor in this world?  2. Slides and book materials are too different, althought quizzes so far are basically all from the book (plus 5-8 page long articles she expects you to have read b4 class) 3. Expects too much from you (read book & articles before class, quizzes of new materials at the beginning of the week)

Way too much work for an intro class. The tests should have been easy, but they weren't because she didn't get to half the material in class that was covered in class. We barley ever got through powerpoint and were behind after the second day. Didn't enjoy the course and I wish I took it with a different professor.  Also there were a ton of quizzes

I've taken two classes with this professor and she's one of the better professors in the Psych department, IMO. She genuinely seems to care about students' success and definitely knows what she's talking about. Though she can be almost too politically correct, it's all with good intentions. Make sure you put effort in and triple check formatting.

She explains the material pretty well, but does not cover that much material in class. She does not show any emotion. If you painted her silver, you would never know she is not a robot. Has no sense of humor and makes class feel tense. Quizzes are extremely specific. She basically asks how many commas were in the third line of the 5th paragraph.

Very clear in her expectations, but it really isn't that much work. It just seems like a lot. If you do your reading you will definitely pass. She is also very understanding. There are some small in class group assignments so do your reading or you won't know what to do!

Expectations were very clear, and tests/quizzes rarely went outside of what was covered in class, and never outside the textbook. Not the most interesting class but very straightforward. Just do the assignments, take decent notes and you'll get an A

Meh, that's all her class is. Quizzes are open notes, open book, online and last 10 mins and have 10 questions. The biggest problem is that you LEARN the week before via the textbook, then you LEARN in class again AFTER YOU TAKE THE QUIZ. The class is backwards. Also takes participation grades randomly. If you have her for 8am like me, you'll cry.

She is the most boring teacher I have ever had.  Her lectures are bland and she has absolutely no personality.  Her study guides absolutely suck and  the textbook is painful.  Psychology can be fun but not with this professor.
She's very clear about her expectations and her lass. Class is pretty useless because her power points are literally just notes of the textbook readings. Her class is veryyyyyy boring.
Clear and concise. Most information needed is in the book but attending class is crucial, as well. Offers extra credit for attendance!
She lays out the entire course in the syllabus and give an abundance of reminders.  Her lectures aren't the most exciting, but she speaks very clearly.

She was completely monotonous and didn't really teach. She only read from her powerpoint which contained little, to no information. For not teaching a lot, there was a TON of info on our exams that she never went over in depth. I really just dreaded going to her class and if you can opt out from taking this course, DO IT
tests are difficult, reading the textbook helps, as it is like a vocab test. and they are open book. critiques are simple and easy to do, she drops the lowest grade if you do all three
Very hard teacher, the lecture exams are not easy. Even the research papers she gets very nitty gritty with small details. very challenging class.

Your grade is based on 3 papers and 3 tests. The papers are very straightforward. You MUST read the textbook as much of the test is based on the readings. Take notes while reading the textbook and use it as your study guide. She's very clear with the material. Extra credit is offered.

Honestly not a fan of her course nor teaching style. I'll be honest I dont really go to class, its just straight lecturing and its far from interesting. Reading the text book is a must for her class as well as attending ALL lectures if you truthfully want an A. She does put her powerpoints online though and the class structure is very doable.

This professor has very tough tests. Many many hours of studying are required and only when I killed myself studying for days, did I get an A. minimal studying doesn't cut it. You HAVE to read the textbook and pay attention. She teaches onlyyy through powerpoints which are also available online.

Very straightforward class. Basically you go to the lectures, listen, take notes, & leave. Attendance isn't mandatory but is completely necessary if you plan to do even remotely well. Read the textbook. She won't "check" if you did, but your test grades will reflect it. I learned to like her teaching style, but if you hate lectures don't take her

the class is two straight hours of lecturing. attendance isn't mandatory but if you don't go to class, you miss a huge amount of content. DO THE READINGS. if you don't you will get no higher than a C on her tests, guaranteed. her grading is based on two essays & three tests. definitely not a class in which you can slack off.
She wasn't easy, but I learned to love psychology. She is an amazing prof. The class size was small and the examples were interesting. No quizzes, the tests were mostly out of the book.

Professor Nagappan understands that Math Models can be abstract and difficult, and he makes sure to explain things as many times as necessary until everyone in class gets it.  He's very clear in his descriptions and often brought candy to class for students who answered review questions correctly.  Assignments and tests were fairly easy.

Although Mei is new think a pretty good job  teaching, in my opinion, a bad course. He knows his stuff and is very helpful if you have any questions. He also pushed back assignmentsprojects when the class had no idea what was happening. He's definitely a great guyteacher just stuck with an obscure course to teach.

Prof. Mei is new at RIT. I really enjoy him as a professor as he was recently a student himself and he understands the difficulty of it. He excels at giving lectures and is always available outside of class. He cares tremendously about how students perceive him and often asks for feedback. I would take more classes with him.

Teese is a good choice as far as physics profs. here go. He's caring, and a fun guy once you get farther into the semester. He gives plenty of time for homework, and the lectures are relatively clear. The class itself is hard, but Teese makes it bearable (though a somewhat boring).

Don't get me wrong, he is a good guy and appears to be a fair grader. It's his teaching method I struggle with. It relies a lot on self teaching, and he doesn't really explain the material or procedure beforehand. He'll prod you in the right direction if you ask him, but it's still asking us to figure out challenging material on our own.
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GROUP PROJECTS']

comment: He generally explains what you're doing (sort of) but it's mostly on you and your group to figure out what to do.  Lots of labs and group lab reports.  The class wasn't easy, but he was good about partial credit when it was due.

I liked Teese. The material is not easy, make no mistake, but this is true of any Physics class. He has a very off sense of humor, and might be a little old to be still teaching, but he was always very kind and helpful whenever I asked for it. He doesn't take time to coddle those who don't pay attention, however; you'll get out what you put in.
clearly he is bad in teaching and he couldn't deliver the clue so it will be self study class  but maybe he is good in another field that has not teaching.
He doesn't explain anything clearly, and treats you as if you know everything. He made me hesitate of wanting to become an engineer.

As far as physics professors go, Dr. Teese was one of the better ones in my opinion. Has an enthusiasm for physics and explains things fairly clearly. However, sometimes he can be a bit boring, so it's hard to pay attention to his explanations. Is very willing to help students in and out of class. I would recommend him.

Dr. Teese is a good guy and tries to bring some humor to physics. He explains the material well and then gives practice problems on it and comes around helping you with the problems. I would recommend anyone take his class

Nice guy, different sense of humor, but that adds to making the class more interesting. Explains things fairly well. Has lots of patience which helps when you are a new to the course. Clear to understand. Show commitment and you'll gain respect.

I personally loved him. He explains every topic very well before we go and do problems on it. His has a dry humor which can be refreshing at times for such a boring topic like physics. Many people would say that he isn't good, but it isn't his fault. Physics is a hard subject to teach, and he does the best compared to other UP1 teachers.

This professor is actually very clear in his lectures. If you can stay focused and listen to him he does explain things clearly. He gives you tons of example problems and he drills it in your head. He is much better than the professors that just talk theory all lecture and dont give you anything to work with. I dont know how you could fail

This professor is horrible. i failed his class and now it ruined my GPA. i went to his classes as much as possible. i took physics 1A and the extra day was no point. DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN AS A PROFESSOR!!! he does not help you and does not care to fail you

Don't expect him to teach you if you're in 311, as you're supposed to be dependent on your group. The only thing he does is hand out worksheets. He spends more time helping out individual students one at a time than the class, but that means you just have to wait two hours get help on something. Not a bad guy though.

The best advice is to not take this class at 8:00 if possible. Dr. Teese doesn't really grab your attention, and if you need help with something, he'll just tell you that you're a future engineer, so figure it out yourself. But luckily, our TA wakes up from the dead to "help us". "Help us" as in calling Bob Teese over. The tests aren't bad though.
Very dry in teaching, unlikely to provide useful help in class.... better luck getting help from the TA. Not a horrible person though.

Does not teach. Expects us to learn material and finish web assigns on new material before class, then puts us through the lectures on the material we just self-learned. Relatively easy tests. 85 class average
Good professor. Boring at times, but better than others I've had. He tries not to talk too long so you can work in groups. I understand everything he taught.
No Comments
No Comments

Prof. Lott did very well teaching Beginning ASL 1. She is Deaf, which helped me learn the language much faster than I expected, and the way it was taught seemed very good. Even though the class was scheduled for 2 hours, it generally ended after only 1, which was nice.

If you like reading, and I mean lots of it, then you'll definitely like this professor and the classes that she teaches. Very minimal homework aside from reading, and there are very few assignments that count for a grade. She is also a very lax grader and will give you opportunities to better your grade if you ask. Attend class and you'll pass.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Do you like almost daily reading? If so Genre Fiction is for you, her lecture is a bit dry but she always gives time for discussion. There's two big papers as well as a group project, but you get to pick what it's based on and overall was a lot of fun but a lot of work.

Professor Shackelford is extremely nice and patient with her students. Lectures are a tad dry, but the content was interesting and gives you a new perspective on technology. Its obvious that she is very knowledgeable about her field, but can come across awkwardly. Interesting class, would take again.
Really sweet, gives extremely helpful feedback. There is barely any work, you have to write 3 essays, but everything else is a short writing assignment. The reading is quite boring.
Nice person but lectures are dull. She does too much group work.  Medium-grader. Not an easy A, but obtainable.
Friendly, clear, and helpful- a good all-around professor.
She's really super nice and the class is fun.

An inviting and enjoyable professor. The class is fun and interesting, assuming you do the reading. She makes use of the library's resource sharing, so be prepared to print 80% of the reading assignments (or go to the printing place on campus). Be prepared to discuss the reading in class. 3 shorter Essays, and 1 long one at the end of the quarter.

Had Bob for Single Frame and he was so laid back and nice. He's helpful and explains assignments a lot before you have to do them. The last 30 minutes of this class is boring, he kills time but he is easygoing and you learn a lot. You get what you put into this class.
A really nice and well-meaning guy.  He knows his stuff but isn't the best at teaching it.  Give him a few more years here and he'll improve.
Does not understand how to use Maya. Asks TA for answers to most questions. AVOID. AVOID.

Dr. Kinsman is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. Every lecture is engaging and he provides personal anecdotes or stories to help you gain a truly deep understanding the data mining topics without feeling overwhelmed. Pay attention and participate in class; you learn A LOT and your grade will reflect that.

One of the best professors I've had. I finally got to understand and remember the fundamentals of data science after 2 years of self studying and not getting anywhere. My favorite aspect of prof kinsman is how he teaches the topics by incorporating data mining and stories about his own life. I think it really helped make his lectures engaging.

Clearly cares about students. During my time with him he had to take over for a professor who had just left a month into the class. Regardless, I think he not only effectively worked with the time he was given, but also provided some rather inspirational input that made me want to pursue data science outside of the class.

Best lectures I've had in all my time at RIT. There's a lot of content to go over, but you listen to the very easy to understand slides, and you're all set. If he goes over something twice, that's important.

Dr. Kinsman is very wise; most everything he says is worth paying attention to, even if it isn't related to the class. The homework and tests are geared toward helping students learn and test true understanding. You cannot simply coast and memorize simple facts to pass his classes, but he makes it easy and enjoyable to learn the material.

Undoubtedly, Dr. Kinsman is the best professor I've had. Every lecture was engaging, informative, and well-paced, with anecdotes that helped to understand the material. Always willing to help during office hours and gave great feedback. Homework reinforced concepts without being overwhelming. Do the homework, pay attention, and you'll do very well.

Dr. Kinsman makes material genuinely click. His assignments aren't just busywork, they actually prepare you for jobs. I found myself drawing on concepts from his class directly during interviews & I'm convinced it played a part in landing my summer internship. If you get the chance to take a class with him, take it!

Dr. Kinsman is an incredible professor and really cares about his students. The lessons taught and homework assignments given were useful in talking to companies for interviews. I enjoyed his undergrad level class and elected to take this grad class with him as well because of how much I enjoyed his teaching style. I would highly recommend him!

Dr. Kinsman is, by far, one of the best professors I had class with. Our Data Mining class was required to change Professor midway. Overall, Dr. Kinsman communicated the materials clearly, and he allowed us to bring cheat sheets to mid term and finals. It could have been better if the online materials were a bit more organized.
He is a great professor that genuinely cares about his students and wants the best for them. He makes the class material easy to digest and makes class engaging.

Honestly one of the single best professors I have ever had the pleasure of taking a class with. He is very knowledgeable and wants you to pass his class. While he does go on tangents from time to time, I find them to still be interesting and applicable to the material at hand. If you have the chance while at RIT, take his data mining course!

He introduces every topic in such a creative and engaging way, it instantly grabs your attention. His teaching style makes complex concepts feel simple and fun.
He's cheerful and genuinely cares about students' learning and well-being. Even if you're shy, he'll make you feel comfortable and included. Fun, insightful, and full of positive energy!

Dr. Kingsman is an excellent lecturer. He provides a wealth of learning resources and clearly explains how algorithms work and how they operate in class. At the same time, he uses interesting teaching methods to keep me listening attentively, and his analogies reinforce my understanding of algorithms.

No one in class learned any Advanced Computer Vision. Lectures about unrelated topics like lighthouse lenses and how GPS/LORAN radio systems work. Any CV topics covered are 20+ years old, with ZERO lecture topics on recent CV advances. Disorganized to the point where 3 assignments are due tomorrow, when none have been mentioned. Waste of time/money

This guy is an icon. I took csci420 and csci431 with him and had a good time. Sure, things were really unorganized and grading was confusing sometimes, but the lectures were fun and he always had some wacky demo to show everybody. Very knowledgeable about the content and exams were pretty easy (open note). Homeworks were few and mostly easy.

This is not a computer vision class. He instead teaches you imaging science and you learn almost nothing relevant to computer vision. He's an okay professor and a nice guy, but I feel like he pulled a bait and switch as the course I had was completely different from the course description in SIS. I would avoid him for computer vision.

Didn't learn much from the class, lectures are very simple, you're better off studying the topics covered yourself with online resources for enough depth to do good in exams. Writeups are confusing, and oversimplify easy projects with bad wording. Would take for easy A, but don't expect to learn a crazy amount of Data Mining from him.

Dr. Kinsman is an amazing professor who puts great effort into his lectures and cares for the success of his students. He sometimes preps live demonstrations relevant to the topic and presents topics in an engaging way with the class. While this might not be an easy class, Dr. K makes it very easy to stay focused and learn.

Dr. Kinsman was a professor truly for the students. Even though the content was hard at times, he really simplified and explained it in a way that made sense. He dropped our lowest homeworks, quizzes, etc. and was extremely understanding if we needed to hand things in late (not taking points off). He was always flexible and very easy to talk to.

Dr. Kinsman cares deeply about his students & their welfare. He walks you through the weeds of high-quality data analysis with ease & makes the journey fun. The homeworks in his class are moderately heavy, but practice vital skills; the projects, such as working with raw GPS data, can make a resume light up. Prioritizes students health and success.

Kinsman can be a bit awkward or present content in a tangential way but his lectures are always so engaging with fun and practical samples that it makes it easy to get into the content on your own time.

Professor Kinsman taught the course in an engaging and enjoyable way, making the concepts easier to understand than I had experienced before. I found that keeping an open mind was key to fully grasping the material as it was presented. His ability to make the lectures more interactive and thought-provoking really enhanced the learning experience.

I completed an online course with Professor Kinsmann, and it was excellent. The lectures were engaging and made complex data analytics topics easy to understand with real-life examples. The assignments were challenging yet manageable. His detailed feedback and individual support were invaluable in enhancing my learning experience.

Professor Kinsman is a great, quirky professor who is eager to have his students succeed- he's accessible outside of class and is happy to help whenever he can. The projects are unique and due dates are flexible.

Dr. Kinsman is wonderful. This is a man who cares deeply about each one of his students. He is really knowledgeable, and he is very good at answering questions and encouraging people to do their own research as well. He's also really fun and makes lectures interesting and engaging. He is one of my favorite professors at RIT, I highly recommend him.

Dr. Kinsman was one of the best professors I had during my time at RIT. I took several classes with him and I learned A LOT. His homework is very practical, I learned things that I've been able to apply on co-op, in classes, and in full-time work. He also genuinely cares about every person he teaches. Just be ready to cope with his quirkiness.

Prof. Kinsman is very eccentric and overall a great professor. He goes through lecture slides and also shows demos during class. These demos are pretty similar to future homework assignments so be sure to pay attention to them. Prof. Kinsman is extremely helpful during office hours. His exams are kinda rough but he goes over the topics beforehand.
He's hilarious. Can teach complex subjects in an easy-to-understand manner. Easily one of the best professors I've had at RIT. 10/10

Dr. Kinsman is one of the best professors I have had here at RIT. His classes are fun, very interactive (he always welcomes questions). He is brilliant in computer vision, and everything makes sense when he teaches it, regardless of complexity. Unlike other professors, he genuinely cares about his students, is understanding, wants them to thrive.

Kinsmen is an amazing prof. This course teaches you a lot of helpful information. I did not know much about pandas or matlab beforehand, and I know students who take this course, and praise it for their job. The course does have heavy programming assignments, but it conveys helpful real world information and techniques not offered in other courses.

He has a policy that says he cares about student health. But he also he reused the syllabus from last sem and didn't update it, assigned a bunch of quizzes at once and got openly irritated when students complained (but he did make them optional after that), and agreed to put a time window on an exam that was near break, but then didn't do that??

Do not take a course with him. Class was a logistical nightmare. When reported for giving us too much work out of nowhere, he kept telling us how good of a person he was for fixing it and made the exam question: "Thomas Kinsman made all of these assignments optional. Which of his qualities allows for him to do this?"

comment: I love Dr. Kinsman's lectures. He engages the class and clearly explains the concepts with demos.

AVOID. Gives horrible explanations of concepts using metaphors that end up making no sense, way too much homework (horribly documented as well), awful exam formatting, terrible at giving feedback, and to top it all off, he's really arrogant.

You will not receive feedback on anything. Tests will not always be related to course material. Exams may not even be complete and when you take them and then you will later get an email saying oh hey here is a part of the test that is required, even after you submitted it
Saturday Exams.
