comment: He's forget's to give grades for final exam and doesn't know how to upload pictures or loss for any students who took his course and wasted his credits for this professor. This is highest I can give to this professor.
Good professor.

Dr. K is easily one of the best prof. at RIT, but his class is not for everyone. Expect very detailed lectures with many examples and great explanations. Expect lots of HW, projects, group work, quizzes, and exams. Expect to be thoroughly quizzed on every little detail of everything. He is understanding, but his class is not for the faint of heart.

Too much emphasis on the format of the assignment. Homework always posted on Thursday night and due on Sunday. Many meaningless questions in the test, such as: Did we cover this in class? What food did I use when talking about this?
Hands down one of the best professor in CS. Take him and you won't regret a bit. Loved his lecture and the conversation. He does not take this as a job, but as a way to connect with students.
One of my best classes at RIT. Everything I learnt about Big Data Analytics is from this course and this professor.

The nice part is, he's like a high school teacher who cares about his students. But it is also a bad part. The assignment itself is too easy but is overly concerned about the format and details. Have you ever seen a professor who asks you to write about what you've learn from the assignment? He will, and it will be the most important part.
He is my favorite professor I've had at RIT!

Dr. Kinsman really cares about his students. He teaching style is unconventional, but he really focuses on you understanding the application of the concepts, rather than the theoretical details: which is refreshing for CS. Don't expect concrete details on grading, but he makes the class difficult to not do well if you just try. A great professor.

This was the best course I have taken so far in Big data cluster, Professor is amazing in teaching, I never missed any of his classes, and all were worth it. If you really want to understand the Big data analytics and why part to the algorithms take this class. Thumbs up!!
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Inspirational']

comment: KInsman? More like Kidman because he can't go for 30 seconds without telling some dumb joke and getting distracted. His lectures he rambles through. He's seriously like a kid sometimes. Then he dumps this big thick packet for a final with questions we never covered and all this new random verbal questions. What a mess of a person. STAY AWAY

Midterms thoroughly cover the material so be prepared. Don't expect the final to have much of anything from either midterms. Tons of time intensive homework, so make sure you have the time to commit. Group HW/Projects sadly consisted of two, so choose your partner wisely. Unlike undergrad, they actually require significant effort from two people.

comment: Kinsman is fantastic and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. Class is super informative, and he focused mostly on the application of various data mining practices. He explains everything super clearly and makes difficult concepts easy to understand. Exams were pretty difficult but fair and everything else was pretty forgiving. Great class.
Great professor! Lectures are very clear and interesting. Homework might be a lot of work but helps you actually put everything together. Got interested in Machine Learning after taking csci420.

Great overall professor, does get a little distracted it feels, and lectures aren't always very coherent but he makes sure you understand the key aspects of everything. Great outside of class and wants you to succeed.
Hilarious, Participation matters, Don't miss class, Great lectures, Fuzzy syllabus.

comment: Great Teacher, helps develop interest in the subject and gives good feedback on work.
Always helped with any questions asked. Great way of teaching. His classes never got boring. Provided a lot of examples so that we remember what was taught.

Usually explains examples and concepts well, but has a very hard time talking about the same thing for more than a minute. Switches back and forth between lecture and tangents, and constantly talks about his kids. Generally fair grading, but feedback is minimal. Tests are reasonable - you need to study, but not more than other high-level courses.
Easy homeworks and he makes it very clear what to expect on tests
Has been programming for 20 years and teaches as if to students who have been doing it for just as long.

On the first day, Professor Lam gave a tough lecture to intentionally weed out the class (literally 5 out of 15 students dropped before the next session). His lectures are very fast, and his is very hard to understand.

Had to go to the chairman in order to get changes made. He tried to support the students, but it took multiple people to come up to him in order to get some kind of aid. Believes a 70% class average is normal. Talks way too fast + doesn't do exam reviews or go over exam questions because exams aren't cumulative.

comment: Lectures moved very fast and would often move to new material ahead of schedule if time allowed - no getting out early! Grading was 25% homework and 75% best 3 of 4 exam grades, with exam 4 being the final and therefore optional. You could only get your exam back through office hours. If you can get a study group going the class is bearable.
He talks super fast and is hard to understand.  Dont expect much from the lectures.

definitely not an easy course by any means. Only grades that go into my courses are your homework's and the three tests(worth 25% ecah). Beware of the last test, The class is pretty easy until the end. Proffesor Lam is is a chill dude, blends in with the students on campus lmao. make sure you take notes on his lectures, he moves pretty fast.

Need to attend every class and be attentive. Ended up taking like over 5 pages of notes every class so be prepared to pay attention. If you complete the HW and PPs and pay attention you'll succeed in the class. Takes a decent amount of effort to get an A.
Can't miss class ever.

It is easy to succeed in this class. You have to show up for lecture. Exams are basically the same as practice problems that he assigns and checks over for you. Start studying a few days before the exam using just the practice problems and just memorize the whole thing. Super cool dude, as well. Likes to crack underappreciated jokes.

Eddery is inspirational, friendly, and upfront. He tells you day 1 what you need to do to succeed and checks in on his students frequently during class. He gives every opportunity to ask questions, guides you in what to prioritize, and is overall a really cool dude.

By far, one of the hardest classes I've ever taken at RIT. He goes WAY too fast through the slides and I barely learn anything keeping up with taking notes in class. He gives too much homework and doesn't care about us as students. I wish he was more accessible for office hours and/or provide supplemental instructors.

comment: He would often make rude comments to students' passions. He posts his power points online before class so you can take notes but you have to listen to his lectures to do well on tests. He goes through material insanely fast so it is hard to keep up with. Starts class by saying average test scores are around 60-70% and he doesn't curve.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: I took him for Macro Econ and it was fine. Homework was multiple  choice online. Exams were also multiple choice and easy. He goes quickly in class so sometimes you have to get him to go over something again but he makes Macro Econ easy to pass if you go to class and pay attention.

His lectures are fine, if you pay attention and take notes, you should be good. His slides and notes are useless. Not much homework, maybe 6-7 online quizzes for the whole semester. 2 midterms and a non-cumulative final. He does know his stuff well, he just can't communicate it properly.

For subject area, economics, his lectures are pretty entertaining, and full meaningful content. If you pay attention, take notes, do the homework (which is easy), and review, you will do fine. He always holds office hours (I've never needed them) and his home work gives a pretty indication of types of questions he asks on tests.
Horrible teacher, will never take again or recommend
You would get value reading online or a textbook than taking him for ECON 431 - Monetary Analysis and Policy. Save yourself the trouble now and avoid this professor.

Boring subject, but very nice guy, tries to make it more interesting and has good stories, but sometimes it just drags on forever, extremely understand and will offer extra help and a couple extra credit things, a lot of times all you to do is ask, he's very down to earth!  Don't wait until last minute for that though! Showing uphe will pass you

He's the most relaxed, casual professor I've had, to the point where he blends in with the students on the quarter mile.  Super funny guy with a slight Chinese accent, but it doesn't affect the material too much.  I found the lectures very easy to understand, and homework and exams were pretty easy if you paid attention in class.

He's a great teacher. He prepares you for tests through great notes, weekly quizzeshomework, and review classes. I didn't really like that there was a group project in this class but a lot of professors do them, especially at RIT. I think it gives the teacher more control over your grade.. (helpful if you are a student who shows effort)
He is a fun professor. He doesn't speak as loud though. He is helpful. No need for textbook.

Disappointed with class organization. Inequal time for topics, so more difficult concepts were a struggle for the class, and we lost points on the midterm. Grading was harsh especially since some instructions were unclear and expected very specific answers. Need more in-class practice. Dull class at times. Didn't always check for understanding.
Didn't adapt to online learning very well. Harsh grading which felt undeserved due to basically learning all words from YouTube videos. Wouldn't recommend this class online.

The professor is nice at first. However, is not understanding of the pandemic and other factors. Do not be late for an assignment by a minute! Or else she will give you a zero. The class is very lecture heavy with little practice, feel like I didn't learn much. Do not recommend for online, choose a different professor.
Creating a positive work environment to learn in and an enjoyable class.

She has a great balance of being professional and personal. She uses personal stories to support the topics we cover in class- it also helps us to connect with her and enjoy class more. There is work to be done with online discussions and labs but there is nothing but benefits that you gain from this class.

Professor Boling helped me improve my ASL grammar more than I ever thought possible. That being said, she was a very challenging teacher that really pushed you to succeed. I think that if you are up to the challenge and willing to put in the time and effort, you can really improve from this professor!

Despite her lectures being dull (purely a content issue), she was a good professor. She stressed topics that were relevant and came up on exams. Activity sheets are actually useful in this course. She gave clear feedback about the final project and was accessible via email within a reasonable amount of time. Graded fairly.

Emily is a kind and engaging professor, but the class is one of the most difficult ones I have taken, considering it is bio for non majors. Everyone gets different versions of the exams with different questions, and the short answers are graded harshly. There are weekly quizzes and activities that are mandatory and time consuming.

Professor Coon-Frisch is the ideal professor. Her lectures are engaging, she's kind and understanding, and she even grades her own exams! Attendance is tracked through engaging in-class activities. There are weekly homework assignments and a final group project instead of an exam. Exams are strenuous but she provides plenty of helpful resources.

Very nice teacher. The classes feel like middle school. I did not pay attention in any classes and barely studied for the exams and got a B+. If you study for a few hours for each exam (Or just do the weekly worksheets) this is an easy A. If you pay attention the lectures can be interesting. All assignments are the same across every bio class.

Took her for bio I and was fine, however bio II was an absolute nightmare. Extremely hard exams despite regularly going to class and studying (very low class averages, first exam was like a 65%). She is a nice person, just bio itself needs to be entirely redone and I would not recommend the class. Too hard for an intro class for non-bio majors.

Gen Bio II is the same layout as Gen Bio I: short online quizzes every week, four exams, and a final group project. I found Professor CF to be a great instructor for the course. She was passionate about the content, gave us helpful tips for studying for the exams, and gave me great feedback on my exams when I stopped in for her office hours.
Best bio prof of the 3. Grades timely, super nice and reasonable, and has the best lectures in my opinion.

Overall, very good professor compared to other gen bio. She keeps lectures to the point and engaging. The grading across gen bio is all the same. There are online weekly quizzes (easy), quarterlies in-person (mid/hard), and a project (lots of work). If you work hard, you will get what you put into it. She is willing to help and is nice.

OK so the professor is great and ALL . But they chanegd the whole course system . bio 101 and bio 102 has to be the hardest I have taken yet. Mind I am a CS major and I find the other ones easy so that tells something.The quarterly's  are all in person and super hard . you need to study a lot and there is a final project at the end and also HARD !

A super caring professor who gives great feedback regarding projects. Lecture-heavy class and content do not really connect well with one another, but that is more on the class itself and not her. Tests are in person and brutal, but all the bio profs collaborate to make them. I recommend meeting with her to discuss the project; it's super helpful!
Really great energy and good lectures. She is good at meeting eye to eye with the students. Make sure you study well for the exams.

The effort to get an A in BIOL2 is not worth it in my opinion but the class is an easy B or C. There is a online textbook assigned but isn't worth reading. Quarterly tests and weekly quizzes are online and open-note. There are four projects that are strictly graded. Don't expect much feedback on your work and lectures are very fast.

Grades harshly (especially for quarterlies) for a biology class that's designated for non-biology majors and crams in a lot of information to the point where you have to do a lot of additional self-teaching.

I took this course as a perspective and i was very happy with it. Professor Coon-Frisch is nice and clearly passionate about the subject. The work load is very manageable as well as interesting. I recommended taking this class if you have the chance.
Tough grader.

comment: A very clear and straightforward professor, presents the material well and makes participation and lectures fun but not mandatory to pay attention during. Would 100% recommend for Gen Bio, though the quizzes and in-class activities don't really prepare students as well for the quarterlies and projects.

Lectures are long and boring, however, she does put in jokes to keep the class fun. The only issue I have with this class is how she expects us to answer 30-40 short answer questions on the 4 quarterly exams with only 75 minutes, while expecting each answer to be what she thinks is perfect. also doesn't help that theres no feedback on whats wrong.
Really passionate and caring professor!

Mrs. Coon-Frisch is a fantastic professor for Gen Bio. While she is a lecture-heavy professor, her classwork is extremely helpful and always is designed to help you advance your knowledge in the subject. The coursework all feels cohesive and well-thought-out, and she is a riot in class. If ever there is a course to take with her, please take it.

Even in a class of 200 people, Professor CF clearly showed that she genuinely wants us all to succeed. Her lectures are engaging, but not too fast paced to the point where you miss stuff. If you do though, all the lectures are recorded in advance, and the slides can be found online. Overall a super kind, accepting, and trustworthy professor!
Emily was a caring and understanding. If you had questions, she answered them amazingly. She truly cares about her students. Best professor yet!!
superb, a breath of fresh air for non-major bio classes. Kind, funny, makes topics interesting, has reasonable and clear expectations, and grades fairly and fair.

Emily is an amazing person, her lectures can get dry at times, but the assignments are rather easy and short. There are a lot of grade boosting assignments in class that are easy 100s as long as you show up. The tests arent horrible, but the feedback does take some time to get back and it typically isnt very helpful.

Emily makes the class enjoyable. She's very clear with what she expects of students, and the class is very organized so you know what is coming up. If you don't read the textbook you will likely pass, but you will not get an A. Overall she's very relaxed and was one of the best instructors when classes unexpectedly moved online.

Great choice for Gen Bio Lab. Clear instructions and expectations as well as fast and reasonable grading, although the labs can get long and tedious at points. Quizzes aren't too difficult as long as you study the slides and know basic concepts. I always found practicals difficult, but she provides everything you need to succeed. Great person too!
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Coming from Connelly and Weatherell, Emily is like a breath of fresh air for non-major bio classes. Kind, funny, makes topics interesting, has reasonable and clear expectations, and grades fairly. The class is still modeled after Connelly's, but hopefully she'll be able to change that soon. Take her if you want Gen Bio lecture the way it should be!

Great French teacher. She is a native speaker and therefore is always available to give you cultural feedback. She is tough but understanding if you are honest with her. She is definitely the best French professor I had.

VCouderc is a great French teacher! She's a pretty tough grader but she's very willing to help and you can re-do assignments. Also, she doesn't really have a strict late policy. It was a lot of work but worth it in the end. I would definitely recommend her as a teacher

She was extremely rude to me, and abused the early alert system to berate me - she sent an "early" alert in week 10, and even though I was one of the most knowledgeable students in the class! She knows her stuff, but needs to be much more professional in her reactions to students.

I loved having her as a teacher!  Soo nice and very willing to help if you ask! She is a very tough grader, but only because she believes you have to be precise in order to learn.  It was a fairly difficult class for beginning French, and there was a lot of homework, but practicing and repetetive work is necessary to learn a languag. Great teacher!

Treats students as though they're in high school. Rude if you have any sort of conflict with her; doesn't listen to reason and always insists that she is right for no other reason than that she is the teacher. She seems to be applying French grading standards to RIT, as well. Gave Cs to quite a few students who got As in Advanced, which is harder.

She is a wonderful lady. Her classes are highly interactive, a lot of in class work and participation is necessary. She will definetly put you outside your comfort zone. No textbook, no tests or quizzes.

I find I usually do very well in Cresswell's classes. She speaks very clearly, and explains concepts well; I took Dynamics with her, and found it very fun. Every new concept has problems worked in class, which is huge for understanding. She is also very understanding of absences and late work.

She is probably the nicest person and instructor I have had at RIT, and clearly knows biomaterials science HOWEVER, she does not know how to run a class. Her assignments are not related to what you learn in class, and 9/10 times you teach yourself test material (a lot of math) from the textbook. Her class is very busywork heavy.
She was very helpful and willing to answer questions.

Creswell is fine, she is a relatively new professor and it reflects in her lectures. She is nice, but outside of that her lectures are boring and unintuitive. You have to take either dynamics or statics with her and I had to do both with her. Whenever Gomes or Ivanic teaches it's generally clearer. I'd recommend trying to learn outside of class.

Taking her again for dynamics. The course is structured in a way that makes you do work every day, so it seems overwhelming, but it will prepare you. Has office hours and Slack if you need help. Engaging in lectures and cares about students.

She was very nice, but that was kind of it. Her lectures were not engaging, there were multiple times she spent a third of the class on a derivation of any equation just to say we didn't need to know it. Also, while she was accessible outside of class, she was not the least bit helpful when asked a homework question.

Professor Stone for PUBL 201 assigns a ton of reading though the assignment aren't hard as long you put in some effort. He also has 50% of the grade based of off two group projects so hope you get good group members or your grade might suffer.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Group projects']

comment: Prof. Stone is a nice guy and the class is pretty easy, but you really never know what your grade is in the class. There's a group project and essay, but you'll never know how you did on them. He likes us doing current events assignments from NPR, but aside from weekly readings, there really isn't much else to his class. Lots of discussion.

Dr. DiMarco is one of the most difficult professors I've worked with. He's not open to criticism and when I went to the ombudsman, he stopped responding and acted difficult. His homework is insanely long and I had to answer a couple 24 and 35-part questions.

Failed to provide any study material for exams and, despite having a TA, did not have nearly enough opportunities for exam preparation. Grades exclusively with homework and quizzes, which is fairly easy, but lectures only from Pearson provided slides, which only confuse students more. Don't take.

I really like the guy, but he relies heavily on the textbook and makes you print notes to follow along. He has weekly(ish) quizzes that count for 20% of the grade, the other 80% is a midterm and the final, which rely heavily on the textbook as well. I did mediocre on the midterm, and spent the rest of the semester trying to pick myself back up.

uses mostly lecture slides from textbook and gives 1-3 assignments per week. assignments have 15-20 questions with multiple parts each (some up to 10 parts). because there is so much covered in 1 period, you may struggle if you miss a class. decently approachable through email outside class and willing to answer questions during Friday "labs".

Hours and hours of homework every week. Does not care to make the class enjoyable. Expects all information missed whether excused or unexcused to be figured out by asking classmates. No reason to go to lectures as he just reads of slides that are in MyCourses. Missed one class and have to teach myself the rest of the course. Do not recommend.

Dr DiMarco does not teach. He reads directly from the slides and does not provide any form of application on content outside of the homework's where problems would have up to 12 parts to them. would not recommend had to teach myself most if not all of the material.

Worst professor i've ever had. Evil. Assigns 3, 20 question pearson HWs a week (each questions has like 6 parts). Horrible at lecturing. Doesn't even make his own lectures—downloads them right from Pearson making it VERY hard to learn from. No review. Won't tell you anything that will be on his exams. Very condescending. Plz avoid him

There are 5 major coding assignments done in groups and that is all of the work for the semester. You have one week to complete each and set up will take a majority of it because it is pretty confusing everytime. The grade is heavily weighted on tests but there are only two, and he is pretty forgiving with the questions.

Awful tests that are weighted too heavily considering how bad they are written. Final exam was supposed to be 2h, but he only gave 1h30. Expected us to code tests without sufficient time to set up the environment. Got upset when a large majority of the class got questions wrong on midterm but they were bad questions. Gaslighting us for his mistakes

Taken for Non-Majors and was a wonderful instructor. Very nice, explained things clearly, and taught me very important things when it comes to my own art outside of class. If you can take Clinton, do it!!!
Her teaching style is pretty straight-forward. Gives good feedback and homework with clear instructions. Is very understanding and patient unless you blatantly disrespect her time and patience.

Sally is one of the best options for a basic drawing course. She understands that a whole bunch of different majors have to take drawing and tries to tailor the course to people's specific needs. She is super kind and helps a lot when you are struggling, and definitely made me care more about drawing. My friend switched to illustration bc of her.

I loved having Sally as a professor! I wish I had her for FDTN111. She gives great feedback on all your work and really shows that she cares about your time and about what your specific major is, despite this being a foundation class. If you have the chance to have Sally as your prof definitely take that chance!

Sally was a great prof. I learned so much in her class and my drawing skills definitely improved. We had a lot of different projects which was nice. She gave really helpful feedback during class and critiques. As long as you put in the work and effort and she can tell, you'll get a good grade and learn a lot.

Older reviews do not reflect how this class is run now. He has clearly improved and listens to student feedback, adding more examples that help for exams. Very knowledgeable and connects concepts to real world ideas. PHYS 2 is tough, but he makes it manageable and provides helpful resources. He genuinely cares about students learning and improving!

Not the best lecturer. I did not understand a lot of the material and he seemed unmotivated. Written and online homework assignments. You need to know the material for exams. Gives some opportunities for extra credit but for a very small bonus.

Very homework heavy, you have online homework and assigned homework on paper every week. He doesn't seem motivated to be in class any more than the students as well. Lectures can be boring but end early sometimes.

Professor YG is right for you if you don't mind consuming ungodly amounts of caffeine to sit through his mind numbing lectures. I once witnessed 4 of 30 students in the workshop sleeping. Class isn't too hard if you manage to pay attention. Good luck soldier.

Mr. Gunja is the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures were lackluster and the notes that were discussed during them. He literally just goes over the lectures and then during the workshop classes, he just gives you the weekly assignment and has you and your group do the whole thing yourself without teaching anymore. Literally doesn't teach.
Lectures aren't the best, but they are clear enough. There is a decent amount of homework but it doesn't compare to UP1.

Professor YG was the worst professor I've ever had. His lectures were entirely him reading off his slides and writing with an unreadable handwriting. Do not take his course. Over half my homework assignments for the whole semester (as a 3rd year MCET) was his course. I got a good grade through teaching myself everything, not at all due to him.
He loves to go on a tangent a lot that doesn't matter to the course. I also spaced out a lot in his class and definitely need a good group to work together and help each other out.

Literally just piles work onto you.  He likes to claim he wants to make his lectures different then the rest of the other professor's lectures, then turns around and monologues for 1 1/2 hours.  Has good intentions (seemingly) by providing you lots of practice and resources, but then it turns as he requires you to do absolutely all of it.

Does not know how to interact or create a remotely interesting/interactive room. 
Hard to understand handwriting, slow grading on exams, and forgets to upload answers to weekly active problems. 

The HW questions on the required online textbook make me seeth with rage and the points in myCourses aren't worth the work.

this homeboy is not my favorite . He definitely knows his physics but can't teach anything. Online or in person I learned nothing. Just very confusing, writes in cursive no one can read and tells us its not really his problem we can't read his hand writing.

The light that bounces off his head far succeeds my future, his grim but comforting beard perfectly matches the feel of the dorm mattresses. His voice could soothe a thousand crying babies, his build one of a roman warrior wont escape your eyes, even in your dreams. His eyes have a stronger attraction than gravity no matter your sexual orientation

I had him my first semester Fall 2018 for UPI-Waves, a 7 week 1-credit class. His lectures aren't terrible, but are quite boring if you are already knowledgeable in the material. Interesting labs to go through, although the TA (who graded everything except exams) was exceptionally harsh but fair. Grade is 80% exams (per policy). Overall a good guy!

His lectures are boring since he has a monotone voice. He'll spend most of the time adjusting his camera. Then he'll spend way too long putting people in breakout rooms, which cuts into your work time. You'll spend more time figuring out how to do the work yourself (or your group if you get one that's talkative) than by him.

Good professor at going over material and making sure we understand what's going on, but has a hard time "dumbing it down". Really have to focus in class and almost teach yourself and review after every single lecture in order to do good. Exams are challenging and there is a lot of homework given during the week, but nothing that isn't doable

Decent teacher, can cover the material fine for physics 1 fine and at a good pace for everyone to understand. Exams can be challenging, but if you know how to do the questions on your own, you should get a good grade on it. There are mostly conceptual and calculation questions on the exam. Homework: 10 sapling questions each week and assignments.

He rarely responds to emails quickly and gives very vague responses. Was not the best at giving lectures and mostly made students do problems with no introduction to the topic. Did not enter 80% of grades until 5 days before the final grade deadline. Always has some excuse why he misses class and makes other professors lecture/give exams.

comment: Lectures are useful when he explains a topic but besides that he just puts up example problems for the entirety of it, not giving any clear instructions. Homework is excessive and often does not coincide with what you are learning. Due dates are a mystery until the day they are due. Can barely get an email response until after the fact.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']

comment: This is my second semester with YG, the quality of his lectures tanked. If you want help, you won't get it because he won't even respond to an email, so if his office hours don't align with your class schedule, good luck. The class is extremely disorganized, with random assignments from topics from weeks ago, or from weeks ahead.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']

comment: He explains everything carefully and thoroughly, although occasionally this can lead to lectures being a bit dull. But if you stay awake through them, you will certainly learn the subject, and if you are struggling he is patient when answering questions. Tests are very similar to study guides, which is always nice.

Its hard to get a good grade in his class because theres only about 6 labs, compared to other physics professors who give 11-12. Also does not tell you when mastering physics assignments are due.  Tried arranging office hours, which he did not show up to. Tells you not to be in depth with your lab reports then gives you a 50. Doesnt teach well too.

To put it simply, he can't teach. He asks the class to solve a problem and refuses to show us how to solve it. He specifically tells the class that he will not show how to solve a problem and then gets mad when the class can't come up with an answer because no one understands the concepts. Also doesn't respond to student emails.

Minamida-sensei is a fantastic Japanese professor. If I had to have a complaint, I would say that she often doesn't fully understand questions if you ask them in English. Other than that, I have no qualms. She is a generous and fast grader, and you will do very well in this class if you properly memorize the few required sections and do the work.
One of the best Professors RIT has to offer, brings a new youthful energy to class, just make sure to perform well on tests, she is very helpful. It doesn't hurt that she is very pretty.

Very good teaching style and makes material easier to learn. Will clear up questions and guide you in the lab. His grading is very clear cut and is virtually the same every lab we hand in. His lab is very relaxed and we all generally have fun while we work.
He always answers my questions during lab and outside of lab. I really enjoy his personality and the way he runs the lab.

Labs can be challenging, but this professor will help you understand the content before and/or after (without simply giving you the answers.) I also appreciated his immediate effort to get the pre-lab videos captioned, since I'm hard of hearing, and for helping me through the first lab for which I could not understand the un-captioned video.

Childishly funny. His first priority is to help students understand the material, which he does very well. Creates a funeasygoing learning environment in the lab. Assignments are the same week to week, so the routine is easy to grasp. No typed out lab reports- woo!

Darren is a fantastic teacher and really breaks down Orgo so you can understand. Really funny guy and knows his stuff. Cares about his students learning. I learned ten times more in lab with Darren and help from Jenn than I did with lecture with Coleman. Labs are long but is actually great to focus on understanding techniques not yields amounts.
Tough grader but explains things really well. Will always make things more clear if you go to office hours or ask a question. Probably the best lab instructor I've had to date.
Bill is a great teacher and has a fantastic sense of humor. He will definitely be missed when he retires!
Fantastic teacher and joker who knows a ton about pool and has a real passion for the game. One of the top professors on campus.

Prof is funny and knows his stuff about pool. Lectures are entertaining and informational, also not long (max 20 mins) so you can spend most of class at the tables. He's great at allowing make ups for missed classes (if you miss more than the allowed amount during the semester). One of my fav professors and classes I've taken at RIT.
Friendly, fun, and chatty. Great wellness class experience!

Bill is a strong candidate for the funniest man I know. He gives solid advice: Both regarding billiards and real life. He harbors a deep hatred for computer science majors which I, as a C.S. major, appreciate. In 2016 he was rated by the American Knitting Home Magazine as the sexiest man alive.
Great class, very laid back and funny professor
He's a great professor who is enthusiastic about what he teaches. He also happens to be hilarious.
the most fun class ever
We play every Thursday for 4 hours.  Good discussions while playing pool, eating donuts or scones and drinking coffee.   Definitely would take the course every year.
By far the most charismatic teacher at RIT.
Bill is the best.

Absolutely Hilarious! He is so witty and amusing to listen to, and all while talking about billiards. It is a participation heavy course but you are there to learn the basics of pool. Take the class with friends or without; you will certainty make new friends regardless.
The most amusing professor I've ever had. He's very knowledgeable about billiards. Literally show up and pass.

Bill is the best. He's funny, and he's really good at teaching the skills you need to play pool. His class is easy and a lot of fun. I recommend him to everyone, even people who have already taken two wellness classes.

Bill is hilarious.  His one and only goal is to make you a better pool player and focuses on form to do so.  Really considering taking this wellness class again.  Just make sure you don't miss more than 3 classes.  Not only will you not pass, he's far less likely to give you the same attention as the other students who really make the effort.
His class is a lot of fun!  He keeps the atmosphere friendly and it was extremely enjoyable.  There is also an advanced class if you want to keep playing.
Hilarious and personable guy. Can't think of anything else to say.
Bill is the man.  He understands that this is just a wellness class and he keeps the lessons simple and clear.  He is funny and he cares about making you a better pool player.  Highly recommended.
Zandy is a fun teacher. He tells fun stories and teaches you to 'respect the game'. You will get out of the class exactly what you would want.
This man is hilarious. And a great teacher. Highly recommended.

Took him for pocket billiards wellness class and he is the best. Knows how to play and teaches his students well. Gives great advice. I've definitely gotten better at pool since I took the class. Definitely recommended!
Really nice guy. Genuinely cares about his students.  Will help you if you listen to him. Made a dumb mandatory class fun.
Fair, clear professor.  Was available if needed and did a good job facilitating the course.
Really nice guy, very personable and approachable professor. 10/10, would take again.
Great Professor, to the point and very personable. He made a unbearable Freshman orientation course quite bearable.
Good professor, fair grader.  Complete your assignments and it'll be an easy A.  DON'T talk while he's talking.

A great teacher. He met with everyone one on one sometime throughout the course and it was apparent that he cared about all of his students. He tried to connect with you and give you advice on how to help with your future. The overall workload was pretty easy; we worked in groups for most of the class and for the final project/presentation.
He understands that this isn't a class that students really want to take, and therefore he is a very fair grader. If you do the homework, then you are set for an A. Also is very nice
A very nice professor.  However, was poor at responding to emails and often made last minute changes.
chill guy. good professor

Cool guy who was passionate about helping his students, but not too overbearing. Requirements were all reasonable and he made expectations clear. Grading was fair and reflected the effort you put in. He also did a great job keeping the material relevant to the students he knew were involved.
Overall, a nice professor. Didn't respond to e-mails.
Had him for a Pathways class which is now called "year one" Cool guy, Really helpful
Great professor! He is really nice and helpful. Pathways and discovery are boring by nature but he does his best to make them more exciting. Would definitely recommend.

Really nice guy! Discovery and pathways classes are boring and a waste of time but it's not the professors fault. It's an easy class as long as you complete the assignments! Would definitely recommend taking from him!
as a non-drawing major, greg was extremely helpful. he is also friendly and overall a great professor; i learned a lot from his class.
Great Professor! Very helpful and cares about his students. Would recommend taking class with him!

The course is not the most exciting to begin with but he makes it as interesting and laid back as possible. He doesn't ask a lot of his students. He is understanding and pretty easy going as far as homework/attendance. Not bad to look at either... I would definitely recommend taking it with him.

Nice man, got along with him fine. seemed very open and easy to talk to for me. I think the class I had him for was very easy, simple, and uninteresting by nature so I feel that I cant give an accurate rating for him as a professor.
He is an alright guy.  I had no problem with him.  The class was simple and easy enough.  It's hard not to get an A in the class if you do all the work.

I had a terrible time with this teacher for YearOne. He gave me a hard time about my work and would never respond to my attempts to contact him about my work. I have never been so angry that I cried before having Mr. Lawson.

Really nice guy, he gave us very easy and often fun assignments. There were even A and B options for some assignments so all students were happy, including art assignments to relate further to creative students in class. He really got freshman to meet each other and see the school. He was effective and nice.
He is one of the best

He kept everything really chill. He realized most of the students didn't want to be there, so he didn't throw too much pressure our way. If you do the work, it's very easy and you won't have any problems. He is very approachable and understanding.
Discovery is a terrible class. Greg is a good person but none of us took the class seriously and I felt bad about that.
Good guy overall, not the most interesting class however for Discovery (Now FYE) I would not have expected an interesting curriculum.
The class is stupid and pointless and we goofed around a lot. Greg was a really nice person but none of us took the class seriously. I personally felt bad about that. Take a real class with him.

BORING!!! I had him for pathways(or whatever freshman seminar is called now) The projects he had us do were a waste of time, we had to stay for the whole class even if we weren't doing anything and no laptops allowed D: Most of the time it was like, ,watch this ted talk for an hour and talk in a small group about it.

As if these classes weren't boring enough, Greg just makes it even more dull. He seems to be a nice guy, but as a FYE teacher, he stinks. However, he grades pretty easily. It's a 50/50 shot with this one.
His lectures are interesting and is treated more as a discussion.
Harvey is a legend. He is the only person who can make you this excited about chemical processes. Take him.

He's incredibly enthusiastic and obviously loves what he's teaching. On top of that, he's fair with his grades and probably one of the most helpful guys on campus. Take a class with him if you get the chance. The only con is that he isn't a reliable grader, but everything gets done eventually.
Dr. Palmer is just the best, no contest.  If you have the chance to take a class with him, just take it.

Harvey is the man! Sure he rambles a lot, but when you get used to him he's probably the most badass mother effer to ever walk on this earth. I'm pretty sure he has patents, and he's on Forbes... need I say more? Also he drinks a lot of Seltzer water.

Good guy, rambles on about a lot of things. Loves talking. Very straight forward guy. Lets class out early often. Makes topics interesting, but can also make then boring by extensive lecturing. Approachable guy by all means, I recommend him.

I would recommend taking this course if you know ahead of time that your workload for your other courses that semester is going to be light. Be ready to spend most of your week and weekends working on the 3 projects assigned for this class. Like I said, only take it if your workload for other courses is light.

For me, he did not really teach well, and I have to learn everything either with the TA's or look online. Weekly lab reports which are fine. Midterms are easy and have multiple days to do it. Final is just a lot of writing.

This class can be rough at times but Mark will do his best to make sure you understand the content. Do not procrastinate in this class unless you don't like having free time. If you can listen to or read instructions correctly then you will do well in this class.
Where boys turn to men
Amazing professor, super hard class. Loved it. Don't go into it alone. 10/10
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: This class was genuinely one of the greatest academic experiences I've ever had. Mark is a passionate, experienced professor, who never failed to give a great lecture. Any of the complaints you see from others are simply people salty they actually had to do any homework/labs at all to pass the class. Pay attention and you'll have a great time.

Honestly, I started off loving this professor, but the only people you can really turn to for help are the TA's. I wish that Mark was more involved in the lab because those take up the most time, and when you have fellow peers in charge of your success, they act like they are above you and knowing that they have the power to fail you is awful.

Mark is the GOAT. He makes EE worth it. He doesn't put up with excuses or BS, so just do the work and show up to class. He will notice if you miss. Gives you plenty of time for exams, so don't procrastinate. This goes for the labs too. They are really important and help with understanding. Just do what Mark says and don't be like Dale or Ali.

This professor was awful. He did not explain properly and he expected us to have background knowledge even though he said he didn't. When you went to him for help he got upset when you did not understand it at the first time. I don't understand how he has so many good reviews since he was an awful teacher. My 13th reason.

This class was easily my most demanding in terms of time spent per week. I think that if you don't enjoy this at least a little bit, probably not the major for you. However I did REALLY love this class. Mark is a very engaging lecturer, quick to respond to emails, and the labs go a LONG way in reinforcing the concepts he teaches

The class has a lot of work which will take a large chunk of your time. This will however not be that strenuous since the TAs are typically nice graders as long as you do your work. This class is also very enjoyable because of the interesting topics and the labs which reinforce ideas along with the lab reports. I highly recommend this class.
Pretty nice guy, but not the best at teaching in my opinion. You're better off learning the material on your own.

Professor Indovina is fantastic, an absolute pleasure to learn from. He has a dry humor that lends to hilarious moments in class--like his notes on hygiene in the syllabus. This class was memorable and important. I learned a lot and through Professor Indovina was able to develop my skills as an engineer. Re"mark"able guy.

Prof. Indovina believes in students doing their own learning, but he'll do everything he can to give you the tools you need. You'll need to experiment on your own and ask questions, but he's very accessible outside of class. If you're motivated to learn, he'll make it fun and easy. Be prepared: he'll pick on you (in a good way) if you aren't.

This course is the go-to for IC design. You get to learn in depth about the logic gates and the FSM you learned in DSI. The projects are very cool and rewarding as you are kind of designing chips, but they will demand substantial time-commitment so be prepared for that. Mark is very caring and will promptly reply your questions around the clock.
He's a professor with a lot of experience. It can be a little difficult to ask him questions, but other than that, DS1 is a typical class. There's a lot of homework, but the grading is fair.

Professor Indovina is a really great guy. I knew nothing about taking digital systems prior to taking his class, and felt very overwhelmed at first. I went to office hours, and he broke things down really easily for me to understand. He's a really caring professor who will go out of his way to make sure you have everything you need. 1000/10
pretty straight forward for DS1

This man is a real gem. He is exceptionally knowledgeable and capable. He can't help but make you a better engineer when you're around him. He treats you like an adult, and expects you to pay attention and digest the material. Be prepared, as he likes to pick on those who aren't. In the end, he wants to make sure you understand the material.

The project workload in this class is insane. If you are not ready to spend weekends working on projects, don't take this class, but it's a fun class, you get to design digital IC from low level. Mark is great professor, as long as you try hard, put lot of efforts on projects, you will receive a good grade and incredible design experience.

DS1 felt like a foreign language and i felt like I was in the twilight zone every lecture. he kinda seems to assume it makes sense but it doesnt and a lot of self teaching happens. Once a topic clicks tho, its very easy and the tests r easy too. HW is impossible w/o chegg. he is so leniant w any issues that come up, so nice, yet teaching is poor.

You can read the other reviews about Mark, I just wanted to talk about this class. If you're an EE with a digital focus or are interested in any RTL, this class is a must. The skillset developed during the semester is critical. The course is all about verification. You'll use Python, Perl, SystemVerilog and UVM over 4 projects. I highly recommend.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Hilarious']

comment: Mark's a bro. As long as you shower, study, and can take a joke you'll do alright. This course had the most work of any I've taken but it's fun stuff (chip-level design). He curves the exams so even if you don't do super well you're not gonna tank. The grad part is just a research paper. It stinks, but is a valuable experience.

Mark is the best professor in the Electrical Engineering Department. He teaches a number of courses yet he knows his students very well. He is the only professor who responds immediately to any queries. Very inspirational and helpful.
One of the best Professors at RIT. The content he teaches is relevant industry wise and also, his feedbacks and projects are really helpful.

The only professor who replies to student emails even at 2 in the morning. He is an amazing professor who cares for you and is always there for you. He wants you to learn and apply the concept effectively.
Professor Mark Indovina is one of the best professors in Electrical Engineering Department at RIT. He is a real gem of a person. He wants you to learn and struggle. He is very caring and helpful.

Professor Mark Indovina is one of the best professor I've had in my lifetime. He is very clear in this thoughts and appreciates our effort.  He has lots of industrial experience and was willing to help us anytime round the clock. I have never seen any professor replying to mails so quickly.I would strongly suggest one to take this course.

He has to calculate Elmore delay four times to correct himself in front of class. His power point is wrong. When people ask him, he sometimes gives wrong answer. Lab in the class will be useful for future. If you take his class, you have to teach yourself.
group projects

Seth is the best professor to walk the face of the planet -- jump through any hoop you can to get in his class.  Extremely smart guy who can break things down in simple terms.  Ask him about quantum dots in the intrinsic layer of GaAs solar cells for brownie points.
A true god among men, will give throw as much sass as you throw at him. Be sure to complain about the music selection, and always ask him about preacher curls.

Tom Cornell is a great professor! As long as you do the written evals on time, read the assigned readings, and participate in the discussion, this class should be an easy A! He grades harder on the midterm and final essays, though.
Thomas Cornell was a good professor, but lecture heavy and sometimes a tough grader. I would have preferred some prep material such as worksheets to make sure the class knew the material.

Cornell is a great professor and he truly cares about what he teaches. I found discussions to be very interesting. You could probably get an A by only going to discussions and exam days (about 8 of the total class days)
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Prof Cornell is one of the nicest professors I've ever had! Super accommodating, only takes 1/5 point off (out of 5) for late assignments, and gives thorough (But brief) feedback on every submission. A bit old school, but an absolute gem. The field trips for this class are great! Highly recommend.

Not the most interesting class, but Professor Cornell is very kind and generous. Class is graded on two essays and discussions every other week, but if you take some notes and understand the readings you'll be fine.

Honestly one of the best professors I had. If you did bad on the test no worries you can always make it up the test. Is willing to sit down with you and talk you through what went wrong and how to correct it. Would take any class with him in the future.

He puts forth significant effort in his lectures and cares enough about the material to explain things in depth. You will never end up confused by the lectures, but you likely will never leave one enthused. Grades are easy and mostly participation and two main writing assignments.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Graded on 2 paper tests (open note and given topics ahead of time) and small discussion papers and discussions. Lecture notes are given, you just have to follow along/ pay attention. There are 'required' readings but you don't really have to read them/ can find them online. He learns peoples names quickly and really wants everyone to do well.

Interesting material, just make sure you leave time to complete the readings. Lectures are interesting and easy to follow, but make sure you take notes. Evaluations are easy A's and his grading system makes it easy to get good grades. A great lecturer, gives handouts for every lecture that makes it easier to follow.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Really passionate professor in what he teaches in. The material can be very interesting when given some thought. He provides a reasonable and completely doable amount of reading so you shouldn't have a hard time.

This class is great. If you show up to most of the classes and somewhat pay attention you'll be fine. The only grades are a few discussions where you make one comment and get full credit, a few paragraphs that could be off topic as long as they are 200 words, and 2 essays that are a little tough, but he allowed notes while writing.

Dr. Cornell is a really nice guy. He's very passionate about what he teaches, which is good. The lectures can be dull, but if you do pay attention, the material is can actually be quite interesting.  Even though he's a tough grader on essays, it's very easy to do well. Part of the grade is participating in discussions, which can be interesting.

He's well respected and a good professor, but the class itself was boring.  You read 3 books, and for each do two discussions and a paper.  The papers add up to be 75% of your grade (the other 25% is extremely easy to get).  Not the worst class, but make sure you're a good essay writer.

Dr Cornell is a good professor. He is very friendly and has great enthusiasm in what he teaches. His assignments take little effort, providing you read the material. His lectures can be somewhat dull, but if you listen they're actually very interesting and informational. You'll grow fond of him.

Very easy class with interesting topics. He assigns only a handful of pages to read in interesting books then offers discussions to review what you have read in the book. The only homework you have is writing about what you read and the tests are basically the same thing. He gives you an outline of the test before the test. Such a great class.

He is a good professor and definitely is an expert on the material. His lectures are very dull but very informative. He is a difficult grader. You're almost guaranteed a B in the class unless you write perfect essays. Nice guy though for sure.

Pretty good at what he does. Class gets pretty boring, so it's easy to get lost in what he says. Fairly tough grader on exams. Very passionate about his subject, so if you show enthusiasm he will like you.

Great and Interesting class!  There is a fair amount of work, but not overly boring. Would suggest it to anyone with interest in history or various earth landscapes. Teacher is a great guy and will help u with all that you need.  I would strongly suggest this class. Oh, there are fieldtrips too.  Fun class!

Very sweet. Lot of knowledge in his subject. Boring class but easy A. Very helpful. Helps you if you show interest in class. Keep him updated with your work. Take feedback. Always there to help after/before class. Lets you take exams again. Keeps the discussion going. Wants students to learn. Keeps updatig whether or not you understand what he says

Really easy class. Dull teacher, but an easy  A. Just do the readings and go to discussion days and you're set. He gives you the questions for the tests ahead of time. I don't see how anyone could get less than an A.

Dull. Awful grader - pretty much everyone gets a B. You have to be absolutely either perfect or terrible to get anything else. The better you do, the harder he looks for something to mark you off on. Bring a pillow to the lectures.

He has interest in what he teaches and he welcomed questions, was available for help. However, his essay-exams are rather hard to get an A for - he wants understanding of all the material and, apparently, very good thought organization to give a student an A. My 37th class at RIT and my first B... Do not underestimate his tests/exams - prepare.

Prof Cornell is pretty much what you would expect from a mandatory liberal arts professor at a tech school. Not very interesting and he keeps class pretty dull. Grades pretty harshly but there are only two written tests for the course.
She's kind and not unnecessarily difficult, like a lot of other professors. Very clear on expectations and quizzes are not hard if you read the textbook.

She is a very nice lady and is friendly. However, Professor Kwon is not very clear when it comes to work. not much instruction is given and she expects you to know when stuff is due. The class was based on group work which was fine but when it came to individual work I had no clue what and when to do something until it was too late. Wouldnt recomnd

She's extremely organized and on top of the coursework, which is great. She also is more than willing to help outside of class either over email or in person. Assignments had a written out grading rubric ahead of time, too, so you know exactly what she's looking for. She does struggle sometimes with controlling loud members of class, though.
test heavy

After taking her class I feel like I did learn a lot from EunSook. She challenged us, which I liked. Other students complained about the math, but it's part of media planning! Her lectures need some work, but she is fairly new to teaching. She was really good about answering my emails and giving feedback on my work. She's so kind and brings candy!

Awesome guy!!! He cares a lot about making the class relevant to current events and also really tries to make the lectures engaging. There are a LOT of readings each week but I'm always motivated to do them because 1) the course content is highly interesting and 2) Phillips is so nice that I don't want to disappoint him by not participating.

For a 3 hour class, instead of dreading it I look forward to it. Super nice teacher and makes the 3 hour long lecture not bad. Usually lets out of class 30 mins - 1.5 hours early which was a nice surprise. Highly recommend taking this class, even if it's at a weird time. You will not regret it.

Great professor for Cybersecurity Policy and Law. Very approachable and he tries his best to keep the 3 hour long class interesting. He is an adjunct professor who mainly focuses on his day job, this means that class is not always his #1 priority. This is reflected in the way he can be slow to respond to emails at times.

This man is so sweet and I had a lot of fun in his class. The way he runs his classes is a little strange, but I think that's because he's old-fashioned. Fair grader, pretty easy to get a good grade if you do the readings.

If you are looking for an easy class, this is the one to take. Professor Hull is super nice and laid back. He posts an assignment of poems to read and you just write 2 questions or comments you have on a piece of paper and give them to him in class. He reads all the questions and answers them. At the end you have 2 papers and a presentation.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Do not take his class at 8 am, he forces you to read a bunch of poems before class as an assignment. Lectures are very dry and your grade is 60% contingent on a in-class presentation on a poem of your choice as well as a incredibly long essay at the end of the semester.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Read the books early as the assignment dates will tell you to read a 1/3 of a given book in a day which isn't possible if you are in any stem major. Overall, 210 is not a difficult course and is scheduled very nicely. A lot of reading but the class itself is not a lot of work.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: He is overall a very good professor. He always has stories to tell or to relate to the reading materials. He also gives very detailed feedback on your term paper. Do your readings and follow the syllabus, it will be an easy A.  He can be a bit forgetful so beware of that.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Guy likes to talk, but he really wants to understand your take on the material. Not many grades in  the class so try to stay on top of things. Don't take at 8 a.m.

Prof. Hull is a very impressive English teacher. I've had good teachers in this subject before, but there's something about Prof. Hull that makes him stand out. He not only knows the material we discuss with the class, it's almost as though he has lived through it himself. He always has stories that relate to the material, and it makes classes fun.

This is a lab that is run entirely by TAs, so your experience will be completely dependent on the TA you receive. The labs are all pretty straight forward, so if you already have taken a chemistry class before this should be easy.

I literally never saw her, the lab was completely ran by the TA. I got lucky with a chill one, but that's unfortunately not guaranteed. The work is mundane if I'm being completely honest, but the labs can be ran through quickly and the lab reports don't take too much time.
Virginia Chang is not your professor. Your TA is. Just pray to God you have a good TA who can actual explains the material and break it down for you. Don't get behind.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'So many papers', 'Graded by few things']

comment: She is not an instructor she simply oversees the undergraduate labs. The TA is your instructor and grader for this course; however, Chang does write all of the lab procedures and analysis instructions. She does this poorly. The instructions often make little sense and are filled with errors. It makes an easy course needlessly difficult for everyone

Virginia Chang is a mystical figure looming over the heads of RIT chem students. She enslaves TA's to teach all her labs and gives them poor sheets with awful instructions that irrationally tick the students off.

Though, she walked in one time and seems nice. Plus, the TA's have been good. Is Chang great, no, teach a class please, but whatever.

She never actually taught any classes, as they were all taught by TAs. She writes the lab procedures and they are so poorly written, it is almost impossible to follow the directions. Info would be straight up missing sometimes. The TAs struggled to help us and often had to seek outside help from other chem professors.

I never met Dr. Chang or was able to get in contact with her. I emailed her the week before the first class with a very sensitive topic before I knew who my TA was and never got a response. The lab instructions are unclear and I was only able to understand what to do because my TA rocked. So much work outside of class, but easy A if you do the work

This class is Chem I Lab, which is taught entirely by a TA. Dr Chang writes the labs herself and they are very hard to follow. The TAs try their best, but they take forever to grade your lab reports. Sadly you can't avoid this lab or experience.

Every class, without a single exception, was taught entirely by the TA. I have never even SEEN Dr. Chang before. This wouldn't be a problem, but she writes all of the work, and it is INSANELY hard to follow. Instructions feel like they came from ChatGPT. The TA did the best she could, but her instructions from Dr. Change were similarly confusing.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'So many papers']

comment: Mostly run by the TAs, but she showed up a few times towards the end. The TA for my section, Corey, and her are very kind and help in lab with the data analysis. The pre-labs are very important-- if you do them, your data analyses and post-labs will get done easier and quicker. Overall not too difficult, just make sure to do everything and show up.
