Professor Ciccarelli classes will not exactly be easy, but you will learn the material. Of course, ask questions if you need to. He's happy to help clarify anything.
He is a good professor. He is also very reasonable. If you put the work in he is more than willing to help you out.

I would recommend Professor Ciccarelli to anybody. He is great when it comes to breaking down the big ideas that we need to understand from the lab. Office hours were reasonable and he was always helpful whenever I came to see him during his office hours. I would definitely take any of his classes again, if I had the chance.
For a lab teacher he is good in explaining what we got to do for each lab. I learn more from him then my lecture class.
Having a textbook in case you don't understand something is essential. I also enjoyed working with both real circuits and simulated circuits.
He's tough but a good guy at heart. Taking his lab next semester again because he's fair and straightforward.
Very good teacher.
Awesome teacher! Very knowledgeable, engaging, and effective!

Good professor. Not always so clear in describing labs but is more than willing to help you work through it. Prelabs are easy assuming you pay attention in your lecture section and are a vital part of the grade. It seemed as though we were expected to know our way around the bench and know how to use tools such as a multimeter and a decade box.
Very good instructor. His labs are easy to handle and he is very helpful in class and during his office hours as well.
Good professor who is passionate about the subject. Can be a bit confusing when class time is running low, but he is always available during office hours for clarification.
Pretty great professor. Sometimes the requirements he requested to be turned in with each lab were a tad confusing, but great overall. Definitely recommend!
Had him for DC Circuits lab, very helpful and concise. Would definitely take him again.

Prof Ciccarelli teaches and answers questions very well.  Concepts has a lot of material to cover, so exams are not fun to study for.  He gives quite a bit of homework and the grader was very tough on us so make sure you work on it well in advance.  The matlab questions in the later part of the course is very annoying.  Quizzes are fair though.

Nice guy, down to earth and great one-on-one. But Concepts was designed as an online course, and unfortunately is still taught as such. Ciccarelli reads from the slides and doesn't explain the material well. Textbook is horrendous (useless). Good luck 'learning' the Matlab
Tests and quizzes are 90% multiple choice and are chained questions (if one part is wrong, subsequent parts end up wrong).Lectures are good, lab is good. He loves Dilbert cartoons.
Very very good Circuit Theory prof, Best professor I've had at RIT. Very clear, strict but fair. Usually helps students out with grades towards the end of the quarter. 10 out of 10.
Very nice professor but tests and quizzes are hard.

Possibly my favorite professor so far in CAST. Makes circuits very simple to understand. Creates his own notes that are much clearer than the book. Very prompt grader, sometimes has tests graded same day. Gives out food in class :)
Superb teacher; he puts an amount of effort into preparing notes and lectures that I haven't seen paralleled in any other class at RIT.

awesome professor homework was manageable and useful posted all of the solutions on mycourses and all of the notes tests were defiantly the most difficult part of the class. overall best professor i have had so far and loves to put Dilbert comics in his notes.

He is a great prof. I would take another class with him. Prof C does a great job covering the material and testing you on it. Workload in Concepts is usually a lot. If you get the homework, you'll do well on the quizzes. If you do well on the quizzes you will do well on the tests.

One of the best professors at RIT. Distributes his own notes in classes, because the book is useless. Encourages students to understand material he presents. If you attend classes and care what he says, you will do well. Certainly recommend him.
Great professor.  He really cares about his students and if you do what is required and show up to class and show respect you will do well.
Overheads were awful for the material being taught in Concepts in Systems and Signals.
One of the better professors of the department. I recommend you take this class with him.
Fantastic Prof, really cares about his students and that they LEARN
Works hard to help students who are struggling, throws you snacks if you answer questions, or ask good ones. Interested in much of what students are interested. Overall, he;s awesome.
Couldn't have been a better experience.  Difficult material, but he was there to help the whole way.  Highly recommend this teacher for any class...

My favorite professor so far.  Very clear, bends over backwards to help you.  Makes class more fun because he is so into the subject and gives out bags of chips for anyone who answers questions. Overall, great prof. if you want to learn and are willing to follow along with the moderate hw and studying that's required.  Highly recommended.
No good ppl...
No Comments
No Comments
He's a great professor. Always there for help, always on your side. He has a wonderfully unique teaching style, and even posts most of his lecture notes on MyCourses. Highly Reccommended.

She is very knowledgeable and brings insightful ideas, using current journal articles to guide discussion. She allows students to engage and share perspectives, which is valuable. Workload can feel heavy for a one credit course, and experience depends on the topic, but overall a thoughtful and engaging seminar instructor.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'So many papers']

comment: A nice person to talk to, but not a good teacher. Lots of work for one credit class. Seminar topic changes every semester, so if you don't like the topic, the whole semester will be boring

Class was heavily based on readings. Most of the grade comes from projects and quizzes which are also based on the reading so be prepared to read a lot. However Dr. Fedorovskaya cares a lot about students and brings a lot of outside application to the lectures.

HOLY BUSY WORK I learned nothing from this class and professor has little to no instructions on weekly group projects, but then will grade you harshly. Make sure to consistently ask for clarification on rubrics. This was one of my least favorite classes and the amount of busy work/readings was so annoying and useless
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Students have to read entire chapters for homework and discuss it seminar-style in class instead of being lectured at all. Her slides are pictures only with no text, not that they help. Also grades randomly, returns grades weeks after, and gives no feedback. Her expectations for assignments and class and answers to students' questions are unclear.

Her accent makes lectures difficult to understand and her review slides and feedback during lectures are not helpful unless you study and review every aspect of the textbook beforehand. This is a heavily individualized study class, focused on reading the textbook and teaching yourself the material while keeping track of weekly group projects.

Professor is very intelligent and insightful. I really enjoyed her class and learning from her. She had interesting ideas for group projects and provided current journal articles in the world of neuroscience. She was able to guide discussions while also taking a back seat and allowing us students take the reins.

Took her my first quarter at college, read the textbook, made 1000 flashcards (no joke) and put in way more effort that I should have had to for a 101 class. Got one of 3 A's in the class. Class average was a C.. Would not recommend taking her class. Her accent and her useless PP slides just makes it impossible to focus and excell in the class.

I'm a a graduating biomed major and her class is like an upper level neuro-science course. She has a very heavy accent and I couldn't focus much in class because of it. Class could be interesting if you're willing to put in A LOT of time reading the book.  3 major tests no cumulative final. Some random assign. In between.

Her psychology of perception class was the worst. Tests are hard if you do not read the book. Almost half the time the exams have nothing to do with her power points. Sometimes she doesn't really know how to explain herself well. I would not recommend this class wit her.

Laurie is a fantastic professor. Very flexible and gives you confidence and a little push. The one thing I would probably be weary of is that you have to teach yourself and experiment with how to use Adobe Illustrator and Indesign. Love the structure of classes, the first submission is a Pass/Fail and then you resubmit for revisions for a grade.

Laurie really grows on you. At first, I didn't like the course, but once you get in the swing of things it gets better. If you're interested in the topics its really fun and if not, she is always willing to add new assignments or throw away old ones. She also gives really good feedback on assignments, which is why critique can be so long.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']

comment: Laurie is awesome to work with!  She is available to talk if you need to talk to her about both personal and academic matters.  Her feedback is to the point and while there's quite a bit of homework, I know for a fact that it will benefit me in the long run!  A zillion times definitely recommend!

All of the assignments are done in Adobe InDesign, Adobe Photoshop, and Adobe Illustrator. Expect the class to be difficult if you have little to no knowledge of these programs. Expect to teach yourself how to use these programs, she does not go over them much in class. Long critiques, easy grader. Wish this class had a lab portion.

She gives too much work. she is a kind and nice lady but the amount of work, a film project each week on top of other courses is overwhelming.. submit all her projects on time and you'll receive a B at least.
Does not actively grade work, gives exams with vague questions/questions missing crucial context, lectures include lots of filler which makes it hard to stay interested.

An extremely sweet and caring professor. Probably the nicest professor I have ever had without a doubt. Only thing however her teaching is not the best during lectures and requires a lot of effort outside of class to understand what is going on and being taught. Her exams are very fair, and she does not make them unnecessarily difficult

Has a few drawbacks from the way they teach, but all around fine for taking a mandatory requisite. Course material seems a little disconnected from the textbook, but whatever you see on the homework is on the test. Be wary of a last minute group project disguised as a lab.
Not a good teacher, clearly just a researcher who is required to teach classes. Spent half the class fixing her simple math mistakes.

Not a bad professor, but also not the best. Breaks down concepts well and repeats explanations whenever asked. Makes small mistakes during lectures but is happy to be corrected. Lectures are not at all engaging. Very disorganized with online assignments.

I wouldn't mind taking her again if I had to but I also wouldn't actively choose her.

Lectures are slow. she occasionally messes up / doesn't know what's going on. Class was easy. Always posts lecture notes after class. Never responded to emails, though she did read them.
If I didn't care about learning the topic and was looking for an easy grade I would take her. If I cared about the topic and wanted to learn about it, I wouldn't.

Doesn't know material and won't admit it, so gives incorrect info or teaches simple math unrelated to class material. Deliberately wastes time. Laughs at you for asking questions, but also unable to answer. Exams stolen from other schools' online archives. End of semester, she told us not to submit bad feedback because "it's not productive". AVOID!

Blessing is a very nice person, but the class is 100% lecture, and she can be somewhat difficult to understand or follow. I found that she would go on tangents often. Still, overall, She was good, and she didn't assign too much work

You get easy but tedious homework assignments every week, she is slow to upload quizzes to WebWork and sometimes even forgets (they are normally uploaded at 1pm or later). Kind of difficult to understand at times and gets lost a bit but I found her class to be just about average. Tests semi-mirror labs. If you get her you will b fine just study
easy activity course for your undergrad. Super easy quizzes that take absolutely take no time to complete each week as your "participation grade" and saves you a lot of time. Highly recommended

I agree with the review from Jan 2nd, and I also wanted to add a few things. Professor Blessing has an accent, but it didnt interfere with the lectures overall. She takes the time to make sure everyone can view and understand her lectures. Lastly, the labs she assigned were done in groups, and they were graded on completion and not correctness.

One of the nicest and most encouraging professors I've ever had. There's enough homework to understand the material well, but not so much that its overwhelming. Lectures are clear and informative, and she likes when people ask questions. Uses Webassign for most homework assignments and test review.

One of the nicest and most encouraging professors I've ever had. Lectures are clear, and she likes when people ask questions. I liked the amount of homework, it was enough to understand the material without being overwhelming. But I didn't feel that we always had enough time to work on labs. Uses Webassign.

Your grade is what you make of it. If you go the extra mile and asks lots of questions to do your work correctly, she will know. Definitely not a class you can slack off in and expect a good grade. She is always willing to help out if you reach out. She incorporates her real life experiences in packaging and applies it to what she teaches. Love her

Proctor definitely knows her stuff when it comes to packaging so it makes her classes really interesting. Mktg & End Use is all dependent on the group project so get good partners. She tends to be really vague about what she wants and changes her mind throughout the class, and will rip you apart if she doesn't like it, but gives good feedback.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GROUP PROJECTS']

comment: She was tough, but she really knew her stuff. A fantastic resource for all things packaging. She teaches from her own personal experiences in the field making me wish that I could keep her in my pocket and ask her for project advice at work.

SHE KNOWS EVERYTHING ABOUT EVERYTHING! Great or should I say BEST teacher if you  really want to learn without cracking open a textbook! You earn your grade however. labs are easy but the Test(s) require a crucial amount of studying !  STUDY!!!!!

Quite the stickler, but knows her stuff! As long as you take proper notes (which are based off of the lecture slides she gives you) and you study properly, her tests are no big deal. She can be a bit temperamental wen it comes to grading, but will give you the credit back if deserved. You will learn so much!

Had for Rigid Containers (Fall 2000), got C; Process Control, got A; 1/4 of Graduate Seminar, which I took as a Professional Elective.  Rigid was ridiculously hard, my only C at RIT and my only non-A of the quarter.  Process Control was unbelievably easy.  Not the greatest explainer, and multiple choice questions could have up to 7 choices....

Great Professor, loves packaging and it shows during her lectures. Class is challenging and engaging. If you go to her for assistance and listen to her advice you will do well. Hard to  squeeze an A out of her.
Karen is one of the only Packaging professors with real world applicable experience.  She speaks with a knowledge level that is well deserving of an RIT education.  Be GRATEFUL if you have her.
obnoxious voice, difficult tests, knows her stuff though

She has no tolerance for people who are not part of her "inner circle" or her favorite students.  If you're not on her side, forget it. She also talks REALLY fast, and it's impossible to follow everything. The only teacher I know who manages to squeeze 2 hours worth of material into like 40 minutes, due to the rate of speech. Gives me a headache.
As long as you sing to her tune you'll be alright other wise you're just another thorn in her side. Her only good appointments for professors are Fritz and Robinson.

THe first comment must have been by someone who does not like Packaging.  Karen cares about her students and is the first to come and defend packaging.  She stepped up to the plate for me many times when she did not have to do it.
The worst teacher int he whole program, i don't have any idea how she became the chairman

Humble, Caring, Helps student to every possible extent. Easy going. New to teaching but is good at it. Has good industrial experience and shares it pretty often, discusses his past projects. Lectures are clear but boring sometimes. lab experiments: easy but brainstorming. In the end you will almost master PLC automation. Recommended for Automation.

I would say that Vee has improved a lot from what the previous reviews have said about her. She ensures you understand the material, is a bit of a harsh grader but gives good feedback, and is understanding if you're going through something mental health wise!  Overall, I'd recommend her classes, she's a great professor!

She assigns so much homework & barely gives us time to complete it. We would have to make a puppet rig from scratch and animate it every week, but we wouldn't get to all the material we needed to learn till Wednesday - if at all - and the assignments would still be due Monday. She also claims to be accessible and understanding but really isn't.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Content is not digestible through in-class demos. Weekly projects are not manageable. No rubric to see how she is grading. Feedback is often subjective and not about the use of the software. You will likely get a failing grade on projects even if you hit all the requirements in the written assignment. Makes you feel bad when you are lost in class.

I took her for 2D digital. There was a lot of work expected each week for things not explained. Inconsistent grading without a rubric. With all instructions completed, most students can expect a failing grade due to unlisted requirements or preferences unrelated to assignment criteria. Vanessa clearly does not like teaching or answering questions.

Vanessa does not like teaching and she does not like her students 😐. She's not encouraging when you are struggling and makes you feel stupid when answering questions. She is unforgiving with her grading and is inconsistent with the requirements. She will give you a 50/100 even if you met all the requirements

I took her Character Design class for animation, and the class was somewhat difficult with a steady pace of work.  In the simplest terms, the professor is someone who will see a students concept and tell them to redo it entirely if it doesn't fit her vision, rather than offering critique on how to improve on the concept.
Class managed to be interesting and papers were fairly graded. Couldn't ask for anything more.

A great teacher! Class was never boring! A tough grader, but gives you a lot of outlines on what your essays should look like. Gives you readings that you don't need to read. I would highly recommend him, he will definitely change your ways of thinking!

Had him for writing seminar, he knows his stuff. Pretty funny. Class is kind of boring though. 3 Essays and you choose your own topic. He's very skeptical and his class is based off of that, so it's pretty boring if you don't agree with him. Essays are not too bad.
Had for Busting Myths. The class is basically on skepticism. Awesome, amazing, incredible class. Really changed my way of thinking. Requires a lot of reading and writing, but it's worth it.
Excellent teacher; Classes were fun and interesting

Desoremeaux is without a doubt an opinionated guy, but he will challenge you each and ever day.  He really is a fantastic teacher, and his feedback on graded work is very useful.  The assigned papers are on enjoyable topics and our final project(analysis of music lyrics) was very entertaining.  I hope to have him again and recommend him to others.

Wonderful professor! Very caring and creates a positive class environment. He's easy to reach during office hours and is accessible through Slack. He's unfortunately retiring, he will be dearly missed and remembered for his amazing dedication to Software Engineering students.

Professor Reichlmayr is really nice. Class can be boring but I think that is just the material of the course in general... Homeworks are doable, going to the SSE/asking the CA/going to his office hours really help. Also you can ask him to schedule one on one if you don't have time in his office hours. Practicums EZ if you do SSE practice practicums

The way he explains is confusing. Prepare to learn by yourself. He is NOT accessible outside class. I emailed and asked about the project and he did not want to answer me. One good thing is he extends deadline. I do not study from him, just by myself and the help of SSE.

Professor Reichlmayr is a good lecturer and doesnt have a high workload. Most of the classes are for lectures, with some project work time. Homework grading is loose, with some based on if something was submitted and others for completion.

Though his lectures can be boring, he has a lot of energy and is clearly passionate about the topics he teaches. Always willing to answer questions. Made grading criteria clear and provided good feedback on projects.
Nice guy who's a pretty leinent grader. He's not the most entertaining lecturer and coupled with the fact that SE 220 is a boring class makes it pretty mind numbing
Cool guy.

Nice guy, but is kind of hard to understand. Stays on topic well, but can really drift off and confuse a lot of people. He is cool though. The class itself is pretty had. Homework and practicums are somewhat hard. Projects are very difficult though.
He is a good professor, but the class was bad.  He explains things well when asked to, but otherwise just briefly goes over the material.  He is a fair grader.

Good professor. He was provided useful feedback on questions brought up in class. Reasonable workload. The only issue I had was that some of the lectures did not appear to be that useful because the material was already stated in the required reading.

Good professor. Very personable with his students and always willing to help out on all assignments required for the class. In addition, a very fair grader in terms of the practicums (if everyone did bad on one of them, he would allow a resubmission to get half points back).

I was very pleased with the first weeks of class, thought he did a good job of presenting the material (even if it didn't matter for the course). Nice guy, but not great if looking for constructive feedback.
Reichlmayr gets a positive soley on the fact that he is very personable with his students and really wants to see them all succeed. His lectures are a little boring, but he's a nice grader.
Very nice, helpful, clear to understand. Knows what he's talking about. Makes the subject interesting. Highly recommended professor!

Brilliant Professor.  He is definately one of the best professors in the department, if you get the chance to take him, you should.  He is a fair grader (I got a 104 on the first exam for crying out loud) and takes things at a pace that is managable for most people.

Awesome professor; I take him every chance I get because he's really good at making boring material fun and easy to learn.  He's also friendly and generally available and helpful outside of class and during his office hours.

Good guy, helpful and cares about students. He didn't get as involved as I would have liked in helping us resolve an issue with a troublesome team member throughout the quarter, but he did help us try to handle it ourselves and we got good grades (not sure about the other team member, though). Take his class if you have the chance.

He actually cares about his students; as such he is very helpful and generally available in his office to take questions related to class and even those that aren't.  He explains things well and doesn't assume that everyone knows what he's talking about.
This guy is cool.

Took this guy cause he was the only one left, very glad i did.  He is a nice approchable guy, and a pretty easy grader.  He made the SE experience much better than any I have heard from people who have previously taken the course with others
He is very friendly and always willing to help; he is an enjoyable professor who encourages questions and makes hard material fun to learn.

Teaches online classes only so it is hard to compare to a normal professor. Pretty slow at answering emails and posting grades. Also unclear about assignments at times. Pretty easy going when it comes to grading.

Professor Keady is laid back and very caring for his students. One important part of his classes is that he utilizes activities in order to teach the subject. Students often will pair up and pretend to be a coach while the other student is a patient. You will learn a lot by listening and paying attention, as well as doing the required assignments.
Landi is a very fair and helpful professor. Would definitely be happy to take classes with him again.

He covers the material in class so that you have a really good understanding, and is willing to elaborate on any question until you fully understand. Homeworks are much more difficult than quizzes/exams.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']

comment: He's a great teacher if you want to die from learning. He'll assign you 40 page articles and expect you to know them for the pop quiz the next week.

He has definitely grown on me since CPA, I get why he doesn't always give much time to do things now because you have to be efficient as an engineer. That being said he gives just enough time on tests now and is overall a much better teacher than I originally gave him credit for

Good person, however he gives little time on exams and in class problems. He explains things very well but he does not seem to understand that some of his students are much more analytic than others.   In reality if you make a mistake in engineering you could accidentally kill people or easily get fired, and I don't see how rushing students   helps

Perfectly structured class. Taught exactly what you need to know, how to apply it, and when to use it. Gives clear notes and lectures followed by example problems. The homework is weighed the same as an exam. Lowest exam dropped. Fair graders and good attitude. Highly recommend.
Subject matter was not my favorite however, I was content with Dr. Landi's instruction.

He is the perfect teacher. Clear notes on white board, does examples, then lets the class try one. Hw is required but rly helps you prepare for the exams; the exams tend to be easier than the hw. His teaching style is easy to learn with. Definitely take his classes. A plus is that you dont NEED to buy the books, he will print out tables for you.
Not overly difficult. Frankly a lot of people in his class were just plain stupid

Dr. Rob was a very good bridge for me into Calc-based Physics. He's very engaging, but also straight to the point. If you want feedback, he'll give it without hesitation, but it's all to make his students better. I really enjoyed class with him, and now that I'm in UP2, I appreciate what he focused on in class, because he get's you ready.

Lovely teacher! First time teaching CP2 and with his teaching style, I did considerably well compared to CP1. He gives lots participation and extra credit. Notes and quizzes are well thought-out and helpful. Truly cares about his student's performance in the class!

Dr. Rob is amazing. I was not the biggest fan of the class style (workshop) but I lived with it. I personally believe that if the class was a lecture, I would have done 10x better. The labs that he chooses to do really help reinforce the material and are enjoyable. You will suffer with UP 1 here because of departmental issues.

Great professor! Dr. Rob is very helpful outside of class during his office hours. Unlike many other teachers, he does not use the flipped classroom format. He occasionally gives out extra credit for participation and homework.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: Dr. Rob is a genuinely a nice guy and wants his students to succeed. I really struggled with physics so I attended his office hours regularly which helped a ton. He actually teaches during class rather than using flipped classroom that relies on videos to do the teaching . Take his class!
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Caring']

comment: Great personality, however this class was overall brutal because of the heavy lecture style. If you skip even a day you better make sure you get the notes for that day because he has quizzes every class and it can be taxing for your grade.
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: Good guy at heart, but I just do not like his style of teaching physics, personal preference really. Quizzes every day which is very taxing. Lots of extra curricular things are taught (which can be a good thing!) but overall, meh teacher.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']

comment: The professor has odd grading and teaching styles. They grade mostly on a completion basis so as long as you meet the criteria you're good. They have a "Grading Contract Survey" that allows the students to have influence over grading and attendance. BUT I don't think I've watched more useless lectures ever. I learned NOTHING through the lectures.

Bad lecturer and not reachable outside of class. Strict about deadlines, wont accept submissions late by even a minute. Gives off mixed vibes from day-to-day. He might be friendly one day and annoyed the other day.

Easy online class, when you can understand what the syllabus and assignments say. The syllabus is vague, and the assignment descriptions are not much better. Getting clarification from the professor is like pulling teeth--requires constant poking and prodding. The lack of responsiveness makes the class a lot more difficult then it should be. Beware

She's a nice person. Always submits feedback late, grading criteria unclear. This class was frustrating. We are not receiving grades until the end of June, even though they were due May 10th. This class felt disorganized and rushed. Either she needs someone to help her teach a class of this caliber, or she shouldn't teach it.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: Constantly late to classes and TESTS. One test she was even 10 minutes late to, how is this acceptable?  Unprepared to deliver tests.  The tests were confusing Included topics on the tests that she DID NOT TELL YOU would be on the test. She is an INEFFECTIVE TEACHER, would do better just reading textbook  NOT an appropriate professor for this level
The tests have almost nothing to do with what you learned in class or from the textbook

Made my life having to take circuits as a mechanical engineer so much better than I thought. She's extremely accessible via email or office hours or after class, is extremely organized and concise, the course pacing feels right, and her lectures move through things quickly but are fun to participate in and she always takes questions.
tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: She was an amazing explainer, the quizzes were all open note and extremely helpful for later on the tests. Her explanations were clear lots of examples, homework was extremely helpful and easy to do.
The material is difficult, however she's extremely well versed in explaining the material and makes everything so much more bearable. Make sure you study hard, but other than that it's an easy class.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Beware of pop quizzes']

comment: Jing Zhang is one of my favorite professors. She introduces all the material really well. Pop quizzes happen, but she almost always tells you when they are. They are open note. She is a really easy grader and a really sweet person. Keep up with the reading and assignments and the class should be easy. 5/5
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Super nice professor and clearly knew a lot about the subject. Very passionate about the class.
An amazing teacher. Creates a great atmosphere and always makes the lectures enjoyable. All tests had extra credit and made sure you would succeed if you put the effort in.

She is a very very good teacher. I normally zone out during lectures but not her's. The material is very easy to understand and the homework helps A LOT, and you're almost guaranteed to get a 100% on every homework. There are weekly quizzes which also help a lot in reviewing material that you can use ur notes for. great professor overall!

Really nice professor, lectures were really nicely organized and all lectures are posted online incase you do miss one. Quizzes are open notes and really easy if you just pay attention to lecture. Exams were also really simple, with reviews showing example questions. Overall really good professor.

Really amazing professor for Circuits 1, exams were really straight forward, she would go over what each question is on the exam and if you study the material well you will pass this class easily. "Pop" quizzes were also really nice and easy as they were open book and also good study material for the exam. Overall really good prof.

Professor Zhang truly wants us to understand the material and clearly explain the topics in a digestible manner. She often warns us of pitfalls and provides us with ways to prevent them from happening.

Highly recommend her as a circuits 1 professor. She grades very easily and there is extra credit on exams to make up for any minor mistakes. As long as you attend her lectures, follow along with the in-class problems, and do the homework, it is an easy A.

Dr. Zhang is a great professor. She explains everything clearly and respects your time, no rambling or running 10 minutes over the clock. She is also fairly generous with grading so long as she sees you were on the right track. The only problem I've had is reading her handwriting from the back, but she uploads all of her notes to follow along.
Great professor, makes class very easy to understand.

Professor Zhang made class really easy to understand.  She would provide good examples for all the tests that you could practice, and then made the tests themselves fair.  As long as you show up to the classes, you should be able to get a good grade in the class.

Professor Zhang really cares about making sure her students learn, and will go over multiple examples in class while explaining how to solve them. There are weekly quizzes, as well as online homework. If you take the time to go over the material on your own after lectures, you will do fine in this course.

comment: Dr. Zhang is a great professor. She interacts with her students during lectures and is very clear! I am not an EE, but I am taking circuits and she makes it very easy. She is also very helpful in office hours! Her english is also very good! Highly recommended

Professor Zhang gives extremely clear lectures and makes sure to do a ton of examples so that you know what to expect for homework and exams. She is extremely organized and definitely knows her stuff. The tests are challenging but Zhang adequately prepares you for them. Especially for electrical engineering majors I would definitely recommend her.

I would highly recommend taking Dr. Zhang.  At times she may be a little confusing, because English is not her first language, but she is extremely helpful.  If you are ever confused she is always more then willing to meet with you until you understand.  She cares a lot about the success of her students.  I would recommend taking her.
Dr. Zhang started fall 2014 and her English needs improvement, but she is understandable she just doesn't use good sentence structure and her word order is at times confusing.

Cole's GIS classes usually consist of about equal amounts of time spent on a lecture and working on an assignment in a typical week. His lectures can be pretty dry and sometimes walkthroughs are not always clear, but Cole is very knowledgeable about GIS and is always willing to fill in the gaps if you are having trouble understanding the material.
tough class, but probably the easiest to fulfill the scientific perspective requirement.

To people taking GIS classes- All of the GIS classes he teaches are project based and he gives you significant freedom on them. He grades based on the given criteria of the project but you usually end up delivering more than required anyway. He is flexible and helpful when you are having trouble. Great guy.

comment: Fairly boring lectures. He cares about GIS a lot and has a lot of experience with it. Just 4 labs and a group project make up 80% of the grade. A lot of work was required for some of them though. He can be extremely helpful if you have any trouble though.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He reads off PowerPoint slides like it's his first time lecturing. Don't waste your time going to class. He also had us purchase a subscription to a website for homework which has the wrong answers in multiple assignments.

Takes little to no input from students. Refuses to believe that he's ever wrong even when he is. Most likely the worst professor i've ever had. Likes to read off walls of power point slides. Unclear in his teachings. Very boring class.
excellent teacher. Good at dealing with students
- unorganized, had an incomplete syllabus, hard to communicate with, he doesn't respond to email regularly.
I took a course in general chemistry and enjoyed learning the fundamentals from hi, He is thorough and systematic.
Excellent teacher. Microsensors  are very nicely explained. Uptodate knowledge
Excellent teacher. Lucid and clear in explaining the topics.
take a class with him
learn more
Teacher is horrible. Tests are online. Don't bother going to class, its a waste of time. Very hard to understand and can't teach to save his life.
Very knowledgeable, but can't teach to save his life. Tests are online.
Useless professor. He gave exams online, so obviously everyone did well. Can't teach whatsoever. If you take a class with him, don't bother attending. Just read the book at home.
The worst professor ever, and the most unhelpful director of materials science that we can have
his english skills are lacking and a very difficult man to communicate with.  he is very good at repeating your questions back to you, as opposed to actually answering them.

Decent teacher but rushes through slides. Slides are dense and difficult to understand. Can't really do the homework unless you ask him what the questions mean, because he uses his own terminology. Lets you use GenAI for all homework and projects, but I don't think this is wise in an ML/AI course. Good at explaining in OH, however
Very nice and chill, you'll learn a lot if you pay attention to lectures, great ways to learn through grp projects, and practicing making the models and math he teaches.

comment: Professor Lima does the best he can teaching such an abstract topic (machine learning). Sometimes his lectures may be boring or confusing, but he will gladly help you out during the problem-solving sessions if you ask questions. The class is not easy, but if you give it your all on the programming assignments, you should be prepared for the exams.

Lectures are unengaging and difficult to follow, be prepared to teach yourself all the concepts. The activities are very helpful but he struggles to give useful answers if you have questions on them. Programming assignments are scheduled to be due the night before exams. He knows what he's talking about he just can't communicate it to the students.

Extremely accessible outside class, helpful, replies fast on email and discord. He explains the concepts better outside class and holds weekly zoom meetings for the online class. His lectures are not very detailed, he skims over the presentation slides a lot and refers to the textbook. I felt lost and confused in almost all assignments

Well the lecture notes and code examples are good but sometimes the professor himself cannot explain very clearly about some points. And sometimes he taught some point which is equally essential in the test too fast. But he's easy to access during his office hours or in discord group, from this aspect he's student-focused.

Such a great professor. Very helpful during office hours. He doesn't give a lot of homework, but there is a group project that is a big part of your grade, so make sure to start it on time. Problem-solving is getting harder throughout the semester, but they are basically boosting your grade if you do it in class and ask questions.

He is a great professor; he cares for his students and is helpful during office hours. There are four individual programming assignments, which are not too difficult. There is no final exam but a group final project, which is a big chunk of the grade; make sure to start early and ask him questions since the write-up is not very clear.

Really chill and a nice professor. The material is not easy, but if you solve the activities, you will be fine even for the exams since they are based on them. Only 4 individual programming assignments, not super hard, but start them on time. Get a good group for the final project and you will be fine.

He is a good professor and is very knowledgeable in what he teaches. His lectures do however tend to drag on and become boring as he pretty much just reads off the slides. He is always available to help and wants to make sure you understand the material.

Good professor, although lectures can get a bit long and boring. I sometimes had trouble keeping focus and had to learn the stuff after. He is caring and funny, and I really liked when he shared little aspects of his personal life. Good professor

He is super nice, and is a really caring guy, but the lecture is mostly read off the slides. If you make a simple mistake such as submitting a wrong file or didn't read a lab, write up properly and email him what happen you will give up the proper grade.

Great professor. Has good lectures, and is around during labs to answer any questions and to clear up any misunderstandings. He also has ample office hours, especially after exams. He wants you to succeed, but you need to reach out to him if you need help.

While I do think he understands the material, he does not know how to convey it to students. The homeworks don't really teach anything and the in-class recitations were either tedious or irrelevant. He claims to care about students but none of his actions reflect that. The class wasn't hard but I also didn't learn anything.

Prof Lima is a nice guy but needs to learn how to organize a class. Homeworks were delivered broken and students needed to fix the questions, the final project outline was vague to the point of uselessness, and grading was totally arbitrary. The topics are so out of date as well that they're useless on co-ops. Don't take for higher level classes.
Comp Sci is difficult for sure but he was really funny and definitely cared about his students. Lectures can drone on a little but for me it was the topic not him.
Very hard lecture & lots of homework. Would not recommend if you have no prior cs background. Very chill person during lab tho.

Lectures are helpful but labs really solidify the material and help you learn a lot. At least in my experience, working with a group was very helpful when it came to the bigger assignments like labs. Lima is not too lenient but cares a lot about your success and will help when he can.

I had Lima during his first year teaching at RIT. I believe that he is a good teacher but is stuck within the bounds of the RIT CS department and the higher ups who determine the curriculum and the assignment workload. He is an honest person with an overqualified background who will help you if you make yourself available and use his resources.

Professor Lima is a sweet and understanding guy. He is always willing to sit down and help you in office hours and is nice about extensions. However, his lectures are long and boring and not much is to be learned from them. As other people mentioned on his page, the recitations are MUCH more helpful in regards to finishing assignments and labs.

Lectures are boring. Recitations seemed to teach more than the lectures. His class is only easy if you have programming experience. Lima is a good person by himself but I hardly took anything in from his lectures. New topics felt like you were just reviewing them. Good professor in terms of personality, hard class.

Professor Lima was a decent guy. Very helpful during lab sessions. Lectures were hard to follow, long, and dull. Most material was learned from recitation. Tests are difficult compared to other CS professors. Would recommend his class if you have prior CS experience.
He just doesn't explain anything only reads from the power point presentations

Attendance is required, lectures are the worst ever. Never explained what he was writing, just scribbled on the board with a random slide up. He skips most of the slides, why bother showing any? He'll act obtuse when you ask for clarification on a quiz (poor English). I learned from MATLAB projects only. This class was truly a waste of my time.
His mini quizzes are poorly worded and dooesn't make sense. The MATLAB projects are incredibly hard and also felt he was very biased towards the native guy.
Very helpful

Lyshevski is AWFUL at teaching. He is all over the board. His accent is very heavy. His homework & lab assignments are quite difficult & his quizzes/mini exams are way too short for the content & adjusted enough so homework & lab assignments are worthless. And you're expected to know classical controls which is a known joke at RIT. He's also rude.

He wrote the textbook. He lectures from the textbook. He gives homework from the textbook. The labs are from the textbook. He is the textbook. Simulink, Simulink, Simulink, Simulink... All in all, the course wasn't that hard. I skipped >80% of the lectures and got an A. Reference the past quizzes/exams and you'll be fine.

Do not take any course with this professor! He is the most difficult man to deal and learn from in all my 5 years of university. Exam questions must be answered PERFECTLY,or you will not get ANY credit. Questions in class will be met with rhetoric remarks. RIT has failed its students in being able to learn and ceases to do anything about it. AVOID!

I recommend not to take this course because u will absolutely learn nothing Professor is higly knowledgeable but cannot teach effectively MATLAB assignments will be given and don't expect them to be easy one must spend awfully lot of time doing them One can expect easy A if they perfectly do the exams and assignments Exams are very easy

Cannot understand what the professor is trying to say most of the times.. Even if raised a question on an unclear topic, he would be repeating the same.. Has a very hard accent.. Teaching is not that efficient.. Poor grading..

I was really disappointed by my choice of this course. I didn't learn anything in the class. Professor teaching was not clear. Professor have good knowledge and have written some books but he doesn't help you. Grading was done randomly i guess. Most of friends got screwed. I would recommend you to avoid taking courses under this professor.
Good teacher if you take the time to understand the subject.  Easy to approach but he won't give you the answers.  Instead he will make you think through problems.  Great character, hard professor.

Worst professor I've ever delt with as a 5th year. I had a 93 going into the final, got a C in the class. He REFUSES to use logic while debating a grade. He thinks 377 is a better answer than 120*pi. The book is written by him, so naturally it makes little sense. Bases class off of book, then tests on different things. Homework is impossible. AVOID

Terrible Professor.  Makes you use his book which is an unintelligible as his lectures.  Expect no help from him in class, in office hours, or at review sessions.  Grades totally at random and harshly too.  Avoid at all costs.

Absolutely horribly teacher. tests and quizzes unrelated to material, grading is random at best. I found a mistake in his answer key and he took it personally. avoid at all cost. I'm serious, If he's the only prof teaching it, take it a different semester... the dean owes me a letter of apology for having this man on staff

Very very difficult.  Makes me wonder about RITs commitment to education over research.  Difficult to follow and difficult to understand.  Didn't give any homework which made it very difficult to prepare for exams.  Makes you buy his textbook, but doesn't even use it for half the class.  Don't take him if you have any choice.
Very difficult professor, not helpful, hard to understand, no practice problems are given and you have no clue what is going to be on the tests. Dont take this prof!!
Avoid this class at all costs! Totally unclear and poorly developed, average class score on first test around 50. Not helpful one little bit, and hard to understand. You've been warned!

It's clear that he's passionate about his job. He likes to talk about his own life experiences to tie culture into lecture, which is nice. The way he teaches Spanish is via conversation, so speaking/listening skill are definitely a focus. His MyCoruses is very disorganized and lectures are quite boring, but he is an overall easy professor.
Class was always in good spirits. He tells a lot of stories about his experiences and takes an interest in his students.

Very easy-going and caring guy. His stories about different Latin cultures were always very intriguing and fun to listen to. Classroom environment is very cheery, lots of laughs! He is an easy grader but can be a little slow at times with getting it back to you.

As with any language class, participation is key. He asks questions about the English language while teaching you Spanish which creates a good, almost-conversational class dynamic. If you answer his questions, he will call on you more often, which can be good if you're looking to practice your speaking and bad if you're trying to sleep.
Solid choice for Spanish 201! Love his teaching style!

comment: All around a very polite guy. Very patient and tends to go off on tangents. Definitely a solid choice. There needs to be more professors like him!

I really did not want to take Spanish but wow did having this professor made it so much better. He is very clear and fair with deadlines. If you don't know something and he calls on you, it's never a big deal, he'll just explain how to do it. He is extremely kind, helpful, caring, and thoughtful. My favorite professor so far.

Professor Godys is one of the best Spanish teachers I've ever had. He really cares about his students and is passionate about what he does. He likes to tell stories when he's lecturing which helped me remember what we learned better. There are a lot of small homework assignments, so make sure you keep up. Overall I recommend taking him.

Great guy who always tells interesting stories during lectures. He is a native speaker but makes sure to speak slow and clear so understanding him is not an issue. Only thing is that homework was graded slowly, but it's not as if you will be surprised by a bad grade since he is a very easy grader.

I had him for 3 semesters; definitely one of my favorite teachers I had at RIT. He's a really cool dude who's easy to approach with issues and fun to talk to about non-school stuff too. His anecdotes about traveling Latin America and growing up in the Dominican Republic were highlights of class time for me.

Godys is a great professor and a great guy in general. Sure, he'll get off topic and talk your ear off, but he's so friendly and helps you practice your Spanish. He assigns weekly group audio recordings and occasional writing assignments or online homework assignments. His class is nothing to worry about. Participate in the class and enjoy it.

He is such a nice guy! Is able to communicate well and gives the material out in a way that you can understand. There is a bit too much to fit into a semester but he works with the class to make sure everyone can keep up.
A nice guy, willing to work with you to make sure you do well.
Such an amazing professor! The fact that he is a native speaker really makes a difference! He is charismatic, and really can make you motivated to learn Spanish like nobody else
Easy grader, really friendly guy. Makes lame jokes. I recommend him
Overall nice guy and good teacher. From the Dominican so he has a bit of an accent but nothing thats too hard to understand. Online textbook required for classes.

Good professor. As is common with Spanish classes I've taken in the past, a lot of work is assigned but not collected or graded. Gives into complaints of students a lot and maintains a pretty easy class. Like most language classes at RIT, there is a decent amount of work associated with the course.

He is a super easy grader, and if you do any amount of studying at all, you'll get an A. Very funny and easy-going. I don't really see how you could do bad in the class. I really don't know what the other person was talking about.

I took spanish with him and it was horrible for me because I have never learn spanish before and all he does is mumbling by himself. he's not organized, and he always lost what we turned in, like our midterm exam. he doesn't know how to speak english. BUT if you already know spanish, take him!

I've had her for a couple marketing classes and she's a great professor! Her classes will not be easy A's but you'll learn a whole lot from her. She gives great practical advice and feedback on assignments.

comment: gives lots of reports!!!!

Laura is a good professor. Her classes are focussed on discussions, group projects and participation. Her class is not an easy A because of the exams but you will learn a lot. She gives tons of feedback and you will remember it at age 50. Her classes are designed to make you learn. If you love easy A's and no learning then must not tak her classes.
Great professor she tries to help everyone remember the most amount of material by being very interactive.

She won't just give out A's, but you will learn a lot and you have a fair chance to get good grades with Laurie.  I took 2 classes with her, and both were enjoyable experiences.  She keeps the lectures interesting, has plenty of case examples, and she's sneaky funny.  Enjoyable teacher and great teacher with significant experience in marketing

Laurie is awesome! As long as you show up to class and work hard while you are there it's an easy A. She respects those who respect her and she keeps her lectures interesting. I am not a marketing major or minor, but I after her class I thought about adding it!

Professor Dwyer is a great professor, but I worked pretty dang hard in this class to get an A. Her lectures are good and she keeps things interesting, but you should expect to study at least 10 hours before a test if you want a decent grade.

was a good professor, made the criteria more enjoyable and not boring during lectures. Tests were difficult but she looks for points to give on essay questions and short answer. Very reasonable teacher, would recommend!

For a summer online class, the amount of work you are expected to complete is exceptionally tedious. She gives horrible feedback on group discussions, journal entries and exams. I wish I would have never taken this course with this professor. I used to enjoy marketing until I took this course. No, I do not recommend this professor.
If you want a professor who really care about how to improve students, DO NOT take her. Just a Joke
I loved Laurie, she was interested in knowing everyones name and making the class fun. The marketing project/presentation was a lot of work but I learned a ton and she was awesome.

her classes are only based on case discussion, mostly cases about small company marketing failures, and it does not contribute to the overall marketing knowledge so much. She made me quit marketing as my concentration. She might probably give good grades to natives.

A bit more memorization and a little less use of skills and ideas than I generally like, and the online homework setup had a lot of vague questions that led to some low homework/quiz grades, but overall not a bad teacher. I've had better, but I've also had FAR worse.

Vague expectations, hard tests, requires you to memorize material rather than understand it. She knows a lot, but doesn't prove it, b/c many class exercises and projects rely on the class/student to come up with strategies and extrapolate. I did not feel there was an emphasis on research, and some of the projects were ridiculous and tedious.

Professor Dwyer is an amazing professor. Yes, she sees through peoples' crap and will call you out on it. But, if you want to truly learn about marketing, not to mention professionalism, from one of the most knowledgeable professors at RIT...take a class with Dwyer. You will not regret it.

Professor Dwyer is intimidating, but helpful.  She really pushes you to learn through 4 projects (2 team-based), and 3 tests.  Her tests are kind of hard, but if you study her review packet then you'll do fine.  I never had a problem with her and thought she was quite good.
just...bad
Great Professor. Good lectures. Is clear with her presentation. Helpful outside of the class.

terrible professor - only HER way or opinion is right.  don't bother thinking for yourself in a field like marketing that should be free thinking - only what she thinks counts.  gives no real guidance along the way and doesn't let you know what she expects.  if you really want to learn, don't take a class with her
She's a great professor. Relies on the textbook a lot and tests are HARD! But if you study and do the work, and go to class you'll be fine! Not an easy A.

This was her first time teaching MMP. Having the pressure to follow Tyler's footsteps while creating her own, she was able to fulfill both. Definitely both sides (her students and herself) had learned a lot.

Amazing professor, so, so sweet. Responds to emails within good time and really gets to know her students. Relatively relaxed grader, just make good use of her exam study guides, do top hat questions (right or wrong, points awarded), and don't procrastinate on engagement activities.

Dr. P is an amazing lecturer. She gives detailed feedback on assignments, and her exams truly are not that difficult if you pay attention in lecture and make good use of your notes for a few days before. Engagement activities can get a little bit annoying, but they keep you up-to-date on the reading. She's so sweet and always open to discussion.

Caring professor. Lectures are engaging with Top Hat and she tries to keep it interesting. Homework doesn't take up too much of your time and helps you understand the content. You must participate in psych studies, which isn't bad if you try to get it over with sooner rather than later. Exams are easy if you pay attention in class and study a bit.

Beware of exams she gives are very tough if you do not pay attention..Also be aware she lectures heavy. If your on your phone she will keep going and you will miss Tophat questions if your not paying attention to lecture. Make sure to take good notes. If something is said going to be on test, then it will be on the test.
Fun in-class assignments (do mock psych studies in groups) and decent lectures. Very little work and lenient quizzes/exams. She is very understanding/caring and will help if you reach out to her.

Despite the tough exams, I really enjoyed being in her class. She was always accessible outside of class and willing to help me understand certain in-class concepts or instructions on homework. So long as you attend class and keep up with the materials, this class is not too challenging.

She is great with explaining the topics if you need more clarification. She's willing to help you if you ask for help. But no extra credit is given except for SONA credit. If you fail one exam you can take the final to replace one bad grade. Take advantage of her office hours for help and clarification.
She uses Tophat for her lectures.

This Professor is willing to help you at office hours... if need help with your assignment or need clarification... go to her office hours immediately. Lectures can be boring but I say try to pay attention to details. She provides a study guide to use to help for your exam but you can not use it on the exam.

Professor Prokosch is such a kind person! Her lectures were always informative and interactive with the use of TopHat. I learned so much from what she taught and she made learning psychology fun. Even though our class started early, she was very energetic and knowledgeable regarding every topic.

Lectures can be boring, but that is due to the material, not professor. Implements plenty of fun activities to stay engaged and gives clear criteria when it comes to the contents of a her tests, making the class less stressful.

She's great. I had a D because I never did any of her work or went to class, and only took 2 tests. At the end of the day, I had a 58%, so I begged her for a 60% and she gave it to me with some minor extra credit I had to do. Great teacher and if you don't do the bare minimum as I did you would def get a better grade.

Lots of lectures that have a lot of information, but always available online for study guides and homework. Not a whole lot of homework, but what little homework there is is always relevant and never busy work. Plus, she gives out extra credit and the final is optional. Plus gave warnings for unsavory topics when needed.

Overall she is very nice and you can tell she is interested in teaching the material. She used to teach at Tulane University and her lectures are pretty good. Class can feel a bit long and boring at times but we do in class activities/mini labs to break up the lectures. Class is mandatory, but with all the participation points, you can miss a class

Joel cares so much about his students. Class was mostly in a group discussion environment, with reading assignments before class. He was able to build a sense of connection between all the students very quickly, and he was very understanding about balancing workloads. Also he does magic tricks!

I met Joel outside of RIT and he recommended that I take his magic class; easily one of the best classes I've ever taken. It was so much fun and I learned some of the coolest stuff ever. TAKE THIS CLASS
I had Joel for both ITDL 151H and SOIS 299. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Homework is meaningful and not just busy work! Ask to see magic tricks!!

Joel is the best prof ever. He's incredibly kind and understanding. This class is really just reading  (which is a lot, but skim-able). The only homework you ever have is discussion posts weekly (one paragraph) and a monthly "journal entry" which is just a reflection. As long as you do it, you'll get credit. He does magic tricks for you too, lol

Hands down the nicest prof I've ever had. Chooses great readings, mostly ~20pgs. Very fatherly and understanding of extenuating circumstances. Assignments are 1 paragraph discussion posts on reading and one response, and a journal entry per unit. He'll do magic tricks for the class, and he's terrifyingly good at them!

LOVE JOEL. 10/10 best prof Ive ever had. Readings and discussion board due before every class but discussion is amazing. Very lenient grader but offers good feedback. His specialty is education and he knows how to make an ideal class environment. Very kind, accessible, and endlessly patient. Will give magic shows if youre good :)

Even students that did not have Joel as a professor could see that he is a very good teacher. I did not care about the content, however, that is by no fault of Joel. He is lovely to interact with and really cares about his students. Beware, there is a heavy amount of reading as this is an honors class, but I got away with not reading anything.

Professor Joel is probably one of my favorite instructors at RIT. I can't say anything bad about him. His class should be easy if you do the work. Homework consists of reading an article and contributing to a discussion each class. Lectures are pretty interesting, and he even occasionally does magic tricks that he connects to the class content.

His class was my favorite class by far that I took that semester. I actually looked forward to every class! While he gave a lot of reading and required us to do discussion posts it was engaging subjects and I learned a lot

This class was very enjoyable, and Joel makes it so. His class was always my favorite that I looked forward to, as class discussions were very interesting. There is a lot of reading to do for homework, but he is a very easy grader, so skimming readings is acceptable. Overall amazing guy and class

I have had Prof Link for a couple of semesters, and he was one of my best teachers at MCC. He made class fun and pushed me to get outside of my comfort zone. I appreciate that he made himself available whenever I needed extra help and was understanding when life got in the way of school.

He is at MCC now. One of those professors that really care. Always willing to help if you come to him before deadlines, even made himself available on weekends. Labs make up majority of grades, and if you show up and try, he will get you through them. Final project, no final exam. Blink is da man

Prof Link is at MCC now. Assigned homework and assignments are extremely long, the labs are well walked through and he always checks them over before you submit to see if anything needs to be fixed. Two projects, no final. Get an A on the first project documentation and you are exempt from the 2nd project documentation. Link wants you to get an A!

For the lab, Prof. Link provided a video overview of what was required starting from a block diagram with additional details for the lower level. If you needed additional help, all you had to do was ask. Don't wait to ask. He was readily available via zoom and was even available on the weekends.

Prof. Link may not be the best professor on teaching the theory part and explaining things, because it is little old fashioned, and reading from ppt, but on the up side his quizzes and exams are 90% directly from the slides. the labs are tough but the great thing with him is that he will truly help you get the grade you want! he is very nice abt it

Not a great professor. Still teaches like it's 1995. Provides information in his discussion posts on how he wants programming examples coded a day before the assignment is due. Then takes off points if it's not done the way he specified in the discussion post. Waste of time and no respect for student's time.

Although Link was a strict professor that ran a tight ship, He was extremely knowledgeable in the subject. He knew every possible error that could happen and was very good at helping you fix the errors. This course took more effort than other similar courses in the department. Link was also fantastic at feedback, and making sure you left the course

Bruce is a good guy, lots of real world experience in VHDL to give out. If you give him respect and show that you care about learning in the class, he will definitely help you. If you try to be too grabby for points or game the system he might not respond well though. His question wording for tests, quizzes, and homework is left to be desired.

Professor gives work on things not even remotely covered in class. It is often known this professor is "Old Fashioned" both his teaching method and material. When coding you must be able to code in both VHDL 1989 and 2008. This professor really does not like being corrected when he makes a mistake. You will do a lot of self learning in this class.

comment: Has no office hours until before class. Give no extensions on labs. Exams are just straight riddles, did an exam where I got  the same question right on a older one ... and managed to get no credit on the new one. Dropped courses to complete work in class and still needed more time for assignments. Not worth it taking his class.

This professor is extremely strict in grading, he prides himself on not allowing students to get As. Grading is inconsistent, points being taken on later assignments for work identical to previously un-penalized sections of assignments. Work load for the class is unrealistic, do not take with any other lab classes, or other classes for that matter.

First- If your class is available by another professor, take it with someone else!!! The man is very knowledgeable in VHDL, but is abnormally strict. If he give you a lab and the whole class ask for an extension, he will give an extension but you already lost the points for not submitting on time. Dont take class if taking 14 or more credits!!

Professor treats you like you are at a job in real life which some students dislike but is it is realistic. If you are willing to work hard and ask questions then you will learn a lot. This Professor is extremely knowledgeable and I would recommend to anybody taking this course.

comment: Picture a large lecture hall with a whiteboard. Her lectures are dense and her attempts at interactivity are useless because  her students are in a catch 22. The most difficult EE instructor at RIT, but highly recommended in E&M fields knowledge.

Amazing! GREAT TEACHER. Funny, interesting, etc. Pretty easy as long as you do well on the tests which are all based on his PowerPoint slides.

comment: Rui was a great professor! He cared a lot about the success of the class as a whole. He gave a lot of practice problems and weekly quizzes which were easy as long as you went to class. he is awful

I had Gupta for Statics, Mechanics and Dyanmics. He forced me to learn these subjects very very well in order to pass the class. He was very helpful outside of class with any questions I had.

we got 4 homework problems for each class, ive had no trouble catching up after missing a week of homework he only collects it on test days. he makes himself available to everyone at many times. does not single students out for asking "dumb questions" or questions at all. very interactive and effective class environment. great professor, teaches by examples.  very helpful, knows the answer to everything.  tests are somewhat difficult, lots of hw

Pros: Excellent analytic skills doing discussion in class. Decent knowledge according to global deaf studies. Give detailed feedback on students homework assignments and projects. This is my second time having this professor and it was great experience! She still very nice and friendly. She is funny and willing to help you out so much. Even willing to meet on the weekends. Very chill and understanding. Best of all she is very patient so if you don't understand how to use a program don't worry. I learned a lot in her class.

Very unclear and talks about her experiences with Harris more than anything. I suggest finding another Professor or you will probably fail the class.

Miss a couple of classes and you'll really hurt your grade. Otherwise she is very kind and informative on all topics related to and about accounting. comment: Fantastic professor took spatial alg and tech with him learned a lot about geo spatial technology and liked that we could choose our final project.

Lots of quizzes, but they aren't that tough (although some questions can be a bit contrived). Projects and labs are generally graded fairly easily.   Everyone's favorite part of the class was when we spent a few weeks flying drones around, doing scavenger hunts, etc. How neat is that?

Doing research with him.  Really awesome professor!
Great Prof, His class will make you learn a lot, but he teaches it well. Great guy too, helped me outside of class more than once, and got me to get myself an A

Absolute gem of a professor. Always available to help you with the work in class and will definitely be willing to help you better understand any type of chem if you ask. Also the most hilarious and fun professor ever. Always has a good joke or story for us, and lets us play music in the lab.

Gen & Analy Chem Lab 1. He was nice and honest about expectations for the lab. Pre-lab quizzes were easy with only 1-2 multiple-choice questions. Lab procedures were fairly easy if you can follow instructions. Feedback on lab reports was fair and actionable. p.s.: WRITE the lab procedures in a notebook BEFORE lab starts with your NAME and DATE!

comment: He's amazing! He would bring us breakfast for Organic Biochem. Lab. I would have him as a professor if I had the chance again.
Best professor

I had him for my gen chem lab and both quant labs. He is an amazing professor. Sooo helpful! He even came in on a Saturday to help me with quant lecture material. He is a very fair grader and gives you plenty of time to complete assignments. If you have the chance, choose him!!!
Spectacular professor for lab. easily accessible outside of class. will look at drafts of reports and give you feedback. not very strict about due dates.

Dr. Hans is a very nice lab professor. He is extremely helpful and has a very generous late work policy. He may seem a bit confused at time, but he will do whatever he has to in order to ensure you understand what your doing.

Dr.Hans is a wonderful teacher t have. He is very lax in class and in his grading and is very understanding on multiple situations. He is always willing to listen and I've gone to him multiple times about other classes and he is always wiling to help. Take a class with him if you have the chance.

amazing lab professor. explains everything however many times you need to understand. easy grading system. accepts late work no matter how late. very sympathetic to personal problems & stress. goes out of his way to make female students welcome. overall great guy. i wish he taught all intro chem courses.

A really nice and funny professor. Talks really fast and can be difficult to follow at times. Labs are a lot of work, don't procrastinate on them. All the tests were take home, and he was flexible with deadlines. Overall a really cool guy.

Loved this professor! Such a nice guy. Very funny and entertaining to listen to. Had him for digital foundations. Course is a bit fast paced so good notes and submitting labs on time are very important. Didn't get any grades till end of quarter but he had a family emergency so this probably isn't typical. Ended up with an A!

Excellent teacher. He definitely knows his stuff and he knows what he's doing when he's teaching. Great guy too, pretty laid back and keeps humor in the lectures. He grades pretty strict, but the assignments are quite straight forward. Best teacher I've had this quarter by far.

How you do in his class depends ENTIRELY on if he likes you, regardless of the effor you put in.  Brilliant professor and great guy but I can honestly say I?ve never seen someone play favorites more than he does. Also, if you ever break down because of the work load he?ll give you an A

Great teacher. Nice guy, relaxed, realistic about how college students are, passionate about the subject. Easily excited. Allows for some assignments to be resubmitted. he kind of makes his students feel like they don't know anything.  he's a pretty nice guy and definitely knows his stuff, but needs to realize he makes it impossible for us to learn stuff when he goes through it 100 miles a minute.
makes everything way harder than it should be.  too much work. not a fun time.
The best Prof. ever. He is very helpful and understanding.

Excellent Professor. A little difficult to follow, but if you ask for help or clarification of help, he will drop everything to make sure you understand. Loves what he does, and it shows. Highly reccommended.

Amazing prof and person! I've taken several classes of his. Extremely intelligent, always willing to explain things. Knows material inside and out. Tons of energy. I highly recommend getting into any class you can with this guy!!!
I've gotten good grades in his classes both times. He's a good teacher, it may be just the material he was teaching is boring. I didn't pay attention fully and still passed.
