he is the man, tought me more than i knew
Awesome teacher, definetly the best one for this class. He's very intelligent, and makes the class fun and interesting

Great teacher!  Very helpful.  At times he gets so excited about the subject matter he needs to calm down and talk slower. You can tell when he gets really excited and enthusiastic because he will start to talk with a very slight stutter.
Pretty cool guy.  He does his job the best he can.  The other teacher was boring, though I showed up to 3 of the classes, I still got an A.
Good teacher, but unclear about projects at times.

Jenifer is an excellent teacher.  Granted that she teaches FYE and Pathways the courses are a BREEZE.  She's very passionate about service and easy to talk to.  I HIGHLY RECOMMEND HER CLASS FOR A GOOD TIME.

Very loud and upbeat. She can be a little too much to handle sometimes, but overall is a very nice person who loves what she does. I found her very easy to talk to, and she was very easy to please. No peer evaluations, so good if you're a slacker and bad if end up carrying the group.
She is very perky and sensitive. Will prefer the students with emotional issues over the normal ones. Class is easy, but she is not an instructor you want, you'll be annoyed every time you see her.

She truly loves what she does and is easy to become friends with. High energy and has tons of personal stories to tell. If you can handle her upbeat personality, she is totally worth having, and makes FYE classes more bearable.

Class was made up of open-note quizzes and tests, a group presentation and weekly participation activities. Lectures are interesting and keep you engaged, then tie directly to the activities you do in groups. She's easygoing and approachable, often joking around with our class. Great professor who makes it a fun elective to take!

This was for Crypto class. Super awesome teacher, really helped me learn more about the subject. You get 2 certifications(exam score) and talks from the FBI and others. No homework, just 2 exams and 1 big paper with a presentation. She's super knowledgeable and very chill.

Dr. Stiehl is one of my favorite professors at RIT.  She is extremely clear when teaching, and takes notes (that she then posts!) along with you during class.  Her exams are hard, but fair, and she provides an overview of what will be on each exam beforehand.  Amazing professor and person, very supportive if you go to her outside of class.

I have never programmed a day in my life before her intro to programming class. I definitley had to go to class because the examples and in class assignments are important. All the exams are only worth 40% and the lowest can be replaced with the final. She teaches kind of fast and all her classes are basically the same. Example, then in class work

She was an okay professor. I have nothing special to say. She is okay at teaching code, although I feel like she goes through it too fast and she can be helpful when asking questions 1 on 1. Her homework assignment sucks but a lot of help is provided by TA's. Her exams are average as well. It is a doable class, just need to put in a littlew ork.

Dr Stiehl is so kind and is the everything MatLab whiz. I recommend drinking a coffee (or 2) before class just to keep up with her fast pace walkthroughs the first few classes so you can adjust to her teaching style. If you get lost, ask! She's very accommodating to every level of coding, but be aware she can be kind of sneaky on midterms.

We basically did the same thing every day which was kind of boring but at the same time, it was easy to get into a groove. It is not an easy class and working on assignments with other people makes it a lot more bearable. It takes some time to get to know Dr. Stiehl but if you get to know her she can be a very kind, caring, and bubbly person.
Literally learned the very basics of VBA coding in class.. but she expected us to code a whole game as a project???

She was very understanding and accommodating for the varying ideas, skill levels, and time constraints that each of her students had for painting. Even the act of just talking about ideas out loud with her helped clarify plans for working on a piece. She is a very positive being and it's hard not to be positively motivated by her happy vibes alone.

Prof. Glass is so awesome, she changed my viewpoint on critiquing art and art competition. She focuses on each individual artists goals and what they want to achieve within their work. She genuinely cares about her students and gives ample opportunities for gallery shows, art internships, etc. She's a great resource and prof :)
She will let you go back and rework assignments for an improved grade.

Emily is one of the kindest professors I've had this semester. She is very down to earth and cares about you not only as a student but as a person. While there isn't a lot of homework for this class, the homework you will be assigned can be quite time intensive, and expect to work hard if you want to do well in this class.

Absolute sweetheart of a teacher. Gives feedback in a way that is fair/constructive while not feeling abrasive, and definitely bolstered my confidence in using charcoal and pastel. Projects start observational and get more conceptual throughout the semester. They're time consuming but she is also very approachable if you need help or feedback.

Emily's class is difficult and time consuming, but incredibly rewarding if you're willing to put in the effort. She's very approachable and understanding. While the homework is a lot, she allows resubmissions for regrading. Ask her for feedback one on one!

Really relaxed environment, but very homework heavy (at least 6 hours on each HW drawing) compared to class time (all exercises with skills, speed, etc.). Critique was completely open for both students and her to give feedback within the time, which was very helpful. Emily was also open to one on one feedback for anything, homework or other.

This class is hard. Even if you like traditional drawing, it's gonna be grueling for you. The homework wasn't as bad this semester, but you can't shirk on any of your work. Despite the difficulty, Emily is a very understanding and helpful teacher; she's always open to meet after class whenever she's open to assist you and wants you to succeed.

Her class is much more about hands-on drawing, and she rarely teaches. However, drawing is all about practice, so it's not a bad approach for the drawing class. She's also a pretty kind person, and gives good critique without making you feel like trash.

comment: Difficult class for me, you have to really work to get good grades and improve if you're not already really good. Very friendly teacher, you can go to her for individual feedback which can be really helpful. If you're willing to work, you learn a lot, solid teacher.

She's young and very quiet. Her feedback and artistic sense is good. She is a little odd. She's not exciting by any means. Classes are pretty boring but if you like drawing then its not too bad. Overall solid teacher, but definitely not the kind of teacher that students love and joke around with.

Emily Glass gets away with being a truly bad person by using a sweet little voice and framing criticisms nicely. Her advice is unhelpful, she doesn't ever do hands on instruction, she wastes a significant portion of each class, she comes up with dumb news ideas all the time for you to do, she has no other methods of teaching than negative criticism

Prof. Glass is a good painter herself, but is really not a proficient teacher. Her assignments, for this studio level class, were something I would have expected in an intro course, and although she might know what she's doing, she has a hard time imparting this knowledge on her students. Don't expect an A unless you are a very realistic painter.
Definitely knows what she is talking about but has high standards when it comes to grading. You will do great if you expect to get 15-20 grade points lower than you want

Emily is extremely helpful and knows what she is doing, but this class is hard. All homework and class work can be reworked multiple times for higher grades. Never turn anything in late! You can always rework something bad later unless it is turned in late.
Javier is a good professor. Very passionate about typography.

Javier is very knowledgeable and passionate about typography and design. He gives constructive and helpful feedback on every project. He also assigns creative and challenging projects that allow you to explore different aspects of typography.  He is not only a great teacher, but also a great mentor and inspiration.

Javier is a nice person. But lectures are dry and he only does basic overviews of necessary subjects. Most of the learning is done outside of class using sites like w3schools, not in class. Assignment parameters are vague, but quizzes are open note so that's a plus. 7 weeks in and apparently we've learned everything for the entire 15 week semester.

He's a nice enough person and very laid back but the way he words things + instructs is very disorganized. Lectures tend to be quite dry + assignments were vague. Provides a free PDF "textbook" to reference for the term + quizzes are open note. Take advantage of sites like w3schools because that will be where you'll learn things, not this class.

Professor Johansson provided a very well-planned and structured course with almost no deviations from the plan. Grades were handed back quickly with rubrics and feedback, although follow-ups felt incomplete/unhelpful and no reconsideration for grades was made. With how it was set up, the professor didn't feel that involved with the class.

This is the second of his online courses I've taken. In his class you must do assignments his way with some variation, but usually his way trumps all others. You must go to all zoom lectures, get ready for at least 2-3 wkly tasks on top of the 3-6 wkly readings. You learn a lot only cause you're buried in work.

comment: The class was very good. He is a little bit of a tough cookie but he genuinely cares about his material and the students. Study and you will pass.

His exams ask about the most random, unimportant things from the readings and videos. He subtracts points from homework assignments for small spelling mistakes and grammar, despite his own several mistakes throughout the course material. Essentially, he cares more about dinging students for small mistakes than he actually cares about the material.

I thought this class was an easy A, I was doing great, finished most of the work in the first couple weeks and had a good time with all of the reading and materials... but in the end, my grade was surprisingly low for the amount of work I put in (with consistent As.) Do ALL of the discussions and do them on time and you'll get the grade I deserved.

Ive written a lot of papers over the years and I've never had someone be so clueless about propper writing tecniques before in my life. You will get points off for having paragraphs that are too long and capitilizations that do not belong (despite checking in MS word and proofing that there are not). Everything you say had also come with a citation

Mike is an incredible professor and contact to have at RIT. His classes are "easy", but he expects and rewards hard work. Lots of room for growth and creativity with Mike as a professor, you will learn a lot of value bale writing and Social Media skills along the way.

A class with Mike will be one of the hardest classes you'll take at RIT, but it is completely worth it! Every week I would hand in copy and he would find 10 things I could have done better. He gave me the feedback I needed to hear, and didn't sugar coat anything. Because of that, I am much better prepared for the field of advertising. Great Prof!

Get ready to learn how bad you are at copywriting. The class is very tough but if you pay attention, do work outside of class, don't procrastinate, and apply yourself you'll get a loooot out of it. Plus, Mike's accent is great and his bow-ties are delightful.

All of the tests (including the final) are online aka open book and extremely easy. Weekly readingsquizzes with 5 tries to get a 100. One final paper. Easy class and Johansson makes it super interesting. (and he wears a bow-tie every day and has a fun accent.) Favorite professor so far!

Mike is the best! He is very clear with assignments, and expects punctual quality work in return. Do the assignments well, and he will give you an A! He is really involved around campus also, which is great.

Mike is a great teacher.  The online quizzes are easy and can be done with out reading text book.  Friday is not held just reading out of class.  One research paper is due at the end of class but just do the draft and you will get an A.

He is an excellent professor. He will give you help any time you ask for it. He allows you to rework past assignments to get a better grade. In my three years at RIT I have taken a total of 4 classes with him and have loved them all.
Very good in getting the content across. Helpful, encourages you to rework material handed in. Overall an excellent professor, with real world knowledge.
Helpful if you ask for it. Able to rework assignments for better grade.

What sticks with me most is h9ow married to his own subjective opinion he is. In copywriting it was his personal opinion that determined the grade we got. In other classes I was told that I "had a hammer and everything looked like a nail," but no specific advice to work to improve. Half of my Cs are in his classes for these two reasons alone.

Not quite sure what the problem is /w some people. He lets you rework graded weekly assignments. The final paper is pretty intense but overall you learn a great deal in his class. Took him for PR Writing and Copywriting and Visualization.

Horrible teacher. Takes points off for something he never informed you of. Ridiculous grader on papers and projects. Expects your work to be at a professional level when this is most likely your first class in apr.

Not a bad guy and the way he plays devil's advocate is enough to make anyone question themselves about even the simplest of comments. Fun and interesting guy and he makes the study of Public Relations less boring than it is in reality.

It was his first time teaching at RIT... no, just no. He's nice kind of? But is a really harsh grader on papers he isn't even clear about. Obsessed with blogging and Twitter.. so just write about that...

Prof. Karim is awesome! He sometimes can be confusing, but all he wants is for his students to learn. Dances in class, loves Lady GaGa, and refers to himself as a "cool daddy". Tests are easy if you prepare for them

Absolutely terrible. Attempts to teach "his own" version of the book, using useless diagrams and going off on rants about the local school system mid-class. If you aren't a select favorite, he will ignore you. Brings his 7-year-old to class when he has to babysit. A kid's Nintendo DS is extremely distracting when the professor is this bad. Avoid!

He is so funny and make everything simple. He is easy grader in assignments and final project just do what he asked for don't make difficult stuff follow the instructions and u will be fine. DON'T forget to bring calculator to the class. Most of my friends and I got A.
terrible

He is a great professors. Easy to get a high grade. But few things I didn't like about his teaching. His sense of humor is horrible. He also talks about the "contract". You need the book and calculator at all times. If you don't have it, then face a tirade and a bad joke that follows to neutralize it. Otherwise he is a good professor.

Great professor. MoveOnDotCom, Hard Cookie, and Piece of Cake. Has a great sense of humor. Do the homeworks and study the slides, and exam is gonna be piece of cake. Overall, the class is fairly easy.
He's fantastic.
I'm serious. Moveon.com? The train is at the station. If you don't remember this, you're going to be in DT, deep trouble. I love this professor. Not only smart and a great professor, but funny too.

GREAT PROFESSOR, AND A NICE PERSON.. EXCELLENT TO WORK WITH, ALWAYS INTERESTED IN HELPING OUT STUDENTS. CAN GET A VERY HIGH GRADE VERY EASILY.. GO AHEAD AND TAKE HIS CLASS, ACCOUNTING KNOWLEDGE IS MIND-BLOWING..
Awesome instructor! Very knowledgeable, helpful and genuinely interested in students' learning the material!
Great person and great professor. Kind of like a drill sargeant in class, but you will learn.
Prof Knows the subject well and gives clean/clear explanation. Attendance recommended. Grading includes 5 homeworks ( Dropbox submissions ) , 2 midterms and a final

This class is set up similar to many ECON classes at RIT. 3 exams and 5ish homeworks. The hardest thing about class is the professors accent for me. Very dry lectures, struggled to stay away every class. She writes some homework questions with weird wording, overall she really knows her stuff. You gotta work for it but you can do ok in this class.

Super hard Asian accent (like can be seen even in her writing) that makes it harder to pick up the info than it ever should, but does care about her students. Overall would not recommend unless you can pay attention and are good at self-teaching. Askign questions usually leads to reiteration of the previously stated material

comment: Class average on tests are around 65-70 , which is around a C or C-. I've gotten 90+ on all my exams but I can tell my classmates have an extremely hard time. She speaks a bit too softly, so sit up front. Definitely take the time to study. Micro is a lot harder than most other COLA classes, so don't expect to waltz in and get an A
she was very helpful, recommend.

New but a very good professor. You can feel she cares. Some of the econ concepts are difficult to understand in reading but she always can make it easy via examples. She is enthusiastic, encouraging and makes herself available outside of class.

I took CSCI 720 Big Data Analytics with Prof Romanowski in Summer, and had a great time! Get ready to do lots of research though! Her style of teaching relies a lot on the effort you put in - you really need to work on your homework(which she gives once every two weeks) and discussions. She's always prompt with email responses.

comment: Tian is a great teacher. You can really tell she cares about her students. Her classes are not designed to make you fail but rather lift you up, but I will say they are heavy on assignments and tests(2 of each per week). As long as you do your best and show up you will succeed.
An amazing professor. She even brought us snacks occasionally. I learned a lot from her lectures. They are all very engaging. She is also very lenient when it comes to grades
By far a amazing professor! Would take again. Very great at giving feedback to you when needed.

comment: I LOVE HER. I took her CHIN 151 class at University of Rochester my first semester of college and it was my favorite class. Definitely get ready to memorize vocabulary and speak during class, but it was harder for me because I didn't know how to write chinese characters before this class. I ended up passing with a 99. something. Highly recommend!
She is such a sweet person, and I genuinely love her.

I think she's a really sweet person. However, when you take her classes for long enough, you start to feel like things are being made up on the fly. Instructions and deadlines for a lot of assignments aren't clear, and class moves by so fast that it feels uncomfortable asking for help. Nice lady, but sometimes ill-equipped to teach.

You could really tell that she cared about each of us. A lot of the class relies on participation, but she was good at drawing us out of our shells, and by the end of the semester, most of us were pretty comfortable speaking Chinese in front of the class. There is a decent amount of homework but she will change deadlines if needed.

She would assign homework due everyday, but some days she wouldnt put the assignment out till the afternoon or evening that was due that day. I wish she would make the homework available ahead of time so we could get ahead.
Do not take a course with this professor unless you genuinely care about the material. Teaches elective courses, but gives more homework than any other professor I've had (I'm a science major).

Elisabetta is a great professor if you ever plan on visiting Italy or would like to eventually become fluent. She is very very strict when it comes to attendance and laziness and if you are looking for a fun easy language course she is not the professor to take.

She seems really nice at first, and for the most part she is, but she chooses favorites and makes no attempt to hide it.  If she likes you, you can float through the class, if not, watch out!  She also likes to assign lots of work that can get hard to keep track of.

Excellent teacher!  Her class is a lot of work but you learn a lot!  She gives lots of extra credit opportunities and is very helpful if you seek it.  She wants everyone to do well, and will help you succeed if you put forth a true effort.

Dave was one of my best profs ever. He's an inspiration to anyone into comics, gives great feedback on your work and breaks down the medium in a fun way. Class is 6 hours long, but if you like comics it's great, and he gives 30-min breaks. This class, for legal reasons, is sadly not part of the comics immersion as it should be, so consider that.

David has a lot of fantastic advice about the comics industry, but tends to talk about his own life more than give feedback on student work. The class itself is also a bit grueling, spending 6 hours in a windowless studio is not for everyone. Also expect to spend time outside of class working if you want to make a good comic.

Took IGME 202 async-online. Lecture/demo videos were helpful but pacing was a bit slow, and I thought some parts were overexplained while others were totally glossed over. Wanted a bit more rigor/technical explanations of things in the curriculum, so hard to say I got a ton out of it. Overall friendly & helpful person, but didn't enjoy the class.

Sean is a professor who actually cares deeply for his students. I had a difficult time this semester and he always helped me in every way he could. He makes time for his students whenever he can and goes into very helpful detail when working with a student. He does everything he can to make sure his students do well.

He is great, and she truly cares about her students. I honestly was just looking for an easy-A class and ended up really enjoying the material. It is easy to do well in this class, her rubrics are more based on following directions than the actual assignments

He's the goat. Can hit him up at random times on Slack and he responds if he's not asleep and apologizes if he doesn't immediately respond. He sets up like checkoffs for projects where he gives you super-detailed and helpful feedback, while also not punishing you for messing up there. Take him to know how real professors should teach.

Sean Brennan is not only an awesome professor, but he is a total Bro! He explained the concepts of writing good research papers, Photoshop, HTML and CSS, and more in a consistent and concise manner. If you are falling behind or need help, Sean is always there to help! In addition, he is a great resource with questions concerning the game industry!

Class is pretty much based on how much money you are willing to spend on materials. I cannot stress enough how much this professor is an ineffective educator. 90% of this course is the online quizzes from the $70 textbook that you have to buy online. She is very nice but shes a horrible teacher. comment: We were graded heavily on the group project. The few tests were easy, online, open book. She graded very liberally and the class didn't seem all too important, but I loved meeting local entrepreneurs. Listening to them speak was absolutely invaluable and made the class worthwhile.
She tries to be interactive but mostly lectures throughout class. It becomes dull. Her tests are very specific. She's overly excited for class.
She's a great professor, and I would take any class taught by her.

Extremely organized for teaching this class for the first time ever. His classes are literal bootcamps, but believe me when I say completely worth it. He was amazing !..I enjoy his professionalism, and his teaching style..I felt really good after attending his Marketing concepts class

O. M. G.  His assignments are a life time of work.  Say goodbye to your social life.  But his knowledge of internet marketing is amazing!  If you can take his class and survive, do it!  He makes you a cut above everyone else and gives you real world experience.  He's awesome.  Oh, and call him Uncle Neil, he loves that.  :]

I had Neil for Principles of Marketing.  It was so much fun every class!! It was a 6-10 class but it didn't even seem like 4 hours because it just flew by.  One of the greatest professors I have ever had. Take him if you EVER get the chance.  No tests, just 2 papers and a project. The work is hard but it is worth it!! Real world experience as well.

Neil is Awesome! You will work very hard in his classes but it is all worth every minute. There is not text book or tests, just lots of classwork and group work. Do yourself a favor and go to every class and to his office hours. It helps a lot

Neil is awesome! He knows what he is talking about when it comes to Internet Marketing. His slides are possibly the greatest thing created! No books!! Lots of experience and working with a real client. Hard class but worth it!

Neil has been the best professor I have had in both undergrad and graduate school. His knowledge of marketing blew me away. I highly recommend all of the classes he teaches at RIT. The more opportunities you have, the better. Consultancy experience I gained from his courses got me my current job. I still seek advice from Neil today.

The best professor I had at RIT...bar none. What he taught in the classroom wasn't just for a letter grade, it helped out in life as a whole.  He built confidence, character and inspired us to push ourselves to the max.  His teachings are STILL relevant 2 years later.  I hold him with high regard and am grateful for having taken his class.

Hands down the best professor in the business school. This guy knows what he is talking about, and can really change your views on marketing. Relates everything in the course to how you can successful make money in the future. If you put the effort in it will be one of your most rewarding experiences at RIT. Highly recommended for all business stud

Excellent professor - one of the best I had while at RIT. Class includes a LOT of work, but it's totally worth it and you'll leave his class having accomplished some very important business practices and strategies. Lectures are interesting and extremely well presented as well. I would recommend would of Neil's classes to anyone.

Professor Neil Hair's teaching has had a major effect on my career. I had very little computer skills prior to taking his Internet Marketing Class. It was there I learned about HTML, Flash and how to develop effective web pages. If it wasn't for him I wouldn't be doing what I do today. I am working for a Fortune 500 company using those same skills.

Bar none the best professor I've had the pleasure of taking -- twice. I, unfortunately, discovered him my last year of college, and was unable to enroll in more courses with him. His standards are high, he's tough, but he knows his stuff and you WILL leave the class with lethal weapons -- an ironclad grasp on marketing and the internet. RECOMMENDED

Neil is a great professor and really knows his stuff when it comes to marketing. As a recent alum, I can say for certain he is one of the only teachers that  gives you real world knowledge that you will use. His class is difficult but if you keep up with the work, it's completely manageable. Tough but fair when it comes to grading. A+ from me!
No Comments

Tough class. TONS of work. The final consultancy projects give you real world experience, downside is that if you are put into a group that stinks, considering the majority of your grade is based on the project, its hard to get an A.
Awesome professor. Must take if you are a business major!
great prof. tough, but everything becomes all worth it in the end.  his "5 questions" can be applied to nearly every fecet of daily life.  be ready to bleed and sweat, but the rewards are sweet.
great professor.  great experience both in the classroom and real world.

After taking 3 of his classes i must say, Neil is the best professor in the college of business and probally in the whole institution, his teaching style and method is interactive and he views him self as a facilator instead of an expert with all the answers. Take his class you will love it; you will have a ton of work and a ton of presentations.
A ton of work, A ton of presentations, A ton of projects, but at the end of the day you have absoult satisfaction with what you have learnt and achived.
Excellent Teacher and very helpful

Neil Hair is an excellent professor, absolutely no complaints.  His class is the most informative, smart lecture I've taken yet at RIT.  Sit his class if you are taking marketing and he's available. Neil is an interesting professor, but the amount of work that he assigns is way too much to do, along with your other classes.  I wouldn't mind taking him for a class, but only if he reduced the workload, because it was impossible to balance what he expected from me and my group, along with my other courses.
neil hair will run your life for 10 weeks. lots of work, but he really knows his stuff and makes class interesting.

This dude is very very british and very very intelligent - fricking awesome sense of humor, i mean if he makes fun of my inside-out clothes in class then he definitely is a sweet deal. Really knows all of his stuff so I'd reccommend him to anyone

This man's class is simply AMAZING. Highly underrated, and not a lot of people know who he is. He's British, but you get used to the accent very quickly. Plus you get to hear someone say "bloody!" in class. He is helpful, engaging, and more importantly makes you THINK in his class. Highly reccomend!
Only flaw is can't speak American. Y?

I have never taken a class that taught me so much yet felt so easy. Get in the habit of doing the work and this class will take itself. Podcasts, occasional 2 pagers, and actually interesting exams. Not easy, but interesting and the work (yes, even XC!) pays off massively in grade points and understanding. Killer course schedule, too.

The class is Leading Teams in Organizations, the professor taught the class in a very interactive way. As the name of the class says we were formed into groups to complete the course work. It is a fun and great class. The grading was non-bias and was based on the level and the amount of work that was put in.

LOTS of busy work! Had her for Leading High Performance Teams and she assigned 2 papers each week (1 by yourself and 1 with group), and a quiz. The content learned in class doesn't help much with quizzes either. She is nice, but the class requires a lot of work outside of class.

Terrible professor. Expects work to be done at a graduate level despite this being a foundation course. Work isn't hard but she won't give you an A. Unreachable outside of class and doesn't even properly answer questions. She doesn't take account for student input either and is very unforgiving in critiques. Please take any other 4D professor.

Professor Guardiola expects a lot from students, especially for a foundations, 100-level course. I personally find this course more stressful than my other 500-level courses. Her lectures are not very engaging, though she does post written instructions of demos, which is very helpful.

Lam is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about Matsci. She can sometimes be rude if you ask for help but you'll get your questions answered if you can put up with that. The Matsci curriculum is all over the place and most of the information on the slides isn't tested. Pretty harsh grader.

Had to retake MECE 320, took it with Lam in my second go around and she was one of the best professors I had at RIT. She is always available out of normal class hours for help and truly wants to see her students succeed if they put the time in. I recommend her 110% for systems.

Lam is a decent option for system dynamics, but Chirico/Kennard might be better. Two downsides are that she can grade rather harshly and be somewhat stubborn about things. Overall, she is an understanding person though. She conveys the course material clearly and knows her stuff. Most of my troubles with systems came from the class being at 8 am...

Doctor Lam-Anderson was extremely tough. I didn't have a great experience with her teaching style. She got some of the material across, but I had to consult with other professors and the TA often because I didn't find her office hours effective. She was also fairly rude in lecture, and my experience in this class made me dread system dynamics.

MECE211 with her was tough. She has a coach-like teaching style. She will not blatantly provide you with an answer, you have to work for it. However, I feel I learned way more this way. Overall a great professor, although can seem intimidating. Make sure you pick a good partner for class, or else projects will be difficult.

Does not work through the homework with the students compared to other professors. This is more difficult than others, but if you work with others on homework it is not bad, and I believe I have learned more this way.

This is the second class I had Professor Lam for. Systems is definitely not the easiest class in the program so I was STRUGGLING in the beginning of the semester. I decided to start going to office hours to learn the material more and Lam helped me raise my grade by more than 30%.
Lam is one of my favorite professors. She is very accessible for outside of class hours and willing to help understand material.

The curriculum for matsci at RIT is a bit of a mess, with powerpoint lectures that are packed with information, a lot of which is not tested on. That being said, Dr. Lam does everything in her power to make taking this drag of a class as enjoyable as possible. Exam contents are clearly outlined and easy if you at least attempt the homeworks/quizzes

Dr. Lam is a great choice for systems. It is not an easy class, but she makes it as enjoyable as possible. She is very good at helping with assignments, as she helps point you in the right direction without completely giving answers away.  The exams are not easy, but they're doable if you at least attempt the homework sets (which are optional).

Not a terrible prof, but goes off on random tangents a lot. We spend most of the latter half of the semester watching 240p youtube videos of Indian guys making bowls or something. Do the homework, you'll pass no problem, concepts are very basic. Lectures are just sporadic and not consistent with tests (which are 85% of final grade).

comment: Homework was optional, but encouraged. Answers were never simply given for the labs, but guidance was; instead of telling us what to do, she taught us how to think about it which is far more useful.

She speeds through a ton of material in lectures and goes through few in-class problems. It's hard to understand what lecture material is on the exams, but if you do the optional homeworks, you will pass. She definitely knows what she's talking about, but it can be hard sometimes learning at her pace.

Professor Lam is overall a good professor. Her video lectures often left out the small details needed to gain a full understanding of the topic however she was more than willing to explain things in-person and was very helpful. Beware though, she can be a tough grader, especially for the small things such as layout in A3 reports.

Dr. Lam knows what she is teaching. She is very understanding and she wants to help all of her students succeed. She is transparent when it comes to changes being made to the course, and she is very helpful when asked questions. The workload was very reasonable and as long as you pay attention in class, the assignments were very simple to complete.

I haven't had Dr. Lam before, but she's been amazing at handling things during this pandemic. Often course requirements could change, but she always let us know in class and changed things online to match. She's a great professor and I would definitely take another class from her, especially a lab.

All the pre-2016 reviews drag her rating down. She's a wonderful professor that wants you to understand the material and do well. She makes expectations clear and doesn't like compromising on them. However, if like me you missed a quiz or two and taking them would bump you up a few percentage points, just ask and she'll probably open them back up.
I don't understand why Dr. Lam is rated as only a 3.1! She's wonderful. Very caring and understanding.
Best materials science teacher at RIT. Take the class with her and not with someone else.

System dynamics was a class that doesn't teach usable material. What we learn is like a prereq for classes such as controls. Nonetheless I enjoyed the methodical methods of it all. Lam is a good teacher, she does care but is sometimes a bit passive-aggressive.  They have some weird pet peeves on how you must do problems which I disagree with.
Her teaching style is effective without taking up a lot of your time.  Tests are most important so study up for those.  I've had her for a few classes and she has always been great.

This honors class has many guest lecturers who are very interesting. However the professors in charge, Lam is the main professor, did not have a very good course plan. There are a couple group projects which aren't horrible but everything they assign is extremely unclear.

Really easy class and enjoyable too. She puts all the material on mycourses so you don't have to take notes but just follow along with the slides. Homework isn't required but definitely do it and you'll ace the test. Solutions to homework are posted too so you can check your answers. Knows what she's talking about and makes the material interesting

Only homework. Kinda long but super easy if she manages to explain literally anything during class. Doesn't care about anything. Can't answer simple ?'s. Examples are worthless. Project is easy. Easy A but you won't learn anything at all. DON'T BUY THE BOOK! You can't sell it back and it's worthless.

Teaches the CAD portion for 104. Very straight forward with material. Doesnt make it interesting and often times I would fall asleep during the 45 minutes I was there. Knows CAD well, but sometimes had to ask the TA why something wasnt working. Average overall. Rubrics for weekly HW are posted with clear cut instructions

She rushes the lecture, can be hard to follow, if you miss a step she is done by the time you get help from the TA. Even when she is doing nothing she won't help you she will just call a TA over. Grading sucks. Being a CAD class, you can draw something any number of ways. If you don't draw with the method they want you lose points(same end product)
Class was easy, just show up and you've got an A. Group projects weren't bad, but don't expect any clear directions on them.

Lam knows a LOT about Materials Science. Her lectures seem very long and cover a TON of material that you wont need to know. The content on the tests are 90% from the homework, which I don't think she makes very clear. Do the homework (even though it is optional) and you will do well on the tests. Course was fairly well organized but dull sometimes

She opens the class with any questions, which is helpful. She goes over the EXACT problems that appear on the quizzes. She uses powerpoints, videos, graphs and images to illustrate the topic. She teaches everything with powerpoints in class. She does example problems, but they can be difficult to follow. Some lectures are extremely interesting, but these are infrequent. The class is relatively easy, but if you don't understand a problem you need to use the book to figure it out because there aren't any worked out problems in the notes.

Very confusing and lectures are rushed.  She basically reads facts all class. She rarely uses examples and when she does they are hard to follow. The textbook is where you can try to actually learn the material. If you can get somebody else, do it.
Terrible,just not clear.  Very confusing when teaching and does not provide any examples to clarify concepts.  Tends to ramble

She's not that bad. Explains the material effectively and demonstrates a good understanding of the software despite it being her first time using it. She can be ambivalent at times about what she expects, but when she does help you, she will do so to the fullest of her ability. Definitely not a bad teacher
By far the easiest grader I have ever seen. Lectures are interesting and informative. Lets you know exactly what will be on exams which are basically copies of the quizzes. Would highly recommend.

Rushes through lectures, doesn't care if students fall behind, makes TAs do most of the work, tests/quizzes are on things not discussed in class, expects you to know as much as she does. Avoid if possible

The lectures were almost intolerable to sit through. Too much information is covered with very little structure or explanation. She teaches as if it's all common sense and there's no depth to the material. Don't expect to learn much on the subject, if anything. The tests focus on problems with little relevance to the lectures.

Great professor. If your grade is borderline in the end she takes everything into consideration and may raise the grade. He lectures are just basic and sometimes confusing, however she is very helpful during office hours.

Lectures on the most general concepts in the course, while the tests cover the tiniest most inconsequential details. Grades extremely harshly and absolutely does not care about students falling behind as she moves over material faster than Speedy Gonzales. Obviously an expert in her field and expects you to be too. Recommend avoiding her class,

Materials Science:  Her lectures consisted of powerpoint slides and were focused on what to know to pass the tests.  The material that she teaches does not seem to be important for anything other than the tests however which was unfortunate.  The lectures were not particularly engaging however.  Fairly average teacher.

Liked the class a lot. sometimes things are unclear simply because class demos are rushed, but there were 4 TA's who constantly helped everyone out. I had a great time and did pretty well. if you try, you will succeed.

I enjoyed her in class a lot.  She explained everything well and if you were confused it was easy to ask her on the breaks.  She didn't test on things that the class did not cover and gave equations and hints for things that we should have already learned.

Prof. Lam-Anderson is new to RIT, and I had her for her first two quarters. She was still adjusting, albeit, but her class was still extraordinarily difficult. this teacher not only knows her material but is genuinely interested and concerned with her students well being.  She may be unclear at times in class, but she cleans that up in her office hours.  Also she is always giving independent study classes.  We need more marcas in the mechie department.
nice smile, but...
does she know her stuff?  hmmmmm.
Bad teacher/Easy grader:  I got an A, but have no knowledge of the subject.  Unprofessional:  She's grinding the same axe as Dean Baum, and it comes through a little too often.
marca, marca, marca.
basis of argument not founded by basic laws of thermodynamics and explanations are way too simplistic to even comprehend the true essense of materials science....... bad....

Sometimes seems to have more memorized knowledge than actual knowledge.  Often is unclear in describing.  Will, however, help outside of class and will continue to try to explain something until it makes sense.
Great prof., Class is easy as long as you go to class and do the homework. The material can get tough, but she makes it easy to learn
I like tall chicks

Professor Yenisey is the absolute GOAT. He is the best professor I have ever had as he effortlessly explains the material in the class flawlessly which anyone could understand. He is also very understanding and understands that students have things going on outside of his classroom which makes him very lenient for being absent. 10/10 Professor

Positively delightful teacher! Always kind and always helpful. He's a patient, soft-spoken man who never makes you feel judged in any way, even if your question is a little dumb. The grading is fair and the feedback is useful. Also when asked what his favorite dinosaur was, he said it was Brachiosaurus.

Very kind professor that will help you in any way possible when you reach out to him for help. His grading  motivates me to want to do better since it gives me more opportunity to try and do better the next time. Would take again, and again.

This professor really wanted his students to succeed and was very accessible outside of class. Would always explain everything in detail and make content easy to understand. Would definitely take again!

Yenisey is an amazing professor, he's easygoing and if you are going to be absent, email him and he will mark you present. Very lenient for quizzes and exams, and his grading is very fair, to say the least. Although he is soft-spoken, he is very kind and cares for his students. I would want him to teach every one of my math classes.

Professor Yenisey is awesome. The only downside is that he is a little quiet at times but otherwise he is great in all aspects. If you need individual help he will help you until you understand clearly. Good with words. Best calc teacher i've had.

Professor Yenisey is soft-spoken and the lectures can be hard to keep up with but he is very considerate and helpful in and outside of class having lots of office time where he sits down and explains the problems thoroughly.

Took some time to get use to his monotone accent heavy voice, but thankfully I am used to monotone math teachers. He wrote the lectures on the whiteboard and would stop if he is going fast or to answer any questions. He was easily available outside of class. The grades were quizzes, tests, and online hw. Mehmet was a fantastic professor. I would 100% recommend having him. He doesn't use the textbook in class all that much but encourages you to reference it for some things. He's very helpful one on one and you can tell he wants to make sure that every one of his students succeeds. Make sure you pay attention in lecture or you will get lost.
He started off the semester by assigning a lot of long papers, then stopped after the first two. He retired last spring and he threw our class a pizza party. Super funny chill dude

I took Intro to Management with Dr. Luxmore at SUNY Oswego. I remember him talking a lot and being very strict, but fair. I learned a lot from him about how companies are run, and would take another class with him if I needed to.

But when you submit your paper, he will keep telling you that it's not what he wants. And he will interrupt you when you ask questions.  If you want a good GPA, then don't take his class.

The tests are all written response. This may be daunting at first, but test questions are easy to guess. They are the main points of the chapters. He also tries to give away many points for the tests. The group project is long and daunting. Here is where points start dropping. Sometimes seems like he takes off additional points here. No textbook.

Professor Luxmore is a great guy. Nice person, very knowledgeable. But, his lectures are so boring I can't pay attention. Tests really aren't that bad. He doesn't have a syllabus so homework assignments are often and random but don't take too much time.

He sets you up for failure. He has no course schedule, no homework schedule and no exam schedule. He is extremely rude to students outside of class and he will belittle you for not knowing something. His slide are not helpful and he is by far the most unorganized professor at RIT (Just go visit his office and you'll know how unstructured he is)

Takes off a ridiculous amount of points for any classes missed but lectures are boring and pointless. Don't ask questions that go off script, actually just don't ask questions, he doesn't like it. comment: He is a great professor to have had a 3 hour class with. comment: Had this professor for an 8 am last semester, and it was so frustrating to wake up so early to only come to class to watch a movie or read an article and work on it on your own. We had a paper every week, and he took points off for no clear reason. I felt like we were doing most of the work on our own. The only positive of this class is no tests.

He's a nice guy, BUT you will have a paper or 2 every week with him. These papers also do not have clear due-dates or instructions. comment: Boring lectures. He almost always gives the same example (of Toyota) to explain every business term. He tells you to redo papers for extra credit but when you do it and give it to him, he will tell you that correcting that paper is last priority for him because it is extra credit. He forgets to correct or revaluate papers. Keep reminding him.

He is a great professor who tells his life stories to the class which makes it less boring. When it comes to tests, he does give many bonus questions. Also, his teaching style good but doesn't follow his power point slides in order which can be annoying. He isn't a strict grader and is willing to fix if you find a mistake in your work.

He's a great guy and fun professor in class. This class is structured to be very writing intensive. Basically you get a group fro the year and have to write 6 15-page papers. He grades tough at the beginning but eases up once you get into it. Frustrating because you don't always have the time to check over what your group members wrote.

The Professor  is a great funny guy,with clear cut lectures and expectations. Being in a 3 hour class, his lectures are long, but he usually keeps them entertaining with one of his classic childhood stories about Canada. Tests are not that hard as long as you study, also he gives bonus points. He will take off lots of points for missing class.
Good guy, very helpful always has time for his students.

He's a cool guy, don't be a dumb ass and you'll do fine.  Makes the class interesting even when it's not.  Don't buy the text book I haven't looked in it once.  Only difficult part is he when tests come around you better have studied well.  If there's 3 chapters on the test he does, though he'll never admit it, make 75% of the test from 1 chapter.

Lectures are boring but he is always willing to help even in times other than his designated office hours. Gives study guides for tests and homeworks are not very difficult with ample time to to them.
All he does is lecture. Very boring and tests are very hard and worth a lot.

In class lectures can be a little boring, although I didn't have much interest in the topic to begin with. He is surprisingly helpful and will spend significant amounts of time in class or afterwards to ensure he can help students. Group projects require a lot of time each week, but grading is relatively easy.

Tests are straight out of the summary in each chapter, no joke. Group project was the toughest aspect, but he gives you plenty of opportunities to correct/extra credit. Overall very helpful if you go to his office.

Extremely boring to listen to.  He tells a lot of stories relating to the topics, but really is very ineffective teaching you the course material.  Nice guy, just wouldn't recommend taking his class unless you like to listen to lectures for 2 hours straight.

Very helpful. ALWAYS in office for questions. Plenty of chances to re-write papers for better grade. Friendly and knowledgeable. Posts materials ahead of time on mycourses. Almost no homework besides quarterly group project (broken down into small pieces). Fair grader, relevant tests, should get good grade with normal studying. Overall - awesome!

Good professor and very fair. Definitely knowledgeable and helpful if you ask for it. He does, however, tend to go off on tangents and can talk for a long time. It's hard to pay attention when he does, particularly in a long night class.
Had him for Global Business. Professor was really helpful. Class isnt a cake walk though.

Told us 1st day he hasn't taught this course in years, & it shows. Did nothing for the 1st 5 weeks in terms of the project or homeworks, the last 5 weeks we have 5 milestones and 3 cases due making it almost 2 papers a week. When a question is asked, he looks at you blankly and asks you to be more specific or he will ignore you. STAY AWAY

He tries to make class interesting, you learn a lot from the class. The work he gives you sometimes takes a lot of time to do, but he is really helpful outside class. Test are reasonable, they aren't too hard.

Interesting guy, good examples and Luxmore knows his stuff forwards and backwards. Challenges you to think but you leave knowing your stuff. His project is a beast but he grades fairly. Multiple choice were difficult but is liberal with the short answers on tests. Recommend him without question. Would take a class with him in a heartbeat
great teacher, very helpful if you actually take the time to care then he is there to help you out

INTRO TO GLOBAL Class is HARD!  Class was strict lecture from power point entire class, every class.  Tests were impossible and he refused to curve the tests.  Do not take if you want a good grade.  DO NOT TAKE LUXMORE
Great teacher if you go to his office hours he is always there and very helpful

His class is pretty easy. Lectures are somewhat boring although they help a lot when you are studying for the exams. He's an understandable guy that is willing to help. Professor Meneely always finds creative ways to penalize students.

Had him for performance engineering. For once in a Software Engineering class, I didn't have to push myself to not browse Reddit during lecture. I got lost in listening in his passion for the subject. Best professor in Software Engineering by far.

Andy was a super helpful and understanding prof. Pay attention (at least most of the time), and he'll work with you if you don't understand or if you mess up.

Took performance engineering. He's great at pushing you to go further and learn more on your own. Very rewarding class if you put in the time and effort. You will not learn from just showing up to lecture. The labs are the true value of the class, take them seriously.

comment: His lectures are dry. It's difficult to follow him. A difficult grader and a difficult person in general. I wish I had taken this course with another professor.

His passion is unable to be matched (you can tell he loves security). He enjoys this course and it shows. Some aspects needed a little more planning than was given, but overall, I learned a lot in his class. It was not an easy a, but I expected that going in.

Professor Meneely did a great job with 331. He took material that would normally be considered dry or uninteresting and actually made it intriguing and his passion for the subject shows that. The projects were kind of fun. Some people don't like them only because they don't want to do the work. One side note, he very rarely replies to emails.

Meneely is superbly brilliant.  Any software topic you've got a question on, he has a realistic answer for.  He knows what's important to teach and his lectures are more organized than any other professor I've had.  He definitely cares about the success of his students too, if you try hard and seek out help, you'll do just fine.
He is a great professor, and would highly recommend him to anyone. The assignments are tough and many, but is very helpful if you go see him outside of class. Sincerely wants his students to succeed.

A great guy. Enthusiastic about security and his lectures are engaging and useful. I enjoyed coming to this class.  I did not enjoy the homework. Expectations are unclear. Be prepared to be graded like this is English class, not SE. He's always right for the things he takes off points for, but they were not laid out in the assignment.

Awesome class. The lectures are great and if you do not attend you will not pass. Available outside of class to help. There is A LOT of work in the course and he makes you work for it but is very understanding at the same time. Would definitely recommend.
Awful. Very unhelpful. Avoid at all costs. Lectures were very unorganized, obviously didn't really care about the class. Very arrogant. I got an A in the class and still loathed the experience.

Really helpful guy. Sometimes his explanations were a bit lacking (he stutters a bit when he talks, which was sometimes confusing). Always willing to help if you need it. Foster is a sweet woman, but sometimes I believe her issues with computers/online courses gets in the way. terrific

Awesome professor. Very laid back and a lot of freedom on the final paper. Great in class discussions. Great in class format overall. Grades are lenient, but also fair.
Very laid back class, lots of room for individual interpretation of the course content.

Very easy going professor. She makes the class interesting with thought provoking discussion. Participation will make this class more enjoyable. Fair grader as long as you follow the criteria. Highly recommend her.
Amazing professor. Really helpful and a pretty easy class. All assignments have really loose topics and are relatively short. Highly recommend her.
Make writing seminar fun. What else can you say. Grades most assignments on completion. You can show up late with no penalty.

comment: If you can't get to class on time, this guy's not for you. He'll make you stand in front of the class, explain, and apologize. Didn't happen to me, but happened to a lot of other people. Lectures have a nice theme every week but once the anecdotal story is over it gets dry. Exams are tough. Nice guy in general, but can be rude. Don't recommend.
Bad teaching skills.

Puts all notes and lectures online. His tests can sometimes be extremely difficult due to the fact that its required to memorize an entire program from a lab and write it by hand.  Sometimes can be misleading during labs and is very hesitant to help you. Google is your friend here. Required essay (whole semester to do it) and grades rather harsh.

You have to read the assignment sheets to understand what the written assignments are all about.  The final group assigment allowed us to be creative, but it was hard with 3 other people on the team.  Liked the two tests being only 30% of the total grade.

He likes creative critical thinking, and this makes some of the assignments difficult.  Assignments have a sheet on what it is all about, yet there seems to be a wide range on what is acceptable.  Liked the open book tests, but they were not easy.
The grading and assignment requirements are so unclear, it is nearly impossible to know what to do for his papers.  His feedback is completely useless, and every assignment is an absolute crapshoot.

On the plus side he likes to mix it up with guests and videos. Unfortunately, he changes his mind on what he's looking for constantly - even changing requirements after the submission date. He says it's to "separate the As from the Bs from the Cs." What he says and what he means are often two totally different things.
Liked the mix of special speakers, videos, and discussions.  Some assignments were hard, because of lack of clear outline and wanted creative answers.

Took course online. Textbook was necessary. Participation was mandatory for online group discussions. Needed to post more than 5 times a week. The topics for the 3 papers are very vague, while the long length required is not. Tests were held online and were open book. Additional paper and reading on "The Goal."

His assignments are the most vague, incohesive things I have ever laid eyes on. I generally cruised through my entire college career getting As and Bs, and this guy just gave me a 50% on my last paper. No clue what he's looking for and his feedback doesn't help.

Professor Traub is a nice and knowledgeable guy. While I think he enjoys the subject his class was to lecture heavy, and lectures were just powerpoints from the book publisher. He did bring in two great speakers however which aided the learning experience.
He's amazing teacher. He's sweet and very good with deaf people. He will make sure that deaf people understand it clearly. He also believes in giving deaf people an hour extra for exam. He's awesome.
Professor Traub is a great professor he is interested in his students learning and is helpful.

If you come to class it's an easy grade. Open book/notes midterm and final. Essays can be a bit complicated and hard to understand what he's looking for, but hes willing to clarify if you go for help. Overall not a bad teacher.

WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! I could teach the class to myself. It was pointless to go AT ALL! Tests are open note open book and pretty much a joke. Take this professor if you want an easy A and to be annoyed for 10 weeks

Alright teacher, not real clear on expectations, and brings in graduate level professors to grade the undergrad presentations. Brings in local business leaders.
Great Professor.  Brings a lot of industry knowledge into the classroom!

Professor Wood is lovely and the class is very low pressure. Do the work and attend classes because they're fun, and you'll be fine. He doesn't give feedback right away so you can enjoy the writing process, but when he does it's very detailed and helpful.

Really nice and funny guy. Not too much reading, and he shared some really good short stories with us. Grade is based off a few writing assignments and a cumulative portfolio, neither of which were very demanding.

Chill professor but be ready to receive homework on the first day!

His power points are completely useless. I got SO lost, especially because on mycourses, they are in a different order than he presents. Some aren't even there! Easier to just keep up with the reading by yourself in the book. Recitation n tests are HARD, REALLY hard, but he does let u use a cheat sheet. but it's week 3 so we;ll see haha

Monotone voice and boring lectures but overall nice guy. Drops the lowest test grade which is nice because his tests are damn near impossible. The online HWs are difficult too-- super finicky about your answers and usually cover things we haven't even learned yet.

Dr. Langner is very willing to help.  I think this class was very difficult and I struggled through the entire thing.  The school should have a pre-req for someone who has never taken chemistry.  I am hoping the next 2 sections get better!!  From what I have been told, if you have to take this class Dr. Langner is the one to get.

He is an excellent teacher who never gives up on any students so long as a student is willing to work hard. His lectures are difficult to comprehend if you do not have the background but overall he is a great teacher and wonderful person. The amount of material you learn outside the class if you can find him is enough to pass the class very easily.

Great teacher... if you go to class. Make sure to read the book and study the quizzes during the week (online) for the tests (most questions are similar to these) Go to class too, because about 1/3 of the questions come directly from lecture. Good teacher if you go to class.
Excellent lectures! Organized and a great sense of humor! He is dedicated and willing to help me achieve a clear understandign of the subject matter.

Boring as hell, need to work on his presentation, but a nice guy.
Nice as he is, he's also pretty boring and the subject's pretty difficult.  I also find that he's not very good at explaining things in class. =/

Nice guy. I slept through a test and he let me take it after he said no retakes. if you're not a morning person there is a lot of catching up and outside work involved. he's def. a monotone. test's were fair.
a good teacher overall, could work on his voice, very monotone, and explain things a little bit clearly.
Dito on the last entry. Monotone @ 8am...not good. But a great teacher sometime in the afternoon. Record lectures and listen to them later if your not a morning person.

this teacher is very good. he's really care about the students progress and really able to help you. i love this teacher

awesome teacher, I love how he teaches and paces the course for us all to better understand!

Professor Gordon made this class so enjoyable with fun lectures, reasonable work, clear grading. Awesome class and professor!

What a wonderful professor and woman, and an interesting class to boot! great class, thank you
His class is incredibly useful and he genuinely cares that his students learn. Always willing to help if you come to him too.
His classes are among the most useful at RIT, and teach more than what any student expects to get out of the class.  As a photo student, you can't afford to miss a chance to take him.
Very nice guy.  Knows the course material very well.  Is slow with grading and can move a little fast over some subjects.  Answers questions in class readily and is very approchable.

Professor knows what he is talking about. Easy going, and is helpful as long as you ask questions. Only down side to his course is that he is slow with grading. Other than the grading, I have no problem taking other classes with him.

great guy, teaching is ok. he is very lenient with grades, but never got ANY until last couple weeks so you never know how you are. lectures had NOTHING to do with labs nor did labs to tests or tests to lecture, just really sloppy jumbled class/lab/test material although most of it is departmental wide stuff so not sure how much was his fault

This man is full of himself. He loves to overly explain useless parts of the lecture slides (which he rarely follows) to demonstrate his knowledge of the subject. Exam questions were always a shocker; he never prepared us for them because he was too busy drawing on the whiteboard. Asks obnoxiously specific questions in class. Just useless and awful

I think he did a very good job at allowing Cyber Self Defense class to drive itself with the discussions brought about in class.  No textbook, fair grader and very approachable.  Show up to class, do the little work required, and get an easy A.

Good guy, but not a good professor. Teaches off of a pre-made powerpoint, asks tons of hypothetical and rhetorical questions, and then doesn't explain himself. Overall, did a bad job at explaining the course material.

Giving a lot of lectures but homework not much. Participation doesn't really matter but can make up for it by some submission the professor can offer. Very sweet and motivating professor if you love politics, criminal justice, society.

Wonderful Professor, she was very well knowledge in her field. Reading the textbook was required as classes supplemented the readings meaning you had to do the homework AND attend class. She is a very nice person, but a poor teacher. She contradicts herself. Her power points and reviews aren't descriptive. Took the Auditing course with Dr Dey. She was great and the course was amazing. I learned so much about auditing and how auditors look at companies. I highly recommend this course with Dr Dey. She is great and the course has been very helpful.

Dr. Dey is a high quality instructor.  She is an expert in the field of auditing and is concerned that her students learn the material. Furthermore, she makes the class enjoyable by bringing in guest speakers to discuss accounting careers.
The professor really cares. She is passionate about what she does and really learn from her class. She also brings in professionals and you learn a lot about auditing.

Took prior accounting classes with another prof because he was recommended, but Dey was so much better! I got lower grades with the other prof and found that he was difficult to follow. Dey is very straight forward, and her interactive notes were lifesavers on her open book quizzes and tests!

take her, she's knowledgeable. don't expect lots of clip art and cute animations in the slides, she is an accountant she just does black and white straight INFO no fancy graphics. also she doesn't grade HW so you better do damn well on the weekly quizzes...

Prof Dey is pretty laid back and she knows her topic extremely well. She gives extra credit on the test, and she does half online and half in class for quizzes and test. The quizzes are open book open note. Easy to get a good grade if you attend class and fill out the powerpoint notes packet she provides. I would suggest you take her for managerial

no HW only quizzes, online quizzes and exams none of which can be retaken. online quizzes are tricky as heck. you can take in class quizzes home and return next class but they will be graded out of 40 instead of 50. quizzes are open book. i wish there was more HW so my whole grade didn't depend on tests, i suck at ACC so i am nervous as it is...
