Her class was very difficult, but she definitely knows what she's talking about. I was really struggling but I went to her office hours every week, and that really helped.  the second test was much easier than the first which was terrible.  I didn't like the online homework system we used because there were flaws, but the practice really helped.
She's nice, but kind of confusing.  The first test was hard, but the 2nd test and final weren't bad.  HW was online and annoying, but she was lenient with it if you made an effort.
She made the material more complicated than it needed to be, how ever she was nice an fair.

She is a good professor.  Clean notes and explanations.  If you do the HW, you will do fine on the tests.  Some of the test questions come right off the HW assignments.  She is always willing to help if you don't understand.  Recommend!
Fluid Mechanics:  He sets an easy pace and is easy to understand.  Tests focus on core principals rather than anything abstract.  Easy to get along with.  Would highly recommend.
Mechanics of Materials:  Dr. Gee is very good at teaching the material.  He is easy to get hold of outside of class and is eager to offer help.

Nice guy, but not the greatest professor. Likes to repeat himself a lot and his notes can be pretty disorganized.  He would always rush at the end which would make everything even more confusing. You really need to read the book if you want to learn the material and do well on the tests.  I wouldn't take him again.

Great guy, writes really fast, OK at getting the material accross, He really wants you to do the HW. Tests were hard - he really wants to make you think - test questions weren't necessarilly like HW..he really stretched it. It was personally a very challenging class for me, got a C
Great professor. Kept me awake by going through the material quickly and precisely. I am taking him again for Fluids. His tests were fairly easy but I took him when it wasn't common core tests.

Anton was a great professor. The class grade was 70% homeworks which were similar to the class problem sets. The midterm was take home and the final was a project. He cares a lot about his students and is accessible through email and office hours. The in class content is heavy and his lectures are at times slightly confusing to follow along to.

Anton was a wonderful professor. He was always ready to help in office hours if need be. Most of your grade comes from homework, which was nice. Homeworks were interesting! I would for sure take a class with Anton again.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Anton is a great professor. Most of the grade is homeworks, he encourages the use of external help, and will help you generously if you go to his office hours. I would take him again. From what I hear he had a rough start to teaching as he was relatively new but he has now gotten the reins and is great.

Overall very  professor! wants to help you and is very accessable in office hours. Homeworks are a good part of your grade but if you understand the material you are good. Midterm was online which was nice but also if it was in person you would have been fine. Final grade is mostly from homeworks and there is one final project ( 2 options u do 1 ).

Overall, nice professor, wants to help you understand the topics.  Homeworks were straight forward and usually interesting.  As long as you regularly attend class and listen to the lectures you will learn a lot.  Mid term was take home which was nice.  Final grade is mostly from homeworks.

It's clear he knows what he's talking and passionate about the course material, but he is an awful teacher. Very difficult to understand due to his accent, does not lay out the subject matter in a logical way, and doesn't answer questions succinctly. I would recommend you avoid his Machine Learning class at all costs.

Prof. Selitsky's class was not what I expected at all. His teaching method was underwhelming and disappointing. If you're repeating the class, then I guess his class is for you, but otherwise, I would not recommend it for a first-timer. Again, I wholeheartedly believe he wants the best for his students but he is not fit for his position.

It's really hard to understand his lectures, it seems like it's his first time teaching this class, however, he never prepares the contents before he teaches us, whenever he pulls out a slide, it's like his first time ever seeing the slide. While he is teaching, he kept looking at his TA for guidance. He's a good guy, but just not a good professor.

Selitskiy demonstrates genuine concern for students, yet spends lectures not going over what's on quizzes or even upcoming labs/assignments. He can be hard to communicate with when you have problems, but I ended up figuring out assignments myself using notes and google. Watch out for written exams, they end up having stuff you wouldn't consider.

Was difficult to understand his lectures, and the materials didn't seem like they were created by him. You learn a lot more from the TA recitations than you do during his lectures so just listen to those and go to SI sessions and you should be fine

Does not seem to know the material as I would normally dismiss his forgettfulness, he was using chatgpt and having multiple tabs of it open while teaching to remind him. I do not think he made the material/ slides himself and I would also go as far as to say that he does little to hand check and review assignments. Very hard to contact.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Test heavy']

comment: This guy does not have the best teaching style in terms of getting material across. I think he just kind of rolls with each lesson as it comes. But honestly, he made me want to come to class because he has such a good vibe. In the end, make sure to pay attention to recitation and review slides before class and you should do okay.

It feels like Prof Selitskiy is out of his element teaching. He often is forgetful during lectures which slows everything down. Many concepts are explained at surface level and then you are expected to know how to implement them in more complex scenarios. Pick a different professor if you're able.

This professor completely fails in conveying the material required to do well in this course. When he gives his lectures, it feels as though he is looking at the PowerPoint slides for the first time, and he tends to speed through them because he doesn't feel like teaching.

If you have some programming knowledge, you should be fine. If not, GL.

This is professor doesn't not take the time to explain anything. He speeds through the lectures and expects you to know things you have never learned before. Sometimes he will end lectures eraly and you feel like you barely learned anything. This is for CSCI-141.

An incredibly talented mathematician and computer scientist. He gives fascinating lectures that, sometimes, can be a little hard to follow. He's a good communicator but his Math PhD (versus CS) shows through. Overall though, once you get used to his style he really is one of the best professors I have had at this school.
Lackluster education, difficult to understand, expects you to know topics without any teaching. Completely learn Python yourself before taking the class.

Very nice and accomodating. Very passionate about what he does. The HW is most of the points, so don't skip it. Midterm I found pretty difficult, but it's worth less than a HW. No final, only a project which is a glorified HW. Biggest issue were lectures being hard to follow, and can be a little chaotic with the class participation exercises.

Professor Selitskiy is a fun guy and seems like a genuine person. However, you don't really learn anything in class from him. Lectures are dense and hard to understand, he's a math PhD and teaches like one. expect a bottom up approach. Its hard to synthesize concepts. Study groups are a must in this class (HW is 77%). But office hours are helpful.
always good feedback, ty

Forest was an excellent professor, really knew his stuff and brought a lot of real world knowledge and experience to the classroom. Critiques were fun and insightful. The working photographers are always the best teachers, Forest is a good example of this. Sadly Forest was adjunct and only taught for two quarters, I hope he comes back.
Literally the nicest person in the world. Gives off Hannah Gadsby vibes with her comedy during class. Super knowledgeable and caring, would 10000% recommend
Lorraine makes this class very easy but still keeps it interesting. She's very enthusiastic during lectures and tasting.
Great and entertaining lectures. Informative if you listen, but it is definitely possible to pass the class if you don't pay attention. Light on assignments, but not a fast grader.

Lorraine is a wonderful lecturer and a great person.  She loves what she teaches, and it makes you love it too.  She is VERY well qualified, and it shows.  Don't buy the textbook ahead of time, it will likely be included in the lab fee.

Attending class felt like going to a comedy show. I could listen to Lorraine for hours. She made everything interesting and easy to learn. If there was one thing I didn't like about the class, it would be that we had to pay over $50 for the online textbook that Lorraine wrote to be able to take the mandatory quizzes.

Really, really nice and understanding person, just not a good professor. Is not accessible outside of class, does not post grades until the end of the semester, and is unclear about assignments. I definitely recommend her but warn you about this.
Everyone loves Lorraine. shes a riot. The class is fun, not too much work and very informative. I highly suggest both this class and professor.

Great class & great professor. She's very animated and this class won't bore you. She suggests a textbook written by herself. I bought it and I know of a few others who hadn't... and I became very annoyed by people asking to borrow it. Theres only two exams, midterm and final, and a final project that you will absolutely get an A on. STUDY

Incredible teacher- she knows what she's talking about and LOVES it, and it shows. She inspired a passion in me through being funny, caring, and most of all, understanding. Impressed with the way she structured the class, and how she gave students no opportunity other than to pass. LOVE her.
nice class. Around 6 types of wineclass
Very good prof. Keeps you interested all class (plus you drink wine). Learned a lot. Looked forward to every class. Highly recommend.

Hems is an amazing teacher and makes the class fun and interesting. WOW II is a little more advanced then WOW 1 and focuses more on the specifics but still introduces you to new things. Attendance is optional but you're own loss if you don't and drink the wine. midterm and final are only 45% which allows you to still do well overall

Lorraine is my favorite teacher that I have had. She is very knowledgeable and keeps you interested in the material. Very energetic and positive. Does not take attendance, but coming to class will help on the tests.
One of the best Hospitality professors in the department. Extremely fun, and will keep you laughing. Class is extremely easy as well!
took lorraine for wow 1, wow 2, and beverage fermentation and distillation
Great professor, extremely knowledgeable on the subject matter, you will learn A LOT about wine. Makes the class very enjoyable and something to look forward to every week. Highly recommended!

Focuses a lot on lecture material and gives A LOT of reading, then proceeds to give super heavy exams throughout the semester that include things from outside the material but relating to the topic, so also expect to have to read online to score well on his tests. He's a little flexible if he's in a good mood, but usually expect hardship with him.
cant really understand what he is saying, thick accent and slow teaching style, lectures are legit the most boring i've ever seen, save urself and dont take his class

Overall really nice old man with funny grandpa vibes, but lectures are incredibly boring and it's hard to understand his accent. Very kind and understanding for the most part. While exams could be difficult, he was very lenient on the grading (especially for more open ended questions).
He was not in many lectures, but it was fun to learn the math perspective behind the cryptosystems for some of the topics.

I would never take this professor. Exams are worth a lot, and it is EXTREMELY unclear what will be on them. Expect things that were briefly covered in class to be worth a large part of the exam. He is very smart and knows the subject, but he doesn't teach well. He will teach everything about something but give no examples or practice problems.

Exams are worth a TON of your grade and are not straightforward. Expect random minor things covered for 2 minutes in lecture to be worth between 20-30% of each exam grade. If you don't study, you won't pass. Homework is hard but completely manageable if you stay on top of it. You do learn a LOT from lectures and dude is usually super chill!

Very knowledgeable but not so good at explaining concepts. Long, slightly disorganized lectures. He is very accessible and helpful outside class and polite, explains solutions very nicely on white boards. Easy-going exams with cheat sheets allowed.

I had the unfortunate experience of having Professor Radziszowski as an instructor. He was not only very rude to students when we needed a little more help, he was often innapropriate with how he handled conversations. He would make creepy remarks that no professor should make. This is all on top of him being a rediculously hard grader.

As respectful as I could possibly be, Professor Radziszowski was just awful. With all due respect, after all these years at RIT, he is by far the worst professor I have had. He is clearly very intelligent on the subject of Cryptography, but his abiility to teach is terrible. The fact he continues to teach at such a prestigous school is beyond me.

Had him for cryptography. On the one hand, he clearly loves this subject and is enthusiastic to teach it. On the other hand, several times during class when explaining new concepts he would skip over crucial steps, leaving you to try to put the pieces together in your head. He assumes you know what he knows to often.
Poor organization for unstructured 761 class. Lectures are dense and topics are not explained well.

No programming projects, rather the exams are used to gauge your understanding of the material. Highly recommended that you take MATH-371 (Number Theory) before taking this course because it is so theoretical. The professor is indeed a genius, but not necessarily the best at teaching.
Stazek might be the smartest person I've ever met. He can be hard to follow sometimes, but if you go to office hours he will make sure you understand.

The bonus is that you see a working mathematician/computer scientist in action. He succeeds in demystifying some concepts. What I'd change with the class: Assign specific pages to be read before class, then spend valuable class time by solving problems. Unfortunately, I still haven't developed the intuition behind algorithm design.

He taught me Algorithms. He made his classes so boring by only focusing on the theoretical parts and not indulging in any programming or algorithm development part. All his exam and homework questions are like that. Too much theory, very little fun.

Extremely intelligent, always willing to help if anything is unclear. Assignments and exams can be very difficult, but they are appropriate for the course. Definitely my favorite professor in the CS department.
It was honor for me to take his classes. He really loves wht he is doing. Lectures are very interesting and inspiring. Great professor!
Had him for Cryptography. He was impossible to understand and not good at answering Questions.

Lectures were always a pleasure to attend: he has a very warm and friendly demeanor, is skilled in presenting complex concepts in an accessible manner, and has a profound understanding of the material he was teaching (CS Theory.)  Constantly made an effort to remain aware of the level of comprehension of the class and adjust accordingly. Great prof

Awesome with a side of awesomesauce. Staggering amount of crypto and math knowledge. He has an accent, but isn't difficult to understand. Grades hard, but curves a lot. For example, I got a 40% on the midterm and a B in the class. Don't be discouraged by the grades - he knows the material can be difficult. Do the work and you'll be fine.
Awesome professor. He's really excited about what he teaches and is more than willing to help if you don't understand something. Class is pretty tough, but you really learn the material well.
Tough tough professor, but couldn't be a nicer guy.  Wants you to learn and is willing to go the extra mile to see that you do.

Seemed like a realy hard, strict guy, but he's really great.  Has an effective teaching style, and is always fair.  He even has a sense of humor.  If you can make a class like foundations of cs theory interesting, you got to be good.

Chaim Sanders is the most condescending professor that I have ever had. He's pretentious, gives difficult assignments, and doesn't help students or teach the content of homework in the slightest. Any review that gave him above 2 stars is either flat out lying, or Chaim himself giving himself a review. The school literally fired him. AVOID HIM.

Expect to spend on this class as much as you spend on all of your other classes combined. I questioned whether or not he knew he was not the only class of the semester due to the amount of load he threw on us. Secondary to your main assignment, you'll be spending the majority of your time learning how to use tools that are not taught in this class

His class is taught entirely through videos and labs, the tests have nothing to do with the videos, half the time the labs don't either, and he's extremely hard to get a hold of on top of all of that. Even when you manage that miracle, he tends to not be especially helpful. On top of that his custom site for the class is broken as all get out..

If I could rate this prof a 0 I would. They are terrible at responding, you might hear back in an hour or you might hear back in a week. The lecture videos are old and outdated. The assignments require knowledge of tools that are not taught in the class (or any of the prerequisite classes). Most people have to retake the class at least once.

Chaim is by far the least organized professor I've ever had. He is almost never accessible via Slack, the website that is necessary for homework is often down (it's his own site) and his lecture videos are rarely helpful for doing the homeworks. He even forgot to give my class the password for our final! Definitely avoid Chaim at all costs.

Learn the LAMP stack before taking this class and you wont have any issues. Learn Docker (and docker compose) as well, and the class will be a breeze. If you know nothing about web technologies, this class will be incredibly hard.

Chaim was nice to me and always went above and beyond to answer my questions. That said, the class is so poorly organized that he forgets his own deadlines, is often unavailable via Slack, and makes you teach yourself the material. Homeworks and project can be hard if you don't have the background - start early!
Doesn't teach class material.

The material is decent but the way he plans out the workload is terrible. You have to figure out a lot on your own. A LOT. He puts us under so much stress that it's hard to learn or enjoy the content.
He made me feel so inferior to him, I decided to change my major.

The homework and project are a little bit messy but if you spend enough time with it, you'll figure it out. This is an online class so you will need to really motivate yourself to work on stuffs, or else you will get dumped with it along the semester. Although Chaim is a little bit harsh, I can say that I've learned a lot after this class.

This man is the saving grace for the Computing Security department. Passionate and devoted to making quality security education available for students. I strongly advise as many classes with him that you can.

Lectures are interesting and consist of lots of tangents. Very meticulous grader but you know exactly where to improve. If you are offended by profanity take someone else. Frequently available outside class for help and advice. Workload for the course wasn't too bad, but other classes with him can be heavy. Moving CSEC dept in better direction.

He is definitely a difficult professor - but you will actually learn something. I have been going to RIT for 4 years and can honestly say that I have learned more in his classes than I have in all my others combined. I would definitely recommend taking him.

He may be smart, and witty, he's pretty funny, makes loads of pop culture references and really loves what he does, but he speaks so fast that anyone whose first language is not English, of if they require interpreting (ASL) you're screwed. Rude, swears all the time, and does not respect interpreting services and doesn't care about adapting.

The guy is pretty harsh. He sets the new standard for the CSEC department, where the older students are screwed if they take a class with him. Prepare yourself for x3 the workload of a standard professor

Would not take again. First time ever teaching and is outright rude to his students. If you don't know something he does you're insulted in front of the class. Assigns labs not relevant to the class and isn't there to help at all with them. Takes forever to grade anything. Wanted to get way more out of this class than I did.

Class --> MEDS 440H 
Super sweet lady! Loved her. Classes were all lectures but no tests/quizzes. Just one big presentation that is an easy A if you understand the material well.

Took her Diagnostic Imaging class. It's a 2 credit joke. Class is mandatory (& extremely boring so bring other work), but it's only once a week and she usually cancels it. Tests are online through mycourses and are directly off of her powerpoints. It is impossible to fail her class.

The RIT scheduling system has him listed as SRIRAMACHANDRA MUR, but his real name is Raj Murthy. See his other RMP reviews here: http://is.gd/sDm6AS - He's an amazingly good prof, knows marketing, tell stories, gives great examples, and is willing to help in any way he can. No mid/final, 4 quizzes, 5-6 hmwks, 1 large ongoing project. highly recomm.

The lectures are very well done, and he does a great job at explaining each topic. There are 2 online tests, a midterm and final, along with a few online assignments and quizzes. There is an attendance sheet that gets passed around every class, but you can miss 3 times without an excuse. Also, he ends almost every class at least ten minutes early.
A good professor imo. He knows his stuffs

Super nice professor. He knows his stuffs and are always available for office hour. Tests are open book and online. You will be tested on whats on the slides as well as some of the important things he says in class. Make sure to take note and you will be good. Highly recommend!

Professor Wang was alright. It was a very easy class with little workload and for the most part simple concepts, but he didn't explain things well. His lecture part of the class was for the first 10 minutes of class and the rest was doing examples. Much of the class time was waiting for people to do the work on their own.

Wang's ECON 101 is extremely easy. All quizzes and exams are fully online and open note. You're given a week for each homework assignment. Each assignment only takes about an hour, and there's only 4 assignments. As long as you take basic notes, you'll be good. If you need your global or social perspective, take ECON 101 with Wang.

Smart person, but lectures were dry. He doesn't use PowerPoint and only talks during lecture, so it was hard for me to follow. Not helpful outside of class. If you miss class, it's on you to get the notes from someone else. Exams are online. We never used the textbook so you don't really need to buy it. Only 2 homework assignments. Overall not bad.

Extremely knowledgable and smart, good at explaining the material. Lectures are interesting based on the subject itself, but no fluff otherwise. All online quizzes and exams, and homework consists of a couple assignment sheets throughout the semester. Helpful outside of class and answers student questions thoroughly.

Actually best teacher in RIT. Online Exams + Final. Basically 0 homework. Attendance doesn't matter as you have like 3-8 days where you won't attend class anyways. No class on exam days. Lectures are top tier with actually good explanations and not just slides no jitsu. If you hate this teacher or fail please get help as you cannot be saved.

He's just alright. Lectures are dry, and some explanations better than others. Textbook is wholly optional (don't need to buy it), as everything you'll be tested on is mentioned in class - especially obscure examples.
Yiwei is a chill guy, and meh professor, and lets you out early sometimes. It's a 101 course so he gets the job done.

He was a pretty good professor who cared for the students and wanted them to succeed in his class and others. There were not too many assignments, 3 online homework assignments, 3 online quizzes that were done outside the classroom, then a final + midterm.

Overall not bad. The class is basically all lecture, and his lectures can be a bit dry. He gives a good amount of examples, but I didn't always find them to be helpful. He is willing to help outside of class, though, and I would recommend taking advantage of office hours as well as the practice problems he posts online. All quizzes were online.

He has a lower score than I would have thought. He is a very straightforward professor, gives lots of examples, and tries to get the class to interact with the material. Homework/quizzes are very fair and for the midterm and final he allows a cheat sheet. If you are having trouble, go see him, he will be happy to help. An overall solid teacher.

Prof. Wang is ok. His lectures are incredibly boring and he doesn't seem enthusiastic about teaching. The class has 3 HWs and 3 Quizzes plus midterm and final. His examples were hard to follow for me. He does let you out of class early a lot though.
He teaches with a lot of graphs like a regular econ teacher would so it was helpful for me. He always let us out 5 to 10 minutes early. His midterms were also online.

Yiwei is a very inoffensive professor in the sense that he does exactly what he says he will do. If you are really there to learn and are interested in the material you will have no trouble; and if you do he will answer any of your questions and stay after class to answer as well. Easy grader and quick to reply to email.

His lectures don't make any sense and aren't engaging at all. Also relies a lot on textbooks. He also doesn't give a study guide like most professors so basicly for finals and mid terms you are screwed. But his home works are fair.

The lectures were either extremely easy or extremely difficult. Difficult topics were not explained well at all. The homework and tests were overly difficult. You could find him outside of class, but the help he offers suffers from the same problems as his lectures.

You're expected to attend class. If you miss it, you're to email her to let her know beforehands. Basically every class she outlines the steps and go over a sizeable amount of mock problems to show you the step by steps of those formulas she provides. Class attendance matter if you rely on that type of teaching style

Pros- If you do bad on a quiz or test, you can take it home with you to fix for a higher grade.  Cons- She expects people to participate but it doesn't help that she picked on the same people over and over again.  She lets students use MyMathLab or the textbook to do homework.

Great prof.  Canceled class 13 of the time, let us go early most of the rest of the time, but she taught us what we needed to know for the final.  Tests and quizzes are very fair if you study for them-- drops lowest quiz and hw.  Makes you participate.  Easiest A  I've ever received.  Does not require the online code.

Clear and straight forward. Gives you the chance to do quiz corrections and test corrections. Lowest quiz grade gets dropped. Homework every night, but only a few problems, it doesn't take long. Pretty easy class.

Joe is the GOAT, all of his classes are a must-take if you're interested in the Graphics Industry. All of the assignments are super open-ended (you can use the languages/framework of your choice) and there's a semester-long project instead of a final.

Low workload. Good at explaining during OH. Decent at explaining graphics concepts, but usually rushes the lecture and lets you out 20-45 minutes early lol. Don't have to fully understand what you're doing (I recommend you do), just need to implement the code from lecture slides. Friends and I thought subject material was boring but easy.

Awesome professor. He makes the classes fun and to the point, discussing the implementation of graphics concepts rather than the theory. Assignments can be resubmitted to regain any lost points. Sometimes lectures finish before time. Weekly activities are fun too. I actually looked forward to doing assignments in this class
Very helpful if you get stuck. Wants you to actually learn the material. Grade doesnt matter.

If you would like to develop an interest/ pursue a graphics career in the future, this course helps you get a gentle introduction to the field. The Professor is amazing, cares for the well-being of students, and focuses on how much the students learn over how many grades the students get.

Joe is probably my favorite professor at RIT. He will make you work for your grade, but if you do work for it, you're guaranteed an A. His lectures are incredible and he keeps things interesting and easy to understand. He's very available outside of class for help. Great sense of humor, great lecturer, great professor.
Best professor, makes you learn the concepts.
Very thorough with explaining the concepts and giving out assignments. Doesn't let you worry about the marks, just makes sure you understand the concept in detail.
The professor really liked the topic, and the class was easy (a little too easy in my opinion).  Class consisted of a mini project each week, as well as discussions and two exams.
Excellent professor. My favorite so far!

Evolutionary Algorithms.  Class was easy, lectures were pretty interesting for a CS class. No tests, only meaningful projects.  You're guaranteed to learn a lot, if you do the work.  Geigel is a good lecturer, and tries to spice things up with videos, guest speakers, etc.
Nice guy, popular for setting up the great and painful CG2 course(if u know what i mean). Knows his stuff, helpful might be a little unclear during class but helps outside class so its even..

great guy.  i've had him for multiple classes and have enjoyed him every time.  he's consistent and fair.  he's always been approachable for me, and if you're having trouble he will work with you.  he has all his notes online and they're very helpful.

Extremely nice professor.  Good structure and layout of the class.  Will guide you toward an answer but not outright explain each step. While it may be challenging, it helps with learning the material.

Useless professor.  The only things I learned in the class were from the textbook and other CS4 professor's slides (so if you have him...make sure you get the book).  I ended up going to other non-CS professors for help, because nobody in the department had a clue how to help his students.
Useless with CS4.  I had to go outside the department for help because he spent an hour staring at my code, then took a cell phone call and left.  He's nice but clueless.
Best CS prof I've had yet.

He's a nice guy and has a very structured class setting (i.e. he lays out what you need to know in PowerPoint presentation notes).  He is sometimes unclear and unavailable for questions, but when he is available, he is very approachable.

All he does in class is just reading powerpoint slides. He expects you to read textbook, but he never goes with it in class.  You will have quiz every week, 60% of the course. Quiz is not only based on powerpoint, but also on textbook ; you have to study by yourself. Quiz problems are sometimes stupid. I will never ever take his class again.

Amy is incredibly amazing and it's a joy to have her as my professor for capstone classes. Clear, communicative and you know what exactly she expects of you. That expectation can be quite high, but it is not unachievable.
Very passionate and loves what she does. Clear project criteria. Make sure you pay attention and put in the work. Group project heavy. Listen to her feedback.

One of the worst professors in the math department here at RIT. Makes his boring lectures mandatory, which are filled with mistakes that inadequately prepare you for the homework and exams. Provides little to no valuable feedback on tests and curve grades to cover up poor averages. Get ready to rely on the book for homework and test preparation.

(Ignore the class code, I had Zlochower for MATH-411 but that wasn't an option)

By far the worst professor I've ever had. He acts like you're the problem every time you have a question. He's eager to leave office hours as soon as the clock strikes 6. Curved grades generously to make it look like the student's were learning, but it's all a lie.

comment: why is this guy teaching? he is not certified to teach college algebra in MCC. just about the most ineffective lost math professor you will ever see. avoid at all cost.
Yousef is clueless, absent-minded. i am not sure how is allowed to teach any math course. this guy is less prepared than Mr Bean to teach in a college.

Professor Zlowchower makes several mistakes throughout all of his lectures and constantly goes down lines of thought that lead to nowhere. He will also spend half of some classes talking about something students will not be tested on or need to know. His style of lecture can also gets to be very boring after 2 hours.

He will show you a long convoluted example just to get a single formula that doesn't even show up on the test. He will tell you that you don't need to know something and then will put it on the test in some shape or form. Rambles on, makes mistakes, and doesn't explain what is going on. Instead he says "check the textbook". Do not recommend him.

comment: While he knows his stuff, his ability to teach is absolutely non existent. He goes off on disorganized and incoherent rants that only serve to confuse the student. His problems don't test the basics, only super high level math problems. Prepare for extremely difficult tests where 40+ hours still get you low test scores. Never take Zlochower. Ever.

comment: Super smart, but does not explain why or how to do anything. Tests are rarely curved and they aren't easy. Get ready to spend time at Bates or Sol, if they even know how to solve his problems. Would not recommend.

His lectures were unorganized and nonsensical, the assignments couldn't be done just with the information from the lectures or the textbook, and he didn't see anything wrong with assigning 4 things at a time. Zlochower is also pretty tech-illiterate and this was a computation-heavy course. He shouldn't have been given the course to begin with.
Great professor ! He makes agreat cement filler. There are agreat deal of pot holes in Western New york that Yousef can fill adeuately.

I'd recommend skipping every class if I could.  Just a waste of time.  It seems like he goes out of his way to make things appear harder than they are to make himself feel smarter.  If you have to take a class with him, good luck.

Doesn't grade homework, but there are weekly quizzes that are homework problems so you have to all the homework for the week. Had some problems understanding him sometimes, but over all not a bad teacher. Makes himself available to help you if needed. Be careful about the group project in Calc, he will help if needed but it will still take effort.

Professor Zlochower is very intelligent and completely understands calculus. However, this does not equip him to be a good teacher. Prof Zlochower is not very good at communicating the material to students for them to understand it. I found him more concerned about proving that he knows calculus than making sure us students know it.

Professor Zlochower is probably one of the most useless, incompetent professors RIT has ever had. It is hard to understand why someone like him is even allowed to teach. His lectures are incredibly unhelpful and confusing. The class average is bellow any other Calc II class, and he has no interest in his student or anything else. NEVER ZLOCHOWER!

Professor Zlochower is a very intelligent person however, he's NOT suited to teaching. He skips a lot of steps and tends to move EXTREMELY fast. He does not explain problems well and as a result, everyone in the class gets confused and loses track of the lesson. Do NOT take him unless you are EXTREMELY confident in your math skills.

Just not a good teacher in any way shape or form. He is an incredibly smart person, but an awful teacher. His lectures are very confusing for almost everybody in the class, his tests are extremely challenging (so hard that the curve is usually around 10%), and he is a very tough grader. Avoid at all costs unless you are extremely confident in math.

He is honestly the nicest and most understanding professor ever. He will accept late work, and will make every attempt to help you. Unfortunately, this is not enough to balance the awfulness that is his class. He moves too quickly, can't explain anything thoroughly, and makes many mistakes. Don't take him if you already struggle with calculus.
Doesn't explain well. Skips a lot of steps when solving problems on the board. It's very easy to get lost. The tests are extremely challenging.

Professor Z was an excellent professor. After having him for one quarter, I made sure I had him again for the next. He's very helpful, quizzes and tests relate to the material, and he is fast paced in class. You must pay attention to get a good grade. He makes it very possible to do well in the class, though!

Basically the nicest professor in the world. He moves quickly in class and makes mistakes during examples, but if you pay attention, you will learn something. If you don't, homeworks are set up so you can learn from the book easily. Very hard tests, but the problems are interesting. Gives fantastic partial credit so tests and quizzes are fair.
Knows his stuff but skips steps and moves very quickly. DO NOT TAKE HIM UNLESS YOU ARE READY TO MOVE FAST. Tests and homework are difficult.

Fast writer; you must pay attention. Makes mistakes every class & wastes 5 mins trying to correct them. Otherwise very time-efficient. New topics introduced with proof followed by many examples. Reviews HW @end of class. Will answer questions no matter how long it takes. Avg hw, extensions, bonus points. Fair grading, partial credit, weekly quizzes

PBII. Zlochower is brilliant, for better or worse. If you are a genius, I recommend him. If you're just smart, his style might not agree with you. He spends a lot of time correcting or proving his math rather than teaching what's important. He skips a lot of important steps, so you might lose track of the lesson. Grades projects, homework harshly.
Good professor. Has helpful and somewhat interesting lectures. Lots of helpful office hours. Average homework load and well written tests.
He does his best at everything. Sometimes he is little bit unorganized but he pulls it through. A very fair decent professor.

Prof. Z is an excellent professor. He is really helpful, willing to help you  after office hours. He def. knows what he is doing. However he sometimes will skip steps and do math in his head. If you are really interested in math and want a good challenge, you will learn a lot from him.

Dr. Z is the one of the most helpful professors I've had. His lectures are good, the notes on the board tend to be unorganized however. I would highly recommend taking a course from him, he is genuinely interested in making sure you understand the material (but be prepared to be in his office a long time when you go to his office hours, lol).

Kuehl is extremely knowledgable about the content he teaches; this review may be due to the covid semesters. But we were faced with group project deliverables every week to the tune of 10+ pages per submission, on top of coding a protoype and individual assignments (which may have been 3-4+ pages in their own right) 3x a week. Workloadnuts. Disorg

Very knowledgeable about the course material, clearly cares about the subject matter. He does ask lots of questions, so you'll get the most out of the class by participating whenever you can and asking him valuable questions in turn. Project grades felt very fair, and the course material is very clearly outlined to you (projects, slides, etc...).
The professor seems to grade quizzes more leniently than the exams and projects. There's lots of busy work to be done, but the class is relatively easy. On a 5 point rating I would give him a 3/5.

This professor is a hard one to figure out. At times he seems to know what he's talking about and other times he doesn't. There's lots of busy work and his grading seems inconsistent, sometimes they're lenient and sometimes they're not. Overall he's an OK professor, not sure if I would recommend him.

Positive: Clear grading criteria. Very nice person. Negative: Took a long time to grade assignments. Class was not useful, unless you have literally never made a resume before or never been to a career fair. Busy work for the sake of busy work. Just take a different COMM class this is too much busy work for no reward.

She's a great professor, I wish the class wasn't a partly online class, but it was fine. Just be prepared to work very hard and don't forget about any deadlines, because you will get some points taken off.
She really cares how you do in her class and will work around things to help you out. The class its self is boring but it is easy.

Alsop was great. As long as you follow her guidelines for assignments, you will be fine. However, she never ever responded to any of my emails. I emailed her probably about 6-7 times total this semester and never got a response to any of them, which was frustrating for sure because it makes it feel impossible to connect with her away from class.

By far the best professor I've had. She genuinely cares for students who want to succeed in her class. She's very understanding and is gives great feedback in presentations. However her assignments due dates are strict and she is also strict on attendance, but all of her positives make up for it. She is also a very lenient grader on speeches

This class is pretty easy. If you follow the outlines she gives you you're almost guaranteed an A. When we didn't do speeches we had occasional quizzes based on the readings assigned. Those were a little confusing but if you actually read (which I didn't) you'll be fine. Arianna keeps things interesting and is a great professor, just a slow grader

Great Professor, really nice. Dosen't grade things till the end of the semester. Online quizzes in person seemed like a waste of lecture time but were easy as long as you read the textbook chapters. Lectures were interesting and engaging. Discussion posts & projects were relatively simple and tests were consistent with the textbook and lectures.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Professor Alsop is great. She has very clear grading guidelines for speeches. Lectures are fun. Grade is made up of a few speeches, quizzes on the textbook, and attendance. She is a fast grader and is always available for help or to give feedback.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Easy all around. If you have a free elective take this with her. To the dude who gave her a 1 what did you expect to get out of a communications class. Only issue is you do have to go to class but I suppose if she didn't make it a requirement no one would go since it's so easy. Online quizzes/exams/discussions and she's a slow grader.

She is one of my favorite professors. She was so kind and made me feel safe, which was nice in a public speaking class. I learned a lot from her and she gives thorough feedback. She's very passionate.

The lectures were more of a waste of time than an actual class. Everything discussed was something that you knew previously. You were taught how to write an email + maybe 3 chapters of the textbook were used on throwaway quizzes. Grades were put in at the end of the semester, so there was no way to tell how well you were doing. I regret showing up

Professor Alsop is very passionate about what she teaches, and makes her classes fun by having class discussions once or twice a week, with some classes dedicated as workshop classes to get feedback on assignments before submission. Homework is usually a discussion post or online reading quiz usually due every Friday. Would recommend this professor
He loves real life case studies

Very chill guy all around, his lectures tend to deviate from the slides but even the anecdotes are interesting and bits of humor are always fun. The writing prompts were fun to engage with, although you get thrown in the deep end for the final. It's obvious he is knowledgable yet willing to learn more when there's questions and discussions.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: I took HIST261, History of Modern China, this site won't let me add a new course. The syllabus requirements for papers are extremely vague, and if you don't remember the vague directions he gave in class about the paper, you're SOL. It is asinine that a professor is allowed to have such vague directions for something as major as a final paper.

Professor Laver made an otherwise boring history class interesting with his knowledge and sense of humor. He often shares interesting historical stories in class. Attendance is not mandatory, and you could theoretically do the reading and review slides to pass the quizzes and finish the papers. But you shouldn't miss his class because it's fun.

I've taken him for two classes. Both classes have had the same grading setup which three quizzes, ten questions each, and four papers, 3 pages each except for the last which is a seven page researched paper. If you show up to class everyday and pay attention you will get an A on the quizzes. If he shows a movie he will have a question about it.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: He's the worst professor I've ever had at RIT. He just too strict in grading and I would not recommend taking his class if you worry about your result.

Had him for History of Premodern Japan. Very knowledgable on the subject, which will show during his lectures. Assigns 4 papers, each 5 pages long and double spaced: difficult, but doable. Quizzes were not very straightforward, but were only 10 questions give or take. Very nice guy, and always tries to crack a few jokes.

Professor Laver is straight forward for HIST 160 Hist. of Modern East Asia: three quizzes and four papers. Lectures can sometimes get dry but he explains the big themes well. Notes from the power point might not help - take notes on what he's saying and you'll be fine for the class. He is laid back but he is a good guy.

Class is interesting with a simple schedule of assignments due and quizzes. However, written assignments are given no feedback when handed back. You may have thought you did a good job but get a bad grade and not know why. This doesnt help when these assignments add up to help a final research paper. Lectures are dull and lots of reading.

Laid back and reasonable. Entertaining classes with good opportunity for discussion if anyone felt like discussing anything. Easy to ask questions. Relatively few assignments and grades with excellent, timely, feedback. Would recommend taking his classes at every opportunity.
Had him for Asian Civilization, pretty easy as long as you read the book and pay attention in class.  Need to write two papers, both 2 pages, double-space super easy.

Very interesting lectures. Tests and quizzes are all essays and defining terms (usually 2 out of 10 given). Grading is so ridiculously easy that if you have any idea what the answer is you will get full credit. If you want an easy A but at the same time have a very interesting course to fill your electives, take a class with Laver.

A pretty good professor who spends each class lecturing. The lectures are interesting, and if you pay attention and take notes it can take the place of the main textbook. There are supplemental readings, but are only used for the quizzes. The quizzes and exams are all essay writing, but you know what they will cover ahead of time and the grading is

Probably one of the most chill professors ever. Grading is ridiculously easy; if you fail his class... I don't even know. And I think his lectures were really good, it was less of a lecture and more relaying a really good story, so it kept me interested. Just pay attention and read (even just skim) the textbook.

Really good professor! He is a bit boring in class and his lectures sometimes seem long but his quizzes and tests are not difficult at all. He is a pretty easy grader and does not reall care if you never show up and stuff like that. Although if you want his help at some point in the year you will have to show some interest and have decent attendanc
Rude and disrespectful

Absolutely horrible professor. He was snarky towards students and clearly had favorites. He didn't follow his syllabus at all and almost never sent out emails about schedule changes. He would often say something wasn't important and wouldn't be on the exam and then that exact question would show up on the exam. Don't take this class.

Worst professor I ever had, and I got a good grade in his class. 
He is biased and will judge you based on your life choices such as religion, etc. He is a UTTERLY unfair grader and will give students he likes bonus points or "miss" a mistake they made, but if he doesn't like you? He will take off points for anything he possibly can.

Dr. Thomas is a great professor. His class is mainly lecture with weekly reading assignments due. The grade is based off of three tests, final research paper, and final group presentation. For the exams, he tells you what will be on the exam. For the research paper, he allows you to turn in drafts to him  where he will tell you how to get an A.

Dr. Bolaji Thomas is the worst professor I have yet to encounter. His class slides are full of misspellings and bad grammar, and incorrect information which I had confirmed by an Immunologist. He does not care if you are failing his class. He just wants you to sit, hear him talk and leave. Textbook is a waste of time and effort. Just use Google.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']

comment: Skip class and you really wont pass. Attendance is not graded or required but if you dont show up he might start docking points from your tests or presentations. Tests come straight from textbook. He claims to care about his students a lot but he really doesnt show that he does
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Group projects']

comment: Love the way he talks and lectures, but the way he grades presentations is TERRIBLE!! He makes comments DURING the presentation, and many of them are left to peer evaluations (which normally is fine, but people in biomed give poor grades to their peers). So he's a great immunology teacher, but epidemiology was a bit strenuous.

He is the most caring professor I have ever had, if you get to take a class with him, I highly recommend it. I wish I had more space to type but, he cares about every student and loves what he does. I wish Could take more classes with him. the class workload is not overwhelming and is very manageable. I wish there were more professors like him.

Definitely makes students work for their grades. But, he provides an extremely positive learning environment, takes feedback from students, and is clearly a professor who is on the side of his students. The class is hard, but still enjoyable.

This professor will prepare you for graduate and/or medical school.  His expectations for his students meet or exceed those of the average PhD or MD program.  If you're looking for an easy Bioscience professor, or a soft class to pad your course schedule, I'd keep looking. He has high expectations for his students.

I had him for Immunology. As long as you read the textbook and study the slides, you WILL be fine. Easiest A for me because I actually read the textbook, attended class, and studied. If you don't study you wont get a good grade, simple as that.
Excellent teacher, all he wants is for you to attend and an A (with some studying) is extremely doable!
If you aren't interested in the class, don't take it. He expects you to actually learn, and that's what college is for. Excellent teacher and has a great accent, like Mr. Eko!

Dr. Thomas makes you LEARN for your grade. Yes, you have to read the book for better clarification, because the subjects he teaches are difficult. I had him for Parasitology as well, which was more intense than his Immunology class. Overall, I would recommend his classes because once it is all said and done, I feel confident in that subject.

Very intimidating. Took the first test and he LAUGHED at the class after they handed it in!! Test true/false questions are ridiculously difficult- be prepared to study every single slide to do decently in the class (aka I studied an entire week/flashcards/the whole nine yards and only got a B on the test).

The worst professor I have ever had. Doesn't lecture at all, simply tries to give you life lessons. Horrible tests. He constantly contradicts himself. Complains about teaching at RIT. Be his pet and you'll get an A, be a student and you'll get a D.
Everyone likes to complain about this guy but it boils down to one thing.  You came to college to work hard and learn, and that is all he expects.  You want to learn take a class with him.

Sped through lectures, spending more time talking about he family and his trips to Africa than the topic. Ended once class with a tirade about how we should all abstain from sex and how his fife had done so so he loved her more for that. Incredibly awkward, tests were ridiculous, avoid if at all possible. Made me hate the class.

I had him for Parasitology Spring 2010.He is a ridiculous grader.The worst thing is,he tells you on the first day that he doesn't give out A's. The material is interesting,but he expects your test performance to be at graduate school level.I will never take one of his classes again.I suggest you only take this class if you want your GPA to drop.

This professor made me hate the field of microbiology in reference to parasites. I cannot stand his teaching style. He expects too much to be remembered for the exams and they are practically impossible. He will run out of time and skip over 15 slides then expect you to know this information on the exam. NEVER TAKE HIM - I cannot stress this enough

I had him for molecular bio lab and he's probably been the worst professor I had at RIT.  You cant understand him and he never gives anyone above an 80 on a lab report unless your 4th year and you already know everything. He most likely gave out one A to the entire lab section so if your looking for an A in lab you better be the top student.

i had him for a friday bio lab at 9 and he made it funny.  his accent is kind of hard to hear but you get used to it and he tries to speed everything  and get you out early. also helps when the procedure gets hard. i recommend him

Barely graded anything throughout the entire semester, failed to give feedback on numerous occasions, changed due dates frequently, did not respond to emails in a timely manner or sometimes at all. Take a different teacher if you care about knowing how you're doing in the class/how you can improve.

Did not grade anything the entire semester (including tests, labs, quizzes, projects, presentations, etc), mostly responded to emails on time. If you actually want to know how you are doing in your class and want grades at all, find another professor.

She is a great teacher, gives good feedback, and super easy to talk to about anything. She has a problem posting grades on time. The semester has been over for almost a month, and tho I have my final grade, she has yet to post several individual grades that I would like to have.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Marge is an excellent professor with great interpersonal skills. She makes learning fun and interactive. She does not exactly grade things in a timely manner, but she gives you plenty of feedback on goreact and in class to make up for it. She is very willing to work with students as long as they communicate their needs with her.

you won't know how you got your final grade. be grateful if you pass higher than a D  given she may cancel a lot of classes, will not answer emails she doesn't want to answer, and will delay giving grades and feedback as long as possible.

If you like knowing your status or grades in a class, don't take any class with her. never uploaded grades to mycourses. she cancelled class 3 times and put it on us to catch up on our own. no feedback ever. graded my paper without even opening it on mycourses, doesn't answer emails. what more do you want in an awful professor?
gives grades back too late. little to no feedback for improvement except in class. misses details in lectures.

i don't think the onlinein-class blend class style is her thing. skipped a few classes for being sick, went through the last few units too fast, no feedback from tests,about what you did wrong, just nothing. slow with grades too. when she tells you she will have grades tomorrow, don't count on it.

Skipped classes, covered 2 units in two days, test the next class. Gave no feedback to improve for 2nd expressive test. Took her 2-3 months to grade the 1st expressive. Didn't read reflective paper, doesn't post all grades before final grade. Didn't answer my email asking how i got my final grade. Doesn't hand back grades in timely manner.

She lacks giving grades back in a TIMELY manner, slow with responding to emails most of the time, DOES NOT give you feedback (she didn't for me or my class) after expressive tests, signs too quick for beginners, and rushes through because she can skip classes (3 times for me). You won't even know how you got your final grade... idk how i got mine.
Very nice and approachable- strict with attendance but understanding if you make the effort to explain. Great teacher!
Marge was very kind and encouraging, very good for a beginner class. She's very approachable if you have question sand does her best to make sure you understand.
Marge has great personality and charm with ASL. You'll almost forget she's deaf. However, she rarely responds to emails and can be a tough grader.
BEST ASL teacher. Do not take course with anyone else. Fun, interesting, relaxed, great teacher. You WILL learn ASL.

Marge is the best ASL teacher at RIT, don't take it with anyone else!  Homework and tests are fair, she really teaches you a lot about the subject if you are really into ASL.  I'll miss going to this class!
No Comments
Really nice and helpful, keeps class interesting, but one of the hardest graders I've ever had. Overall would recommend, but make sure you do the homework and do it thoroughly (not hard to do).
very nice, but she is a hard grader

Professor Benso was a nice person, but not a good professor. The way she structured the class was like she was trying to get students to fail. We had one exam(10 weeks of material and no study guide) during the semester and a final. She went against her word many times during the semester, and required attendance when she didn't take it.
such a great teacher who knows all things about philosophy

She is a great professor but if you aren't interested in philosophy you wont enjoy it. I'm not into philosophy and I enjoyed the first half of the semester when talking about Socrates and Plato but the rest was not very engaging. If you want to do well on her exams you should read as they are hard and not everything is covered in the lecture.

Professor Benso is wonderful and thoughtful. She makes the class want to talk about subjects and look forward to talking about things that are harder subjects to talk about. She gives a lot of readings and a few writing assignments but she is passionate and its very interesting. She also has a accent and sucks at technology so be a little patient.

This was probably the hardest course I've taken, but it was worth it. Dr. Benso really explains complex and difficult philosophers in ways that are digestible, which is not at all an easy thing to do (especially with a language barrier). Just be prepared for very, very long and difficult readings, on top of hefty amount of writing.

Dr. Benso is a very knowledgeable scholar of philosophy and you will have a blast studying the Greeks with her. However, be prepared for very sudden long papers that are sometimes due sooner than is reasonable.

In order to do decent in this class you need to read everything assigned and study intensely because the exams are not forgiving. For an intro to philosophy class the amount of material expected of you to commit to memory is absurd. Would not recommend

Readings are too long. You will struggle to keep up considering the density of the texts. She can sometimes give superficial or weird readings of philosophers. Easy grader; you can slack off on those heavy readings a bit and not have a problem. She is very nice and likes to get personal with students if they approach her.

She picks interesting philosophers, but sometimes she can give inaccurate representations of them. Rather difficult tests for an intro class. Annoying discussion sections that last too short. Readings are also pretty hard for an intro class. You will leave this class with pretty robust philosophical knowledge considering it's an intro class.

It's a 200 level class and it's too serious with no group work. I met zero classmates. Attendance only allows 6 absences. There are five extensive discussion pieces. All exam questions require a response of 500 or 750 words each Q. She is passionate and loves to talk about her cat.. I think RIT students leave her at a loss for words sometimes.
Very easy Liberal Arts credit, enjoyable to learn. Paper every week but they are very easy to too. Tests are easy, just review notes and read the text and you will be fine.
do the work, look over notes before tests, and participate in class and you'll have an easy A. vocabulary is a crucial part of the tests, so pay attention when she stresses certain words

Wonderful teacher! Slight Italian accent, a pleasure to listen to. Really made me think about issues I had never thought about. Very helpful explanations of at times difficult texts. Requires regular reading and note-taking. Fair exams. She truly has a passion for her subject matter, and is very enthusiastic. Open-minded, listens to every opinion.

As stated before, she dismisses opinions that differ from her own. Hard to understand at times. She teachers Philosophy as if it were a history class. Hard to get an A because of how few graded assignments there are. She is always late to class. Most classes are boring, circular discussions that are never clarified.

Poorly organized, always late, writes the letter 'a' like its an 'e'. Terribly boring, and sparks painful discussions, but dismisses any opinion that conflicts with her own. Occasional misinformation. Poor grading scheme: Everything is worth the percentage points its worth in your final grade, but she almost exclusively deducts whole points.

Shes got a slight Italian accent but youll barely even notice it after a week.  Class is fairly easy, just listen and take good notes and read the readings you'll do fine.  Grades based on 2 response papers attendance and 2 take home tests. No final.  Take home tests are fairy challenging, response papers are easy As as long as you explain yourself

Passionate professor who loves Philosophy. Lectures are very interesting, although the books we were asked to buy were not really needed since she pointed out quotes and went over everything in the readings each class. I rated her class as hard because the only work we turned in was two responses, a midterm, and a final, so an A is hard to get!

The class was a special topic:Phenomenology. Benso is an intelligent professor and speaks the material well, but phenomenology is just hard stuff to grasp. That is the only reason my easiness rating is medium.
A privilege to have had this very brilliant and generous in passing knowledge to students and a warm Professor. She is not shallow because she has EXPERIENCED not just educated in LIFE. I LOVE HER

She was the best teacher I had while at RIT, the only one who actually cared about her students and the only one who realized that she wasn't the only class we were taking.  I would take anything she taught just to be in a class with her.

The previous review was dated in May 2009 but it was not possible to rate this professor's performance because she was on medical leave last year. Maybe that's why the other reviewer gave Dr. Housel such a negative rating--the reviewer didn't actually have Dr. Housel.
Very nice person, however her views are very biased.  If you don't agree with her, the class can be a nightmare...

Professor Housel is just an amazing teacher. She covers very interesting topics, and is very nice to the class. She doesn't test, but there are papers and journal entries to do for writing seminar, all of which were either easy, or at least interesting. All of her assignments were very interesting and made you want to do them.

She is one of the best teachers I have had at RIT.  She makes class fun!! She is one of the few teachers that really cares about her students!! I would highly suggest having her atleast once in your RIT experience!!!!

This is a writing class, and as a technical person I hate writing. Even this small comment panel is arduous for me to fill. I have never found any interest in writing until I took one of Dr. Housel's classes. I will be writing my first published creative story, and loving every moment of it. Her writing classes did not just teach me, they changed m

She is totally amazing.  Really funny and fun and wants everyone to do well.  She doesn't believe in tests but encourages you to do your best.  She kept my interest the entire quarter and was a easy grade. She makes going to class really fun and worth your time and money
fun, interesting
An amazing teacher and one of the best English teacher's I've had yet.  Also one of the easiest classes you will take in college.

She is and amazing teacher. We watched three movies and as long as you follow directions on the papers you get at least a B if not an A. Go to every to as many classes as you can, if you can email her and explain why and she most likely wont mind if you dont miss to many, very friendly

She has been the best professor I've had so far in my 3 years here.  She made the class sooo fun and we still learned a lot.  She loves talking about movies.  We acutally watched Gladiator and A Mid Summer Nights Dream, the newest one.  She really cares about her students and it's also very easy to get an A.
Housel is the coolest professor I have had.  Great sense of humor and always tries to help you out.  She has helped me out of a couple of pickles already and she is just plain awesome.
You can't get any better than her. Shes the greatest! She managed to keep me awake at 8am. What a miracle. Easy class. TAKE IT!!!

Housel is AWESOME and knows how to make you chuckle/smile! I loved her class & looked forward to it. Some of the readings were downright awful but she made it bareable. She cares about ALL of her students & is willing to help in EVERY way. Point Blank: I wish I could take more classes with her.

One of my favorite professors here.  No tests, no quizzes, just a few papers and none of them long.  Definatly the professor you want to take writing and lit with!!  If you mention that you like comic heroes and action movies, you will be in great shape for the class!
Very easy teacher, however, if you don't agree with her, class can be very unpleasant.
She is great! I would definatly recomend her for Writing and Lit.
Best Teacher Ever. 'Nuff said. This is the only class I made a real attempt not to miss. Prof. Housel is the teacher you want to take W&L from. No questions asked.

She is VERY nice.  Grades rather easy, she teaches the way teachers should.  Her goal seems to be to make students learn something.  I HIGHLY recommend her for first year's, it makes a nice break from in your face teachers.
great professor, fun, interesting, gave me a grade i didn even think i deserved

She was one of those professors you always wish you will have in your college career.  She was always there to help in not only your academic life but also your personal life and really cared about each and every one of her students.

comment: Special Rel. is a very difficult topic to teach but Zwickl finds a way to make it make some sense. He encourages group discussion and helps to answer questions throughout class. He is understanding and tries hard to make students think through the issues in front of them to work their way to the answer.

Professor Zwickl is super enthusiastic about teaching and he's a super cool guy. The way that Intro to Special Relativity is structured means that we read and did a lot of worksheets, but when he did get to lecture he was very clear and spent a lot of time answering questions. He's always available after class and by appointment just email him!

This was such a good class, and it really reaffirmed my desire to teach. The workload is pretty brutal for an undergraduate, just keep that in mind. Zwickl asks you to read two 20ish page papers a week with the occasional homework, which can pile up with other undergrad stuff. But this truly is a great class, and very easy to succeed in if you try.

comment: He is one of the nicest professors I have met. I interviewed him once, during which I asked about his hobbies. His primary hobby is gardening with his wife. He helps students when they need it. He also responds to emails and works well with students with disabilities. He checks in on students who struggle and is always willing to help.

Dr. Zwickl is fun and I found him very easy to understand and approach. His physics education background stands out in the way that he explains concepts and allows you to make your own conclusions easily. The work is difficult to wrap your head around but he will do his best to get you there. I would take him for a more in depth class for sure.

Dr. Zwickl has set Electronic Measurements up in a really nice way, allowing you to learn both programming skills and typical lecture content about electronics. I can honestly say this felt like one of the most useful and genuinely educational courses I've ever taken. All quizzes could be retaken at any time, and assignments were quick and simple.

I didn't interact much with Zwickl and found his lectures to be rather drab but he's an entertaining guy and exemplified that during lab tours. Zwickl is a dopey coding kid that became a professor. Very smart and teaches at a level that makes concepts intuitive and clearly understandable. Short online "quizzes" before almost every class, graded on completion. She acts like this is the real world and not college which I guess is good since that is why we are in school. It takes you for a surprise but I learned a lot.  She really cares and is  passionate.

Good luck...you are going to need it. She makes it very difficult for all her students. She believes that failure is the best way to learn.

Has a 24hours email respond time but doesnt really follow through. Always seems lost in class. Goes to fast through material, and has very vague discriptions for everything. Unfortunalty most people who are in the Print departement have to take this class, however its not to hard.

While the class is incredibly easy and the only reason I didn't get an A being I couldn't be bothered to show up after midterms. VanWinkle is an incredible poor teacher who spends upwards of 30 minutes doing preclass ice breaker instead of teaching the material. Her lectures slides are frequently screenshots of google ai explaining the topic.

I took molecular biology with Dr. V, and it was incredibly easy. All exams were open note open textbook and she frequently used the same questions in the review sessions. I think that someone who knows nothing about biology could easily get an A in this class. That being said, the class is so easy that I feel like I didn't learn a whole lot.
Best teacher around, easy A, don't really know how here rate my prof is so low, she's probably the best teacher at RIT.

I love Dr. V so much. She was really relatable and was always clear with what she wanted in assignments. The assignments were easy but still taught us the basics of lab work. We got out super early most days and really cared about learning more about us as people. I couldn't have asked for a better professor.

Clearly states what she wants in your lab reports, if you check all the boxes you get 100% pretty much. Weekly quizzes are easy as well and you get two attempts to do them. There are writing assignments but you have plenty of time to get them done and is flexible with extensions, once again she tells you exactly what she wants done.

Really good professor; not only does Dr. VanWinkle make an effort to create a good learning environment class-wise, but she's also almost always accessible for questions. What I LOVE is how she grades - every single assignment, Dr. VanWinkle provides a clear list for everything that will be graded, and allows resubmissions.
