comment: There's quite literally nothing bad I can say about Dr. V, she was the best lab professor I've had so far. While doing experiments she is so engaged with each student's work and findings which has created such a positive learning environment, making me actively want to be in lab. If you have the option, please take lab with Dr. V.

Dr. VanWinkle seems to be very unclear about the concepts taught in class. Whenever a student asks a question, she tends to reflect it by asking, "Well, what do you think?" She further reflects it by directing it towards other students and asking if they can explain it. I feel as if she is not well-versed in the world of molecular biology.

Worst teacher I've had at RIT. During many classes, she hands out models for the class to play with. Others, she will play a somewhat related video. Her lectures make absolutely not sense. She does not follow the book. First test, she essentially gave the answers to the class before and everyone did great. Second test was nothing like the review.

On the first day of class she told a room full of Biomedical Engineering students that it was okay if they didn't know what DNA was. Also she completely failed to show up to teach one day because she thought the class was an hour later than it was scheduled. She also messed around with iclickers for about 15min of our 50min class almost every class
Probably the only good math professor at the school he is incredibly kind

Professor Barlow is one of the few math instructors at RIT who truly deserves to teach. He is genuinely supportive and will believe in you instead of tearing you down, making his class one of the best experiences of the semester.

Do whatever you can to get into his courses. If you have to push off a class for a semester, so be it. You will learn the content better than with any other professor. Literally the best mathematics professor at RIT. Fight and claw your way through every waitlist, do not kick rocks and settle for less. Take Barlow.

Prof. Nate is amazing! I enjoyed every moment of this class. He is easy to understand, and also posts all lecture notes on MyCourses. I have not gotten an A in a math class in a while as I have bad test anxiety, but his test prep is like no other and he never has any "trick questions". I hope you like tea though! He loves bringing tea for the class

Terrific attitude and a clear lecturer. The classroom environment he facilitates is one where you not only feel that you can succeed, but where he also gives you the tools you need to make that a reality. He answers questions thoughtfully and if someone makes a mistake, he always turns it into a positive teaching moment. I HIGHLY recommend him.

Barlow's lectures are very clear and engaging. He keeps the class interesting by showing 3D models of the equations you're solving and relating them to real world scenarios. He's very clear on what to expect for exams and is a fairly lenient grader. He's also great at answering questions.

He's a super caring teacher and made class a pleasant enough experience. Lectures will a little long and drawn out, however that's just the nature of the topic too. His x's y's u's and t's all look very similar when he writes them (leading to confusion), but he'll make you tea at office hours *:･✧*･ﾟ✧

Barlow is good at teaching you how to do differential equations and makes the class very easy to the point where I thought it was boring. If you want to get an A go with barlow, but if you're more interested in theory and deep understanding he may not be for you. He is available and approachable.
One of the best teachers I've ever had.

One of the best professor in our college. He know how to 'teach', not like other professors.

That's the most important things for educational institution.

Barlow gives amazing lectures and makes the material easy to understand. Make sure you take good notes during the lectures, as the online versions are harder to understand. He puts a lot of energy into the course, and offers candy/tea as rewards to encourage people to ask questions. The workshops/quizzes are review of the homework, so pretty easy.

He's an amazing professor! My only complaint is that sometimes the lectures drag on, because he's so thorough on problems that it feels like it's moving wayyyyyy too slow. Not really a huge problem, because otherwise he's a great teacher and makes the class so easy!

The professor was amazing. The class materials are not that easy but he teaches very well, and 
explain in student's level. Gives us good feedback always. And if you have lots of question about or not about the class, he will answer that sincerely.

GOATED. Nobody else teaches DiffEQ but dressing up like a wizard and handing out 3D glasses. Top-tier lecturer, never ever felt unfair. Actively wants you to succeed. Even Matlab assignments actually made sense with him. Energy is infectious. Recommended for ANY math class, take it with Barlow.

Professor Barlow is the best professor I have ever had! He cares so much about his students. He makes sure all the material in the lecture is clear & is open to helping people at all times. He makes himself very available.  The tests are extremely fair because he tells you exactly what to expect. I definitely recommend taking a class with him!
Had him for diff eq, he is an excellent professor and not only makes learning the material engaging but is willing to help you through it.

One of the best professors I've had so far and I feel like I learned a lot in this class. He is also just a genuinely nice person who cares about his students. He makes it almost hard to fail- his expectations are clear and assessments are just like the quizzes/class examples.

Professor Barlow is easily one of the best professors I have ever had. Each assignment he gives is very clear and there is no confusion with deadlines. Homework is generally difficult, but this makes the exams seem easier. Prof Barlow is the type of professor to stay long after the class is over if it means helping someone. I highly recommend him.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: I have never been a fan of math, but he kind of made me love it. He is the best math professor I have had in my life. He breaks down examples really well and is always willing to help you. His lectures are super fun (a word a never thought I would use to describe a math class). This man changed my life, and I hope he changes yours too.

Nate is a fantastic professor. He made lectures engaging, even during COVID with everything online. He also has optional HW questions where students can talk about how they are, as well as answer silly questions. This class has been extremely enjoyable, and I normally dislike math classes. I HIGHLY recommend him as a professor.

Nate is the best professor I've ever had at RIT. His class was the first math class I've ever gotten an A in. He makes the lectures engaging and easy to follow, and is super easy to talk to in office hours as well. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students a lot. Would 100% recommend taking a class with him if you get a chance.

Best math professor I've ever had. I normally dread math courses, but Prof Barlow makes learning so easy and fun that I find myself actually looking forward to class. Participation is encouraged and everyone in class is clearly enjoying the lectures. We're all inspired by him. Prof Barlow is the sort of person I want to be when I grow up.

One of the best Professors I have had so far and definitely one of my favorite Professors as well. Hilarious guy who makes learning Differential Equations interesting. I genuinely wanted to attend his lectures because he explained very well. His office hours are amazing as well and he always had chocolates and tea for students who came in.

Barlow does an excellent job of breaking down the steps of how to solve some of the very long problems we did in his Boundary Value Problems class. He definitely is more than willing to chat with you in his office when you are having conceptual difficulties especially when he knows you care about the class.

Dr. Nate is awesome. He lectures very clearly and thoroughly and helps you work through examples after first seeing his examples. He posts practice exams with fully worked out solutions for all exams, including the final. We only had a few easy quizzes and he drops one. Homeworks are short and easy. He brings candy on Thursdays.
terrific teacher
One of the best math teachers Ive ever had. Always helps if you have a question, clear and concise.

Hands down, he's the best professor I've had at RIT so far. He actually wants you to learn and understand the material. All examples are broken down into easy to follow steps. He also provides many practice exams, which are nearly identical to his tests so you know exactly what to expect. Go to class and complete the homework and you'll be set.
Daily in class worksheets are annoying, but he drops one of four exams so a decent number of people can skip the final. Mostly reads off slides but manages to convey the material relatively well.
Awesome professor. Lectures are easy to follow and he and the TAs were very helpful. About 2-3 hours of homework per week and the exams were very reflective of the homework and lectures.

His class was great! The final took place of your lowest exam so if you're happy with your grade you don't have to take the cumulative final. He has a worksheet you do in class that's due at the end of class so attendance isn't checked but the worksheets are graded. His lecture can be boring but the content is easy to review by yourself if needed.

Jobby gives a good class and is a decent teacher. His lectures are mostly skippable (he is helpful outside of class hours though) but his in-lecture worksheets are the most important part of your success in this class. They are very heavily correlated to the exams, are a good part of your grade, and the homework questions are overly difficult.

Very considerate of students and their time. Graded super quickly. Daily graded worksheets with questions exactly like those on the exams, so you are prepared very well. For exams, great reference sheet provided and you can bring a notecard. Exams are very fair and can be prepared for with the worksheets.

Awesome guy. Very considerate for the students and grades stuff super fast. Daily graded worksheets due at the end of class which can be difficult, but prepare you for the exams super well. Tests are exactly like the worksheet problems, and you are provided a great reference sheet and can bring a notecard for exams.

Bad lectures in my opinion, he goes WAY to fast and students have to ask him to go back on the notes 3 times per class. The way he runs class had my entire table stressed out. The daily worksheets are due right after class and we often don't have time to finish them. Just way too rushed overall.

Jobby Jacob is my goat. He explains and gives examples very clearly in class. Exams are basically like the examples in class and gives homework almost weekly, but the homework is easy and short. Also, some weeks he doesn't assign homework to give us a break and there are 3 midterms and 1 final. He's genuinely a nice professor.

comment: He is a good teacher. The exams are pretty straightforward what was on the homeworks. He is a pretty tough grader. If your final answer is incorrect, you will get almost no points of effort. He gives examples during class which is extremely helpful. I would choose him to take again.

INCREDIBLY solid professor. Every day he presents a single idea, then gives comprehensive examples, and answers questions the whole time. His exams are exactly what you expect based on the lectures; nothing will be a surprise. His grading is also incredibly fair: partial credit for effort galore. Take notes, don't skip, and you'll do great.
Makes an easy class even easier. No trick questions on exams, everything is as simple as it gets. Hw once a week, sometimes no hw. If you want a free A in linear take Jobby Jacob my goat
Delivers the coursework in a clear manner. Good lectures, cant complain. Seems to enjoy his job teaching.

He goes over problems multiple times, and tries to explain them well for you to understand. This can make lectures boring if you get it or be extremely helpful. He gives out many homework's, but they are typically short and easy to complete. He also gives 4 exams including the final. I would take him again. Not the best and not the worst professor.

Overall, a very approachable and caring professor. The tests were very manageable and were on exactly what we went over in class. The homework was a bit much, but I was a little more prepared for the tests after doing them. I hate to say it, but he was a bit difficult to understand in lectures and wasn't really able to explain a few concepts.

Dr. Jacob gives homework that takes about 10 hours a week and has problems he barely went over in class. His exams are extremely difficult and he doesn't curve grades, so keep that in mind if you're looking for a professor who curves grades. Overall he's a nice guy, but a bad professor. I'd avoid at all costs.
Professor Jacob is very caring and always shows up to lecture in a good mood. Teaches a little fast but as long as you're paying attention its not hard to keep up.

Jacob uses his iPad to write lecture notes on the screen. This was fine for me, but if you are dyslexic you might have difficulties reading his handwriting. Very nice and caring, always willing to answer questions. You will need to do your own test prep.

Professor Jacob mostly lectures and sometimes goes kind of fast but will go back if you asked. He genuinely cares for his students and will explain anything you don't understand until you do. I had to use YouTube to really learn and understand the topic. The recitations were really helpful for review but you need to study to do well.

When I say you need to study, you NEED to study. Exam prep is practically non-existent, the final tanked my grade because he did not prep us well for the common core MCQ section. Otherwise, he's dope. Polite, respectable, a bit quiet but overall great. Homework is tedious and graded on accuracy, don't screw up and lose easy points like I did.

While I would love to place the blame for my grade on the professor, Professor Jacobs makes that genuinely difficult. He truly cares about his students and his class has a fun environment. He does not help with studying for a test, instead remarking to simply, "look over your notes". This is a hard class, so ensure you actually learn the material.
He is helpful in class with questions and cares about his students. Tests and homeworks are not easy. Lectures can be boring but he does a fairly well job conveying the material.

He is a very caring teacher. He changes the order in which he teaches to make it easier for us to understand. He emphasized no computer in his classroom (because of distractions) unless you let him know in advance for note-taking reasons, but is pretty loose with it.

He was a great professor! His lectures were clear and he always answers questions clearly. He is a tough grader, however, and he likes to focus on details. He is not a stranger to "trick questions" so study hard and make sure you understand the material. The tests are also quite hard, so you really need to know the material inside and out.
He seems passionate about math, but his lectures are boring and can be difficult to comprehend. Also, he does not prepare for the common core final much.
Dry lectures, heavy accents, and homework is graded strictly on textbook problems. Late feedback on homework. Not giving review materials for exams.

He is interested in the material he is teaching, but he's not a perfect instructor. He's lectures are definitely good, but the homework questions were not picked very well, and the turnaround for getting homework back was way too long to be useful. He also didn't seem to prepare for the common core final exam very well.

comment: Feedback was usually good, though there are a couple times I just got a mark down with no explanation. Lectures were online which made it hard to pay attention. Little help preparing for exams (why this is so low), if you don't attend the lectures you are screwed, no recording or other ways to learn material (other than text book) Homework was ez

comment: The lectures were okay but often left a lot of questions to be answered. The textbook he used was far more useful than his lectures. When he posts homework solutions there would often be missing solutions or poorly scanned pages that could not be read. The textbook was a significantly better teacher than he was.

Professor Jacob is a very passionate teacher and I thoroughly enjoyed his class. He is one of the best teachers I have every had throughout my schooling. The material was presented very neatly, and notes from the lecture were provided online after class. I highly recommend this professor.

He splits the class up into 45-minute videos you should watch before the lecture and the lecture which adds nothing to the videos which lack a large quantity and quality set of examples. Exams have few questions making them harder than they should be. The HW is terrible and it is hard to learn from. Not many ways to get feedback or practice.

Jobby Jacob is a kind man. Love his passion and enthusiasm for the subject. Any professor that gets excited about what they teach and clearly enjoys teaching it is great, and Professor Jacob has this in spades. He is good man!

Not a terrible professor but not the best either. Went into the class with no calc knowledge, and many students with calc knowledge struggled. Lectures are fine, but homework is very tedious (took me 10+hrs sometimes), and some exam problems can be harshly graded. RIT has other worse math profs, but maybe take someone else for calc1 if possible.

comment: Overall a pretty good professor. He takes the time to make sure that everyone understands the material and will gladly answer any questions. HW isn't too bad. Tests are fine as long as you study and learn the material. I walked away from the class very confident in my knowledge on the material. Also Jobby Jacob is a great name and fun to say.

I knew taking calculus again would not be a breeze, but this was not what I was expecting at all. The questions he gives for both exams and quizzes are ridiculously hard, even on simple concepts. The homework is even worse, with them sometimes taking over seven hours to complete. I would find a different Project-Based Calculus I if I were you.

comment: Dr. Jacob is a nice person, and clearly understands the material, but teaches the class as if everyone has taken AP Calculus before. He doesn't curve grades, offer bonus points, or have test corrections. Even when no one in the class has a grade higher than a C. If you go to his office hours he'll try to help you but it doesn't help much.

comment: Hands down the best Math professor I've taken at this school.

Dr. Jacob gives very informative lectures that (at least for grad courses) are mostly discussion-based and interactive. He gave extra points for "class participation," but he didn't require you to speak in class, just to pay attention. He was always available outside of class, super helpful for assignments, and he really cares about his students.

comment: Assigns an absurd amount of homework, lecture is very dull, and required a brand new textbook, with no support for earlier additions. Attendance is mandatory...

He's a super nice guy with a great sense of humour and he's actually my favourite professor. He's silly and cheeky and he likes to challenge his students. If you're looking for an easy A, this isn't it, but if you want to learn the material, he'll do everything in his power to get you what you want.

Not the best teacher, but there are definitely worse. Professor Jacob is not always the most clear in explaining something, but if you go to his office hours with a specific question, he will do his best to help explain in a better way that you will understand. Sticks to the syllabus, refer to that before asking for special treatment.

Lectures are long and boring. Often makes mistakes which will throw whole class off. Tests and quizzes have nothing to do with what we learned and the homework. Better off looking the stuff up online because you won't get anywhere in his class.
If you haven't had calc before, prepare to fail. If you have, you'll be fine.

Least helpful professor I have ever had. If you go to office hours he will answer every question with "look in your notes" and refuses to go over examples. Gives TONS of time consuming homework problems most of which will never be on a test. I felt helpless every time I didn't understand something because he is zero help outside of class.

Jacob is tough. Weekly homework that is usually quite confusing and graded harshly. Usually like 4 problems to hand in for a grade and 5 recommended problems that will take you hours. Tests are tough but fair and usually come from the homework. He curves grades in a couple ways, but an A is still quite hard to get. Not always very clear lectures.

He's one of those professors who realized they were giving out too many A's and started making everything insanely hard all of a sudden. You can't trust ratemyprofessor for this guy due to scaled (past) assessments the students give.

Professor was very very nice. He was hard to understand at times but I got used to. His tests were difficult but you would do fine if you studied. However, his tests were fair. I liked this teacher but the class had a lot of work involved.

He was an ok teacher. I felt like i understood the material in class, but the tests and quizzes are hard. The workshops are quite difficult as well. he's a nice person, but also a pretty hard grader. He gave minimal to no partial credit.
Be careful with this teacher. Quizzes are 1-2 questions and he never scales even when the class needs one. Prepare yourself for redundant work and if you want an A, that's tough to get with this guy.

This professor is horrible. His grading on homework is VERY harsh. The problems on the homework are even, so there is no possible way to check your answers unless you come in and see him. His quizzes are also very difficult. They contain 3 problems and they are extreme hard compared to what is given on the final. His tests are equally hard.
Difficult to understand accent, ridiculously long homework, absurd attendance requirement, not very useful when asked questions.

Difficult class, difficult professor. Lots (*lots*) of busywork for homework. Quiz every week, homework actually graded. Three exams. Does easy examples in class then gives the hardest ones of quizzes/exams. Good instructor but a little too much in the difficulty department.

Had him for discrete 1 & 2 and graph theory. Usually very clear in class if you pay attention, but if you have trouble he is very good at explaining things one on one in office hours. He is very likely to bump you up a letter grade if you are on the border (eg 89.0 -> A), as long as you came to class and showed that you worked hard.
Home work and exam are really hard. some homework problem are not even cover in class. Not clear explanation.
I thought that while he explained the subject well, his tests and grading were too harsh for the class. Most material was copied straight from the text.
He is good teacher explain everything well. super organize his material. very nice guy. take with him.
He is a good teacher. He really explain everything well and super organize his materiel. love him....take your class with him.
he is good professor, everything explain clearly. nice professor. take with him
Homeworks graded harshly. Weekly quizzes.  Overall a pretty good teacher.

Accent tough first week, but once you get to used it, no problem. Grades the homework a bit rough, but it doesn't count for too much. Quiz once a week, but very basic - helps you stay current. Does tons of examples and speaks in easy-to-understand language. Will not move on until the entire class is ready to. Will take again!
Accent is tough at first, grades the homework strictly
Awesome professor. His accent is a bit tricky, but once you get used to it he's really nice and very understanding.

Good math professor. Gives many examples and makes sure that there are no questions before moving on to new material. Very patient and helpful. Gives very little homework; just enough to make sure that you understand the material. Also added a very nice curve to the grade at the end of the quarter, very fair grader.
Avoid at all cost...

I also too 484 with him. He really wants students to succeed, and will give you credit for work even if you have the wrong answer as long as the process was correct. The material can be intimidating but he is very helpful in his office hours, as well as with questions in class. Lectures are manditory, and using the text is very helpful too!

comment: Amuso? More like Amus-bro! Great guy, keeps class interesting with stories from his career in industry, easy to talk to outside of class, and an extremely fair grader.
Be ready to work hard.
Dr. Amuso is very helpful and patient.  That said, his tests are very difficult and he expects much from you. I enjoyed his class overall.

Goes through material very slowly. Does not go through enough examples. Book is useless and homework problems are mostly irrelevant, but he gives you check-off points for completion. Tests can be hard but he usually curves them. An awesome guy.
Great Professor, read the book and talk to him though. Linear II is much better than I and a lot more practical applications. Practically gives you the exam questions, but with a twist

He is amazing! you will work hard, and his tests fluctuate wildly in difficulty, but he is so helpful, and he grades easy when the class does bad on a test. Entertaining guy, really cares about his students.

I had him for BME 250 (Engineering Analysis 1). Absolutely hated this class. Amuso was not fully to blame for this, he is a decent teacher and is willing to help with questions. Tests and assignments are open book/note, however this is no help when many cannot decipher the question...

Great Linear Systems (I and II) professor.   Explains the math very well but the most useful aspect is his focus on abstract thinking and good explanation of block diagrams.  Tests are usually open book and notes so write down EVERYTHING!  Take good notes and you will do very well.  He was incredibly helpful in office hours as well.
He doesn't know how to use the programs and his way of teaching is ineffective. His course is very disorganized and doesn't have a clear plan.

Eric is a good guy, he really means well. That being said, his teaching style is very scattered and thinned out. Eric isn't very well versed in digital ill., and will likely learn more than you throughout the semester. The only lessons that our class  would learn from were taught by guests. You will need to learn independently outside of class.

He always shows us the YouTube videos instead of teaching us. I did not learn anything helpful from him. If you have took the Design Drawing, you have learned everything that he showed you in Design Drawing This class is Digital drawing but you will not be asked to use the computer at the first three weeks. Moreover, he gave us low grades.

Shah is a great professor for UP1 don't let the ratings fool you. He is very fast at teaching, but always ready to help in conceptualizing content. Be weary of HW this goes for all UP1 and UP2, but he is fantastic addition to the schedule. I would say maybe later in the day once your brain is all there and warmed up. HELPED ME ALOT GOT EASY A!

Dr Shah cares about his students and astronomy, but he is not a good professor. His lectures are directly from his slides but the content between exams, quizzes, and homework varies wildly. Doesn't review exams in class and no study guides so they feel like complete shots in the dark. He will be lenient with due dates for valid reason though.

Shah is nice to talk to but does not provide any kind of clear criteria for what the exam material is going to be on. "Everything since the last one" would be fine if there was a clear set of concepts/topics, but there isnt. Weird grading: Got points off on an assignment that asked for my opinion for seemingly "picking wrong"... among other things.

Dr. Shah is a bad professor. His lectures are boring and unhelpful (rough at 8am), homework is confusing and only sorta relates to in-class material, and key concepts aren't taught well. Exams, which he provides NO study guides for, tend to vary between fair and unfair which makes the class discouraging. Don't take him unless you have to.

comment: Hridaya Shah is a very special professor. He will always engage with his students, and care for his students. The lectures and the experiments were very interactive, I personally loved it. It made me very engaged in the class and made me also really invested in further topics. He is a busy person to reach, but he cares.

He was a chill prof. The class is flipped, but the video notes, daily checks/ quizzes, and Labs are easy A's. The only reason people do bad is bc of the exams. I failed the first exam and found out the meta was just redoing all the daily checks before the exams. There's two exams and a final. Final is easy and replaced lowest test grade.

He's clearly passionate about what he's teaching, but the way he teaches just does not work. He often goes off on unrelated side tangents during lectures or just loses his point entirely, and the questions on homework and exams are phrased so confusingly that most of the work is just deciphering what he's actually asking of you.
Very nice and he really cares about the subject. Hard to relate to though. The expert TA homework were awful and unnecessary and not very helpful.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: I took his class for PHYS 104 Stars and Galaxies. It was a 2 credit course, but it felt like a 3 credit course, which surprised me. His lecture was very mediocre, and he sometimes got off track with unrelated comments on certain topics. He said it wasn't in tests, and it throws you off. I won't recommend people to take his class, that is for sure.

I had him for PHYS 220 last semester, which was his first at RIT. I don't think he was that organized and his lectures were difficult to pay attention to, even though I honestly loved the subject.
I honestly wouldn't want to take him again, though.
He's a fine guy, and is excited to answer questions, but his teaching quality was subpar honestly.
Pretty good professor who knows the material well. Homework and online quiz every week but is manageable, and exams are pretty simple. He's a nice guy.

The 2 is solely based on it being his first semester at RIT, so I'm cutting him some slack but man did this class stink. Scatterbrained lectures, long homeworks that required you to read the entire chapter he covered in class just to get a semblance of what was going on. Strangely easy exams though.

Sweet lady, but hard exams. Says to study "bigger picture," but exams had specific questions. Exams 45% of grade and you must meet w/ her to see it, no handing them back. 20% of grade is online quizzes about gene diseases with short readings with the info. iClickers require attendance (10%) and group project mostly makes up the rest of the grade.

Took her for Virology and Euk. Gene Regulation and Disease. Gives great lectures that keep you interested. Exams are conceptual and can be challenging, but as long as you take good notes and attend class, you will do fine. Very fair in grading both the exams and term long group projects. Would definitely recommend taking classes with her.

His tests are take home and open notes, which is nice.

comment: Prof. Reynolds is very friendly and engaging during lecture and encourages students to ask questions (make sure you do!). He was also accessible for help outside of office hours if you sent him an email. That being said, outside of a live setting he's mediocre. His recorded lectures were dry and the online notes were not very coherent.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Really enjoyed his class. His passion for the subject matter really shone through and enhanced my interest. Sometimes was a tough grader, but he was always willing to help with any questions you had. He gave a full week to do the exams and quizzes.

Class was more bearable after you get used to his grading expectations but everyone flopped the first quiz. Definitely do the homeworks and review quizzes for the extra points because it will save you once you forget to write a sentence and lose 50%. 10 minutes for a quiz and 10 min for submission makes you pressed for time and stressed.

Avoid if you can. This professor has historically had many problems and complaints raised against him but apparently, he and the department head are close friends. The man is incapable of teaching, his grading doesn't follow any specific rubric and takes off different points for the same wrong/incomplete answer. Bad jokes too.

He is very helpful during the lectures. he constantly asks if anyone has questions and makes sure to answer them as thouroughly as he can. Super easy class and the homework is optional which he tallies at the end of the semester as bonus points to your final grade. A good teacher overall.

The notes are crap with bad formatting (seriously, learn to use latex for mathematical expressions). Course resources are unstructured and you need to look for videos for a topic or example codes in ten different places.
harsh and petty grader, he'll mark you down for stupid little things in exams, no compassion for students in the middle of a freaking pandemic, had to teach myself everything

When I had to meet with him for my poor grades and I asked him if he could write the exams to be comprehensible he said " tough luck" When half the class failed a quiz because he didn't announcement it, he openly mocked all those students in the next class He only asks for questions, never teaches, in the zoom a-syn classes; or teaches in general
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Tough grader']

comment: Important: he stated on the first class that this is a-sync Doesn't make a mycourses post or send an email about a quiz and then sets the time limit to 30 minutes, normally all of the quizzes are 20 minutes but alright I guess. Following day, im really surprised to see that a lot students didn't do the quiz and those that did went over on time...

He gives weekly 10 minute quizzes. He cares more about writing the answer in a sentence than the actual answer. I got all 4 questions correct but didn't have time to write it in sentences and got a 60%, while the person next to me got 3 wrong and got a 70%. He's a harsh grader and his jokes aren't funny, but he's the only STAT-205 prof so good luck

The class material was easy enough that his mediocre job at explaining things wasn't so bad. He is pretty amusing, has great intentions, and knows his stuff, but I did have to consult outside materials a lot to actually grasp what he was trying to say. He is ALWAYS available to help though. But beware of the group projects everyday !
Too many quizzes and tests, it felt like there wasn't much time to actually learn and comprehend the topics. But it is not particularly hard to get a good grade.

Quizzes every day, 3+ page group busy work that you lose points on if you don't finish before class ends. Lectures run into classwork time with boomer humor. He will always find a reason to take points off, and I only got 1.11/1.11 points on classwork once. Only professor I know who removed the lectures from mycourses during online tests.

Lays out the material in a very neat and concise fashion, and walks you through examples using the software. Very helpful outside of class if you have questions regarding quizzes or homework assignments. He even helped me with a project outside of class that was related to the content.
He sucks, very unreasonable and won't listen. Also very unfunny

Reynolds does not round grades up and states you should know the material when you learned it last class. There is a quiz every class that counts at 5 points of that days total grade. You get a grade every class so if you are out sick like I was you won't do good in the class.

Reynolds is not a bad professor, but not a good one either. He is very strict on grading because he wants specific words. Also he doesn't tell you the correct answer, but makes you work to find it out. His exam is not very difficult if you understand the materials and you are allowed to have cheat sheet. You work in teams unless you don't want to.

Professor Reynolds has really clear and understandable lectures. It seems easy to not show up to his class, but don't. I did it once and was very behind for the next few days. He gives a lot of partial credit on the tricky exam questions, so try not to just give up on them. Make sure to write a solid cheat sheet for the exams.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: Professor Reynolds is good at lecturing and providing resources outside of the class. All lecture material is provided online, and 8 hours of open office hours per week were provided. Lectures arent exciting but are clear and easy to understand. Feedback is rather inconsistent on exams but can be given by asking for clarification on lost points.

He's very ambiguous on his grading criteria and he doesn't give good feedback either. I would email him and ask him specific questions, he will just respond to me very minimally and if I ask him to further explain, he will just ignore my emails. I put into a lot of effort in the assignments but he's not giving me a grade that I deserve.

He may be by far the worst professor at RIT. I am surprised that positive comments exist (but came to the conclusion that he may have wrote them himself). He is very passive aggressive. Make sure you laugh at his dad-jokes in class, he takes note of that and might even comment on it. If he notices you don't, he's the type that holds a grudge.

Prof. Reynolds gives you all of the tools you need to do well in his class. Lecture notes are stored in a shared OneNote document. Practice exams are given two classes before the real exam. Demonstrating effort on the practice exams nets up to +5% on any exam. He's always available for more review material and questions. Don't believe bad ratings.
I would say he is a good and humorous teacher. I take his morning class but I never feel sleepy. His class is interesting

Actually a very nice guy. Make concepts digestable enough. Cares to answer questions a lot. Many extra credits are available. Examples are all provided online, so no homework needed. Everything you need for test is there. However, some concepts are lightly touched but can appear on exams. Can be quite nit-picking with complete sentence answers.

He's the only prof teaching 205, which sucks for him. He tries his hardest to make the class easy to understand for the engineers required to take it. If you put in the time to go to office hours and ask him to clarify or explain concepts (or messy notes) to you, he will be happy to help. Other people here are just frustrated with stats concepts :)
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Caring']

comment: Tries to make class fun, not the best sense of humor but is really nice. Fairly easy class, work in small groups for workshop each day, and allows a cheat sheet for exams. Doesnt require textbook and only tests on stuff from class.

One thing I learned from his class is to use complete sentences. Like others have said, he will take off points if you don't do so. His tests are much harder than the problems discussed in class/packets. Make sure to come in with a cheat sheet the day of the test. His grading is very inconsistent. Be prepared for weekly quizzes. Drops lowest test.

The morning of a quiz, he emailed us saying that we needed to print out some tables in order to take it. People have things to do in the morning other than worrying about printing out a 23 page table. He didn't care to give any more advanced warning than that. Otherwise he is mediocre and uses very inefficient wording during lecture.
All his class reports are supposed to be based off what he taught for that specific day but about 50% of the material on his class reports are never based off what he taught.

He throws a lot of lame jokes, make sure to laugh, he notices and holds a grudge if you don't. Make sure to worship him like a good to fill his ego, he needs to feel powerful and mighty (some students laugh about how he is overcompensating). Tests are long and don't really match any of the material he teaches but are manageable.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Okay, since he is the only teacher for this class, it's kind of hard to say much about how he compares to others. The class is extremely difficult. If he sees you trying, he more than willing to help you out. Office hours are a little weird, but overall, they show you care. Not the nicest guy, but I learned stats.

Four exams, excluding the final (one of the non-final exams gets dropped). Some parts of the class were not made abundantly clear, such as the fact that he drops the lowest quiz. Pretty brutal when grading. Inconsistent course structure - sometimes there were lectures, other times not. Notes are accessible through OneNote. Lots of stupid dad jokes.

Very solid professor. He's not going to hand out easy grades, but there is plenty of opportunity to do well if you apply yourself. Solid notes, solid lecture, accessible for questions outside of class with helpful answers to questions, and consistently makes grading clear.

This professor is unrealistically brutal on his exams. Do all the practice you want, chances are you'll only be able to prepare for about half the points. Writing in full sentences isn't an issue but when 3/4 of the class is staying 10 minutes past the exam due time there's obviously something wrong with the exam. Nice guy but horrible professor.

Provides straight forward assignments. He gives you online notes, review bonus quizzes, and exams directly based on the quizzes. 1 take home quiz about every other week. Everything is open notes. Offers plenty of time to students outside of class. He cares that his students learn, so bring your assignments to office hours if your ever stuck!

A lot of reviews criticize his humor, but the far more glaring problem with this professor is his rigidity of grading and larger-than-life expectations on exams. Be prepared to write in full sentences on EVERY assignment, and study a lot. Made a simple class extremely over-complicated. Don't let the open note exams fool you, they're HARD!

The class is way too hard, wouldn't recommend him. He is a very nice guy on a personal level however. The questions on exams are much harder than anything you will ever see on a quiz or a review packet. On top of that, he is a savage grader. Expect to go to office hours and work harder than ever if you want to pass for such a simple gen. ed.
Pretty bad. Didn't structure the course very well. Grades rather inconsistently. I got all of the questions right on my first exam and got a 70% because I didn't use complete sentences.

Terrible Professor!!! Somehow makes a simple subject like statistics halfway impossible to learn and understand. Whats the probability of living if you jump off a bridge? (make sure your answer is in complete sentences). Consistently is not at office hours so getting help is difficult.

Although all of his notes are online, he still has mandatory attendance. He tries way too hard to be funny when he isn't. During his lectures, he doesn't make much sense and then the next class is a worksheet. ALL answers on homework and tests must be complete sentences, even if you show full work and got the right answer.
Overall terrible professor. Avoid him like the plague. Doesn't know how to lecture. Nice guy, bad professor.

If you flip two coins what is the probability of getting two heads? Did you answer .25 and move on? Then you are wrong because you didn't write a complete sentence to go with it. Horrible professor. Spends way too much time trying to be funny and arbitrarily marks entire questions wrong if you forget to explain the simplest answers.

Good prof. Lectures weren't the best and he tries too hard to crack jokes and go on tangents. Minoring in stats though because of him. He was around when needed and really knows what he's talking about. Tests aren't bad and the problems are interesting. You need to do the work though.
Hands down worst professor I've ever had. If you like bad jokes and the though of dropping out of school because of how awful this class is then he's the professor for you.

Absolute joke of a professor. He tells jokes that he thinks are funny but aren't - not even close. If he does something that is nice or human, expect to praise him like a god.  He puts huge stock into being in class, doing daily and weekly assignments yet it's such a marginal portion of the grade. Tests will make or break you. Find another prof.

One of the best math teachers I've ever had. He explains the material very clearly and will frequently stop and ask for questions from students. Online homework was tough at times, but you will have multiple attempts to get it right. He also allows index card cheat sheet for tests. If you show up to class and pay attention, you'll do fine.

Overall a decent professor. Spends too much time on easy material in the beginning and then randomly the last couple of exams are really hard.  Really funny so class isn't boring. Weekly quizzes help for the tests. Has a good review session before the final.

Reynolds is definitely a character -- in a good way! He has a  really hilarious attitude and tries to make lectures interesting. His testsquizzes are generally easy and predicable, as long as you pay attention. Don't be fooled by the easy first-half of the class, it definitely gets challenging towards the end! Don't listen to the others, take him!

I had him for STAT 205 and he was a decent professor but the material in the course isn't very interesting. If you ask questions he'll answer them and make sure everyone understands. The class is incredibly easy with no homework you have to do and easy tests and grading policies.  Attendance is taken and is part of your grade.

He attempted to engage students but due to the course material it was not effective. He takes attendance which was the only reason I  went. I took AP Stats in high school and this class is easier than that. I knew most of the material beforehand but even if you don't he makes this an easy class. Exams are short and pretty easy.
He was an awful teacher!

My experiences with Professor Reynolds is neutral. The way he explains things is so technical and confusing, that he makes the most the simplistic formula hard to understand. He is very willing to try to help you, as he offers the most office hours out all my professors. The textbook is not really necessary but the access code for MyStatLab is.

He will try to capture interest of the class with silly jokes and the like, but try to stay awake and take good notes on what he teaches. Ask for example problems, as he won't do them unless you ask and the homework is difficult without this kind of help. Study hard for tests and make good notecards (very helpful! Do not underestimate)
Was by far the worst professor I've ever had at RIT !!!

posts all notes online, is available outside of class for extra class, tests are challenging but he offers a huge extra credit quiz at the end of the semester. daily homework assignments as well as weekly quizzes that are all online. textbook is not needed, only online access code . even with the notes online, still show up to class everyday!

I went from having a high B to a D in less than two classes. He spends a lot of time on bad jokes. His equations produce incorrect responses on myStatsLab. He as manually changed the times that assignments are due, WHILE you're in class, from the next day to before the class started. Takes points off for irrelevant reasons. doesn't provide feedback

I recieved a C, 79.5, wouldn't round it. Test and quiz questions were poorly worded and made it so that no one had any idea what he was asking. Avoid taking at all costs, I don't know how he is still employed at RIT. Made class attendance worth 10% of grade. Posted class notes online. Refused to post quiz/test solutions to mycourses.

Horrible Teacher. Students actually lash out back at him DURING class. His methods for teaching aren't sound. For example, he'll assign homework and then have a quiz later the same week, and the homework doesn't help with what's to be expected on the quiz. Office hours are Ok at best, but with an intro course more instruction should not be needed.

Avoid this teacher like the  PLAGUE. Absolutely the worst teacher in existence. How he has a job is absolutely beyond me. I think he takes joy in stumping his students. His tests don't cover material from class. His classes barely give you a basic understanding of the material. Overall the worst experience ever. Don't make the same mistake.
He is unable to teach. Do not take his class!

Absolute worst professor I've had. His exams were not on the in-class material, he rarely gave example problems, and wouldn't explain why/how a problem on an exam was incorrect. Also unhelpful outside of class. Brought my 3.8 GPA down significantly.

Avoid at all costs. He has no leniency or mercy when he grades and it seems that his personal mission is to make sure you get the least amount of points possible on questions where you didn't give him the exact perfect answer he was looking for.

He seems to be a nice guy, and teaches well enough for me to understand. But I swear that he prolong his lectures on purpose so everyone will have to stay in class longer. And he is one of the worst, no, he is THE WORST grader. It has to be his way/wording or it is wrong, even if it means the same thing. RIDICULOUS.

He was a TERRIBLE teacher. He will take off points for any reason, even if you obviously show you know the topic. His class structure is a pain in the ass: daily assignments in class, daily assignments online, and weekly assignments. Awful. Please avoid this teacher.

He looks for reasons to fail students. Not helpful or understanding at all. 30 seconds late with turning assignments into class he will not accept your work. Even if the clock in class in wrong. If there Is a Fire drill during an exam- he will expect you to finish the exam and not curve it.
Probably the worst teacher I have had. The day before the final he took the notes offline and no one was able to study. Avoid him.

At first he seems like a decent guy. But he hates to be wrong, he hates to explain things so you can understand them, and he hates to be helpful. I am always really fair to rating professors, but this guy is seriously one of the worst RIT has to offer.
Really teaches the fundamentals, which helps with all subsequent data classes. He may be stricter than the other professors but his style is easy to understand.

He's a good person, but his teaching skills are awful. He teaches extremely fast, almost never takes a breath, and leaves the class feeling confused. You never do class work, if you want explanations you need to go to the group "office hours" right after class which conflict with nearly everyone's schedule. Avoid this guy.

Professor Reynolds did not know how to teach if it wasn't for his teaching assistant none of us would have made it through his class. The assistant basically had to reteach everything after class. It was all wrong.

Seems to be a good person but TERRIBLE teacher! Do not take him unless you absolutely have to! He leaves things out in his lectures and then makes them worth heavy points in quizzes/tests. Grades very harshly for no real reason. Homework objectives are unclear and harshly graded.

Avoid at all costs! My class's homework average is consistently a 51%. He is only interest in showing you how much he knows, your learning is completely irrelevant to him. There is a definite reason he was suspended three years ago, and they should have never hired him back.

Very nice guy, his jokes are so bad they are funny, but sometimes they actually help you learn.  He is very helpful and available and will even stay after class to talk.  He presented the material clearly and organized.  He allows you to bring a note sheet for tests.  I am good at math so this was an easy class for me.

THIS GUY IS AWFUL! I could not understand anything in class, his teaching skills are horrible. I would always email him to get one on one help and he would NEVER respond. Whenever I went into his office there were always 5 other people in there trying to get help as well. VERY DIFFICULT.

I don't understand all of the hatred for this guy.  I had him for data 1 and he presented the material VERY clearly, graded fairly, and made the class about as interesting as it could be. Easy A if you show up and do your homework.

HORRIBLE, Worst teacher I have ever had here. Grades horribly, takes off for random things without explanation. Everyone fails test/quiz. NOT FUNNY AT ALL (thinks he is). Makes assignments due at 4:00 exactly and takes off of 4:01. DO NOT TAKE EVER UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES unless you want to teach yourself the whole class.

By far the worst prof. I have ever had. I am in his class right now. Be thankful of online HW. As his grading is TOUGHER than the online assignments. I dont think he curves grades but he should, no one seems to do well. I don't know whats worse is teaching or his jokes, but both are horrible. DO NOT! Take his classes, under any circumstances.

TERRIBLE pacing. No slides. Inarticulate test questions. Terrible review for quizzes/tests. Hard grading. Requires online homework. Requires lab-computer only work. Both are irritating and would better on paper. Answers questions- but expect to ask about *EVERY* *SINGLE* *EXAMPLE*. Complete waste of time- take it with someone else.

Terrible, I only took his class because it fit my schedule and it was one of the worst mistakes of my life. I was constantly going for extra help and he would just make me more confused. He nit-picked absolutely everything with his grading. I would avoid him at all costs if you want to pass Data I.

I feel he is seriously one of the worst professors i have ever had with 6 months before graduation. Blows through material and does not post relevant stuff online. He is not funny in the least, but will drag jokes for (5-10) minutes during class. Avoid at all costs, he just got his masters.

Assigns 3 homeworks a week, and actually punishes students for mistakes he makes. Is not nearly as funny as he thinks he is. Why do math professors insist on online homework? Its the dumbest thing. Just hand me a paper with the problems on it. Stop being lazy and actually grade the work you assign. If its the department's fault, RIT math sucks.
i'm taking his DA1 class right now. i'm serious he is a bad teacher. everyone fails his tests and quizzes.

I took Data II with this professor last year and got a B. I'm typically weak in math and have to work really hard at it. It's a tough class  but you have to pay attention and ask questions. I had no trouble asking for help and even felt free to seek help during his office hours. No excuse for not asking for help when he's so available and nice.

Wanted to take the class over the summer to get it over and done with. 5 weeks in and I'm failing the course. I made a B in Data I and I'm an Honors Student. This man just cannot teach. He believes students should understand the material the first time. I didn't feel comfortable asking for help. I had to withdraw. Tra was supposed to teach not him.

I found the class to be relatively easy. If I had any questions, he was able to answer them. The classes usually didn't run the full 110 minutes. He does place an unnecessary emphasis on formatting though. Even though I understood everything on the tests, I would still get 10-15 points off due to formatting. He allowed a page of notes on tests.

do the homework. ask questions. don't screw around during lecture.. ASK QUESTIONS. very organized, will work with you and repeat all of the material and restate information different ways until you get it. Good prof if YOU communicate.

Well besides the content normally being fairly easy.  His teaching style is horrid, and do not look at the practice tests they will hurt you more than help.  Makes tests extremely hard. Avoid like AIDS!!!

DOES NOT KNOW HOW TO TEACH, expect to teach yourself the material if you want to pass the class, I completed and had 100 on every homework assignment, failed 1 test and received an academic alert because I was failing the class and had to withdraw.

The class is really easy if you've taken calc in highschool, if not, pay attention and do your homework. Seriously, if you take the time to study the material it isn't really that hard.  Gives a formula sheet during exams and doesn't expect problems to be reduced; if you can keep up, you'll do ok.
Cannot teach so you end up teaching yourself from the textbook.  Also goes far to fast the other classes have only done two thirds to half of what we have covered.
Very bad teacher doesn't know how to teach.  I agree he's smart guy but he cant explain anything I had to withdraw from the class because I would have an F in the class
No Comments

Hardest grader you've ever seen. He just got his Masters a few months ago and thinks he knows it all. Nice guy but take exactly Zero feedback from the students. Does examples fast and only once and expects you to remember it all. Self taught class unless you always know it. I took it for an easy A and I'm failing. Avoid like the plague!

Show up, participate, engage. Due dates are flexible, and Prof. Duncan is almost always willing to work with students if something doesn't work for them. No textbooks, but a lot of reading! At least skim the articles and have something to say during discussions.
Does a great job walking you through the writing process on each essay assignment, provides great feedback, and is a flexible/light grader.

Professor Duncan is a great teacher, she takes a lot of time to talk to students one on one during class and is very active if you have any questions. She is also very accommodating to students for late work or missed classes (as long as you communicate).
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback']

comment: Professor Duncan is a good professor for this class. Considering it is a graduation requirement, she knows that people have lives outside of her class, and will often make accommodations with students for late work or missed classes. The class work was simple and I would definitely take her again if I had to retake this class.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback']

comment: I liked Prof. Duncan! Her grading was lenient, she gave helpful feedback on essays, and late work was fine. She is younger and was chill and relatable. My only complaint is how much she talked about "coming to terms" with reading/writing, and how writing is a conversation. She does take attendance, I wish I had counted how many times I was absent.

Caring and was understanding about the fact that people have things going on in their lives outside of class. The class consisted of a weekly online forum post, a couple of brief presentations, some essays, and small readings outside of class. I wasn't looking forward to taking the class, but Duncan made it a bearable experience.

Duncan was really great, she cares a lot for her students, was very understanding, and tried her best to make the class interesting. I was initially not thrilled to take this class, but after having it with Duncan I can honestly say I enjoyed the class.

ENGL 210. Her grading policy was reasonable and clear. nothing was graded too harshly and the 2 books we read were pretty easy and interesting. occasional movies and only one homework assignment per month. A nice person seems to care about her students.
tags: ['Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']

comment: took molecular bio lab with him. very chill guy he doesn't grade the lab reports. the final exam was hard tho especially for a lab

I had Dr. Savka for molecular biology lab. He is a good teacher and a tough grader for writing assignments, but probably the most lenient grader available in this course. He likes to talk a lot before labs which can be a bit frustrating, but overall he's pretty helpful. He's willing to look over writing assignments before you submit them!!
I took the molecular bio lab with him. not a bad professor can be very helpful if you reach out

Slides were super text heavy which made studying hard and overwhelming. Tests were nearly impossible to get a good grade on. This professor complained that making multiple choice test questions was too hard, so the exams were mainly short answer. He can be lenient with grading. He is a very nice guy however I would not recommend him for a teacher.

He is a very funny professor who cares a lot about the subject matter. Depending on the lecture, he would bring in chocolate or we would brew coffee. Tests are a little difficult but he is a fair grader and is willing to give points back.

I liked him as a person, but he had a tough time teaching my bio 125 class because some students in the back were disrespectful and he wasn't used to it and didn't try hard to stop it. He was very good at helping students understand the material if students didn't distract him.
you actually need to know your stuff for his class but that just made me more interested in the material. I mean i didnt do great in his class but definitely a decent teacher.

Another quality biology professor at RIT. Tests hard and gets frustrated that he dosn't know how to teach the material. Struggles to pronounce words he reads right off his own power point. A weasily little man.

His tests are difficult and you need to understand/know the material well.  His classes can drag but he throws a joke here and there.  He does know his stuff, he's not really just reading off slides, he explains
He has difficult tests and you have to study for them.  funny at times.  need to know everything.  devote yourself seriously.
If you take his class you are making the biggest mistake of your life. He does not know how to teach and his test are impossible! He tries to be funny but fail at it! His is not approachable at all!
Tests are HARD! Classes are boring and he drags on for half the allotted 3 hour lab time. Do not recommend.

Tests are horrible.  He's nice, but a little boring. Rarely adds anything to ppt in lecture so absence doesn't hurt.  Too much material for most people (even brainiacs) to memorize in the time allowed in RIT's miserable quarter system.  Don't get me started on that.

An ok teacher. Tests are really ridiculously hard. Must know to heart ALL material whih is almost impossible. Teaches like you'd assume tests and material are easy, but no. Labs were ok but kind of the same thing over and over. Overall just ok... and be prepared for the evil tests!
A little too animated for my taste.
Good teacher, not that great in intro to cell bio but in plant biotech he has more interest for the material. Tests are a little tough but if you keep up you should do fine.
so boring... slept through every single class because i just couldn't keep my eyes open
Ted is a great professor, show up, and show you care. Truly wants the best for you inside and out of class.
Great professor, wish we would have cooked more though.

Lectures were engaging. Class was easy and easy to participate in. Grades were all submitted quite late, but I think personal issues were the cause of this, and wouldn't expect this to continue. Was funny and helpful, learned a lot.

I don't know why this guy has such bad reviews...he is unclear in his delivery of information and does not respond to e-mails in a timely manner, however if you do ask him a question and he can not help you he takes that into consideration with grading. If you attend class, listen, and put effort into your work you will get an A.

He knows what he is talking about, but his delivery of the material is very rough. Kind of a strange personality and he usually seems overwhelmed. You constantly have to remind him of things. Don't expect a response if you email him for at least a week.
Extremely boring and confusing professor. Hes kind of young, and it seems like he wants to fit in with everybody, and it just doesn't work. Completely incomprehensible when teaching a class.

Chris Lyons is the absolute best professor, and person. He genuinely cares about you and your goals, but will push you really hard to achieve them. He's always there when you need him with honest feedback and real advice. Chris has made my time worth it and I have improved and achieved everything because of what he has taught me.

The best prof you can get in the design school. Take every class possible with him. His real world experience will inspire and motivate you. If you expect to pass without working your ass off, go home. He's the best, prove yourself worthy to be in his presence!

well, as "real world" as it gets and he knows how to get good (or great, depending) work out of his students. He doesn't play favorites, though if you show initiative and demonstrate that you get it, it'll help you in the long run- being when you graduate, love RIT

If you can't apply yourself in Chris's class, change your major. He's as "real world" as it gets and he knows how to get good (or great, depending) work out of his students. He doesn't play favorites, though if you show initiative and demonstrate that you get it, it'll help you in the long run- being when you graduate, and have to get a real job.

everybody's favorite teacher.  the dude ROCKS.  but he's not easy.  learned a lot about myself, and what I'm really good at. he really cares about his students, and helps you understand your career options.  wish I had him before senior year.  my book improved muuuuuuuucho grande from working w/this guy.  thanks chris.  you're awesome.
he knows what he's talking about.  he does not allow people to make excuses for****ty/unfinished work. he is extremely critical and pushes you to work your hardest.
Very straight forward, very down to earth. Class was informative and helpful. Chris is highly recommended, and a nice guy

She's extremely knowledgeable about marketing, especially with her experience in the industry which she will mention a few times. Her lectures can be a bit boring but they're pretty straight forward. She's really nice and caring and gives great feedback.
Nothing to say. Meh, boring lectures, standard text brook autogrades. Doesnt seem to care much but easy grader.

Nothing overwhelmingly good or bad about Professor Chung. Pretty much standard across the board, both in lectures and grades. As a design student it was difficult for me to get through her daily lectures without dozing off. Could definitely work in some engagement outside of random questions to liven up lectures, but otherwise I have no complaints.

One of the best teachers I've taken. She makes me want to pursue a marketing minor. Her teaching style is great, she is consistent with her PowerPoint slides and her lecture. I highly recommend taking her!

Dr. Chung is extremely knowledgeable and cares about what she is teaching. Her industry experience is evident as they provide many first hard stories from their time working at Nike. Attend office hours, they are useful. Dr. Chung wants her students to succeed. The class is set up with a clear outline in the syllabus. Use the study guide, it helps

Chung is a wonderful professor that is well experienced in the marketing field. Her lectures are to the point and are a great learning experience. For recitations you will be continuing what was learned in lecture as well as the beginning of a semester long group project so choose partners wisely or you'll be screwed

Dean is amazing. Knows and loves what he's teaching. Go to office hours and ask for help if you need it, he's incredibly supportive. I still go to him to this day for database questions and he's always happy to answer.

For ISTE432 wasnt in the list of selectable classes. Super helpful professor, gave feedback, talked to each group in class asking us questions giving us guidance. He answered our questions even when they werent related to the course, just our careers and lives in general. He cares a lot about his students. Answered my emails over the summer quickly
One of my favorite professors at RIT. Extremely knowledgeable but isn't afraid to call himself out when he messes something up. I can tell he genuinely cares about student success and wellbeing.

I don't think I've had a more supportive professor at RIT. His class material is quite frequent and it's a bit difficult, but he's always open to help even outside of office hours. I had him for two separate classes this semester and he really helped quell my stress at certain times during that period. Super friendly, super helpful, easy recommend.

Don't think twice for taking his course! The curriculum was great & he is an awesome professor. The classes were fun, it made me want to participate more & good grades just followed. Homework was not as much & I was able to finish them even if I started on the last day. The assignments were great & the exams were based on what he taught in class.

While he expects work from you, he puts in an equal amount of effort to prep for his lectures. The course work is well designed and relevant. Be prepared for quizzes in every class and a lot of textbook reading (which actually helps) . He is very accessible and helpful. The best part about his class is - loads of coding! It is a great course.

I really liked this course. Honestly, I am a slow learner & always thought that this course was tough but now looking back, it was really fun and I ended up learning a lot of new cool things. The lectures are very interesting & prof makes it fun with his witty jokes. I have an attention span of 10 mins & still ended up well.

Great guy, course curriculum is pretty good. I feel like the projects can be worked on a little bit (the second one, especially. Getting data for each tab and filling it manually quickly becomes repetitive and a little boring). Definitely would recommend though, if you want to learn JS from the ground up. PS: Why wasn't promises covered? :(

He is a nice guy. But he doesn't have clear requirements. So when it comes to project, he grades on what he thinks, and he is very restricted about grades. Also, he does not cover enough topics to cover, he just writing code. I don't think he has a professor vision, he could be Youtuber recording videos about coding, not a professor.

Dean is a really solid choice for a professor. Had him for both 240 and 252. For 252 he is clear about what he wants for projects and follows the rubric exactly when grading. Responsive to questions both in person and over e-mail. You will learn from him, so take him if you can.

Amazing professor. Class is relatively easy if you know some code and pay attention at all. Be ready for daily quizzes. Projects may be time consuming but are necessary. Homework can be usually done in about an hour. Everything he teaches is valuable, so learn it.
