comment: Great choice as a web 2 instructor. He knows his stuff and teaches it well. He does assign a lot of overlapping assignments and his grading is a little rough for projects but as long as you stick to the rubric you should be fine.

A fine instructor who knows the materials related to the course well. He gives good feedback on assignments and projects. He assigns a lot of tasks especially homework and 4 separate projects (group and individual)

Dean is a great professor with a few shortcomings. His lectures and in-class exercises are great, but sometimes his grading criteria can be a little difficult to understand. Some homework/project requirements were worded poorly and led to many students missing that requirement. Otherwise, he's a good choice for Web II.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Dean is an amazing professor. He made Web 2 fun and understandable. He is very clear when teaching and will always answer your questions well. Just make sure you always pay attention during class or you will get very lost very quickly. He grades tough but fairly, so just do all the things on the rubric. Probably the best prof for Web 2.

This is my second class with Dean, and hopefully not the last. Dean is the most caring, inspirational, and effective professor I've ever had. I always retain everything from his lectures, he's a friend to the students more than a professor, and is super available outside of class for help. Dean is an amazing human being and the best professor ever.
Get ready to work.

He is the best instructor I have met. He is always there for you. So sad that he only teaches small amount of courses. I would take what ever courses he teaches. On the other hand, he is a rough grader, especially for the individual project. There is only one test, two projects and about 15 homework. Best class ever!

He is a great teacher. A quiz almost every class but there like 3 questions long on material covered in the previous class so you should do fine if you can recall the info. A really chill guy. No extra credit so do the work. When hw is late he takes of 10% for each day late (better than not letting us turn it in at all). A good teacher to have!

Good professor. Very helpful if you go in during office hours or send him emails. Not too much work and you do not need much programming experience to understand what to do. Make sure you go to class and pay attention as for this class we had quizzes every day over the lecture material.
H e was very helpful and supportive for every student in his class. I highly recommend him for your web class.

Really great guy. One of the best professors I ever had. He supports his students of all skill levels and wants to see you succeed. He is not to serious and leads a pretty laid back - but very interactive lecture. Works in industry so he knows his stuff. He even will extend talented students potential jobs if he happens to find them. 1010
Great teacher and is always willing to help.  Outside of class, he is great at responding email most of the time. I definitely recommend this guy!
I learned lot of materials in class and it's worth taking him for Web II.
you can tell he enjoys the subject that he teaches. He is a fair grader, just start his work early enough to get it finished.

Dean provides a lot of examples in his lectures and is able to communicate course material very well. His assignments are not overly difficult and he is extremely helpful when you ask for help. He's very casual and laid back. Most importantly, he can relate to his students effectively.

Great teacher, always fair, will help you whenever needed.  Had to text him a few times and responds quickly.  Does teach by example that helps greatly with programming.  I would strongly suggest him.  Very down to earth  guy who is easy to talk to.  Great Prof.

By far the best Prob/Stats prof.  Gives handouts for each class with examples and explanations. Daily quizzes but lowest 3 are dropped. Quizzes help you understand the material. Tests were somewhat long but he gives you a lengthy equation sheet. Highly recommend.

Super sweet man. Had a tough time following his lectures, very dull.  Quizzes are easy if you follow the hints he gives on syllabus. Exams were long, but very easy if you did well on the quizzes.  Don't be alarmed at first, he's very soft spoken, but willing to help.

Nicest prof I've met so far at RIT. He is genuinely excited about statistics and insanely smart, as he commonly points out the maker of the book is wrong,and likes to disagree with famous stats people
He is really good teacher. I really enjoyed his class....he will help you whenever you have the question. he gives exam and quiz whatever he cover in class. good teacher....take with him.

He is a good professor. He explain really clearly and every day you will have a quiz but those quiz form whatever he cover and he will let let you know which one will cover. Easy and nice professor. He loves to help student. Take with him...

His tests and quizzes are very easy, HOWEVER, he is not clear at all and you literally feel like you are learning nothing. He tells you useless information that takes away from the lesson and at times makes no sense. After the first 3 weeks I felt like I was going to die. DO NOT TAKE HIM BECAUSE HE IS EASY, YOU WILL REGRET IT!!!!!!

Very nice guy.  The first two exams are easy, but the final is very hard if you don't actually understand the concepts, so make sure you keep your grade as high as possible going into the final.  Requires no homework, but does suggest problems to work on for better understanding.  Did a pretty good job of explaining the material in class.

Extremely easy class but you'll learn something too. Quizzes and exams are open book and lots of review problems are given to make grades a piece of cake. If you miss a class, Farnsworth will make sure you get caught up and is willing to help you succeed. Definitely the best professor for Engineering Statistics!

Farnsworth is the best professor in the math department. He obviously cares that his students learn and he puts in a lot of effort to help you out. He makes all old quizzes and exams going back years available online. All tests and quizzes were open book, and you can write in the book. As long as you make it to class, you will do well with him.
Quizzes are in nearly every class.  Posts old quizzes and tests which help with the current one.  Speaks softly.

I didn't know how to do any of this stuff before and I still don't. I memorized equations and just barely passed the class. He was horrible at understanding questions. I couldn't wait to get out of that class. He doesn't explain anything at all. Now I have to suffer through DA2
So easy...didn't do any work! DEF highly recommended!!!!  Posts online tons of old quizzes and tests to help out as well.  Easy easy!

nicest man you could ever meet in your life, but honestly i cant analyze data after taking his data analysis class.  i memorized how to do the problems and had no idea what they mean so the final screwed me
Nice guy but not a good teacher at all,  i know i could have done a lot better under a different teacher.
Great teacher!  Easy to learn from and tests are simple with a little studying and effort.

He's a really nice professor, and teaches well too.  Always available for help.  Homework was optional and quizzes were easy, but tests were tricky...especially because he chose certain questions to be worth about half the test, and if you didn't know how to do it, you'd basically be screwed.  Plus, the final was a beast.
Nice guy.  Easy class.  He hands you an A.  But not in the sense that you didn't learn anything.  He teaches you too...
Very Easy class. He makes the quizzes just like the priactice ones on the web, just with differant numbers. Skips the Method of Moments in favor of mor Hypthosis testing.

She was honestly a good professor, it was an asynchronous course and as far as i remember it was 3 tests, 2 presentations and 2 discussion posts. Nothing felt too heavy, just put in enough work and you're guaranteed a good grade. She also gave us a bonus assignment and she did overlook an issue i had in a ppt and still gave me the full score.

comment: Once she grades assignments, even if you submit them before the deadline, won't grade resubmitted work with feedback.

Solid professor, gives a good kind effort through the semester and is really understanding about issues during the semester. Exams were all online and projects were pretty simple if you put in a little effort.

An intro to film class that i used as a perspective and this teacher seemed to think that we were majoring in film. There was long discussion board posts, tests, a group presentation , and you have to do an individual powerpoint that is 15 slides long. She takes this class entirely too seriously and there's way too much work for a film course.

Really nice professor! Her lectures were pretty interesting and based on various different readings. Tests were based on readings and lectures, so easy as long as you attended class. Given a lot of freedom when creating our final project.
Lectures are interesting and relevant. The assignments and tests are really easy, just show up and pay attention with an open mind and you will be fine.

I took ECON211 with her it was one of the worst decisions I have ever made. The course grade was almost purely based on the 4 exams, 3 of them making up 93% of the final grade. She is very often late to lectures, always makes mistakes on the exams, and the exam questions are sometimes not even related to her lecture slides. Do NOT take her class.

She seems incredibly unprepared for many lectures. Routinely gets lost in her notes, does not explain the material well, or at all. Has, without fail, had multiple errors in her exams (that being grammatical or conceptual). She additionally does not seem to have the capacity to answer questions, despite many being asked during lecture.

Avoid taking this professor at all costs! Terrible professor, completely unprofessional, and doesn't care about students' grades. Shows up late to multiple lectures and constantly has to be corrected by students for incorrect calculations. Expect to learn on your own from the lecture slides, which are years old and don't correspond to the exams.

. Wants you to succeed
. Gives great explanations when confused
. Make use of her office hours, they are quite helpful as well.

Shes very knowledgable and open to assistance but lacks energy. I often get bored or just confused by the way she explains things. I recc her only because she is super nice and willing to help. ECON is hard and you will prob have to go to her office hours often and study a lot. I had her for both ECON 201&433 and wish she had more practice problems

Dr. Ko was pretty fair overall. There wasn't much homework and of what there was it was easy. The exams were take home, cumulative, timed multiple choice, which was stressful; I recommend keeping her lecture notes open and study with the homeworks. She also does a lot of examples in class before exams that are sometimes identical to exam questions.

This class is only lectures. She goes through slides for the entire class and rarely does practice problems. Grade is based on 4 exams, 10 HW and a final assignment. Tests are Cumulative and very hard. There are a lot of questions for the amount of time given. Pay close attention to lectures and ask for clarification if she goes too fast.

The class is very lecture heavy and your grade is based on 4 exams, 10 homework assignments, and a final assignment. The tests are online, cumulative, and very hard as there are too many questions in the allowed time. There is no extra credit, but there is a curve at the end of the semester. Pay very, very close attention to her lectures.

The class is very lecture heavy so you can get bored super easily but she can teach relatively well if you can pay attention closely. Her exams are extremely hard, they are somewhat accumulative and she gives way too many questions for the time period we were given. Homework for every chapter/week.

comment:
Matt is a nice professor. The lecture can be either boring or exciting, depending on your mood. 

You are likely to pass the exams thanks to the important and helpful study notes provided by Matt. 

If you overcome the poor overall grade, you may be lucky enough to have the opportunity to earn extra credit.

Really great professor and really great class. The class was a lot of work. So don't take the online class unless you can manage your time well. There are a ton of tests, but you are given a huge time period to work on them when it's convenient for you. 4 receptive tests and 3 expressive tests, 1 paper, weekly practice. Never answers emails.
She's a good professor but gets fed up with questions easily. Especially when it comes to tests and mycourses.

Prof. Briggs is a great professor! She moves quickly through class but is completely willing to repeat herself as many times as needed. There's a lot of practice in class which prepares you perfectly for her exams.

Professor Briggs was a great teacher and she was always willing to help you in class if you were having difficulty understanding a sign or topic.  I would highly recommend any student to her.  Also, she has a working dog with her that is absolutely adorable.

Tests are cumulative and may contain signs that are not covered in the textbook but are considered in class.  Class could be annoying because we would spend a lot of time practicing.  If you have a strong pictorial memory, then you should do fine in ASL.
Each absence is 10% off your final grade. Don't take a class with this teacher. She is way too strict and the class is boring.

Professor Briggs is a great ASL teacher and exhibits the immense patience of the Deaf community. I had her for ASL1 and she seemed like the perfect fit. My only complaint is that her one of her assignments was slightly unclear; it was difficult to obtain an article we were supposed to read.

Good Teacher, not great. She knows her signs and is a Deaf professor and like all ASL teachers is very good at communicating with lower level signs.  She is very strict for grammar which I think is a plus.  Her tests are fairly easy, but inconsistent difficulty from test to test.  Recommend this teacher, but I know there are others who are better

I had her for cognitive psych. she is very laid back. lectures are entertaining. she lets you use a cheat sheet for tests but there is ALOT of possible material to be covered. could be a bit more clear about her expectations for group projects and things like that. however i got an A in the class and really enjoyed it!
She is a great teacher. I have taken her classes before. She makes the class interesting and easy to understand. Very helpful.
Seemed nice, answered questions, really helpful with problems.

I also don't get why people think shes so bad, her lecture are entertaining. She's nice and willing to explain anything if you ask, besides that shes nice and not that strict. She lets you have a cheat sheet for the test and the test is mostly lecture stuff. Overall there are way worse professors at RIT and I would take her again.

She's really not that bad. I had her for cog psych over the summer (two hours do days a week) and it wasn't THAT bad. I was reading these comments and it makes her seem horrible. You just have to ask if you don't understand anything. I went to almost all the classes, kind of studied a little, and got a B. Shes not THAT bad.

Hart is probably a good person who is NOT cut out to be a professor. Her lectures are extremely unclear, she often makes mathematical errors during her lectures, and she is extremely unorganized. I'm never taking a course with her again.

Overall, I really liked this class. Dr. Hart's teaching style is very chill...which allows a student some room for mistakes (getting things in late). There really weren't that many assignments, and the tests were pretty easy. The group research project is super easy and MUCH better than having to write a research paper like in other psych classes!

I don't feel like I learned that much in this class that I didn't already know. She allows you to have a note sheet during exams, and the exams are made from the power point slides. She also isn't the most helpful prof... especially when it comes to explaining what to do for the group research project.
Lazy.  Always on her phone.  Brings her kids to class.  Inconsistent with her words.  Isn't prompt.  Not friendly.
Seems like a nice person, but extremely unclear on assignments and due dates; overall her class was very confusing and unclear. Lacks the rigor a professor needs.

Shes not a bad teacher but she i boring. She is unclear about everything, will not tell u about test before u take them. She does let u use cheat sheets typed in any font which u use her slides. the tests are hard but not unmanageable or impossible. Lecture is extremely boring but she doesnt care if u sleep. over okay teacher. but try to aviod.
I wasn't expecting to enjoy cog psych, but it was actually pretty fun. Prof Hart seemed to know what she was talking about. I would take her again.

She acted as though she did not care about teaching, made multiple excuses for why papers were late and for absences. At the end of the quarter I had no idea what my grade was. She was also very bad at replying to e-mails. She was too relaxed about our class with her absences and lack of communication about grades and project requirements.

She brought her kids into class on a few occasions.  She was supremely unclear as to how the running project for the whole quarter was to be set up and gave no advice (including basics such as page length) unless asked.  She constantly is 2-3 weeks late giving back tests and you never know how well you are doing in her class.  Horrible teacher.

Brought her kids to class and had them sit in the corner.  Very distracted and uneven in her presentation of information.  Said ummm and ahhh so much that I stopped paying attention.  Returned tests and quizes late on a regular basis.  I would not take another class in which she is the instructor.
Overall, a very bad professor. She obviously has other things that she would rather do than teach.

Prof. Hart is a very laid back teacher. She is rather quiet, but she really relates to her students. All you need to do to pass her take home tests are take notes in class and write directly from them. She tends to not be the most punctual teacher, but that means she will let you slip in that respect. Overall, there are worse Psych profs.
She is a pretty good teacher, tries to connect with students, seems to really like teaching.
SHE OBVIOUSLY DOES NOT WANT TO TEACH!
Incompetent. She will fail you if you disagree with her liberal views.
Does not grade fairly. Is not prompt at returning papers. Does not appear to be knowledgeable in the subject area.

Unclear in course outline/syllabus, inconsistent and arbitrary grading techniques, slow in grading, often unprepared and late did not give appropriate amount of time for preparation to have an effective class.

Teaches the course very effectively, and gives insight along with each topic. Good sense of humor and easy to talk to. Also very understanding of mitigating circumstances. Great professor overall, and one that I would highly recommend for anyone interested in Psychology.

Professor Warp provided a very warm and welcoming class. She makes sure to meet with all students almost every day to make sure everyone's staying on track. There was not too much work outside of class. I learned a lot about design

Very sweet and genuine professor. Projects pretty open-ended but still had clear guidelines. Heavy on group feedback which I enjoyed. A little more relaxed than I'd like only because I feel like some students took advantage of her a bit. Fun class; would take her again. Take advantage of the labs PLEASE!

She's a very kindhearted + knowledgeable professor, frequently accessible outside of class, but her lectures were dry + her critiques were timid and wishy-washy. My section had a large chunk of computing/non-NMDE students and she did a good job explaining Photoshop and Illustrator techniques in a way that made sense for us all. Fairly easy class.

Melissa is genuinely such a nice professor. Taking her class was a pleasure and I wish I had been able to get into a course of hers next semester. She meets you at your ability level and gives critiques that are realistic for you. She's super understanding and while she says her deadlines are hard, I haven't actually found that to be the case.
Professor Warp is such a supportive professor. She is so knowledgeable on the subject and gives great and thorough feedback. I hope I have her again!

I love Melissa, and I'm lucky to have been able to take many classes with her. She is one of the kindest people I have ever met and is very supportive and helpful when it comes to your work. Sure, she is not very critical but all of the other NMD profs really are, so her and her class are a nice break. I've learned so much from her regardless!

Kindest teacher I've ever had. I do wish she would be more critical to the designs, but she gives good feedback and the assignments are pretty fun. She's clearly experienced in the design world and is a good lecturer.

She's not very good at feedback, kind of scared to be honest with you. Like if your work is bad she wont really tell you, just be nice about it which isn't good in the long run. Projects are pretty easy if you just listen to her lectures and spend time.

Melissa is an amazing professor! Her due dates and projects are reasonable, but not too easy where the class becomes a bore. Her lectures tend to drag a bit, but the info she gives is important. She makes sure to give individual feedback to her students and she really tries to connect with them. I would highly recommend taking her class!

Such a sweet hearted and caring professor - she is very interested in the field she is working in and the work of the students. Professor Warp doesn't belittle your work and gives great feedback to help you develop your own style no matter the current level of skill.

Professor warp is the best. She gives good feedback and is very knowledgeable with Adobe products. She shared her industry experience and gives good insights on what clients like and dont like. She has a great personality and I would take her again if I could.
Gives out clear criteria of projects. Lectures are pretty dense and filled with concepts but tries to make it interesting. Gives good feedback about work.

I would never take this professor again. The amount of work given is insane, at least 3 to 4 in depth research based assignments per week. His grading is awful because he takes off points for no reason, even if you thought you did your work exactly how he asks. There are also weekly quizzes that require too many sources. Avoid this professor.

How do I say this. No matter how specifically you try to cite what he asks you to cite he will dock you for no reason and give the worst feedback known to man for the most mundane, brain wrenching assignments. This class shouldn't be this hard but it is extremely frustrating because his grading is just lazy. Avoid him at all costs.

This course is insanely difficult for no reason. Professor Gassama gives "try hard" a new meaning. All of the tested material is insanely specific and is to be pulled from 6 different resources without access to notes.

Professor Gassama and his assistant are such try hards. They give little to no assistance with assignments and have the hardest assignments based off of two books, videos, slideshows, and additional lecture material. I will NEVER take another class with someone like this. Some people just shouldn't teach and this is one.

His class was easy and I got an A in the Astro course. But I would never recommend him as a teacher. During lectures he seems really confused and when you try asking questions he seems to be in a rush and gives you a very useless response. I did good in the course by just reading the notes. He wasnt any help at all.

The course itself is very easy as its all memorization, but he himself I would say needs improvement. Most of the time, he just reads everything off of his lecture slides and doesn't sounds very enthusiastic. As well, when students ask questions, he doesn't sound he answers them with definitiveness. Easy A though.
Good teacher. if you keep up with the labs, and dont just do them to be done, you will get a good grade.

He wasn't very helpful. VEry bad at explaining the material, basically handed out worksheets and graded them. The tests were nothing like either the homework or the in-class work, and although the one TA was beyond phenomenal (thank God) the other basically lurked around and did nothing to contribute. DO NOT GET HIM.
He was a horrible teacher. Just handed out worksheets and had us do them. He didn't teach any at all. Everything I learned from the class I learned on my own. Find another teacher like Koberlin.
Very easy professor, did not make us use any  calculus, gave you the workshop anwser if u asked, i got an A and probably diserved a b
Nice, very helpful if you ask. If people do poorly on a test, the next one is easier :-)

Seems like a nice man, but NOT a very good teacher at all. I had to learn everything on my own since nothing he did was actually teaching. Tests wouldnt be bad if we ever actually learned the things on it... I recommend finding a different teacher.

Dr. Martins is a cool guy. Very understanding. I personally thought that Science Writing was a very light class 90% of the time, with the other 10% being the days before a major submission is due. The biggest pitfall of this class was that revisions relied on his feedback, but the feedback often felt vague and thus I couldn't revise effectively.

comment: Nice, cares about his students, and really seems to enjoy teaching. The structure of the course was interesting, with short weekly essays to apply the concepts you learned, and then culminating into a final project the second half of the semester (overall fun and effective). There is lots of dialogue in class, and readings/examples are very modern.

Professor Martins is a very good professor. He clearly cares deeply about what he teaches, and about his students. This class can get political, so if you're not comfortable talking about that publicly, this class might not be for you. Most of the class was conversation, so get ready to talk.

When asked a direct question he almost always responds with "well what do you feel about that" and never actually answers the question. he is nice enough but does not grade most things efficiently. does not give feedback on work even when feedback is needed to revise an assignment.

This prof really wants you to learn something in his class. He was very engaging and routinely encouraged participation (which was a chunk of the grade). He is very critical of your assignments and writing only because he wants to push you to be the best writer you can be. He is very open to feedback about his teaching and material.

Prof Martin is a very sweet and caring professor. Not much work is required for this class aside from the occasional reading, but most of his class is discussion and group project heavy. As long as you do the readings, then you'll do great in his class.

Professor Martins class is all about discussion and participation. He rarely ever lectures for more than a few minutes, and focuses on fostering discussion between class-members. He does assign quite a bit of reading as homework though, so be warned. Still, overall I enjoyed his class a lot!

Professor Martins is one of the kindest professors I've had at RIT. It's refreshing to see a professor care so much about his students and being so open to new ideas/opinions. He also allows you to continue revising major papers up until the end of the semester, so you can keep revising for a better grade! Also gives great feedback.

Solid professor, tries to keep discussion in the hands of his students and keep the conversation light-hearted and hopeful even when talking about the effects of climate change

this is his first time teaching this course, as of spring '23, he only grades on mainly two things: QCCQ due every class, and an interview report

Definitely one of the best english/writing profs I've had at RIT. Every class was well structured and thought out. Very caring about your success in the class and provided a welcoming environment each class session.
Took a long time for essay feedback but very lenient and clear in what he wants

If you do not like talking/debating the current political and social environments, this class is not for you. He wants everyone to participate in class discussions every class, so if you do not like talking politics or social issues, you will not enjoy this class. Work level wise this class was fine though
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']

comment: Martins was the nicest professor I have ever had. He was really caring and always ready to help you with anything. His assignments were not too difficult and discussions in class are great. He may not always stick to schedule and change things around, though they are mostly for your benefits. He does not post grades till the end but it works out.

He's one of those professors who appears to be on your side first but you'll learn that he isn't after the first few weeks. He doesn't grade his assignments so you won't know if you're failing or passing until the semester ends.  Also in his class all you do is read about writing and write about reading.

Cares a lot about students grades, and will spend a lot of time explaining what he wants in assignments if you ask.  If you don't ask, is very confusing and you may find yourself being lost.  He is willing to change up the class for his students, and does a great job moving class along.  I learned a LOT about writing and overall, a good teacher.

Seems like a good teacher in the beginning but doesn't give you any indication of your grade until the end.  Most assignments are pass/fail except for one paper worth half your grade and you can only do well if you write it exactly the way he wants it.  Don't take this class (Writing the self and others) or this teacher.  Stupid class, bad teacher

Great guy, love his lectures. Participation is important to him, and if you don't participate "enough" he'll grade your work harshly. comment: I have to give props to Prof. Santana for not making us buy a single material for this class. All books were uploaded as PDFs, the only thing we had to pay for was certain movies (I much prefer a 3 dollar rental than a $90 text book). comment: Monster Lit is an awesome class, but it requires a lot of reading. That said, some of the reading is just watching a movie, which is pretty neat. There's a homework assignment due every week, but it varies from 2 page paper to easy quiz, so it's never too hard. Really fun in lecture, but lectures are short and not very productive.

Love the professor. The class is how much you put into it. If you choose not to read, you'll be looking a lot of things up and the short essays will be much harder. The actual books/movies you have to watch are interesting, so it's worth it to put in the effort, but not really required if you just want to skate by. Gives great feedback on essays.

This class will challenge you intellectually more than academically. Prof. Santana sets an appropriate level of work for a 200-level course. Discussion in my section was great, and the essays are VERY open ended. Do the reading, or be prepared to spend a lot of time looking things up. His feedback is incredible and he is very knowledgeable .

comment: I took his online class Monster Lit and he was very organized and helpful. I had just as good an experience as I would've had in a physical class. He was a fair grader and gave thorough feedback

comment: Show up to class and you will probably get a B as long as you do the minimal homework and papers assigned.

comment: Listen, Santana seems like a great guy. But the amount of reading is insane. Yes, this is a literature class and you should expect to read - this class is overboard. The way he grades papers is incredibly picky. It was an 8AM and wow is he loud - unnecessary. His sense of humor is twisted and not in a good way which made the class that much worse.

Professor Santana is a great guy. His class is very easy to get a B in with minimal effort. If you actually put in some effort you can get a B+ or an A easily. He goes off on random tangents at times but they are always entertaining and they usually teach something, even if it is not exactly what the class is about. He is a very relaxed teacher.

Santana is a lovely guy. He's so upbeat and fun to listen to. Participate if you can in his class, literally you just have to read the Shakespeare lines. Otherwise, he can ramble at times but it's usually somewhat pertaining to the discussion. He's a guy that you can show up and you'll do well. Get ready to write papers, though.
I love when he goes on his tangents because he is honestly very interesting. Drama and Theater was okay,  he made it somewhat tolerable.

Awesome dude, but spends too much time talking about (semi)irrelevant political issues, and not enough time talking with his class about actual assigned reading.  He's hilarious and sometimes conversations get deep, but too often, I feel that just  when students start to delve into a topic, he'll continue the conversation by himself, or steer away.
I've taken Professor Santana quite a few times now and I really love his classes. Very easy and as long as you keep up with the online discussions then it's pretty easy to get an A.
very good professor! I took his online writing class, it was easy if you do all the work.

Funny presentation, lectures are good but might not help you write your papers as much as talking with him after class. Textbook material can be extremely dense to work through. What sets him apart is that he actually gives comprehensive, extremely helpful feedback on rough drafts. Not a stressful class.

Ive had Santana for writing and for literature. He is by far one of the most agreeable teachers at RIT. Writing is not a fun class to take but he was able to keep hilarious discussions flowing and still teach at the same time. He is never angered unless you interrupt his class and makes fun of you if you walk in late.
what an awful teacher!  he makes lots of sexual jokes that aren't offensive, but also aren't funny to anyone but him.  he's pretty much just obnoxious.  and a needlessly picky grader on papers.
Nice guy but doesn't really respond to emails much. He's into discussions and comparisons, very vague on assignments and flexible on grading. Just do the homework and show up.

DO NOT BOTHER PAYING ATTENTION. none of the material covered in his lectures appear on any type of quiz or test. quizzes, papers, and online discussions make up your grades, and they are all based on extremely difficult readings.
best teacher i've ever had. so laid back and fun. wrote about your own personal experiences
Best ever i've taken two classes with him and i plan to take more next year.
he is a really good guy, funny likes to joke and he knows when he is being boring. pretty fun class with good videos and 1 time a video game.

The class was a joke, but an easy A. The lectures that didn't put everyone to sleep were actually rather entertaining, becuase of his irreverence. However, he DOES inject all his lectures with his lefty political views. If you are a conservative, be prepared for his ignorant stabs at the right wing, and his anti-war propaganda.
guys crazy good teacher tho
You'll learn more than you think, just nothing about writing or literature.
We didn't learn ANYTHING... All he did was talk with the morons in my learning community about cars, booze, and sex... Great prof to get if you're a slacker...
cool teacher

Professor Bae works very hard to ensure that all students are capable of learning and doing what they must in a project-heavy based class. Professor Bae is open to answer any questions students have and interview those who ask.

Friendly and helpful professor, and I learned a lot of interesting modeling techniques. HOWEVER the computer projects throughout the class were incredibly time intensive and overly complicated. Especially in the last 2 weeks, way too many things were assigned in too short of a time period.
probably an alright guy but do not ever take mece606 systems modeling garbage useless class that you will learn nothing from

Didn't seem to even know what he was teaching. If asked for help on homework, he wouldn't know the answer/ how to code what he was asking for either. I think he was a very solid professor. Def among the best MECE professors Ive had at RIT. Right up there with Landschoot and Dr. Schrlau. I do note that even though the workload was a lot, I think its on par with the nature of the class being into Classical Controls. Great professor, did his best in spite of mostly online class with physical labs

Dr. K is a pretty solid teacher. The class itself isn't too different from the undergrad systems modeling class; the project reports just become more involved. He explains everything pretty straight forward and the material isn't incredibly difficult to understand. Covers just about everything in his copious notes.
cool guy, nice course, thanks

Projects are numerous, long, and tedious but very worthwhile. Very available and helpful. Grades very fairly. Work felt worthwhile. Projects helped with technical writing skills. Lectures are chock full of notes and he goes the whole time.  You will learn advanced Matlab skills. Highly recommend both the class and prof.

Great teacher with a great personality. Very down to earth.He's been in the field so he knows whats important. Quizzes and tests were challenging, but definitely covered what was expected. Extremely fair grader, if you got the general concept you do well.

Great teacher.  Does a good job of balance between theory and example problem.  Example problems are relevant and really help understand the material.  Gives weekly quizzes and does a great job answering questions.  Highly recommended.

Very good prof. Explains well, many examples, makes sure you know it, extra review sessions. Easy quizzes, wants you to do well, grades fairly. Tests are hard but only because of common core multiple choice section. Must take him if you can. Also, good time slot.

Very clear, focuses heavily on example problems but explains the theory behind each step instead of just working through them.  Hosted review sessions for all sections before exams.  Usually announces quizzes unless half the class skips, not too strict about attendance.
Oh you'll be fine. Two or three assignments throughout the whole semester, make up you do a bit of work and easy A. Easily one of the best prof I had

Every week we would watch a film Thursday, then have a quiz the following Monday about the film. You HAVE to complete the readings he assigns to do well on the quizzes. Make sure you check your grammar too. Frank is nice and cares about the subject and the students.
Great feedback. Very friendly and helpful. Make sure you participate in class, if you do youll be fine.
Great teacher and great class, we went on so many field trips and she was very knowledgeable on Environmental Science. Make sure you give yourself time to complete the writing assignments

Her lectures tend to be boring, and sometimes all over the place, but everything you could ever need is in her power points. Gives a reliable amount of work each week, with only occasional extra assignments. Uses simulations, group work, and more practical work, so good if u learn by doing. Overall, u learn what u need to know, and shes super nice.

She knows her stuff and tries hard to be helpful but she constantly doesn't understand questions and when asked to clarify something she just repeats te same thing. She does not finish her thoughts and often times speaks through short, fragmented sentences. She is passionate and informative but sometimes tough to learn from. Also she has an abundance of different assignments, doesn't really give credit for going to class, and is unhelpful in face to face help. But this is a fair class.

Ricky is an inspirational professor who is enthusiastic about the material he teaches and is always available to help students. Class is very lecture heavy, but he is engaging and knowledgeable. In my experience, students received take-home quizzes & final exam. Fairly generous with grading despite the low opportunities for grades in this class.

While the lecture can feel quite long in some cases, Ricky tries to make each and every one important. He challenges you with the meaning of the topics rather than pointless equations and definitions. The labs, even though the topic they are for was taught weeks ago, are fun and a great way of learning. He is always available to talk after class.

Ricky was an absolute joy to have as a professor. This course felt like a breath of fresh air to me as an engineering major, despite the workload. The lecture portion of this course was online when I took it, but Ricky made the labs interesting, and made the assignment expectations clear. If you ever have any questions, ask! He loves to help.
Tough but fair

comment: Ricky is a great professor, he is always available outside of class and office ours are great, he explains anything you have questions on in detail. You can tell he really cares about what he says and his students. His slide shows are important but what he says is the main material tested on. Ricky makes the class very enjoyable and fun.

Awesome Professor!!! Confirmed my passion for imaging science with interesting lectures that, while often went deeper into tangential topics than necessary, definitely conveyed his love for the field and passed it on to his students.

Ricky is fantastic. He loves his job, speaking with students, and making sure they understand the material. While many lectures involve random tangents, it makes the time go by faster and the material more enjoyable. Homeworks take hours upon hours of completion, so don't leave them to the last minute. He and the TA are willing to help! Enjoy :)

Ricky is friendly, knowledgeable, and makes a technical subject easy for the artists in the class to understand and apply. He gives very little homework; grading is mostly pass-fail labs and a few quizzes.

Ricky was an amazing professor, perhaps one of the best I've had at RIT! While the subject matter addressed may not be very interesting, he does his best to make students invested and does his best to make getting a good grade as easy as possible. He drops your worst lab grade, there's little homework, and you only need a 90 to get an "A"!

Great teacher, very easy-going and accommodating. He has an accent but is generally very easy to understand and nice to listen to.  Won't call on you if you don't want to talk, but participation is preferred.

Great professor who loves his profession and teaching! Very friendly and understanding. The exams can be tricky but as long as you take the time to study (all lecture notes are posted online) you will do well. Would recommend!

Insanely nice guy, he's really clear about what you're going to be tested on/what's important. Powerpoints are up on mycourses. It's not always the most interesting class in the world, however it's painfully obvious he loves what he's doing, and that makes him awesome/more interesting. Just do the work and put some effort into it and you'll be fine

He's a pretty good teacher and his class is pretty easy if you just do the work and study for the few quizzes and exams he gives. He does like to ramble about things that aren't going to be on the test but he always makes what is going to be on the test very clear.
Fantastic.

DIFFERENTLY WIRED BRAINS: Definitely one of the most interesting classes I've taken at RIT. Read the book for the week and post on the given topic as well as other students' posts. Gives out three grades, heavily weighted on the discussion.
A bit lofty, but a good teacher.

Differently Wired Brains: Not my major, but by FAR the BEST class I have ever taken, and she may be the Best Teacher in Existence!! Every day she would give us the opportunity for a 5min beak, but the whole class was always so interested that we ALWAYS voted UNANIMOUSLY to keep going. I wish I had another chance to take one of her classes again

this class is a joke, to start off. but she gives you at least three writen pages of homework a night plus 3 papers that have the worst subjects ever. it's 9th grade english all over again. just as painful and paintless as ever. avoid at all costs.

Holmes is the best teacher, he will help you no matter if your stuck with one or more problems.He explained a lot to me and i understand what he was telling me, then i just finish all my work before it due on that day.

Garret cares about his students, and it really shows. Course consists of 6 labs, 4 scripts, 2 quizzes, and a final. I learned a lot, would recommend.

Hands down, best professor I had so far. If you are stuck for more than 5 seconds, and raise your hand, he would do the task for you, never condescending even if you mess up the shebang, goofy as hell. I cant stress enough, W Garret

Garret was amazing. He teaches well, cracks jokes often, is accessible through email and Discord, and is overall just a great professor. Garret is hilarious. He really makes an effort to be entertaining in class. He is extremely knowledgeable and cares about students. For example, he is flexible with due dates. Garret is my favorite professor at RIT so far. His lectures are boring but short and he's a jokester so it makes it bearable. Speaks in Reddit language but it translates well to a solid sysadmin foundation in labs and script assignments. Take if available.
His lectures are informative and interesting and he makes the course easy and straightforward. He is the best Professor at RIT.

Garret is the best professor I've had to far at RIT. He is hilarious and does get sidetracked sometimes, but overall can finish all material by the end of class

6 Labs, 4 Scripts, 2 "projects" overall a very easy course. Garret would constantly move due dates to be later which was very nice. Helpful in office hours for the labs and just an overall nice guy. Funny and understanding. Pay attention in lecture if you want to grasp the material otherwise you probably don't need to show up. Still a great prof!

He is one of the best professors at RIT, his lectures are interesting and fun. He will help if a student is struggling. His feedback on the labs, assignments, etc is helpful and to the point. Would 100% recommend anyone to take courses with him.

He has a good personality and he definitely adds to the lectures unlike most professors. Ask questions! However the grading of this class is unusual and I don't feel like your grade accurately reflects how well you do in the class.

Class is not required, but you will miss out a ton since this prof is extremely knowledgeable and well-spoken. Labs are not too difficult - the most tedious part is opening up rles. He puts up external resources too and it will be even easier if you cover those.

Garret is the crown jewel of the IST department, but Sys II is no cakewalk. Garret is a passionate teacher, and you'll succeed as long as you put in the time.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! He always was able to make everyone laugh and make this class way more enjoyable. I would've taken one of his classes next semester but it didn't fit in my schedule :(

- Provide wonderful class atmosphere - Gives funny and sarcastic jokes in class - Flexible on due dates for labs and assignments - His lectures are non-stop, he can give a break between lectures - Sometimes forgot to do little things in myCourses and students have to remind them to do things in myCourses
If you're given the option for any class with Garret as a professor TAKE IT. You will love life.

Garret is a kind, hilarious, and knowledgeable person. Great and funny instructor who is always willing to help students with their labs and assignments especially for those who are struggling. Garret is really funny and has interactive lectures that make concepts interesting. He is always there to help you understand labs and is a really laid back guy. He is one of my favorite professors ever.

Garret is my man! I love the guy. He does a stellar job actually teaching the material instead of regurgitating information from the slides. Funny guy, lenient grader, and by the end of the semester, you'll KNOW networking. Just go to his classes, ask questions and get ready for his crazy rants. What a guy.

Pros: Great lecturing skills about his topics, provide sufficient assistance to students especially on lab work, and offer rewards if specificed number of students complete the course evaluations and get good grades one exams. I hate this subject but I didn't mind this class because hes a great professor. Really cares and listens to student feedback, clearly wants to teach and adjust to his students needs. I would absolutely take another class with him.

Professor Arcoraci is hilarious, funny, caring and generally amazing. Would highly recommend, very reasonable and enjoyable
Garret is the best professor I've ever had. I have a strong understanding in the material he professed, and his amazing humor was enjoyed.

Garret is an amazing professor! He really knows his stuff and he is very enthusiastic at teaching. He will stay after hours to help any student that needs help in the labs. He is also very engaging with the students.  His tests adequately prepared me for interviews I had at the career fair.
test are tough

No one will be able to say enough about how amazing this person is. You will never be bored in his class. He is there all the time to help you, and he will always make you smile. He is, by far, the most amazing teacher I've had in my entire life. He loves his students so much. With all of that, You will learn A LOT.   TAKE HIM WITHOUT ASKING!

This is my third class with Garret. He is one of the best professors in the IST department. Take him every chance you get. He's just so awesome. I had him for Network Services this time. You're the best Garret!

Fantastic professor, incredibly helpful, even helped me out with my other classes frequently. Teaches material well and makes class interesting, very funny and nice. Take him for every class possible.

Garret is the best. He was my adviser for an independent study  I did in IPv6. He was as genuinely interested in the subject as I was. This was my second class with Garret, and won't be my last. He's the best. Highly recommend for any subject.
Really nice guy. Knows his stuff and is always willing to help you out.

Now I'm taking my THIRD class with Prof. Arcoraci, and he has been and will always be my BEST professor all the time. He is really knowledgeable, smart and you'll never get bored in his class. Very informed in his field, personable, super duper hot.
In one sentence, he is the best professor I have ever seen before.

One of the best professors in the department. Knows his stuff, knows how to teach, and cares about his students. He is almost always in his office to help students and stays late and comes in on weekends to help people. He's also one of the nicest professors I've had.
in one word-very good professor- recomended
Great Professor. Always goes the extra mile to find out anything he doesn't know and is very understanding with problems and such.
The best for ever
Great professor. Really smart guy. Knows his stuff. Would be awesome to have him as full time faculty.
Great professor. Bought us pizza on last day of class! Sometimes goes on tangents, but knows what's he's talking about, and is very helpful in lab. Would recommend!
She knows her stuff and grades fairly. She has an interesting life. Her problem sets were more much difficult than the common core. Make sure to read the syllabus.

Lectures are boring and less than helpful. She just reads things verbatim from the textbook and puts them on the board, all class, every class. She hardly explains anything, the closest you'll get is her proving a theorem or doing an example on the board. At least she doesn't use cengage.

If you have the opportunity to take this class with Professor Narayan, DO IT! She gives easy weekly quizzes and sometimes even makes them collaborative. Her tests can be tough, but as long as you study for a couple of hours, they won't be an issue at all. She will stop or review things if asked. She gives lots of extra credit on tests and quizzes.

Lots of lecture, she talks the entire class time, but calc 2 just has a lot of topics. She'll explain a concept then goes through a bunch of examples on the board. Great lectures. I understood most of them, except for series at the end, though those are taught terribly everywhere. Gives a 10min brain break halfway through class.

Professor Murphy had amazing lectures and really livened up learning the material. The material itself was tough but he works through problems both during office hours and as they come up in class to give genuine thoughtful responses. The homework is harder than the tests but he constantly tries to improve his lectures and help you understand.

Lectures were fun and kept me awake, but could've been better at actually teaching me. Plenty of time was given for the homework's, but the content of the homework's was usually taught the lecture before it was due. Quizzes felt hard on memorization and I felt I didn't have enough time for the larger exams compared to the question difficulty.

He is one of the most funny and energetic professors I've ever had. His lectures are as engaging as they are entertaining, and he also teaches the material very well. He will make absolutely sure you understand the material before moving on, although sometimes this can lead to tangents, which are always interesting nonetheless.

wants his students to learn and his office hours are very helpful. However, he is a little disorganized when explaining and takes a long time to grade. He tends to overcomplicate whatever he's explaining which makes things confusing and is all over the place. Despite this, he really does want you to learn, and is very lenient with grading.

Overcomplicates whatever he needs to say and is all over the place. Also gives a quiz right after a midterm and doesn't tell you until the day before. Slides are not updated at times so you cant study in advance. Sometimes will tell you to look at a slide for 5 minutes and then expect you to know how to use it on a quiz a few minutes later.

Funny guy, the material is chaotic. posted lectures are made to be seen in class and make no sense without the context of lecture. homeworks are really hard but manageable, and worth 40% of the grade. exams are pretty easy too. just overall a headache of a class that isnt worth it if other well rated professors are available.

with time and experience teaching he will become an excellent teacher. right now, however, his class is pretty chaotic and unstructured. hes a real funny guy, he will help you if you need it and he doesnt make you feel bad for needing help. if you try you will do very well in his class, you just need to pay attention and keep up with material.

Professor Murphy goes on a lot of side tangents that results in taking a long time to get through a seemingly basic topic. Quiz every 1-2 weeks, homeworks annoying but not hard.

One of my favourite professors! He teaches well, makes jokes, is approachable, sets a clear grading criteria and provides detailed feedback and chances to help improve grades. He's very approachable and helpful but this particular class is not very well structured.

This class is really hard, as hard as everyone says it is. Professor Murphy is new here, but did a pretty solid job given the circumstances. nice and really gives great advice about social media, both in the classroom and for personal use as well. Shes really relatable and wants to see her students succeed. She also always gives career opportunity info that she finds

Great professor. She goes so far out of her way to give outstanding feedback on assignments. She really wants to see her students succeed.
Took his class. Not bad. Just a lot of projects and case studies, but he gave us reasonable time.

Lectures okay but don't relate to homework. She's a pretty chill (she usually ends class early) but her grading criteria isn't really clear. Her instructions for assignments and group work are vague, or she would add rules as the assignment was being done in class which could be frustrating/confusing.

Professor Valentine is amazing and the sweetest. Her class was Diversity in the Deaf Community and it is very hands on, very engaging. You work among hearing, hard-of-hearing, and Deaf students in small communities and it is very simple work (Readings + Simple responses, Group work, and Discussion). Highly recommend her as a professor.

Her 1-3 averaged tests are your grade for the semester. Graded extremely specifically so pay attention to the textbook work and do it ON TIME! My tests with here were open notes and were still a struggle even with writing every name/definition down per chapter. It was difficult but she was willing to help with projects and offers extra credit.
She is an extremely helpful and very nice teacher but the material she teaches is incrediablly boring. The average test score of the class's first exam was 67.
Barb Birkett is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had, she even allowed students to call her Mrs. Birkett. I enjoyed having her as a teacher.
Great lady- will do anything to help a student in need.
A real expert in what she teaches. Sweet and understanding to boot. Old fashioned in many regards, but most of all, very willing and eager to help when you need it.
One of the best professors I've had. He always goes the extra mile and provides lots of additional (useful) resources.
Best physics teacher ever. Kind of a quirky guy, but that's what makes him fun. Exams and quizzes are straight-forward and homework is relatively easy.

My favorite teacher at RIT, despite the fact that I'm not a COS major, I still took multiple classes with him as electives because he's just that good. Truly enjoyed all of his classes, he's qwerky, awkward and hilarious all at once. If you have to take Physics, do it with Becker!! Highest recommendation I can give!!!!
really  good I highly recommend him
Seriously the best god damn physics teacher ever. His beard is full of answers.

Dude is an awesome teacher, he answers questions, hw correlates with class work. He wants to make sure you understand the material. Will answer questions. Quizzes and test aren't bad if you go to class and do hw. He makes horrible jokes, but I'm fine with that. I really wish he was teaching the transition physics course next quarter.

Quite helpful in class, makes sure you know the material. Homeworks are kind of sporadic, and they're Mastering Physics as well, so it's a little unintuitive. Very helpful in labs, if you have questions, he'll answer them. For the RIT Physics Department, he's one of the rare good professors.

Really enjoyed the way he taught the course.  If you visit during office hours he WILL make sure you understand the material before leaving.  It's not often you find a professor who is actually willing to teach the students for the students sake.  A lot of professors at RIT will just talk about the material, this man lives and breathes the material

He's a damn good teacher, always clear and he really shows you how to solve the problem and he doesn't go on mindless babbles about theory and he just shows you how to do it. He's really flexible and always available during office hours and he's so easy to work with. I plan on taking this teacher again for future physic classes.
Willing to help via email or during office hours.
Homework goes with class work. Test wasn't bad. Quizzes are fine if you pay attention and do the homework. Not half bad, even if I do hate physics.
Smart guy. Young, so he isn't old like most profs. Good looking, doesn't hurt.

Erin is very nice and understanding, however if you do not read the full lab handouts every week you will not do well. The labs themselves are typically not that hard, but a lot of the quiz/practical questions can be very specific which makes them more difficult. If you email her with any questions, she'll be able to help you.

comment: Erin is a graduate student lab instructor for Bio201 lab. Pretty usual stuff, you come to lab each week, finish the lab protocol, then leave. Labs take on average 2-3 hours to complete, which is most of the classes time. She is a nice LA, and will help you when you ask. Not too strict with grading, but takes off points for small details incorrect
Acting for Interpreters was a great class for students to Interpret A-E and E-A. Also, good opportunity to interpret in different events.

Haggerty is amazing! This was an asynchronous course and definitely had lots of tasks but they were very simple. Every week there is one lecture video and from that you take a quiz, do a discussion, and an assignment. She gives lots of time to do the assignments and is very supportive! She stresses that if you are falling behind she will help!

She is a gem and a sweet heart. I wish i could take her again. You learn a lot in this class about learning to relax and be yourself on stage. Interpreting also has a lot of acting and gesture involved and this class helps along with that. Not just for Deaf students and Interpreting majors, anyone can take it.

As a Cybersecurity major, taking a theater class online with this professor has been fun, you get to learn a lot of things about theater. The class is very easy (I literally got a A+) with minimal effort >1 hr a week. She provides very positive feedback (Actually spends the time to go over all posts to offer feedback). Would definitely recommend !

I was super excited to take this class at the beginning of the semester, but soon realized that it wasn't quite what I thought it would be.  She is so goofy and animated that sometimes it is overwhelming, but she has great energy and the students seem to feed off of that.
She is an amazing teacher. All of her HW assignments are pretty easy. That is if you have common sense. otherwise don't bother if you can't come to class or be stupid.
She's a great acting teacher. However, if you're Deaf in a Deaf/Hearing classroom, she sim-coms when she speaks and it's VERY English-y and hard to understand.
hard teacher but very nice lady.
She's pretty tough, but excellent teacher.  She also teaches performing arts, too. Love her!  Take her!
The best acting teacher in the theater department.  Audition for her plays!
Tough acting teacher, she's so sweet, and pushes you into a better actor.

literally the best. She loves what she does and you can tell. She's enthusiastic and supportive and always willing to help in any way she can. If you're fine arts and have a class with her, consider yourself the luckiest kid
Great professor, who loves exposing students to new artists. Very willing to listen & help if you're having trouble on an assignment.
She is fantastic. One of the best classes ever taken thus far. Highly recommend others to take her class.

Kelly is literally the best. She loves what she does and you can tell. She's enthusiastic and supportive and always willing to help in any way she can. If you're fine arts and have a class with her, consider yourself the luckiest kid on earth.

I'm sorry to say but he is pretty boring. He does not bother to let us engage with other students and he speaks with a monotone voice. The quizzes he gives are DIFFICULT, unless you have time to read more than 20+ pages from the textbook for each lecture.

Edward White is by far the worst professor i have ever met. he spends the entire two hour class explaining simple things in great detail which in the end makes them insanely confusing, and on most occasions he spends over 50 minutes critiquing one person's photos. I highly suggest that you find another class with a different professor.

I ignored the reviews hoping he wasn't as bad as people said he was. It was a mistake. His lectures are so boring. It takes him 5 minutes to explain something that should only take 30 seconds. He constantly repeats things over and over and over again so get ready to hear the same thing several times.

Took him for an intro to digital photography class. He talked way to much about his work and never focused on actually teaching the class. Half of the days spent in the class felt like wasted time. Very boring. Can miss a couple of classes. Hates mycourses so get ready to use dropbox.
he sucks, talks way too much, never comes to the point, always get out o track
Just don't get her furious(o)

She is very understanding of people's situations and is willing to help and answer questions, whether they've been asked before or if the answers come naturally to others. Her office hours are very limited because she works for the state, but she gives everybody her full attention during her designated office hours.

Professor Furioso genuinely cares for the wellbeing and success of her students. She follows a rigorous teaching schedule, and you can expect an excellently curated range of topics that are very relevant to your path as a civil engineer.

Her availability for office hours is limited, but understandable since she works with NYSDOT.

comment: First of all she is very nice and you can tell she is a respected person. She is good at teaching and honeslty will help you understand the material. At times can be confusing but very good.

She has so much info and you will learn so much. She is nice too and will lay out exactly what is on the tests and they will be open note. She does have a full time job outside of this so she is really busy and does not really have office hours, but usually you will not need them anyways.

comment: She is very knowledgeable about concrete. All of our tests were open-book, and she laid them out during class. She is not at all accessible outside of class as she has a full-time job outside of rit. She is a very nice person and not a bad teacher. Just seems like your class will take the back burner in her life.

comment: Lois is a good professor. She has a ton of experience in the field and is able to teach her class knowing what is important and what isn't. Lectures were ok. She really relies on the book and it is necessary to read for the homework and for your own understanding. Homework was easy and not too common. The tests were hard but she prepared you a bit.
