comment: Great class

Lois is not a great Professor. She will go off tangent for about 5-10  minutes about her personal life every lecture. She will get visually upset at students for questioning her. Often seems like she does not know what she is talking about.

Lois is nice. Only thing I didn't like about her class was that sometimes it seemed like she forgot that it was our first time performing some of the concrete tests. One time we were yelled at because the wording wasn't clear in the instructions and we asked for help, she took it as us not reading the instructions. Other than that, solid choice.

super friendly, gives good feedback, is a fair and easy grader, and assigns interesting projects. Everyone in my class always worked hard on projects and it always came from a place of enjoying the material and wanting to produce good work
Awesome professor would take his class again
Wants everyone to do well, teaches very well. Worth taking this class!

He is the nicest professor, he wants all his students to do well in his class and will provide extra credit when anyone needs it, only 3 tests including the final and simple weekly homework, overall great professor

BIME270 (intro to biomaterials) is a really fun class. Interesting lectures, opportunities for bonus points, some in-class activities. There's one short group project. Quizzes and the final are all on MyCourses with no other exams. Be very analytical and specific, she is a good professor but can be a very harsh grader.

Dr. Wuertz is the best professor I've had at RIT. Her lectures are extremely engaging with group activities included. You can tell she has had a lot of experience in what she is teaching, and if she lacks knowledge in a specific area she lectured about, she will point you to someone who can answer your questions. Group project was very useful!
Dr. Wuertz is great! She runs a very organized and interesting class. She spruces up lectures will in-class activities, kahoots, and group presentations. Definitely recommend.
Engaged, approachable and cares about students

Cliver is one of the best Profs on campus by far. GCIS is a hard class to begin with, but Cliver makes it so much easier. His lectures are clear, and he is always willing to answer questions; in fact, he encourages it. On top of this, he's a great guy. I know he primarily teaches engineering, but I was blessed to have him as a csec major.

Good guy, my favorite professor at RIT. Made circuits 1 enjoyable, and easy to understand, both which are not typical of the engineering professors. Before you take a class, always check if Cliver teaches it.
Fantastic professor who works very well with students to succeed

Professor Cliver has really figured out being a professor. He constantly encourages questions; I was skeptical at first but it became clear that he is right, you learn while you talk, not while he does. Great person who truly cares about student success, I wish more professors were like him.

Very nice guy and great professor. Quizzes and exams are just like the homeworks. Lectures are clear and informative. Only problem was he got behind on teaching VHDL so the lab section was teaching me VHDL a week before he covered it in class.
Cliver is great. Kinda dry lectures, and easy homework. He is well respected and knows his stuff very well. Great professor and great person overall

Professor Cliver is an incredible lecturer and a very kind individual. He has worked in the industry for decades and is always open to learning. He is very open with what he knows and provides helpful feedback. Professor Cliver loves questions.
good guy

Professor Cliver is a truly incredible lecturer. His lectures can never be boring and he has made an environment where we have inside jokes in the class. His lectures are still very informative and he provides the information in a way that all of us can understand it. Even with the amount of classes he teaches, he is still accessible outside.

The Goat, best DSD teacher makes lectures really fun, really enjoys teaching his classes. Labs might be a little tough but the lectures for the labs are really amazing if you pay attention. Quizzes are not that hard and Exams allow a Cheat Sheet.

One of the best instructors I have ever had. He is incredibly knowledgeable and can go far beyond the material in class, drawing on examples from his time in industry to explain the application of what you are learning. He effectively managed a class of over 100 students and took the time to answer every single question, no matter how small.

Cliver is definitely the best professor I've had at RIT. I entered DSD1 with lots of prior knowledge and experience, but I can say that I couldn't have taught the material any better. He's the most flexible and chill, yet effective professor you'll find in a major-based course at RIT. All of the students love him and he LOVES questions.

Cliver's lectures are incredible. He's very animated and while he doesn't often use slides for his lectures, he draws out the concepts and breaks them down very simply. His teaching style may be challenging for those who need slides to learn. He's very friendly and loves questions. By far my favorite human in the EE/CE department.

I legitimately love this man. He has such a contagious passion for what he does, he is hilarious in lectures, and he LOVES questions. Cliver will explain the same concept in 7 different ways without a qualm to make sure that everyone understands the material. He's got some amazing stories and you will never find a better DSD teacher. Truly a 12/10

Cliver knows his stuff and wants to help you do the same. He loves when people ask questions (and he'll make sure to let you know that every chance he gets). He makes his lectures engaging and fun, but still makes sure that you learn something
Cliver is amazing. Amazing support outside of and in class. He's so clearly excited to teach and highly encourages questions. Such a great experience taking his class.

Took DSD1 with professor Cliver in the spring of 2020.Wonderful lectures, clear explanations, and he cares about the material. When I had him for this class, he had recently just left his engineering job to lecture full time and he brings a wealth of knowledge from industry into the classroom.

I took Circuits 1 with Professor Cliver in fall 2019. Cliver gives amazing lectures. He has real industry experience makes it clear that he cares that you learn. He will actively seek out questions by pausing his lecture and going to the back of the room and waiting until someone asks a question. He is passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Cliver was honestly the best professor a 1st year could ask for. He was laid back and loved to connect with his students. He loved questions, so if you ever are confused, never hesitate to ask. Cared for each of his students and worked diligently to make sure each one understood the content in class.
Cliver is the GOAT, this man is so funny. He cares about his students and makes sure you know the material. 10/10 would take again, wish more professors were like him!

He assigns homework assignments with content that he hasn't taught in class. He is also teaching content that differs from what you are supposed to be learning for lab so you will be struggling in two classes at once.

Cliver is the GOAT in the ECET department. If I could, I would take all my classes with him. Just be aware that all the knowledge you learn builds off each other so if you ever get stuck or confused ask questions. Cliver loves ?'s. He will do his best to make sure that everyone is on the same page so that you succeed in labs and on exams.

Cliver is an amazing professor. He is always answering questions and wants you to ask a million questions. This was one of the first EE courses I took and truly enjoyed it. I was nervous about labs because I had never used EE equipment, and he went with me to a lab after class and explained to me how to use the equipment.
One of the best professors here at RIT. He is a divine entity worth every second of your time. If you don't stay for the incredible lectures you'll stay for the unmatched charisma.
Honestly, one of the best professors I have come across so far. Knows his stuff, and will not rest till he makes sure you know it too. Super kind and caring. Fair grader.
Best Professor at RIT

Professor Cliver genuinely cares about the success of his students. He is very good at breaking complex content into easily understandable material and often uses humor to keep lectures interesting. I highly recommend professor Cliver.
best professor here on RIT. He enjoys teaching and makes it fun
Probably my favorite professor here at RIT, can't wait to attend his class in person next year.

If you have the ability to take a class with this professor do so! He is one of the nicest, most chill, and most amazing professors RIT has to offer. His philosophy is for students to worry about actually learning the subject instead of learning how to pass quizzes and tests in the subject. Ask questions especially when it comes to his career.

Probably one of my favorite teachers of all time. He's hilarious, super smart, and answers every question a class has, whether it be super simple or super complicated. His motto is "You have a limit of asking 1,000,000 questions, so after that limit is passed, I'm not going to answer anymore". He teaches super well and connects with the students.

I specifically made my schedule so I can have this professor for a year straight. I took four classes with him and regret nothing. He is super organized and student-oriented. If you are lost in class ask questions since he loves them and he will explain the same question from different perspectives if the message isn't being understood completely.
I felt like we rushed through the lessons too much.

One of the best professors here on RIT. He enjoys teaching and makes it fun. If you have any questions he'll do his best to help you and make it easy to understand by giving examples. HE LOVES QUESTIONS!

Professor Cliver LOVES teaching, and LOVES to see the reaction on a students face when he explains something in a way that is easy for them to understand. This man TRULY cares about the wellbeing of all of his students, and is extremely accessible outside of class. Also, his wife bakes cookies, and on Wednesday, you can go snag one from his office!

Professor Cliver is easily the one of the best professors at RIT. I took him for DSD2, and he did a fantastic job organizing the lectures. The lectures were actually fairly easy, as long as you paid attention and did the homework then the quizzes are very easy. Lab is very difficult, but Cliver was very helpful during office hours.

Love's questions, like loves them. Great person. For DSD I, here's how class goes: -Starts with an example of what you'll be learning and goes from there, can be confusing, so ask questions, he loves them -More and more questions, and you start to understand. -Everything clicks in the "Aha!" moment and class becomes both fun and educational

I might have to take points off because you are only allowed to ask 1E6 questions per semester, and if you go over your limit he will have to allocate you more and its inconvenient. Seriosly, probably the best professor at RIT, and his humor helps you understand the material.

Genuinely a nice person, and cares deeply about his students. He will have cookie days to encourage students to his office hours, understanding towards if a student is having a hard time, and just a overall amazing person. You can just talk to him about any and all problems whether it is related to class or not

The lecture from Cliver was actually incredibly easy, but it was probably due to the nature of the course - DSD2 lab was extremely hard. Cliver is an amazing professor who cares for his students. Super reasonable and wants you to do well. Definitely go to his office hours and you will get great feedback and help.
Loves answering questions. Explanations are precise and clear.

Classes are enjoyable - Cliver puts a ton of effort into making sure students are getting material. Office hours are very helpful & he allows note sheets on most tests. HOWEVER!!! He has a tendency to jump from topic & imply stuff. If you find that you do not do well in loosely structured courses, don't take his course.

Very caring person and understands the students, like he's in our shoes. Very empathetic .Office hours are enjoyable. Be sure to take notes/understand topics that he covers for multiple days: most likely on the test. One thing I disliked is the switching from topics to lab discussions, ruining the organization.
Easily one of the best professors on campus. Makes sure everyone in the class understands the material and is always willing to help. Super friendly, super funny, and all around a great guy.

He is a really fun professor, don't get me wrong electronics I, is a very difficult course. But he somehow makes it a little easier. He absolutely loves questions. He is very willing to help even if you are completely lost. Easy to talk to and find. Fair warning he does give lots of Homework.
Great and understanding guy. Super nice in lab and is very helpful no matter how lost you are. If you can't make it to lab it's very easy to reschedule for another lab time.
Professor Cliver is a great man and great professor. He is hilarious and worth going to at 8AM. You will not be disappointed.

Professor Cliver is the best professor I've had. I've taken 2 different classes with him now and both have been amazing. He doesn't just understand the course, but his students. He will re-explain things multiple ways if he senses people don't understand him, an will adjust the material day-to-day based on student feedback and understanding.

Knowledgeable professor who is always fine explaining concepts/questions multiple times(and ways) in class. Also accessible outside class; hosts office study sessions with cookies. Cliver is very good at understanding what might throw students off and then ameliorating. HW is from the textbook. TAs are not all as great but grading's standardized.

comment: Take his classes, you won't regret it. This man is amazing.
Professor Cliver is perfect. Even though I only took one freshman level class with him, I continue to learn from him even 3 years later.

I've taken as many courses with him as I could. Cliver is the single best professor I've ever had. He really cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. He is always there if you need help. In class he always makes sure to answer all questions so everyone understands the material.

Professor Cliver is hands down the greatest professor at RIT! He truly cares for his students and makes you comfortable to ask as many questions as much as possible. Overall, if you see Cliver for any class, take him!

The best professor I've ever taken at RIT. His lectures are incredibly useful and enjoyable. He had regular office hours and was very helpful during them. He makes sure everyone in his class is very comfortable and encourages questions to the point where he will stop lecture until someone asks something. Worth the 8am 100%. TAKE HIS CLASS

Took Digital System Design 1 with him. Probably the greatest professor I've ever had/ will ever have. Enthusiastic  every day, high energy lectures, pleads class to ask questions, bribes students with cookies to attend office hours, "Cliver House": on Friday nights provides free dinner at his house in addition to tutoring.
Sparked my interest in computer engineering. An amazing man and an amazing class. You will not regret taking Cliver.

Professor Cliver may very well be the best professor at RIT. In his lectures he breaks down complicated concepts into simple easy to understand concepts. After each concept Cliver will literally stop and beg the class to ask questions. He is incredible in office hours, and he bribes students to come with cookies. He loves teaching and is the man.

While he may show up several minutes late to lab often, and frequently disappears for 20 minutes to go get coffee, or goes back to his office and gets distracted by some project only to be reminded that he was in the middle of lab. I love having Cliver as a lab instructor, he is funny, upbeat, clear in his explanations and is willing to help you.

Really tries to help his students, and makes lectures extremely bearable. He constantly stresses the importance of questions and how they take no time at all to answer. Can go a bit fast sometimes but always slows down when requested.

He loves when you asks questions. So never be afraid to ask. He will encourage questions and will try to make sure everyone understands the material. The material is hard, but he makes learning it as easy as possible. Take his class! he is funny and very helpful

Everyone should have a class with Cliver, there's no other experience quite like it. The course material was hard (Signals, Systems and Transforms), but he's really good at explaining it. Go to his office hours, even just an hour a week can make a huge difference, and sometimes there's cookies!

Awesome professor. Really cares about your success in his class. He feels that your grade is a reflection of him as a teacher and does everything he can to make sure you succeed. Absolutely loves answering any and all student questions. One of the best professors I've ever had.

Great professor! Takes things at a good pace in class and is willing to answer any question in or out of class. Fair tests, makes sure you're well prepared for them. Really cares about his students on a personal level. Used the textbook a lot for examples and homework.

TAKE HIM!!! He attended RIT and understands what it is like to be a student at this school. He lets students come to his house on Fridays for dinnerextra helpfunwhatever. Only some of the questions on his exams are a bit unclear as to why they are worded the way they are. He assigns HW with required and recommended problems. DO ALL OF THEM!

I had Prof. Cliver two semesters in a row and he definitely did not disappoint. He is an amazing teacher who really knows how to make you understand the concepts. If you're struggling and you go to his office hours, he troubleshoots to see how he can explain the concept differently in terms that you understand. Extremely helpful and very kind.

He's clear, hilarious, and extremely helpful. The only negative thing I could think of is the fact that the exams had to be crammed into 50 minute periods and were therefore really short, and he didn't give partial credit. So a mistake cost a lot. But other than that, he's fantastic.
Seriously, Take him for every class. I guarantee it is worth the 8am. Trust me!
Take him every chance you get!

Professor Cliver is so enthusiastic and cares so much about his students. He is an amazing professor because he truly tries to get into the mind of his students and sees what teaching methods work well for the class as a whole. He loves it when his students ask questions in class and see him during his office hours. Extremely helpful and nice guy.

Cliver is the best, he really puts his focus on the students and their needs. And his wife bakes. I didn't have any problem taking this class, he practices what he teaches so it's easier to learn from him, he's great.
Best professor that I have had at RIT. Going to class is always fun and Cliver is always willing to answer any and all questions that people have.
Great teacher. Really invested in his students, has gatherings outside of class to help. Class is usually a lecture supplemented with lots of questions and him calling on people to put up answers.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. He's a great teacher and has a great personality. He makes students feel totally comfortable asking questions. He moves fast in lecture, but stops often to answer questions. The lab section of this class can be difficult, but the lecture is easy.

Cliver is an amazing teacher with a great attitude toward teaching. He loves to teach, and he makes students want to learn. He is very helpful and makes it very clear on day one that if you do not ask questions you are wasting your OWN money. My only criticism would be that often the homework assignments were not on material covered in class.

Professor Cliver is a good professor and is great at relating to the students but sometimes tends to get off track. It's sometimes frustrating to sit there when you don't fully understand a concept and he's making jokes at the front of the classroom; still, a stellar teacher and if you pay attention it can be an entertaining, moderately easy class.
Extremely good professor, funny and always enthusiastic about class.

Professor Cliver is the best professor in the world. He knows what he is doing. I guarantee that you will smile and enjoy each class with him. Also you will finish the class with the best knowledge you can get in the class. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND taking his classes.
Great professor who really cares about the students both in and out of class.
My favorite teacher at RIT. Hands down. I'm not a nerd by any means and this guy made me smile every class, a great teacher to get to know out of class as well. A great teacher, a better man.

Makes the material enjoyable and makes sure everyone understands it in the classroom. However, in the lab, you're pretty much on your own. If you take good notes and pay attention in class, along with keeping up with the homework assigned, you should fare decently enough in his class.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. Despite having class fairly early in the morning, I enjoyed this class a lot. Cliver encourages questions if you don't understand things and has a very clear teaching style. You will learn a lot.

A phenomenal teacher.  Every lecture sort of revolves around questions as they are the best way to learn.  Knows exactly what he's talking about and can explain everything in numerous ways to accommodate different mind sets.  Very little homework with one quiz every week.  Should be an easy A with average effort.
Great teacher, really makes sure everyone understands what he is teaching.  He even does this thing every Friday where you can go to his house for tutoring and free food.

Great professor. Knows everyone's names on the first day and LOVES questions. Very helpful professor. Quizzes tend to be a little tougher than the weekly homework assignments but not too bad depending on your grader. Hosts Cliver house nights every Friday night. Never got the chance to go but heard they're pretty fun.
A very excellent professor.  Always encourages questions that are answered clearly, has a great sense of humor, and above all, COOKIES!!!

Very animated instructor. Asks for questions like crazy. However, you must ask questions to understand everything. That's how he designs his lectures. The book is extremely hard to understand but his lectures clearly lay out the content. He is very funny and excited about the material. One of the best instructors that I have had at RIT.

Top-of-the-line, incredible professor. His lectures consist of explaining everything in beautifully perfected detail and clarity. Practically squeezes questions out of students, and encourages students to ask questions about virtually everything he says. Attend his Friday night parties. The food is INCREDIBLE. Exams are easy if you do the homework.

Cliver was my favorite freshman professor. His quizzes were the only very hard part (but if you do your homework you've seen it all before). Tests were very fair. Homework was as long as you wanted. He however was very fun and loved questions. He had friday night parties at his house as tutoring sessions for students!
Go to class, do you homework, and do your part. And you will be more then fine.  Best Professor at RIT.  He cares for his students, and wants to answer any questions you have.
The best professor I had in RIT! Explanations are clear, but u have to do HW and attend  classes.

Great professor! Knows what he's teaching and knows how to teach. Keeps students awake. Loves questions and makes you love to ask questions! Quizes go straight from hw,  Tests are not easy, but not too bad. Do your hw, ask questions in class and you will succeed!

One of the best teachers I have ever had! He works at Kodak doing the same thing that he teaches, so he truly understands it. HIGHLY encourages questions and is very good at responding to them. If you do your work, his class should be easy. If you do not understand what you are doing, ask and he will help you until you do understand.

lots of fun. Had him for circuits 2. He knows his stuff and makes the material very easy to understand. Maybe oversimplifies material sometimes. Optional homeworks kept me from retaining material very well because I didnt do them.

One of the best Professors at RIT. Explains very nicely. Good teaching methods. Labs are fun. Encourages lots and lotssss of questions.

Amazing professor. Happy to have taken his class.
The professor is very good and intelligent and will help you when you are requiring it. The teaching is cool and helps you.
Nice professor. Actually learned from him

Amazing professor. Tend to always walk away from his class smiling

Like most everybody else said, professor Kwon shows exceptional interest in the class and in how well his students are doing.  Work load was rather heavy (data comm II) but you learn the material extremely well! For sure my favorite professor at RIT

Kwon is a great guy and a great teacher. Explains everything thoroughly and actually cares that people are learning. He is a good grader too and always helpful if you need it. Just make an effort and getting an A or B is not a hard task! One of my favorites

He is a very very nice person again, and very engaged in class and outside of the class as well, I had him for data comm network 2 and I thought all the projects and homework were very interesting.

This guy is so unclear about what he wants us to do.

JKwon is a really cool guy, makes jokes in class, very friendly. Some difficulty with understanding what he is talking about from time to time, and sometimes he has trouble correctly understanding and answering student questions. Definitely worth taking though.

Awesome prof, would gladly take her again given the chance. Dr Comer makes lectures worth coming to, super lenient grader, extra credit, great at explaining things, and offers more things than the textbook as well as a different take on the content in it. She's an amazing professor; she makes things very easy since it's an intro class. She has a sense of humor, which definitely helps me keep awake in classes. Very good lecturer, genuinely passionate about behaviorism, well written projects and assignments. Strict but quite reasonable late work policy. Professor Comer was amazing, and if you could take her class, take it. She drops your lowest grade for almost everything and gives a lot of extra credit. Go to class because she randomly does participation activities. There are weekly assignments too, but you can do the whole course ahead of time if you want to.
For Comer, all homework and turn-ins are online, making the class easy. However, if you miss class, your grade tanks.

Dr. Comer's teaching is very enticing and makes her presentations very engaging. You often have paper-based activities within class that you do for attendance, so attending class is very important. Took intro to psych with her. Really easy class with a plethora of material available to use for the quizzes. She's also hilarious which helps keep you awake. Attendance is partially mandatory as you need to be there for the activities which constitute 20% of the grade (she won't tell you when they are but they're really easy).

Her lectures are fun, and the material is easy to learn. She does open internet quizzes each week and the final is open internet. Easy class, fun professor.
A thoroughly engaging teacher with clear and concise expectations for grading. Also has a great sense of humor.
Amazing professor, super engaging and I enjoyed the course a lot. Would love to have this prof again

Absolutely amazing! Would totally recommend her for any of your psych classes. Her grading is very common-sense and she gives great feedback. She puts a lot of weight on discussions, but if you participate you're good. She knows her stuff and is very insightful!
Comer is GREAT! Go to lecture, participate when she asks, and enjoy it. By far one of the best psych classes I have taken. Final exam was online and she gave a study guide
All online grading things except for class participation, only reason to go to class. Lots of "busy" work. Very nice and funny professor. Have to buy online hw application. Easy A if you do the work.

Very easy lecture to sit through despite being a 9am, not very difficult, especially if you took AP psych before this. If you didn't i could see you struggling more than I did, but the work is very manageable. Overall really good class and really good lecturer

She's great. Her lectures are pretty good and she pops a few jokes here and there. Homework is online and needs to be purchased. The textbook comes with the purchase and is heavy on assignments. Amazing lecturer, absolutely no complaints there. In terms of pure teaching skills, she may have been the best professor I had this semester. comment: Easy to fair amount of work. Just a weekly textbook reading (skippable) and online activities. Generous extra credit opportunities, and multiple assignments dropped. She makes Psychology fun to learn, her lectures are entertaining and engaging, her quizzes & tests are open note, what more can you ask for? Absolutely loved this course and Dr. Comer.  She is a very easy grader, and she splits up the big paper into multiple sections, so it is not that much work. I mostly enjoyed the celebrity project, but boy, it was A LOT of work. Nonetheless, the class was good. She was a tougher grader than in PSYC 101. Take advantage of her office hours, it REALLY helps out significantly! DON'T skip class; you only get UP TO three freebies.

comment: Dr. Comer does a wonderful job in turning the dense content of the course into an easily digestible lecture. The way she teaches clicks for me and I feel encouraged to immersion in psyc because of her. All tests including the final are open-book and online. The textbook is imperative as it has most of the HW, and she periodically grades attendance.

Dr. Comer is amazing. Her lectures are fun and the homework load is not heavy. She is well educated and will answer questions in class. It is a goof course to take, just to be familiar with the content. There is 3 writing pieces throughout the semester and one gets dropped. All quizzes are online as well as the final.
Such a great teacher. Genuinely learned so much and always looked forward to her class.

Easy A for $80. You have to pay for the online textbook bc thats where you do the hw. Final was online and can be taken anywhere. Certain days would be taken down for attendance. Attend 10 out of the 15 days, it would be 100 for attendance.

Professor Comer is a fantastic professor! She has awesome lectures and provides lots of opportunities for extra credit and drops the lowest scores for papers/quizzes. I've really enjoyed my time taking intro to psych with her, and I can't wait to take upper-level psych with her again!

Dr.Comer is a lovely teacher. She has an online quiz once a week and homework assignments that are multiple-choice. She does a random participation activity but no attendance besides that.

Turned boring perspective into an interesting few hours each week. She uses an online textbook for all HW, which can be frustraing but okay. Tough grader for essays, but drops some low grades.

An hour of homework a week with quiz questions straight from the textbook or lecture slides, it's an easy A if you do the work

Really fun lectures, participation is earned by attendance and it random per lecture, not every lecture has a attendance but her lectures are really fun to learn. HW is easy just a few questions online and response pieces are graded easily

Good experience with her for intro to psych. There are basic assignments to do every week but they are graded for completion only. comment: Dr. Comer is an amazing lecturer. She makes sure to relate the course topics to real life. Excellent professor, engaging lectures, and the tests are fairly easy if you show up to class, pay attention, and skim over your notes a few times. Would take again. Attendance isn't "mandatory", per se, but there are some small bits of graded classwork that you'll miss by skipping.
Very fun and easy if you pay attention in lecture. 10/10 would take her class again
She's one of the best teachers I ever got at RIT. Hilarious lectures and very passionate about what she teaches. She helps out a lot and makes class fly by. I would keep taking all her classes.
Dr. Comer knows her stuff, and her lectures are interesting and easy to understand. I ended up double majoring in psych after taking her class!

She is a great professor. I am a Computer Science major and I seriously considered changing  to Psychology because of how great she was. Comer is an excellent professor. She puts all of her lecture powerpoints on mycourses before class, making note taking easy! Her tests are fair; make sure you study. She also gives numerous extra credit opportunities and makes the class interesting. This class made my double major in psych.

Dr. Comer is a great professor - HIGHLY recommended. Her lectures are interesting and she only gives 4 tests all semester. There's absolutely no way to fail these if you study, she basically gives you the answers in her practice handouts. Only 3 papers all semester, also, which are simple. A++ on this professor  course.

She is a fantastic lecturer. She explains material well and makes it interesting. Study guides are posted for each test which covers all material on the test; these are long but if you do it, you will do good. Would like to have again.

Loved her. She is definitely pretty strict, but when you have classes with over 150 students, that's not a bad thing. It was a class I definitely enjoyed going to. Exams were tough, but she gives you a clear outline of all topics that will be on them so you can focus your studying. Overall not too bad at all if you go to classes.

Very tough grader. If you don't come to her classes and take notes from her power points, you are screwed, because the book doesn't help you much.  She expects you to memorize everything on this planet Earth that is related to psychology. Wouldn't recommend it for people who are not into psychology.

AWESOME professor. Extremely hard grader and tough tests but I learned a ton! I want to sit in on her lectures even if I'm not in the class! She is really a great professor and I highly suggest taking her if you are willing to put in work.

If you plan on taking her. Read the textbook. Her lectures can be helpful. However. Her study guides for the test are massive. Need to know too much for too little on the test. Doesn't use textbook at all. Read off of slides. Test challages are worthless.

This class is NOT easy, but certainly worth it. Dr. Comer is an excellent lecturer and really knows her stuff. Her exams are pretty tough, but she gives you tips throughout the semester on ways to memorize. As long as you come to class and take notes it should be easy to keep up. I Really really liked Dr Comer

After taking this class, I decided to get a minor in psychology. Dr. Comer made the class really interesting by supplementing the lectures with video clips or interesting photos. 3 easy essays, 4 tests, and a participation grade (which is given by the amount of in-class exercises you hand in). As long as you study and pay attention, you will pass.

Class was interesting, and Prof Comer was a good teacher, however, the tests were extremely difficult as they each contained so much material, and the study guides don't really narrow anything down, so you have sometimes hundreds of topics to go over before each test, which I found very difficult.

I like Prof Comer a lot, and I found her classes interesting, however, the tests are extremely difficult as they are so far apart and you have to know so much material for them. She's an awesome teacher, one of the best I've ever had. As of this year, her tests are IDENTICAL to her study guides. Not an easy course, but anyone can get an A if you just look over study guides before the 3 tests. I highly recommend her. She's awesome, great sense of humor and willing to help you in any way. She wants her students to succeed.
The class was very interesting and she is a fun teacher,  but her tests are really hard and a lot of what is on the long study guide isn't actually on the test.

Great teacher! Definitely sit in the front of the class so it's easier to pay attention. Tests are definitely harder, and so taking good notes is essential. If you do not print her powerpoints before class then you are screwed. Take excellent notes and study and you're golden! She's awesome!

Great teacher! Take good notes, print out her lecture slides and actually study the information! Yes, you actually have to put in some work... shocking! If you want to be lazy and get an easy A don't take this class. You do need to put in some work to learn the info but it is well worth it. Compared to other psych classes this class is a breeze!

Class is a serious GPA killer. Reads off PowerPoint slides the entire class. Doesn't assign homework so how you learn the material is up to you. Don't take her class if you can't memorize concepts or hate reading out of a book.

This teacher is okay for anyone who can learn easily by reading a book. However, everyone else can expect a C or less if you do not learn from reading easily. She will not help you develop different strategies for reading and rather will just tell you to go see the tutors.

the course is not too hard. had to study a little bit but as long as you pay attention in class all you need are her power points. The book can be used for things she didnt cover in class but only a minimum number of questions are asked from the book that wherent covered in class. plus she usually gives curves on exams. 2 exams and 2 easy papers

If you miss a class, you're screwed. If you can't memorize 10 pages of vocabulary for each of the 3 term tests, you're screwed. Seriously, this class is damn impossible. She explicitly told the class "I expect the class average to be a C through the course". GPA killer.

You will be graded for two term projects, three exams, and attendance.  Be thorough with her lectures and the detailed book.  She grades you for participation in the class.  Very picky grader.  She talks for 110 minutes per lecture.  She focuses more towards the research rather than understanding the subject.  Not a very helpful course.

She expects you to be thorough with her lectures and the book.  Book is elaborate.  There are 2 term projects and 3 Exams.  Exam include 50 X choice questions and 5 SA. All her lectures are based on power point slides which are available online but you have to be in class to have all of the info. Only 3 exams based on at least 5-6 chapters:50 multip.choice & 5 short answers where you have to be very specific!! its super hard to remember 6 chapters and be specific on any possible question she may ask.Must read book

Bill is VERY unclear about what he looks for in the projects. .  . Very annoying professor.

Bill is a great guy who really cares about his students that ask for help. However, he does drag out the time of the studio class and requires you to email him projects and color comps later in the quarter instead of just bringing them into class - this can get very annoying with conflicting due dates.

I thought he was a great teacher and you can tell he has a passion for what he does. Class requires a significant amount of time though but it is worth it. I had 30-45hrs in each dimensional project but I received all A's so just try and you'll be fine.

Bill is a very honest and no-nonsense professor. If he knows you're a slacker, he'll give you a hard time. (I'm sure everyone here who posted bad feedback fits in this category.) This shouldn't be a full class.  Bill frequently runs out of things to say, and then makes uncomfortable chitchat for hours rather than letting the class go early.  The content in both is so limited you wonder how 10 weeks of class are filled.  Bill comes off as a desperate salesman with frequency, so afraid of not being taken seriously.

I still remember the first day of INTRO. to digital illustration.  He said and I quote, "This is not a class to learn new programs in." Uploads all his slides online so you have no excuse to do badly in his class. (tip: don't take the 3-hour class. His lectures are interesting but very heavy and you might not be able to handle it)
Very funny. Very willing to help you and clarify things if asked. Very passionate and loves to see students who want to participate

He is definitely a nice guy, and knows his stuff when it comes to art history, but his grading criteria is ridiculous. He tells us to write papers in MLA and doesn't know MLA format himself, which infuriates me.

If every professor was like Peter Gabak, the world would be a much better place. Peter is what a professor is supposed to be, an expert in his field, engaging with students, and demanding when it comes to expectations. I'm a recent graduate of RIT and I've never rated a professor before, but I felt compelled to come back just to rate Peter. 10/10

Peter is awesome!  You have to be on your game and ready to actually work, but he could make any topic entertaining.  If you write the class off and don't show up, you won't do well, but as his classes are more entertaining than anything on TV or the interwebs, you'll be glad to go!

Peter is by far the most engaging professor I've had, and he's not even a professor for my major. He makes an effort to get to know you as a student and his lectures are engaging. You will have to write a fair amount, but he grades very fairly and allows for early paper submissions so you can rework it. I would recommend Peter to anyone.

I'm a software engineering student and was really not looking forward to taking art and architecture 1. After taking the class with Gabak, I know find myself wishing I could retake the class again. Fun, engaging and overall a pleasure to listen to. I was fascinated by this class. The grading was fair and justified.

Peter is the most passionate and engaging speaker, his lectures are interesting and you want to listen to him talk. He can make the most mundane thing seem like the most interesting thing in the world. I regret not taking all of my art history classes with him.

Fundraising and grant writing class -> Peter's lectures were concise, effective and extremely beneficial.  I cant imagine staying awake in the class with out really good professor.  If you care about learning about art history or grant writing take Gabak, even if you hate the topic you will enjoy it after his class

Peter is INCREDIBLE! He is so easy to talk to and just a generally funny and friendly guy. He's also brilliant- he knows a ton about art + architectural history and he makes everyone excited about learning it. Take as many classes with him as you can!!
teacher is awesome and energetic. easy to talk to. I never used the book. the title was fundraising and grant writting but 90% of the course was marketing (making brochures ect.)

Peter is awesome. Cares about you inside AND outside of the classroom. He grades a little harshly (got a 94 in his class and still got a B), and he didn't mention that in the syllabus. BUT Peter is amazing and I highly recommend him to anyone and everyone.
Such a great teacher.  Really cares about students learning and can make even boring classes and topics extremely interesting.  Take as many classes as you can from this incredible professor.

I accidentally butt dialed my mom while in Gabak's Western Art lecture one night. I looked at my phone at the end and realized she had been there listening to his lecture for the past 40 minutes. My mom knows nothing about art history and she said she couldn't stop listening, it was that good. Gabak's lectures are amazing.

Peter is amazing! By far the most passionate, interesting, and helpful teacher I've ever had. He knows so much about art history and you can tell that he absolutely loves teaching it. He does not give multiple choice tests, but rather gives take home essay tests. This is a great way to learn the material. I highly recommend him as a professor!!

Everyone should take Peter,not only does he offer extensive knowledge in art history he is the goto source for all of your grant writing and fundraising needs.  Great to have a professor as inspiring as peter

Prof. Gabak's Survey of Western Art class is great! He knows art history inside and out and loves it. He speaks quickly so make sure to listen intently. Whether you do well is entirely up to you. Some people slack off in his class but those who don't will do well. He is a fair grader and gives you multiple chances to raise your grades.
so bad. i didn't learn anything
Dr. Marengo is a very kind person. The class was very informal, with no exams. He often would go over time. Overall a great person and an okay professor.

As a person I love him however as a professor not so much.
He only checks the exams. 
Hw can be almost a blank to get 100%. The exams are difficult and don't relate to the material covered in class 
The textbook doesn't help.
He is very quiet and needs to bring his own Bluetooth microphone. Which doesnt help. Essentially you learn nothing

Dr. Marengo is a tricky professor to rate. On one hand his classes are easy to pass and don't take much effort to get a good grade. On the other hand when he is teaching topics you should be knowledgeable in he is fairly useless. His lectures have no substance to them and rarely relate to homeworks or exams at all. He just talks about whatever.
Very quiet and goes off on random tirades about math history that are not important to the course

He's very nice and understanding. Even though he may be soft-spoken he enjoys teaching mathematics and is very knowledgeable. All exams are done online (also final). However, it's difficult to raise your grade. HW is not collected so your grade is just your tests and quizzes. Do the HW because many of his test questions are from the textbook.

Gets sidetracked a lot in lecture and can spend multiple days on a single topic, putting the class behind schedule. Only grades two midterms and final. As long as you put in the effort and he sees you're trying, you'll pass.

Prof Marengo is one of the sweetest professors I've had at this university. He upgraded his personal home internet after complaints of poor stream quality. He goes out of his way to make the class as low stress as possible - If you show up and do the assignments you will pass with at least a C. The only way to fail his class is to turn nothing in.

I'm sure he's great in person but online was just not good. His lectures looked as if he was recording with a potato. His answer keys he sent out were blurry as well, couldn't read them and when students complained, he didn't even send out a better one. Hopefully he can go back to teaching in person soon..

Prof. Marengo has failed to transition to online learning. The audio/video often cut out, the doc scanner he uses makes his handwriting illegible, & there is NO POSTED CONTENT in mycourses. 95% of the grade is quizzes/exams. You'll be self-teaching the entire time, there's no point to showing up to class. Every other prof I had adjusted fine.

I enjoyed taking Prob & Stats with Dr. Marengo this fall. The class challenged me for a level 200, but he understood that and graded exams/quizzes leniently. He also replaced the lowest exam with the final, which boosted me from a B to an A! The only way to really fail is by doing nothing. Pay attention in class, do the optional HW and youre good.

Great professor for Mathematical Statistics I. I'm looking to take II with him as well (since he's the only prof to teach it). Go to class, read the textbook, attempt the homework. He'll give you full credit (even if the answers are incorrect or incomplete) if you put effort into it. I'd recommend him to anyone.

comment: Don't do it. He will pass you some how but if you want a decent grade in his class don't take this. Go anywhere else. I found calculus 1 and 2 to be easier than this class and more fair. This class was harder than University Physics 1.

Class was very tough but lectures were very interesting. His tests were very tough but grade seemed to be on effort shown not on grade on tests. Don't receive homework back after turning it in. Great professor, just expect class to be difficult.

Fantastic class. He really cares that you learn the material; always doing stuff to bump peoples grades up so that they weren't so focused on them. Goes slowly and in depth to make sure you actually understand things, rather than just regurgitating formulas. Also, he may be going completely insane (but in a good way)!

His lectures are very clear and he generally has good charisma, which makes lectures not boring. The only complaint I could possibly bring up is that sometimes he's a bit quiet, which is a bit of an issue if you're in the back of the room. Otherwise, the class was great. Homework is optional too, but helpful.

"I have spoken for 42 minutes and have told you nothing relating to today's lesson" is an actual quote from a Tuesday lecture. He decided to then quiz us that Thursday. He instructs us to memorize things only for them to not appear on quizzes. Personally I do not know how I should prep for my next exam. Textbook is a must, you gotta teach yourself

Dr. Marengo is an incredibly nice professor. He's very understanding towards his students and gave 2 weeks for each take home exam. Homework was worth the most points, and he offered a HW help session each weekend where he would go over the HW solutions before the HW was due.  He really loves math and statistics, which made the class very enjoyable

Very good professor, goes over the material well, does a lot of examples on the board and goes over the solutions in detail. Homework is not collected and he's a very fair grader. He gives quite a bit of partial credit. He gave my class 2 tests instead of 3 like most calc professors.
GREAT PROFESSOR! He is extremely helpful and makes sure you understand everything before moving on. I would recommend him to everyone. His tests go hand in hand with what he teaches in class.

he is funny and smart.He is extremely helpful and makes you cannot live without math.He doesn't want students to use calculator i like this cause I don't like to use calculator.easy grader.clever teaching and flexible with anything

Great professor! He knows the material in great depth and is willing to explain it to you. He does get really close if you don't speak loud enough so really project your questions. Funny enthusiastic and clear professor. He is slow so bring the text and stay ahead if you tend to get bored the tests are hard.

Nicest and most helpful teacher I had at RIT so far. He is more then willing to help you if you don't understand. He's definitely not the easiest teacher but it's not hard to pass his class at all. DEFINITELY recommend him. He's my favorite teacher. He LOVES classic rock  and loves to talk about music if you want to get on his good side!

Teaches laboriously slowly. Assigns brutal homework problems. Elaborate test questions involving several weeks of content. This guy was born to be an Honors professor. You will learn, oh, you WILL learn. I think everyone got Cs or lower on every homework and every test, but I had a B, and others got As. Honors classes are so weird.

Teaches at a very slow pace. He's very approachable and helpful but the material is presented slowly and carefully. Some classes we barely made it through 2 examples in an hour. This can be a blessing or a curse. It's all about your style.

Dr. Marengo is an excellent teacher. He goes slowly, but you learn the background of everything. He is great at breaking problems down and explaining each step, how to do it, and why you can. You will learn the subject inside and out. He has a hearing problem, especially with women's voices, so don't be offended if he doesn't understand you!

I had Engineering Mathematics with Professor Marengo for the 20094 quarter. I found him to be a very good professor. I loved to explain the topics beyond what the book cover.  He often repeated himself, to make sure you got the point.  He was very interested in getting the students to succeed.  No attendance, homework not graded (bad for me).

Sometimes the material was dry but he did his best to keep it interesting.  Didn't take attendance, didn't collect homework.  Tests and quizzes were fair and enough time was given.  Is very helpful during office hours if you need them.

Extremely boring and frustrating.  If you learn at a slow pace he's great but if you know what you're doing you'll just pull your hair out, he repeats things way too much.  Only went to one hour of each lecture and did fine the other lecture is just a repeat of the first, his tests and stuff aren't too bad.

Sometimes he has trouble understanding students questions, but I thought that he explained things pretty well overall.  A really nice guy.  He gives you partial credit on quiz and exam questions based on your work, so that is really cool.  His notes that he writes on the board are very neat, organized , and clear.
Insane. Very. I learned way too much about Calc in that class.
Best for the person who's an independent learner. Doesn't hold your hand but presents well. Can be quiet, try sitting closer to the board. Easy grader.

Pros: VERY easy grader, nice guy  Cons: extremely boring, tests are on the difficult side, doesn't seem very organized.  I personally didn't get anything from his lectures - I might as well not have ever gone to class!  Take him if you are good at learning the material on your own.
He is one of the best math teachers. Will make you feel like a mathematician.  very smart, and always knows the answer.
Stresses common themes, never changes the way he presents material or the way he approaches the problems so students learn. Sometimes it gets a little dry and tiring, but its worth it.
My Grade: C. Dr. Marengo was very helpful. Though he wasn't always easy, he thoroughly explained everything. His grading was pretty liberal (lots of partial credit).
very fair, will help you if you ask
Talks to the board all the time, class falls asleep, boring, easy to get lost
Hes a chiller

Makes a 3 hour night class fly by. Extremely knowledgable and structures the class so everything builds on itself, but he makes it accessible and interesting. Already signed up for another course with him. Sense of humor and is great at explaining/assisting if you are struggling. Need to go to class if you want to understand anything.

comment: My favorite professor by far! If you have the opportunity to take him, DO IT!

Great use of real-world examples for problem solving.  Several times I said to myself - "So THAT'S how you do that!"  Useful stuff, not just theory.  John is very engaging to everyone with a sense of humor.  I will take any class that he is teaching.
nice experience

My interest going into the class was extremely low. John was able to inspire me to want to learn more, and more about finance. His teaching style is all about involving the students, he will not move on until the students are comfortable with the material. Granted, the class was not a cake walk, but it is very possible to receive an A!

Professor Striebich is awesome.  He is really helpful and outlines the problems clearly before tests.  Tests are open notes, but they are not cake walks.  If you do the hw problems and practice then they aren't bad.  Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you expect to do good you must attend.
Very interesting lecturer.  Combines theory and current events with a sense of humor.  Class time flew by and was never boring. Will definitely take other classes from him.

I never liked my economics courses at my undergrad college.  He brings in articles and current events to make economics interesting.  I've learned a lot and see how economics can be used in business. Will definitely take other courses with him.

Great course with team and individuals projects and papers.  He's a real interesting speaker using current events.  I learned alot in this class.  Would recommend him to everyone for any econ or finance classes he teaches.
Such a good class.  He really makes you understand the material.  Alot of HW that is pretty hard, but all the test are open book and it helps you.

Katie is extremely kind and obviously wanted her class to have a good experience; it was her first time teaching in the department.  However, she took human-computer interaction, already not the most interesting topic, and made it worse.  There wasn't too much work, but what there was was tedious.  Lectures were horrible.  Avoid if possible.
such a great man funny with lots of fun for the whole class
Funny guy if you get to know him. Very straightforward when explaining tasks, pretty chill overall.
This professor is the freaking best. Also, he will make the best jokes about any student.
Blended course. Half class Half online. He's nice. Sometimes boring. But easy.
Yells at students, frequently loses train of thought, unhelpful in lab. Tests and quizzes have incomprehensible and misspelled questions. Avoid.

Do not take his class. During the labs he seems to not know what he is doing. Gets mad when students do not ask any questions.  But doesn?t answer the questions that are asked. Take wireless with any one else, NOT HIM!
Useless lab professor for wireless.
No Comments
Good Guy but a little hard to understand. Monotone voice put me to sleep sometimes but he was always there to help out.

Doesn't speak English very well, is very unclear in his lectures, and gets very upset when you get one of his in-class questions wrong. Very boring. Not helpful. When asked a question, he usually just repeats the last thing he said. Also gets very upset if no one has any questions.

I had Ms. Pickard for both orgo 1 and orgo 2 lab. Overall shes not a bad teacher, but I feel like there are definitely better choices. She is extremely slow to turn around grades, to the point where she actually submitted our final grades to the school late. In class shes friendly, generally helpful, and a relatively easy grader.
Excellent Teacher

This guy is awesome. He does curve the final grade a bit so that's great and on top of that he really helps you review for the exam. Just come to class and actually pay attention and go over his slides and you will do fine.
Great lectures, great feedback and support for students genuinely interested in the course.
I disagree with the previous review.  Dr. Lalonde is incredibly helpful and I found his tests to be more than fair.

Dr. LaLonde does not really focus on teaching.  He just challenges his students with hard exams.  Grading is straight-forward but knowledge is not really conveyed through.  Online lecture slides are boring with a monotonous voice.
nice
I enjoyed his class to the point of taking him again next semester! Be prepared to shoot alot, and don't let his early time slots freak you out! It's worth it!
Kirby is the best photo teacher I've had in the three years I've been here.

Not in photo illustration, just SPAS. This guy is great. Totally knowledgeable, sarcastic, and really helpful. He's someone I want to interact with and someone I'm not intimidated by. He's not afraid to tell it like it is and people really need to hear that. Please take his class, if you're committed to photo, you won't regret it.

Gary is an awesome teacher! I had him for ethics in bio and medicine. He starts the classes by playing music. We have fantastic discussion and he is very funny. There are no exams in this class, and there is very little work outside of class. Would recommend.

Exams took me 15 minutes max the entire semester. Easy material and easy-going personality. Attend class because the slides alone will not give you the info needed for the tests. Has fun guest lectures and gives more than enough freebies. The only shame is how much the material is repeated from other courses, but this depends on your schedule.

Professor Skuse is a really good professor and I enjoyed his class. You definitely don't want to miss his lectures because they have a lot of good information that you won't get from just reading the power point slides. His Exams can be tough but he gives you a lot of great study materials. I would definitely take another class with him.

Waste of time. It felt like Skuse gave up halfway through the semester and the last few quizzes and exams were complete jokes. On one hand the easy A is cool, but it's disappointing that I'm spending money and time to learn absolutely nothing. Skuse was nice but he would be kinda snarky to students and it didn't seem like he wanted to be there.

Dr. Skuse rocks I can't even lie. His lecture notes are vague but his actual lectures are very informative and helpful, so even though attendance isn't mandatory, it's a good idea to show up to every class. His exams are always online and entirely multiple choice/true and false, whatever. Easy class. SO EASY.
Show up to class, take good notes.

Good is as far as I can go for him. He is alright, knows his subject quite well, can make a joke here and there, and can be understanding about students. At the same time, he can be quite rude/condescending. I can definitely tell he cares about being a good teacher, sometimes he just misses the mark.

Amazing teacher. Third class in a row with him and I wish I could take a fourth. This class was my favorite that I've taken so far. Interesting topics with no busy work. It was a big paper on a topic of your choice and a presentation of a topic of your choice. Super interesting and I was always excited to go to class.
Dr. Skuse is an amazing professor and just an amazing person in general. He is  really fun and cares about your success, always always always take again!!1

Ethics in Bioinformatics. Dr. Skuse is an amazing professor and person, and you should take every class he offers. Course itself was taken for Writing Intensive req. Dr. Skuse is excellent at lecture, but he tries not to lecture at you too much. Topics are interesting. He always knows somebody that... story which is interesting and relevant.

Skuse is a great teacher!  Really chill, funny and wants you to understand whats going on in lab.  Always willing to help till you understand the material.  Labs are generally pretty easy, and you can leave class as soon as you finish.  Best yet, no tests, quizzes or homework.  Would recommend in a second!
Awesome teacher. No for for Intro. to Bioinformatics. Funny and always plays rock solos are beginning of class. 3 tests, amazingly easy.
Excellent teacher! Really talks a lot.

One of the greatest professors of all time, offering the best lectures on campus. He truly cares about class and loves it when people ask questions. He provides real-world examples to help relate the class to everyday life. He is also almost always available to help with an assignment or just give some advice. Highly recommend this professor.
Pretty solid professor, no complaints. There is a decent amount of homework, but he posts everything early, so you have a lot of time. He is one of the best professors I have ever had.

For a 200 level course, Professor Kesgin makes this class seem harder than it is. The lecture speed is okay, but the workload is insane. Be ready to do two chapters' worth of material some weeks. I wish I had taken this class with a different professor, could've been more interesting.

Kesgin is very nice and the class is very easy! My only complaint is that he is so unorganized. He often has due date posted at the last minute and the lectures or so boring. He take the lectures very slow and I feel like they could be sped up. Unexpected due dates and unorganized assignments are my biggest concerns.
While his lectures can sometimes be boring, you do end up learning the material. Not a lot of homework, 3 tests, 1 paper and a group project.
Basically just teaches right from textbook. Very strict will call on you even if looking down for one second. Seems always in bad mood. Not helpful.

She was awful.  She was worse than awful. She thought she was the only one with any knowledge of nutrition and refused to acknowledge anything anybody said.  I actually watched her notice someone's hand in the air and purposely turn away so she wouldn't have to answer it. She shouldn't still be teaching.

Made and interesting subject very boring. She will show a video, then expect you to stay in class while she reads from powerpoints exactly what the simple little 20 minute video just said. very uninteresting
Professor Jesse was a very nice Professor. He gave perfect feedback, and was not a tough grader at all. Really enjoyed the class with him, and would definitely take it again!

Took MKTG-430.He had high but reasonable expectations. Projects were designed to increase our knowledge of working with potential clients and how to navigate that by having us work with businesses local to Rochester. You do need to have presentation and communication skills. Easy A if you just do the work, which is reasonable given the class level.

I have terrible anxiety with group projects/presentations. This professor failed to acknowledge my anxiety and failed me from the course because of my inability to complete the group project for the class. He was very difficult to work with and did not care about my situation at all.

Professor Redlo is great! His lectures are fun and interesting and he gives many examples and practice activities. Projects consist of working with a random partner or group but are straightforward if you pay attention in class. Quizzes are based on the textbook and tests are based off lecture, he usually gives test review that is very helpful.

Dr. Redlo really knows his stuff. He is a phenomenal lecturer and keeps the class lighthearted with his sense of humor. The work is not difficult, one paper or other assignment roughly every 2 weeks. Always willing to help if you are struggling and is forgiving with his grading as long as you participate. He is extremely organized in myCourses.

Dr. Redlo is an amazing instructor. He is open-minded and often encourages students to share their perspectives and ideas with the class. In my experience, Dr. Redlo grades based on paper content and a few short quizzes every now and then. I thoroughly enjoy his class and hearing him speak, especially when he ties his own stories into his lessons.

Professor Redlo is a really funny guy I took him for one of my learning communities Freshman year it was so engaging and I loved the class not very many lectures it was more discussion based and you have 5 question quizzes pretty often
Redlo is an amazing professor, a little tough on grading but gives amazing feedback and really cares about your success,

Redlo took a boring subject and made the class fun. He gives a lot of homework, but it's a bunch of small things, like chapter reading quizzes or two page assignments. It's a decent amount of work, but never too much, and he's a great guy who will tell hilarious stories that make the content relevant.
Lots of simple work so assignments and quizzes are low stakes. Enjoyable and upbeat, if not sarcastic, personality. He genuinely wants to see you succeed.

Professor Redlo is a humorous professor with good lectures. Homework is given 1 week in advance, and all quizzes are take-home. Feedback for the writing assignments is comprehensive. Since he is an adjunct, he doesnt host any fixed office hours but is willing to meet up outside of class.

Is very passionate about his subject. Easy and fun to talk to in and outside of class. . He lets his opinions out about the world a bit, but it is related to the topic.  Overall, he cares about each student, and knows exactly what we have been through, because he is a recent RIT grad.

Dr. Professor Dude Guy is a new instructor at RIT, but he's bringing his A-Game to the job. He's funny, charismatic, heavily encourages an active classroom, and is all around a great professor. Do what's asked of you (which isn't much) and you won't have any issues.
Very nice and wants the best out of the students, even though it was a YearOne class
Very professional, yet funny.  Down to earth, great for a conversation.

This man made a boring class fun. He is easy going and ready for a laugh. Just do what little work he asks of you and participate and everything will be great. He is extremely relatable and someone who is ok with you just stopping by and making seemingly pointless small talk. All in all, a phenomenal professor.
nice stuff

comment: She is GREEEAT!!!! She is the most awesome teacher I have had through out RIT! She is very friendly, nice and she is really funny! She is very helpful towards her students she thinks about others than herself. Great teacher! I would recommend her!
Love her!  The best art teacher in the art department!
Awesome teacher! TAKE HER!!!

She's a great person to host Freshman Seminar! She's interesting, and had her husband, Quinsland or as per many, Dr. Q, to be part of her in-class activities to teach about the reproductive system.... Though don't get me wrong, when she teaches, it's like high school all over.

Sad that he is retiring, probably the best professor i have had so far in my CE flow chart. I realized during every lecture he never said a single filler word like "um, uhh" he knows his material very well and can teach for hours about a single small thing. Amazing professor!

I am absolutely devastated that he is retiring after this semester. He takes ZERO flack and writes epically sassy emails. Dr. Moon has inhuman grading speed; where there will be thorough feedback within an hour of submission. Dr. Moon has now set unreasonable expectations for other professors to not be able to meet. I aspire to be like Dr. Moon.

A lot of the class is equations derived and discovered by Moon himself. He knows the material better than anyone. Lectures are informative, but not overwhelming and he often lets students out early. For labs, you get infinite resubmission attempts if a reasonable effort is made on the first try. There is no reason not to get 100% in that section.

Awesome professor. You can tell he is genuinely passionate about what he talks about and is also never late and never takes up too much time. He also posts all his notes in the exact tone of voice he would speak them in which is very helpful. Also cracked at grading and emails, usually having responses within an hour and great feedback.

Dr. Moon is one of the most phenomenal professors I have ever had. He is extremely patient and incredibly clear when answering questions. I was very intimidated in taking this course as this was the first Electrical Engineering class I ever took, but pay attention, ask questions, and do the homework and there is no doubt you can succeed.

Dr. Moon is built different when it comes to grading lab reports and tests as fast as possible. His lectures are great and he gives students every possible chance to get a 100% in the lab section because there are unlimited resubmissions to make up lost points as long as you submit on time the first time. Tests were open notes.

Very solid professor. Good policy of having exams open notes, it shifts your focus from trying to memorize everything to understanding the concepts more. Only thing I wasn't a fan of was homework assignments 8-10. It felt like they were overly convoluted for no reason. Besides that, I learned a lot from digital electronics!
Best professor I've had so far. Super quick at grading and is super fair.
Amazing lectures, Amazing office hours, Amazing organization; Amazing professor
Dr.Moon provides his students with every resource necessary for them to succeed in his class. He is a very fair grader, and is always accessible outside of class.

I also took both Linear/Digital with Moon this fall and I agree with the rating below. There were no quizzes, but the HW/sample tests more than prepared me for the exams. Lectures were entertaining with plenty of jokes while at the same time crystal clear. Most of all, he structured the workload of the two classes to never conflict with eachother.

I took both Digital Electronics and Linear Systems with him this Spring. He is the absolute GOAT of the EE department. There is a ton of homework but its for a good reason so you learn the material. For me both of the classes were like this; Homework were the Quizzes and the Quizzes were the Tests. Easy A if you pay attention and put the work in.

comment: Best Professor.

I also had Moon for EEEE353 (Linear Systems). He gives homework every week, with more than enough time to get it done. He'll have homework and exams graded within a day. Easily accessible, doesn't teach you more than you need to know but tells you before if he's about to. Great guy, take him at all costs. All the work you do in class is purposeful.

Took him for Digital Electronics, Fall 2017. Best professor I've had at RIT. The homeworks are definitely tough, but if you can do the homeworks, you will be fine. Extremely helpful in class and office hours and gives great insight on the material covered. Would take and will take again.

Dr. Moon was the best prof I've had as an EE student. I had him for Linear Systems and Digital Electronics. These courses were tough, especially Linear Systems, but he is very accessible for office hours, which you will most likely will need to go to in order to get a good grade. He is clear about grading and is very helpful in office hours.

I feel like I got a really good handle on electronics 1 by taking it with Dr Moon. He's a crystal clear lecturer and very open to questions. Homework is out of the book, but all homeworks are given solved solutions after the due date. All notes, homeworks, homework solutions and even the textbook can be used on exams.

More interested in helping students succeed than any professor I have had. He never pampers students or has weirdunreasonable rules. His classes are quite difficult, but they are easy to do well in if you put in the expected effort. I'm  glad he teaches the difficult classes; no other professor I know could convey such complex info so effectively!

He is the best professor in the department and the most dedicated. With that said he also excepts the most out of any professor. His tests are very hard but they're more than fair and if you understand the homeworks you should be fine

I can understand why his ratings are so high but it is very misleading. While Dr. Moon is probably the most dedicated professor it's well known that you avoid Dr. Moon at all costs.
