Quizzes and tests are fair; you never see anything on them that you wouldn't have expected to. Homework is due weekly and the weekly quizzes based on the homework. He can be a bit awkward but it's worth it in the end.

Eric is a great guy. He tells you why you should care about what hes teaching. Linear is a tough class because it deals with a lot of conceptual topics in math. Weekly quizzes that are very fair. He's a little nerdy, but the best math professor I've had at RIT yet. very much recommend him for any class.

Eric is a great Professor. Very kind, a little nerdy, and always available. If you cant make office hours, he will schedule appointments and always answers emails. The topic is tough and Professor Ottman is very DEFINITION heavy. You have to understand many concepts to answer a singular question. If you ask for help, and study, youre good!
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Overall Eric is a good professor. He is a good lecturer that tries his best to keep the lectures from being too boring. It feels like he is more personal than other lecturers in his lecture. His quizzes are a good representation of what will be on his exams. He is a fair grader that will try to give you as much credit for your answers as possible.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Lectures are good, though they can feel a little "ripped from the book." He's sure to make connections to past material you've already learned, and to things you'll be learning next. As a person, he's a cool guy, and it's really nice to have a younger teacher. He can make you feel dumb when answering a question, but it's totally unintentional.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']

comment: For about a month, Dr. Zacharakis filled in for my Phys-111 class. This was BY FAR the best month of that entire semester. I talked with a few other students, and they all shared the same sentiment; that with her, they learned far more in far less time than with their original professor. Zacharakis also hosts a handful of reviews prior to tests.
Course requires effort but she gives you what you need to succeed. Overall great professor.

She's incredibly compassionate and manages to keep an academic focus in the class, while still behaving and treating us as human. Understanding of student's struggles and willing to meet them where they are. She has very clear and very reasonable expectations for the course, which she articulates well and in appropriate frequency.

Prof. Z is a great professor. Her lectures are clear and time is managed well. She conducts the labs in a way that is both fun and educational. She gives very clear feedback on exams and quizzes and offers ample time outside of class to get help 1 on 1. 9/10 would recommend!

This professor is simply amazing. She gives wonderful lectures and is committed to her students success. She works incredibly hard to ensure everyone does well. There is a fair bit of homework but it is there to ensure you have a good grasp of the course material. If you do the work and put in effort during labs you will do great in this class.

Simply amazing professor. She is committed to the success of all of her students and will work incredibly hard to ensure that everyone does well. She has a fair bit of homework but it makes sure you have a good grasp of the material. If you do the homework and put in effort in the labs, you will do quite well.

Very condescending and immature.  If you don't understand a subject she says she wants to help, but then is demeaning when you ask questions.  I end up teaching myself most things outside of class or asking the TAs who are also not the most knowledgeable but at least try to help.

This is the only course I have had to drop, and I graduated Summa Cum Laude. Within the first week, she was rude, condescending and provided zero helpful feedback or assistance with understanding the material. I would have to guess people that found her "nice/caring" were males. I noticed special treatment to certain individuals...

The immediate diving into the subject of physics was unhelpful as concepts are gone over rather than explained, so you just have to understand what you can to a certain extent, so instead I had to learn physics from watching YouTube videos so I could actually do the work.
Lectures were completely off-topic and unhelpful

To be straight up, Prof Z is probably gonna be my top 3 professors of all time. It is extremely rare to have a professor come in on weekends to help you prepare you for an upcoming exam. Yes, the other comments are right on how harsh the exams are weighted, but that does not reflect on Prof Z, that's the horribly job of the department. Just show up

She actually wants you to learn and improve and will always spend extra time outside of class, even on the weekends, to help. As long as you are willing to put a little time and effort into class you'll be fine.

She was very nice and open to providing extra help, but the tests were weighted so insanely high that a 70 on the first test basically ruined my grade. She also assigns these absurdly long packets in class. Attendance is required except for the lectures. You also can't pass with a test avg less than 70, even if you get 100s on everything else.

This professor was racist (frequently mixed up the few Asian students in the class and was rude to them as well as touching black students' hair), incredibly condescending and disrespectful, didn't provide good feedback on assignments, had boring and unhelpful lectures, and refused to help when we were struggling. Very uncomfortable experience.

Andronique was such a GOAT this semester. I was a little worried about her and physics before this semester started but OMG is she awesome. She is really caring about her students and all she wants is for you to do well in the class. Saturday sessions before exams were an incredible asset in getting a good grade and her doing that shows she cares.

I have never before had a professor that would come in for a Saturday review session and she will absolutely do it every time we have an exam. She takes a minute to grade but she is one of the best professors I've had at RIT in the last 4 years.

I took this as an online summer course. Our weekly assignments and labs were group work, which sucks if your teammates aren't good and can bring down grades. Exams basically followed the homework problems and were at the same level of difficulty. She would post slides and make us watch videos with *few* in-class examples unless prompted for them.
She is very dedicated to helping her students do well. As long as you apply yourself and work it is a good class.

Dr. Z is awesome! Forgot major concepts and equations for the course but she made me understand everything, albeit slowly. The lectures are fast-paced but it's not her fault (that's how dept structured it). She tries to teach to the best of her ability and would redo equations. Lots of homework but it is for your practice and understanding!
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes']

comment: Horrid. Her lectures are worthless and she talks down to you, then in the same breath gives you difficult problems that are so much more difficult than anything remotely on the lectures and that you are completely unprepared for

She frustrated me so much! She told you about homework on Tuesday or Thursday but wouldn't assign it until Friday night and it was due Sunday night, which meant you had to do homework over the weekend. Her lectures were very monotonous. During labs, she did not go around as much to help groups with problems, the TA was more available than she was.

So, for starters I am not the best at physics or math in general. I took this class and found it to be the most difficult one I have ever taken. Dr. Zacharakis, however, was a very approachable professor and was willing to assist, but there was a great deal of self learning that needed to occur for the course that I couldn't keep up with.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: She is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is very clear and concise and I feel like she really does care about you learning the material.  She was also very approachable and always available to help.

Lectures are clear and concise, and she explains the concepts really well. At first, I thought all we were doing was learning remedial math, but a look at the textbook I realized that we actually just went over two chapters worth of materials. She's that good. She's also very approachable and helpful. Exams are easy if you know what you're doing.

She is one of the nicest professors I've had. Unfortunately with teaching a class of nearly 100 it is hard for her to help you out. If you do ask her 1-on-1 questions she can be very helpful. Class wasn't structured the best, but I feel that the department is more to blame then her.
She is a terrible professor. Won't give any examples and thinks you should be able to teach physics to yourself. The only thing she thinks we need to learn from her is remedial math.

I hated physics in high school. This professor made me think that I should have chosen physics as my major! She uses great examples and animations, is always cheerful and encouraging. You get help whenever you ask right away and her grading scheme has substitutions to help you get the best grade you can. Choose her sections for this course!

I did very poorly on the first test and quiz, but she let the class retake the first test and quiz as homework assignments if you did good on the second quiz. I thought I was going to fail halfway through the quarter, but ended up with an A because she dropped the lowest test and quiz also

Had her for quantum chemistry and she is by far the best! Will work with students after class and is always cheerful and happy which makes learning better. She gives extra credit and there is alot of homework but the homework will only benefit you. Definitely recommend her to anyone!

She gives ample opportunity for extra credit and even threw one of the exams out. She was very receptive when the class was doing poorly and was a great help when I didn't understand topics. I highly recommend this professor.

Seems extremely knowledgeable about polymer technology and chemistry in general, but lectures can be confusing if you're not good at chemistry. Most quiz questions are straight off the homework, so if you do the homework you will do fine. She also gave multiple very easy extra credit questions that add points to your OVERALL average. Easy A.
will never take her for physics again

MacDonald was a great teacher- sometimes she drove me crazy and it wasn't easy, but I worked really hard, and when I didn't understand some concepts she worked 1 or 1 with me to make sure I understood it. If you need to take NTID math class, get this teacher! (better than Miriam)

Judy is a nice teacher to be with. Very patient and motivating. She is not strict or hard but will be very flexible with every student who pass through her hands. I have no regret recommending her to any student.

This class is unbelievably easy, as for my case though.  A very straight-forward class -- simply complete homework, study little by little daily, and should easily be able to pass quizzes and exams.  She's willing to help students for those who are in need of help.  However, the classes can periodically become boring.

One of the best professors I've had. He's really good at explaining math conceptually, not just going through the process. He answers questions very well and always double checks to make sure the student understands before moving on. He's also very generous with exam grading, and very easy to talk to in his office hours or after class.

If you get this teacher, prepare to learn everything on your own, his lectures are very hard to follow and the tests are terrible, the only advice I can give is expect the unexpected because no matter how hard you study there is going to be everything you didn't study on the test.

Dr. Hoffman is very enthusiastic about math, which I love. He never shies away from students' questions and cares deeply about them. His lectures were initially incredible, but got worse throughout the semester. Exams are significantly more difficult than the homework (WebAssign required) and he expects you to apply the material in every which way.

The professor himself is a very charming and approachable guy, however during lectures he would go off on tangents and get sidetracked very easily. I stopped attending lectures after the first exam and used my time to get help from outside sources. His exams are very easy once you get a proper understanding of the material - not from him though.

Pros: Exams aren't too difficult.

Cons: We would have homework (graded on accuracy) on a topic, then get a recitation quiz on it, and only THEN, after the homework and quiz would we learn it in class. He gets sidetracked in class a lot and could do more examples.

First math professor I've ever had who's lectures are not completely useless. There are weekly in-person recitation quizzes with zero make-ups which can be a little annoying, but they aren't too hard. Tests are about as hard as the homework, meaning if you understand the homework you'll do fine. Also kinda cute.

Professor Hoffman is the calc professor you want. He breaks down complex topics into easy to understand pieces. He always posts lecture notes so you can get caught up if you miss class. Quizzes and exams are graded fairly and lots of partial credit is given for understanding the topic. Absolutely would take another class with him.

Hoffman does a great job at making sure you don't just know how to do something, but also why we do it a certain way, ensuring that you have a conceptual understanding of all the math you're doing. You'll have to spend time learning a lot of formal definitions, but will come out of it understanding everything fully.

Great professor-- extremely knowledgeable, very clear communicator and does a great job explaining anything you ask him. Very straightforward/thorough, when appropriate, will stop to make sure everything makes sense and is clear mathematically before moving on. Positive environment to ask questions, good class pacing, & group work is super helpful.
Tolerant of jokes as long as they don't disrupt class. Very comfortable atmosphere. Nice looking face.

Dr. Hoffman is a great guy and great professor. He tends to over complicate things and will throw a lot at you at once, but he is very fair and gives help to those who need it. He prepares you for tests by providing a review guide on my courses and the homework's provide videos and extra problems. Read the textbook and do the work and you're fine.

Very formal lectures, sometimes he can make things in calculus seem overcomplicated, but that's partly because he teaches the formal definitions for concepts in math. It might take a little bit more effort to understand if you're new to calculus.
Like a second father figure, always has great conversations with students that does and doesn't relate to the material
Knows what he is talking about. This course is really hard, exams are open note but still difficult. Took this course during covid so it might not be online anymore.

Hoffman's a certifiable genius, he knows everything about the class and can answer any question you have. His lectures are great, and as long as you write down what's going on you'll be fine. The class itself is really confusing, especially at the beginning, but it's mostly examples you use to solve similar problems.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Hoffman is amazing. He has recently been made head of the Master's Program at RIT. He is very easy to talk to, and very friendly. He will do his best to answer every question, and he provides the right amount of challenge in his classroom. I have to work for my grades, but he does grade fairly.
His teaching isn't very intuitive but if you pay close attention you'll do well. He is helpful in answering questions.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Take him! Don't think about it twice. If you want a professor that cares about your grade and is really approachable this is him!

He takes the time to make sure you understand the material. His lectures can be a bit hard to understand theoretically, but he gives good examples so it's not a huge deal. Pay abstention, take notes, do the homework, and you'll do fine on the quizzes and tests. If you do need extra help he's there for you.

He is way too theoretical.  In the one or two examples of problems shown per class, he would often not explain his steps or say to 'guess' that a certain equation applied to the problem.  I felt that I was often teaching myself all of the material while doing the homework.  Exams are straight forward, but expect doing a lot of work outside class
He did a great job of making the course easy to follow. He had many methods for relating the hard-to-grasp subjects to well known applications. He kept the class engaged and was a blast to talk to.

Great guy that makes lectures interesting. There's a lot of material to get through and he will make you laugh and make the material easy to understand. Very helpful and understanding, he cares that you master the material, not if your homework is a few days late. Take him if you can!

Makes you generally interested in the subject. Always taught concepts remarkably well, such that I could usually understand the first time around, or would clarify well if asked a question. Definitely take him.
Fantastic professor. Truly, the best.

He's very helpful if you go talk to him one-on-one. A lot of his lectures get really boring and are hard to pay attention to. The homework isn't bad and quizzes aren't hard if you review for them. Tests can be a little challenging. A lot of other Calc teachers at RIT will curve grades but so far Hoffman hasn't so its far from an easy A

Dr. Hoffman is an extremely good calc teacher. He makes concepts clear and uses excellent examples in class. Weekly quizzes are easy. HW is moderate. Tests are challenging but fair since problems are about the same level of difficultly as class examples. Would def recommend.

Matt Hoffman is the best.  If you have the option to take his class, take it.  He is a brilliant man who is down to earth, nice, funny, and very helpful.  He's very understanding and will help you out in almost any situation.  Make sure you show up to class though, he isn't the easiest teacher, but you'll definitely enjoy his class.

Dr. Hoffman is one of the few professors I've had that is willing to change how he teaches based on student feedback. He's eager to help students and actually helpful when you ask him questions. He has a few pedagogical tendencies that can make class frustrating or unclear, but overall is a good teacher.

Good professor, teaches a difficult subject reasonably well, and makes sure that you do understand the subject in office hours. Sometimes he does ramble on for a proof or long derivation for a while, bu he does tie it all back together.
Moderately helpful.  More helpful one-on-one, but if you take the class at 8 am, he is not awake. Ask questions as he is helpful in answering them.

Although Dr. Hoffman just began this quarter, he is an amazing professor. He is very energetic about his work and encourages thinking beyond the application of numbers. He is willing to work with you and is very approachable. Two exams and a final, one quiz (besides exam weeks) and a homework assignment every week. Pay attention and do the
Blunt but kind. Engages in good dialogue with students and is willing to pull you aside and give extra instruction. Does expect a lot from you and grading criteria was very nebulous.

a professor that i respect a lot. a tough grader, though gives a lot of useful feedback and is very accessible out of class. he has a chill vibe overall and is great to conversate with. definitely got a lot out of this class

Grades are only posted at the end of the semester, and unless your projects were outstanding, expect a B. Most of the work can be completed during class. Prof. Aslam is professional and no-nonsense. It;s clear that he's been teaching figural sculpture for a long time. He has a wealth of expertise on the subject. Participate in crits! Give feedback!
Very chill and lowkey professor, but tough grader. How are you going to put 2/3rds of my sculptures on display for half a year then give me a B?

he was a nice guy. always said out of pocket things, caught me off guard a lot. very helpful with his advice. hes a quiet dude, i dont think ive ever seen him sit in a chair. he only gave As to outstanding projects; it might've had to do with the student's dedication too. i was lazy during class sometimes. 

overall a nice dude, gives good feedback

Pascal's classes are engaging, casual, and fun. There is a required online textbook and quiz software and lots of small homework assignments that count for a significant portion of your grade, but they are easy, and Pascal grades them on whether or not they are done vs whether they are correct.

I love Pascal. He is such a funny guy, and I always enjoyed his class. He does call on people randomly, but even if you don't know it you can just say you don't know and he will help you out! A decent amount of homework but nothing hard.

Pascal is an amazing professor. I am a Nazareth College student. I took the French class for the beginners. He will make you participate but in a fun way, won't embarrass you. He is very fun and passionate about teaching his students French. Always comes with excitement in class. One of the best professor I would say. My course name is FRN10101.

I like Pascal. He's a great guy, and wants you to learn. I don't like MLFR201. The class was incoherent. I often had no idea what topic we were talking about, and Cengage's HW served only to frustrate and never reinforce. If you need a tight structure to learn, this ain't it chief. I honestly feel like I would have been just as fine self-studying.

He's very easygoing and hilarious. Let's you do test corrections for half points so even if you get a 50 on your test you can make it up to a 75. Lot's of online homework but nothing crazy hard just daily assignments. He cares a lot about his students and tries hard to make the class fun all while still teaching valuable materials. One of the best.
Really cool guy who kept class positive and made me feel like he cared.
He's a funny guy, but as a teacher has no idea what he is doing.
Skip is absolutely hilarious - a delightful professor and a really interestingrad person! He will definitely be missed when he retires.
I like Skip, he's a great teacher.  He's very deaf friendly and I liked the fact that he would put closed captioning on for them, that what makes him a great teacher.  Take him, it's really worth it.

Lecture was useless other than to hand in the essay which was due. I always paid attention and sat in the front row every class but I always walked out each day questioning if I actually learned anything. Essays can be hard, strict grader, final is ridiculously easy. I can't say I'd recommend him but he certainly is a cool dude, very Jeff Bridges.
Skip is the man, take him!  His essays are tough but very exciting to write!  Take him!!
Great man, horrible teacher.
English teacher as a Film Teacher?  What?? Take Carageorge istead.

He can be cool, but does not like those live action films, he only likes odd animation films which means that he will fail you on your live action.  Take other teachers for this particular class.  Don't bother.
skip is a nice guy, but he only talks about himself 24/7 and we get to write about our thoughts, but he judges too harshly. avoid him.
He is a horrible professor.  Doesn't agree with students' opinions.  Avoid taking him for Film Language, and take other classes with him.

He's a good professor! Very easygoing, fun, and extremely helpful. Likes to make students feel good about themselves and make more inspiring work. Would definitely recommend you to take him if you got the chance!

Skip is perhaps one of my favorite teachers ever. His class is easy because he gives you the freedom to experiment and do what you want. He always has positive comments about everything and helpful criticism. Plus, his STORIES ARE AMAZING. I mean, how often to you get hear about filming in the arctic with temperatures way below zero? Totally cool.
Skip is a god. He knows all there is to know about film.
Good class...you'll enjoy it and learn alot!
Bit of a nut but wants to see everyone do well. Likely to take you out for a beer after class
Skip is a fun Professor. A little wacky and usually a little tipsy...? Generally accepting of alot of different film/animation styles. A good professor and alot of fun in class!
Excellent teacher - very challenging. He has a lot of knowledge and glad I took the courses he offered. I enjoy the emails and am sorry that they have stopped.

Freshman need to quit rating Kleper. This man has shaped and reported more industry knowledge than most will ever understand. Ask him about his research sometime. Kleper isn't an easy-A, but he's among the most interesting people you'll meet in your lifetime.
Without a doubt in the top 3 worst classes and professors Ive had at RIT.

Terrible.  Words can't describe how wretched both the class and teacher were.  He cracked his stupid inside printing jokes.  Never helped to anyone who struggled.  On top of all this he spams people with useless printing news.

tests are INSANE, long, winded lectures, TONS of junkmail, but very approachable. if you have a hard time with him in class, approach him outside and talk to him--he wants students to do well, he's just out of touch with reality.
awful, awful man. boring lectures, trivial tests - sends massive amounts of junk email (im still receiving stuff from him)
No Comments

Professor Yang has great lectures, very engaging. Although much of the course material covered is a review from prior knowledge he makes the class fun. Attendance is a must for lectures and labs. Homework is 1 quick assignment weekly. Would absolutely recommend Professor Yang.

Yang is super helpful and actually cares about his reputation with students.  He was helpful when I needed it, extremely nice and charismatic, and was able to make such a cookie-cutter class enjoyable. He is the only professor I've ever had that sent out an email reflecting on his evals. It's been said before, but I'll say it again: He's the man.
Great and easy class. Show up and you pass.

Dr. Yang is really a good guy. He cares about all his students success and is willing to work with you no matter if you are a head or behind on the subject matter he makes sure you understand it. There were only 6 really easy hw assignments. Definitely reccomend

His class was incredibly easy, only 5 homework assignments. He cares greatly about his CE students and is a hard worker. I'm glad to have taken his class and getting to know our head of the department better.
He's very clear in presenting material and tries to make sure everyone is on track with the curriculum through both office hours and peer mentors. Overall, the class is fun and easy.

This class was both easy and fun. Dr. Yang presents information very clearly and, for what little time the department head has, he tries hard to make sure everyone is on track, even setting up peer mentors for students.
Helpful, gives you clear cut examples, easy to understand.

The class was very straightforward and Professor Yang did a decent job teaching things. He mainly puts things up on a projector and we took a few notes but other than that it was a simple class. I have to admit that I find his powerpoint presentations that he posts online more informative than his actual lectures.

He's extremely nice, and very helpful outside of class if you can find him. He was harder than the rest of the IDS professors, and sometimes didn't explain things very clearly, but just ask him to clarify and he will. Overall, you can't go wrong in IDS with Yang or Melton.

Caring professor. Usually avaliable and helpful. Tried his best to explain materials. Understood that students have other courseworks other than his class, deadlines were extended if reasonable request was made.

He's a good professor; tries to help his students any way he can.  The class can be hard but if you work hard and see him when you need help, he'll help you and make sure your grade reflects your effort and improvement.
Unbelievably good, I hate circuits, or at least I did until this class, Yang is the man.
Nice, good professor. Try his best to make students understand the materials. Always avaliable and helpful.
He's the man. Enough said.

Dr. Bondy made his class extremely easy and accessible. All tests and quizzes were open everything, so our class average was high since we could use our notes and look stuff up during tests. Even with that, I still learned Python very well from him. Nice guy as well.

This man is a terrible professor. The coding is not hard at all but oh my gosh he is so annoying. His grading schedule is perplexing at best having readings, labs, and projects start and end all on different days throughout the week. He'll posts labs on stuff he hasn't taught yet “because you guys are real clever” like what is the point of that???

Professor Bondy is very kind and understanding of new programmers. His course has a very rigid structure and takes adjusting to but as long as you talk to him he is always happy to help. He is great at responding to his Slack messages, even on weekends the day before a project is due. Anything you need is in the syllabus and lecture was 1.5hrs max.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lots of homework']

comment: If you email him he will direct you to the slack or his old prerecorded videos. This course is available to NTID students but he posts the captions external from the videos. He will not respond to your slack messages and if he does it will be to watch his not very helpful videos and blame you for not paying more attention to them.

Lectures were fairly boring at times, and usually are unnecessarily long, but he always posts the slides on slack.  He is very clear about course expectations, and gives very helpful feedback on project deliverables. There are also ample opportunities for bonus credit. Very nice guy as well.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Gives good feedback']

comment: I don't think anybody liked Bondy. 3 hour classes consisted of incoherent rambling and tangents for an hour, and then the remaining time to complete the "labs", really basic programming projects done through google collab. If you know anything about coding you'll pass no problem, but you will learn absolutely nothing because Bondy cannot teach.

The first 90 minutes or so of each 3 hour period consisted of him lecturing, and the rest was used for lab work. However, the contents of the lectures had nothing to do with the labs. Leaves the class of over 30 alone in the hands of the one TA to do labs. In short, dont expect to learn anything about coding or computing from this professor.

The lectures, homeworks, and exams were all unrelated. The only part of the course I felt like I learned something from was the create project. Google was allowed but essentially necessary for all assignments. Bondy always left halfway through class, but was easy to contact through Slack. Difficult to understand assignment expectations.

Ray is an excellent coach who helps everyone at their individual skill levels to improve at table tennis. It is definitely not a slack off wellness course though, he really want you to improve and works everyone. So yes, there are drills and you might get sweaty.

Ray Mack fits the typical stereotype of a PE teacher, lacking the intelligence to pursue an actual career. I hoped to take a class that would be fun and laid back. Instead you'll run laps, do drills, and be constantly bombarded with personal questions. He is also treats the few women in the class as inferior to men. Avoid at all cost.

Coach Ray is one of the top 10 table tennis players in the country for his age group, and it shows.  He really knows what he's talking about, and makes it his job to see everyone improve throughout the course.  While fun, table tennis with Coach Ray greatly improved my skills.  I'd recommend this class to anyone looking for a fun wellness.
Professor. Antonoff is very enthusiastic! But don't make her angry...

For Biocompatibility and the Immune system, he was awesome. Very knowledgeable and easy to pay attention to, will gladly elaborate on confusing parts, has a study session where he tells you exactly what you need to know for the test, and will remove a question from the test if most of the class got it wrong-explaining it and giving everyone points.
Very understanding
the best teacher ever in RIT!

He is AWESOME. Sometimes I am listening to him during the lecture and I just want to come up to him and tell him that. He knows how to motivate his students by rewarding them and giving them an opportunity to improve. Clear,organized, passionate, great communication skills, experienced. Simply the best of the best.
Best teacher ever for an upper level bio class! He's so passionate about immunology that he makes you want to learn. Lets you use double sided PRINTED cheat sheet on exams. Def take his class!
Seriously the Best teacher at RIT, extremely helpful and wants all his students to succeed if you ever have a chance take a class with him, you will not regret it

I LOVED THIS CLASS! I love immunology but he made everything SO CLEAR and he was EXTREMELY organized! Unbelievable! He gave tons of bonus points. Buy the CLICKER! I have more than 20 raw bonus points because of it.

BEST teacher I've had in the Bio department yet! Portrays information in a very clear and easy to understand way. Go to lecture and take good notes. Grading is very fair and he loves to give away extra pts/pts for ambiguous questions on tests so question everything!

Very interested in what his students want. Many oppurtunities to do well in the class. If a test is even the slightest bit ambiguous, he'll give the whole class the points for it. If you argue a question, he'll most likely give you credit for you. Very interesting, kept me awake at 8 am.
The man loves to hear himself talk TOO much. Mostly redundant drivel - and also one of the most unhelpful and pompous college instructor I ever had the misfortune of coming across.

Simply the best professor in this field. Take him and you'll see why. He's usually eccentric, but that makes it all much more interesting. Exams are perfectly reasonable and he's willing to reason when it comes to grades. TAKE HIM!
I really did not enjoy his classes at all

comment: I feel that sometimes Abdul can get a bad rap, so I will share my overall experience with him. Overall, he really is a caring professor who knows the material, and wants his students to succeed. If you put in just a little bit of effort, he will try to make sure you succeed. His main weakness is sometimes the lack of organization within the class.

Crazy amount of work on the group project. Feedback generally unclear or not far enough before the next deadline to incorporate. Make sure to get any requirement clarifications or grading criteria in writing because he changes his mind. Meetings outside of class to discuss project are pretty much mandatory.
Had to take his class bc it was required. Hard to show up and attend regularly. Dosent grade assignments in a timely manner… very vocal about his dislike for police officers

enforces a strict no-electronics policy, even during emergencies, and publicly calls out students who break it, which can feel humiliating. He also discusses students with others and often treats the class in a condescending, childlike manner rather than with respect.

He has made comments that come across as biased or dismissive toward certain groups, creating an uncomfortable learning environment. Additionally, they often share strong personal political views that feel one-sided and unrelated to the course material, which makes it difficult to feel respected.

Easy class. Professor is satisfactory for what the class is. Gets excited about the subject matter which is always nice to see.

Professor Leipold is a decent professor.. She's very boring.She tries to make it interesting but I cant help but fall asleep. She's not very clear and doesn't seem to know the material well. She speeds through all the slides.
The most demanding professor ive ever met ... nice in person, but his policies are terrible. Made me stop taking french courses.

She was a great teacher, really made it easy to pass the course if you payed attention. Would def take another class with her.

She is a really nice teacher. You can tell she knows the material, but she is not always cocky or confident like many professors. As long as you show you care, and make an effort in class and discussions, it's easy to pull off an A.

Tessier does assign a lot of coursework, but about half of it is online discussion. As long as you are able to keep track of homework and submit it on time, show up for lectures, and study the book for exams, it's easy to get an A/B. Offers extra credit. Worst teacher ever way too demanding, thinks she is nice, but in reality there is nothing you can do in any of her classes to honestly earn a good grade (and we are talking even a B). They give vague/unhelpful feedback (only saying "No") that is often negative even when graded well. It's hard to stay passionate about the course/material with them.

I've taken four of Dr. Olmstead's classes and I loved every one of them. They assign a lot of reading if you're not taking this class for your degree, but they communicate their expectations very clearly and are eager to work with students. Multiple readings each week. Nearly all are by white authors. You can't have a class that claims to explore the lives of a marginalized group while only analyzing one facet of said group. Dr. Olmstead is very nice and a great professor. There's 25 readings to do before class around 30 pages each, but you can skip 10. Actual class time is lecture/class discussion on whatever was read. comment: I was inspired by the dean at that time of the multidisciplinary studies. He truly transformed my life. He led me to ask myself important questions: What would wake up every morning looking for clues to solve rather than an 8 to 5 job? I completely changed my career. It's clear that he's knowledgeable about the subject and frequently talks about things outside of the textbook that I found interesting. Homework was done on Mindtap, but he was generous enough to give us ~10 attempts on each assignment and 2 on the tests.

He was the worst professor I’ve ever had. He didn’t give us class materials fo the first 6 weeks of class then tried to give us all of the materials from the semester in week 7 to give us an exam the same week. If you can get a different professor, do it.

He deserves a 0. His class was the worst experience I have ever had. It was concerning when he started the semester discussing a disability, but seriously, if you have a class with him, strongly recommend dropping. Learned off cengage b/c he went on tangents in class for over an hour. Lectures were useless, and he was very disorganized.
This class was asychnronous. He never answered emails, not once. He assigns over 3 hours worth of reading and work to complete EACH WEEK. There was no way to reach him at all. Terrible.
all I learned in this class was the definition of technology and 9/11 conspiracies.

This is my second class with Prof McQuade and the experience was even worse than the first time. We had two assignments, no exams, and no final. This class was online asynchronous. It was the worst managed class I have ever taken. By far the worst Prof I've had. We've gotten 5 versions of a 16 page syllabus and yet have done nothing and have no idea what is expected of us. Unorganized, unprepared, somewhat rude, just overall terrible professor.

I took this class online in fall '20 in the middle of COVID. The professor had an accident over the summer and the class has come to a standstill. Almost no relevant or useful communication. No work to be turned in I'm not sure how we're gonna be graded. All these things just made a perfect storm to fail. Don't do it to yourself. Take anyone else!

You know that person in your life, whether it be a grandfather or neighbor, who seems to talk about nothing for hours upon hours, rambling about anything that can enter the labyrinth of their mind, and every time you leave them you think to yourself, "God, I worry about him". That's Samuel McQuade.

Not the most PC professor, pretty inappropriate at times, considered reporting several things he's brought up in class. He's a good guy at heart, but not very good at lecturing. A lot of tangents and hard to take notes on important things for the class. He showed up 45 min+ late the first weeks. BUT, if you are patient enough, this is an easy A.

This is the first time Professor McQuade has taught undergrad in 10 years, so it was a bit of a rough time during this semester. All work is online so it's very easy to complete and pass the class with an A. Lecturing for 3 hours is way too much, considering he goes off topic 99% of the time.

I took CRIM 110 as a perspective curse, and I honestly feel like it's the best course I ever took. The lectures, though they did go off topic quite a bit, were extremely educational and I feel like I learned more in class than the textbook could ever have taught me. Prof McQuade definitely knows what he's talking about and is really knowledgeable.

This class was a hour lecture once a week and at first I was not looking forward to it at all. But Sam made the class interesting and easy with his crazy stories he shares. Overall class work was very easy and he was very flexible because everything was online and you were able to take everything until you aced it!
This professor demanded your attention and you were rewarded with a wealth of knowledge and experience. I had him for one course and it was probably the best I have ever had.

Very good teacher, knows what he is talking about.  Has some interesting and funny stories.  His class is actually one I enjoy going to.  A good amount of reading needs to be done, but its all fairly interesting. He gives open note tests.  Get a different teacher if u are easily offended, but if u can take a joke youll really enjoy him as a teacher

Excellent professor. He knows what he is talking about. I must say that you should't take the course if you don't want to work hard but after all the work you have learned a lot. Great teacher! I wish I could have him in other classes. Unique teaching style.
exams are hard (NEED TO READ EACH QUESTIONS FIVE TIMES). Very tricky. A lot of reading. I did get an A but it took way lot of effort. He knows what he is talking about though.

To start, I did get an 'A' in the class. I would recommend avoiding this prof at least for this class. No real knowledge of comp crime. His tests are unfair and have nothing to do with how much of the material you know. You'll either like him or not.

I learned quite a bit. Tons of extra reading not covered on tests which were pretty difficult. He is very full of himself but it is understandable considering his background in policing. My biggest complaint is that i was late to my next class every time
He was teaching for the first time at RIT so he sure made everything VERY complicated. Should teach the graduate courses!

If anyone trash talks Dr. McQuade it's probably because they are a horrible student. He demands only the best work, you will fail miserably if you are lazy. This man is THE source for computer crime studies in the USA.
The name's actually McQuade, moron.
And you spelled his name wrong!  it's McQuaid.
Oh wait, he's actually really good and knows what he's talking about.  Afraid of actual academic work?  Scared to read and do some research?

Teacher is an Egomaniac who babbles endlessly about pointless things, doesnt cover proper material, gives extremely complicated tests and refuses feedback from students. On a last note, you will never get out of this class on time since he loves to talk.
So boring and pointless

Lectures are incredibly boring, he loves to yap. He grades incredibly hard with no set rubric for responses. Every word you use needs to be precise on the exams, exams are all written no MCQ. Attendance is graded and you will lose points for stepping out to use the bathroom (insane if you ask me). He kinda acts like a high school teacher in a way

Handwritten notes due before every class and flipped classroom format. Very nice guy, but he ends up just talking about his childhood for 20 minutes which isn't acceptable for the amount of money you spend on classes here. His grading is also very harsh & subjective especially from what I've heard from other students in his other classes.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']

comment: My biggest complaint with Professor Mathers is his exams. I wouldn't recommend taking him based on how he grades . He grades very harshly while never telling us in lectures or in notes what he expects from our answers. Those who understand his thinking and are able to guess what hes looking for will do well (mindreaders)

Collins lectures are very interactive and never boring. I like his teaching style and the way he formats assignments. Only things is he's a harsh grader because he's looking for very specific things. You can't have an ounce of generality when doing assignments or exams.

He cannot give a clear rubric for assignments for the life of him, and feels the need to force students into a set direction without giving any clear guidance or help to get there; he teaches like this is a high school English class, but grades like it's an MIT 4th year course. Class time is always spent sitting doing nothing.

Classes are discussion-led instead of lectures. Videos and texts are assigned for homework – notes are graded. All exams (including final) are weighted the same and  have SAQs. Ff you understand what he's looking for, they're very easy. No laptops or phones in class, many ways to get extra credit, approachable. Overall, interesting and easy class.

I had a really good time with Prof. Mathers this semester. He runs a flipped classroom, making most classes discussions while having 2-3 pages of notes due every Sunday. While all classes are recorded via Zoom and uploaded, attendance does help a lot. Exams were pretty easy as long as you pay attention in class. Extra credit opportunity everywhere.

Nice guy with good intention, but very tough grader and some of the test are almost subjective, which makes getting consistent good grades tough. I had an A in the class and then took the final and do not do good, and when I went to talk about it, he said he "disagreed" with my answers, although my answers were correct according to our resources.

No phones allowed, no computers allowed, no tablets allowed, and participation is graded. Honestly the worst professor I have ever taken nitpicks your exams for specific wording and grades YOUR notes that he makes you HAND WRITE. Every class ruined my morning will, never take one of his classes again.

Prof. Colin is an amazing professor! He is able to get his point across for every lecture exceptionally well. He made it clear what he expected of us and what he wanted us to learn from his class. He was very nice and easy to talk to. There was a decent amount of homework, though doing the homework pays off and is normal for a philosophy class!

He's a great professor who makes the material as interesting as possible. The videos are the most important part out of class, if you don't do them, you will fail. But, as long as you do the videos and attend lectures for discussion, you will do well in the class.

Prof. Mathers definitely knows his stuff! If you are interested in PHIL I highly recommend taking a course with him - however if you aren't PHIL focused, there is a steep learning curve. Nice guy, puts heavy precident on attendance and participation. Class is almost always discussion based, rarely lecture. If you prefer lectures, skip this one.

Very good and approachable professor. Homework is ~2 sets of notes per week (must be hand-written). Lectures are engaging so long as your class neighbors are willing to have meaningful discussions about the content. Does a good job getting everyone involved in the class discussion, so don't expect to glide through lectures without contributing.

Honestly, he's a great guy and I love his style of teaching. My only big complaint is how tough of a grader he is. To be fair my writing skills are not great and I do not enjoy philosophy. If you have some decent writing skills and an actual interest in the topic, it's an easy class.

Lectures are very interesting and Prof Colin very knowledgeable in the course material. Heavy emphasis on group work and participation. Only downside is really just the workload, but it is manageable once you have a routine set.

Gives interesting lectures. Is very clear about what material is going to show up on the exams; simply watching his videos and paying attention in class is all that's really necessary to succeed in his class. Was a pleasure to talk to outside of class as well.

Wasn't expecting this much work for a Gen Ed but he was a great teacher. Definitely make sure you are revising the weekly assignments or the final will be hell. I learned so much from this class and have taken Phil 205 with him as well. Overall would highly recommend Professor Mathers for those who are interested in philosophy and want a challenge.

I believe Professor Colin strives to foster an excellent learning environment. However, the fear of point deductions due to perceived judgment hampers participation. It's crucial to recognize that not every student excels in moral issues, particularly in a gen ed class. Feeling inadequate shouldn't stem from a less firm grasp compared to some peers
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: This class is way too much work for something offered as a perspective. The class is fast paced and you need to take good notes in class to complete the homeworks. His solution to this is telling you to watch the class recordings when you need to. Colin is a nice fellow but I never thought philosophy was supposed to have right and wrong answers.
Pretty cool guy and makes the class interesting. Lots of work but wasn't very difficult.

Professor Mathers is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he does. My only small complaint is that he isn't super clear on his expectations for assignments, but once you get the hang of it it's not a big deal.

The amount of additional work you will need to do versus other phil 102 professors makes me not recommend him. If you are a philosophy major or have a heavy interest in the subject he may be a good choice as he is a very good lecturer and his class is pretty interesting. You must also put in consistent work into the class or you will be swamped.

Great professor! I wish I was able to take his class in person, because I genuinely looked forward to his lectures each week! Gave a lot of really awesome insight into the things he discussed, and was always willing to see every viewpoint from every perspective. Just make sure you follow his standards and you will definitely have a good time!

Philosophy classes can be hard to conduct with all the discourse in the world. Still, Colin taught an informative and unbiased class that covered various interesting topics for any student. His teaching style introduced thoughtful class discussions that were calm and collected; even when students disagreed on different topics.

Prof. Mathers is an interesting professor. The style of the class was really fun and the material is unlike anything I had seen. Colin made the material easy to understand and graded fairly. This class in particular had him telling stories every class as well as asking students for their stories too. If you're looking for a good class, this is it.

Overall, he's a solid choice. At first I was a bit intimidated by his strict manner of grading, but if you meet with him, he clearly explains why. He explains concepts very clearly in class, and if you pay attention, he will do his best to help you understand. The one thing is to TAKE NOTES in class for the final "lab" or you'll pay for it later.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Prof. Mathers was great at leading group discussions, in spite of our reluctant participation. He's one of those people who you can tell really cares about his students, and he was always willing to stay after and discuss things with students. There were weekly assignments, but as long as you kept on top of things it wasn't too bad.

At beginning of semester, create a word doc in the format of the final "lab report" you need to do for class. Take notes within that document and do all of your weekly assignments in it when they're assigned, copy them into another document and turn that in. If done, you should have zero trouble with the class. Otherwise have fun on finals week.

Tips for success in Phil 101/102: understand midterm/final paper structure on syllabus, then structure EVERY assignment. DURING LECTURES: TAKE NOTE of PEER EXAMPLES (only 1 good one needed) AND prof's answer to assignment questions. Write your revised responses after every lecture and you'll slowly contribute to a completed midterm and final. GL!
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: I found Mathers's lectures to be very clear and pretty interesting. There is probably 1-2 hours of homework due twice a week, but that's nothing unreasonable for a college class. Mathers seemed to really care about his students and gave us a day off to recharge. I thought he was very clear in grading.
The assignments aren't too hard, but the lab report grading is really unclear and doesn't match the rubrics he gives you beforehand.

He can be a tough grader. He certainly expects you to know your stuff. It would be best if you took notes other than what is on the slides. He has some fun trivia for extra credit and other opportunities for more credit. As long as you apply yourself, you'll be fine; otherwise, expect to be in for a long semester.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']

comment: He gives feedback, but isn't clear. I submitted a 13 pg lab report (Midterm) 3x on mycourses, and he sent it back to me, all 3x, saying it was wrong with vague descriptions why. He failed me for the midterm. Couldn't even give me a 65 being that I cared about the assignment. If you don't like to read, DO NOT take this class with him! 45pg final, 85
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Tough grader']

comment: His lectures were some of my favorites, he explains topics thoroughly and always made me interested in everything we discussed. It does require a good amount of homework, but not anything crazy. I even found his stories interesting, even if they were irrelevant. I thought his grading could be a little unclear, but overall fantastic professor
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Very discussion heavy, and he makes you participate. Not too much homework and tests are easy. He tells lots of stories, gives extra credit, will help you on homework and always makes himself available for students. If you are an introvert and don't speak up a lot in class, be ready to get called on. Very caring and kind, get help if you need it.

Although the workload was not incredibly high, it was still more work that you would expect from a typical 100 class. However, that being said if you do the homework the tests are easy. If you are confused about anything, even the upcoming homework he is very willing to talk and help you out. Definitely talk to him if you are struggling.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: The ONLY good thing about Mathers, his exams were straight forward and easy. His classes were exhausting, and the work needed in homeworks for a perspective was more than needed. You need to be present and indulge in discussions, or you ain't getting no grades. You do not want to take him if you do not like reading boring stuff for like random qns.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']

comment: Great professor! Had him for Introduction to Moral Issues. The HW was very doable and he gave a lot of chances for extra credit. Made class fun with interesting discussions and topics.

Though I didn't like the subject Colin Mathers made it interesting. He was a fair grader and his lectures were funny and interesting. Sometimes the homework expectations felt unclear but it was easy to clarify with Colin's readily available office hours.

Yes, it's more focused on his Philosophy, but who cares you still learn a lot and the class is super easy. There is a lot of homework, however, if you show up to class and go to office hours he will help you complete the work. All exams are based on the homework and the key phrases he gives you. There are no papers either.

Very big into group discussions and participation. A little bit obsessive about things. Does not talk to students as equals, gives simple one-sentence answers to legitimate philosophical inquiries and makes no room for disagreement. Decent choice of readings. Solid lecturing, though he doesn't lecture much. Somewhat hard tests.

He's a nice person and all, but has very specific views about topics he covers so you're either right or wrong, there's no in between. It kinda takes out the philosophy from the course. His homework is relatively easy, and its not that hard to score a good grade as long as you show up, but its not fun either.

Pretty alright, nothing too difficult. Often has students discuss amongst themselves what they feel the meaning behind an image is or a question etc. Randomly calls on people for questions, which really aren't a ton of work. Goes off on tangent a bit too easy, but other than that pretty solid.

Dr. Mathers is not a bad human being, although not a great teacher. He cherry picks which questions to grade, so you don't get credit for all of the work that you complete. Any work you complete conforms to his opinion and he views, leaves very little room for your philosophy. As a 4th year student, this was the most unclear class I have taken.

He is a very good teacher for learning the material, but not great at helping philosophical thinking, but that's difficult to teach in a course that has a lot to cover, so I will give it to him. He is a nice person, but a bit intense. He sort of turned me off to atheism advocacy, as he was kinda strawman-ing the few religious topics there were.

Memorize the key phrases and show up to class! Cannot emphasize enough and it's not hard. He assigns exercises, you do them and discuss answers in class, and then he assigns a phrase that you have to know and use on the test. He's a pretty nice guy and very available as long as you try, but I don't think this is real philosophy.

He is all in all a great guy. Very clear in what he wants you to know and how to get there. Readings can be tough but he is very willing to clear things up if things are unclear. As long as you take notes and study those notes, you're getting an A. However, if you want a genuine liberal arts or philosophy education, he does stifle creative thinking
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read']

comment: Strange class, I didn't like it at first but grew to enjoy it more as time went on. Study your notes and you're golden for the tests. Easy homeworks, easy tests, no projects or papers. Just make sure you memorize what you need to.

Very structured, NO PAPERS which I loved. He LOVES his key phrases, just take notes during class and study those  super easy A. If you aren't sure on HW ?s, you can ask at office hours, he'll usually tell you how to improve them so you'll get better HW grades too. Content usually interesting, if you want real philosophy maybe go elsewhere tho

This class is by far the worst class in my college life. It is not like a typical liberal arts class where you express your opinion and back it up with arguments. He gives key phrase. And if you are not MEMORIZING key phrase and using it on the test, you are completely destroyed in the test. Doesn't care effort of the student.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: I felt like the workload for a 102 class was too much for me to handle. The readings are difficult to comprehend and you never actually get the right answers for homework questions. You take notes and get the "key phrase" and must improve your answer on your own. Too intensive for me and much more work compared to other professors that teach this.

A lot of people don't like Mathers, but I think he's a great professor. He is very caring if he sees that you're putting in effort. Few opportunities for extra credit. Lectures are very clear and thorough. He also makes his own videos with captions to explain his topics.

Discouraging is the first word that comes to mind when thinking about this Philosophy class. I had joined the class late and reached out for help, only to be treated like I was wasting this mans time. This was my first and only experience genuinely negative experience with a professor. He discourages other students during class discussions.

He was pretty opinionated. Made it known that he is not a fan of any religion, so that was a little off putting to me. Anyway, read the textbook, write what he wants you to say and you'll be fine. All in all he is a good guy and is very easy to talk to. PARTICIPATE. It is very important to him. Gives extra credit opportunities.

Prof. Colin is very serious about participations and attendance, and remembers every student very well. He likes to call on any student during lecture for group or homework answers, and encourages open discussion in class. Always keep in mind to pay attention and take notes since his tests always base on the answers he gives in class.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: A lot of the complaints regard Prof. Mathers is he kills discussion, I think these are typically the people most challenging the traditional view which is fine, but as he said he follows a Socratic method of teaching . Unlike other PHIL courses, not every view is valid, arguments can have flaws. He will listen but expect him to challenge you.

Mathers really doesn't believe in discussion. He runs his Intro to Moral Issues course around a set of questions that he calls the "workbook". His goal is to get you to memorize his answers to these questions and grades you on that. The class has almost 0 real discussion because it's all about these questions and his answers to them.

I didn't really like how he conducted the class. Almost any answer given to him was wrong in some way or another, even if you just used some sort of wording that he didn't like. The discussions weren't very interesting. However, it was an easy class to pass, as long as you did the work, participated a little and paid attention to his key phrases

He's ver opinionated on all topics, especially involving the existence of God. Basically, it's his way or the highway. Most of his lectures were interesting, I especially enjoyed his side stories. Overall, I don't want to continue with Philosophy  mainly due to this class. I wish there were more options allowed.

The best teacher I had this semester, he is very smart and passionate for Philosophy. BE AWARE, you will have a lot of homework but you will learn a lot and he is very good getting students involved in his class. After having a class with him you might consider doing a Philosophy minor or double majoring, best professor ever!

Mathers is a pretty laid back teacher, he often tells stories and actually likes talking about Philosophy. What he wants from tests is very clear, so passing is easy if you pay attention. Make sure to participate if you want the A, and taking notes is a must when he goes over homework. i would definitely take him again.

This philosophy professor is pretty easy. You have to do the homework, but you don't really have to take notes in class, just pay attention to the discussions. He gives out a lot of extra credit. NOTE: you do NOT have to worry about getting the textbook for this class. EVERY reading assignment can be found online, and he gives you a list of them.

His teaching is clear, but he is offensive.  Be prepared to be offended, he makes his opinions clear and if you disagree with him you will not do well in the class.  Also was unfair, gives random bonus points if you know the answers to random trivia questions, overall unfair and a terrible teacher for making his students feel uncomfortable.

It was a very clear cut class. You always knew what was expected of you and these expectations were pretty reasonable. The tests weren't bad either. As long as you payed attention and made sure that you corrected your answers as necessary for the homework, you'll do well. He takes thesame questions from the homework and places them on the test.

Cool guy. Keeps it interesting. Not too much workload. As an introvert, I disagree with the below reviewer saying the class is uncomfortable for introverts. You can speak up one time per class and get full credit, which is perfectly reasonable.
Very predictable, not much room for opinions. Didn't run the course in a way that was comfortable for introverts. Four hours on a Saturday is unpleasant.
You knew what to expect every class. Examples were good and clear. Participation is necessary for a good grade.

Some people are misled to think that, since this is a liberal arts fluff class, any old answer to a question will do. This isn't the case in Mathers's Intro to Ethics. While you needn't agree with him on moral issues (he doesn't make his opinion known), he expects you to find certain flaws in certain arguments, etc. Overall, a good teacher, though.
Great teacher, awesome class. If you're interested in ethics, I would definitely reccommend it. Saturday mornings are a bit tough, but worth it IMO!

The class is easy if you have a tolerance for it. Four hours of ethics on saturday mornings is pretty rough. Descriptions are unnecessarily long and his word rules. You dont get room for an oppinion here. He makes his class rules very clear and they show no tolerance.

Cool and entertaining guy. Made a relatively boring class enjoyable. If you want an A, study the answers to the homework questions (which he gives you in class). That's pretty much all that's on the tests. Easy class.

Colin is a good teacher. Easy to get an A if you attend class and take notes. Homework is to read a chapter and ask questions in a packet he gives. You get extra points for answering questions in class and attending in general. 2 exams - questions come from packet given to you prior to exam. Take this class!
Not bad at teaching.  He always gave me hard times to make perfect opinions that should be matched with his opinions.  That's all you can do is completing questions and read the book.

Awesome, easy teacher. Show up, read the textbook, do the questions and you'll get an A. The tests are made of the questions you've already answered - just study those and you'll do fine. Also a really interesting teacher.
he is a horrible teacher. He has one test and if you do bad, your done for, also his class is boring.

Mathers is an excellent professor.  He is very clear and comprehesible.  He does not grade harshly and is very open to help out with assignments.  The textbook is used for about half of the work done.  The other half comes from discussions in the lecture.  I recommend this professor.

Good professor. Questions on exams are straight out of the workbook. As long as you attend class & pay attention you'll do well in the course. Class is fun & interesting-- the professor does a great job of explaining concepts.
He's such a troll in class. He takes advantage of the subjective nature of philosophy by preaching his own philosophical ideas. He's pretty slow on grading.

Good: Attendance NOT mandatory, easy+blended class, approachable. Bad: SLOW GRADER, limited and unclear feedback, does not check email, inflexible with argument topics, teaches nothing in class, completely useless! My grade would be better if he provided timely feedback. We were on our 7th assignment when he graded the 3rd! Grade Approx: B-
Good human being and whenever I went to ask doubts, he was very much there to help me with his ideas. Would recommend to everyone.
He is a great person and gives you whole lot of space to learn and explore new things.
vague in teaching, not helpful.

Prof Mooman's course knowledge seems very surfacial as he stumbles if you ask him a question and usually replies with a non definite or very generalized answer. Lectures are vague and have no depth and the guy doesn't even make his own notes or slides and lacks organization. Doesn't expect much from students either.

Professor Mooman is an intelligent guy (as could be presupposed) but he is not an effective lecturer for early CS courses. I can imagine his higher level courses are more his level based on talking to him. Being self-taught, I did learn.   He does want his class to do well and encourages exploration, but he will be a difficult lecturer.

Professor Mooman is a nice guy, but he is not very good as a teacher. He tend to just read off the power points, and it's hard to get help from him, as he usually sends you to other people. Hs lectures are long, and it seems that he is not always 100% sure of what he is teaching, You have to teach most of the material to yourself.
Good professor, great sense of humor, but sometimes its hard to understand him and goes way off-topic most of the times. Always there to help you.

He truly is a nice guy. Was very umprepared to teach our class as it was given to him 2 weeks before school. Very helpful on tests . Wants you to pass his class. Not sure if he'll be teaching this class again as he usually teaches the higher levels. Only gives Midterm and Final for tests.

He is a good human but has a long way to go as a professor. He is not clear with his course structure and highly lacks organization. He is too wavering, therefore, after a while into his course it gets difficult to trust him. You will often find him go off topic and discuss irrelevant things. You have to be a self-learner to get thru his course.
Industry oriented guy, Helpful, tries his best to teach, but sometimes not very clear. Not tough at all in grading.   Exams can be tricky though

Well, Mooman's a good guy and earnest in trying to help you succeed but there's so much to Computer Science and he doesn't really explain anything- most lectures go off topic and are generally a waste of time. Start the labs early and get whatever help you can, if you don't know Comp Sci- well, if you don't know Comp Sci, god have mercy on you.
You wont learn much from the lectures. You have to practice hard for the exams.
great teacher
Good and helpful professor. Try his best in whatever teaches. Exams may be unexpected!

Didn't seem like she knew what she was talking about. Assignments were incredibly vague, projects were unnecessarily tedious. Assignments and coursework were clearly not her own. Presentations were hundreds of slides long and incredibly unhelpful. Nice person, awful teacher, and hoping that she gets better next semester and makes her own slides.

Seems like she means well, but she's pretty worthless as a professor. Assignment are 'easy', but only in the sense that one could access the information online. Expectations are not clearly reflected in lecture and she is often caught off guard, many times be erroneous/unclear information in her own slides. Would not recommend.

She's doesn't seem to know how to lecture, most of the slides we get are clearly not her own and sometimes she seems to be reading them for the first time with us.  Homeworks/Quizzes fairly easy.  Tests were on the long side but it seems like she's working on that.  Projects seemed like they were outside the scope of the class.
She's really nice, but not a good teacher. Lectures seemed unorganized and unclear.

I think this was her first semester teaching (and RIT's first semester coming from quarters), so assignment requirements were unclear and the curriculum was unorganized.  Future sections with this teacher will likely have higher clarity.  Professor is easy-going.
Lousy.

By far the worst experience I've had in an online class. The final project is a 10 page research paper for which he gave no feedback on, just a grade. His exams are RIDICULOUS. 100 questions, 2 hour time limit, very specific questions (e.g. in what year was the Magna Carta signed? 1213, 1214, 1215, or 1216). I greatly regret taking Siena's class.

Siena is great, although he had to leave during the middle of the quarter the time we did have with him was very enjoyable. Most entertaining 6-10p class I've taken. He teaches with stories from his experience. Very funny and helpful professor. He is awesome... and not bad on the eyes!

This is my second course with sps and I highly recommend him as a professor. His teaching style and methods always spark my interest..he also isn't bad on the eyes. I would strongly suggest taking a course with this instructor.
If he marked you as incorrect for a test question but you provided a good argument such as citing one of his previous lectures or the textbook, he would award you full credit for the answer.
Great class!! He teaches from experience and with a lot of great stories! Made the class fun and the material memorable.

Awesome guy, he tells a multitude of stories that relate to the topic on hand... most are very humorous.  His tests are fair, just read the main topics of the book and you'll be set.  Probably the best teacher I've had so far, very enjoyable and I looked forward to it every morning at 8am so that's saying something.
One of the best professors around, gets us to THINK!
Great prof. Always available during offices hours. Made the class project orientated, with no exams. Learned a lot about the topics and how to make a PCB.

Attend class or else you will get lost. He does not bother you about attendance. He is an AWESOME teacher and VERY helpful during office hours. I would love for him to be my professor again! By far the BEST EE teacher I ever had.
No Comments

Glen records all his lectures, so you don't really have to come to class, but you should if you want to witness his funny comments when presenting any 3D project/demos. He cares a lot about his students and will help you solve any issues with your 3D project(s) in or outside of class, just email him/talk to him/communicate!
Solid professor, gives great feedback and very helpful at office hours!

this class was the easiest B you possibly earn

Great class - the globalisation topics that were covered made the class more interesting and makes you want to go to class. Amazing professor who is clear on their teaching material as well backed with an experienced background. Professor has genuine commitment and interest to their students and class topics.

Wendy is a lovely professor who knows how to do her job. Even in an online class, she ensures that all of her students' voices are heard and that they are engaged in the conversation. She is an effective teacher and does not give a lot of work but is a hard grader. Only 1 pop quiz so reading isn't really that important. Seems concerned about how her students are doing in the class.

0/10, would not take again. This professor spends maybe 20 minutes on a topic and will immediately jump into examples without thoroughly explaining. The material covered on tests will be in the general ballpark, but mostly nothing you've seen before.

DO NOT TAKE!!! Wanda's classes lack formulas and definitions. I had to drop her class because this mingled with her own math errors made the content nearly impossible to learn. If you have the time to read the whole textbook maybe she'd be fine but I lacked this time.

Oo lala! She's so nice but if u want to pass u need to literally just pay attention and do the problems, maybe sit in the front. Legit worst professor I have ever had or ever will have. Pleas avoid

I almost pity her, as she does not seem to be all there. She is often confusing herself and cannot make it through a sentence at times. Great human being, fantastic office hours, terrible Mulitvar & Vector professor.

Wanda is a nice woman but a bad professor. She is easily overwhelmed by her own examples and heavily includes physics concepts in her teaching. Show up to class to do your homework and hand it in. comment: This is the worst professor ever. AVOID! grades only on homework and exams. Homework is submitted physically and does not respond much to questions.

Don't take this class unless you love to self-teach. The teacher is very quiet and oftentimes I can't understand what she is saying in the class. Her lectures are awful and the tests are unorganized. Her lectures are very difficult to follow. I would avoid taking this class if possible.

The instructor is hard to follow when she is teaching, she does not talk loud enough and has messy handwriting on the board. I truly hate to give people bad wraps since she seems like such a nice woman, but she is the reason that I am switching out of math major. She is a great professor. A nice person too. Believe me. Wanda may be past her prime and makes mistakes when going through problems, but if you pay attention in lecture, you will learn. She also clearly cares about her students, only one homework assignment is given per week, and test question mimic homework and examples shown in class.

If you mention you have Wanda on campus everyone has heard about how bad she is. I couldnt understand her. The tests were impossible and half the time the tests were so unclear. Terrible. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. It is dull and you never learn anything. Makes mistakes at the board. Only does problem examples. There is always somebody sleeping in class.

Hard to understand but thats not really the problem, she doesn't teach or explain anything at all and you pretty much have to teach it to yourself if you want to do well.
