Hard to understand. Does not teach. Hard to even understand test questions.

Just awful. Worst professor I've ever had. She cannot teach and lost our graded papers with her other class numerous times. Could not answer questions, half the time couldn't understand the question. I don't know what she does to make her a professor but she is awful. Avoid like the plague.

She was a true challenge at first. Her thick accent is hard to understand. She gets confused by questions and only goes over examples during class. She gets better later in the term as you start to understand her. She has a sense of humor. Frequently says "excuse me" for no reason and to no particular individual during class.

She know's what she's talking about but hasn't mastered how to pass her knowledge onto others. She can but funny at times but basically, you need to teach yourself the material if you want to do well. There is no partial credit on exams so make sure you study hard. She does come up with some clever examples to help you remember things.

AVOID AT ALL COST!!!! DOES NOT GIVES PARTIAL CREDIT. Only one hour exams... Disorganized. On one of my test (out of 8 problems) I got 6 perfectly right and the other 2 problems I was expecting partial credit. Guess what!!!?? I got a 69. NO PARTIAL CREDIT. AVOIDD!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Can't understand a thing she says. Explains things in the worst ways. Just avoid at all costs.

She is very funny at times but also very hard to understand. She works through problems very quickly, usually too quickly to follow. Her exams are nothing like the homework and are very difficult; she does not give much partial credit. If you are naturally good at math and can teach yourself she is a good professor otherwise she is very difficult.

Avoid.  Accent isn't as bad as some people claim; it's manageable.  What isn't manageable is the teaching quality.  Working through "such problems" have little to no bearing on the tests, and she makes more mistakes than any professor I have ever seen.

Refuses to answer direct questions from the students. Works through problems on the whiteboard while ignoring over-arching concepts and principles.  Does not come prepared to lecture the class beyond one small scrap of paper.

Refuses to answer direct questions from the students. Works through problems on the whiteboard while ignoring over-arching concepts and principles.  Does not come prepared to lecture the class beyond one small scrap of paper.

Very friendly teacher, with some corny jokes. You will get used to her accent quite easily. She teaches what you need to know but you still have to make use of the book to understand the material properly. Low level for homework and exams. Easy A if you study a little bit and do the homework.
She speaks 5 languages, and English is not one of her strong languages. Extremely hard to understand. Avoid.

She was a very hard teacher. Urgg so frustrating listening to her everyday gave hw out from the book every class. Test were mad hard. dont listen to tht guy up there must have been tht kid tht knew everything in class...
She is definitely one of the best math teachers at RIT.  I took her class last year and she was really helpful both in class and during her office hours.  Would definitely recommend taking her again

absolutely terrible. gives little to no partial credit on test, cannot understand her lectures, gives wrong equations, messes up examples more often than not, and gets confused by students questions so she just moves on and leaves it unanswered. do not take unless you want to teach yourself
Heavy accent and chicken scratch handwriting, that's all you need to know about Wanda.  By far the worst teacher I've had at RIT so far.  Avoid.

She isn't all that bad. Her writing and speech can be tough to understand, but she is kind of funny and definitely teaches what you need to learn. Definitely use the text to help. Homework level is low. Grading policy is nice especially if you can ace the Final
Her foreign accent makes her hard to understand sometimes and her writing is illegible but the homeworks and tests are very easy to pass if you understand the basics of the material.
An absolute joke, her class is an easy A if you read the book, do the homework, and DON'T listen to a word she says.

Wanda is a terrible professor.  She might know what she's talking about at some points, but can't teach it.  She stumbles over words, and her handwriting is ridiculous. However, if you go to class and do homework, you can pass.

Worst calc professor I have ever had. Stumbles upon her words. Did not know what the fundamental theorem of calculus was. Makes constant errors on the board. Thick accent. The only good thing about her is that homework counts at 30% and final replaces lowest test grade. Useless teacher, I taught myself. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!
Hard to understand most of the time, writing very hard to read, ridiculously hard tests
She isnt a very good teacher. avoid her if u can. i already knew the material before the class and the way she taught got me confused. Shes nice and all but shes a horrible teacher
Terrible. Confuses herself often, rarely understands students questions and can never answer them.
Avoid at all costs!

Seems easily frustrated by the material.  Confused by students questions so she leaves them unanswered.  When half the class leaves in the middle to go read the book themselves, something's wrong.  More like an independent study than a lecture.  If you skip and do the problems yourself, you're no worse off.
other instructors at the Rochester Institute of Technology should be ashamed to have her hold the same title as them.

She reads the book to you, gets confused and messes up examples. Don't commit anything she is saying to memory... It's probably wrong. When asked if the test is open book her reply was "I don't care".

Absolutely useless. Has really no right to be teaching us discrete math. Has trouble counting to 13 (she skipped 12).Much of her time is spent saying, "hokay" or "back up" because she makes so many mistakes. Many times (2/3) she would grade our tests, give them back to us, and not record the grades. She is horribly disorganized and lectures = crap.

She has a accent... and when she starts stuttering and repeating herself SHE DID SOMETHING WRONG and doesnt know where it is in her example.  The tests were fairly difficult.  She can't really explain things too clearly while talking, but if you follow along in the example you should be fine... that is if she doesnt mess the numbers up midway.
I had her for multivariable calculus.  She has a strong accent, but it is managable.  She goes through examples in detail, and draws very good pictures that help understand the topic.

Not the best teacher, but very nice.  Willing to help if you need it.  An easy class if you have a backround in the information; she is a good teacher to have to review stuff but not to learn it for the first time.

She's easily confused during examples, the class is a waste of time she doesn't explain anything, she assigns homework but doesn't collect it, gives weekly quizzes directly out of the homework and you can use your notes and your book if you ask, and we had formula sheets for the test, probably all to make up for her lack of teaching
Has a very strong accent, but nice overall.  She actually let us use our notes and book and all three tests.  If you can handle accents, then take her class.
Easy...not bad just do work
you dont undertand her, she doesnt know how to explain things, and shes always making mistakes for everything
Her tests are not incredibly difficult and her quizzes are easy if you know the material.  She doesn't assign homework and attendance is not mandatory.
Unless you already know the topic, avoid her like the plague.
Very friendly and personable once you scratch the surface. Very thick accent.  Moves very quickly through the course material. Always willing to give extra help.
No Comments

Horrible teacher.  I never missed a class and sat in the front.  She still never knew my name.  I couldnt understand anything because of her accent, she gives no homework to help bring up grades and her hand writing is unreadable.
She's no nonsense...kinda difficult ..moves a long soooo fast! Im still writing down the problem when she has already finished explaining it.  I cant learn this way.

Kinda hard to understand, and just teaches out of the book. Still cant figure out how we're supposed to do the problems when she cant. Oh, and it is a she, for whoever didnt know why his name was Wanda :P.
Has a strong east european accent.Very helpful outside of class.Makes sure that everyone understands the subject.Exams are easy.I can't figure out why his name is Wanda!
Difficult final

(She retired after Fall 2017) Prof. Clark is one of the most caring professors I've known. Lots of homework and a few heavy tests, but she is in Bates every weekday in the afternoon to help you. 5% extra credit if assignments are turned in a day early. Lectures are very theoretical, but still clear. Her class was great, she will be missed!
Dr. Clark is a tremendous professor. There are innumerable opportunities to learn from her. She is incredibly accessible and very kind. Make sure you do your work, and you will learn a lot from her.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: Dr. Clark is a sweet lady who knows everything there is to know about Calc pretty much off the top of her head. On top of being really kind and patient, she allows you to be flexible and offers a lot of extra help outside of lecture. She does indeed care for the mathematical success of her students.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Caring']

comment: Best math professor I've ever had. I hated math in highschool but she got me really interested in the subject, her Bates tutoring hours are super accessible and daily, and she's super patient and genuinely wants to see her students succeed. Probably the best teacher at RIT, she's amazing, so thankful I had such a good experience with college math

Professor Clark is the best professor I've had so far! She is always available for help in Bates and in her office and she is very good at resolving any questions that you have. Her tests are very fair and she gives extra credit for early assignments. Also, she is very understanding if you're out sick. HIGHLY recommend!  AMAZING professor!!!
Best math professor I've ever had. Always available for help at Bates study center, so patient and genuinely caring.

If you are opposed to doing workshops and HW or already have a hectic class schedule, Dr. Clark's classes are not for you. Prepare for a lot of assignments but also be prepared to walk away actually learning the material. One of the most patient professors I've ever had during my time at RIT. Is very frequently in Bates Study Center to help.

She is such a great teacher who will help you with anything you need. She is almost always available for help and offers tons of extra credit. Just try a little bit and you can easily get an A. She doesn't have too many hard set deadlines and accepts late homework, so just don't loose track of all the stuff you have to turn in.

Fantastic professor for anyone who is willing to actually put in effort and learn the material. I had her for Project Based Calc II, and we got 5 points extra credit for every early assignment. 4 worksheets per week and one homework, all really relevant to the material. She was always in Bates from 4-6 for extra help. Highly recommend.

She is one of the best professors I've ever had the privilege to have. She sincerely wants you to pass and gives you plenty of opportunities to catch up if you fall behind. Not only would I take her again but I'd suggest her to anyone that has her as an option. It's hard to think of a better professor.
Clear and great at depicting manipulation to derive functions and definitions. Great at showing examples. Verbal explanations are a bit more clumsy, but more often she shows an example.

There is so much extra credit built into this class. Each homework/workshop assignment has a 5% bonus if it is handed in early. These assignments combined make up a greater percentage than exams, slightly. Exams are straight forward. If you put in the time for the assignments, you'll get an easy A. Dr. Clark is also always available for help.

Professor Clark is a very sweet lady who provides many opportunities to succeed. She assigns a lot of homework, but offers help sessions that allowed me to get an A while also understanding the material. It's a lot of work and the tests are long, but she is a great teacher who grades fairly and does a great job of actually teaching the material.

A wonderful professor, she goes over the material very well and gives you plenty of time in-class to try practice problems and go over the material.   All of the course assignments are on her website as early as day one, and any work you finish early, you get extra credit on.   Tests are straight forward, and she tries her best to prep us.

Really learned a lot from her. Was in the Bates center all the time for extra help which she was willing to give. Fair grader and knows what she's talking about. There was a ton of homework so make sure you have extra time to spare to get it all done.

I took Clark for both MATH181 and MATH182. As someone who isn't great at algebra but loves calculus, I did very well in her class. She does give a LOT of homework, but I thought it was really worth it. They assignments are very similar to her exams which means the exams aren't bad at all.

Very nice lady. Accepts late work, allows make up exams, and gives you lots of bonus points. Her lectures, however are quite boring. I suggest only taking her if you know the material well and want an easy grade. Otherwise, you're very likely to fall asleep in her class.

Professor Clark is awesome. Be warned that it is a lot of work, but it is easily manageable. A lot of extra credit opportunities. A downside though is the fact that you're not taught *why* certain methods work or the derivation of the theorems. But, hey, that's what the book is for!

The best math professor I have had by far. This is the second class I have taken of hers and I don't regret it. Her class is very structured and she shows plenty of examples and is willing to explain when you don't understand either during or outside of class. Her worksheets provide useful practice. However, sometimes she confuses herself.

Absolute best math professor. Anyone here giving her a poor rating is most likely due to their poor effort and laziness. She knows her math inside and out. You could walk up and ask her any question from any class, she will think, and tell you how to approach it. Amazingly brilliant and easy to talk to. Always available for help. Do the work.
Fantastic professor. I didn't realize we had from the book homework for six weeks and so I had a D in the class. She let me make up all six weeks for full credit. Nicest. Professor. Ever.
Lots of work but there are no surprises. Weekly homework, workshop labs, worksheets for each class period. The review tests are very similar to the tests that are given.

Had her for all my first year calculus courses (pbc2, pbc3, and multivar).  Take this professor for your calculus classes.  There is lots of work, but it is worth it.  She is available for help.  If something wasn't clear in lecture, the worksheets step through the material well.  Exams are fair.  She keeps a timely update of your grades online.

This professor is extremely helpful. She answers questions well and is available every day M-F in Bates. She has a lot of smaller assignments that make up a decent portion of your grade, and posts practice tests online that are very similar to the test. VERY HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!

Easy teacher. A lot of HW and Labs though, but since they are required they result in doing well on the tests. The tests are easy plus she gives you a practice exam that is almost the same as the test.

Dr. Clark has been the best professor that I have had at RIT. I wish she was teaching Multi next quarter. She is a very liberal grader. There is a lot of work. Something like 9 homeworks, 27 worksheets, 15 labs and 5 exams. But she is always available to assist you if you get stuck. Gives extra credit if you hand in your assignments early.

The material is the level to be expected, but she is one of those profs who talk to the board and stand in front of what they write. the homework covered things we didn't know how to do in class and her grading is very inconsistent.  Honestly I have no idea how she has such a high rating here, everyone in her classes strongly dislikes her.

She was an extremely good teacher for very difficult material.  Her lectures were concise and notes were understandable.  The worksheets definitely helped for learning the material.  The only thing I disliked, the homework included applications we hadn't learned (had to read sections of the textbook in order to do the problem).

Easily the best math teacher I've ever had. I haven't done any calculus since high school and had no issue just jumping into multivariable with her as the teacher. She's extremely helpful and always in the Bates study center. Exams can be difficult, but homework provides a good grade buffer (and she gives extra credit fro early submissions).

The Doc is very kind & very willing to help. However, she assigns a lot of work. Expect 2 worksheets every class period and book work due Friday. You do get class time for these but it usually isn't enough. On the final you get to use a cheat sheet but it tends to run 3-4 hours and be pretty difficult. Would definitely take again. Amazing Prof!

She's a great teacher and very interesting. She will spend the time to teach you outside of class, and she spends 2 hours a day in Bates, but if you just drop by, she'll also help you. For honors kids: she'll let you make the class count for honors as long as you do her three extra problems every 3 weeks or so.

Had her for calc 2,3 and diff eq.  She gives 5% EC for early work and is always there to help you.  Definitely recommended for anyone taking the calculus classes.  She is very organized and hands everything back the next class including hw, tests and labs.  Got A's for all 3 classes

Dr. Clark has it all: the talent to solve complicated mathematical problems, the skill to teach her knowledge to others, the motivation to create her own labs and worksheets, the dedication to grade all work promptly and comprehensively, and the conscientiousness to take the time to address all questions to the satisfaction of their posers.
Her lectures can be difficult to follow at times, but she is incredibly helpful when you ask for help.

Sometimes the work can be hard but she's always able to help. She's walked me through entire problems, she's checked my homework for errors before letting me turn it in, she's just a sweety. She tends to make mistakes in her notes and examples, but if you stay on top of things you can pick out the mistakes and she'll correct them.

Professor Clark was a fantastic professor in terms of how much she was able to teach me. Unfortunately though she gives quite a huge load of homework (though she packs in 5% EC). Other than that she is very helpful in her office and the tutoring center and is a very kind woman who will explain something right after the exam if you are interested!
Had her for calc 2 and 3 and now diff eq. She gives a lot of work but it's worth it. She's extremely helpful if you don't understand something.

Project-Based Calc III: Awesome professor! Only 40% of grade is exams. Workshop + worksheet every class + weekly homework = a lot of work; however, it is worth it. Extra 5% credit for handing in any assignment a day early. TONS of office hours..she will practically do your HW for you she is so helpful. EASIEST WAY TO GET AN A IN CALC III! TAKE HER!

I took Dr. Clark for the entire calculus sequence 282,283 and 305. She is the BEST professor I have ever taken and I do not say that lightly. You have to do the work but if you do, you will understand calculus. She is willing to answer any questions and is always available to help.

Worst class. She gets frustrated when you ask questions. Gives 8 packets a week that are at least 4 pages each plus about 20 book problems. Labs are very hard. Our TA didn't even know how to help us half the time. Tests are every other week and the material is on topics we covered 2 weeks before. Just way too much work and stress.

She is the best professor ever!  She gives a lot of work but it is all very manageable.  He lectures are very clear and the tests are based on exactly what she teaches. She gives a lot of partial credit and is always available for help at any time.

Dr. Clark was a great professor. A typical week consists of 3 worksheets, 3 labs, and bookwork. They are all pretty challenging but I've never gotten less than a 95 on any of them. She's always willing to help and anything that you turn in early, you'll get five extra credit points on. Exams are every other Friday and they are easy. Take Dr. Clark!

Gives alot of work. 1-2 worksheets per class. But the work is do-able. She gives you time at the end to do it as well. Extra credit for handing work in early. Very nice and approachable. Tests are a big difficult, but if you study and ask for help when you need it you'll be fine. Definitely one of the best math teachers at RIT.

She gives really good notes and is very approachable. The daily worksheets aren't that bad and she will always answer any questions. Take advantage of the extra credit on the worksheets and homework...They can really give you a cushion for the Final Exam. The only tricky thing could be the exams.

Assigns a lot of work, but it's doable. Lectures are easy enough to follow if you are paying attention. Extra credit for assignments done early. Practice exams online are helpful. Though fast paced and a heavy work load, I would definitely recommend for a thorough understanding of the material and applications.

Very nice lady, but assigns excessive amounts of homework, does not explain the relevance of topics, does not include practical examples in class or on assignments, and goes out of her way to make lectures thoroughly incomprehensible.  Writes with one hand, erases with the other; stands in front of example problems.
Teacher gives really hard and pointless homework. She has no life and grades for hours on end. Her tests are really easy I have a 100 average, but her workload is off the deep end
Awesome math teacher! Lots of homework but a ton of chances to pull up your grade. One of the nicest ladies you'll ever meet.

Worksheets are a joke and homework is pretty easy cause shes in the lab alot and answers all your questions.  Also very clear teacher and makes things really easy to understand.  Tests aren't bad at all and she puts up practice exams that are close to the real thing.  Labs are a joke you just click and press the mouse.  Plus shes like my grandma.

Worksheets are pretty easy, especially if you see her for help on them in the study center, HW is usally easy for same reason.  Labs can be pretty hard, and Tests can be difficult but cheat sheets are alowed.

Extra credit on hw and worksheets if handed in early. Worksheets are sometimes impossible though. Tests are often vague/ambiguous, but usually (not always) similar to the practice test she posts online before each test. If you do the work you should be fine in getting at LEAST a B, probably an A.
Very easy but alot of work Very very helpful
The best. Nice old lady, very helpful and clear. gives fair amount of work. If you do the homework and worksheets, A- guaranteed.
Awesome teacher. Gives a lot of work. If you do the work you can't fail. She gives opportunity to make up worksheets. Her grading policy greatly benefits you.

Doctor Clark is a good prof. Her teaching style is great and she hands out worksheets on the material that are very helpful. However, she gives way too much homework. Despite this, I definitely recommend her.
Very approchable, very helpful.  Lots and lots of HW, almost rediculous, but if you do it, it boosts your grade alot, and you will ace the tests and quizes
Great teacher.
great teacher, uses mathematica
One of the best professors I have had at RIT. He is very knowledgeable and constantly looking for feedback from his students.

design thinking and concept develepment is easy and he knows it. He likes that it's easy. It's not supposed to be hard he says. He even admits he has RIT come after him saying his class is too easy and he says "ik, that's just the way the subject is". This, my amigos, will feel like a 5th grade class. do ur essay (no more than 1 page!) and get ez A
Generally unhelpful and makes it hard to succeed. Not very understanding or compassionate. I would not recommend this professor to anyone who does not like unfair and unjust policies and procedures.

Zeke is a great professor, he's really down to earth and wants you to succeed. He said in our first lecture that he tries to give as many As as possible, so if you participate in lectures and do the work, he'll reward it.
Easy going guy. Willing to help you along. Lectures are very short, most of the class is working on a semester long project. If you put the time into the project, it won't be a problem.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'GROUP PROJECTS']

comment: Zeke's Design Thinking class during student exchange program made me pursue a career in Design Thinking after graduating from RIT. 'nuff said.

Zeke is funny and cares for his students. He is very approachable and gives honest feedback. His purpose is not to create a stress culture in his classes but to help students go out of their comfort zone to learn about the cases and apply theories for analysis. If you put efforts, its easy to get an A in his class. Pay extra attention to deadlines!

Design Thinking & Concept Development was one of my favorite classes. Zeke taught it in a non-traditional way where it wasn't so much about the grades but about the fact that you were learning and truly utilizing what he was teaching. You get to pick your semester long group project and honestly you learn a ton about product design. Easy A
Great guy.  Tries his best to make a boring subject interesting.  Definitely recommend taking him.
great management class, great guy

Zeke is a great professor, really helpful and very good about getting the information across.  However, due to some serious circumstances outside of the classroom, he struggled keeping up with grading and filling us in on project details.  Super nice guy, would recommend him any day if he comes back after this semester.
Take this professor for Strategy and Innovation. Should be no debate.
He comes off as a hard teacher but in the end he aint too bad
this is hands down worst person i have met in school so far.

The MOST condescending, LEAST understanding professor I have ever had. I would highly recommend NOT taking his classes. At least twice as demanding as my other Anthro class worth the same amount of credits.
He is very rude and hard professor. He gives a lot of assignments which are time consuming. Midterm and final examinations are long papers.
The man is like Steve Jobs, minus the innovation, genius and creativity. So basically just an ass. Fortunately his reign of terror is over, a gift for the next generation of engineers

Probably my worst major-specific professor to date. Topic seems straightforward with lab and reports, but he makes it much more difficult. Tries to act like a "supervisor" but comes off passive aggressive/arrogant. I get reports need to be clean and concise but he's more of a nitpicker. I suggest you make good chemistry with your team and tank.

Parthum is easily the worst professor I've had at RIT to date. He gives the impression that his assignments are open-ended and is therefore vague on details, but has very specific expectations that are never stated. He acts contradictory as well, and is very difficult to talk to due to the fact that he never allows others to finish a sentence.

He is an extremely hard grader. He will say one thing, then say the complete opposite thing the next. I've gotten into a habit of recording his lectures because he takes back his word so many times. He will take points off of your report if it isn't the carbon copy version of what he wants. You'll have to read his mind to get a good grade.

Average grade on his labs is in the 60s because everybody loses 20+ points on the landmines he's hidden in each lab...of course he never mentions this until well after he's harshly graded you. Grader tells you how to title graphs & grades fairly as a result; Parthum randomly takes over a section's grading & penalizes you for "bad graph titles".

I don't know what the other students problems are (maybe they did not get it, or were too lazy to do the work) but Prof. Parthum has been one of the best teachers I have had here at RIT. You may have to work hard and he is VERY detail orientated, but I am paying a LOT to go here and I learned more in his classes than anyone else.
Good teacher... knows a good amount(a huge amount about wafers)... can be hard at times at grading... good tests and quiz's... an amazing lecturer and clear concepts...

Overly strict, but in the end it works out kindasorta. He treats his students like employees to the end. I agree with the previous; I get the impression that he fabricates many stories and experiences. Don't get the book (nontrad), read the notes for quizzes, write the papers well, kill yourself for the project and with great luck you will get an A

Another one of the MET program's worst.  He may be qualified to make wafers, but he is not qualified to teach.  Lecture notes are scans of the textbook, and he just reads them.  A senior level class and the only thing i know from going to class is that he's wasting my time.  Fire the Xerox and Kodak leftovers and get some qualified teachers.
very good teacher highly recomeneded. He knows his stuff and is good at teaching and answering questions.  He is a fair grader.
A very informative professor with industry experience and insight.  Makes you do your work, but is very available for help.
Good guy, knows his stuff. One of RIT's up and coming professors.

Parthum was ok. His quizzes were very unclear. He admited to putting trick questions on his quizzes. Just gives you notes right from the book. Fairly lenient on grading too. You will learn more with him than with Castro, but Castro grades easier.

Had him for astronomy. He would manage to cram at least 35 slides every lecture and after the 2nd week I gave up trying to actually take the notes. Also, since he relied so heavily on Powerpoint slides, we didn't have time for in class problems. Class was overall boring and difficult which is disappointing because astronomy is so interesting.

He's not a bad person, but he kinda sucks at teaching. He's genius when it comes to astronomy/astrophysics, but won't make you understand the basic kinematics and such. Gives a tone of in class stuff. Uses WebAssign, which is waaay harder than his test. Which, btw, have a little to do with whatever we do in class. He's really willing to help thou.

hes a good guy. i didnt have any trouble in the class. he is always helpful if you ask question. not the most interesting lectures but the rest is good. tests were easy if you know your stuff. not an intimidating guy, very laid back.
He's a good guy, always willing to help you. great 1 on 1. kinda boring in class. grades tons of in class stuff, that gets kinda annoying.  curves the tests, not terribly hard to do well in.

Seems nice, teaches off of powerpoints wish he had a little more info, tests are kind of hard, class based on inclass examples like a lab and it can be hard if you dont know what you are doing because you do it in a group and either you know it or not

Worthless professor. Uses difficult third party homework system, bases tests on very little actual classwork, very hard and vague labs, spends more time drawing cute pictures on his free body diagrams than actually teaching. The TA's will be the only help you'll get. He's a genius on his own, but this man CANNOT TEACH AT ALL.
The man has a pine tree in his ass.  Not helpful at all, though weights tests alot which helps.
Bad.

Weekly quizzes, they were tough and you definitely need to study. She's a very fair teacher all around, you have to earn yourself a good grade in her A & P lab, you learn a lot about A&P in her class. If you put in the work you will be fine, not a class you can just cruise through.

Lennox is intimidating at first but is actually very kind. She gives weekly quizzes every week in lab. The quiz can be literally anything which makes it difficult but thats with any lab teacher you get. Don't beat yourself up over getting a C because realistically its very hard to get anything above. C's get degrees!

Lennox vs Mastrangelo? Don't pick based on who is "easy." Lennox was amazing and taught the material straightforward. No xtra credit but you can get an A if you put the work in. If you are taking anatomy, you need to work hard. AP lab is hard because you are pursing a career in this field and they want to prepare you. Life isn't meant to be easy.

I got an "A" in A and P for the spring semester, but it was hard work. Some of her quizzes about 70-80% of the time are right from her powerpoint, the other 20% of the time, you usually have to complete a weekly "lab guide" and sometimes she puts a lot of questions on the quizzes from there. She's a good lecturer, and explains stuff well

If you study from the material she gives you, you should do well on the quizzes. She is mostly understanding about missing class if it is a reasonable situation. Very knowledgable about anatomy. Strict on spelling, but will usually give half credit if a word is close but misspelled. I would take a class with her again if I had the choice.

comment: If you have to take MEDS250 or 251, I recommend Lennox - she is a TOUGH GRADER and she can be very particular about answers and SPELLING - she's worth it if you want to learn more and be challenged! If you've heard reviews be wary that these might come from students who thought they could breeze by - A&P is NOT that type of class.

comment: Professor Hosseini is the best Professor I have had in college. Gives a lot of insight into how to examine the structure of a problem, and how that would affect how a possible algorithm would be designed.

Professor Hosseini was very well versed in the subject and encouraged us in every sense to take up the subject and perform better. Had a significant amount of examples for the course material. Has good knowledge on the course topic. Gave super good feedback on the course research project and how we could make it better.

Professor Hadi is enthusiastic about algorithms and uses a lot of in-class activities during lectures. Homework required problem-solving but didn't require formal proofs. Reviews of previous lectures were also given at the beginning of each lecture.

Currently taking him for Algo 261. He really cares about the student and one of the best professor in RIT CS Department. Even in the 9AM class, his lecture does not make you sleep and its also very interactive with lots of jokes and insights. May he sustain this energy for rest of his teaching career. Loves his students and really cares about their success. Covers a lot and does so very well in an interactive way. Could not recommend him more.
Amazing and very knowledgeable. You will not get bored; he uses various things such as videos and group work to keep the class interested and involved. Definitely take the course.

He is a very passionate professor who really tries to make the material interesting and makes sure the students actually understand the material. I think honestly if you share the same passion, he is definitely a person you would like to take classes under or do research.

Great person to add to your professional network. Very informative, kind and experienced professor.

He is extremely helpful and always willing to take the time to explain anything you ask. He also tries very hard to make sure students understand the material rather than just talking and writing on the board. I would recommend him.
The goat. That's all you need to know...

Probably the best professor I've ever had at RIT. Lot of work, yes, but it never felt like busy work or that it was getting out of hand. Very helpful during office hours and her exams are very fair. The labs are pretty difficult but that makes sense since this is a lab heavy class. The IEEE papers can take FOREVER to write and also a learning curve on how to write them. The TAs for this class are also very helpful during office hours since some labs are a bit confusing.

This is easily one of the best 3D animation professors at RIT. He makes sure everyone gets thurough critique and does his best to involve everyone in class. He is pretty laid back while also staying an effective teacher. He not only teaches about animation itself but about how to care for yourself during the process.

Mark is, without question, the best animation professor at RIT, but his classes are what you make of them. You can get good grades with simple projects, but he'll also support you every step of the way if you choose to push yourself. Though he's slow with returning grades, his energy and care for his students far outweighs the inconvenience.

I would highly recommend her for any class, I'm sure she'd be awesome!

If you listen to what she has to say and put in effort it is an easy GPA booster
She was super nice and graded the essays and quizzes fairly easy. good teacher overall

I would highly recommend it to anyone who needs an arts of expression credit.

great class at RIT
