comment: While Dr. Barth-Hart has to be the sweetest professor I have had at RIT, he is not the most efficient. He goes off topic a lot, and his two hour lectures are hard to get through. That aside, he does care about his students' success. He will do just about anything to help you pass, and he gives ample extra credit opportunities.

His lectures consist of him talking for the majority of the time, with the occasional equation being written on the board. This style of teaching works for some, but most of the student, myself included, found his method to be ineffective at absorbing any knowledge. He is passionate about math but needs to work on making sure we actually learn.
great guy

He doesn't necessarily 'teach to the test', but that is generally expected in higher level math courses. His primary objective is making sure you understand AND enjoy the material. He gives a lot of tips and tricks for doing what could otherwise be very tedious calculations. He is generous with grading as long as you explain your ideas/work.

Lectures can be dry and a little scatterbrained, but his examples and explanations are among the best I've ever seen from a professor at RIT. Incredibly passionate about the subject, which shows in his lectures. Some homework, but not too difficult. Tells you what is on the test ahead of time. Highly recommended.
Very pristine and pure treatment towards concepts and abstract approaches.

Barth-Hart is the greatest professor I've had at RIT.  He is so passionate about math and teaches to the test. He specifically told us the layout of the final, including what the topic of each question was. His lectures can be boring, but he is an excellent professor.

He is the nicest and sweetest old man. He knows his material so well and you are truly blessed if you take his class. He teaches slow, but that's only to make sure you fully understand the material. -spring 2015

The man loves what he does. If you share his passion for math, you'll love his class. Otherwise, you may find it painfully boring. Class is all lecture and no participation, and very little required homework is assigned. Go to class and pay attention, and you'll be alright. If you don't understand, he is more than willing to help you until you do.

8 o'clock lecture will require gallons of coffee, zero class participation in lecture and very disjointed and scattered teaching style. The material isn't bad but he displays it haphazardly.  If you need help or extra time on something he is accommodating.

Scatter-brained. Brilliant, but impossible to follow. Lectures are disjointed and have nothing to do with homework or exams. Office hours may help, but only if you need just a little help. Few assignments, but VERY HARD, because his lectures will not help you. Literally everything in every lecture is incomprehensible and assumes too much knowledge.
Lecture material much different from assignments...
I didn't enjoy his class much. It seemed very unorganized and hectic. He didn't rush teaching, but he went back and forth on topics quite often. It was tough to keep track with what he was saying.

Professor Barth-Hart is one of the kindest, overall best professors I've ever had.  He loves math and truly cares about each and every one of his students.  Homeworks and exams are very fair.  I would definitely recommend him to anybody for any class he teaches.

Good teacher very interested in field.Very enthusiastic. Sometimes unclear in lecture but if you ask a question or go to office hours and makes sure you understand.Relatively easy grader.If your interested take him.If not, then pay very careful attention.Gives homework. Doesn't collect.

Excellent guy, very interesting but lecture can sometimes wear on you.  Very helpful.  One time I came in on a whim for some help and he gladly devoted the next 2.5 hours to helping me understand everything.  Has a very good outlook on teaching and is very considerate.  His tests are challenging but good for the material.

very cool nerdy guy. very interested in his field and if you have scrap if interest in theoretical mathematics take a class with him. likes to go on tangents about stuff that was WAY over my head but still interesting. tests right off of class examples. pay a little attention, and you will be good

Good teacher overall, sometimes the lecture can get a bit on the boring side, but other than that he presented the material in a clear and meaningful way.  I got a D in discrete I yet I got a B in this class - he's very fair about grading things, also.  Only 3 small "due" homework assignments the entire class.

Good luck to anyone who ventures forth into the realm of online learning with this man. His orchestration of the online learning environment is that of a fish out of water. His organization is horrible, his instructions are muddled and don't bother asking for him to clarify, you will only be more conufused . This class didn't need to be this hard.
He can't use a good teaching methods. He focuses on Participate. This is not fair. I got "C" with him

i admit that he is one of the toughest teacher but i learned a lot from him professionally and personally. he is language is hard to understand but he likes to push his students to learn more out of the class. he LOEVS dialogue and examples of existing company and he is obsessed of Tech
This man is useless and needs to throw in the towel, he does not explain any assignments and refuses to help you when you ask.  He takes forever to give your grades if he gets you them at all.
Great Professor.  You will learn so much.

Spent the class lecturing about things either unrelated to the material or things already gone over in the homework assignments. Weekly quizzes with poorly worded questions. Barely graded things all semester (large projects included) and inputted essentially all the grades on the very last day he possibly could. AVOID. AT. ALL. COSTS.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Professor Goodman is an absolute joke. He's infuriating, he decided to grade everything at the last minute, and he doesn't know how to teach. His class is unbelievably boring and he somehow seems to care less about the class than we do. Stay away from this mess of a professor

Gordon's a nice guy but his lectures are too long and don't tell us anything new that wasn't covered in the assigned readings. There's a quiz and lecture every Tuesday; I recommend you skip at least 7 or 8 Tuesdays, since he takes off the lowest 5 quizzes anyways. Assignments are due Thurs, which you can skip if you did it at home; fairly easy work

Attendance was mandatory to a degree, but he isn't really a great teacher. His course is extremely easy and won't really help you ever except for some stuff with photoshop. I wish I didn't have to take the class but I'm glad I got him instead of a harder professor.

Definitely not a bad person, but his class is terrible. He assigns a lot of reading and isn't clear about what specific things you need to focus on in said readings to pass his quizzes. Some of the quizzes range from questions about hardly touched topics to "name one thing you learned in these readings". He's also terrible about grading.

He is a fair professor. There is work. If you do it you will do fine. I had him for an introduction level class, so it wasn't bad.  One thing was that he would post assignments very last minute some times, and his grading wasn't very consistent.

This professor is the worst. He rarely grades anything and his lectures are long and useless. You don't even need to go to class, you won't learn anything. He rambles on random subjects and that's it. He says he'll give homework and then won't post it for days afterwards.

Worst Programming Teacher, I had Joe Pietruch first, and it was such a drop off in quality going to Gordon. I recommend anyone looking at programming to wait for a class taught by Joe because he is so much better than Gordon. Gordon is incoherent and is boring. The code he supplies runs on forever, and has more comments than content.

Terrible teacher all around. Although the class is not hard, there is overall very little graded work, but he takes extreme amounts of time to grade assignments. He is monotone and rambles incoherently. Avoid at all costs.

I don't mean to be mean, but this man has no business teaching. His presentations were dreadful to the point I'd rather endure physical pain. He didn't teach whatever the class was supposed to go over, but instead pushed some agenda of his upon us. I've taken two of his classes now, and regret doing so both times.

Literally the worst teacher I've had. It took him so long to grade projects that he had to give everyone a pass/fail, based on like 2 minutes of observation, in order to meet the grading deadline. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!!!!

WORST PROFESSOR IVE EVER HAD. I HAD NO IDEA WHAT HE WAS TALKING ABOUT THE WHOLE ENTIRE TIME. he zones out during class also and if you even look away from the screen for a second, he does something and while you are copying it down,he switches screens so you cant do anything. I warn ALL NMD students: DONT TAKE HIS CLASS!

DONT TAKE THIS PROF if you are a NMD student. You will learn NOTHING. Does not teach & grades VERY harsh. Refuses to answer emails. Grades are not posted until MONTHS later. Got our grades for the 1st project the DAY BEFORE withdraw deadline(WEEK 8!) - only after complaints to his boss. Other section has all A's and B's - our sect. has C's and D's.

He has to have been the worst professor/teacher I have ever had. Always shows up late to class, hands back grades days before revisions are due (when other sec's have had theirs back for weeks). Almost impossible to get a hold of and never explains his grades no matter how many times you beat his door down. Stay away from this joke of a professor!

One of the most boring teachers I've ever had. He is CONSTANTLY unprepared and bores you to death with his lectures. He talks the whole time and we copy his code verbatim. He could spend ten minutes explaining something that would take a normal person one. He forgets to post code after classes, talks with his eyes closed, etc. AvoidThisClassIfUCan

hands down WORST professor at RIT. knows what hes doing but royally fails at relaying to it anyone else. classes consist of frantically trying to copy his code down before he switches screens and moves on to something else. you have no time to actually learn anything. i've even tried the sit back and listen approach no copying code but absorbed nad

He seems like a decent person and is willing to help if you approach him. I'm sure he knows what he is doing but he doesn't know how to relay the information. He gives guidelines on what he wants in projects but he doesn't give grades back. Do not take him if you need things clearly explained and you don't like learning mostly on your own.

Gordon Goodman is a seemingly nice individual. This being said it takes more than this to be able to teach a class in computer programming. His class had little value and I didn't feel like I walked away with anything useful. He doesn't put up grades frequently at all. His classwork was us copying his code verbatim. I unlearned things I alreadyknew

Without comparison, the worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life. Has absolutely NO knowledge of the subject he teaches, and constantly comes to class unprepared. Most often we spend classes attempting to debug the shoddy program he cooked up 5 minutes before he showed up. No grades until it was too late to drop. Dont give this guy ur money.
Worst teacher I've ever had in my life. He doesn't teach - he does everything himself and makes everyone copy him. His voice is monotone. I want to kill myself when i'm in his classroom.
Worst Professor EVER. No Grades. No Projects. MEAN!!!!!!!
Worst professor I've had at RIT. No grades. No project requirements. Plus he makes derogotory comments and hates minorities.

It's hard to understand her sometimes. She makes it so that you have to do all assignments because the grade is made up of three tests, attendance, and weekly essays. There's no other sources other than her lecture and even then she doesn't out full detail on the slides.
tags: ['So many papers', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: I say "lots of homework" but that just means you have a weekly essay to do with an accompanied reading. She goes by fast with slides, but information is always available on mycourses. Simple, easy, just a little boring in the beginning of the semester when starting out.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Good class to take if you have to take an art history course.
easy just boring class :)

Really great professor, the type you always want to have in college. His depth of knowledge in the material is incredible, not an easy class but commit yourself and you will succeed. Always available for extra help or questions. One of the best professors I've taken.

Had him for Strengths of Materials. Great professor!! Tests were fair, and not that hard. 3-4 homework assignments due per week, but very helpful at office hours. I would HIGHLY recommend Professor Merrill!

Great teacher. Always trying to help. Uses book every night for homework. Lots of homework but if you do it you shouldn't get below an 80. He wants you to understand and will help as long as you ask for it or participate.
Good teacher.  Lots of homework but It does help you learn Statics.  Has a grader do grading, so don't blame him for that.  I would take him again.

Decent professor, had him for statics & strength of materials. He can be tough old man at times. One day he'll say how well the class is doing, then say how little we know later in the week, you get use to it tho. Very willing to help in office hours. Gave extra credit. I would take him again.
His grading is very inconsistent, avoid at all costs.
Global literature last semester with Dr. Ray was, and still is, the hardest class I've taken. Despite this, his class was also the most rewarding and intellectually engaging class I've taken.

I am a CS major and never imagined I could learn so much about the history of computing in an English course! Dr. Ray encourages discussion and we often had lively debates about super relevant topics. I will definitely take another course with him.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Gives good feedback']

comment: Dr. Ray is a truly inspiring professor to have a class with. He is able to emphasize the importance of the class's subject matter and frequently connects lectures to present day events. This class only has 4 grades (3 of which are essays), so that can be a bit stressful. Still, he communicates what he wants on them pretty well. Would reccomend.

Discussion intensive. We got to read some amazing stories that were adapted into motion pictures. I loved the way Dr. Ray helped us think about how a specific medium has certain strengths and weaknesses. Also, I was grateful for the extensive feedback on my essays.

I am a Computer Science major and I learned more about the history and ethics of computing from this English course than from any of my CS classes. Professor Ray really pushed us to questions the pros and cons of technology and provided a lot of context for new developments such as generative AI. Highly recommend.

If you don't do the readings, you'll be very confused. He's open to extra credit, which you might get midway through the semester. Attendance is mandatory, but only light participation is required. 

Whenever he cancels class, you never have to make up work, which is great. Grading isn't awful; there are opportunities to make it up.

I learned a lot in this class. Professor Ray balanced lectures with a flipped classroom approach, where we responded to prompts in small groups. He provided a lot of feedback on my papers and definitely helped me improve my writing. I plan on taking another course from him.
Pretty interesting lectures.  I felt like I learned a good bit about the history of copyright.  I think some of his presentations were dry, however.

I liked the way he lectured. He knows what he is talking about. There were often readings to do outside of class and then he went over them in depth during class time. This class was split, taught by two profs,  and he was in charge of the intellectual and creative piracy part.

Class was largely included student presentations; he had a tendency to be combative. He struggled to understand a perspective a time or two and would bring up other sources to "knowledge gap" others. Ironically he was also very dismissive of other sources if it doesn't enforce his strong political bias. While not wrong he can comes off strong.
tags: ['Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']

comment: The class was split into discussing about the reading and watching the film counterparts. Attendance and participation has the most weight, and there's 2 papers (3 if you didn't present a final project idea). All readings are provided, except Watchmen. He leaves feedback on your essays and the workload was doable. Enjoyed the readings and films.

Professor Ray is great! You can tell he's passionate about what he does. If you aren't a reader I would stay away from this course, however, if you find you have an appreciation for literature this class is for you. The entire semester is based on three essays and attendance and participation.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Prof Ray is really easy to listen to and its not hard to keep up. He's got a really interesting perspective and while he did struggle understanding someone else's perspective a time or two, for the most part he is really open and willing to hear your part.

Amit Ray is an inspiration and one of the only professors I had this year that I actually learned from. On top of that, when RIT told the professors to give less of a workload because mental health has been rapidly deteriorating, he was one of the only ones to actually listen, and he barely gives any work in the first place.
He is really nice. I recommend his class!

Professor Ray is extremely passionate about his work and imparts a lot on his students. My favorite part of his teaching style is how he connects the lines between media, literature, history, and current events. There is never a bad lecture, but they are long winded, and sometimes difficult to follow. Loved his class.

He is so so smart and knowledgeable about not only literature but about technology and current events. As an engineer I've always hated English but I really enjoyed his class and lectures. The ONLY grades given were 3 papers one of which was the final. 10/10 would take again.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Very passionate. Very knowledgable about social history and current events. Provides interesting real world examples. Unable to be concise, rarely provides talking stick to students and quickly takes it back. If he could clean up his rhetoric students could pay attention and follow easier. Even when concentrating intensely its difficult to decipher

Professor Ray is very passionate about his class. There are almost no collected assignments for this class, just two tests and a final, with one or two homework collected. Tends to go on rants for most of the class. Very easy to do well in this class.
Blew my mind. Amazing Prof! Should you seek him out outside of class, you will be rewarded with all kinds of helpful resources and discussion. Go to his office hours. Seriously.

Class discussion often has nothing to do with the reading, assignments are unclear and he is hard to reach outside of class. Also its finals week and we still haven't gotten grades back for out midterm papers...
This was a well-run discussion-based course.  He did a good job of motivating conversation and stimulating interest, and also made effective use of student-designed presentations for this purpose.

Excellent teacher, expects students to prove their worth. As an intl. student I found he has an intl. outlook not just American way of thinking. English is not my first language and I EARNED an A in his class. If you know why you  are in, and what you want out of, college then Amit is your guy. I'm surprised many students here expect spoon-feeding
He is very smart teacher and I really recommend him to take class with him
He was a great professor! He is very smart and if you go to his offices hours you will learn a lot. He gives you range to do whatever you want for the final project.

Very intelligent guy, but the lectures are muddled at best. I still have no idea what he expects from us in regards to work, assignments, or discussions. Not helpful when asked for clarification on anything. What the heck am I being graded on!?

He is clearly a very intelligent man, but he has difficultly speaking concisely and often rambles for entire lectures without saying much. He gives off a very condescending attitude and doesn't seem particularly sympathetic toward students. And he didn't give any grades until the very end of the class so nobody had any idea how they were doing.

Professor Ray doesn't slow down for you. But he has a way of returning to earlier points and building on them. His teaching style seems a lot like the Borges we read. Dense, seemingly contradictory and (to use one of his favorite words) recursive-he regularly used examples from current events to illustrate points. I learned to learn in new ways.

Ray is a very intelligent man and has the ability, and I believe he enjoys, making everyone in the class feel inferior and stupid. I was put into his Honors Lit and Tech class my first quarter, and I absolutely hated the class. He rambles about nothing, makes us read the weirdest books, and he never graded us on anything. Beware!

I didn't like him as a teacher at all. I felt he was very bland and talked a lot.  For the writing, his comments about correcting it were unclear.  He can also be very blunt on how he feels about your writing during class. I did not like him at all.

I found his classes really interesting. The work required really was not all that much. The only big problem I could see people having with this professor was that attendance is absolutely mandatory and he doesn't like when you're late. If you can show up to class, you can get an A. He's pretty interesting as well, which is a plus.
all he talked about was youtube, the election, and radiohead. i put up with this crap and he had the nerve to give me a C when the other members in my group got As

Obviously very knowledgeable on a number of subjects. I really enjoyed the course and I am so glad I took it. I really liked him as a teacher. A lot of the comments on here are really negative, so maybe he teaches certain courses very differently than he teaches others.

Honestly one of the best classes I've taken at RIT. I've taken four classes with him, and have loved all of them. He can be a little dry, but he's extremely intellegent and if you can comprehend 60percent of what he says than you're gaining a lot.   This is what college classes SHOULD be like.

I have no idea why he is rated so low.  If you do the work and listen to what he says, he is more than fair.  You can revise your work for a higher grade.  If I can get an A in this class, anyone can.  Also, he's been nominated for the Eisenhart several times and he's relatively new.  Good teacher, good class.

Terrible professor. Wrote a 4 page a paper which he admitted was good at first. Then I miss two classes and go to see him in the office. For no reason he rips my paper finding out all these stupid flaws in it, which I had an answer for. Just a bad professor who said I was waisting his time.

His Writing Seminar is quite possibly one of the most boring classes you could take. He never clarifys what he wants you to really write about. His ascinine remarks to anything you say that has any relevance to the course but differs from his own opinion gets old after the first day.

Really boring and gets very defensive if you offer an opinion that differs from his & isn't willing to listen to you at all. Just goes on and on, without anybody having any idea what he's talking abt and at the end, it's a mad race to get out of the classroom. Will never take another class with him.

One of the most boring classes I have ever taken, dreaded it every Mon. & Wed. Nobody understands a word he says and he takes great pleasure in 'stumping' the class. Does not like anybody disagreeing with him, even if they have a valid arguement.
No Comments

This class was basically on the Simpsons, but even with that being the textbook, it's still a little dry.  Nevertheless, Amit's a really nice guy and generally doesn't mind deviating from the scheduled discussions, so occasionally the classes are riveting

This course is very student driven and he knows this and provides an open floor to all students to participate. He is very clear on what you're graded on and as long as he can see you completed the rubric checklist you should be all good.

Students run this class. Professor Woelk is passionate about the topic and will engage with good discussions. Lots of reading every week! Students will write a blog topic, present with team members, do a debate, read a book, and have a final paper, but if you pay attention/find it interesting, you'll be good. Sounds like a lot but very manageable.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Graded by few things']

comment: The class I took with him was asynchronous, but from what I could gather he was a good professor. Some of his grading policies were a little strict, but they were at least clear policies. Communicating questions to him was easy and he responded quickly

He is extremely kind and caring. He does improv for fun and got all of his students involved in an improv workshop for class. He has clear instructions, clear grading criteria, and clear expectations. He runs a good class! Lots of reading though!

Has a slack for class. Participation is huge. Midterm/Final are pretty straight forward, you have to try to get below a 75, they are "essays" more like short answers to multiple questions. Generally relaxed. Tends to be passive aggressive. Also 2 "projects" that are required these are blog posts or a blog post and a presentation. Not bad
Professor Milas was great!

An extremely intelligent professor with really good lectures, but you have to go to lectures because he doesn't post notes or really offer much support outside of class. All of the exams and homeworks are primarily multiple choice with not-so-straightforward questions. I would take him again for his lectures but likely at the expense of my GPA.
Test is on wording, tricky. Even you know whats the materials, you still get the wrong answer. The thickest notes I have ever taken.

Many HW and exam questions are designed to trick you on wording and don't test understanding of theory behind concepts. Some questions are vague and confusing. In class lectures / examples often did not line up with hw and exam questions whatsoever. Teaches out of the book which explains things much clearer. Very stringent and nitpicky grader.
His class is very clear and logical with clear and useful notes on the board. He is knowledgable and kind.

One of the worst Prof ever. No organization at all. Does not realize that some student need more help and econ is not everyone's major. Helpful after class but horrible at explaining the concepts. No Textbook use, Mostly dependent on Published Article that he published.  Overall horrible teaching and  shear waste of my time. Learnt nothing.

He is by far the worst prof. of econ. at RIT. He is what you call " the know it all guy" even though he doesn't . Extremely political and only thinks about his ranking and position. No structured teaching and lack of organization. He does not realize that some students need more help than others. Highly disappointed with his approach.

Very difficult class, lots of material. Doesn't use textbook, teaches you from his notes. Fantastic professor, but isn't easy. Poses challenging questions that make you think. Don't be surprised if you come out with a C. One of the hardest Econ classes available, so expect to work.

great professor. I took an International Trade and Finance with him. Very comprehensive. Homeworks are easy. Exam questions are from homework exercises. Piece of Cake. Don't need the book, but it is better to have it and sometimes read it. Highly recommended.

I was a little worried at the start of the year when I saw that Professor Eager had around a 2.0 on ratemyprofessors, but it's very clear he cares a lot about improving himself as a professor. While reaching him outside of class can be tricky due to him being an adjunct professor, the many TAs were always there to help if needed.

Professor Eager helped to make my transition to a college lifestyle much easier. He's extremely well versed in the content the course covers, however that doesn't mean he'll just give you everything for free. In this course, you get out what you put in, but Professor Eager will make sure you do well if you give an honest effort.

The lectures are pretty long, but they're easy to follow along with, and the material is taught really well. Zach is charismatic and knowledgeable, and he, the TAs, and other students in GCIS are helpful and accessible in the discord server. The homework and exams are straightforward and are a pretty reasonable workload overall.

Zach is a great professor who knows what he's talking about. Quizzes, problem sets, and a few other things were all done by him live in class and giving everyone a 100%, so like 20-30% of your grade. 2/3 of the midterms are DIFFUCULT and need EXTENSIVE knowledge of the material. Homework is graded generously but sometimes takes hours. Overall good!

Great professor and really cares for his students. He was a bit dry at first with his lectures but as the semester went on they got much better and the classroom was a much more fun environment. He does a lot to try and help his students succeed but the class structure itself feels as though it works against him. Would highly recommend him though.

He was the professor who made me realize that computer science isn't for me, so I thank him for that. He quickly goes through stuff, which is both a blessing and a curse. His lectures tend to be pretty dry but go and take notes or you won't pass.

His lectures were the most boring part of my semester, which is rough when I'm a computer science major. He would read the notes that a different professor created, seemingly having not read over them beforehand, and consistently ask for help from the class about topics we were learning about. I got more from recitation than from his lectures.
Great teacher and great class

GCIS-123 is a tough course for those with not a lot of coding experience, it's a lot of work and meant to weed out students. With that, professor Andreotta is a really chill guy and I enjoyed his lectures. He is a solid professor that likes when his students participate and speak up about the material, he is always willing to help out.
nice class i had with this guy

Great teacher.  Makes class fun and easy.  I think I finished this course with a 120 average.  If you do the work you will get an A, but it's not difficult or extensive so getting the A isn't hard.  Gives tons of extra credit worth lots of points, hence the 120 average.

Keith genuinely cares about his students and their success. He is clear about expectations and does not assign a lot of work. The tests are tricky, so reading the textbook is a must. Overall, the class is very reasonable and with regular attendance and reading, you should get an A.

In class he's helpful, he knows what he's talking about and he'll answer your questions well but he's a lot less helpful during office hours or at the least less polite. If you have a question in class, go ahead and ask it but for the assignments, get help from a friend or someone else first.

He knows C++ and expects you to know it too. If you have a general understanding you will do okay. His tests aren't the easiest but he curves a little. Asking him for help results in him either making you wish you didn't ask or becoming more confused.

If you're on top of things with comp sci he's a great choice. The assignments are going to be the same as any other CS4 class. The difference is that in lecture he'll describe things more technically than other professors. He knows his stuff. To keep up with the explanations you'll want to read the textbook for sure, you'll get a lot out of it.

Matt Healy is the best teacher I've had for the CS intro sequence. His knowledge of C++ is incredible, to the point where he's able to field---and maybe even expecting---any question about the language, no matter how complex or obscure. To top it all off, he's an excellent lecturer with a very interactive approach to demonstrations. Take his class!

When you are relatively new to programming, it is difficult to understand why healy would expect you to write code as if you had been in the industry for 20 years. Beware of this teach... person who tries to teach. He will insult you, trod on you, make you feel like trash, and then give you a poor grade no matter what. BEWARE

VERY rude at times. Makes you not want to go see him for help cuz he always makes you feel dumb and doesn't seem to care. Strict grader, expects you to remember every slide in the powerpoint for an exam, even if he spent 5 min explaining a topic. Every time he helped me outside of lecture he was very rude. He also thinks he's funny but he isn't.

Matt is quite a character. His lectures are corny and funny, he is the most interesting CS teacher I've had. He is a tough grader and expects you to know your stuff. If your an easy going student you wont have a problem, but i dont recommend asking about your grade on anything, he can be a little moody. he knows his stuff. Overall hes a good prof.

Harshest grader I've had yet, and is a "jerk" (replace that with a 'curse' word). Don't take this guy, he'll deduct points from anything just for fun. Plus he's the kind of person who tries very hard to be funny, and never comes close. Not the funny kind either, the annoying like, "please shut up," kind.

A part-time teacher, works parttime or fulltime in the software biz, and has two kids thus his grading seems rushed/harsh/mostly uncommented, and his hours are limited. He's not boring cause most of the time he's in someone's face waiting for them to give a wrong answer. If you must take him, make sure you know other people who know your class.

Adjunct, but definitely knows the material (CS4). A good teacher for somebody who's interested in a more in-depth coverage (office hours good too). Bad for people that don't like to pretend they're a block of memory as a concept illustration.
Matt keeps class fun and entertaining. He really knows his stuff. But he's a pretty hard grader and if you ask him for help one-on-one he's pretty harsh.

Healy is a no-nonsense, hilarious professor; class is never a bore. He tends to grade strictly, emphasizing efficiency, but he is fair. Though he may be tough, when you complete his class you will have learned a lot and will be much better prepared for upcoming CS classes. I would absolutely recommend him to anyone who wants to work and succeed.

Wow the other ratings are all wrong. He is the 2nd best cs prof. I have had so far. As a hint, the good cs prof's always wear shorts/sandals, thr great ones take off the sandals while teaching. (Phill White does too, and he's the best)

TERRIBLE TERRIBLE TERRIBLE!!! He is very knowledgable in Computer Science and C++ but he is rediculously harsh.  Very quick to take off points without even looking at content.  Often interrupts when you ask a question and provides an unrelated answer.
Very strict grader, knocks off points for everything he possibly can. Tests pretty hard. not a professor, hes a guy with a job that teaches at night for some extra bucks. avoid if possible

Not the easiest teacher, but he knows how to get you to understand material with little out of class work on your part.  He says "um..." REALLY REALLY LOUDLY whenever he's between thoughts.  Knows his stuff, if your projects follow the directions, you'll ace the class.

Matt is a really good teacher.  It's true that he can be a hard grader, but he also makes sure you know what's going on in the class, considering what you're learning will be used throughout the rest of your degree.  He can be pretty funny and is willing to help you as long as you if you need further assistance.
A very harsh grader. He will not go easy on you. His classes do not cover everything that is on the test. DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY.
Matt is a great professor, but is an amazingly hard grader.  You'll learn a lot in his class, but you'll need to work your a** off.

An ok guy, funny but seemed to get confused at a lot of questions.  Gets a lot of things wrong on tests and has to correct them, but still grades pretty harsh.  Not terrible, but not too great either.

Hard grader, hard tests, but if you are serious about being a CS major, and actually accomplishing things that are ona  higher standard that a chat program this is the guy to take. He knows his stuff, he makes a seriously large effort to be available even though he is a part time teacher. Very Very good teacher.

Matt is admittedly a very hard grader. He tends to grade projects no just on correctness, but also efficiency. Certainly not the professor to take if you're a mediocre CS student, but if you're generally interested in CS, he's the guy to have because he puts everything into a real world perspecive.

generally puts down creativity...wants to educate and produce code trolls rather than talented, inspired programmers who might go on to do something useful with their careers.  Does he still do Rocky @ Ridgeway Sat nights?
This guy is the hardest grader i've ever seen.  I submitted a working project and I still ended up with a D.  Go Figure.. Very hard grader on tests.

Okay, you can pretty much never go to his class if you want, he has all his slides on his website, and it's more or less all you need to know.  The guy knows his stuff, but is pretty poor at conveying it.  And if you ask him for help, he is pretty derisiv

This guy should be avoided at all times.He is making extra money talking in his own world and teaching few puppets, ignoring the rest willful students, who are paying $$$ to see his hedious face twice a week. Avoid!!!!!!!!!
No Comments
Avoid like the plague!!
learned comp. science and now taking revenge from humans. be advised.
Maureen is very clear in what she is expecting. Don't skip her class after two absences. If you want a higher grade, participate in the critiques cause that is what saved my semester.

It was during Covid when I took prof Ratkeviciute's online drawing class. All my classmates were all over the world: Turkey, China, India, Korea, while I was in the US. Despite the fact that we were all online - she taught us well, and it felt like a community. We became friends and were happy to meet on campus and I created work I was proud of.

I loved Marika! I think she is an amazing artist and a wonderful teacher. Besides being knowledgeable, she is positive, motivating, and understanding. 

I have learned so much from her! She organized the course so each assignment was harder than the last. Then the final project was a lot of fun- you got to be creative and show off your skills.

I loved Marika. I took Drawing II with her. She created a very positive work environment. She showed me new techniques and advanced my skills. She also stayed after class with me multiple times. I never had a teacher that cared about her students more than Marika does. She was also ALWAYS available to contact via text and email

DO NOT TAKE IF YOU HAVE ANY DRAWING EXPERIENCE! Her own skill level is frankly not high enough to have meaningful advice for higher-level students. Also, assignment requirements are often unclear if not entirely absent. She's flexible with her grading / due dates; and if you're just trying to pass you'll be fine.
It was amazing learning from her, I had a great time and made drawings that I never thought I could do.

Marija did not manage the time for my class well, so our first projects ran way too long and resulted in cramming later on. The timestaking final was completely at-home. She will not say a piece is done, so don't wait for her to say you're done, just move on next class. She cares a LOT about critique participation.

I had her for two semesters and loved it! She's down to earth, makes you feel comfortable, and at the same time pushes you to do your best. I learned a lot! I had an issue that made me miss some classes, but I made up outside of class, and she worked with me. Always responded to emails and texts. She definitely matches the energy you give her!

Marija is a little ridiculous honestly. She never reads your emails and if something happens and you cant make it she pretty much doesnt care. Im behind in my class due to the lack of communication via online. Its not that hard to respond to an email... and if you dont do exactly what she wants you to do she will give another similar project.

She does have an accent, but it's not very difficult to understand. She does get sidetracked, but it's always somewhat relevant to the content. She makes the content accessible for people of all experience levels, and I enjoyed even the most strenuous parts. She definitely matches the energy you give to her, so at least pretend to care!

She's really difficult to understand. She'll stop mid sentence to talk about something completely different and never really finishes a thought. Because of this due dates are really confusing. Sometimes she forgets that something is due and you get an extra week, other times she doesn't tell us when it's due.

This professor does not clearly explain concepts we are trying to learn in class. Though he is available outside of class it is hard to understand concepts when they are not explained differently to the first time. Also beware that the homework problems are quite different to what you will be tested on.
He is a great professor, knows his stuff and gives a lot of credit for homework. just show up for notes and turn the work in ontime and you will be good.

He's my favorite professor here. He really went above and beyond to help me get caught up when I had to miss two weeks of school for a family emergency. He genuinely cares about the work he does and I've never seen a professor as happy as he is. The work in the class can get difficult but hey, it's the major, not  him.
Probably the worst professor at RIT.
He is a nice guy who will help if you ask.  He is always in his office.  Tests and quizs are hard but if you understand the homework you are did then you will pass his tests no problem.

Awesome guy! He does have his quirks, but you will learn a lot. The man lives in his office. I've left the building at 1200 and he was still there. Go to his office if you need help and he will break down so you understand it.
Not doubt, he's weird but he is an awesome teacher. He lives in his office so you can always find him for help

He's quite difficult.  Very inflexible, assigns tons of homework, and gets bent out of shape over stupid things.  He knows what he's teaching pretty well and you will learn if you're ready to break your back for him.
in thi class.. i you wana learn. go to class every day. He gives good notes. def.. recomended for people that wana learn. he is a lil anal.. but great professor. its al lot to learn from him..
Plays favorites which was annoying. Odd sense of humor which was funny in a weird way. Very challenging tests which. Rediculous labs that took so many hours along with the large amount of hw.

This man rocks. He has a doctorate, so you know he knows his****. He's always willing to help, no matter how long it takes. His work can be somewhat tedious, but he's great teacher to have and to learn from. Don't hesitate to choose his courses, if you have the choice.

Very nice professor personality-wise. Willing to give extensions, feedback, and overall help with whatever you need. He's very good at coding and obviously knows what he's doing, although it feels like the rest of the class rarely does. 3-5 hours of homework once or twice a week, plus a semester-long group project at the same time.

He's a great teacher who cares the most about your learning. He will extend your deadlines within reason and would not dock a point as long as you're learning something. His level of detail in his feedback is amazing and very helpful. It's his first time teaching this class. If u really wanna learn- take this class. C# doc is helpful for new things

Although the lectures are sometimes cloudy, he makes it really easy for you to succeed if you put in the time and effort; very helpful is always available to help/answer questions. Homework level is nothing unexpected for college level programming majors. His extraordinary coding expertise is a great resource, learn from him and ask questions!

comment: New to teaching, brilliant at programming. He needs to improve his teaching style but will provide help outside of class when asked or when you submit homework early. Although he assigns lots of homework, they're good for challenging your understanding of the content if not done last-minute. He will prepare you for the future when work gets tough.

comment: Avoid at all costs; unhelpful and expects literally all of your free time to be spent teaching yourself things he should cover in class, while he sits back and gives unhelpful examples and throws the blame back at you for failing to understand the material.

This professor is very knowledgeable and very enthusiastic; however, he expects too much out-of-class time from his students and has a narrow view of how he believes coding should be learned. To put it plainly, he's an extraordinarily experienced programmer, but a mediocre professor. This could be good or bad for you depending on who you are.

This professor likes to give homework every day on topics that we barely go over in class. All of the examples he gives are all from code he's done previously, which in and of itself wouldn't be a problem if he were to give us those full files as well, but he doesn't. He just expects you to be able to copy everything down in less than 5 minutes.

comment: This guy takes forever to grade *anything*, and isn't very helpful in class overall. Do not recommend.

Obviously knows his stuff, but he can't relay it for the life of him. I took a college calc class in HS, got an A+, yet struggled to keep up here. Lecture is way too fast. He did not prepare us for the level of questions on tests. The final exam- oh GOD I only finished half of it. He's helpful with office hours but you have to make time for that.

Very hard to understand, exams are 10 times harder than the examples, we are still learning material while other Math 111 classes have been reviewing for a week, doesn't even give us full explanation of examples, doesn't review some material that is included in our homework. Worst math teacher ever!

Professor Thomas knew a lot about math and number theory but he was very difficult to understand. His lectures were very quick and if you did not pick up the lesson, you were left to fall behind. He is intimidating and does not connect well with students. Tests and quizzes presented questions at a much higher level than lectures and homework.
he was very difficult, and admitted as such. He gave harder questions and examples than other teachers and taught us more, or so he told us

Professor Thomas is a fairly nice guy, but unfortunately a HORRIBLE professor. His tests and quizzes are extremely hard. He is also very intimidating and condescending when it comes to students going to him for help. UNLESS YOU ARE A MATH MAJOR, STAY AWAY.

HORRIBLE!!! His style of teaching is terrible. His examinations are impossible - most students would fail them. He would teach an entire lesson in one class time and expect far more complicated understanding on his homework and tests. He is not helpful - and sometimes condescending.

Though Prof. Thomas is a really intelligent guy, he only teaches material one way.  If you don't get it, there's not much you can do.  Attending office hours helps a lot, however, and this is a must if you want to get a good grade in the class.  Take the time to get to know him, take the time to do the homework, and you should be okay.

Brilliant mathematician, terrible teacher. Can't teach what he knows. Quiz every Friday made up of homework problems copied exactly, but the homework is very difficult. Attending his Office Hours are a MUST to receive a passing grade. He's also a very aggressive person, tends to intimidate students heavily whenever they ask questions.

The only reason I understood anything was because I took calc in high school. He is not a great teacher and cannot explain things clearly. His tests are also pretty hard and he takes questions from the textbook that he never went over in class. The only positive is that he does offer frequent office hours.

Goes way too fast and covers more than necessary! Tests/Quizzes much more difficult than expected. Unless you go to every office hours and spend your free time in the Bates lab, you won't get close to an A.

He understands the material himself, his problem comes from the fact that he hasn't yet found an effective way to impart his knowledge to his students. The homeworks are the quizzes, but the content on them is far more difficult then whats taught in class. Office hours are generally a must if you want to keep a good grade. Exams are quite hard.

This class isn't easy but he will help you if you ask, quiz every Friday and a good amount of studying to be done before every exam. A lot of office hours but still a tough course if you're not a math person

I attended all classes, all review sessions, and frequently went to office hours and I still did not do well. His homework assignments are incredibly hard and the exams even more so. If you aren't great at math, working hard and doing the work isn't going to be enough to get a good grade in this class. The exams are so much harder than expected.
He's a nice guy, but isn't the greatest teacher. When I do understand a concept in class the homework and exams are usually 10 times harder.

Has tons of open office hours, really approachable, but a poor teacher overall.  He isn't clear on most things and falls behind on work often and has to play catch-up at the expense of the student's understanding.  Teach yourself Discrete, then come to class in order to succeed.

Great at teaching. You will learn a lot from him. He will do anything you ask grade-wise like making a test take-home (even the final!), dropping old grades, making questions optional etc. However, don't expect this to make things easy. The take-home tests are extremely hard. It started boringly easy, then he got behind and it got hard.

He is extremely difficult in comparison to all the other Discrete Math for Tech teachers, but he does offer a lot of help and he makes it pretty clear when he explains it during the office hours he offers. You are going to have to work a lot harder than anyone else in the same course with a different professor.

He is a good guy who is easy to get along with and he knows the material. The problem is he is a new teacher and does not know how to pass his knowledge on to the students. I would avoid this teacher if you can. To pass his class you need to get lots of out of class help. HE IS A VERY DIFFICULT TEACHER!!
Great guy, but he is an extremely challenging professor. Course work is very difficult.

Professor Thomas is a great guy, but not a great teacher. I took his discrete Math for Tech 1, and I was unable to grasp anything throughout the semester. He does not give enough examples during class. He also give you homework that goes WAY beyond what he teaches you. He is one of those teachers where you have to learn the material yourself.

Overall solid professor but lecture drags for much of the class. Current events presentations are usually the easiest part of class to pay attention to. Tests are pretty hard and not based on a lot of in class content, more based off textbook content and can be confusing at times. Very important to heavily study for this class.

He's very nice but don't expect to learn anything in class, very boring. The current events presentation and critical thinking papers were the easiest part of the class. Exams have nothing to do with what was taught and you have to teach yourself.

352 is a writing intensive course so we have a silly paper for every chapter which sucks. He's amazing at explaining things, and will repeat things no questions asked. very positive and encouraging teacher. Exams are somewhat difficult but if you attend class and do your hws you should be fine. My favorite finance professor by far.

Had us write a paper before started each chapter, probably wrote 13 papers just that. 2 other longer papers were assigned, 4 exams, and a final. And a current events presentation. Lots of work, he's a nice guy though

He seemed to focus on the writing-intensive aspect of the class more than the actual finance. Tests are difficult and often times hw and lectures are dry and unrelated to each other. Weekly essay prompts were not deep enough to write his required page amount. The final exam was short, very difficult, and not structured like any of his other exams.

Took this for an easy A and was kind of blown away by how harsh the grading was. Still managed an A and it is a very simply class (for reference I finished almost all the work I had to do by early November). All I can say is he is a tough grader but not a bad dude. I emailed him for how to get my grade up and he just said write more so.

He is a nice professor and he did alright with the lecture. However, his exams is difficult. He provided the study guides but it doesn't really help and very few from the study guide applied to the exam. I suggest not to take his class even if it is necessary.
Do not take this professor. I'm warning you it won't be fun. If it's a required class that you have to take. Don't take this class. pick a different professor or wait to take FINC 220 next semester.

Honestly I am sad to see that professor Curran has low reviews. I had him during the semester COVID hit and he transitioned to online learning better than anyone else. You have to care about finance and do the work for his class but he really is an excellent professor. His class is not easy but if you participate in class it helps a lot.

If you like to read textbook and PowerPoint, then this class is for you. He is expert in his field, finance, but not good in explain it to students. No hand-out for classes, which is difficult thing to take Accounting and Finance subject. Office hour is no more than, "You got it"!

comment: His speech is not related to the homework and exams at all. I agree he is an amateur, or he just doesn't know how to teach. You need to learn yourself, unless you will be failed in this class. Many in my class are shocked when they see the exams. I can't imagine an exam which only includes multiple choices would be nothing related to his lecture

A really nice guy, 3 exams and a final. Read the textbook and you will be good. Exams are based on the slideshows and the textbook. He really knows lots of finance things and explains well. He made me determine that it is worthwhile to choose finance as my major.

This guy is a total amateur. Absolutely no business teaching a college course. Gives horrible/if any preparation for exams. Class AVG was less than 70%. Uses textbook powerpoints and gives NO practice problem handouts. Worst professor I have ever had. NOT helpful in office hours. AVOID JOHN CURRAN AT ALL COSTS.

comment: Liza is a great person. She wasn't the best professor, but was very open to critique and asked us all how she could be better, which I know she took to heart. She also cared about all of us very much, which created a comfortable class environment for everyone.

From what I can recall, she taught very clearly and pays extremely close attention to her students. Material was conveyed clearly and easy to understand. This instructor is a person that deeply cares for her students and for education in the field she teaches.
Wonderful teacher, you can tell she cares very deeply about each and every student, and tries to get you outside your creative comfort zone. It's a great foundation course for designers!

There aren't too many projects in this class and she is very supportive of different ideas everyone has. Instead the 4 projects span the course of the semester with the last one being the final. Once you fall into the rhythm of the class its fairly simple to navigate.

Every single project we did, we were FORCED to use adobe photoshop and illustrate, which I hated. Not only is adobe EXPENSIVE, they SUCK. Microsoft paint is easier to use. If she found out we didn't do the project with adobe she would take points off. The only thing I learned from this class was how to use other apps without her finding out.
I like how the professor encourages everyone to have a group critique and always make ways to improve. She gives time to finish projects. Regular check-ins are a must.
She's always willing to help outside of class and really does care about her students. You'll definitely learn something from her!

Liza was a great professor who gave me a solid foundation in design, but above all she was caring and compassionate, something which cannot be said for more professors. She gave tough critiques, which I appreciated because I always tried to make my work better.

It is without a doubt that Liza is a very caring professor, however her teaching methodologies don't seem to be fully developed, especially with the lack of knowledge of the software. As a result, I do not believe that she sets good foundations for beginning designers. She is also always talking about the startup that she recruits students for.

Liza is a good professor that tends to put a lot of thought into how students are doing on top of giving easy to understand assignments. As long as you show up to class and put some effort into the work you do, you should be fine taking the course.

Shes a very nice and caring professor who like group feedback an discussions during critiques. Although the grading criteria/directions are sometimes a bit unclear, as long as you ask ahead of time (in class) she should be able to clear up a misunderstanding. Just make sure to completer your work and do it on time and you should have no problems.

Liza is a great professor. The feedback on projects and assignments were specific and helped me become a stronger designer. Above all, Liza genuinely cares about her students. She's kind and attentive, while creating a positive, safe learning environment in the class.

She's a very kind and understanding professor and always cares a lot about the students' wellbeing. I loved having class with her, and her feedback on projects was always clear and helpful. Grading can be a little tough, but you can always ask for feedback before handing in a project to see where you can improve.

Really sweet and nice professor, she's always open to discussing classwork and such and she clearly wants to see you succeed. She's very open to getting creative with projects but having some more focus on design elements and principles could've helped more during the course. She has a good balance when it comes to projects and exercises too!

She's very nice and clearly cares about her students, but man she is not a good teacher. Her grading criteria aren't very clear, and when I asked for feedback she didn't focus on my work's design principles as much as its "story." This class might be good for someone who's got background in design, but as a computing student I struggled.

Probably one of the the best Chem teachers at RIT. Orgo is VERY hard but she did an excellent job teaching it. The course is very exam heavy (both Orgo 1 and 2) exams worth 70% of the grade. Be prepared to spend at least 1-2 hours a day studying the mechanisms. Tests were all MPC with 3 extra bonus questions. 4 exams total with optional final

I know its Orgo and its supposed to be difficult but the exams make up 70% of your grade and she makes them really hard. I would say she was a pretty good teacher but she just makes the exams very difficult, even when you study super hard her exams will always mess you up. If you take her Orgo class make sure you master stereochemistry!

Your grade is only based on exams and homework. You really have to know the material to do well on exams. Homework can take a while and the hw program is finicky at times. You have to put in the work to succeed. Dr. G can make class entertaining!

Most encouraging chem prof I've had. Will answer questions outside of class & offers help sessions for extra credit, as well as a bonus final exam. VERY exam heavy, but you can pass as long as you do well on 1-2 exams. Some online homework due every few weeks. My grade was due to my lack of understanding of chemistry in general, but Dr. G is great!

She has been one of the best chemistry professors I've had at RIT. Great at explaining concepts in lecture and is very easy to reach out to. Gives a bonus final and extra credit for HW. GOh sessions were very helpful for questions/doing work. Provides lots of supplementary resources (practice quizzes, lecture videos, notes templates)

Absolutely wonderful. She is the person you want to teach you OChem. Very kind, approachable, and her lectures are never dry. OChem is a tough class, however she provides a lot of study material, as well as study sessions and will even meet with you one-on-one if you ask. She provides extra credit for the study sessions and a bonus final.

Dr G is friendly, a great teacher, and wants her students to succeed. All interactions with her have been helpful and encouraging. Her lectures make sense, she encourages you to go to help sessions, and offers extra credit when it comes to going to them. If i could have every class with her, I would.

Dr. G is a great OChem professor. It's a difficult topic but she explains it well and provides lots of resources for extra practice. It's usually a big lecture, but she wants you to succeed. Dr. Tusch is also a good option for OChem, if you're deciding between the two, Dr. T usually has 3 exams + final, and Dr. G tends to have 4 exams + a final.

I struggle a lot in chem but Goudreau is the best I've had. So kind and gives you every opportunity to do well. Tutoring, practice problems and quizzes, work sessions, office hours-- so many resources are invested in students. I relied a lot on her recorded lectures. She even has classes just for questions before exams. Take her class if you can!!!

Dr. G is a wonderful professor who cares about her students and their success. Organic Chemistry is a very difficult course path, but she is able to break it down as much as possible. Do the homework, practice with her examples, and go to the GOh (study) sessions and you will do wonderfully.

She's nice and good at explaining difficult concepts. Grading is lenient as she drops three questions per exam and there's a bonus final just to boost your grade. Lectures are helpful but you can just teach yourself the material with the flipped videos and the textbook. Only thing was that the Wiley HW was not representative of the exams at all.

I have mixed feeling about professor G. If you really struggle with chemistry she isn't very helpful and the GOH sessions can sometimes make you even more confused because they are run by her past students and she isn't always there. It seemed like half of the time the people in the GOH sessions didn't even know what they were talking about.

AMAZING professor. I was scared going into Organic Chemistry I but I finished with an A and got a 100 on multiple exams. The class is designed to see you succeed, but you HAVE to practice and put the work in. Go to the GOH sessions for help/practice, do practice problems, study for the exams, and you will do fine.

It doesn't get much better than Dr. G . She really puts in the work to make sure that students understand lecture material. She organizes Goh sessions for extra help. Lecture material is tough but doing well in the class is super doable if you study and do the practice problems. Dr. G knows her stuff and is there to help you succeed.

Professor Goudreau is the best ORGO teacher. She is very excited to teach the material and makes it easy to understand. class is graded on test and homework only. however, the tests are not that bad if you put in the effort. I am not close to a perfect student, I skipped class A LOT and still managed to do well with all the resources supplied.

Professor Goudreau is a great professor for a tough subject like Organic Chemistry. The material is definitely difficult to understand at times, but she's willing to meet with you outside of class and help you with any material you're stuck on. Her lectures are also very organized and informative, and she has online versions of the lectures too.

Professor Goudreau is very nice and easy to talk to. I had her during COVID so the class was entirely online. This made lectures rather boring and hard to get through, though it was obvious that she tried to make them as entertaining as possible. The class is pretty easy, if you just watch the lectures and do the homework you'll ace the exams.

Super helpful when it comes to explaining things however, your grade is basically dependent on your test grades. If you don't do well with tests, at least they're multiple choice. Class material is difficult so good luck!

Dr. G. is such a lovely person and a really great teacher. Orgo tests were easy considering the subject matter (you do have to learn the material for sure though). She will definitely help you at any time. She gives lots of opportunities for you to get help and also to raise your grade (X-credit) etc. throughout the semester. Absolutely rec.

I SWEAR DR GOUDREAU IS THE NICEST PROFESSOR EVER, SUPER APPROACHABLE AND NICE AND FRIENDLY. IM NOT JUST SAYING THIS BC I GOT AN "A" IN THE COURSE, BUT ALSO SHE IS LITERALLY THE BEST AT TEACHING, I ACTUALLY UNDERSTAND ORGO BECAUSE OF HER. SHE MADE RXN MECHANISMS 1-2 ADDITIONS SEEM SO EASY TO DO, AND THEY ARE!! I WOULD DEFF RECCOMEND HER FOR ORGO 2

ORGO 2 with dr. goudreau is way too easy. I took it with her for fall 2019 and it is a joke cuz her lectures are very simple and I got an A in the course. There are 3 exams throughout the semester and are hilariously way too easy and my lowest test grade was a 96, I got 100 on the other too. I also got a 100 on the final and got a 98 on course
Far too easy. You will not develop as a scientist.

Dr. goodreau is Mrs. honey from Matilda. She is a gem and a gift from God. I really struggled in organic chemistry in the begginining but with her help, care, and motivation of me and every student she has, I didnt only pass but I got an A, A far cry from the 60 I received on the first exam. She motivated and inspired me to work harder than ever.

Dr. Goudreau was amazing for Organic I lab. She uses her ReActivities lab workbook for this class and it outlines all of the important introductory steps for an organic chemist's lab. If you put in the work and ask her questions, you will learn and excel in the class and in chemistry.

Best professor ever, so inspirational and amazing lectures, the notes-style for this course is really useful, helpful office hours, she literally inspired multiple people to switch majors because of how well she taught. Made me appreciate chemistry a lot more, and I looked forward to coming to class everyday, she's really the greatest

Her Organic class is by no means easy, but she is extremely accessible if you need help. She obviously enjoys the content and tries to make it relate able. Grades are 80% tests and 20% HW, and the content builds on itself so be sure to be sure to start studying early. She grades best 30/33 so that helps a little with the grades. I'd recommend her.

To get the absolute best experience in this class, read the textbook ahead of time. The book she uses is amazing and easy to read. Her lectures are like a crystal clear summary of the chapters, so sometimes she has to go a little fast to cover everything. However, she's extremely helpful in office hours and genuinely wants to help.

I really liked Dr. Goudreau. She explains things pretty well. Orgo is the worst class I've ever taken and she made it a little more bearable. Final exam was extra credit. Only regret is that I didn't pay attention more in class.

Dr. Goudreau is amazing!!!! I wish she was teaching Organic Chem 2! Her notes are amazing, she is lovely! I was so scared of organic chem but she made me confident. There is plenty of opportunity for extra credit! Go to class and pay attention, and you will pass with an A.

comment: I had Dr. Goudreau for Advanced Orgo and it was the best class I took at RIT. The exams are all take home and open notes, so as long as you pay attention in class and take good notes you'll do fine.

Dr. Goudreau is a great professor.  She can take the complicated topics of Organic II and explain them in an easily understood manner.  She has multitudes of memorization techniques and posts fill-in the blank notes for her students to follow along with.

She is an amazing professor; she really knows how to teach and makes this dense class seem easy. All tests are multiple choice where 30/33 is a 100%. Additionally, the final is all bonus and she doesn't do minuses on grades! Go to class, take good notes, do the homework, maybe go to a few workshops, and you'll do fine.

Great lecturer and understandable. However, there is no way to get feedback in this course. I know it is a large class, but I felt uncomfortable going to extra help because she'd say things like "So many people get this wrong, lol, that's cute" ...I made the mistakes she was mocking.. So I felt really dumb in this class. Must self-teach. Practice!!

Dr. Goudreau is amazing: 350 characters is not enough to describe how much I respect and look up to her. She explains orgo concepts so clearly and easily that I can only marvel at her intelligence. Needless to say, you shouldn't go in expecting an A, because you still need to work for it, just like any other class.

He knows how to run an online course, very knowledgeable. I enjoyed the first module more than the second. Grading is based on several quizzes and two tests and all are open book and open notes but time limited.

Tough material, was pretty much the only useful analytics class I took at Saunders. Almost felt like this one class surveyed all 11 analytics techniques that were 6 different classes. He was very open, and blunt. Very accessible outside office hours for me and others. Very industry relevant which was a huge surprise
Great teacher, best online class I have ever taken. Even with 38 people the class was managed really well. Liked that he didnt take any crap from anyone.

Wonderful guy. I enjoyed talking to
him during office hours even though it was online. Online asynchronous class could be daunting but he made it close to how it felt to be in an online class. Very insightful and extremely helpful. Take him and ask him questions that you want answered. He is blunt and very honest and you get the truth.

Excellent professor , I took three graduate courses with Raj and I have to say i took the courses more for him rather than the subject. With each class Raj made me enjoy the subject and increased my interest in it. I learned a lot and he even helped me and a few others outside class to handle interviews during the pandemic. Great guy very relatable

Amazing lectures period. 2 hours went by like nothing and the dicussions in class were fantastic. Just take the class. You will learn a lot, probably laugh a little while you are at it. Very connected to industry.

Every class is 2 hours of lecture, a timed assignment, THEN a (HARD) quiz. Professor as an enormous ego, doesn't care about his students, and has inconsistent grading criteria.
