comment: I took Data Management over the summer and I learned so much. His recorded lectures are great and engaging. I loved learning MySql and have a new found interest in scripting languages that I never thought I would have. Great professor all around!

I took database with him. The others are right in saying that he is super smart. Probably the most smart guy in Saunders. Take him but know that he works you hard. Gives a lot of leads for jobs and also gigs if you ask him. Even if it was online I felt like he was in front of me.
Tough but valuable classes, one of the smartest professors I have ever had
Best professor I have met at R.I.T.

Tough class but Raj made three hours go by like it was a few minuets. He is a tough grader not in a picky kind of way but in that he has high expectations. Hes hilarious in person and talks real fast. Keep up in class every week, no makeups
Fantastic class - all around. I took the graduate flavor of the analytics class and it was tough. Raj always stayed back to explain more after a night class. Take it.

Literally an award winning professor. Raj's class is the only relevant class in the whole new media program. His examples are relevant and he is current, no textbook in any of his classes ever. He really cares for the students.

Amazing class, he is the real deal. Clear class organization with every grade criteria laid out. He is so passionate that you feel energized. This was my third class with Raj. Just take whatever he teaches.

I was lucky to have Raj for a professor before he took his sabbatical. Every word that my friends told me about him was true. Classes were so great I looked forward to going to class on nice spring days. Conversations with him are so inspirational, great guy overall.

Hands down the best professor at Saunders. He is awesome, lectures are fun, applied work is great and even got me coding by week 7. Only useful class in the new media major. Register early, his classes fill out in minutes
Raj is da man.  Learnt more than any other class so far. Also got a couple of google certifications. Also great class for resume building. Just lighten up on the attendance
Massive workload but overall worth it. Learned more than any other class. Ettlie and Murthy will work you to death but you somehow enjoy it.
I would take hsi class just to listen to the guy, lots of work but fair. If you ever read this, stay cool raj, no texts evar and rock on.

Raj was fantastic.  The class requires a large time commitment but he is the best professor I had in the school.  Lectures are engaging. Raj brings great perspective and real world application to class.
Fantastic Professor. Engaging and relevant. Great, well executed lectures.
His real world knowledge and examples really make class worth  going to. Raj is energetic and animated, best grad class to date.
I fought to get into this class. Worth every moment. Only class I wished was actually longer. Now i work SEO and SEM for a living and loving it. Get in early.

One word , AWESOME ! Highly engaging class, best learning environment, extremely helpful and insightful, astute industry observation, practical and contemporary knowledge ! Best professor so far I have had at Saunders !!
Deserves a 10, engaging and kept me awake the entire quarter in a night class after work. Be prepared to work hard though.

Aweosme, just awesome. SEMA was really the only useful class at saunders. Was sick of writing useless 40-80 page marketing business plans filled with bs for 4 years. I had to take this class for my major and what a difference. Raj is a stand up guy, he practices what he teaches. Take him before he stops teaching the class or leaves RIT.

This guy was an amazing teacher. A lot of class discussion and a TON of practical application. Group project was challenging, get yourself a good team and spend time on it. Raj is overall a good guy. Take his classes.
I changed my major to marketing after this class. He is possibly the best teacher in my 2 years here. If he teaches it just take it
Marketing 001. Good teacher. Easy if you put in a fair amount of work. Take him he is pretty funny

Awesome class, Cool professor who crams in so much work during the 10 weeks. 4 assignments 1 video 1 research paper that sucked 1 real client consulting project that rocked and 5 quizzes. No textbook No busy work and you make a website using wordpress. Register for his class today.

Great professor really knows his stuff. You need to go see him early an often. Tough tough class I almost dropped but stucked it out. You realize a lot of the potential of the information in the class well after the class is over.

This professor definitely knows his stuff. However, he assigns way too many assignments and projects on top of two big papers/projects and gives you too little time to complete. He also seems to play favorites with students and won't give you the time of day if you're not one of them.
Possibly one of the most work in one class that I've ever taken.

the business school seems to hire the good guys. Intense 10 weeks, expect no life whatsoever during that time, Raj Murthy will work you to death. He is very helpful and very intelligent. Some  review lectures were boring but from week 3 class was great.
Simply wonderful proffesser. A real exception at RIT. He changes your whole view of business and marketing. I loved this class. Watch out for his strict email policy.

This is was one tough class and this guy is a tough grader. No textbook even. I know several students who did not do well in my group. I learned many things and I made a website which I liked but way too much work for 4 elective credits.

Fantastc prof. Very passionate, just one of the very few classes i took that I can use. No textbook policy is great. Very applied and you need to make your own website. Mandatory attendance sucked but you need to be on top of things for this class.

He is brilliant and changed my interest in internet marketing. I am not a mktg major and dont want to be one but he made me realize the importance of learning business skills. Tough but very fair grader, gives you tons of comments. Very helpful if you go see him. Class needs a research paper.

He's a good marketing teacher.  He has very interesting information, does not bore you with information (he even showed us a powerpoint on "how to make good powerpoints") He knows his technology and brands. His exams aren't too hard, his projects and assignments are reasonable.

Had for Needs Assessment ... a quick look at the Needs Assessment wiki page will reveal a vast world of things we never learned about.  Does things his way, and there's no textbook.  He's a nice guy who should have stayed in the business world.  Proceed at your own risk.
well, very good grader and he comes up many activities for us to learned.

Liz is the best professor I've ever had at RIT. Not only does she care about her students, but she will go out of her way to make sure you do well in your classes as well as doing well in your personal life. Liz has a wealth of knowledge and loves to share with eager students.
Great professor. Super enthusiastic and very supportive of students. Assigns reasonable amount of work.

Liz is a Grad student and an amazing teacher who understands what its like to be in a students shoes, I never felt stressed by her class but still learned an incredible amount! She cares a lot and is there for you 100% of the way.

Great prof, really cool project ($10 Business Challenge), and very good at getting the best from his students. However, he grades inconsistently. Several peers and I made the same mistake on a project, only I lost points for it. Evidently he 'expected more from me.' Besides that, he's great.

Great individual, with a good sense of humor. Not very knowledgable, can be unclear at times and contradict himself in class. Will negotiate quiz questions that the class gets wrong. Exams are very difficult, study hard and pay attention in class-he gives hints. Very strict and demands respect which is annoying. Overall, ok

I loved him as a professor. He really encourages group discussion and jokes around alot. He really wants you to understand the material. You can argue back points on online quizzes. I thought his tests were pretty easy, but alot of people had trouble with it. He uses real life examples that make it easier to grasp the material.

I never officially had him in a class, however he has stepped in on my highschool class. and i found he is very helpful. he is tough however he took the time to explain about his business and how we can better ourselves to make a successful business venture.

If your attending college to learn, and better yourself take this teacher his are difficult but he pushes you, and one of the few teachers that actually care that you learn and understand his subject.

He make you learn his stuff real good, or you wont pass the class. Usually 85% of students fail the first test, because students don't know what to expect on those essay exams, which are often confusing and tricky. I am usually an A student, but in his class I would be happy to get a C. I am so glad this quarter is over.

One of the best professors I've ever had. This course would be bland if it were taught by someone else. Class discussions are exciting, even for 8 AM, and the topics are relatable to every day life. Exams are NOT easy, so it's advisable to attend class. He will tell you that statistically students don't do well on the first exam. It's TRUE.

Just read the slides and focus on what he emphasizes on them and you should do well on his essay style exams which have like 8 questions and you get to choose like 6. He also grades real easily on projects, quizzes are open book, open partner online, and there's lots of extra credit so its pretty easy to get an A if you play your cards right.

I was not impressed with his class teaching. I didn't understand what exactly he expected on his essay-format exams. I asked him for help outside the classroom but he didn't help me at all. I was quite disappointed in him. He doesn't seem to care about his students as much as he does about his own business.
Needs to realize that not everybody is as obsessed with the subject as he is. Doesn't always come off as genuine in lectures. Sets very high standards considering the course material.

GREAT professor! Ties in his real-world activities/experiences with lecture material. Interesting to listen to and speak with. GREAT take-aways! Attendance is optional, but you should go if you want to do well on exams. No required textbook. Very practical and fair. RIT could use more professors like Dr. Smith!!!

Great teachers, a four hour night class flys by. He hints at test questions, you don't have to go to class but should if you want an A. Everyone does well on projects, and he is really nice, fuunny and super cute!

Class isn't mandatory but if you want any chance of doing well in class you must go. Tests are esay format and you and you must be able to apply the information you learn in class. If you pay attention he makes hits about the information that will be on the test so you'll know what to study. The test format ensures you actually know the information
If you do everything he tells you to, expect to get a A. He gives essay questions, but as long as you study what he specifically tells you to study on the slides, you shouldnt have a problem.

Makes the class interesting and enjoyable. Projects/games in class are kinda fun and you get bonus points for coming out on top. Only uses the text for weekly quizzes, which are straight from the book, word-for-word. Not the easiest exams unless you really study, but you'll get a lot from the lectures regardless.
He's horrible instructor be away from his courses.

Knows his stuff.  Not interested n coddling "You pay close to $40,000 to be here so I better give you something".  Constantly looks for ways to bring the dry material to life.  Down to earth approach.
Great teacher. I have him at 8am and he manages to keep me awake and interested. He knows his material and presents it well. I recommend him.
I had him for both organizational behavior and leadership in orgs and he is great. Just study exactly what he tells you to and you'll be fine.

We loved Professor Smith but we like to call him Dell. He was amazing. He was our world. He allowed us to grow not only academically but also individually. We are ever greatful to him. Thank You so much Professor Smith. And not to mention, I never had difficulty paying attention.

I don't care what anyone else said! He's a great professor. Yes, the tests are hard, but I really learned a lot because I had to study so much for them. He gives out a looottt of bonus points, so participate and you will do well. Don't miss class, and take good notes.

Exams are all essay, but they only relate to small portions of what he talks about in class or what's in the book. He won't tell you much before an exam and then expects you to know so much about EVERY CONCEPT that you could write an essay on it. He grades extremely unfairly!

Despite the reviews, D. Smith is a great professor. A lot of students in the class did have trouble with the tests...but he GAVE the test questions for each test. At the end of the quarter I had about 107. He gives LOTS of bonus points. I got 100 on 3/4 tests and got a 93 on the third. Go to class, take notes, and you'll do fine.

The grades on his exams are not about what you know but how your word it. Not a fair assessment and very objective. I am an A student but am lucky to get a C in his class. Seems like a nice guy in class but very unapproachable outside of class. Makes you feel like you're rushing him and he doesn't seem interested in what you have to say. Avoid him
Great teacher. Really cared that students learn the subject. Very encouraging of discussion and opinions. Tests are very hard though...

Class had the mandatory boring parts, but Dr Smith tried to make it less so with activities. Tests were easy, but I usually study for a couple of hours. It also helps to have good exam skills: ANSWER WHAT THE QUESTION IS ASKING FOR. To try it out, I flat out didn't study for the final, and got a 50% (needed 36% for an A).

Horrible teacher. Worst exam I have ever taken. Exams consist of nine essay questions. Grades extremely harsh. Class average is currently a 66%. I have been an A student for the last 3 years, until I had this guy. Constantly brags about students complaining about him and shows disrespect for RIT. WORST TEACHER I have ever had! Avoid this guy.

This is a class where the teacher grades an exam base on what he is looking for. If you are not good with written exams, then don't take the class. The teacher claim that this was the easiest class to take, but when if u take the class online, u would have a better chance of passing the class.
horrible teacher who doesn't know how to teach at all. He grades his tests extremely unfair, and never listen to students' complains. "I am the expert right here you know."
He tries his best to be fair and he takes constructive criticism well.  It seems like he still has to learn how to teach and be consistent.,

Literally one of the best professors. She is extremely caring, flexible, and easy going. If you want an easy A, just get your work done, and try your absolute best! She will help you and is extremely understanding

Professor Larizza is an old school professor. His lectures are on transparencies but, they contain current information regarding energy and the environment. Your grade is based on a midterm and a final exam, so if you don't pay attention during class then you won't have the information. Study guides are given and tests are straightforward.

comment: Here is the grade weighting breakdown : Midterm 39%, Final 55%, Attendance 6%. If you do poorly on an exam you're out of luck. Very long and dry lectures. No study materials. Not a fan.

The lectures are fairly dull, but for such a boring teaching style I have to say I was very interested in his class.  Since the switch to semesters there is no longer an essay, just a midterm and a final.  Take these tests seriously and study what he tells you too, since they are the only grades.  I just narrowly missed an A, shouldve studies more.

This guy is boring as hell, uses an overhead projector, and puts everyone to sleep.  On the plus side though, all notes are handed out in packets, and he gives easy tests.  The only grades are midterm, final, and an essay, which also may appeal to some.
Material is frequently outdated and presented as an OVERHEAD. seriously?

wow this guy isnt audible past the first row. He speaks in a single tone which makes the most interesting topics boring. His tests are multiple choice and very short answer which are pretty difficult, but manageable. Do not recommend unless you are as boring as this guy

Drones on and on. Falling asleep is inevitable. Even browsing the internet it is so difficult to even maintain alertness. His voice is just so... monotonous. He also manages to make it seem entirely reasonable to talk to yourself, as he constantly does this. Asking rhetorical questions that he answers to himself. Do not recommend.

Class is all lectures. His words make a lot of sense, but his slides are very dense and formal, and only really helpful for reviewing material, not learning it. His exams are very fair and he provides ample practice exams for review. You will not regret taking him, since he does a quite solid job at making discrete math understandable.

If you can get into Towsley's class, do it. Discrete math is a pretty hard topic, but his lectures made almost everything much easier to understand. His notes and slides are a lot harder to understand just by reading them, so coming to class definitely matters. His exams are totally fair, and he'll even give you the answers to the hard questions.
Dr. Towsley is a very clear lecturer and will help if questions are asked. His notes style may be hard for some, but he will clarify when needed, gives plenty of information.

Fast pace, will be on the next question before your done writing down the current equation, no time to ask questions. Doesn't explain well, just does the problem. Already took calc in HS and was confused with his teaching, adds parts not needed. Simple questions to learn from, hard on the test. No calculators allowed in this class.

Dr. Towsley is a great math professor. He is very direct and clear on what he teaches, making sure to show definitions of everything, as well as the reason behind how and why things in math works. You should show up to his classes, there are quizzes every 2nd class.

Clear explanations but lectures can drone on a little. Most exam questions resemble in-class examples. Felt to me like grading criteria was a little elusive for proofs and such. This class feels easy initially but ramps up. 

Caveat: I didn't attend lectures as often as I should have.

Genuinely the easiest math class I've taken at RIT, in part because of Towsley. He follows a very simple (but effective) formula: Slideshow lectures with examples, quizzes every other week, and three exams (final in non-cumulative). He explains things clearly and all of his homework and exams are super fair, you won't regret taking Towsley.

Towsley is a great professor! This class has a lot of material, so it is slightly hard, but he makes exams and quizzes easy. Gives reviews before exams that mimic the actual exam. Would 100% recommend!

Really good professor, even in a class of over 100 people he made sure to answer everyone's questions. Grade based off of 3 tests, online homework and quizzes, recitation workshops and attendance checks. Provided us with review materials before tests, which helped out a lot. Would recommend

The workload is fair and reasonable, exams and quizzes are designed to be straightforward and easy to do well on. Lectures are boring but attendance is not mandatory and all lectures slides are posted. Calculators are allowed on all exams and quizzes but they are more proof heavy.

Makes complicated math concepts come naturally on test days given you use the resources. Very good at explaining and communicating what students need to know. Take him when you get the chance, trust me.

Calc 2 is a hard class but Professor Towsley helped make it a lot better. We had one in-class quiz a week, and Towsley gave us a list of workbook problems for each quiz on the syllabus that he would pick questions from, so you could do every question on a quiz before you take it. He would also drop the two lowest quiz grades. Very nice guy!

For weekly 4 problem quizzes he pulls the 4 verbatim from the textbook questions he asks you to study for each unit. He has online class videos & notes, and practice exams that look exactly like the real exam. He gives back every quiz and exam with feedback. If you ask a question during an exam, including final, he'll lead you towards the solution.
This is the best math professor at RIT, without a doubt.

Dr. Towsley is a great professor. The class is really easy and he gives about one reasonable HW a week. The exams are not too tough and the workshops he gives in class are really good review for them. Be sure to do your best on the quizzes he gives. There aren't many, and they're weighted fairly heavily.

Linear Algebra is a very easy class to begin with, but Professor Towsley made it very interesting! His lectures are amazing, you should make sure to attend his lectures even though attendance is not required. Homework is once a week but it's pretty easy if you don't leave it to the last minute. Also makes very fair exams!

comment: Great professor, he has in-class "workshops" which are a good practice for the exams, and lots of WebWork assignments. Quizzes are online on WebWork, slides are online, and there is a textbook but you really don't need it to do well in the course.
Very organized, very approachable, explains concepts very clearly. I cannot stress what a good professor this man is. Highly, highly recommend if you get the chance.
He is the goat, made calculus II a breeze.

I love Towsley so much! He is so kind and such a lovely professor. He's kinda quiet but he knows what he is doing. He is so sweet and honesty he is a safe choice for any class. Go to his office hours! He is such a cool guy!

By far favorite professor at this school. Clear lectures, homeworks, quizzes. Hard content but gives it in an easily digestible way. Gives example problems that show up on quizzes. If you pay attention and ask questions you will do well. Took this professor for 3 math classes and he taught them all similarly. Would take again in a heartbeat

By far favorite professor at this school. Clear lectures, homeworks, quizzes. Hard content but gives it in an easily digestible way and gives very fair quizzes over his lecture content. If you pay attention and ask questions you will do well. Took this professor for 3 math classes and he taught them all similarly. Would take again in a heartbeat

No purchases are required for this course, everything is done on Webwork. Lectures consist of going through his custom slides along with demonstrations on the whiteboard. Towsley is a reasonable and kind prof, and while he doesn't employ much humor, if you get talking with him you will always enjoy the conversations.

He is the best professor I have had at RIT so far, he cares about his students so much. The quiz questions are pulled from the book so you should get an A on that. Exams are easy if you do the work. If you need extra help go to his office hours, he will be there to help you.  Lectures are clear and workshops are only graded for completion.

For future students Dr.Towsley is a really nice person; however, he goes into theory a lot and is decent with his lecturing, but he didn't teach me to where I could understand the material. If you do take him do well on the quizzes he gives in the beginning it could be the reason you get a C- or a D+ he gives you the quiz questions in the textbook!

Towsley is an amazing professor who respects your time and work. Grading criteria is clear and quizzes are pulled directly from the textbook, ensuring success if you put the work in. His lectures are concise and clear, and every homework question is selected to teach you concepts without becoming a burden. He's also always available outside class!

Had Towsley as well for 182 and he was just as good for 190. This class is a lot more lecture heavy, but that is just the class itself and not Towsley. Gives workshops that are very similar to the tests and is very clear about what will be on a test. Gives multiple attempts for quizzes. Towsley is just the goat.

Towsley is amazing; lectures are very clear and engaging. As long as you pay attention and attend class you will do just fine. There are weekly quizzes but these quizzes are based off the textbook (free and online) and he tells you which problems, so it is easy to get an A. He makes the class as easy as possible for such a hard subject.

Makes learning Calculus genuinely enjoyable. he helped clear up a lot of the questions I had brought over from my previous calculus class. However, he does pick up on work near the end of the semester, but if you're willing to put in a little work, his class can be very rewarding.

Towsley is a fantastic teacher!! His slides are really nice, there's just enough info that you can understand the material when looking back, plus he uploads the slides. He also solves examples on the whiteboard during the slide show which helps improve understanding; He is one of the best math professors I've had at rit, overall I recommend

His lectures go a bit fast, but he explains everything very well and does well answering questions. His notes/lectures are very organized, which made it easier to study when I went back through my notes for tests. He also posts a lot of resources on the course page.

Professor Towsley really cares about the success of his students and puts a lot of effort into his classes. The material is difficult but lectures are well organized and many already have extra notes which are accessible online. There is one group project and weekly quizzes alongside regular exams.

I had Towsley for Prj Based Calc II. Considering the difficulty of the class itself, he made it seem manageable. he had 3 midterms and a final with a quiz every week. quizzes were copied and pasted from the optional and ungraded textbook homework, so do it. lectures were dense, but he was easy to understand and actually had legible handwriting.

Professor Towsley is great at the standard criteria of a math course, presents the material clearly, makes sure you understand the topics, and giving fair exams. However what I really enjoy about his class is that he connects the material to other topics and future uses with a focus on computer science, showing us why we are learning the material.

Overall a great professor. He gives workshops after lectures most days and they are perfect review material for any exam. His exams are very fair. I will not say they are easy but if you properly devote time to study you will do just fine. He gives a quiz every Friday but the questions are given to you in the syllabus so review is easy.

Towsley has been one of the best math professors I have ever had. He explains everything extremely thoroughly (take notes and youll be fine) and does not require you to buy the homework. Also, the quiz questions are all in the textbook. Extremely caring man and is very approachable. If you can get him for a class, do not hesitate to do so.

He's amazing. I have no idea how I got an A in the subject when I literally hated the second half of the material (not his fault, if anything he made it a whole lot easier). Took him for another class later- material was easier and he was still great.

One of the best Professors I have ever had especially for math. Professor Towsley was very patient and caring when I was struggling with the material. You don't get that with many university math professors. It was hard material. Even helped me out with my Calc II class. 100% recommend.

He really does everything he can to help you get a really good grade. His homework are harder than the tests, but you have unlimited tries on most of the homework so it essentially forces you to do the problem correctly. His extra help directly correlates to test problems so I would highly recommend going. Overall very understanding and helpful.

Towsley can teach clearly and efficiently. His lectures are good, detailed explanations. He uses WebWork so the textbook is optional. He gives a reasonable amount of HW, 10-15 problems a week and a weekly quiz (4-5 questions) which you can retake at least twice. His tests are fair + he provides a formula sheet. Always available to answer questions.

Towsley is a bit awkward, but he can teach very competently. His lectures are pretty good, and brownie points for textbook-optional (WebWork GOAT). He doesn't give a crushing amount of HW, usually 10-15 problems / subject. Exams are fair, provides a formula sheet. I need to note his support during COVID remote learning is outstanding.

Professor Towsley is great. The lectures are very clear and teaches exactly what you need to know for homework/quizzes/tests. Tests are fair. Quizzes are easy, they are just textbook problems given ahead of time. He will give a 10/10 for workshops as long as you show up and attempt to do the problems. Overall, pretty nice.

comment: Professor Towsley is a really great teacher for calculus 2. Going into it can be nerve racking after hearing about how difficult calculus 2 can be, but he makes it easier than it sounds and really teaches the content well. As long as you do the homework and study for the quizzes and tests you will be fine.
tags: ['Respected', 'Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: He is very knowledgable and very good at providing a variety of examples showing different methods of completing a variety of problems. He prepares you well for exams and quizzes. don't take cell bio with newman/wright. you checked this site for a reason. here's your advice, rochester.
