Felt like I was well prepared for the exams. Liked the course. I'm planning on taking a few other classes with him.
Would take again. Good guy. Learned a lot.

I know this guy gets a lot of crap from other students but I learned the most from taking a bunch of classes with him than compared with other professors at RIT. I would highly recommend his class if you are looking to really dive deep in the material. It's helpful if you have a good grasp on math before taking his class though.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: You can always catch him during office hours if you have questions. He really helped me understand some of the homeworks and what I was missing on them. His exams are pretty easy. He is a really smart guy, I found asking him to walk through an example with me was really helpful. I do think he really cares about students and wants them to do well.

Exams tend to be easy! Nunes really wants you to do well in his class and to actually learn. but you need to put in the work. Home works are hard but that prepares you for the exams which are way easier.

I'll have to play devils advocate here and say that Nunes is not THAT bad of a professor. He lectures by listing out definitions, lemmas, etc. which I didn't find very helpful. 

Quizzes are usually word-for-word copied from notes. His exams are relatively simple and quick. Homework is hard, so I recommend using outside sources for help. Good luck!

Terrible professor, nice guy somewhat. However, his feedback is horrendous and I don't think he thinks that it's possible for someone to not understand what he's teaching. Beyond convoluted notes, and the class was too scared to ask questions about what we were learning that week because they didn't know the material from 5 weeks ago.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']

comment: How genius can an instructor be to ask you the names of the authors of some outdated programming languages in a programming course exam? Will ask you about special data structures defined in class without any reference. Lectures are basically watching him mumbling and writing code with few explanations. No enough content on necessary concepts.

Nunes is perhaps the worst prof you could take in the CS department that I know. I have heard legends from alumni for how notoriously awful this guy is. Homework with abstract material that teach you nothing, not even remotely helpful feedback on anything, more than half the class dropped this semester, including people I know. Avoid at all costs.

DO NOT take Arthur Nunes at all costs. He will give the easiest examples in class, but for homeworks, it will be very challenging and take you hours to do. There is only one midterm and a final. First week of class, we already had a quiz to take. Also, half the class dropped out (that's ur sign).

Arthur Nunes is by far the worst professor I've taken at RIT, he does not care about your success, he's just there to get paid. His lecture is useless and he makes it mandatory, but everything he does in lecture is on the handout he gives. The homeworks are difficult and do not help you learn the material of the course. Avoid if possible.

Arthur Nunes might be the worst professor I took at RIT lot of my friends enrolled in his class dropped and almost half of the whole class (~120) dropped He doesn't care about his students his lectures are identitcal to handouts he give out His homework is long and often irrelavent to the exam Takes him forever to grade with useless or no feedback
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']

comment: Arthur Nunes is an extremely smart person in his element, however a terrible teacher.  Poor at conveying topics, he will spend most of the period lecturing at the class in what seems to be a different language.  If you end up with him, use online resources to learn the content and the TA hours, otherwise good luck.  Also insanely hard homework.

- Hands out a packet for every chapter that he copies in class with no further explanation 
- Several people got accomadations denied
- Had to know 'everything' for midterm, only over the last two weeks
- Graded quiz on first day
- No makeup for quizzes or exams, no matter the reason
- Homeworks are long and convoluted that take him weeks to grade

Take any professor but him. Boring lectures, can't properly answer questions, homeworks are practically impossible and are never similar or even close to what quizzes or exams are like. On my soul I'd rather listen to Thick of It for an hour than go to this class.

The worst professor that you can possibly take for a CS class or any class in this university. He is not fit to be a professor in any way. Does not care about students, offers little to no assistance on homeworks that are challenging. He should be removed from RIT or not be given a teaching role in any capacity. DO NOT TAKE HIM AT ANY COST.
Avoid at all costs. He bans tech from the classroom. Quizzes were based on memorization and he doesn't help with homework.

Cannot recommend this professor; try to get Deever. My undergrad friends (at a different university) and my grad friends at RIT took algo with Deever and Selitskiy, and their curriculum was largely the same. Nunes curriculum differed significantly and was far less practical. Felt like I didn't learn anything new until second half of the semester :(

If you love math, you will love Nunes. While some dislike his heavy use of formal definitions and proofs, don't treat that as a universal opinion! I personally loved the math-heavy curriculum, and quizzes and exams were mostly just memorizing information from the lecture notes. Homeworks are difficult but graded very leniently as long as you try.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Lots of homework']

comment: While this class is challenging and very math heavy, Nunes is extremely accessible outside of class and I think you can succeed if you put in the effort.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Under no circumstances take him, Im warning you. I know many people that went into this class wanting an A and by the end hoping for a c. He is by far the worst cs professor I've had and I would recommend you stay as far away as possible. If you do take him, good luck suffering through his lectures. Everyone In his classes hate him, me included.

Professor Nunez teaches CS theory from the ground up. Which is cool, but he expects a LOT of proofs and technical work out of you. He often skipped over the basic parts of the class and dove right into super math-heavy stuff, meaning I'd watch him solve proofs while I was still unsure what exactly we were proving.

Arthur Nunes clearly loves his work, and is a inspirational in his class. His lectures are well defined and makes understanding the complex world of functional programs and creating programming languages enjoyable. The homework was complicated at times, but for the right reasons. Overall, I learned a lot in his class and I would take him again.

This professor was very nice as a person but the way he taught was not easy to follow as someone new to the topic. Homework was extremely complicated compared to the actual coursework. There was nothing to go off of for the exam besides notes. Quizzes are easy if you understand the homework. I spent most of my time in his class confused.

Teaches course in a very mathematical/proof-oriented way, as opposed to other professors giving actual coding assignments. Lectures are key, if you take notes you'll do fine on the quizzes. Exams were pretty difficult but he is clear about what will be on it. In my class he did not finish teaching a certain topic and it was on the final exam. Avoid
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: He is extremely inflexible, and practically bans technology (and eating for some reason) from the classroom. He micromanages and controls almost everything, and his grading is way too harsh. He makes his students buy HIS OWN bad textbook (like we are literally indirectly paying this dude). Everything seems to be "not his problem".
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Takes simple concepts and makes them complicated. Killed my interest in the subjects he covered.

Absolutely shambolic! Makes little to no effort in explaining the mathematical proofs scattered all over his slides. Very few explanations provided in terms of examples. Extremely opinionated and fusses with small issues.

The homeworks for this Algorithms class were time consuming and sometimes tricky, but he gives you 2 weeks for each one so it's manageable. The lectures were information dense and sometimes too fast, and he doesn't allow computers in class so you can't follow along. He explains the topics well, though, and answers questions in class thoroughly.
I thought his lectures were really good, he makes things clear and answers questions in depth. The homeworks were definitely challenging and took a lot of time, but he graded them very leniently.
Unkind professor who does not have the capacity to convey information in a respectful or understandable way. It is as if he wants students to fail.

Prepare for lectures that answer every question you don't have twice, and blaze through the parts you don't understand. If you ask a question, you will either get a super indirect answer, or if it's for the homework you'll be told to just figure it out. Professor Nunes is clearly wise, but he cannot communicate information effectively. Be careful.

The worst CS Professor I've ever had. Makes what should be an easy A class into a nightmare where formal proof definitions are given for simple concepts and examples are few and far between. Homework is mostly conceptual and often requires knowledge that we never learned. Thankfully quizzes are simple and taken almost work-for-word from class.

A terrible overly difficult professor without a reasonable expectation for work. Lecture slides are useless outside of class and he takes his sweet time deciding to upload them to myCourses. Ridiculous amount of time spent on homework. Mostly theoretical. I'd suggest any other professor for Algo

He does not care about his students. He does not take questions during exams (even for clarification of problems), and he says talking about the material outside of class is an act of academic dishonesty and grounds for failing the class.

Do yourself a favor and drop his class. I've had many bad CS professors in my 5 years, but none as bad as professor Arthur. His style of teaching is not only very old-fashioned, but also highly inefficient. CS261 is an already difficult course, and tackling it from a pure mathematical perspective without practicals makes it an absolute nightmare.

Bad policies. He doesn't let the students use laptop or phone. Goes through the lecture very fast, so if you missed something on the slides, which you could've otherwise accessed through your laptop, you're out of luck. When asked a question he often gives an indirect answer and uses a pure mathematical approach to everything in this course.

As an undergrad, I took a few classes with Arthur about ten years ago and his teaching style left a deep impression on me. His enthusiasm for theoretical CS is extraordinary. Occasionally he would do some live coding in class and insist we must predict the result of running a program before executing it. I still think about this on a regular basis.

Unrealistically stingy when asking for help on homework. Will not think up a different problem and work through it with you so that you don't get a "freebie" on a homework question.  You better hope you got lucky and picked the right content to study for exams as they are only 4 questions long.  HALF of the final was on one specific algorithm.

One of the "avoid at all cost" professors. He was actually better than I expected, which was not hard to do, because I felt like the material was taught alright, it just had nothing to do with test and quiz material. Claims he doesn't believe in memorization but quizzes are 1000% memorizing ridiculous formulas.

I had a conflict with an athletic event and an in class quiz and, even though professors are required by RIT to accommodate varsity athletic events, this professor wouldn't allow me to make up a quiz under any circumstances. We had to escalate the issue and it was an awful experience. His teaching style is also incredibly boring.

Algorithms is overall a bad class, but Arthur somehow found a way to make it worse. The homework's are just straight up time consuming and provide little to no example of the actual content that he teaches. His quizzes can also sometimes be completely unfair in which he asks you to remember code line by line.

Gave little feedback, requires Python for all assignments. Not accessible outside of class, gives unclear and verbose answers to simple question. Homeworks were inciteful and encouraged exploring new concepts and creative thought. I wish I got feedback on it.

Difficult class. Not a bad professor. If still offered as online/in-person hybrid, take the quizzes and exams online, as they are multiple-choice while the in-person quizzes and exams were short answer or open-ended only. Take notes on the slides, especially the non-descript variable names used when describing algorithms.

Gets a lot of flak for being a very old fashioned professor. Can't say I disagree, but he teaches a very good sincere class on algorithms. You will have to do a bit of your own research for homeworks, and the topics go fast, but if you hold on, I think you will develop a very deep understanding of how things work. Can be a bit too academic.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: I understand that Algorithms is a notoriously hard class, but the experience was 10x worse with Arthur teaching it. He is horrible at pacing his lectures and often skips important material to keep pace. The homework is ridiculously grindy and time consuming for no reason and will bleed into other responsibilities. Beware of Arthur at all costs.

Lectures are very low on detail and it's unclear when you need the textbook. Homework assignments are ridiculously time consuming. Don't expect a response if you email the professor, and if you get one, don't expect it to be on time or helpful.

He doesn't let you use computers in class and he thinks that lisp is a good programming language. That should tell you a good amount about him. His lectures are completely useless and he barely ever responds to discussion posts. In lectures, he shows pseudocode that has 1-letter variables. I feel like I have become stupider by taking this class
I personally really liked his teaching style. He was very straightforward and passionate about the topics. Tests were relatively easy but homework and projects were very difficult.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: (ONLINE CLASS) Average professor, but the thing that gets me is his use of nondescriptive, one-letter variable names. He's a fine choice for algo, but just make sure to rewrite the algorithms from class with real variable names so they make more sense.

Nope. Just nope. Writing down mathematical proofs isn't the right way to learn algorithms. Theory takes away from the beauty of algorithm design. Theory is essential, but it should go hand in hand with the practical stuff, too. For example, we never learnt why dynamic programming is used, just its mathematical formulae. Hard pass, sorry.

Worst professor I've had in my college career. Extremely smart person, literally terrible at teaching. He will not teach you anything outside of the monotonous and poorly made 45 minute videos, since that is all he has to do during these online classes. Have fun asking for help outside that...

I've taken ANH in the past and boy, let me say that the COVID situation does not properly reflect his rating on this site at the moment. He absolutely displays an aptitude with the material of the course, and can even explain a question if you have it. The problem is he's never there, never present. He shows up, waits for the minute hand to strike

Extremely unaccommodating for online learning. Does not answer for days on end, and then gives a half-answer that does not help whatsoever. Problems in the lectures do not reflect the difficulty of homework questions at all. If you have a technical issue that causes a problem in this class, forget about emailing him about it, he will not care.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']

comment: Taught one of the hardest subjects to teach in the best possible way. Beware, if you stop listening for even a single minute of the lecture, you won't follow the rest because every statement in his class is connected.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']

comment: The professor has a good grasp on the subject he teaches, and is very knowledgeable. Though, the professor is not a very good educator. The times when he hands out notes, they are not posted anywhere else. The notes are referenced months later, and if you lose the note sheet or miss class, you're screwed.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Professor took really long on the mundane and easy parts of the course and spent only a day or two on more important/interesting topics. If you have even a basic undergrad understanding of algorithms, this course is a waste. It's made worse by the professor's tendency to do everything slowly(like handing out assignments).

Great curriculum but frustrating assignments. Professor seems opinionated and often less than perfect at addressing confusion about material. Assignments are not clearly written, and have effectively busywork.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: CONS: - Uses math psuedo-code, but the symbols are in-consistent and confusing. - Most of the Syllabus is not covered in class. - Homeworks long, tedious and not related to anything covered in class. - Huge portion of the class time is wasted in writing definitions - Didn't learn anything new in the class the whole semester.

The course content is too heavy on theory and mathematical proofs rather than the practicality of design and analysis of algorithms. The course is spent learning obscure mathematical notations and proofs. The homework assignments also focus on the mathematics rather than the coding aspect of the subject.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: If you're complaining about the class being hard or boring, you're doing it wrong. Don't come to class thinking you'll be spoon fed the material. The material is indeed hard. That's a feature. There's no way to make it easier. Do yourself a favor and do the reading before you come to class. Nunes-Harwitt's strong point is homework assignments.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Homeworks are not worth the time and effort as most of it are mathematical proofs. 5% of the grade for class participation can make or break your overall grade(and you don't know about it till the end). Too much stress on understanding of notations rather than covering more topics and understanding of algorithms.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Too much emphasis on test and quizzes. Very little feedback on the homework. Quite lazy on changing your grades even if the grader made a mistake. His way of teaching is way too mathematical. All he does is throwing definitions on the whiteboard, and all you do is try your best to copy them done.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: Great teaching rhythm!

I can't imagine taking Nunes-Harwitt for an intro level course, but for higher level courses that he's into, he's pretty good. His lectures can be a little hard to follow and homework is sometimes graded a little strangely but overall, not a terrible class. His biggest flaw is that he drones sometimes.
The course itself is challenging. Missing lectures is definitely not recommended because he has a sign in sheet and he doesn't post his lecture notes online. His lectures can be boring and dull.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: I personally can't stand him. Lecture is essentially the same as his typed notes, which is more obtuse to figure out than the book he derived it from. Homework is insanely hard, 2 question quizzes leave little margin for error, and he forces you to go to office hours to know what went wrong. I have never felt so lost in one's class, even with help.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: People give him a bad rap because they go into CS1 not knowing any programming. If you don't, ask your peers or him during office hours. His lectures are clear and if you ask a question he will answer it clearly. As long as you pay attention and do all the work you'll get a good grade.

His lectures are very hard to follow and confusing. They typically consist of him giving a vague description of the lecture topic, skipping over the actual "theory" behind it, and going straight to a text editor to show the lecture code instead of explaining how to do the topic in general. You are better off taking notes from departmental PDFs.

The guy loves Lisp and compilers, and of course, he tells us to write a compiler for some Lisp based language in CS2. The graduate students even have trouble with it and some of the professors think the project is dumb, but of course if he likes it everyone else must like it!

Nunes is incredibly passionate and that shows in his lectures about theory and functional programming. He has a very unique way of speaking and professing his thoughts, and lots of isms. Take him if you're excited about CS theory and related topics. Homeworks are usually pretty challenging, but as a result exams are easier.
Very confusing during lecture. Have to prepare before going to class. Nice person out of class and funny when he can.  Lectures can be super long. Tests are pretty straight forward.

He's pretty good if he's teaching a class he cares about (i.e. theoretical, non-intro classes). Can drone a little, but very knowledgeble, helpful if you ask. Doe s have a weird habit of pausing for long periods of time.

Professor Nunes-Harwitt is very knowledgeable in Language Theory, and does a good job presenting the material in lecture. He is soft-spoken, which leads students to believe his lectures are boring. If you pay attention, ask questions, and think critically his class is informative. Go to his office hours if you need extra help.

If you have experience in coding, especially in Python, or Java, easy class. His tests are very easy. Study, look over you labs and homework, you will be fine. His lectures are very long, and boring. I never was a awake  in the class. and if you ask him a question he doesnt make any sense. Go to your SI Sessions! Make sure u submit the right hw!

Nunes-Harwitt is not bad but he isn't good either. His lecture is painfully boring so get good sleep to obtain the best chances at not falling asleep in class. Also, if you are a first-time student learning this content, this can be a difficult course to grasp and understand. There are better professors but passing isn't impossible.
tough grades
He likes XKCD, quiz and homework every other week. Quizzes are very straightforward on the material. Tests are just more quiz problems at one time. Homework is the worst out of all three.

Very theory oriented professor, loves to talk about abstract algorithms and the math behind the computing. Not always easy to follow the theory notation, but he's willing to take time during his lectures to clarify, and he definitely knows the material inside and out. Tests were simple, projects took time but weren't particularly difficult.

He is not the most exciting professor, but he presents the material cleanly and clearly, loves to answer questions, and genuinely cares if you understand the material.  The homework assignments clearly tie in with the class material.
I had some coding experience before taking this class, so I may be biased. He isn't as bad as most people make him out to be. He was rather dull, but he really did a good job of answering questions.

As said before, if you have prior CS experience this class will probably be easy regardless. However, ANH is not so great of a teacher. He's exceedingly poor at answering questions, and he spends too much time going over some easier things while skipping over more difficult concepts. Take someone else if you can.

While his answers aren't always the clearest and I don't agree with some of the ways he programs, he's better than some of the reviews here make him seem. If you know how to program don't bother with the textbook.

Pretty difficult for a first time programmer to understand with the way he explains things. Doesn't use enough visual aid (TAs were better in this aspect) instead opting to show everyone the code. Laptops aren't allowed so you can't follow along. Assignments were fair, but take a while for someone who has no prior experience.

Not especially challenging, but the lectures are painfully boring.  Trying to count the times he says "Insofar as" makes it a little more interesting, but not much.  Labs and Homeworks seemed to be graded fairly (by the SLIs)    Recitations were more helpful than the lectures themselves

While the other reviews paint a good picture, here is an actual exchange that does even better: (student asks question),(NH answers vaguely as usual), NH: "Now did that sorta answer your question?", Student: "sorta...?", NH: "mhmmm.....good...",(NH goes on with lecture.) You can watch him spend extra time thinking of a way to deflect your question.

Anything he teaches you is the most basic and simplest form you will ever see it. The homework and labs are about 1000 times harder. He is essentially useless. You could learn more from reading Python For Dummies.

The man is smart, and easy going on grades (though he can be a big jerk about small things) The only problem is he's downright useless and dodges or deflects every question asked of him. You don't use the textbook, and he wont help you at all. Avoid him if you can, he deserves the grade he has here.
He is very confusing and does not explain things. Do not take if you have no programming experience because you will not learn much.

Nunesy doesn't exactly TEACH. If you have some python experience, then you should be good. I had a year's worth, and the class is boring as hell. You won't learn ANYTHING if you don't already know it. Switch out as soon as you can. Seriously.

Many will say he is the worst in the department. Sure he is a boring lecturer, but he is very quirky. If you attend SI sessions regularly you WILL get an A in his class! And you will understand the material a lot better. He has very fair exams (that and the lecture are all CS prof's do).

Horrible Teacher...Makes up words that don't even exist, such as "scientifisize." Explains concepts in ways that none of the students understand. INCREDIBLY BORING. Not willing to help students when needed, even during one on one conversations. Avoid any class with him at all cost.
very boring. explains things in strange ways. does know what he is talking about. does not use book at all. goes very little out of the way to help students understand material.
If you faced with the choice of either not taking a CS course or choosing this guy, I suggest you file for an unmet need and request a different section.
Avoid this professor if you can, lectures put you to sleep and unless you already know what he's teaching, you aren't going to learn anything.
Avoid at all costs

Awful. Has a mathematical background, and cannot resist explaining simple things in the most overcomplicated ways. Do we really need to bring Set Theory into Dijkstra's Algorithm? Can't explain his way out of a paper bag, so don't bother asking a question. A master at avoiding questions. Doesn't answer email.

Avoid him like the plague. He is the worst professor ever. If you have previous experience CS and have him, do a favor to everyone else who doesn't and help them. If you don't have the experience, well prepare to spend all your extra hours with a tutor.

If you have no background in CS do not take him.  He teaches you nothing and come like week 6 or 7 you'll be completely lost.  If you mess up one test case he destroys your grade despite having done everything else fine. Just plain avoid him.

He isn't the best teacher if you are learning stuff for the first time, but if you have a background in CS this class is a breeze. Easy grader, our class average was probably in the high 80's. Doesn't use the book at all, although you are supposed to read from it

He did not use a textbook. He did not use powerpoints: all of his notes were written on the board. There were no notes on his website. So that means that you must copy EVERYTHING that he writes on the board in your notes. Very boring lecturer. Tests were difficult. Avoid.

I hate this guy, the book he has you get teaches you better, seeing as he uses alot of his stuff right from the book. I dont know what others meant by 'helpful' because i asked him about how to start up python at the beginning of the class (first time programming) and instead of just giving me a terminal command he referred me to the tutoring cente

This guy is dull.  I can't speak for CS1-4, he'd probably be good, but for PLC, this guy knows how to suck.  Not only did he ramble on during lectures in a monotone voice, he tries to be playful and it comes across as creepy.  Also, his tests are pathetic.  Avoid this man like the plague.  Also, if you try to talk to him, he basically tells you TFB

He knows what he's talking about and will answer your questions fully. You need to go to class willing and ready to wrap your head around the concepts though, because it is hard to follow if you're not being attentive. He was very helpful during his office hours for answering my questions.

He's extremely knowledgeable, and loves his subject. If you are interested, you'll follow, if you come because you have to, you won't. I have no complaints, and I think a lot of people complain because they expect to be spoon-fed the information.

He is very good at teaching the topics, but he doesn't use a computer to write code, so he wastes a lot of his lecture time writing on the board. Sort of boring. Lectures never really used. Better than a bad professor, but not as good as most. Doesn't really answer questions, nor does he admit he doesn't know.

When I went into this class, I had read here that he wasn't that great and was scared... I came in, and I loved his class! He teaches with coding examples, diagrams, and uses the textbook a lot. I don't know about everyone else, but I felt that this was a good learning experience. Also, if you have problems, he is very helpful via email & office hr

First off, he is a horrible teacher. Lectures are painful, as only a fraction of the content relates to the labs and work. If it's not on his notes, he can't answer your question. His class policies are the worst I've endured, and he grades tests pretty hard. Avoid at all costs.

This professor is very knowledgeable about the topic but he is not very helpful when it comes to clarification or reasons why certain things are done.  Tests are graded hard and some questions are weighted more than others.  Don't take his class unless you already know the topic front and back.  If at all possible avoid.

You can tell that he is a smart guy, but he has no idea how to teach this class. I have never looked around a room and see more students lost. He is not helpful when you ask him about quiz and test format. Overall, I was looking forward to that class but within a week hated it.
Incredibly boring professor. Reads everything directly from his notes and not very helpful in answering questions.

I never had a problem staying awake until I went into his class - which usually isn't a problem.  Still, he sometimes makes no sense when trying to explain a topic, often has trouble understanding questions, and his tests need to be syntactically EXACT - or he starts dockin points left 'n right - but he barely checks labs/projects...Not bad, per-se

I didn't know I could fall asleep during CS until I went to his class.  He's extremely boring.  Other than that he's a good teacher and he gets the material across.  He grades pretty hard on tests and is pretty obsessive compulsive about everything (1/2 absence if you're more than 2 or 3 minutes late) which can get annoying.  Decent otherwise..
Very thorough when teaching a specific subject and he encourages asking questions. However the responses you get aren't always helpful and often more confusing than anything.

He has a lot of experience about what he teaches. On top of that he is a good person and genuinely cares about everyone. He does have a passion to teach. Yes, he is strict but is fair in a way that you would be glad that he taught you before the world did. Overall I enjoyed his lectures!
He gave a 27 question quiz due 10 minutes after the end of the first class. Enough said.

Got angry that the ENTIRE class wasn't learning the material & blamed us for it. Scatterbrained during class, ex. repeating slideshows from class before. Purposely makes assignment questions vague to get you to ask questions, then doesn't respond to e-mails. Yelled at us because his computer is slow. Slow to return grades (over a month for some)

Super passionate about UML, so beware if you use the wrong arrows that you will be ripped apart. Really important class and I definitely learned a lot. A big portion of the grade is projects that focus mostly on design, so pay attention to the patterns and pray you get a good group or you will be miserable.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Group projects', 'Tough grader']

comment: Professor Hawker is a nice person, but a terrible professor. Whenever I reached out to him for help, he usually either wasn't available or made getting help hard. His feedback is not helpful, so it's difficult to know how to improve. He didn't enter grades until the day after they were due, so I didn't know how I was doing all semester. Avoid him!
Good luck ever getting grades back, lectures are dense and uninteresting

Terrible professor with little to no interest in teaching this class. Assignments were vague, no clear instructions, harsh grader with useless feedback. Doesn't teach and reads off slides, which has short phrases and nothing is explained. Everything graded in the last week of class so you don't know how you're doing until the week of finals.

Probably the worst professor I've had at RIT so far. Took over 2 months to get most of our grades back, literally reads off of power points for lectures, and barely responds to students outside of class. Most of his due dates were also incorrect and he waited until last minute to fix them (some weren't even fixed >:( )

Lots of negative things to say about this Professor, but there's a word limit. Harsh grader, slow to give back grades. Doesn't teach and reads off powerpoint slides like we can't read on our own. Doesn't explain any concepts clearly and deflects any questions. Don't even bother reaching out to him for any help.
Condescending, hostile, and disorganized. Makes fun of students, refuses to accept he could be wrong about something, and relies heavily on broken video links instead of teaching.

Terribly slow at putting in grades unrelated to the course assistants as we have been waiting on some grades for months. His feedback was not very helpful on the project he had partially graded. The class itself is extremely interesting, however, he makes it not engaging and tends to read off of the slides. Does not add much to the provided slides.

Has done a terrible job of getting grades back to us. One project has no grades back. Two only have partial grades back and projects are a large portion of the class. Is also not good at engaging the class in the material which is a lot but important.

Doesn't know how to teach a concept. Whatever is taught in class has no practical relevance. He explains concepts very vaguely and also is not thorough with grading. A classmate of our's found some problem with final grades and turned out every student's grade was downgraded by a grade. If we didn't pay attention then we would've left with bad grad

I wanted to like this class, I really did. Class overall was a mess. Getting grades back was like pulling teeth. We got our "feedback" not grade back a week before R2 was due with is unacceptable for a class like this, and it was a week cause we fought to have it pushed. This was supposedly an anomaly but left a bad taste in my mouth.

He is horrible at returning grades. There were times where we were waiting over two months to get our grade on a project that is 15% of our average. His lectures are boring and straight from a powerpoint and adds no useful information to them . He also grades very hard

Grades for exams and projects have been unacceptably late throughout the semester. Gives feedback that isn't all that helpful. Expectations for the project(s) were not as clear as they should be. Overall, I was very disappointed in Hawker's performance as a teacher, more so than I could have expected.

I've had Hawker as a professor 3-4 times now, and he's become my favorite SE professor at RIT. He actually cares about how well you do. Will work with you to resolve any issues or questions readily. Tests are usually open-note. He prefers a late, but complete assignment. Stay focused on due dates. Very slow grader, but helpful comments when he does

Awful class. I don't know how much of the professor's fault it is, but the material is really just not interesting. Useful, but not interesting.  Lectures are all powerpoint slides and he goes way, way too fast through them.  He also was constantly behind on grading, got nearly no grades back until really late in the semester.
It was really hard to understand Hawker. He also isnt really helpful when you go to his office for help. He will tell you to read the book.

I don't think I learned anything useful. Only got one grade all semester (midterm). Got some feedback but no grades on other work. Every class was a PPT lecture, with a few group presentations. If we ran out of time, he just would let some groups not present. Was mailing lectures in by the end of the semester. I got an A but I don't know why.

One of the better SE professors. Very helpful. Presents a lot of information and lectures can be boring, but only tests on core principles. Projects are a lot of work but he is a fair grader. I have had him for many classes and take his classes whenever it works for my schedule.

Excellent professor. He presents a lot of material, but he only expects you to be able to understand the high-level concepts of what he has presented. Very helpful in and out of class with questions. Highly recommended.

I agree with other comments - he presents A LOT of material.  It is really hard to study for the class because of this.  Also I feel as if I didn't really learn any of it.  I drowned in a sea of information for a while and wound up with an OK grade.

Best professor and class at RIT by far.  He presents A LOT of material to you, but only the core concepts will be on an exam.  Activities are INCREDIBLY fun and help you learn.  Projects are very flexible and interesting.  He is one of those professors that I will take every chance possible.

This class was insane with tons of material to learn; it really should have been focused around a few central topics like most classes.  It was a lot of work, but he was lenient with grades; he actually looked at the effort you put into something instead of just the result because he understood that.  He's a great guy, too.

I had no interest in this class whatsoever but I ended up coming out learning a whole lot.  Sometimes his lectures can be boring but for the most part he's not bad.  Easy tests.  Easy grader.  Nice guy.

Avoid Joel at all costs. His class is extremely unorganized. He ranted about the terrible political state of the country instead of teaching course material. He assigned excessive amounts of readings and writings for environmental topics (he wrote most of the readings) that were not related to the course title (American Lives, American Values).

He runs class with immense disorganization, making it very hard to keep track of what assignments he will randomly give and then forget about. The class' myCourses page will not help you.

Class time is just his soapbox. It must be hard to be Joel. Politics are important to him, but nobody cares about his beliefs because he's diagnosably annoying.

The professor has a very unusual grading approach. He assigned five tasks throughout the semester, but replaced them all with a single 10-page final paper worth 45% of the grade, which he only introduced in week 13. He often goes off-topic during lectures and is extremely slow with grading—our first January assignment wasn't graded until March.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: I'm surprised to  see such a low rating for Joel. He is a good professor who shows you bunch of films that discuss about social and environmental impacts. There are no test in his classes, but does need to take notes, write two 400 word book review and a presentation, which is very easy. Overall Joel is one of those teachers you will have in class.

The video programs that Joel presented were most awe striking/inspiring (Cowspiracy, Damnation, Pandora's Promise, and Chasing Ice). His sense of humor is in moderation and his self-esteem, though criticized, is justified. However, I wish he clarified his instructions on how we read the text books and writing reviews for them.

Worst Professor I ever had. He literally spent two weeks going over actual course material and the rest of the semester he just lectured about how much we need to save the environment. And then he would show a bunch of documentaries about the environment. Literally the worst class ever. He's also incredibly tough on grading. GPA destroyer.

I don't even know where to begin. I took his sports history class to fill a free elective and got the worst grade I've ever gotten in my life. I got better grades in my graduate level classes. He gave us a pop final. He gave me a B- on a paper and told me I did "amazing on it." He will ruin your life and your GPA. Avoid at all cost

Joel is one of the worst professors I have ever taken. He is very unclear on when assignments are due and his grading is extremely tough. If you want to suffer and lower your gpa because of a perspective class then take his class. I do not recommend his class otherwise.

If you're a self-righteous, pretentious, wanna-be-introspective, try-hard environMENTAList enthusiast then this is the teacher for you. He thinks that his views on life are right and everyone is a bad person(though he would never outwardly show this). He's trying to change the world and makes you feel worthless if you're not along for the ride

Honestly, he values his opinion over everyone else's it seems. I won't say whether I liked him or disliked him, but I would not take him again. He is vague about what he wants on his assignments, trying to push "use your imagination" but I would get B's for this. He is a grammar nazi as well, so beware. He does not use MyCourses. Nice guy, but no.

Very opinionated, mostly bout topics not covered in the class. Extremely strict on essays. No tests otherwise. Must go to class. Missing 2 classes gives an instant participation grade of 75% (and the day before break counts as 2 absences). Since there are not many tests, it's important to go. Otherwise, the class was kind of interesting.

Information Revolution (HIST-180): Okay professor. Passionate about what he does. He tends to come "unprepared to class" (he will ask students if he could borrow a laptop). Grades notes and readings (journals) harshly. Good guy, can be funny sometimes, classes were enjoyable. Does tend to advertise personal affairs into the class using class time.
He was a very bad teacher. Didn't prepare for class and was always late. Boring class and does not know very much about the topic. Wouldn't recommend.
Great teacher, don't expect an easy A.  Lots of papers, but he's helpful outside of class. Don't waste your time complaining about the class. It's college!

I would never recommend this teacher. The classes are horribly dull as all they consist only of him reading from he book the entire time. The lecture information usually has nothing at all to do with your papers, and there are only 3, hard and obscure essays to write for the class at the end of the quarter to be graded on. I learned nothing.

Classes are pointless since he goes over information that isn't even relevant to the essays which are your only source of grades in the class. Also, the essays are vague and difficult. Nice guy but do not recommend him as a teacher.
Depressing class.  Wow, I pity him big time.
Nice guy, awful teacher.  He will make you write 8 to 10 pages every week and get no credit.

I only rated him a "1" because I had to give me a rating between 1 and 5. Don't get me wrong, he knows what he's talking about but the doesn't know how to teach. Expected to remember 15 powerpoints word-for-word in order to even get a passing grade on the exams. Class average was a 62, he was forced to curve it. AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS!

My feelings on Professor Lasky varied throughout the semester and still do to this day. He can be a very nice guy, but can also be pretty condescending about certain questions. Exams are difficult and you never see them again after you submit them and dont get feedback on papers, just grades. Did give EC assignment because many people struggled

Lasky is hands down the worst instructor I've ever had. He has four exams and one assignment over the course of the semester. each exam has about 20 questions on it, and he's exceedingly vague on what will and will not be on the exam. So a lot of this comes down to luck.
AVOID AT ALL COST!!! He just repeats buzz words all throughout the class. His tests are near impossible. DO NOT TAKE!!!
Waste of time

I have to give him some credit as he is a smart man, however he is an absolutely terrible teacher. He provided no feedback to any assignments over the semester and he puts confusingly worded questions on his tests that 50% of the time he does not cover or is even in his notes. Assignments are your only hope for a passing grade. Avoid at all costs.
Takes a class that should be fun and interesting and makes it unnecessarily difficult. Smart man, terrible teacher.
Not as bad as others say he is. Lectures are interesting, tests can be hard but if you review all the material you can get a decent grade.

Hands down the WORST professor I have had at RIT. He provides next-to-no helpful feedback and tests on material that he does not cover. Questions on tests are worded in ambiguous ways that never work in your favor. AVOID!!!

I found his lectures pretty interesting and the concepts well explained.  Some of these reviews are saying that the lecture material is not similar to the test material.  I didn't find that to be the case.  Come to class, pay attention, and review the slides some before the tests and you'll do fine.

See if you can take this equivalent class at a different college and to fulfill this requirement. This is the only way you can bypass Lasky since he is the only teacher that teaches this class.   This class was hard, but in reality - it could have been very, very easy if taught by someone else. He made things seem difficult to make him look smart

Interesting lectures but his exams are  only loosely based upon them but that;s all you have to study. There is no book or other resources. Also gives no feedback on projects and grades them seemingly randomly. I have no idea why one got an A and another a B+. Try to take this with someone else.

This is one of the funniest professors I've ever had. His lectures are effective in teaching course materials to the class; however, most of this course material doesn't show up on exams... These tests are extremely challenging and have little to do with large concepts discussed in class. The projects are the your only salvage for a passing grade.

Terrible teacher, for tests he tells you to just study the lectures he puts up on mycourses and you'll do fine... except the things on the lectures account for only half of what's on his tests. Some of the lectures don't have anything to do with the class and are about whatever new iPhone apple just announced or similar things. Do not take him.
An A or even B  seem long shot in this class. Exams are hard.   Nice guy to talk to- he has a lot of interest in technology. Definitely go to him for help during office hours.
Professor Lasky makes the class very, very hard.

His lectures are actually interesting but he is a terrible professor. His tests are impossible to do well on because he asks such ambiguous questions that no amount of studying can help you answer correctly. He gives absolutely no feedback on any presentations done in class and no direction on assignments. Avoid this guy at all costs!

One paper, two labs, and the rest are quizzes and exams. It's hard to get a good grade with the paper and labs taking up 40% of the final grade, especially when instructions for the assignments are given a week right before or lacks in clarification. Students often have to ask about the instructions before hand.

Great teacher to have a conversation with, but for the class he is awful. The grades based on 3 tests and 3 projects. Attending to class just to listen to his lecture seems easy but only those tests and projects make the course much harder. Dont take him.

Everything you will learn is in the powerpoint slides. His tests are extremely hard and his lectures aren't of any use. I've heard he can be quite helpful outside of class but don't bother during lecture. Also he likes you to know how smart he is. The way he teachers the class is like he talking like an engineering person than IT.

Was a fine Freshman Seminar professor. Talked about some interesting things, and let us talk about things ourselves. Only homework was few-sentence discussion posting regarding our RIT experience weekly, and a paper at the end. Paper was not research, only speculation (no sources/MLA required).

Well... I have mixed feelings about this class... I got an A... so the first poster is wrong.  He is a good lecturer but I think I was looking for something a little more technical in an enterprise security class.

I have never seen anyone get over a B in this enterprise security class.  The class is more business but he seems to have little technological experience for a technology major.He did help me out due to misunderstandings, but with much hesitance.  Would avoid if you can.

Worst Professor I ever had.  Did nothing.  Made us write 4 papers and never gave any feedback on what we did wrong or how to improve.  AVOID AT ALL COSTS!  This guy doesn't deserve to work in IT let along teach in IT.

Dr. Trayling is such a cool guy. He has amazing demonstrations and encourages students to experiment with materials and play around. His quizzes are easy and he cares more about making sure students understand than adhering to strict rules. He's got a super funny dry sense of humor and he definitely made me happy I chose physics.

Trayling is a real student's professor. Hard homework with solution sketches that you could check and open-note exams made this class extremely passable. Classical mechanics is hard, harder than anything I've encountered before, and Trayling did his best to get me to learn and understand the content. Dude is also hilarious, amazing guy
He is one of the best teacher in RIT. His lab and demos help to students to understand the concepts. He also give a brief explanation of topics with historic information. He is very good at drawing.

Dr. Trayling is hands down the best professor you can get for any UP course at RIT. He actually gives understandable IN-PERSON lectures, he drops the lowest 4 quizzes, and he'll give you the pathway to any answer if you ask questions and show effort. He's a sarcastic Canadian and his 8 am UP1 was amazing. Do everything you can to be in his classes

Trayling is one of the best profs I've ever had. He tells the absolute best stories that (usually) relate to lecture, and somehow made an 8 am MTWTh worth it. He clearly knows his stuff and was always available via email to ask questions about homework (he once answered my 3:03 am email with a fully drawn out diagram at 3:10 am).

Professor Trayling is easily the best professor at RIT.  He lectures very well, makes sure students understand the material, and has a dry, absolutely hilarious sense of humor.  I cannot recommend him enough

Good professor. Explains topics well in class, but you will still be expected to apply main ideas in different ways outside of class on your own (homework can take a long time). Only problem I had was when I would stay after class to get help on the homework from the professor, he was not the best in my opinion at explaining so I could understand

Professor Trayling is an excellent instructor. He knew the material well, had amazing lectures, and worked through tons of examples. He can sometimes talk fast, so pay attention. Weekly homework can be tough at times (at least for me it was), but if you get extra help you can still pass and do fine. Overall though, great professor!

If you like tangents about where units come from and how Joule is pronounced Jowl (like howl) youve come to the right guy. Also explains topics in a clear manner and does not require much extra work out of class (though following in the textbook wouldn't hurt)

Dr. Trayling is one of my favorite professors at RIT. He is excellent at making the time spent in class well worth it, providing lots of analysis to all concepts learned with visuals and demonstrations. Definitely would take any course with him.
Trayling is a wonderful professor. He is available to answer any question before or after class, or in his office. He also comes very prepared for his lectures, which are phenomenal

Dr. Trayling is a wonderful professor. He is available to answer any question before or after class, or in his office. He also comes very prepared for his lectures, which are phenomenally mind blowing.

Funny and energetic in class. Goes over a lot of examples, but minimal notes are taken. Content is difficult and almost all of your grade comes from three exams. Weekly quizzes help track your learning for the material.

Varela is awesome! He teaches the lectures in class at a perfect pace and stops and makes sure everyone understands before continuing on. Takes cheating seriously. Straight-forward homework and if you do this and understand it then you'll pass the tests easily. Very willing to help in office hours. Highly recommend!

Lecture was presented with clear and concise notes. All lecture material was posted online as well. Practice problems frequently assigned, but were not collected for credit. Exams were 50 min in class as were very challenging. Did crack jokes in class sometimes and was personable. Able to approach him outside of class.

Overall a decent professor. Goes over material fast so you HAVE to ask questions if you don't understand something or you'll fall behind. Final was way too long and hard. Weekly homework and quizzes make up a small portion of your overall grade. Helpful in office hours but they are limited.
Decent professor, answer question effectively and teaches the concepts very well. Hilarious, but he id quite a tough grader on tests. Much better than the other dynamics professor.

He make sure you understand the material and he'll answer any of your questions.  He uses the book a lot with almost all of the class examples from them.  He does a lot of these which is helpful. Overall he's a decent professor.
Easy class if you do many practice problems. Any tests and quizzes were problems straight out of the book.
He's a nice guy, hard to understand at times, and sometimes isn't clear in lectures but his quizzes are from the homework and tests are only a few questions. Overall not too bad.

Exams are only 2-3 questions and can be ambiguous. Grades are only like 8 quizzes, attendance, 3 exams. Can be a picky grader. Essentially reads textbook. Not the clearest of lectures and can't really draw. But he will meet with you.
Terrible teacher. Doesn't explain the material well; horrible at getting papers back to you; unfair grader. Don't take him.
Sometimes confusing, but makes time to study in the ELC.  Fair grader, tests have lots of easy points to get.
i think he is good

Very helpful and very supportive to students. ALOT of bonus points ( participation and quizzes).
Unfortunately, every week he gives a homework and a quiz, and worksheets are uploaded after every single class. Overall, he gives many work to do but amazing explanation and character.

Prof Beck is one of the nicest and most caring professors at RIT. He is definitely an expert in his field, but it sometimes felt like he wasn't transferring a ton of his knowledge to us. I feel like I didn't learn nearly as much as I was hoping to from his class. Assignments are straightforward and exams are mostly vocab.

The class was very easy to understand and very easy to do good in. You have two exams and 3 projects but if you do the weekly assignments and go to the lectures you will do just fine in this class. On the exams he takes problems directly from the weekly assignments and on the projects you can work with a partner which was nice.
Super easy class and very interesting, all you have to do is the homework.

Duane is the definition of a professor who goes above and beyond. Every lecture was enjoyable purely because of his personality. Duane was always eager to teach and gave off the impression that he genuinely wanted his students to learn and be successful in the future. The homework and exams were easily manageable by reading the textbook.
Duane is a real Gem. He is such a great wholesome caring guy that is always there to help. I would definitely recommend this professor.

Prof. Beck is hands down the best professors I have ever had. Hes incredibly easy to talk to and it is clear that he cares about the success of his students! As long as you pay attention in class and do your homework, it should be an easy A.
Beck is the nicest professor I've ever had. He isn't there to trick you. He wants all of his students to succeed and its evident. Just show up and do the work and you'll pass with ease.

Duane Beck is fantastic! His classes are really easy but he keeps them interesting and funny. He's worked in the industry for years so he knows what he's talking about and he makes sure that every student is succeeding and cares about everyone's education. Class and projects are very easy. Just don't bring up Chinese steel around him! (IYKYK)

Duane knows what he's talking about due to his years of experience in industry and in academia. You can come to him with just about any problem and he'll be able to help you find a solution. His classes are definitely too easy, but he does a good job of making sure that students absorb the material.

Duane cares about the success of his students. If you get a bad grade, he will let you redo it within reason. Usually cancels Friday class to let students work on the assignment. Midterm is the trickiest part of Duane's class and is based on one lecture about giving presentations. 5 misses allowed. Easy A if you show up and turn in assignments.
Great professor. Caring, knowledgeable, and flexible. Class is super easy. At least once a week class is option so there is time to work on homework, and the homework takes less than 30min to do.
He explains everything that you need to know in a clear way and is always willing to help. He also makes the class laugh and takes the class outside the classroom to explore other machines.
Class is a lot of fun and everyone is often laughing. Passing this class is easy as long as you do your homework and show up. The tests are easy to study for as long as you do the homework.

Duane has a lot of real world experience and is good about applying it and making what is otherwise really boring material somewhat interesting. He wants all his students to pass and knows it is boring so he makes classes very easy. Provides study guides before exams with all the questions on it, but you have to show up to class to get it.
Tough guy
Very nice professor, always willing to help you. Easy class to pass, just show up and that's it.
Took this course as a technical elective. He's a great professor and very inspirational. Offers help if you need it.
Great Professor ! Two thumbs up,  He teaches with Knowledge and his own experiences. Homework Is easy make sure you do it!

Most criminal justice  professors are great and prof Dicaro is one of the best , he is great. Come to class, participate, take notes and I am sure you will pass.  One midterm and One really fun group project. There is a final put its optional, only two people took it so as you can see its an easy class. its an easy A if you just do a lil work
Great professor, slides were very informative and the two grades are Midterm (easy) and Group Project (fun). Great CJ class

Great Professor and funny guy. Took roll call by last name. Kind of lengthy take-home midterm, big but fun group project and no final. We even had a field trip to the Rochester 911 center. Very approachable after/before class. Fun class participations. Answers emails quick. Great person to stay in touch with. Cares about his students.

Easy class, he said in the beginning of the quarter that there might be a final, there wasn't, there was a group project, and a mid-term, put in a little effort and its easy. Also, he a really nice guy and classes are short.

Whoa, completely wrong. This teacher is fantastic, he's extremely friendly and easy to talk to. His class's are short and he gives you a handout for every lecture which he bases his midterm on. The class consists of a lengthy take home test and a big group project. Put in some effort and it's easy. One of the better professors in CJ, and no final.

Nice guy who I think genuinely cares about students, but he is just not a good teacher. A bit more helpful in office hours, but still tough to understand what he is trying to teach you. Also, he assigns way too much homework, although he gives a lot of extra points on homework at the end of the semester

Changed tests to all short answer and is relentless with how strict his grading is on each problem. Useless lectures, I spent most of my time with every grad tutor. Lectures wasn't mandatory but there was a pop quiz every week. Unclear about what material to emphasize on and made us do many MasteringChemistry problems without teaching us how.

Absolutely terrible, assigns 50+ homework problems on MasteringChemistry, none of which have anything to do with what you do in class. Nobody in the class has a clue what is going on. Be prepared to teach yourself an entire course in organic chem.
Class was relatively easy, he provides old exams, of which half the questions are copied word for word. Haven't learned anything, but not too hard to earn my A.

The class isn't easy, but he is a really nice guy. He is really intelligent and sometimes has a hard time explaining things clearly, but not a bad teacher. The class wasn't too boring and getting an A was possible if you worked for it!

You would be better off teaching yourself. He gives 5 bonus points for going to class but lectures are useless. His tests have nothing to do with what he teaches.And the essay questions are ridiculous. grading is inconsistent. it seems easy at first but tests are 90% of the grade and they are very difficult.  but 75=B.

Worst professor I've had so far at RIT. Can't teach, makes the subject impossible to learn. After 2 quarters with him, all I've done was lower my GPA by getting 2 B's in his classes. DO NOT take him. If he's the only one teaching organic, WAIT for someone else!! You will be thankful. His lectures consist of him drawing random reactions.

He really is evil. This class is horrible bc Smith doesn't know how to teach. He is always 5 minutes late to class, and never answers question students ask in a straight manner. He called me stupid once, when I went to his office hours. NEVER again. I had a freaking 4.0 until I had to take his class!! Read the text. His lectures are useless.

CAN NOT TEACH. What he covers in lecture seems simple, but the test questions are WAY more difficult. Often takes the first 10 minutes of a 50 min lecture to set up, or 20 minutes to pass out a test, and wonders why people don't complete it. Assigns homework to topics that will be covered in future lectures. Incredibly frustrating. Avoid.

Attendance isn't mandatory but might as well be due to extra credit. Never administers tests on time, usually 10 to 15 minutes late and wonders why students don't complete exams. Lectures are difficult to follow and never follow the syllabus. The only way to learn anything in this class is to talk to the TA's and to read text independently.

Dr. Thomas is a great guy, with that said organic is hard and his teaching style is so so, but there is so much to the subject that he did the best he could.  Ive seen grades for other classes and he seems to get an avg of a B for his , The book is very helpful and is used constantly he may not get to everything he puts on a test,which is a problem
Organic is hard enough...dont take him. Nice guy but horribly hard to follow when he is teaching. Had to curve tests by 30 points and willing to give a D to students with 30%.
He is never on schedule with the syllabus but he expects you to read the chapters on you own time and he tests you on them even though he didn't lecture on them! Seems like he is totally clueless.

I went to every class, I went to office hours, I had a private tutor, My dad is a chemist and gave me supplemental reading material, I did all homework assignments, I read the book cover-to-cover, I asked questions and reviewed every test and quiz with Dr. Smith, AND I had study partners... and you wanna know the result? A C+! WHAT?!?!

Great Professor if you really want to learn stuff. easy accessible, and very knowledgeble, if you just want to earn the course credits, you might have a hard time. it is really a good course for some body who is interested

Worst teacher I have ever had at RIT. Might know a lot about the subject but definitely does not portray it to the class. Can NOT teach. Stick with Turner if you are thinking of dropping, he is much worse!!! Each test is formatted differently so in addition to memorizing the book/material/hw you have a different test each time. :(
Unfair and unclear grading. Avoid this professor if possible.

Professor Jacobs is very passionate about open-source and covers it in-depth and breadth in the class. Plans and assignment times changed a lot, sometimes being moved weeks forward. Attendance was mandatory with no benefit of going or paying attention, and lectures could get boring.

Cares about student feedback and working with them to make course better with each iteration of it. humanitarian speakers boring are for people who care more about private industry but I signed up for the course that has "humanitarian" in the name. other than the speakers, great class.

comment: Very kind and accessible. He is one of the most understanding professors I have ever had, and is a lenient grader. Always available for outside help and responds quickly to emails.
Very disorganized. Not recommended if you enjoy any semblance of structure in a class.
The class is pretty easy, but assignments are not explained very clearly and can be confusing.
Incredibly disorganized. Input the wrong grade for assignments on several occasions. Not recommended.

Overall a very fun professor. You can tell he is really passionate about open-source and is involved in many communities at RIT. My only complaint would be class organization. There are always discrepancies in the syllabus and projects are very vague. Both SJ and the TA seemed to have poor planning which was annoying at times.
Overall, good class. Not very difficult. Its one of those classes that you get out what you put in. However, you can use this class as an easy A too.

comment: Fun professor, even at 8am. Prof Jacobs was very personable, and I enjoyed his class a lot. IGME 110 was kind of a special case in which the meeting times were more of a workshop/work period, and all of the learning was asynchronous, but the way the class was structured was pretty good. There were some bumps bc of covid online learning, overall ok.

Oh god. This has to have been the worst class I ever took. A Production Studio where we produced almost nothing. The class spent the semester working on a Point and Click adventure. There are 19 people in the class, and it's a PROGRAMMINGDESIGN major. No dedicated art majors, no motivation, and teacher missed half the classes. Avoid at all costs!

Was great for GDD1 was critical of some project ideas but only because the students didn't take time to really research or pitch game correctly.  Lots of reading, sure but often draws exam questions straight from the main ideas of the passages not the little details.  Easy exams as long as you mildly pay attention
Often too critical about student ideas and projects. Canceled class FIVE minutes before it started (8am class) TWICE. Horrible communication skills and is often biased towards women.

While I understand Game Design is a new and upcoming field, that should be no excuse to teach it like one. We were required to buy 4 textbooks; one was barely referenced on the exams. He procrastinated grading. He cancelled class twice (one time 14 minutes before class). His lectures have little focus. Do yourself a favor and avoid this professor.
More work than any other HCI section.  Assigned overed 300 pages of reading material on the 7th week!
Oh yea, Jacobs is the man!

Insightful and understanding about the difficulties of the program. He is very knowledgeable about the material he teaches, and is great at explaining difficult concepts to learn by providing a plethora of examples and visual aids. Assignments for his classes match their intended objectives with fair difficulty. He is an overall caring professor.
Very kind and understanding professor. Always prepared with great lectures.
sweet and wonderful

Wonderful and sweet professor!  Kurz gives us insight on the history of American education as well as the history of Deaf education and gives us the opportunities to look back at what education was like in those times.  Very eye-opening and fun course!
His lectures are on point and he invites class participation. It's usually easy to sit back and enjoy. It's also very applicable from the literature.

If you're genuinely interested in philosophy of mind, I couldn't recommend professor Suits enough. One of the most brilliant professors I've ever encountered, he teaches with the intention of imparting knowledge and wisdom.

I'm not sure whether my experience with Dr. Suits was positive because he's a good professor or because Symbolic Logic is a good class.  It's probably a combination of the two.  You should take Symbolic Logic, and you should take it with Dr. Suits.

Suits hit the sweet spot between math and philosophy for me. This class, Symbolic Logic, is pretty simple if you have a logic or engineering background already, but Suits did his best to make sure even people new to boolean algebra have plenty of footholds. Assignments were short, frequent, and quickly graded. Easy credit for my immersion, too.

Suits is calm, patient, an interesting lecturer, and seems to genuinely enjoy philosophy. Abstract concepts have never been so successfully communicated to me before taking his classes. As long as you show understanding of the topics he's presented you will do well in his class. If you are truly interested in philosophy, take his classes!

Taking Intro to Ethics with this professor can be easy since there is no homework, just quizzes. The attendance is not mandatory. You just show up in the class for quiz and exams. But beware, there is not a lot of points in quizzes and tests. You can lose a lot of points over bad quizzes and etc. Easy professor but Be careful of quizzes and exams.

He is a very nice guy, always making little jokes.  Teaches the course at a bit too much of an elementary level, but explains things well.  I can't speak for his other courses, but if you are considering taking Philosophy of Mind, take it with Aguilar instead.  It's his area of expertise, and he teaches it *incredibly* well.

The textbook is a little hard to understand but he clarifies things in class. However, he is extremely BORING! Most people are on their laptops but if you are able to hear his lectures you should be able to pass easily.

Great teacher, made topics a lot of fun and really enjoys having conversations with students in class and is open to their ideas. Would love to take more classes with him. If your are a Philosophy major or concentrator make sure you take a class with him. And ask him about Epicurus!

This guy is utterly useless. He creates his own text is an absolute egoist about it. His lectures are mundane and put half the class to sleep. He doesn't make himself available outside of the class. Avoid at all costs

Great guy! Interesting lectures for the most part, and clarifies difficult readings daily. With the exception of 2 philosophers, he makes understanding difficult-to-read passages a breeze. Tests are take home, quizzes open book. However excitement of class discussions depends on your class.
The notes you take can cover 50-60% of what is in tests. The rest -- you find yourself through reading.Lots of difficult reading. Overall the teacher is very nice and helpful

4 tests, 3 of which were take-home. You never knew when he'd hand out a test because of his disorganized nature, but you get a week & they're all straight out of the reading so time was never an issue. Lectures broadly covered the material and went into several  philosophical sidebars. Take if random discussion is your thing; avoid if it's not.
This is the most chill guy you will ever meet. He's a fun teacher, nice guy... Take his classes if at all possible, it's an easy A and fun.

A great, great teacher. Has a fantastic teaching style. He has a great sense of humor that makes being in class and participating a joy. It is true his test are lenient but the lack of emphasis on the grade makes me want to sit, listen and interact all the more instead of trying to memorize everything. I would take him again in a heartbeat

This guy is great!  He makes an interesting topic even more interesting than it has to be the uninteresting topics are better.  He is really funny and energetic and the way he teaches keeps the class awake.  His grading is really lenient and his tests are really easy, if you copy everything he writes you are sure to pass.
Easy grader, makes the class interesting. Definately take him if you get the chance.
Just excellent.  I don't think any professor in the Philosophy department can beat Dr. Suits' teaching style.  His lectures are never boring, and his grading is very lenient.  An A+ professor!
Class was Asyncronous, with one weekly lecture followed by work on Achive. I learned a lot from this class and Dr. Schenkel made it super interesting to work with these topics!

This class was mostly online, there are lectures once a week in person, but they often got cancelled. Shes a good grader and is quick through lectures. You will be required to buy an online textbook and complete most the assignments through there. One thing to note is, she has a pretty strict no technology rule in lectures.

I like this professor since she was easy to talk to through email or after class. The lectures are okayish. But it's a super easy class in my opinion. attend class and you will be good. Theres only two exams. Most of the homework is on Macmillian and only four discussion posts and one 4-5 page essay is all you have to do to pass the class.
Uses mandatory outside textbook for assignment submissions. Getting above a 40% costs 108$. Dropping this class and looking for another.

Took an online Health Psyc course from this instructor. She's pretty knowledgable and gives you good feedback. A lot of cool topics and interesting videos. The last project is awesome. Read the book, do the assignments, and you'll be good.

Dr. Schenkel is a really nice professor, but I don't feel like she did anything to teach us. It was an asynchronous class and the main source of learning was an online textbook with quizzes. No lectures or work from her. I don't feel like much stuck with me either. But if you're just there for the A, I'd recommend her.

Loved this class!! Really interesting topics and learned a lot. She gets back to you quickly when you email her. Good at helping and answering questions. Quizzes are straightforward. Very cool videos that make the course interesting. Take her if you can!
