comment: Wants you to read everything 4 times. If you don't get it try again. Missed negative sign makes the answer wrong and no partial credit. If he likes you you'll do well, if not you're screwed. Tries to be funny and fails miserably.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: He claims to give partial credit if your work shows you understood the question, but will give none. Will often cancel office hours when he shows up to them for various reasons. Gets extremely upset and defensive against any ind of criticism or disagreement. Is proud of how many students drop his class as if he thinks it means he's a good teacher

I learned a lot from Takahashi but it wouldn't show in my tests. I'm typically a pretty good test taker but I was pulling C's on all of his. He does warn you about the difficulty in the beginning of class and he's not wrong. I think half my class ended up dropping. He also has a ridiculously strict attendance policy.

Takahashi is the worst professor I have ever had. People say that if you pay attention you will learn a lot, but that's not true. You will have to spend hours teaching yourself on your own because he will do nothing but berate you and claim you don't try hard enough. He is a tough grader and gives zero partial credit. Avoid him if you can.

This class was impossibly hard. I got a 58 on my first exam and that was actually a pretty good score compared to what other people in my class got. Exams are graded unfairly with no partial credit. Homework has no completion component to the grade, just 3 random problems are selected and graded for correctness. I'd avoid this class at all costs.

Takahashi is a very reasonable professor, he lays out what he expects and he does not joke, all the things on the syllabus are for real. But you will learn a lot if you are willing to.  He is extremely passionate and willing to help to students and goes to great lengths for both the material and the students. You won't get an A, if you care.

Don't count on him for any help in his course. He does not teach material in class. His tests are impossible and most questions/ subjects were never mentioned prior to testing. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. Most take this course because it is required, but as far as Takahashi is concerned your life is Linear algebra.

This course was extremely tough and it will require everything you can muster. However, he warns you on the first day. You need to pay attention every second of the lecture or else you will be left in the dust and have no idea what's happening. Switch professors or drop immediately if you struggle in the first few weeks. Office hours are important.

On the first day he will give you a list. Be honest with yourself... if you are not ready to do EVERYTHING on the list then switch classes immediately. The tests are all questions from the homework and class. They are difficult to complete though so take the time to learn it well the first time and REALLY understand it.

Takahashi is a great guy and really wants his students to succeed. However, he does not make that success very easy. Many of his test questions are directly from lecture notes or hw, but those problems are not at all easy to do in a testing environment. He moves quickly, but will also go out of his way to help if you need it. You won't get an A.

Takahashi will tell you on the first day of class that his class is tough and if you just want to get it over with and get a good grade to change to a different section. However, he is a fantastic professor and really into teaching. You'll learn a lot in his class, but you might not get very good grades since the exams can be long and challenging.
Difficult class, not the worst teacher but definitely not the best either.

I took discrete with him, and he must be one of the most genius professors at this school. Can be VERY hard to keep up with, so don't get behind!!! If you're willing to put in the effort, though, I'd highly recommend taking him. Gave lots of partial credit in discrete, I can't speak for other classes. Class average was a C .

If you get stuck with this, drop or switch immediately. He is obsessed with proofs and often derails from the topic at hand. I had him for Calc II. His tests are extremely difficult despite being direct copies of examples sometimes. He gives almost no partial credit. If you do all parts of a question correctly but get a wrong answer you get 1/10.

Mr. Takahashi is a genius professor, but his exams are very very difficult and the way he teaches students is so confusing and hard to follow his lecture. If the question worth 10 points and you do the process right but the final answer is wrong, he will give you 2 out of 10 points. I DO NOT RECOMMEND TO TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

His classes are constant notes with no explanation. If you don't attend office hours you will likely fail. He has little to no partial credit on exams. The exams are the hardest thing I have taken in the entirety of my college career and they are extremely difficult to prepare for because of the amount of proofs that need to be memorized.

For most, Takahashi was probably a hilarious professor. He's really knowledgeable and sometimes derails. One day in Discrete Math we began talking about Linear Algebra topics. My suggestion if you get him is to study your notes religiously and go to office hours. If he knows who you are, he's willing to help you out.

Do not take a class with this guy, your life will be living hell! His tests are impossible! Every question consists of proofs and not anything that is like normal problems the homework. Grades extremely harsh. Does not get the hint that people are only taking the class because their major requires it.
Will reduce your grade drastically if you miss more than 2 classes in the semester. A letter grade for each one after if I remember correctly.

He holds students to higher standards than most. Tests were alright, except for the final, which focused a lot more on the material at the very end than the previous material and was overall very difficult. He is a very funny guy and cares about his students.

He is brilliant, but I would never take this class if given the option. I got shoved into this class by my advisor for my first year. Drop the first chance you get, he seems like a very level headed, good professor, but he grades EXTREMELY HARSH. Only graded homework and tests, tests are worth 300660. Class Avg was C, he tests are very hard.

Takahashi is extremely passionate about math and it shows. It is a very do-able class if you are prepared to put the in the work needed. Homework due every other class. Attendance is 10% of grade. Only 3 tests and a final for graded assignments other than HW. Awesome teacher, goes on tangents sometimes, but overall would definitely take again

Takahashi is a very great individual and he is truly there for his students. He will help you until you fully understand a topic. He will help students until 12AM during his office hours on many occasions. Given this, this will likely be the hardest course you will take. It requires many hours of studying. Lucky to get a C without 110% effort.
He is a really good professor. I learned a lot from his lecture and he also inspired me to declare a minor in mathematic

Prof. Takahashi's passion for math really shows in his lectures. His energy during teaching helped to keep me alert and actively listening. Also, he was consistently available for extra help and always willing to help students as much as it took to get them to understand.

He always says that if you understand his lectures, you will do well in his class, but therein lies the problem.  His lectures are a giant mess  of poor handwriting and personal notation scribbled in almost random locations about the board; they are extremely hard to follow and very fast paced.

Like many have said, this professor goes on many tangents. He is not extremely helpful during class and hard to understand, constantly pushing you to go to his office hours. He will not go over homework problems in class nor post review problems for tests. Tests are far a part, meaning they cover a lot of sections. Formula sheets are not allowed.

Very hard class. Very hard to keep up with note-taking, and are almost forced to come to office hours as a result(which he sometimes cancels). When he does have office hours though, he is very willing to help. Be ready to put in 3x the amount of credit hours in extra, per week. Also, give up weekends.

I'll start with saying this man is very intelligent, but should never step foot in a classroom.  His lectures are incredibly hard to follow, makes up his own homework and lectures. Didn't even finish all the material and expected us to learn it all on our own for the final. Somewhat helpful in office hours, but cancels them often and unannounced.

Very very tough professor. Really makes you go above and beyond the basics of the class. He's a very nice man, but I know of many friends that took diff eq with other professors and easily passed, and I'm most likely going to fail his class. More than half of the class failed his 2nd test, no curve, just keeps going.

The worst professor I have taken so far, and most likely the worst I'll ever take. He goes off on tangents, uses his own notation, doesn't explain concepts very well and is just an overall bad professor. The average grade for the class is an F, and he does not curve the grade. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. BEWARE!!!

He is quite possibly THE worst professor I have ever had. Half the class failed the 2nd exam, and he only you extra credit if you got above a 90. Can't explain the subject at all, keeps going on tangents, then scribbles the remaining lecture on the board then dismisses class without explaining anything. Expects student to use his notation.

Lectures are clear. He does go off tangent all the time and rush through the rest. However if he doesn't cover something in class then it's not on the exam or homework. Very flexible and accommodating homework and test schedule. Test are taken straight from lecture examples and homework problems.

Uses his own notations causing confusion in the class. Does not curve any tests even when roughly 2/3 of the class is at risk of failing. Goes off on tangents about things unrelated to the class and then rushes to finish lecture. Goes above what is required rather than focusing on what students do not understand unless you go to office hours.
He is an excellent professor, but he expects his students to do a reasonable amount of work outside of class. Does not curve tests. Has very accommodating office hours.

He acts like a real person compared to other professors, he actually has emotions and cares. Intro to Psych is a GPA booster, his quote. He basically gives you the answers to tests. Interactive and funny lectures. Textbook reading is suggested but I could not find the time, sorry. Take notes during class and show up, you'll succeed. Take it.

This class is easier to understand if you know physics, but if you move past the heavy physics-based portions then the class is fine. Lectures were nothing special but he did demos each week + he went out of his way on review days to make the midterm and final bearable. He's also a hilarious lecturer, which made it worth it to go to class.

He's a funny guy, but my GOD can he go on tangents. The class is physics-based and he's a physics nerd, but those two things make the class impossibly boring/hard for someone who doesn't fully understand physics. The textbook is practically unreadable, and he simply reads from the book or slides during lecture.

He doesn't really enjoy developmental psychology, but he made the class really easy so we would all do well. If you go to class he gives you the weekly quiz answers. He lectures on Tuesdays and Thursdays are class discussions. If you speak once you get credit. Tests are super easy because you go over answers ahead of time. Study the weekly quizzes.
Real passion for the subject. Highly recommend going to his office hours with any question, he will be more than happy to help.

Professor Goodwill was a good teacher for the first 2 weeks but he got some chronic depression and ever since then, he has always come into class very tired and in a terrible mood. He started belittling students when more clarification was requested. Makes students figure out the Calculus instead of giving us an example first. Very strict grader

I hope I have Mr. Goodwill again this year. He stays on task, will take the time to answer student questions, and tells personal stories to motivate us for tests. He doesn't pile on work, and just give us enough to make sense of the unit. Office hours with him were extremely helpful.
Great professor. Cares about the students and actually wants them to do well. Would take him again if given the choice

Taking Goodwill? Get ready for a C. His workshops and homework will not in any way prepare you for the quizzes and tests, as on those he just spikes the difficulty to an unreasonable amount. Also his lectures are unclear. He likes to make a bad analogy and when nobody understands the material he gets upset. Bad lecture+hard tests+unfair graderno

Great teacher BUT grading system is an ABSOLUTE MESS. All the times I have had him, nobody has above a C or D before the Final Exam..... Very frustrating. I have a 3.5 GPA and his 2 classes are my only C's.

comment: Quizzes every week and 3 tests throughout the semester.  Willing to go out of his way to make time to help you.  Makes class interesting

He is super organized and a really helpful professor.  He will fit his schedule around yours for office hours and if he can't meet with you in person will skype with you at crazy late hours.  His tests are tough, but fair so you should use the classwork activities to study off of- not the study guides (they are usually way easier than the tests).

Best professor I've had at RIT. He is understanding and funny as hell. You can go to his office almost anytime, in or out of office hours, and he is more than happy to do anything to help you. Be it rephrasing a topic, putting it in terms you understand, etc. Extremely unorthodox way of grading, but I found it to be more than helpful and very fair.

Goodwill was very understanding on a personal level and very practical on a academic level. He understands that Math isn't everyone's whole life, unlike some professors at RIT. You must take diligent notes in nearly every class to get a decent grade however. Tests are difficult, and he tends to ask odd-ball questions. Good professor.

He was very helpful in class, he'd stop the lecture to answer any questions and everything. Class format is very organized and you always know what you need to learn for upcoming tests and quizzes (it is all laid out on the schedule!)  Pretty cool guy as well. Funny and clever, he'll make you laugh quite a bit. Made me actually enjoy calc

He is literally the worst teacher at RIT. Doesn't teach, puts problem on board tells you to solve it, 20 minutes later when everyone is confused he tries to solve it and can't. Horrible, class average was a 50 by the end of the year. STAY AWAY, GOOGLE IS MORE HELPFUL AT LEARNING CALC THAN HIM

Here's why I'm gonna get a 2nd C in his class: always begins lecture with an example, leavin you oblivious of today's topic until later;  class ends and you have no recollection of the lesson; workshop is 2 days after lesson; makes you work super hard for something with little credit (no one bothers); he has 6 kids and 4 classes -- slow grading

Grades are arbitrary.  Takes MONTHS to return quizzes (not exaggerating).  Quizzes are cumulative which is great unless you haven't gotten the last 3 back and don't know what you did wrong.  Gives you gold star stickers for participation (yes really).  Would never take a class from him again.
can be very confusing and talks about random stuff at times

Great professor! TESTS:none. QUIZZES:weekly, cumulative, in that you can/should retry questions from a previous week. HOMEWORK:usually weekly on MyMathLab, sometimes multiple 20-40 problem assignments due in same week, but flexible in due dates if visit OFFICE HOURS:super flexible, helps explain topics or help with homework. Totally recommend him.

Take this professor. He teaches realistically - he tears math down and builds it back up. He hates "magic spells" and will teach you the logic behind everything (sounds worse then it is, but is tremendously useful.) His grading "skill system" leaves a lot of room for a late comeback, and he will help you pass.

Goodwill is a good teacher and is fun to have.  A few problems with him are that he sometimes gets distracted in class and rambles leaving less time to learn and he spends too much time trying to explain his math philosophies rather than teaching. He is a good teacher and I would recommend him, but he needs to spend more time teaching during class.

Really awesome professor! Very clear and approachable, and willing to help students outside of class. Interesting approach to grading-quiz on each subject and these can be retaken on following quiz days throughout the semester. Also lighthearted and funny!
His class is so damn fun and chill. 2 hours in class without falling asleep

Professro Tim is extremely helpful. He does whatever he can to make students learn. He loves teaching math and he is significantly good at it. He is a math nerd. He is funny. Students don't get bored in his class, at least I didn't. He has an excellent method of testing students. You can always get an A if work hard.Also, he uses my math lab-v good

Confusing lectures, often allowed students to work at board so rest of class copies an incorrect example. Grading is pretty arbitrary so suck up and go to his office hours. He is fun to have in class though very laid back.

Excellent professor! One of my favorites so far. Explains all the concepts crystal clear and will gladly sit down to help you if you don't understand something. Awesome sense of humor too and very much approachable! Easily, one of the best math professors at RIT :]
Wonderful sense of humor. great teacher
He's the man.  No tests, just collects some work in folder you turn in, can easily copy, and get an A. Just be sure you get him for the next in sequence or your screwed.

Best Professor ever!  He really understands what he teaches and will find a way to help you understand, all you have to do is ask.  I went from a D with a bad professor to an A with Goodwill.  My only regret is that I couldn't take him this quarter.

Excellent math teacher. In fact, best math teacher I ever had. Even though that I suck at Math, with his help and support a got a B. He takes his time to explain whatever needs to be explained, he never rushs when the class doesn't understand something. Very funny and nice guy, always smiling and takes everything easy. ( GO AHEAD WITH HIM!)

Great professor tons of fun to have and his classes are always fun, can grade tough but always makes it possible to help a bad grade. he let my class replace our lowest 2 test grades with the final, we only took to tests too. i still visit his class just to hang out with him

He treats the study portfolio like it's the most necessary component of the class.  More of the students time is spent perfecting past material in the portfolio than learning and understanding new material.  He is very helpful and approachable, but he believes his portfolio is the best and only way to teach, which, it is not.

He can definitely make your week extremely stressful, but he's a great teacher and loves teaching.  Doesn't use a textbook but guides you through building a portfolio of organized notes which is tedious but makes for great study material.  Fun to listen to, appreciates hard work and honesty.

Favorite calc prof. Fun to have and doesn't require a textbook so money saved, BUT WARNING, even though a textbook isn't required for purchase, he makes you create your own textbook through organized notes that he checks for points. It is very helpful but WILL take numerous hours to complete ESPECIALLY if you fall behind at the end of the course.

Tim is an interesting character. He cannot decide how he wants to teach his course, but on whatever method he attempts he will put his heart into it. You can always approach Tim with problems, both personal and in math. He's a great caring guy. He can make your week REALLY stressful, but it will pay off in the end. Does a decent job overall.
The best. Knows how to teach. Never gave up on me, even when i was struggling.

Always helpful and loves teaching! Great professor, actually made me miss calculus when I was done. I would highly recommend!  He wants you to try your best and do well in his class, something that is hard to find in professors now.

TAKE HIS CLASS. One of the best teachers I have ever had. I hate math and enjoyed class, even doing well in it. You'll use the text book he wrote, but he gives you a copy of what you need for homework. He helps you a ton and while some problems are more difficult, it is totally worth it. You HAVE TO WORK, but core questions will seem SUPER EASY.
Great calc teacher!!! Would never want a different professor for this cl03ass. Workshops are easy and tests and quizzes are not hard if you look over note sheets. Definitely Recommended!
Mr Goodwill is the man. That's all.
Awesome
Differential Equations: Best Math Professor EVER; Not exactly easy, but he sure can teach and make things clear, which is the most important thing to look for. Teachers this good are rare at RIT.
Fantastic instructor, taught me more than any other math instructor ever has, highly recommended
Great great teacher. He takes a different approach to teaching calc that really is intriguing for the students. and btw... NEVER PULL OUT!

Both Tim and the TA did not help me when I had questions, they would get me halfway through then give up. I had class during his office hours and he would not accommodate. Homeworks would take 3+ hours, since he uses his own book. Lectures did not teach skills needed on tests, workshops or homeworks.
Study hard for his tests which can be quite difficult. Grades on a curve most times. Funny guy, I just didn't like him for some reason. Had to really earn my A.
very hard, dont take him

Goodwill is the best professor that I have had thus far at RIT. If he is teaching any math course, then sign up with him. He is so helpful, especially during his office hours. Trust me, he is fantastic. You will not regret signing up with him. Greatest guy ever.
Goodwill is the man! Trust Me

GREAT TEACHER! It had been almost a year since I'd taken the pre-req to his class but he explained everything so well that it was no problem at all. Very helpful outside of class, and very understanding if you have to miss a class for something important. He really wants you to succeed, and his optional homeworks let you know what is on the test.

Best math teacher i have ever had, and that is saying a lot.  Very easy to work with and is always available, he makes class hard but if you put in the effort you will learn and remember a lot.  Real funny guy always makes class interesting even at 8am, I always look for his name for math classes.  A++++will buy from again, fast shipper

He is a nice guy, but is very hard grader. His test are not what you expect them to be. He says he will be available, but always gives reasons why he was not there. He was sick a lot of the time, so stay away during the winter quarter. If you like math and you like a challenge take him. If you need to take this course dont take him
I love this guy. He broke the class down into the parts we needed to understand and made sure we knew it. His work is challenging, but you'll know it by the time he's done. Great teacher.

Calculus sucks...but Tim was a great teacher and a really fun and nice guy. One of my favorite professors here at RIT and definitley my favorite math teacher ever. If you wanna learn something and have fun definitley take a class from him!

He was a nice teacher, but very hard grader. His test are extremely hard, and the final was very difficult. If you get the correct answer for a test, you might not get full credit because its not the work he wanted to see. If you want a teacher with a personality take him, but he will be hard.

Awesome teacher! Best math professor I have ever had. He gives a lot of extra credit, and if you do the extra work you will really know your stuff. He hangs out in the library and loves helping students.
Awesome guy, brings a lot of good humor to the class. Tests are very fair, and he gives LOTS of extra credit. However, the homework will destroy you, and it is graded on correctness.

Very nice, very good at teaching, is VERY willing to explain stuff at office hours, but he assigns enough homework to make you suicidal..and to further it, he makes them up, not the book, so sometimes they're hard as heck.  I've finished way too many beers while pulling all nighters of 10 hours of homework straight for his class - but great teach..
Project based calc 3, he doesn't teach it often, but he is good at it. Very generous with corrections, and great at presenting the material.
Very good professor. Tells math stories and is very funny. Pretty hard material but he made it both interesting and fun.

Funny guy who always kept class interesting and lively. Goes at a pretty fast pace but always willing to slow down and explain if you get lost. Hard tests and almost impossible HWs, but plenty of opportunities to get extra credit and boost your grade.  Relies heavily on mycourses and is always on there to answer student ?'s immediately.

Good teacher, very helpful at office hours, very clear.  This was his first time teaching Calc C this semester (20073) and he assigned A LOT of homework and it was VERY hard and it was graded VERY badly (by a TA), that combined with the fact that it was worth 90% of the final (160% of a test) made it barely bearable.  Other than the h/w he's great.

Amazing teacher, with a lot of patiences and understandings with the students' needs. Homework and tests submit online but a good opportunity to get help from him. Good class and good teacher, recommend you to take him!

Best teacher I've ever had at RIT. He writes all the notes on his computer so you can get then if you miss a class. Goes over everything thoroughly, and is always willing to help. He came to every class, even when he had problems with his back. No textbook because he writes all his own homework. Made a lot of jokes and kept class interesting. :)
Awesome teacher, had him for algebra (made extremely easy) and surprisingly a fencing class. Fun in and out of class
Awesome Professor. I took my entire Calc sequence and he has an uncanny ability to make math fun. I highly recommend him.

Really good teacher.  Easy to understand and learn from.  I'm really bad at math and I actually liked this course.  The professor definitely made what I would say is a bad course good.   I would recommend him.

I hate him when i first took his class because he requires you to submit your hws online. Therefore, you ll have to scan like 15 pages of integrals which takes forever. Later on, I found out that he's a great professor, his lectures are good and it was easy to understand whats going on.
Goodwill's cool. The way he teaches is very easy to understand. He makes up his own homework and his own tests and makes it very easy to get a good grade in the class.
He's the hottest hotness.
Great teacher to have, always helpful.  Homework is hard but it prepares you for exams.  Nice guy overall.

I took Goodwill for both calc 1 and 2, and has been my faviorate teacher.  willing to put in the time to help you and go out of his way to help you pass.  lots of work but you really know your stuff when you are done. great professor!
Gr8 professor, gr person. Teaches excellent, explains clearly each and every concept.

Good professor, I hated college math, but his course I did fairly well in. I found it to be a lot more fun than most of the other courses i had taken. I reccommend taking him if you get the opportunity.

Superb! I love Tim goodwill's teaching style, hes extreamly informative and you will actually learn tons from this course; instead of just memorizing theory. he makes math fun by throwing in stories about his life and math history (belive it or not). going to his class is a pleasure and it is easy if u study. he never fails to let students down.
Cool guy, easy going, difficult class but he is helpful and clear.  Good lecture and notes.  Curves a lot to help out!  Def recommended
awesome teacher. takes time to answer questions, and actually cares when his students dont understand something.

absolutely THE best math professor i have EVER had. Amazing, makes sure you understand, goes out of the way to help  and presents it in a way that  is easy to understand (uses his computer so the notes can easily be posted online)his online hw pertains to the stuff done in class the book work can get annoying you actually WANT to go to his class...

Absolutely awesome teacher. I took Calc I previous and I hated Calc before his class. Never got above a C with my last professor.  I ended up with an A based on the way he teaches. I wish I could have him for Calc II, and want him for Dif. Eq.
Eh, he's ok I guess.
tims the man
Pretty cool professor. He explains things very well, and takes time to make sure you learn. Likes to tell stories, but the lighten the mood and make it seem like less of a class. Which is cool.

Wants everybody to understand what he's talking about but understands that a lot of people don't like math. Is a little hard to get a hold of for extra help, has a tendency to not show up once you have arranged to go see him. Over all, a good guy who tries hard.
Goodwill is awesome.  He teaches very well, and makes a very rare occurence happen; making a Calc. class fun.
One of the best math teachers RIT has to offer.  I recommend him a lot.
Definately the best math teacher I have had. Very knowledgeful, always willing to help, shows you where everything comes from, wish i could take him again!
Had Goodwill for calculus 1,2 and Differential equations...great guy, teaches well, keeps the class focused and on point. Always willing to slow down and help you. Highly recommended
Very helpful professor :)
Good teacher, great grading system, cares more about process then right answer, always willing to help you.  Highly recommended, but not during night course
Take this class! It is worth it and it feels good. Lectors are not boring, and class goes by very fast.

Nice guy-- fun class. MAKE SURE you sign up with a partner because lots of dudes show up.. and unless you wanna get paired up randomly- bring your own massage buddy! Pretty long talks and stories for a massage class, but really helpful and informative with massage techniques. Relaxing class for an easy grade-- just SHOW UP he's big on attendance.
Very nice guy. Knows what he's talking about and is passionate about it. Realloy concerned with the well being of others. Long lectures for a massage class, but they can be intresting.

A nice guy but can be boring. Aside from his long speeches in each class, the actual massage techniques are worth it, proving to be effective and helpful. He is very strict about attendance, only letting two absences. Beware of skipping, if he notices he'll get angry and possibly fail you.

I loved this class with Professor Caraballo! It was super fun and informational, and the class always had interesting discussions. The assignments were fair and deadlines were flexible. 110% recommend!!!

Super chill and laid back. Would only use about 50% of the allotted class time before letting us go, and the work that we were assigned to do was always clear.

I took SWEN261 over the summer. I thought he was a pretty good professor, funny sometimes, and homework are not as hard as I think it would after reading the comments. He grade pretty lenient, as long as you have all the work, and stuff that is required, you will be fine.
dont ask help or else, very sarcastic and instead of helping/pushing u in the right direction he will point out flaws and say you're wrong and should figure it out. Suggest anyone other than this one
He cries about discord channels which makes no sense. He makes you sound dumb and on top of that, he doesn't even help you with the answers.
Good professor, just a hard class

He's willing to help students after class if they're that stuck.

In regards to dealing with deadlines, grades, attendance, or other related matters however, he ends up coming across as overly sarcastic and unhelpful. Worst professor Ive ever had He has no idea how a classroom works n teaches the class based off of classes we dont take and didn't change that when we told him. Good luck trying to understand anything that goes on in class, as the majority of us had no idea what was going on. We relied on teaching ourselves most of the material because it is not explain well and leaves you more confused. Labs are poorly designed too.

Horribly disorganized; many lecture slides had calculation errors and typos, and the graphics were unclear. The professor spoke very quickly and mumbled. good teacher inside and outside of class, classes ussually involve some kind of trip off campus. Casino trip was cool, classes were fun, work isn't too hard and there is plenty of room to be creative. I also took FRANCHISING 0619-506 & REALESTATE 0622-205

Really really easy class. You go to Vegas, Canada, really easy A.. the easiest stupidest class I ever took & Warren G is really nice .

Fantastic! Whatever the class take this guy! You will learn, you will get a good grade (put a little bit of effort into please), and he is fun to talk to. I took a class just to have him as the teacher!

He is funny and easy. He makes you do some work, but if you put some amount of effort you will get an A. I had very little interst in the class itself, I was just completing a required liberal art, but I thoroughly enjoyed his class and wanted to attend lectures. Lots of movies too. I highly recommend if completing Intro to soc

He is perhaps the best professor in sociology department. He enjoys what he teaches and cares much about his students. He is young and very cool guy. If you want to have an easy and friendly professor, take his class!! Lecture are a bit long and there is a large reading, nevertheless, he makes class interesting.
He was a really cool guy who tried to make lectures more like discussions. He was enthusiastic about the topic and a really great professor. Grading was easy as long as you paid a little attention.

He is a really cool guy who really just cares about what he is teaching, not little details when it comes to grades. He is very enthusiastic about what he lectures. As much as I enjoyed the class, there is a good chance you will find yourself asleep a day or two. Good chance for a good grade however.
Easy going professor, teaches the class easily, few essays, lots of bonus chances, and non-mandatory attendence.

nice guy. Encourages students to attend lectures but not required. Plenty of options to make up bad grades. Fairly easy also though one essay i got an A on and his comments were "answers are a bit thin, expand them to improve your grade" so he's a bit unclear.

As a Sociology major I had a hard time in his class. The work is easy but it feels just like busy work. It's easy to zone out in his class. When he lectures or explains something he just sits in a chair motionless and monotone.

One of the youngest professors, he's really good BUT he loves to talk too much! He just follows the notes instead of using his OWN words! Well he's smart! He makes this class easy! No finals, tests and quizzes. If you look for an easy prof..then take him!
Awesome professor.  He'll give weekly readings, two papers for the whole term and one of them is a group presentation that counts as the final which is awesome!
I am an engineering student who was forced to take sociology, but I loved his class! GET HIM IF YOU CAN!

Calc three is a difficult class but Professor Jabamba made it much easier. She gives tons of prep questions for exams and holds study sessions. She also is a fair grader and gives lots of partial credit. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

Professor Jadamba is probably the nicest math teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are really easy to keep up with and understand; she is an INCREDIBLY easy graders and gives bonus questions on exams that test your understanding of the material; finally, she is just a really nice person all around. HWs are also pretty short but very useful.

Basca is by far the best professor I've had, ever, period. She is extremely providing for students, and in terms of a math teacher, is the goat. She gives equation sheets, reference tables, and other utilities ON EXAMS to ensure students can do as well as they can based off of ability, not memory. She's also EXTREMELY lenient with grading. 11/10

Basca is the sweetest and most understanding human alive. She's so genuinely interested in her students and wants them to do well, and always makes herself available if students need help, not just on class content but in life outside her class. On exams, she gives as much credit as she can depending on the work you have shown.

I'm terrible at anything math-related, and yet I passed this class with a (mostly) stress-free A. You need to put in a little work, but her lectures are so comprehensive that even I could grasp concepts quickly. Everything in the lectures/homework is on the quizzes/exams, and she gives thorough review packets before exams. Highly recommend!

This teacher will work with you to get the highest grade you can; she gives many chances. I missed many lectures and still got the grade I got. I believe if I (and I'm a business major) showed up to every class this would've been an easy A. Gives study guides and quizzes that closely match her exams. HW is easy; content match her lectures; take her

Dr. Jadamba made the learning environment absolutely fantastic. Probably one of the best learning experiences I have had in my entire life. She provided great notes, study guides (which were really helpful) and worksheets that would help to reinforce the material with little notes on how to do the math on them.
Writes really clear notes in class. Gives out helpful review sheets for exams. Is accessible outside of class and extremely helpful in office hours.

The course itself, if you have a decent mathematics background, is not difficult. But anything that is difficult is made much easier by Professor Jadamba. She is understanding and mostly clear and her tests are very fair, as well as her quizzes. The homework is not overwhelming and if you care, you will get an A with her instruction.

Had her for Boundary Value Problems. SUPER easy grader. You could get an entire quiz wrong due to an error in one part of the problem and end up with an 11/12. Exams are also pretty self explanatory. Very friendly during office hours and always available for homework help. Would take her for all math classes possible.
Professor Jadamba made differential equations one of the easiest courses I've ever taken.  Just a little studying before each test to supplement her amazing teaching and you're in the clear.

Semi-difficult class made easy by her teaching style. Notes and normally an helpful worksheet each class. Grades fairly easy as long as you show your work. Gives practice problems before the test that are a MUST DO if you want to do well on the test. Overall her class was the best this semester, no issues with handling the conversion.

Not too bad of an accent and just when you get sick of taking notes, she mixes it up with a worksheet.  The material was tough for the first couple weeks, but got much better.  She handled the switch to semsters from quarters better than any of my other professors.

Not a bad teacher, but it can be a bit difficult stay engaged in her class sometimes.  Would recommend sitting in the front of the class.  Otherwise good, gives practice exams before real exams that help a lot.

Very easy teacher. Gives you a practice exam before each test which is almost identical to the test. Only problem is she is a little hard to understand. Other than that the class is an easy A if you do the homework.

She is the best professor. I absolutely loved her she is very easy her exams are fair. She gives out a practice one and if you do it you'll get an A on every exam. She'e so nice. She made the most difficult subject easy. I actually waited for her to come back from having a baby to take her in the spring.
One of the best calc teachers I've come across, extremely helpful and her review sheets strongly reflect the tests

Basca is very helpful and a very easy grader. The course is tough, but she explains everything well enough to help you on the final. Definitely take her if you can. One of the best math teachers RIT has to offer.
Very nice lady, very helpful.
She is the best.
Very helpful, excellent.

Basca is the best calc teacher I have ever had. She is a very fair grader, is always eager to help you understand during workshops. She is easy to understand and you are sure to get an A as long as you do the work and come to class.
She was absolutely great. I was sick for a while and she made sure I was taken care of. She grades very fairly and consistently and always answers questions when asked.

I Really feel like giving her many terrible ratings, because with the current round of registration she filled up fast. This woman is a wonderful teacher and you shoud take her class, especially if you hate powerpoint
You'll warm up to her accent within two or three weeks. She's a really fair grader and a good teacher. Take her class if you can.
Extremely helpful, an easy class to get an A

Basca is a really great professor. Homework and quizzes every week. Gives solutions to everything and is willing to answer hw questions in class. Tests were fair. Just pay attention and do the work and an A is not hard to get!

Basca is the hidden gem of RIT. No one registers for her classes because they are usually 8am, but she is THE best calculus teacher at RIT. At first she can be difficult to understand, but after a few days you get used to her accent. She is always willing to help you if you dont understand and is very fair with grading. Take her class
One of the nicest professors at RIT.  I thoroughly enjoyed having her.

Professor Jadamba is fantastic! I have taken her for calc 1 and 2, and am rearranging my class schedule to have her for calc 3 next quarter. She assigns one hw a week, one quiz a week, and two-three exams per quarter. Her workshop questions relate very well to the quiz/exam questions, and she gives plenty of help if you need it. Take her classes!

Basca is amazing! You only use the textbook for homework, everything she she teaches and explains to you herself. She answers any question you ask her efficiently, and she is always happy and smiling. Hands down the best calc teacher at RIT.

Some claimed she was hard to understand; I had no trouble. Fair grader, drops lowest homework and quiz grade at end of quarter. Homeworks assigned every class, minus exams. Exams were fair (lots of partial credit); just show up to class and do the work (problems from textbook). No reason to not get an A if you moderately try. Very nice professor.
Very helpful, easy grader
Very helpful. Gives detailed solutions, review sheets, etc.
Heavy accent. Lots of questions asked were lost in translation. She had a tendency to write her 9 as a g. Had to teach myself out of the book.
Very, very sweet and helpful professor. Always available if you need help outside of class. Lectures very organized, clear and logical. Everything presented in a perfect order. Loved the class :)
Helpful, accessible outside class and caring about his students' wellbeing. The grading criteria was very transparent and reflective of the actual grading that followed.
EASY! He makes this class so easy! Extremely nice and helpful
EASY EASY EASY! He makes this class so easy! Extremely nice and helpful!
Pretty good overall. Watch out as she likes to treat her classes as guinea pigs in her experiments. She is a very left-wing professor that will make many jokes and poke fun at politicians.

Emily is a great professor! She is a bit scatter-brained during her lectures, but she is still pretty clear. She teaches so that you can learn, not so that you can pass a worthless test. Homework is infrequent, and the final project is not difficult if you start early.
I LOVE GRAYSON!! He is so kind and so funny. I wish he wasn't leaving RIT, he was a joy. His lessons were always so thoughtful and lovely. I had so much fun in his class and I hope he comes back!!

Professor Grayson is by far my favorite professor I've had at RIT. I've taken 2 classes with him and in both classes, he made the material interesting and found ways to keep us engaged. He was always accessible after class and his feedback on my writing was constructive and encouraged me to improve further.

I'm so happy that Grayson was finally added onto here for RIT bc he said that he was so excited to be on here. I've had him twice, trying for a third time, and I absolutely love his classes. He's so down to earth and cares about what you produce, always striving to see improvement instead of ripping your work apart. I cannot recommend him enough :)

I truly cannot recommend Grayson enough. If you have an opportunity to take his class, do it. He was able to make writing more fun because of how he encouraged us to break out of the traditional paper structure, allowing us to write essays that were actually interesting to read. An absolute star of a professor, and easily one of the best there is.

Super fun environment, our class is always full of laughter. Tells funny stories about her own life. Answers any questions, and is good at communicating answers in multiple ways to maximize learning but still make sure students understand. Good balance of lecture, games, conversation practice with classmates, and some video/reading hw assignments.

Grades very harshly. Does not take time to fully understand what you are saying in homework assignments. She does not care. Shows no remorse when asking for help. Never answers emails. Waited till last day grades were due to get in contact with me after emailing her daily about grades. Do not take unless you want to be graded poorly and unfairly.

Elayne Fife-Collier was my MLAS 1 teacher and she was so caring always and included every single student in each discussion and activity. She kept us on track for the course schedule while taking the time to explain further when needed. You really have to show up to class and practice the language if you expect to get better, and she's encouraging.

I love Elayne!!! She is so sweet and funny, class with her is never boring. She also provided an environment where I felt comfortable asking questions, which is so important for any subject but I think especially for learning a language. I wish I could have her as my professor for ALL my ASL classes. 100% would recommend taking a class from her!

Elayne is one of the best professors I've ever had! She cares so much about her students, personally and academically. While she keeps the class focused on teaching ASL, she makes it so fun and engaging! Most students had a decent understanding of ASL by the end of the 15 weeks, and it's because of her. Definitely would recommend!

Easily one of the best professors I've had at RIT. She makes her lectures entertaining and informative. Homework consists of a quiz to test understanding and a video submission to test your ASL. She is very caring and gives good feedback to help you improve.
This professor is absolutely hilarious and is always willing to help outside of class! If you are looking for an awesome ASL professor, she is the way to go.

One of my favorite professors at RIT. All of the expectations were very clear and organized for the course. Super caring and sweet professor. Her lectures includes every student and she worked through each topic to make sure you were understanding everything.

Boring lectures. Great professor otherwise, very flexible. If you need help hes more than willing to give and will go the extra mile if you prove to be a good student. Just chug a red bull before class.
He was a great instructor. Taught the class well and helped when you were in trouble. All his grading was fair and I had no problem with him or the class. I advise him for intro to multimedia class.
The lectures are a bit dry and monotonous, but as long as you do the work well and try to participate in class, you will definitely get on his good side and ace the course

Dry, boring, monotone. Endless powerpoints and stupid in-class exercises. The class material itself is terrible (think Internet 101) made worse by a boring professor. They NEED to rework this curriculum...about half of the content should be cut out. 90% of the info could have been self-taught in a few hours. Should be able to test out of this class
Very nice guy, great professor. A little dry and monotone, but if you go to class and pay attention, you'll learn a lot.

I enjoyed this class, even though his teaching was a little dry/boring. I've been doing XHTML/CSS for years but I still learned quite a bit from this class. Be prepared for a lot of reading and PowerPoint presentations, especially if you've never done web design before.

Angela is very sweet and lenient but her class is unorganized and boring, even as a first year class. These photo arts classes are a lot more work than anticipated so be ready to shoot, and shoot a lot. An absolutely wonderful professor. Ms. Kelly is one of the most inspirational and caring people I've ever met. Will push you to your limits with photography with in-depth critiques and genuinely cares abut each student. A true gem.

She grows on you. She isn't fantastic but she isn't terrible either. She is very knowledgable but I was too annoyed by her lack of organization to really get much out of what she said. She is a fine teacher for such a basic level class. I would take her again if I had to but I'd rather pick someone else. Definitely EASY to pass. Just do the work.

Great class. The beginning was dull but, in the end Angela grows on you. Always creating opportunities for the student when you talk to her. Late work is accepted. Clarity is not the best unless you email because documents on mycourses can contradict. Would Take again.

She can really read photographs, and gives helpful insights on your work.

Angela understands the importance of a class that can slow down and really critique. Her realm is fine art/documentary. If that is what you're interested in, take her. I found her critiques very helpful and she is incredibly knowledgeable. Being self-motivated is important in her class.

Wonderful teacher! Loved her to death! Very helpful and very understanding. She requires a lot of work but you will learn from her. She believes in learning by doing. As a artist you have to perfect the technique yourself to learn it. You'll be lucky to get her as your photo teacher!
took her for 2 quarters pretty easy but def has her favorites, grades that way too. no encouragement for creativity, more tech stuff. Wouldn't take her again. Boring lectures.

Great Professor. She pushes photo one students to be creative while still emphasizing technical information. My only complaint was the way she handeled critiques. I thought she went very easy on less than mediocre work. You can definitely slack in her class, but if you put in the time and energy you'll learn a lot.

Was my Photography as a Fine Art II teacher for a full year.  She is very easy going, nice and helpful.  The only thing I did not like about her class was the reading response assignments - those tended to be quite boring, everything else in the class was enjoyable.  Great teacher, great experience.

Amazing professor, seriously! He is genuinely caring, has a lot of perspective to give, and loves to hear what students have to say. I have seen him several times outside of classes, and he recognizes me as a former student!

I took Comparative Politics with professor Kannyo for one week and then dropped. He seems like a nice and educated person but is not a very good teacher. 1. Hard to understand when speaking 2. Posts group assignments the night before they are due 3. Little to no help outside of class 4. 90% of class he rambles on about irrelevant things

His assignments are often misleading, leading to poor grades. This is an intro class, yet it was my most difficult and tedious course so far. Even when the requirements are understood, hitting those marks seems impossible, as something else pops up that you "forgot;" it feels like he's grading you as if you'd been studying INT. REL. for years.

comment: It's difficult to say wether Kannyo simply lacks a grasp on the subjects which he is teaching or spends little to no effort in developing his curriculum. Having taken him now TWICE, I had expected differing results, but was disappointed. His classes felt half-baked at best. I would at least expect to have regular meetings rather than a weekly paper

Dr. Kannyo is very smart and clearly informed on a variety of political science and international relations topics. He even worked at the UN. If you go to his office hours or email him he will help you with assignments/writing/point you to research resources. Can get off topic easily in class, but is an easygoing professor. Get ready to write

Very disorganized and goes on long tangents not related to class material. I feel like I haven't actually learned anything and no one pays attention in class, and few people show up anymore at this point. However, you're graded on writing assignments and they're pretty easy.

I've had him for multiple classes. Agree w others: unorganized, rambles about random topics, graded by very few things, illegible writing, impossible to get an A. If u go to his office hours he will talk to you for an hour about random political topics. U need to know world history & politics to understand his class rambles. But he's very smart.

Put simply, he is a horrible professor. During class he often (and by often I mean about 90% of the time) goes off an random tangents that barely pertain to the course material. He also will randomly assign homework and quizzes whenever he wants and does not announce it. If you don't want to fail, you need to stay on top of myCourses.

Assignments every week & he will call on every single student, so you'd better do the homework. Runs off into tangents / anecdotes in every class but it's what makes him interesting. There is a lot of reading, but if you do it, the discussions will be easy & the class won't drag.
