comment: Professor Kannyo is an intelligible, nice man. However, he can go off topic and talk for a whole period regarding one subject that won't be tested. Overall, there was only 6 grades for the class; participation, 2 paper, a midterm, final, and a quiz. Take this class if you're interested in international relations. Don't take this class for an easy A
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: There were three grades (an exam, a quiz, and a writing assignment) the whole semester when he specifically said there would be many more. Also his lectures were full of him going off of many tangents so it was difficult to figure out what he was trying to teach us and what was expected for us to know.

He counts the attendance towards participation.  Asks you to participate, but doesn't call on many people.  He goes on his own tangents and doesn't always stay on topic.  The homework its very easy.  Every few weeks a set of questions is handed out and you answer one.  Nothing is collected.  Study for the exams.

A great guy,incredibly smart,just not that great of a professor. He often goes completely off topic (course related but won't be tested) and will occasionally repeat stories if you have more than one class with him. He's very passionate and I've stayed talking with him for hours after class. Classes are usually easy, and his accent is awesome

He's a great guy and he's very smart.  He really knows his stuff and uses sophisticated terms to elaborate on his lectures.  However he has a high tendency to go off point 8 or 9 times on one topic.  This is not good because it gets to the point where it confuses every single student.  Hence, every single student gets drowsy from confusion.

Worked for the UN! Has experience & knows lots about politics, history, & current events. Very interesting lecturer; doesn’t need PowerPoint! Unbiased, presents both sides of issue. Likes to call on quiet ones. Few videos. Gets in-depth & runs out of time, seemingly absent-minded in things besides international relations. Read the whole textbook.

I took his class  Politics of Developing countries. The class is very easy. All you have to do is show up and review notes. He always jumps on different topics and he is boring . He is really horrible grader!! He would always give me a B grade for paper. If you want an easy class take his class. But never expect an A. Just a B!
Very knowledgeable and informed.

I enjoyed the class and the topic itself but could not stand  him or his grading. I asked him a question and told me to look at the syllabus. I explained to him that I wanted him to clarify what the syllabus stated and he never responded. The test was easy but he grades his essays too harsh. Expect a B and nothing else.
He helped me learn the material if I didn't understand. Went out of his way to help me with this class. I did receive an A!!

Very easy class but absolutely impossible to get an A. If you do all the work satisfactorily, you will get a pretty easy B. Dr. Kannyo is a nice man but he is very vague in what he expects for his assignments which leave the class guessing about what he truly expects. If you're looking for an easy class that requires minimal work, this is it.

I have never recieved so many B's. My writing has always been told that it is excellent, but not in this class. No matter what I wrote or how much time I devoted to it, I never got an A. Tread carefully in choosing to take his class.

Kannyo is a very wise man and very close minded. His major flaw is being a huge scatter brain. His notes are illegible and attending his class is often unneeded. Many times I slipped out at the break. Just read the book and do the reports and you'll get a B. IMPOSSIBLE TO GET AN "A" IN THIS COURSE!
He was not very clear on what he was looking for and graded far to harshly.

sometimes can be difficult to understand. attendance not necessary. no need to pay attention because he just rambles on and on about random facts that he will not test you on. one in class test, take home mid-term, take home final. 2 papers to write during the quarter about countries you pick and present

I had him for Commparative Politics and Human Rights. Not really a bad teacher. Matieral was interesting if you read the book. Dont really have to pay attention in class. Other people here said he's a hard grader but I got high B's or A's on my papers and I didn't put that much work into them. Deffinatly a lecture class so bring coffee or dip.

Can be hard to understand... he has a really thick accent and completely illegible handwriting.  He doesn't explain what he wants from assignments.  He is a tough grader - the best grade I've seen him give is a 93 so there's not much room for error.  He definitely knows what he is talking about, it just takes a while to get used to his teaching.
worst teacher i ever had, i worked really hard for the class and i got a b, what sucks is that the whole class got a b too, so if u want a b take him, if u want an a look for someone else

I had international relations with him He hates giving out A's. It's not a hard class because it's not supposed to be one; it's a liberal arts class. He doesn't explain what he expects on his assignments. All we had to do was summaries based on the chapters in the book or class lecture but no matter how detailed you wrote, it was always "B" materia

Really need to pay attention and take notes or you'll be completely lost. Very interesting lectures, though he is a talker and classes last for the entire time. Sometimes he gets side tracked but only because he gets really excited about a certain topic. Good teacher.

PSYC.430 - Memory and Attention. This is a challenging course, but she makes it engaging and manageable. Her exam study guides are extremely helpful and keep you on track. The course is well structured with discussions and participation. The final poster project is a great experience. Amazing professor, highly recommend.

Great professor, lectures were engaging and the material was very clear. The content was very easy, but exams were 60% of the grade. There wasn't much homework and what there was was quick and easy. We used ZAPS for homework but I never used my actual textbook.

I have never had a professor that I respected more... She truly goes out of her way to help students and it is obvious that she cares about them. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is needed to pass. You can get by without reading the textbook, but you must take good notes, and she doesn't allow laptops in class. Her tests are not easy, but fair.

There is a lecture every class. She provides the lecture outline that you can print out (no laptops allowed). You have to pay attention and take notes and study all the material for the 3 exams. There are plenty of other assignments; one paper, ZAPS homeworks, and article discussions. She keeps the lectures interesting and is very good at teaching.
Class was a mix of participation and projects. Had to conduct experiment and write a research paper. Class discussions are also required and participation is part of grade.

Fantastic teacher, she covers different material in lectures and textbook so they're actually interesting, there's a little overlap but just enough that you really understand the material. Shakes it up with multiple types of assignments, fantastic class, she's my best professor so far.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Classes are pretty lecture heavy. Important to take notes but does not allow any laptops to take notes. Gives 3 tests and a paper for majority of grades. Smaller hw points come from Zaps. Content is interesting enough. Class is usually enjoyable based off of discussion.
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: I really like Dr. Sutton she explains very clearly and elaborates very well.  Her tests are easy as long as you pay attention in class.  She was one of my favorite professors.

I have nothing negative to say about this professor. She taught off of a PowerPoint, but elaborated very well on the points so she wasn't just reading the slides. The slides were available online as well. She clearly knows what she's talking about and is very good at explaining each topic.

She's really nice and will do her best to help you in class, but she's a bit of a hard grader on exams. You'll never feel that you aren't learning anything but once you get a grade back on an exam, it can make you think that you haven't learned anything.

Great Professor! Easy course if you study and attend class. Very interesting studies and experiments completed in class. She really cares about how you do and reaches out to help students. As long as you put in effort, she will make sure you get a good grade.

She is a great professor. One of the most willing to help. She will meet with you if you need extra help understanding material. She goes over your notes before the test and tells you exactly what to study. If you do the readings and know the experiments discussed, you will do fine. Lab reports are a breeze if you are in class to participate.

Nice lady but class was tough. Reads off a powerpoint most the time and includes a few movies and activities in class. Miss one day and you will miss at least 10 points on the next test. You have to rely on students to tell you what you missed which wasn't that great when they didn't understand something as well. Not recommended for Cognitive Psych

Not a fan of this teacher. Her tests aren't easy. Some of the littlest details that are easy to miss in class are on the exams. 3 exams, 2 papers, and a few small assignments. She's a very nice lady but I would not take a class with her again. Attendance is a must if you want to pass. Take with another professor if your looking for an easy class.

Excellent professor who keeps the class organized, explains concepts clearly, and uses real examples that make the material easier to understand. Fair grading, reasonable workload, and always willing to answer questions. He genuinely cares about students succeeding, and I would absolutely take him again.

Fairly boring class but he did his utmost to make it digestible and engaging, which I think he succeeded at. The structure is fairly straightforward - do the weekly readings before the first class of that week and the rest of the week is discussion and lecture (participation is graded as well). Has occasional pop quizzes, but they are very easy.

Prof. Salar has very interesting lectures and brings guest speakers from his experiences in to speak with us. It is very interesting but he assigns a lot of readings, which cause a lot of time to be taken up from students already busy schedules. However, it is still a very interesting class and made me interested in public policy.

Very tough grader from my experience. Definitely grades just based on how we feels about your work, as opposed to a strict guideline. Most of my assignments were graded harshly. Definitely one of those professors who thinks their class is the most important class you're taking.

If you enjoy films and are self motivated then taking Politics through Film with Dr. Ferber is a good choice. He picks a lot of cool films for you to view. The downside is though he teaches online only so only correspondence is by email but he is really responsive and gives in depth answers back.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: If you are interested in film and/or politics, this is a great class to take with a great professor! Films are almost all enjoyable, textbook is very interesting and Professor Ferber is active in online class discussions, encouraging diverse opinions and offering his own. Quizzes and online discussions make up your grade, as well as a final paper.
I took Professor Ferber online. He gives great feedback. Very good choice for Political Science Professor. Just make sure you are self motivated cause he teaches online.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']

comment: I took this class online, so I may have had a different experience but I thought the prof was great! Had great video lectures, informative emails, well thought out discussion posts, etc. Would take him again!

The class itself was alright, but he's a tough grader and doesn't give any feedback with his grades. If you don't want any individual attention from your professor, you'll be fine, but even if you ask for feedback it's hard to come by. His lecture videos were kind of corny and boring but not too bad. Just do everything independently.

Don't go to class it doesn't help you at all for his grading policy. It is very easy to get a C or a B in the class but his grading makes it so it is extremely hard to get an A. Nice guy, boring class.
Incredibly boring lectures but there's no need to go to class. 4 online tests out of the book, 3 essays, 4 online discussions. His grading can be really frustrating especially for online discussions.

BORING. He repeats things a hundred times, literally spends an entire class going off point and then talks about one thing. Upside is all the work is online, three discussions, four 20 MC exams, and three essays. Also attendance is not mandatory but he gives extra info that helps with essays and discussions. Would avoid this teacher if I could.

Being a CS student with zero interest in politics, I'm glad this is the professor I had to take this class with. The few times I payed attention, I found his knowledge and clarity impressive, this guys really know what he's talking about. His exams should be easy to prepare to, even if you don't pay attention (you will need the book however).

Politics through film. Better or worse, has low expectations for student's political knowledge. Lectures provide useful background to films, but are not intellectually stimulating. Likes to talk way more than necessary. Great choice of films, fair quizzes and papers. A good but not outstanding professor for this class.
State and Local Government class, had 3 exams and he took the average of them. Posts essay questions ahead of time, but they're usually strange questions. Fair grading and non-mandatory attendance.

I had him last quarter. Eh he  was boring, and the class was boring. Make corny jokes that had the nerds in front of me laughing their butts off, and his essay questions were ridicoulously stupid. Also, some of his attempted humor on the tests = epic fail.
Paul Gerber is the best teacher I've ever had. Every class we would work a bomb of peach, s a b, and play zombies. Great teacher and pulled a lot of life lessons away from his lectures.
Great teacher.  Sounds like Tom Bro kaw.  Material is a bit dry, but he gets through it well enough.  Not too boring unless you hate politics.  This guy grades fairly.

Ferber is a great professor, as long as you take notes, review them before a quiz, and actually read the essay question he hands out to you the week before the test, and think about it, its a nice and easy A, B. Highly reccomend to anyone for american politics

Great class. Very interactive. Pro. Ferber knows his stuff and is excited to teach it. No bias that I've picked up on [although.. there are 3 Army ROTC kids]. Usually one overhead slide per class, ~1 hour lecture, not a bad time. If you're looking to fill a liberal arts requirement or are interested in the subject, I recommend taking this class.

This professore is freaking amazing. You have 3 exams in the class, he averages those out and that's your grade for the class. Also, he only thought for an hour. We only did a two hour class when he canceled one class. Take this man, you won't regret it.

Dr. Khan cares about the success of all of his students. Boundary Value Problems look super scary on day one, but he relegates them to elementary math. Homework is not always the easiest, but it flows well unlike book based problem sets. Additionally, tests are very methodical and are not meant to trick you. Near perfect workload altogether.

Amazing lectures and clear notes posted online. Will answer emails within the day no matter when you send them and is very accessible outside of class to meet for help. He really wants to know everyone in his lecture so he will just call on you but he is very understanding and not-critical of wrong answers do not fear. Best math teacher at RIT

Dr.Khan is so kind and funny. Genuinely made math enjoyable as well as easy as Diff Eq can be. he made everything understandable, and if you didn't understand he noticed and made it a good environment for you to ask questions. A great professor overall.

He's funny in the same way an out-of-touch grandpa is funny. Don't get me wrong, the lectures are entertaining, but it is entirely spoiled by the fact he's extremely unaccommodating behind the scenes. He doesn't honor disabilities and takes advantage of loopholes in the DSO office. So if you need DSO accommodations, avoid him I guess. Never again.

Very charismatic and funny guy. Linear algebra can either be very hard or very easy depending on your professor. Khan makes all of the quizzes and exams very straightforward and are based on the homeworks/reviews respectively.

He is the best professor ever. He is funny and gives amazing lectures. The material is super easy. There are homework and quizzes every week, which are very easy and do not take a lot of your time. He gives exam reviews a week before the midterms, which are very easy and based on them. Definitely take him for linear algebra!

Professor Khan is genuinely the kindest person I have met. His lectures are fun and he clearly explains what he expects from us. The exams are easy and exactly what he told us to expect. Professor Khan would get to know us personally and speak with everyone individually. I look forward to going to his lectures.

He is the nicest professor I've ever had, and it's clear he cares about his students. His lectures are pretty good, and if you're confused, he tries his best to help. Homework is assigned after every class, but it's not a big part of the grade. He grades really easy, and just wants you to understand the material.

One of the best math teachers I've ever had. Made coming to a linear algebra class at 9:30 in the morning enjoyable and presented the material in a way that made sense. Homework assigned after each lecture which sometimes takes a few hours or requires asking questions in class, but would definitely take again

Khan is the most caring professor I've had at RIT. He is super passionate about what he teaches although his lectures can be hard to grasp at times. He is always accessible outside of class though and wants all of his students to succeed. He also takes the time to get to know every one of his student. Truly cannot say a bad thing about this man.
Professor Akhtar cares about each of his students, so it is fairly easy for him to get off topic. This can make the lectures seem a bit disorganized.
Very, very nice professor, but very, very difficult curriculum with not great instruction.

He is very caring and loves to teach the class but gives a good amount of homework and doesn't have any outside class support. If you miss class its up to you to email him to make up work, overall not a bad professor can be challenging though.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Definitely one of my favorite professors. He is very friendly and cares about his students a lot. The textbook was used for homework, but I didn't feel the need to use it otherwise because he explains things well.

Dr. Khan is a truly caring professor who will make sure you are doing your best in his class. He is almost always available outside of class if you email him and he is very lenient on his grading. One of the best math professors in the department and would highly recommend to anyone looking to take a class taught by him.

He is probably the sweetest professor I've ever had! He actually cares about his students and he takes the time to check in with everyone at the beginning of classes. His lectures are straight-forward and provide useful examples. He assigns a very reasonable amount of homework. Exams and quizzes are doable as long as you pay attention in class.

He cares a lot about his students, but doesn't get along well with technology. He has some trouble with Zoom and MyCourses and his slides, etc. He teaches well and does his best to make everything make sense. The topics are difficult and he handles it well.
nice guy

Akhtar is literally one of the sweetest people alive. He is SUCH a nice guy. Sometimes he forgets he needs to give more background on some subjects to help students understand, but if for any reason something is confusing he will walk you through it until it makes sense. When classes were online, he was understanding, helpful, & checked in on us.

Calc 2 is a hard subject, but Professor Khan makes it simple. He cares about helping students succeed, and is very helpful when you have a question. He's also a very easy grader. He's very kind, going around asking everyone how they're doing -- I'd never heard someone compliment so many water bottles before lol! He even brought in candy for us.

Great professor who is invested in his students, which encourages student reciprocation in academic excellence. Brilliant guy who loves Mathematics. Would highly recommend you take his courses, they are a delight.

Professor Akhtar Khan is one of the best Math Professor I have ever meant. He care about his student. Above all, he know his stuff. Always prepare and sent lecture note by emailed. To simple describe him he is a genius. I was taking 6 courses this semester, but Dr. Khan class was always a pleasure. you feel connected.

He's a cool guy, but sometimes I got the impression that he forgets that not everyone in the room loved math. He often went off-topic talking about applications for the topic that wouldn't be useful for non-math majors. I don't recommend him for Calc 1, but if my major required higher-level math courses, I wouldn't mind having him again.

So confusing, honestly think I unlearned calculus more than learned it from him. Every time I had a lecture with him I just sat there confused most of the time, and math is my best subject. The only reason I passed this class was because of the TA and how much I studied on my own. Don't expect him to help outside of class either, he won't show up.

He was a person dedicated to math. But the problem with him was that even though he had a lot of information, he did not know how to convey it well. There were times I had to study on my own because I did not understand anything he taught. But you have straightforward tests so it is an easy A with him and he gives many extra credit opportunities.

great guy, one of the best calculus professors at RIT. Took the time to make sure all students were involved and got the content. Very easy to follow lectures. Genuinely took interest in how all students were doing in the class and constantly demanded we ask questions. Wish I could take more classes with him, as he makes them easy.
Truly cares about the students. Keeps the classes lively. Absolutely hilarious.   We need more Akhtars in the world.
He is very nice, will go around before lectures to ask how you are. I don't know any student that dislikes him. Definitely take one o his courses if you are choosing between two sections.
He's very kind and cares a lot about his students. Lectures are clear and not boring by any means. Definitely take a class with him.
A really nice teacher who makes you want to pay attention, notices the small things in life and brings them up in class, reflects on his memories

Absolutely one of the best calculus professors at RIT. Took the time to make sure all students were involved and got the content. Very easy to follow lectures. Genuinely took interest in how all students were doing in the class and constantly demanded we ask questions. Wish I could take more classes with him, as he makes them fun.

By far the best Diff eq professor i ever had learnt a lot because of his clear concise teaching style and weekly quizzes. Tests were easy if you knew your stuff and he was very helpful in class. Somewhat disorganized in Linear Algebra as we had very few quizzes(they are really helpful), and we didn't do many problems, but still a great experience.

Awesome, awesome professor and the best math teacher I've had by far at RIT. If you have an opportunity to take any of his classes, do it. Very caring guy who wants to see his students learning and succeeding. He is very receptive to feedback, and is overall interesting, attentive and fun. Exceptional professor who goes above and beyond.

The teacher is the best math teacher I have had at RIT. I transferred into his class because my first teacher was so bad. I made the best choice by transferring. This teacher is very helpful and clear and genuinely cares about his students. He is very busy with the rest of his life though as a professor. He is pretty humorous. He grades easy.
After over 20 ratings he has an overall helpfullness of 5.. i think u get the point... great guy
Wonderful teacher, makes sure everyone does well. He genuinely cares about his students and is extremely helpful
One of the best professors at RIT. He is a pretty lenient grader and is there to help you if you need it.
Very hard course but extremely useful
My favorite
The best course ever. Learnt a lot
excellent, very helpful

Awesome teacher. Loves what he does and great at it. Cares about his students. He's great at explaining and re-explaining, and offers lots of chances to make things up. Funny, too. The only thing I dislike about him is that he doesn't teach many more of my classes. :-(

Truly the best professor I've had so far. He was hilarious (had the interpreter crying from laughing so hard) and really nice and always stopped to make sure the class was following what he said. Emails mandatory review packets along with the solutions before tests that are really helpful in studying. I can't wait to take another class with him!
Dr. Khan is an excellent professor. He is always willing to explain any questions. His class was always a pleasure to attend and everyone was engaged. I cannot wait to take another class with him.

Always willing to help.  He is genuinely concerned that students have a good grasp on the material, and will listen to any suggestions you have about the class.  Don't be afraid to take a higher level class with him.

If you take an upper-level class, you may be confused by his notations. He tends to assume his students are smarter than they are and tries not to offend them by teaching them what they already know. This makes upper level classes difficult. He is very entertaining and nice. Very smart guy. Take him if you find other professors slow.
Simply great. Very helpful.

One of kindest people you will ever meet. He actually cares about his students. The quizzes and tests are easy and if you do poorly, he will find ways for you to get back some points. Excellent professor and very good person
Very nice guy, very helpful. if you dont understand something he will try to help you the most he can. Test and quizzes very easy. Overall very great professor.

He is more like a high school teacher than a college professor(In terms of caring). There is no other professor at RIT that cares more than him. He is very knowledgeable, approachable and he tries more than you for you to be successful.
Taught our class for one day and taught related one of our math problems to the game Cricket. No explanations necessary.

Such a caring teacher, he gave me a birthday card!  One day I was an hour late and he said he was sad.  Everyone respects him because he respects the students, front row filled.  When he makes mistakes, he feels really bad and apologizes.
Made differential equations super easy. Great at explaining concepts. Gives you a ton of occasions to rise your grade. Very, very helpful. Great teacher.

I had Akhtar for all three of the Project-based Calculus classes. Each of which consisted of a weekly homework workshop and quiz/exam (3 exams not including the final). These all counted towards your grade but what really counted was your attitude towards the class and your ability to show Akhtar that you learned something. Great professor!
Probably the greatest Teacher I had freshman year. He knows his math and he is extremely knowledgeable. He actually cares about how you are doing and if you are learning. Really nice guy too.

The best calc teacher I've ever had! Explains everything crystal clear, makes sure you get it, concerned bout you as an individual. Whatever's on the test/quiz- goes over in class before/is taken from the hw. Attendence mandatory thou.
had him two semesters in a row and absolutely loved the class...looking forward to having him for 283 and also a couple elective classes
Amazing professor, By far the best Math teacher I have ever had, Will explain everything you can ever want as long as you ask

Genuinely nice guy. Made you feel like he was actually concerned about you as an individual. Covered the material well, i actually felt like i learned something. was always available for help and even gave us opportunity for undergrad research!
No Comments

I was intimidated by this class as I have no coding background and this course is R heavy. The professor assured me that once you get over the learning curve it becomes easier and he was right! His lectures were insightful and he gave great examples. Grading is lenient as long as you show you are trying your best. He gives extra credit as well!

He's a really good Prof, cares a lot and knows what he's talking about. Tests are really tough, the questions aren't too bad but you're always pinched for time unless you really know your stuff. You get a decent amount out of class, but I'd probably try to go for an easier prof because the tests are a little unfair because of the time limit.

Definitely a great choice to learn supply chain and operations management. Tells you exactly what to expect for exams and gave a significant amount of extra credit opportunities. Has a unique way of tying course material with comedic statements and keeps the class lighthearted but learning intensive. Textbook needed for group case studies.
Did not think I learned anything new.

Honestly one of the best CSEC101 professors at RIT. Professor Roman works his day job in industry as a high-level manager, so he isn't a "hands on keyboard" guy these days. But you know what he is? REALLY GOOD at explaining top-level concepts which is what CSEC101 cares about and tests you on. Highly recommended!

He's a very knowledgeable, hilarious, and caring professor. Tries to make lectures interactive and more informational than what the department provides. Basically a few labs, a book report, and interesting in-class discussion. Go to class, and you'll learn things and pass. Go to RC3/SPARSA too! (It's practically required if you're CSEC anyway.)

Only use as last resort. He is super underqualified to be a professor, so RIT gives him the simple MECE classes to teach. He copies other professors notes when lecturing and is unable to answer questions in class. His teaching style is as if you gave a 10 year old a piece of paper and asked them to copy it down on a whiteboard.

Mitch never really said much to me, like the other 2 teachers in the room. He was very vague, but he's also chill and very going with the wind, so you don't have to worry about being super criticized and can be free with your art for him.

Mitch was one of 3 professors I had for 3D, and was overseeing my group for the final project. Unlike the other 2 professors, Mitch didn't check in or offer advice unless prompted. Students should take some initiative, but a good professor should also be involved. I've also heard he allows for traditional animation in a MOTION GRAPHICS class.

i enjoyed having mitch as one of my professors for 2d I. He may be a bit intimidating at first but he is very fun and serious about art as a whole. It took awhile for me to warm up to his teaching, however, I enjoyed hearing his feedback, (even if I did not agree at times).

So this professor did kinda pick on me a little bit for whatever reason and it was funny at first, but overtime I would kinda get tired of it. Especially he start class and after 5 mins of class tell us to do whatever we needed to do instead of using the time in class to teach us more. I didn't learn that much at all about graphic design.

I had Mitch for Graphic Design Studio 1 and he did not teach us a single thing. Nearly every single class, we got to the classroom, and he sent us home to "not waste our time" and remained in the classroom for 20 minutes before going off to work on his own MFA or the release of his book. This class was a waste of time + a waste of tuition money.

I feel disappointed in this class. He gives vague instructions and he has never given me advice or feedback on my work. I often feel stuck or confused and my TA is the main one who helps or gives feedback. I don't feel like I'm learning anything and I feel that the grading isn't always fair as we don't get to explain our work.

He claims that grades dont matter and that his opinion isnt worth more than ours and uses this as a way to give us zero feedback and zero grades. I received one grade the whole course which was my final grade. I didnt get any valuable feedback. I had no idea how I was doing in the course and what areas to improve on.

mitch was awesome!! it always seems like he's just bullsh*ting half the time, but he always has a point to make!! funny and honest, i would 100% take again. make sure to experiment and try new things in his class!

Loved having Mitch as a professor this past semester! Takes one of his classes as a remote work day so you don't have to physically come to class and can learn the programs at your own pace! Gives great feedback on your projects and wants to make sure everyone has a project that they are happy with and not one that just does what he thinks is good

I am currently taking Mitch's class and he may possibly be the most fun I have ever had interacting with a professor. He is very great with feedback and overall a really a funny guy and a great professor. Mitch allows students to be very creative in their work as long as it follows guidelines and overall provides as great atmosphere in class.

Really awesome professor! He's very funny and personable and really lets you lead your own projects and work on what you want to do. Lectures are simple and straightforward. You also grade yourself and give a lot of group critiques which I think genuinely made me want to improve my work, not just for the grade. Honestly, 10/10 professor.

Having Mitch for 2D design 1 was a real treat! He is a fantastic professor who really cares about the experience you are having, rather than the outcome of your art. Even though I had an 8 am with him, there was never a dull moment in his class. He never keeps you the full anyway, so you can go back and get some rest.

I'm a freshman in college and had Mitch for 2D Design- he has made this first semester amazing. Interesting class, adequate professor. A lot of information and assignments but it's all doable. Study for the exams though. Great class to clear a lib art requirement though.

Honestly, in the beginning of the quarter I wasn't really paying attention, so it was really boring. But then like midway through I started to pay attention and it was actually very interesting! It became one of my favorite classes.  Pretty easy grader and offers extra credit here and there. Not much homework. Study for tests though!!

really Boring lectures. but the class is easy and Professor Strobl is very nice! she enjoys what she teaches and she will help you if you don't understand. turning things in late will result in 10% off. textbook isn't used. she's kind of cute too! don't take if you fall asleep easy. study quizzes, tests are exactly alike.

Super nice professor, and really easy.  Once in a while gives bonus points for attendance cause not many come to class. For the exams study the powerpoints and know all of the words on the crossword. Never used the textbook, kinda mad I actually bought it.

very easy. attendance really isn't necessary. i would almost suggest not going to class. her lectures are by far the the most boring thing you will ever have to go through. study the PP slides on your own time you will get a good grade on the tests/quizzes. her tests have the same questions as the quizzes. btw don't buy the book - its not needed.
I agree, cute professor and very easy. Take-Home quizzes and the test are meade up from the quizzes and reviews sha gives. Take is you really want an A!
super hot, and super easy

Gretchen was so nice and gave great advice during class. I loved my drawing class with her, I looked forward to each class. She would praise students for their work, but also give really good advice. She loves her cats!!!

Amazing professor and I wish her the absolute best.

I love Gretchen! She was my 2d design professor which was one of my first design class. She taught everything so well and gave great feedback in critiques. Her projects are fun and she makes class comfortable and enjoyable.

I know she teaches a fundamentals class, but if you are planning to be a Graphic Design major, this is a great class. I would definitely take this class again!
Gretchen is awesome! Definitely take her class if you have the chance. I learned so much in that class and she is always willing to help.
One of my favorite art teachers. She has a great personality and wants to make sure you learn smth and be as creative as possible. Very reasonable with grading. A wholesome individual

gretchen is amazing!! she gives amazing feedback and encourages you to create what you envision. she tries to get each student personally. she is a fair grader and for assignments gives students a good amount of creative freedom. she wants each student to experiment with different techniques to bring their work to a whole new level.

Gretchen was one of my favorite professors of the semester. Her projects, grading, and critiques are all thoughtful and thought evoking. If you have the chance to take a class with Gretchen, I highly recommend.

In my first year, first quarter, I took Written Comm I with her.  I thought she was scared teacher in the first place but in least of 2 weeks later, when you really work hard, she did not seem to be scared at all.  She's cool teacher. i think shes the best teacher of all
She's cool.

A good professor who tries to help his students as much as he can. This was his first time teaching this course and it showed as he wasn't that prepared for his lectures. Best professor I had in undergrad or grad school.  Genuine dude who brings real-world examples to every class, keeps it pretty light, gives great feedback, and teaches very effectively. Easy but I still learned so much

Bob is such a sweet guy; he truly cares about his students and strives to make sure we all understand the content. Grades are based on case analyses (2 group, 3 individual). Participate in class by contributing quality input and you will have no trouble getting an A Highly recommended!!
GREAT professor.  really cares if you learn and lots of guidance along the way.
Case based class brings real world feel to this class.  Definitely learned a lot without feeling overwhelmed.
Very matter of fact.

She is EXTREMELY helpful. Allows an infinite amount of revisions to improve your grade, as she believes "writing is revising and vice-versa." Is fair, and if you have an inkling to write, she is the prof. to take.
grades fair, very helpful if you come to see her. LOVES revisions, and allows as many as you want to increase grade! take her!
Hard teacher, snorts when she laughs, loves the nerds. Listen to exactly what she says and write about it. dont try to write what u want, because she wont like it

This class is terrible, you do not want this teacher for Writing Seminar, she will kill any respect you have for writing and will make it the most painful research project of your life. hes funny. a good teacher, but there is definitely a disconnect between his tests and the lecture material. he seems to use banked questions from the textbook but then expects your papers to rely on what was said in class. i wish he wouldn't text with the textbook. he barely talked about it but we were graded on it.
Super funny. A few discussions, a few assignments, quizzes for every topic, and a final. Easy class
Lot of reading, powerpoint wont help you,give me a low essay grade without any feedback, stay away

He's great, if a little passive-aggressive. Due dates are extremely flexible if he has notice and was willing to meet me on Zoom to answer questions after I missed a class. comment: Dr. Herbert is a great guy, and is passionate about what he teaches (I had him for sensation and perception). The class was structured so that you read the textbook to learn the material, and then in class you learn more fun facts and discuss things. The tests are tough, just read the textbook religiously. There are papers too which aren't bad.

When it comes to lectures he tends to go off topic a lot and for me it was hard to follow along even with the slides present. There was a lot of homework from him. You can get away with not going to class since it won't count but you will end up lost.

comment: Andy is a great professor. As long as you keep up with the work, the class is not bad (especially for a class that would otherwise be pretty unpleasant). He is really interesting, he has great lectures, and he is really flexible with deadlines as long as you communicate.

Best professor I have ever had in my life. He really knows everything. He can answer any question you have. He is so humorous and insightful that you cannot help yourself but to listen to his lecture. He is the greatest professor and the most knowledgeable person by any standard.

Extremely difficult grader but means well and tries to make it easier on his students. A lot of his comments were contradicting on the paper and I tried really well on it only to fail. Very knowledgeable and efficient.  Can answer most of your questions.  Very hard professor though.

I don't understand the neg comments- he's a good teacher. He gave interesting lectures but gets  distracted easily (this is usually the fun part). Tests aren't easy, but are fair. Study everything he tell you too, including diagrams. Never had a problem with his essays. I enjoyed his class so much, I'm taking his Perception class.
HARD class but interesting class. Funny professor, but you def. have to work your butt off for a good grade. Hardest psych class I've taken

I do not agree with the person who commented prior to me.  I worked extremely hard in my class and still did not do well. It's not an easy course but he made sure we understood through his powerpoints and videos.  I got a C ONLY because I slacked off.  Dont slack off and you'll besure to get an A or B.

Never worked so hard for a "D" in my life. We had "informal" presentations which he sprung on us at the last minute. These were for each of us to just see what everyone else worked on, but then he graded them. Got really negative toward the end of the course, maybe he's having a life crisis or something.

Moody. Buries students under homework. One has to fight for a passing grade. Answering in class are never "quite" right. He has a great sense of humor, and I think he believes he is encouraging, but has the ability to make one simply stop trying.
good

This prof is very helpful, and positive. He makes you feel like you can do it if you're having any problems. The lectures are really entertaining, he's very witty. The workload is pretty heavy though.
Great teacher. Very interesting lectures, really sparks interest.  Always willing to help students and work with them. Great professor!!
Great teacher. Really helpful.
No Comments
Engaging presentations, good sense of humor, personable. I enjoyed the class and learned more than I expected to. I wish I had more classes like this. It wasn't easy though.

Unless you love art history AVOID THIS CLASS! Weekly reading assignments- textbook + dense articles (30-65 pages/week). 3 papers due throughout the semester based on prompts he gives a week before its due. comment: incredibly interesting and engaging. He is also very aware of art in social context as well as historical context. He assigns a lot of reading, but he's usually very nice about

His lectures are incredibly interesting and engaging. He is also very aware of art in social context as well as historical context. He assigns a lot of reading, but he's usually very nice about the grading.
He is very relaxed but fair, amazing for real world work, almost everything he explains works when I had a co-op!

Professor Kiser is one of the kindest and most understanding instructors I've ever had. Before taking this class, I was not very familiar with C, and learning it was pretty difficult. While the lectures can be fairly dry, Kiser is always there if you have any questions, which is necessary for such a difficult class. Also, all tests are open book.

Kiser is my favorite professor at RIT. He's understanding of everything, always happy to answer questions, presents material clearly, and is just one of the realest professors I've ever had. If you have a chance to take a class with him I strongly recommend you do.

Made things super easy. I can't imagine anyone getting a bad grade in this course.

Very chill and understanding guy.

Anytime you have a chance, choose him. Took this class in spring 2024. He's not a fast grader, but he grades well when that happens. Likewise, if you ask him for an extension, you will get it. There was 1 project that could be a default project or a project you make based on the class. He grades it fairly based on effort and wants you to succeed.
Professor Kiser is the goat. He is loved by students and cares for students health. Would take every single class with him if I could.

Prof Kiser is such a nice change of pace from a usual SE professor. Kiser is kind, caring, and clearly respects his students. Kiser has decades of industry experience and does not hesitate to share his insight and knowledge about his work as well as employs two very helpful CA's.

Best professor in the SWEN department. He is clearly knowledgeable and understanding of a students struggles. He will help you if you're willing to bare with him. He also has a great fashion sense and sense of humor. Only downsides are his office hours can be inconsistent.

Kiser cares for his students so he is pretty understanding about concerns. He is also very reachable during class and Discord for out-of-class. He is sometimes unorganized because, for example, he might need to be reminded that X assignment doesn't have a due date posted yet. Generally an easy course and allows for late submissions.

One of the nicest professors you can take at RIT, no matter what happens he will understand and accommodate to the greatest extent that he can. It seems he was assigned to SWEN 342 at the last minute this semester and he was clearly unprepared, but he still made the most of it by orienting the class towards freely-chosen projects.

Man I wish I could take Professor Kiser for more classes. He is always respectful to students and empathetic to their situations. Started off with a bit of a learning curve, he kind of assumed you could just figure things out on your own, but does cover all the important stuff in a clear and concise way. Also gives time in class for homework help!

By far the most human and reasonable professor I've had. He'll make sure you learn the material while being graded fairly and without unreasonable expectations - very flexible on deadlines, attendance, etc. if you have any good reason. Only thing to watch out for is lazy classmates taking advantage of him and holding back the class.
Kiser is the GOAT

Kiser is probably the best swen professor at rit. He's super nice and seems to be one of the very few reasonable professors in golisano. I never write reviews for teachers, but I had to give a good for Kiser.

444 is a chill class and Professor Kiser is very nice. He values the balance of school work and life while still being able to teach the material and ensure that his students are learning. Most of the class is the group project and he will usually give you time during class to work with your team so that there isn't too much work.

Professor Kiser is a gem. Like a lot of professors in SE, he started in the industry and came back to teach and he shares a lot of anecdotes that put a unique perspective on the course. There were practically no due dates besides exams and end of the semester. He converted an assignment into 5% extra credit when we started to run a little behind.

Lectures for half of the class and the other half is group project time. Very easy grader. My only complaint with Kaiser is the constant miscommunication between him and his TA, who was responsible for grading assignments. Caused a lot of headaches and unclear grading criteria.

Best SE Professor at RIT, no questions asked. Amazing lecturer, very passionate about what he does, and cares about his students. Easy to communicate with and accessible outside of class. Very clear about topics to be tested on exams, there are no surprises as all topics will be covered on a review exam.

Professor Kiser is easily the best SE professor I have had so far. His entire class is very relaxed with everything to the deadlines to the assignments. He often gives you tips or even a head start on upcoming assignments during the lectures. As long as you pay a bit of attention in the class and utilize his discord server you should get an A.

comment: I have truly never respected/admired a professor anywhere close to how I do Larry Kiser. He is loved by his students and in the online era, we all get absolutely riled up for "Larry Stream Days". He has found the perfect formula for an effective course that is educational/challenging yet stress free and flexible, putting mental health above all.

CMPE240 is stuck in no man's land. It wasn't a CE required course, so the CE department never invested much resources into making it an actual good course. Instead, they just threw it to the SE dept and said "your problem now". The course is a bit all over the place, but Kiser is a super fair grader who's trying his best to develop the class

So being in the pilot class for this was interesting, to say the least. A lot of stuff is different than previous sections of this class, and it took a while to get into the groove. Some assignments were not tested before the class started resulting in next to impossible assignments until we asked for clarification. Good stuff for the future.

Professor Kiser does a great job with his class. He clearly and slowly explained lectures and answered questions clearly as they came up. Due to his involvement in SWEN-250 with creating the practicums, he wasnt available during his office hours for a significant amount of the semester. He also didnt require the textbook for the class.

Professor Kiser did an excellent job at taking a confusing class and reforming it for future students. While we did get stuck in the transition semester, he was more then fair in terms of grading and was always willing to modify assignments if students collectively thought it was too much or did not make sense.

Probably the best professor I have had to date. Legitimately cares for the students and their success and he teaches the material as clearly as possible, with no jargon. Extremely fair with assignments and grading. On the first class, the man said your mental health is more important than this or any class. How many profs care like that? 10/10
Well, with all these extra credit oppurtunities, relaxed deadlines, and a great attitude to help students, Larry Kiser is honestly one of the best SE professors I've been able to work with.

Really great teacher. Cares a lot about his students and is willing to make compromises just so you can succeed. The assignments are not hard, but they aren't easy as well. He really teaches you to learn and think for yourself as well as provide a path for you to effectively and efficiently develop your software skills.

Kiser is very caring and willing to help if you are overwhelmed or stuck. He moves due dates when students are struggling and really cares about the learning rather than the grades. I would definitely take him again.

My favorite professor in any class I've ever taken. His lectures are always interesting and funny, and he's one of the most accommodating professors I've ever seen. His tests are always super easy, as are the homeworks. He gave the class a 5 day extension for a project, just because it looked like most of us weren't done the weekend of. Easy A

Amazing professor. C was a hard language to grasp but he was always willing to help. Very flexible with grading, if you have issues with a grade you can usually work it out with him. TA was kind of rude and would sometimes insult you.

Kiser is a very understanding and knowledgeable professor. He has over 30 years of industry experience although has only started teaching at RIT in the last few years. Approaching him for help is recommended since that is how you will get the most out of his classes. I would recommend him and will take him again if the chance arises.
He is knowledgeable of his field, he really wants to make sure his students succeed and is very approachable for help.

A decent professor for SWEN 261. Focuses on (and grades) the process and documentation instead of the qualityhow well your project works. A nice guy who is willing to help and will always listen to what you have to say. Very open to changing grading criteria. Also watch out for his earrings.
Good professor, very knowledgeable but sometimes a bit boring
P. Krutz was always there to help. Be ready for a group project that is dependent on your teammates.
Keeps his classes entertaining and I liked him setting aside time at the start of class to see how we are all doing. Very caring.

Super fun and engaging. This course would be absolutely miserable without him and he was my reason for showing up every week. Very clear with assignments and due dates, and gives occasional lectures. Only problem is that he does not tell us to do the attendance quizzes and so I would occasionally forget.

Krutz is one of the most hilarious teachers I've ever had, makes jokes for almost the entire class when he isnt (and when he is) instructing us on what to do for the class. Very light grader and almost everything besides the final interview and project will be a 100% as long as you are present and do the in class material. 100% would take him again
Goes out of his way to help us noobs succeed. A bit lecture heavy at times, but it's usually helpful.
Always willing to talk with students after class in a friendly manner and has a lot of knowledge about the department and program.
Made the class fun and easy to pass, Not a lot of work in the class
Funny guy, easiest 100 a SWEN student will get.
Krutz cares about his students and ensures lively discussions and activities.

Prof. Krutz is just a great guy and is interested in his students and how they are doing. He is always eager to help us whether its work in his class or other classes or just life. He also throws in jokes around the class which always makes for a fun atmosphere.
Cares about his students and is knowledgeable about the SE department and topics.
After finishing my first year at RIT, I can say that he was my favorite professor.
His lectures are very interesting and he will talk about things that will help you. Best in SE and I want to take more classes with him.
Great guy. He really cares about his students.
Great guy. The best.
SWEN101 is easy just do your few assignments and it is an easy A. Prof Krutz is a chill guy and pretty funny definitely recommend him.
Professor Krutz is the GOAT. He rarely give homework and he oftens spends his class either making jokes or creating assignment that are actually fun.
The best

a really great guy.

he talks a lot with topics that not related to the lecture.
Really funny guy and made sure to make students feel comfortable adjusting to college. Class was a bit disorganized at times but I enjoyed it.

He is fun, I enjoyed this course, it was a break in my schedule. To be honest, he is not very knowledgeable about software engineering or computing in general, but I still appreciate his humor. love RIT and this teacher

Great class. I really enjoyed him. He is the best in SE.

Awesome teacher. Very helpful, balance of material, and easy course. Sometimes he can be a little repetitive and repeat things or topics that we've already gone over, but they stick better this way. Young, knowledgeable and funny.
Great guy, makes SE project manageable. Highly recommend
Super chill!  Easily the best professor I've had so far.
He is amazing professor, really chill and awesome. take him for any class and you will love it
Professor Krutz is the best teacher I have ever had.  He is very intelligent and approachable, yet while being humble.
He is an awesome professor. Had him for intro to SE and 361 class and it was just an awesome experience. Really humble and understanding person. HIGHLY RECOMENDED
Awesome professor. Really tries hard to make teams be the best they can be. Get him if you can.
I love Krutz! He's a fantastic professor!
Great professor, he really revitalized my interest in Software Engineering and the class never really had a dull point. All the activities were very hands on.
Really helpful, and really knows his stuff. Presented the information clearly, one of my favorite professors!!
Awesome professor. Keeps the class interesting. Take his class if you can.

his class is free, but assignments are disorganized and many things are unclear, class feels like he trying to sell you on PR instead of teaching it. Like PR is what PR is you don't have to upsell it to be cool. Especially considering 90% of the class is their to fill up a perspective or immersion

Dr. Wang is a really nice professor and tries his best to make sure students are having fun and getting something out of  his lectures (even when a majority of the class won't participate) I really appreciate the dedication Dr. Wang has to his studies. Very entertaining and fun class. Workload is minimal. Lectures are up to date with current events. As long as you make an effort you will likely do well. He gives out study guides for tests that help a lot.

Very easy teacher and a very nice guy.  Doesn't go very far in depth with most topics.  Has lots of class examples that don't really relate to class (movie clips, music videos, etc.).  A good teacher if you are looking for an easy A with no work, not the best teacher if you want to learn a lot about the topic.

He is the best professor ever you attend this class because 2 quizzes, 2 exams, and less homeworks but mor activities in class with the classmates for discussion. You will get good grades unless you miss only 2-3 miss the classes for absent. You will love it! It's easy to learn and very fun in this class. I'm glad to take this class and pass it!

Xiao Wang is a passive professor who doesn't make the class interesting nor important. This greatly disappointed me as PR is my major and interests me greatly. Impossible to understand. He needs to repeat things at least 3 times for everyone to understand.The whole class is often awkward as he tries to understand us. Professor Wang is such a cool professor! His class is pretty easy as long as you read his lecture notes. Two pop quizzes- though he tells you when they will be. Two exams- midterm and final. Very easy, nice professor.
Took Public Relations. Its a great class. I really enjoyed it. Dr. Wang provides lots of real-world examples. Very organized and fun class. He's also very nice and cares about his students.

Had him for Mass Communications. He is really easy, and funny too. He keeps lectures short then lets you out early. Everything seems to be crystal clear about the course. He cares about his students and tries to keep them engaged. Everything is posted online for later reference. The tests are easy and short. I recommend this professor. A
Mass communications class is intereting and good. Prof Wong is extremely nice and friendly. Super cool guy. Grading isn't bad t all.

Professor Wheeland is a caring professor who both lectures and provides resources outside of class. There are consistent quizzes, but all are online and open-book. Projects are interesting and I feel like learned a lot! He's willing to give you extra help and extensions if needed.
Decent professor, passionate about subject. Found lectures somewhat dull. Fairly nerdy lol.

This class is difficult and requires a lot of time and effort, but Prof. Wheeland is an excellent professor. The class is very well organized. Weekly checklists always make it clear what is expected when. Lectures are usually funny. Projects are interesting and fun, but the expectations are quite high. This class made me more interested in web dev.

Took the online async version of this course. Prof Wheeland made some amazing video lectures. They were informative and entertaining. I consider myself to be successfully "introduced" to web tech for games.

This class should be a 4 credit instead of 3 with how the dude runs this class. Class time is wasted on lectures on material that we are required to learn before said lecture begins. Gives homework that doesn't help students learn and is just "copy this code and submit assignment". Then gives multiple big projects at once that are time consuming.

Introduced far too difficult concepts much too late into the year. Many lectures were unhelpful in understanding the material. Working with actual code was the real enjoyable part of the class. Did not discipline more disruptive students. Larger projects and small exercises are given similar amounts of time and attention in class.

comment: Its not necessarily that the class is hard, but the way he teaches it makes it a lot harder than it needs to be. Theres a lot of assignments that are time consuming and don't help with understanding the material. It's more like just googling the answers. Which is what he literally expects you to do for the weekly quizzes. Should be a 4 credit class
You'll learn what you need to know about web design. Professor is caring and fair.

Way behind on grading assignments, didn't receive project grades (which were worth >50% of the final grade) until finals week. Assignments were evaluated on subjective qualities rather than fulfilling the objective of the assignment. Assigned way too much work, didn't allow nearly enough time to complete assignments. Nice person, terrible prof.
Wheeland's not bad. He's not great at lecturing, but he's a pretty easy grader, so if you pay attention and actually try, you'll do just fine. He's sort of a goob, honestly.

Andrew worked in industry as a web developer for 15 years before returning as a prof at RIT. It was rough in the beginning of the semester because he was so new, but he's improved considerably. He is extremely knowledgeable and I recommend him for any web development classes.

comment: He is a great professor who is willing to help his students with the class. He just came back from a job he was at, and now he is taking time to adjust back to being a lecturer. He's still pretty good at teaching the content. Does laugh from time to time and makes the lectures more enjoyable that way. I'd take one of his classes again if I could.

Is incredibly caring and uplifting towards students. Gives good feedback but also shows you where to improve and also how to do so. It was clear to all that Becca wanted her students to improve and really cared about us. Also lectured very well and made complicated topics easy to digest.
Becca is very light-hearted and loves everything anyone makes. She does give good feedback, and especially for the collage, she came over and actually helped me move pieces around to get me going.
just fine,  funny and uplifting and easygoing. I couldn't have asked for a better drawing 1 teacher. She really cares , thanks

I'm a photo major that has to take this class, and I don't have any drawing ability. She really helped me through my assignments, and was very understanding. If I didn't have her as my prof, I probably would've hated this class. There is a assignment involving painting different squares, and it took me 7 hours to complete, so be prepared for that.
I'm a photo major that is forced to take 2D (i can't draw or paint at all, no skill). She was very lenient and very helpful. Was very funny and made class more fun.

Rebecca wasn't a standout professor, but she was good. I learned a lot in her class and she was always pretty clear about what she wanted. I wasn't a huge fan of subject of the class itself which may have affected my view of her, but I did notice that I had a little bit more work with her than my other art profs.

comment: I had Becca for my 2D Design and she was such a joy! She's very positive and caring and gives critiques a very comfortable environment. Would take her again!!

Becca was such a nice professor and the class was a comfortable environment for critiques and she's very nice about giving feedback. Laid back class and the projects are really unique and fun to do. Would recommend her to anyone.

Becca is really sweet and is a great teacher. If you can't come to class or are having trouble and if you talk to her and keep her in the loop, she'll work with you to make sure you and your grade are doing okay.

Becca is so great! She is so funny and uplifting and easygoing. I couldn't have asked for a better drawing 1 teacher. She really cares and is really there to help you and is never mean spirited about her critiques and always gives you things to work on. She always finds something good to say. She is also not that hard of a grader which helps.

This is the kindest professor I've ever had. She was always willing to stay after class to help any student. She is probably the only reason I passed this class (I suck at physics). She checks on her students work throughout class and is happy to answer any questions you may have.

Dr.Wong is an amazing professor. She really likes to help her students out. She gives us extra time on assignments that we couldn't turn in. She's very understanding of students' situations. I would 100% take a class with her again.

Sweetest and most enthusiastic professor I've had. The class was tough for me, but she was willing to work with me one-on-one and was helpful. Exams must have an avg of 60% to pass the class. Homework can be long, but she assigns the work because she wants to see students succeed. Frequently reminded us of resources to get help. Some extra credit.

Great teacher, even if she's a little difficult to understand at times. Exams are fair and so is her grading. She can tend to drone on in labs, but she's really trying to do what she thinks is best for her students.

This professor cares about students individually and takes her time to get to know her students. To some people, her accent makes it hard to learn from her. She grades extremely hard making it very difficult to pass the class as well as giving lots of homework. You need an average of a 60% on all her tests in order to pass this course.

Incredibly kind, caring, and reasonable, and all the people calling her English rusty have never heard an accent before. Her lectures and lab "briefs" are very long winded and redundant, so prepared to be bored if you're already comfortable with the material. The weekly assignment packets are long but no problem if your lab group works together

Dr. Wong is a extremely nice and caring professor. Her English isn't the greatest so it might be hard to understand her at times, especially during a difficult topic. She very easy to access out of class, and if you finish your work during class you can just head out. Good professor would take again.

She is a very kind person and has a great attitude. If you need lengthy explanations then she might be the teacher for you (not me); her English is a little rusty btw. Be ready to do most of the lab (worksheets) outside of class; she talks a lot. I saw those who already have some grasp of physics had an easier time. It was a struggle, but I passed.

Dr. Wong was one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She wanted everyone to succeed in her class and gave as many bonus points as she could to ensure this. I was really worried going into physics as I am a liberal arts major, but she made me understand the material easily. I would 100% take another class with her again.

Doctor Wong is a great professor; a couple of things make this class hard, including a lot of homework, and the lab packet she assigns is also challenging and time-consuming if you have no idea how to do it. Lastly, If you go to her office during office hours, she is helpful and will help you.

Professor Wong is a great, kind, caring professor. English is not her first language, so she is hard to understand sometimes and stumbles a lot. She also lectures a lot more than she should and needs to. Many people never finish their labs by the end of class at the end of the week and have to do it on their own time on top of a lot of homework.

Dr. Wong is undoubtedly the nicest and most caring professor I have had the pleasure of learning from. Like the other reviews said she does lecture a lot but it's only because she is trying really hard to explain the material in enough ways that everyone understands, she is extremely patient and answered any questions I had.

Extremely nice and smart person who is flexible and understanding. You dont get that a lot so I apprecaite that. She grades fair and will help you. Only thing is she cant convey the material right and clear and lectures way too much. Honeslty not a good teacher and will leave you confused.

Nice, understanding, and smart professor. Unfortunely she has difficulties conveying the material to students and have seen a decrease in her student's attendance throughout the semester. She makes you write your name down for each class but I have no idea if it's worth anything. She finds difficulties keeping people engaged in lab/lecture.

Super nice lady who cares about all of her students. She just talks a lot. It can get confusing and a little boring. Tests are a little difficult. Homework once a week and also workshop problems once a week.

Very nice lady. She does not know how to stop talking. Every class she will over-explain things to the point you will be confused. I have not been to lecture since week 2 since her 2-hour lecture is so boring I'd fall asleep so it made more sense to not go to class. Her exams are easy if you know the material. Two homework assignments a week.

i originally was very excited to take Terrorism in Fiction and Film it quickly became a dreaded class the books were practically archaic and sucked u read six books in ten weeks so u have to rush plus he expects u to remember tiny ass details that are COMPLETELY irrelevant to the over all story he goes off on tangents he simply should retire

Granite is extremely boring and puts people to sleep every class.  I took him for Terrorism in Film and Fiction and the books are hard to understand but the films are sort of interesting.  The only homework is to read the books besides the essays so there isn't much homework to worry about but is pretty strict about the essays
Harvey is one of a kind. Do your work and you'll be fine

I thought he was good, although I know how to write and take some pride in it. As a professor he consistently brought up new and interesting topics in class and also included movies in the curriculum.

Although she was encouraging me and be flexible on my assignments, but instructions were unclear which causes repetitiveness and lots of anxiety. Gives a LOT of homework and which occasionally hard to understand. Not the best with technology which wasted a lot of valuable time in class and is very direct with criticism. I would not recommend taking any of her classes.

Irma really cares about her students and she will do anything she can to help you. However, her classes will never be easy. That is because she always pushes her students to do better. Her instructions can be a tad bit unclear, but if you ask, she will provide you with clarification. She is a blunt person and will tell you if she hates your designs

She is not everyone's cup of tea and at times she can come off a little harsh. However, with that being said she is always available to help outside of class even if she's already home and its not her office hours if you take her class serious you will leave knowing a lot. She's honestly very funny once you understand her.

Heres the thing about Irma, shes actually not as bad as you might think. She is a very blunt person and will tell you EXACTLY how it is. So, if you cant take harsh feedback, than you are gonna have a strong dislike towards her. However, shell also ensure you understand why you received that feedback and how to do better.

Irma is a great professor and is great with technology/online class formatting, but she definitely does not teach an easy class. She expects a lot from her students and if you slack, you will fail her class. I was frequently overwhelmed from the workload, however, I definitely learned a lot from her. She is kind but she's also very brutally honest.

Also she grades harshly and the rubric is vague, not only that she adds stuff on a whim. Avoid!!
Very good teacher! She is very nice if you ask for help. Even though she is strict with the homework. Take her class!
Her accent can get can make her instructions somewhat hard to understand but not impossible and she is usually always available to help you if you need it.

She is very tough in the beginning stages of the course. Towards the end, however, she becomes nicer and you're left wondering why she wasn't just as nice from the start. comment: I absolutely love Irma. I wont deny that her classes can be hard and english isn't her first language so directions can get confusing. Very helpful if her class is in your major but if its not then the workload might be overwhelming.

Had to take her because her course was required. Hated it. Absolutely hated it. She's confusing and teaches us useless things. Class would honestly be better as a foundations course or foundations teacher. Once reviews came up, she tried acting nicer, but don't fall for it!

Irma is a very tough professor, but she's tough because she wants you to learn. She is always available outside class and wants everyone to succeed in her class.
