comment: She always seems to have a negative attitude and her instructions are confusing. The lab assistants help out and explain things more than she does. She's a difficult professor but you get good portfolio work out of her class.
Difficult class, but I've learned a lot. If you like easy courses, this is not for you. But if you are interested about pre-press production, this is the class to take.
Great material, it helps my career
No clarity, unfair, and disrespectful.  Try to stay away from a course of hers.

Irma is the worst professor I've ever encountered. The instructions she gives out in class is far from clear. There is a lot of misunderstanding with her and the students. She can't make up her mind about the dates of project deadlines. She is a tough grader and the attitude she gives sometime stinks. I don't recommend this teacher for printing.

She can be really nice if you're patient with her, but I didn't learn much. She doesn't seem to know about what she's teaching. Most of the important information comes from more experiencedknowledgable students clarifying for other students. Lots of wasted time in classes waiting for her to figure things out that should have been done beforehand.

I never know what she want. Lectures are boring. She seldom uploads necessary files and slides to myCourses, and in the syllabus you cannot see the specific grading formula. If you ask her any questions, she will firstly ask you to follow the instructions with strong accent of Mexican-Spanish. The instructions she gives us are confusing.

Mapes was a great prof, it was obvious she knew the material very well. Makes it clear what the student needs to do. If you read and can write well on the tests (all essay) then youll do fine. Nice overall
A fairly easy class (the only grades are a few quizzes, based on books and 2 tests based off the lectures). The only problem is the lectures are boring, she has trouble keeping the class interesting.

Terrific class and professor. Combo of lecture and discussion. Very enthusiastic and really cares if the students learn. A lot of work writing but worth it. Definitely one of the best profs I've had at RIT.

Overall Prof. Mapes made this a good class. It required a lot of reading and a lot of memorization to do really well on the tests (2 essay questions, 3 short answer), but as long as you read the required chapters and take good notes it's not bad. The class mostly consists of lecture so that was boring, but sometimes we got to watch documentaries.

Great professor!!! Really knows her stuff.She has really interesting lectures and makes history fun to study. I especially liked the reading and the discussions. She wants to hear what we think. . Her tests can be hard but they are fair. All in all a great class and a great professor
Quizzes unrelated to lecture. Lecture is boring, textbook is all primary sources. Do not take unless you feel like being quizzed on material completely unrelated to the lecture.

Took Women's History.  Grades are participation, journals about reading, and a long final paper.  Class was easy, but really useless - you never are tested on material and just have to spit up a page of information every week from skimming a reading.

Good teacher in my opinion. Tests were easy to study for as long as you read the text. My only complaint would be the apparently hard grading on paper and final. Before final and paper I had an A after apparently It dropped to  a C.
Easy enough class if you do the work. Read the chapter before every quiz and you will do well.

I'm a physics major with no interest in history. She kept my interest enough to get an A in the course. She made history bearable, even at 6-8pm. That speaks to her quality as a teacher. Do the reading, take notes and join in discussions and you will succeed.

Grade based on weekly quizzes from textbook reading which isn't bad, participation in class discussions, midterm/final. Tells you what to expect on midterm/final. Overall good teacher, a bit boring at times but knows what she is talking about. Make sure you do the reading for the quizzes and you'll get a good grade.

Boring class, but that isn't to say that she does a bad job teaching it. Very good teacher in that she tested on exactly what she lectures on in class, and told the class what would be on the midterm/final. I rarely got full credit on journal entries though, and NEVER got any useful feedback. Still, a relatively easy upper-level lib arts class.
Really interesting material and easy assignments (weekly reading reports and a paper), but her discussions were excruciating.  Other than that great teacher!
Take good notes and you'll get a 100 on everything. Very knowledgeable and very eager to share info to the class. Do the readings and take notes.

I had to miss two classes and he met up with me and literally went through all the notes as if it were a lecture. This man is a treasure. He did grade me a little harshly though, but his class was a pretty good choice for an elective.
For the 3 hour lectures Professor Dupre makes it interesting and was able to make me more interested in the topic and want to understand more. He also does not give much homework.

A three-hour lecture sounds awful in theory, but this is a non-issue for Prof. DuPre. Workload is fairly light, but not nothing. My only gripe is that he can be a bit disorganized, but this is generally a non-issue, as his passion for film is what makes his teaching successful. Would recommend this class and prof for this class in a heartbeat.

Professor DuPre knows his stuff and would help you better understand the material. He would make you see movies in a different perspective and make it very interesting and fun to learn. I love movies so this class was my favorite and besides, who loves having movie-watching as homework?? I wish I could take another class of his every day.

Professor is very passionate about film, does a good job explaining the concepts. Tries very hard to get technical majors interested in a liberal arts class. Textbook was used on the weekly quizzes however most could be answered with common sense. Would still recommend skimming through the chapters as its pretty light reading and a cheap book.

Intro Film. I have a major with intensive readings and writings. As a senior, this class was the most stressful class ever and it had the most sxtty workloads. This class wasn't that hard but expect reading a chapter every week & watching assigned movies  quiz every week and they are not exempt even on test days. Not flexible grader.

Need a filler class? Take this! Really interesting and easy A. DuPré knows his stuff and does a great job of teaching it in an interesting way accessible to all students. Normally a 3 hour lecture would be the worst thing in the world, but learning about how to read film was fascinating. So clear there's no need to take notes.

I'm an alumni, and I took this class (luckily enough) way back in my freshman year after I convinced DuPre to let me in when it was full.  Looking back, this class was one of the best I've ever had, and it definitely inspired me. Dupre is easy to work with but he knows his stuff. This professor deserves respect- & you can give that by doing well.

His film knowledge really blows you away. Tests aren't overly easy but he gives you very clear and helpful study guides. Papers are annoying art papers but he grades them pretty easily. Only outside of class work is watching a movie each week. Will go the full 3 hours of class, not boring, just long.

DuPre is a good professor. He clearly knows a lot about films. You will enjoy taking Film Arts with him. It is important show up the class and watch the movie and read the textbook to get good grades on quizzes. If you do that, you will get A or B easily.

I loved his class. It was very laid back and relaxed. He was never boring, and very easy to understand. His tests, quizzes, and papers are extremely fair if you do the small amount of reading and study. Take his class! You watch excellent movies and see them in a new light.

I'm a senior writing this, and I had him as a freshman. Since I'm graduating soon, it's apparent to me he's the best prof I've had at RIT. I never knew there was such a world behind film, and I would take his class again if I could. Definitely look into it if you need a liberal arts class. Easy work load, and you can tell he loves to teach film.

Probably the best teacher I have had at RIT yet. This class is not aimed to make you an artist rather it takes more of an engineering approach to break down alot of the components to the movies. He is funny and keeps the lectures interesting. Attendance is taken each class but can miss 3 classes before it reflects on grades I actually wanted to go.
Wonderful teacher. Highly suggest you take this class.

I had Mark for Fine Arts: Film Arts. This is a great class for anyone interested in film, even if you just like watching movies. He encourages a lot of class discussion but the lectures are big so you don't have to feel pressured. Never a boring class! He's super helpful and his essays are easy if you try. Take this class!

Great lecturer.  The most interesting professor I've ever listened to.  If you read the chapter each week and watch the movie you'll do great on the quizzes.  This was the easiest A ever, but this was also one of the best classes I've ever taken.  It changed the way I view films.

This guy is great. He is an excellent lecturer and keeps you interested throughout the entire class. Weekly quizzes are a breeze if you watch the film and read the assigned chapter in the book. Definitely recommend.

Great teacher. Although cocky at times he knows what he's talking about. Can't seem to figure out how to navigate through DVD Menus though. I would recommend taking his class. Essays are easy if you just look in the textbook and tests are easy as he tells you what to study for them. Careful when writing though, he's the worst grammar Nazi ever.

Amazing teacher. Knows what he's talking about, expressive speaker, tests are easy if you read the book. Stay for the movies, pay attention and you'll do fine. Will often give extra credit for silly errands.

Amazing teacher, probably the best class I've taken so far at RIT. It def gives you a new perspective on films, and he always seems excited about what he is teaching in class that day. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Probably an easy A, if u read the book and study. Exactly what i did, barely paid attention to class. O and we got to watch some pretty good movies as well. Overall nice guy, fair grader. Turned in 2 of my worst papers ever and still got an A on both! amazing...

You have the chance to take this class do it. You will not regret it. Mark Dupre is a amazing teacher who honestly is interesting in what he is teaching and this makes you become even more interested. I didn't even have to buy the text book which is $70 to do well in the course. Most of what is important he says in lecture.

Excellent professor.  Class is always interesting.  Only written assignments are three easy papers.  Quizzes once a week that are simple provided you have read the assigned chapter and watched that week's movie.  Movie selection is excellent.  Easy grade and fun class for anyone who enjoys movies.

Prof. DuPre is a great teacher. It's always a large class, so there isn't much one-on-one interaction, but the class is very interesting, and he teaches it well. Assuming you read the book (which is easy reading) you will do fine on the all multiple choice tests. The papers can be a bit trying if you don't love film, but if you do, take this class!
DuPré was a wierd guy. Uses different sayings like, "butter wouldn't melt in his mouth" and "potty trained too early".   Gives three tests, three papers.
Awesome guy, knows how to stimulate thinking on the subject of film. Not for film majors; a 'just-for-fun' class if you're interested in knowing more about film.
Super easy grader. Just do the homework and you're good. Simulation was weird though, then again every Sim software I've ever used has been weird

Professor Guntuka is well respected. He hasn't been teaching super long so I think he's still learning. He is super nice and really cares for his students. He wants to help us and is good about getting feedback from us. I didn't learn a ton from the class though. But he grades more on effort. If you put in the work, you'll be fine.

Overall a good class and professor. Lecture slides were easy enough to follow. Participation was strongly encouraged, even if it meant getting things wrong in discussion. 

Required to be in class, as part of grade is determined by participation in case study talks.

Homework was frequent but manageable (< 1hr) with clear instructions.

Steve is by and large my favorite teacher. I had no interest in 3D art until I took this class, and now I'm wishing he offered more classes. The workload he puts out it very time intensive and he expects you to be in class, so this is not a class to take lightly but it is an amazing experience. Until you take, You have no idea what you can create.

He always made time to talk to everyone individually, which helps a lot especially in your 1st year! His projects were a little more in depth than most other teachers, u could tell he really put time into it. and his crit's were actually NOT boring! you could say that u hated the project he was open to all feedback.

good teacher, strong ethics and morals show through when he grades. you will have to work hard to do well in this class, however it is well worth it and will make you a better designer. has a set design project which lasts a few weeks and is really fun

Steve was one of the best teachers I've ever had the honor to meet. His lessons were meant to intrique and was amazing when it came to really getting the student involved, teaching them the skills they needed for the real world of design, not just for school. He really made you earn your credits.
his class was very intreging, everything we did was something not alot of people would ever get to experiance and that made it hard but very interesting

Steve-o... He is a great teacher, but can sometimes be increadibly picky. He wants things his way or the high way, the class will be easier for you if you just comply to that right away. He has alot of experience and is open to new ideas. I learned alot from this guy and am sad he is leaving RIT.

Probably the only teacher to make YearOne semi-enjoyable. He's funny, proactive, and as much as I hated having to wake up for that class, it was probably more enjoyable with him than with anyone else. Hope to Destler's banjo collection that you get him.

PERSONALITY: This professor is very friendly and tries to get the entire class involved. GRADING: If you don't get an A in this class you've done something terribly wrong.  MISC:  The concept of this class is terrible, but Josh makes it somewhat endurable.  GRADE RECIEVED: A
He's so nice! I love this guy, regardless of how pointless FYE is.

He tries to stimulate discussion in order to make this amazingly boring class seem more interesting. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. He takes the class more seriously than other FYE professors, and expects you to work. Work isn't difficult though, and getting an A in the class involves simply having a pulse. Overall grade: B+

Boedo genuinely cares about pedagogy and it shows - the content, course sequencing, and textbook selection for 305 are all fantastic. The course isn't particularly difficult if you understand how to study - either you know how to apply the material or you don't. Do the homework, write a good cheat sheet, and you'll get a good grade.

Dr. Boedo is a great prof, but he is not easy. His class requires a genuine understanding of the material to do well.
He does not do enough examples in class, and his lectures are very theory heavy. You will have to study for his class. 
He is a fair grader and a great guy. I always felt engaged.
Only 4 total grades is very high stakes.
4 grades total, show up and listen to the lectures and you wont even need to do the homework

117 with Boedo was difficult, but definitely manageable. His lectures are usually very informative. However, he has the tendency to go on significant tangents during class. Very positive professor, easy to talk to, but if you want help in MECE 117, ask the TA's.

This class had 3 hw assignments and 3 projects, the hw assignments are very difficult and he won't assist he "wants to see how well you do alone" which is extremely useless and not helpful when you go to your professor when you're confused. Projects are easier than the hw and less time consuming and contribute more to your grade. huge curve on hw.

Boedo is a typical oldhead engineering prof. Good lectures, industry experience from decades before any current student were born. Can be frustrating at times (won't help with project) but he cares about your learning. Final grade is 3 exams and a project. Everyone bombs the exams, usually the curve is 25+ points. Pay attention and you'll be fine.
Lectures are good, online textbook is part of your grade, but not needed to do well in class.

Dr. Boedo lacks the ability to communicate effectively in a classroom setting. He has a difficult time answering questions, often replying that students look "back to what he said a few minutes ago," and a more difficult time with respect and professionalism. Mocks students openly in class. Final grade is based on 3 exams and a MATLAB project.

comment: Boedo does a good job at explaining concepts in an intuitive way. I tried a few times to read ahead in the textbook, but I never felt like I really understood the concept until Boedo would get to it in his lectures. Always chatty and engaging during lectures. He is visual-heavy, so it can be difficult to understand if that is not how you learn. Reading the textbook after lectures is extremely helpful to get equations he did not talk about in class. Strict grader, but is open about his grading criteria.

comment: Professor Boedo is a good teacher. He may be a bit dry but gets the information across. I struggled staying asleep towards the end of the semester in his class, I think his voice puts me to sleep haha

Boedo provided great lectures for Strengths II. I love how enthusiastic and knowledgeable he is about the material. HW regularly assigned, and while it is optional, it is a must do to pass the exams. Exams can be tricky. Tough grader when it comes to projects of which you will have two (both done using MATLAB). Overall a great class for MECE's.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: I have had Boedo for three classes.  Overall, he is very smart and I learned a lot from him in class.  However, there is NO help outside of class.  If you dare go to his office hours he will make you feel like the biggest inconvenience to him until you leave with no new information.  He is a tough and lazy grader.

Great professor, and really shows his passion for the subject material in a way that moves the class forward. Love his quirky enthusiasm. He 'assigns' optional homework, which unfortunately kills any motivation to do work outside of the lecture. The lack of graded work kind of makes the tests and projects seem like jumping into the deep end

Dr Boedo's strengths 2 class is extremely interesting. He is the best prefessor i have had by far. He is very knowledgeable and knows how to convey information to students. On top of that, he is very helpful.

Dr. Boedo's lectures for Strengths 2 are interesting and he teaches the material well. The homework for the class is optional, but you should do it as it makes the exams very easy if you've done it. He does tend to talk about academic honesty a lot, but he's the committee so that's expected. Overall the class was good and all MEs should take it.

Boedo teaches Finite Elements extremely well and clear! The course has an excellent ratio of theory and practice. Although the projects are not simple you will learn a lot by doing them. Best class I had so far as a grad student.

Very good professor and very available up until week 8. After that he drops off the radar while his class struggles to complete one of the biggest projects most of the students have been assigned at RIT up until that point. He's a great teacher if you handle the final project well, otherwise it is frustrating torture.

Very knowledgeable and helpful. Great class for future Design Engineers. Design project was long but not too bad. Has case studies every Friday that you're graded on. They're a bit intimidating but not too bad. HW takes a long time but tests are a lot easier even in only an hour. Shows a movie near the end of the quarter.

He was my favorite professor at RIT because of his ability to present the material in an understandable way.  His classes moved at a good pace and were always the most entertaining.  His grading was fair.
He is one of the smartest and best professors  in ME
Terrible. Cut class for two weeks after winter break, haven't seen him since. He was probably fired, and if so, he deserved it.
worst professor I have ever had
Horrible teacher, all over board with notes, not considerate and harsh.  A mean  teacher and just overall a jerk. Doesn't answer questions well and doesn't teach well. Find another teacher.
One of the smartest and coolest professors on campus.
By far the best professor in the ME dept.  had Emath1,2 continuum mechanics, non-linear dynamics, and analytical mechanics with him.  Very cool... super intelligent
No Comments
Incredibly laid back and understanding. Jason is encouraging while still challenging his students. Wish I could take a million classes with him.

Hes a cool guy :D, some of the projects are a bit time intensive and tedious to do but thats drawing for you. He does tattoos and ceramics! Very goofy and likes to talk to us :)
He gives pretty good advice for improving your sketches too :3
A funny guy to talk to. He was very nice and lead a good class. Critiques were very long though. Overall a pretty fun course. Would take again!!
Very silly guy- his projects sometimes weren't the most interesting but he made the class fun and was a very easy grader and critiquer.

Had her for experimental writing (creative writing).  She is very easy and the class is an easy A as long as you try and turn things in on time.  Use the textbook to clarify anything you don't understand. Class is a bit boring, sometimes we watch movies that are stupid and irrelevant to the course.  Got an A, just for showing effort and s
Work is unclear. Final project is 50 percent of your grade. She is crazy but a nice person. Put in the effort and you will succeed.

Easy A. Try your best and you're fine. Effort is what she looks for, since it's hard to judge creative writing. Do the assignments and turn them timely. I spent at about hour on homework per week. Sometimes what she's looking for is not so clear, ASK her again and she will clarify! Most often she'll say stuff twice anyways.

WRITING SEM. Professor can't hear, can't hear a word, waste half a class trying to get her to hear one sentence. Can't make up her mind on assignments, very unclear on requirements when she does. Makes bad writing suggestions. Grades easy if you're a decent writer but the class is absolutely painful. This class ruined a subject I once really liked.
Had it for Writing Seminar. Hated the class.
Dr. Reinfeld could be a good teacher, but she doesn't respect other's opinions, and she never speaks in a a clear, understandable way. She is easy, but dull.
Not really much goes on in class, but if you keep up with the online work and at least make an attempt you'll get an A.
An excellent instructor for writing. Gives very helpful feedback for your papers if you put enough effort into them. The rest of the class is easy.
You never are sure of your grade until the end of the quarter.  She doesn't comment on your work unless it's really good or really bad.

Prof Reinfeld is extremely fun and an easygoing professor. she is attentive to students' needs. Due to the nature of creative writing, unless you try to fail, you shouldn't worry about terrible grades. She uses the text and MyCourses extensively.

Took her Arts of Expression: Experiments and Explorations.  She's the kind of teacher who means well, and isn't too hard to get on her good side.  Everyone started the class with an 85 average (good or bad depending on how you look at it) No final exam, we only had 1 quiz.  Weekly reading and writing assignments from the book.
I love her
No Comments

amazing professor--lets you rewrite all your papers for a higher grade. none of the papers were very long or difficult. easy class, homework was reading very short stories. threatened us with pop quizzes all the time but we only got one.

Although she might seem to be tough, but she willing to help you on anything that you don't understand.  Also, the great thing is that there is resubmission for every paper that you have to write.  **NO FINAL** Side tip:  Attend all her class... grade penalty for missed class. Take her if you can
awesome teacher... she is a very nice person and the class is easy... if you think its hard, she offers a lot of help!

"Grandma Reinfeld" is one of the nicest english teachers out there.  She is sweet as pie and will allow for resubmission of papers with no penalty.
she is absolutly insane...but really easy and rather funny...take her if you can
Lots of fun.  Crazy old lady.  Completly gone, but is so much fun to have.  Good

She doesn't give good grading criteria. She is very flexible with due dates if you speak. She wants an interactive classroom .She always gave us a lecture about answering questions or asking them. There was a group project throughout the course, reflection assignments when she wanted to give them out, and them one test.

Professor Felice was highly disorganized in her work. The class was not particularly difficult, but assignments were often handed out last minute and due dates changed at random. If he explained things more concisely and didn't always hide his code the second it's done the experience would've been a lot nicer. Wake is the goat fr, he keeps the class engaged and does some funny jokes throughout the lecture to keep us entertained as they usually are pretty packed. sadly you gotta pay attention for the entire lecture or you'll end up missing some part of the code needed as it is pretty fast paced however Prof Wake makes up for it by being a great teach

127 is a rough class, but Wake makes it bearable. His lecture can be dry, but he's good at explaining concepts. He cares a lot about his students and is very accessible outside of class.
He is the GOAT!
Professor Wake is an awesome teacher and I would highly recommend his classes.

One of the harshest graders in this department. He doesn't actually teach anything in this course (which sucks because he has a lot of knowledge). You learn everything from boring old videos online that don't fully make sense. Unfortunately no great options for this class, but you will not get a good grade from this instructor.
He was great! Had him for GCIS 123 and it was an excellent experience. Gives wonderful feedback, genuinely cares about his students, overall an awesome guy that makes a difficult course a lot better.
Took him 2 times and was the worst decision of my life
fun teacher, wake was always engaged and tried to help when possible, even for students newer to code, he always attempted to help with any problems on the spot.

Professor Wake is an exceptional professor who genuinely cares about his students and is always willing to offer assistance. He goes the extra mile by providing explicit information about exam content, ensuring students are well-prepared.
Really cool guy, personable in class and really seemed to care about students who were struggling.
try to choose a different gcis123 professor

GCIS-123 was rough for me, but it's a mandatory class, so there's no escaping it. However, Prof Wake made it bearable. He was always kind and patient with me despite the fact that I barely understood the material half the time. He went over homework and other works to help us further understand. I did appreciate his occasional jokes during class.

I am making this review 3 years after I took class with him, I was unable to find him on this website when I took the class with him. It was an awesome introduction to Software Engineering at RIT taking both 123 and 124 with him. Could not hold him in higher regards as a professor

He in general is a really good professor and when I got him for my first semester of RIT my expectation was very high, and he surely lived up to it. He makes sure to give everyone importance in the class and he teaches really well. I love him, def taking him again!

Class was great. He has a monotone voice but he actually cares and explains all the material very well. The lectures for the class are department made, but he does a good job explaining and will occasionally use ms paint to draw out diagrams to help. The teacher also allows one page cheat sheets for every exam including the final.

Prof. Wake is amazing. Since he didn't have a Hard Of Hearing student, he asked me how could he make the class more accessible for me. If I was struggling he would send a detailed feedback and the concerning factors to know what to improve. Not only does he make sure everyone passes, but he wants every student to feel comfortable in class.
Absolutely amazing, would go to class again.
Amazing professor

Freshmen (abt class): the class is aimed at new programmers, students often treat programming as wizardry. Don't. Python (lang in class) is very high level; abstract. Think literally/logically, watch some vids on abstract prog. Prof Wake is funny and genuine. Cares about his students. He'll always stay after to help. Course discord is very helpful
An average professor, not as bad as some of the reviews say. Tests are easy if you read the material. Requires iClicker. Mastering Astronomy

Don't take her class. She's nice, but gets angry at students who ask questions and tells them to look it up on their own. Easily flustered during lectures, and labs are just a 1.5 hour lecture and a rushed 20 minute lab that never gets finished in time.

Horrendous professor. Not only is she extremely dull, but she is very negative and is flustered quite easily. She teaches straight form the power-point and does not elaborate well on the topic. You will learn better from the textbook. Great topic, but absolutely horrible professor.  If you want to take Astronomy, do NOT do it with this woman.

She is boring at the first few 3 weeks&she becomes better after that. Try to make joke &ask students questions for paying attention to her. she doesn't penalize for mistakes in homework(do thousands ones). drop the lowest quiz and increase midterm exams score by replacing the lowest one with final.I get A .she is not too bad as Others Can Be Worse

Dr. Monsay is a fair professor.  She is extremely boring, but if you do all of the work it isn't that bad.  She has pre-lab and post-lab quizes which are hard, mastering physics problems, and her tests are difficult.  But, if you put the time in you will get a good grade.

Not only is she a sub par professor, she doesn't really seem to understand how to put together and run a course. Lecture consists of her doing problems straight from the book, and 'lab' is just another 2 hour lecture. She gives online quizzes and Mastering physics HW and constantly changes due dates at the last minute. Very frustrating class.

Lectures are not worth going to, they are extremely boring and you'll learn more from reading the book. She gets flustered and off topic while teaching. She is very nice and helpful at her office hours, but is very slow to return tests and takes points off for ridiculous reasons. If you've taken physics before you'll be fine.

Not a good teacher, forces students to learn and do physics exactly like her or massive points are taken off. Super confusing math techniques. Unfortunately for college phys 1 is either her or Zielinksi who is also terrible, good luck!
Very boring teacher. Lecture is brutally dull. She is not on top of grades. Its week 8 and we still haven't gotten things back from week 1. I won't know if i failed or not til its too late.

Worst professor I have ever had, I actually had to drop the course because of how poor the quality of teaching was. She did not give good examples, is far too strict about naming conventions, and lost nearly 30 students after a test due to the fact that she told us not to study formulas that were vital to the test. Do NOT take this professor!!

Avoid this teacher at all costs I spent more time with the TA because he was able to teach us more. Her lectures are all over the place and she seems like she doesn't understand the information. She doesn't seem confident at all when she talks to the class and gets easily led off topic. Try to take this with another teacher.

Amazing professor. He often ends lectures early because there isn't that much material to cover in this class. He tells a lot of stories during class, and they are all interesting. Easy and fun class to pass.

He is amazing! Super down to earth dude who assigns a minimal amount of assignments. Notes are posted online, but he makes lectures enjoyable. Allows a cheat sheet for online exams. Very chill course, I definitely recommend.

Bro is the goat. Take him, you will do well in the class and will leave with good information about the workforce and his personal experiences (I found it more helpful than the class). He is also really funny, knows his stuff, and is willing to help out struggling students (although the course is super easy).

Take him over anyone!

Good prof! His explaining things didn't work for me since I found the class to be harder, and slides are used, but he's nice and straightforward. I went on the Verizon switch tour which was super cool! He swears a lot and talks about his experience working in industry for Verizon so be ready for that. He says he can be bribed with white Monsters.

William Crowe the absolute GOAT! Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had. He is very funny and good at teaching. The class is super easy too although the TA was a bit tougher of a grader. All and all it was definitely worth taking with him.
Actually the GOAT. Just teaches the important stuff, doesn't waste your time with irrelevant information. Very enjoyable.

The GOAT. Best teacher you could take for NSSA. Explains concepts very well, is helpful on labs, and lets us out of every class an hour early. He worked in the industry and knows his stuff. He has great stories, funny, and super chill. HIGHLY recommend.

Crowe is the MAN. He is the best 241 prof by far. He is an industry professional who loves to tell stories about his work life. He is hilarious and is willing to help you in any way you can. He makes the lectures to the point and interesting adding his own flare. Labs are challenging but he will help you. TAKE THE VERIZON TOUR IF YOU HAVE A CHANCE!

Really funny and chill, really nice too. Had clear knowledge of the material. It was hard but I've heard that's just the nature of the course. Easy grader and super accommodating for students, really wants everyone to succeed. Felt super easy to approach and talk to, I'd definitely take him again.

So he would always tell stories about his old days and how advanced the world has gotten, he teaches really good, and he can explain the logic of the code reallly well. 100% will take him again, easy to medium midterm questions too!

Had a great time with this professor! I was new to coding and he taught Python is such a great way. I would not say I like the course GCIS 123 but I love the prof. Grading was good and precise. Would 100% take it again with him. HE's FUNNY TOO!!!

Crowe just started this year as a professor, after graduating from RIT. This class needed a filler teacher, but he primarily focuses in Network Engineering (NSSA 241). Chill teacher and understands the atmosphere of the classroom. Ends class early if we have gotten through all the content. Tells funny stories and relatable. 100% would recommend.
Couldn't have asked for a better Drawing I professor!

Whenever I would overthink her assignments, it was really easy to get guidance from her so that I wouldn't overplan her work. Her assignments work with different mediums in very open-ended ways. Like she said, she didn't want the class to overwhelm the students, but she simultaneously challenged us to work outside our typical mediums.

I loved taking 2D Design I with Liz! Every week you have one project and she has a very structured schedule that benefitted me Each week you also have critique of the project you worked on the last and you get great feedback from both Liz and your peers You won't use digital in this class because it is a foundations class as what should be expected

Don't take this class if you are looking for a professor that lets you use digital mediums. We had to use all traditional for the first half of the class. Additionally, I have never gotten a 100 no matter how hard I try, she is almost looking for unnoticeable mistakes. The lectures don't really teach much, find a better professor if 2D is required.

I took 2D Design with Liz. She is VERY helpful in what you should do to improve your pieces. She allows reworks on all of your pieces so that you can actually apply the comments made during the critique onto your piece for a chance of a higher grade. Her classes are super organized- you basically always know what you're going to do each day.

Dr. Kray can be a tad boring, but she is incredibly kind, especially with grading. You get to choose what to do to earn credit (either projects or exams). A good chunk of points can be earned just by going to class. Overall, a very easy A.
Did a great job teaching the material and making good conversation with the students.

Professor is great, material is very easy, asynchronous and discussion based with lots of reading. The course was very easy.

Gave by far the most feedback of any of my online professors this semester. I took her immigration class. She is a very caring professor. She will assign considerable reading, nothing excessive or dry if you are interested in the topic a lot. comment: She is a nice prof, but for ANTH 335 she gives a lot of reading and writing. Her lectures are somewhat interesting. She clears every detail well so kind. She gives at least 4 big papers, 2  long readings every week and a one-page paper to write on those readings, three presentations. It important to participate every day.  It not an easy A class

Professor Kray is the sweetest. She is very passionate about the topics she teaches, so she will sometimes explain things quickly, but will always clear up any questions students ask her. She assigns a lot of homework and reading, but the tests are based very closely off of this. Interesting class with an accommodating professor.

Incredible professor & very intelligent. Knows a ton about Latin America and it's obvious how passionate she is about it. Topics that I had no interest in became interesting to me. She mixed up history and culture perfectly. Students in the class also shared their experiences. Great class! Only wish I could've fit her Immigration class in!
I wish Dr. Kray was a professor in my major - she is the absolute best.  I took an online course with her and she provided so much feedbackguidance and is always willing to help.
Great professor, very helpful! the class was easy and an interesting one.
She is Great and friendly professor. Her class is not hard but if you don't study for tests, you can fall behind. Sometimes she does not tolerate late work.
Nicest professor ever! extremely helpful and reassuring helped multiple times with issues regarding other classes and professor. Wonder woman with a big heart. Very positive an loves teachig

She was overall quite interesting and experienced in her area of expertise. Sometimes classes could be boring but if you pay attention it's easy to learn. Homework consisted of reading from the textbook and answering 4 multiple choice questions. There were 2 very easy multiple choice exams and 2 essays. Easy and fun teacher.

I'm bad a multiple choice questions and that's what this class is made of. Luckily extra credit is offered which probably helped me achieve an A. Homework was straight out of the text and easy to get 100% correct. Class consists of 10 weekly homeworks, 3 exams and one research paper. Good class but nothing interesting.

Been in multiple classes with C Kray. I believe in her cause and love her personality. highly recommended for those looking for a truly intelligent and society-minded prof. If you are just interested in getting an easy A on the other hand then you could give her a shot- you'll probably find the lectures boring if you don't care about the material.
She gave us 2 hour powerpoints, which talked about the chapters we already read. Boring lectern.

had prof kray for maybe 3 classes. what a dominator. her voice could put crying children to sleep, so pleasant. lotta kids take the intro to anthro to fill a req lib arts. but she has some fun upper level ones too.
she was very organized
Really nice teacher, interesting reads, fun assignments. Definitely would recommend.

She is a very nice lady, very nice, but very boring. Maybe its because research techniques are hard to make interesting, but it was a snoozer. Talked with my partner throughout the quarter and still got an A. Very concerned with students learning. Study the ppts, dont bother reading the book.
Very easy class but can be a bit boring. Not hard to get a good grade if u pay attention. I got a B and did a VERY small amount of studying. All the tests were mult. choice.

Do not take unless you like the material! It will bore you to death otherwise. She loves to hear herself talk and rambles too much on the topics covered in the reading.  If you read the book and study guide,and like anthropology you can get an A or a B witout too much trouble.

Shes a really nice lady... its just that anthropology is boring, and the whole class was power point lectures.  I got an A in the class by doing a fair amount of studying.  She also gives extra credit oppourtunities as well as bonus on tests
The Jamaican video was awesome... good teacher toga girl

This teacher isn't too difficult, but her lectures are directly out of the book, making the requred reading assignments totally pointless... loves to hear herself talk. Take her if you need a class to sleep through.
super super easy. get A or be ashamed

He explains topics very thoroughly and is very supportive of student learning. He forces students to think through questions on their own. He takes the emphasis off of performing perfectly and puts  it on learning as much as possible. Three tests, plus a cumulative final and you get a handwritten note sheet for each. 8 or 9 homeworks.

He is a very reasonable and fair professor who grades super easily. There is a lot of work, but if you do it you will succeed in the class. Watch out, sometimes he decided students could all just stay after the class period to make up for lectures he missed. Other than that, he's one of the power professors in the department.
Extremely helpful. Calm and composed. Student's friendly
Savakis is the man! So entertaining! Don't take me too seriously though, I only had him for Intro to Computer Engineering.
This man is my hero.  Totally awesome.

Good lectures, especially great to talk to one-on-one about concepts. Extremely knowledgeable and is happy to help explain concepts, or break them down beyond what was mentioned in class. Will point you in the right direction if you want to learn more. Straightforward class, with practice exercises, a few HWs, and some exams. Def recommended

This class was pretty interesting, however, there's a lot of information to grasp in one semester, or at least that's how I felt. Because of this sometimes lectures felt overwhelming. The homework is normally not hard to complete because it is well documented, there are also only two projects.

comment: Austin is a great guy and a really engaging lecturer. He's really friendly and was very clear in explaining different concepts. He's pretty good about being available for help and is quick to respond to emails or discord pings. Homework and exercises are of appropriate difficulty and instructions are clear.

If the class code changed - it was RM 2. The class wasn't hard to grasp, it was a lot of projects to work on (3). Austin was very clear in his presentations & you can tell that he's passionate about full stack engineering. Keep in mind that this class will have volatile topics as the prof tries to keep it up to date along with the web industry.

Not too difficult of a class, he's really good at explaining the concepts. Anytime you have a question on the homework or projects you can message him over discord and he gets back to you really quickly with the answer that solves all your problems.
Be wary of the weekly quizzes, they're the only thing to fear. Otherwise a very nice and forgiving professor who runs an good class
Fun and respected professor who makes learning server development easy.

Austin is probably the most caring professor Ive seen in RIT. He explains the course material very well and will take time to communicate with you after class for the A* project or homeworks. The class material might be difficult at times as it is C++, but overall Austin does a great job

Austin has done a good job teaching DSA 1 considering it is his first year. The material is simple (basically GDAPS 2 but in C++) and there is not a lot of work at all. Austin is in his first year of teaching, over the year he has become more and more confident in his lectures. His grading style is extremely fair and timely, meet the requirements, you get an A. If you do find yourself falling behind you can just ask him to re-explain or go to one of his numerous office hours. Overall a great addition to IGM.

This was Austin's first semester teaching. He did a great job teaching in a practical setting and relied more on showing rather than telling. He was always willing and available to help if you needed it. All around a wonderful professor.

comment: Austin is a new professor, so his teaching skills still have room for improvement. However, he is really nice and always willing to help. comment: Great professor

In his first year teaching, Austin has already managed to break free of the awful powerpoints from prior DSA classes. He's not the best at teaching at all for sure, he's a little shaky with laying out the concepts and explaining it well. Other students I've talked to would agree that his teaching style isn't that good or helpful. Had to go over and reteach the material myself for a while.

Professor Zhang talks pretty quietly and lectures every class. If you don't have much C++ knowledge beforehand, you won't learn much and will need to learn things on your own. Very sweet and laid back. Gave us Fridays off. However very disorganized. rarely got back to emails, only graded one assignment all quarter. Class mostly relies on textbook readings and quizzes. Final grade seemed to factor in zeros for assignments that were not required on the syllabus and she did not write back to me when I asked her about this.
The professor's teaching style was disorganized, and they struggled to convey the material clearly. Key concepts were poorly explained, leaving students confused and unprepared.

Professor often cancelled class and assignments.  Changed due dates leaving new expectations very unclear.  Never graded anything, was just given an arbitrary final grade with no idea if it was deserved or not.  Talked non stop about her graduate classes.  Left the impression that the graduate classes are where her time and effort may be spent.

Shes a good person but her teaching skills I think are not that good. Her my courses and syllabus is very unorganized and changes the due dates around often. Her materials are all over the place in my courses and is hard to find. Group projects for business plan we work with our groups. Most of the time this class is to work with your group.

She's kind and understanding. Very knowledgeable and willing to help if you ask. This class mostly consisted of working on one group project with multiple deliverables throughout the semester. She does not really stick to her syllabus and gives little to no direction when sending you off to work on your project leaving you to figure it out yourself

Professor Thiuri is extremely kind and compassionate, showing lots of care and attention to the needs of her students. That being said, classes can be frustrating as she talks in circles, sometimes never covering expected topics. Be prepared to do your own reading/research OUTSIDE of the textbook/in your free time, as tests are never set in stone.

She focuses more on current events than the textbook readings making tests more difficult than necessary. She is nice and very knowledgeable in business. Most of the class is group projects and reading the textbooks. Be prepared to never know your grade because she doesn't grade anything till the end of the semester.

Most difficult and unprofessional professor I have ever had at RIT. She barely gives instructions for assignments and takes points off for things never mentioned in the instructions. She doesn't lecture and gives exams that are impossible to do well on. She is also extremely rude and takes forever to respond to emails if she responds at all.

The teaching method of this professor doth resemble a jest. Within this lamentable chamber, the professor's disregard doth masquerade as instruction. Students are abandoned, the knowledge unaided whilst she doth impose her limited beliefs without heed for true enlightenment. Verily, 'tis a marvel if any doth attain learning amidst such a trashcan.

comment: Most useless class in RIT Business. Better than a philosophy class at making you regret being born. Teacher feels like she hates you and she forces you to have camera on at all given times. Please do not take expecting easy grade only take if you really don't want to go outside and touch the grass.

The lectures are manageable if you pay attention, the exams can be challenging. He offers a lot of flexibility with assignment deadlines and extra time for submissions, and the course includes one individual and one team project. The course however has a tight schedule, which leaves no room for unexpected events which can disrupt the semester.

Very easy online course and can be done in a mater of days since it is asynchronous. Many but not all the terms can be found on quizlet. She responds to emails very quickly and is helpful. Overall very easy class

All the work can be done in 2 days max. So make sure you do it before classes start. It's the easiest A you can get. All the answers to the exams are on Quizlet. The syllabus is super clear; if you email her, she will respond quickly with clear instructions.

Took MED201 online, it's only offered online. She responded quickly to emails outside of class. Very easy course, chapters and final exam are there from day one. Just takes time to complete it. An easy A for me.

Spent an overall 15-18 hours on the course and got full marks on every task. The final is the only thing that is partly challenging as its timed but does not matter as the answers are all online and you just need to google them quick. Easiest course youll ever take, can finish the whole course at once, the final is available to do from day 1

Easiest class that you can finish in a couple days. I did it as soon as it opened up before classes and did not have to think about this course for the rest of the semester. Most of the question on the final came from the self tests and be sure to study the suffix and prefix terms as those were on the final

Online class that is self paced - do it as soon as it opens up on mycourses!! Should take about 2 or 3 days to complete - biggest time consumers are the 1000 flashcards you have to type in, and the 300 question TIMED exam - must complete all activities to do the exam - great for emailing if you have a problem. 50% of grade  classwork / 50%  exam

Probably one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Finished the entire thing in less than 24 hours. All you do is go through the power points, take some tests that you can take over and over until you get a 100, and then a final exam. The final is 300Q, 150 min (yikes) and 50% of your grade, so just be prepared. Over all VERY easy.

I found this class super boring. You just have to fill in a powerpoint for the lecture. Study from the powerpoint for the test (but she even lets you have a cheat sheet for them). Wasn't interested at all though.

I took her med term class, and I spent a good 5 hours a week on it and the only reason I passed was my sister and Google.  The final did not AT ALL reflect what they emphasized in the course.  The students who reported this class as easy must have  all gotten together with Google to do the final. Answers for the final are not on Quizlet btw.
Extremely easy for Human Biology. Grade is only based on exams. Her lectures are pretty boring, but she always posts her slides online. She is a sweetheart as well. Very nice to all her students.
Easy class, everything is on the powerpoints. Teacher is boring, learned more from powerpoints than listening to her.
Medical Terminology was really easy. Self paced and you do it on your own time. 300 question final was nuts though! Highly reccomend if you need a 2 or 3 credit Liberal Arts (Gen Ed) filler!

I took her online class Medical Terminology- SO EASY. If you actually want to learn the material the course is probably hard, but it's great if you're looking for a quick and easy online class. I finished the course in two days and received an A and four credits.
Very nice online class, it is so good if you know the material. I never meet her, that all about it :). But if you really need this class you can take it. This is all right believe me.

Was scheduled as a classroom course but it turned out it was online. Super easy class-- you can pretty much do ALL of it in 8 hours on the last day if you put it off like I did. Easy quizzes you take repeatedly until you get 100 and the final (worth 50% of your grade) is simple as well. Easy class, easy grade. Take it if you can!
She's decent. Class isn't too difficult, you just have to write 4 essays, which includes a group assignment. It's a small class but easy if you pay attention.
She seemed genuinely interested in making us better writers. I don't understand why the other commenters struggled so much, I had harder writing assignments in high school.
If you're not already good at writing essays, don't take this class. Her essay prompts are confusing and boring and rely on equally confusing and boring essays that she assigns to read.

Stay away from this professor. I'm an engineering major and I was spending more time on this class than math & science combined. She expects way too much and the papers we had to write were irrelevant, confusing and pointless. I feel like I wasted all of my nights staying up till 4am writing because I have to retake the class now anyway.

Completely ridiculous. Don't take her because there are about 20 other professors most of which will make the class an easy A. I took her freshman year and after 4 quarters that class is still my only B. Expects way too much dedication from a class that is required and no one takes by choice.

She really knows her stuff and loves english/writing, but she is not set out for teaching. Her lectures are boring and confusing, and she is a tough grader. She definitely favors some students and isn't nice to others. All of the topics that we had to write about for our essays were dumb. I was so bored the whole time.

Really nice guy - projects weren't too hard. Most people seemed to get a decent grades. Some projects are a bit open, but he generally likes the direction people go in. It's a fun class - he's pretty laid back.

Honestly? James Holland  ruined 2D for me this year. he has trouble explaining/clarifying assignments, and his assignments take HOURS to decipher. if he decides he doesnt like what you create, then he trashes it. He grades based on the "c is average" principle. consequently only one person in my class got an A, even though many deserved one.

Super easy class, but I really only learned about audio terms and not implementation. The projects are simple as long as you record your sounds and don't half-ass everything. His obsession with black and white movies is a bit silly. It would have been nice to see modern examples of everything he talks about.

Al is a fantastic professor, I learned a lot more in his class than any other. He's always willing to help with your code. Even though the concepts behind the code are sometimes challenging to grasp, the code itself isn't that hard. He's also good at explaining everything in terms that you can understand. 12/10 take his class

Great class to take, I felt I learned a lot compared to 101. Al may not be a fan of JavaScript but was incredibly helpful in not only teaching us how to do each concept, but helping us understand how the concept worked and the reasoning behind how and why its used. Amazing professor, and a pleasure to be in class with. Pretty jazzy guy all around.

Takes an incredibly long time to grade, making it very hard to gauge how well you are doing in the class. Programming assignments often went far beyond what we learned in class. Although helpful, he would sometimes leave us to our own devices to figure out complex problems. Great guy and helpful occasionally.

Prof. Biles is a great lecturer, and an even better professor. He is really down-to-earth, and obviously cares about his students. Very approachable and helpful outside of class as well. Would definitely recommend him!

Biles gives interesting lectures, but the projects were completely useless. Really easy class one research paper, a power point presentation (that you do the voice-over), and a 20-things I learned in this class project, portrayed however you wish. Biles never graded any of my assignments, and just gave out A's. Also there is no textbook.
the class is hard not the professor. lot of work but biles is one of the better lecturers. if you can get lawley take her instead

Very good at teaching the material.  If you need help, he will go over any material you need.  The workload is fairly easy, as he wants you to focus on the quarter long project.  Like any class, you will get out of it what you put in.

Lectures were quick and didn't pay attention, the labs are based off of the lectures but you can get by without knowing the lectures.  HW is a 8 pg paper and a 5 min ppt on it, but its easy since you can pick ANY topic.  The "final" is a 5 min ppt on what you learned in the class.  Just take notes in the lecture and you're pretty much good.nice guy

Introduction to Interactive Media was a horrible, useless experience for me, but I sat through the first session of it ever and it was a group class between several professors, not just Biles. In labs he experimented, giving either too little information or too much technical stuff without really translating it in English perse.  Easy class though.

Yes, he does have a monotone and there is very minimal class activity.  He provides notes online so you don't have to take any and he provides a study guide that covers pretty much the whole exam.  Overall, very boring but if you at least try and attend class you should have no problem, I'm no schooly but I got through.

This class was relatively straight forwards, but it was taught through power points with little explanation. I'm ranking him so low because the professor put a zero in the grade book, for a completed and on time assignment, until a few minutes before final grades were due. He did not respond to the multiple emails regarding the zero.
Strong accent which makes him hard to understand at times but he knows his stuff and efficient teacher, no fluff

I took this instructor 30, YES 30, years ago and I've been thinking about him because of the things he said 30 years ago about Israel/Netanyahu and Russia/Ukraine and how they have come to fruition. I wasn't even a history major and I loved all the classes I took with this professor. I'm glad I told him how amazing he was.
I took one of his classes and end up minoring in political science thanks to him. Great lecturer and very accessible outside of class

Kaylani is the most powerful lecturer in the history department. Write down everything he says, and study for 10 hours. Roughly 1 in 10 students gets an A. It is true that he has no tolerance for total ignorance or intellectual illiteracy, so many students get shot down in class for not knowing the word "autarky" or Chomsky, Keynes, and Schumpeter.

Can barely understand him, and cant read anything he writes. Constantly tells the students that they are stupid because they don't know some obscure fact in history. Even the kids that liked history got tired of talking and being told that their opinions were wrong. He teaches his view of what happened in history and is not open to debate about it.

Great Teacher but makes you work extremely hard.  The tests aren't to bad if you take good notes but make sure to study them.  He doesn't require attendance but the things he says in class may not be in the book but WILL be on the test.  Overall very good class extremely smart guy

Modern European was one of the most intresting I've taken. Kaylani is easy to listen to and he is passionate about what he's teaching. Tests weren't hard as long as you went to class and paid attention. I'd like to take another class with him in the future.

Hard, but great professor. Wants his students to understand history, not memorize dates. I enjoyed his class, and learned alot. If you listen to lectures and DO NOT MISS CLASS, and of course read you will do fine. Test based 90% on lecture material. Take him.. You will learn more.. Do not expect an A, but you will learn value of a good education.

Out of any teacher I have ever had, I would say that Dr. Kaylani has had the greatest impact on my academic life.  He is the first teacher that has made me actually enjoy history, and want to know more about it.  Studying for anything became much more bearable, and even enjoyable after taking him.  Because of this, my whole GPA went up.
Amazing amount of insight.  Makes you want to learn the material outside of the class, which is something not many teachers can do.  Sometimes I wonder why he teaches at a tech school.
One of the most intelligent professors ive ever had.

Probably the best teacher I've had to date.  Doesn't waste any time, and knows so much about what he is talking about it sometimes scares me.  Holds students up to the same standards to which I think he holds himself.  He made me want to learn the material myself more than any other teacher I've ever, and that's the most important thing.
Amazing Professor,  will give you all the facts you need to know about the Middle East.  Highly recomended.  All you have to do is listen to class lecture and take notes to get east As in exam.
If you want to read 30 pages a day for the rest of the quarter, take his class.

A very challenging but informative professor.  Grades came from three multiple choice tests, no final.  He has a ridiculous amount of insight into politics and history, and is a really nice dude (as long as you ask intelligent questions!)  Would recommend for anyone seriously intersted in history.

Had Kaylani for European and Mid.East History.  He is one of the most intelligent people I have ever met.  I feel like a much more educated person after having taken his classes.  He is a touch teacher, but if you actually care more about your education instead of just your grades - TAKE HIS CLASS.

The best professor I've had so far.  Has a frighteningly sharp intellect and his lectures keep you hooked the entire time.  He really made me want to learn the material.  Dr. Kaylani should just open up his own institution.  I'd go.
I took 3 courses with him because of his tough teaching style.  Though I didn't do well in his classes, I learned much more from him than I would from other history professors (Newman is also great)

Very tough grader....grades came from only 3 tests and they were extremly hard...does not curve at all...notes are taken directly from his mouth, and he talks too fast and has an accent so its hard to understand...studied a lot but still did not do well..
he sucks, puts down students, don't take
The only professor able to keep my attention at this abhorrent school.  I wish I had taken more of his classes.

One of the best teachers i've ever had.  Extremely knowledgeable and motivated.  He has a way of getting ahold of your attention and being interesting like no other teacher. He is demanding, and an excellent educator.

Kaylani is like no other teacher you've ever had. His excitement over the material is evident in everything he teaches. He has pretty demanding expectations for his students, but all his tests are multiple choice (but usually difficult multiple choice).
very good, but tough
Tough but very very good.

Amazing professor, really passionate about teaching is truly kind and is willing to explain things that I should probably know but don't. I have never had a better professor during my time here at RIT. Relatively easy class if you pay attention and he makes it rather easy since he's quite a good teacher.

Prof. Wong was always ready to help and had a structured, easy-to-follow grading system. HW and Quiz happen once a week pretty easy to study for with the ebooks webassign. Explain things in Gen-Z terms and makes puns here and there. Willing to help you understand problems from bottom to top.

Very entertaining lectures (uses slides, but makes sure to make them fun with memes and jokes to keep you awake). He will help you in any way he can and is very easy to reach. Wouldn't recommend leaving the homework for last minute, but he is lenient on deadlines (that he has control over) if you have a valid reason.

I guess he really did change the structure to his class because he is nothing like the older reviews. He allows you to work in groups in class if you want to. He's funny and explains concepts well. Out of the other 181 professors he is definitely top 3. Makes it very easy to pass the final due to the nature of how he teaches his class.

Dr. Wong is a fair grader. Homeworks and Classworks make it easy to grasp in-class content. Class is structured quite well and exams are reasonable(he gives you an index card to use as a cheat sheet and most formulas are provided).

Always communicates info about exams/assignments very well. Exams generally followed lecture work and review materials/practice exams. Recitations are mandatory but very helpful. Towards the end, the quizzes in recitation had lots of extra credit. Prof. Tony is hilarious and makes lectures funny and interesting.

Funny and makes the lectures very enjoyable. However, he is utterly terrible at structuring his class and setting up materials to help you on the exams. We had to use literally five separate services to turn in assignments and interact with the class. Exams are reprehensibly hard, so be prepared to do everything assigned and still barely pass.

Super nice and fun guy, I guess he changed his class drastically cuz his class is nothing like what the older reviews say. Lots of group work, class average on tests is like a B, lot of extra credit opportunities, and grade is really more from effort than just the tests, since each test is 5% of final grade. Material gets a lot harder near the end.

To preface, I am doing mediocre in his probability and statistics class. So I reached out to him and asked for extensions and he has been EXTREMELY lenient and kind. Just based off that alone, he seems to care more than other professors who couldn't really care about whether you have erroneous circumstances or other classes.
Dr. Wong is a good professor who does his best to make a boring class interesting. His tests are very difficult and cover the hardest material. Averages are usually 50-60.

I abhor stats and he made me enjoy the class. Lectures were great, super accessible outside of class, and very caring of students. After our class averaged a 58 on the midterm, he changed the grading system to ensure less people would fail the class. His exams are hard but he allows notecards and holds review sessions, study and you'll be fine.

Dr. Wong's class isn't necessarily difficult but his exams are. The class does not prepare you for the exams at all. He says that if you study all of the homework, practice exams, reviews, lectures, and example problems you'll be fine. That would take hours upon hours. He is a strict grader and takes pride in the class average being a 60.

VERY difficult exams. He moves very fast, covering things other classes don't, such as R. He is a very good professor but the exams are insanely hard. The average on our midterm was 58 which he was "disappointed with," and the average on the final was 66, which he was pretty "happy with." From what I've seen, tests from other profs are much easier.
Dr.Wong is awesome!!! He makes the material interesting and is actually funny. The tests are very hard, so prepare. He is my favorite teacher at RIT!!

Very caring for students, takes feedback and criticism and alters class accordingly, and is quite hilarious to boot. The exams, homeworks, and quizzes were a little heavy and the concepts were hard, but he made them bearable, fun, and interesting. If you have the chance, take him. Don't say groundhogs are better than marmots to his face though. :)

Great professor. Very passionate about math, makes you want to learn. Puts memes in lectures. Quizzes and exams were take-home, but were pretty difficult as a result. Every assignment (minus exams) had a collaborative Slack channel where you could help and get help from the Professor and other students to get unstuck on problems.
Tony Wong is a great professor. He always brings great energy to the classroom, which makes borings subjects seem fun.

All assignments are straight forward and fair. Only assignments that are difficult are exams, but they are take home. Lectures are funny and you are able to work in groups for most assignments. Highly recommend, but be prepared to put in work.
Struggled to follow all semester long. Hard to contact and reach.

So yea yea he's a great guy. But his Prob and Stats class was HARD. Ive taken UP2 but this class was harder, idk if its bcuz tony or the subject itself, but its not all sunshine and rainbows. He does NOT make easy tests, quite the opposite. Class averages of like 50-60 on his exams occured. Yes hes the nicest + helpful af, but BE READY for math251.

Tony is a great professor who went above and beyond by adjusting his class to help ease the burden on students when the whole school was feeling overloaded and burned out due to no-break COVID semester. Very available for office hours and keeps lectures interesting with random jokes and/or tangents. You definitely wont want to skip them.

Tony is an amazing professor and is great at simplifying the difficult concepts of this class. He writes these goofy-ass questions on his homeworks that make them fun to do, and you can't find a powerpoint of his without a joke or a comic in there. His office hours are some of the best I've been to as well. 100% would recommend.

Professor Wong is an absolute godsend. His lectures are crystal clear, and he is extremely dedicated to being as fair and transparent to his students as human possible. He is extremely accommodating and extremely supportive of his students. Despite my difficulties with the subject matter, I couldn't have asked for a better professor.

Very hilarious and easygoing guy, his problems are definitely /r/fellowkids material. I used to have calculus-phobia, but his teaching definitely makes me love calculus again. Weekly homework is 10-15 problems long, so try not to wait until the last moment to do it. Probably the only complaint is his long midterm tests, 15 problems in 100 minutes.

Tony's dedication to math allows him to help his students through problems without flat-out giving them the answers. Witty, attentive, and always well dressed, Tony is the kind of guy to give you his jacket on a rainy day and at the same time calculate the amount of rain falling on the ground per second. Newton was a fraud!
Tony has passed the vibe check.
Very helpful, great energy, amazing jokes

Tony Wong is one of those rare teachers that not only loves what he is teaching, but also loves teaching in general. If you are ever confused with concepts, Tony teaches you in the clearest and easiest way possible. Tony teaches and speaks with passion, enthusiasm, and with a certain friendliness that is hard to find.
The best no cap.

Not a great class with Abby. Projects were vague, and you were expected to do things to her tastes. We spent ten weeks doing gesture drawings. Felt very much like a Drawing I course, not a senior level illustration course. Abby is very nice, but I didn't learn much.
Abby was a great teacher.  The class requirements were a little tedious but were relevant to the Illustration industry.  After the first project you can choose your medium.

Dr. Shipp REALLY loves physics. He teaches with enthusiasm, tries hard to make the subject palatable, and clearly works hard to make students understand the material. He doesn't just follow the activities manual or textbook, he clearly has thought about what makes sense to teach and how. Made good friends at tables. It's still physics, though.

I liked Dustin a lot more than my UP1 professor. He really knows his stuff, has a passion for it, and isn't afraid to be honest because he knows how to help students. It seems as though the ability to answer questions is hard-found in the RIT PHYS department, but Shipp goes out of the way to help, making videos and giving quizzes and etc. 910

Loved taking from him. The average for the quizzes were really low but he curves at the end and they really help you prepare for the final. We never use the textbook and mastering phys. is used only for the homeworks. Tests are department-wide so don't expect them to look like the quizzes. Incredibly fun guy, loves optics to death. Would take again

Well physics 2 is insanely difficult. However, Shipp knows his stuff better than anyone. He goes loves having tables work to get equations on their own, before giving them to you. If you don't come to class.. you'll fail.. end of story. Definitely one of the most fun professors I've ever had, even though I probably won't pass his class.

This was my first course in quantum computing. I really enjoyed listening to Dr. Vogt, as he puts it, "ramble about quantum". He is very knowledgeable and really easy to talk to. I was actually surprised how down to earth he was. If you are interested in photonic quantum computing he knows an extreme amount about linear and nonlinear quantumoptics.
Good class. Good professor. He is easy to talk to and knows his stuff. I'm taking quantum machine learning with him next semester.

I really enjoyed being introduced to quantum computing in this class. The class is homework and project-based, with no tests. It's pretty easy to get an A if you dedicate yourself to the homework. If I were to describe him, he is a combination of a frat guy vibe (in a good way - he uses their verbiage a lot) and Albert Einstein. Fun professor.

Very kind professor. If you paid attention to the lectures alone, you could do most of the homework with no problem. It is clear to me that he didn't go out of his way to make his class impossible; instead, he tried to make it as accessible as possible. He is really funny too.

Ryan was hands down the most hilarious professor I've had at RIT. It's clear that his goal was not to make the quantum computing class hard, but rather to create an opportunity for students to learn the subject and ask questions. He offered many extra credit quantum computing questions for the homework (I think this is a feature, not a bug).
clear stuff

Great lecturer, but the exams were difficult without reviews. Expects you to really understand everything for the exams without providing much information beforehand. Homeworks were not hard, the final practical was easy, just the exams should have had more prep. Take him.

Very lazy, doesn't provide practice problems and hw is just part of a 7 part project, so we don't have any clue what the exam looks like. Grades way harder than he has to, and very slowly. If you care about your grade, AVOID HIM AND TAKE PARK. Lectures are interesting but that's it. Slides are no good. You're on your own pretty much.

As amazing as his lecture is, his test is very difficult, not much review materials for test and the slide sometimes do not incorporate include materials for the test, very informational but the grade is not worth it

knows his stuff, can explain things very well, and is caring. however, there is no good way 2 study 4 exams (major part) other than office hours. completely blindsided by format of exam, the slides arent helpful bc tests are handwritten + application based (lots of stack diagrams) and they don't rlly take u thru the process. grades painfully slow.

I was COMPLETELY blindsided by the good reviews for this section. Don't listen to what reddit and RMP says if you care about your gpa, stress levels, and a proper structure TAKE PARK INSTEAD. Olson is a really great person; but the way he carried this class was overwhelming, unorganized, and extremely confusing.
