comment: Mr. Olson definitely understands and is passionate about information security, and it shows in this course. During my time in this class, he ran a flipped classroom type of format, which wasn't great but from what it sounds like, he won't be doing this same format again. If you care about the topic, he will teach it to you.

Professor Olson is the most underrated professor in the department. He grants extensions without needing to check in with him, he holds a zoom meeting that anybody in the class can attend instead of coming in, and he keeps his students updated on current cyber news. But, assignments are lengthy and they are often quite returned late.

I think Olson is the most underrated professor in the CSEC department. He is knowledgeable and actually does a lot of red team stuff on the side. He is genuinely caring and is willing to answer any question. Gives free extensions if needed. He provides the option to go to lecture online. Only weird thing is that he makes everything due at 8pm.

Olson is great, lectures were fine. The whole class is Zoom optional. Assignments were way harder than what we learned in class but AI is allowed so 2 week assignments were easy. Only about 5 assignments for the whole course. The Midterm was online with 3 tries, similar to final. Not a single lab. Late form automatic yes for a week extension.

Amazing professor, and is genuinely awesome in general. One of the best CSEC professors at RIT, and is totally awesome in class. The weekly quizzes were hard and a bit unfair sometimes, but the labs are awesome and really taught me a lot and that's where the class is the best. Made sure we were doing things right and would help if we ever got stuck

comment: Olson is overall great. Lectures were engaging. Attendance was not required, and lectures were always streamed on Zoom. Assignments were often confusing, but the next lecture would help. Extra credit is given for turning in assignments early. Our (online) final didn't open until very late in the final period, and assignments were due at 8pm.

Good professor cares and is smart. Only issue is his weird grading style where he makes things due at 8:00 and refused to move our final which he assigned to open on the second week of class, and was somewhat difficult to reach outside class/office hours.

Olson revamped the Web App course in a great way! He changed up the assignments and made the class very manageable for his students. The homework can be a bit vague with directions, but they are not too difficult to complete, and they now only make up 35% of the your grade. It's a significant improvement from the old course structure.

mid... literally like I don't think he actually grades his assignments. I submitted assignments half complete but because of "you get extra points for turning in early" I got over 100s. Is he scary bad? no. but if someone else is out there with a 4 or higher just take them.

Took this professor for CSEC 380 online asynchronous.  He is the single laziest professor I have ever been unfortunate enough to have.  Doesn't give live lectures, instead opts to use pre-recorded lectures from another prof.  Grades months late, doesn't respond over slack or email.  Sadly this course was mandatory.
He doesnt really do or teach anything. Idky attendance is mandatory. Also, he is not accessible outside of class, so if thats important to you, stay away from Olson

Professor Olson knows his stuff. However he is not the best at teaching the material. He is a bit relaxed when it comes to posting class content. The class itself is hard with a lot of material. You got one lab per week.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Professor Olson is a great professor and definitely knows what he's talking about. Yes he is a tough grader and he isn't one of those professor where you just go up to them and they give you the answer. He makes you work for your grade, but in the process you learn a ton! I learned a lot from his lectures and I would definitely take him again.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'Tough grader']

comment: Lectures aren't terrible and generally a good guy. Just very disorganized. Rambles on during the beginning of lecture about "The Security News" frequently causing us to lose lecture time or have incomplete lab code. All in all, if you're taking this class, go with this prof.
He doesn't know as much as he thinks he knows. He has poor lecturing skills. He's disorganized and lazy.

Professor Mohammed is a great guy. He is always cracking jokes and funny metaphors to help drive his point across. Unfortunately however, it seems that we miss a lot of key things because of it and tests become harder than they should be. Good professor though but just remember to actually study.
Great professor. Hard but, explains the concepts really well.

There's genuinely nothing negative I could say about Dave. He gave enough work to make you actually start to think about the material without being too heavy. He's super kind and helpful and gives great feedback without tanking your grade.

Dave is the BEST. The class is set up perfectly so you do not feel overwhelmed with work, while still learning a lot. What he teaches is really important in writing and will definitely help me in the future. You have two essays, one of which is a research paper that you do for the last 7 weeks of class. I'll say it again - DAVE IS THE BEST!

Professor Dave is one of the most down-to-earth professors you will come across! He says "as long as you show up to class and put some effort in, you'll happy with your grade." Only a few papers, each of which he guides you through writing, with lenient deadlines. I've never received such helpful feedback from a professor. Great class!

Dave is an amazing professor. He is an excellent teacher, but also makes each class enjoyable. It is obvious he cares about his students, and I would recommend him to anyone taking UWRT150. Nothing but my highest praise for Dave!

Loved having Dave's class! It was very straightforward, do the readings, participate in discussions, write a few papers, etc. The Big Research Project is great, you present on a topic that interests you and I enjoyed it overall. Take the class with Dave, he gives great feedback and shares cool info about his life. Not difficult, show up and enjoy.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback']

comment: He has been the best professor I've had thus far at RIT. Super caring, very clear on his grading requirements, not a lot of homework or big assignments, very very easy class if you just do what you have to do. Additionally, he was really accessible outside of class.

Super good guy. Cares for students and understands that other things happen outside the classroom but still wants you to learn. I took ENGL-210 with him (Engineering student) and despite hating writing/reading, he made this class not too bad

Yockel is such a great dude and professor, seriously. He's laid back and while there is a lot of reading, he doesn't limit how you write about it. You hated the stuff the text said? Alright, write about that. The final project's topic is entirely up to you and he just carries such a chill realistic energy. His writing feedback is really helpful too

Gotta love Yockel. He's a great, funny, guy and he keeps writing class as entertaining as it can be (even for students who don't like it). He's really awesome to talk to outside/inside of class for feedback and is ridiculously flexible with every due date he has. 10/10. if you need a writing class take him

You do have to do a lot of reading in this course, You will probably be reading more interesting and relevant readings in this class then in another professors. David is very flexible and he understands that writing is a flexible topic as well. His class was probably the most fun I've had in a college course and I enjoyed my time in his class.

Professor Yockel cares about what his students think about the material and understands that most people did not have the best experience with writing in high school. He takes this into consideration and aim the course at providing a better perspective on writing and what it could be for each student.
One of the best professors I've ever had. He keeps students engaged with his lectures and is very accessible for help is needed.

I took him my second semester here, Spring 2021, right in the midst of covid and his classes were a highlight to my semester. He genuinely cares that you succeed as long as you put in the effort to do the same. The assigned readings and writing assignments were straightforward and easy as long as you prepared, took time and didn't procrastinate.
He is the best!

Dave was probably the best prof. I've had for the entirety of my first year at RIT, and he made this class very enjoyable. That's saying a lot considering I usually despise writing classes. He makes the class fun by keeping the workload low, letting class end early often, and he's a really understanding guy who will take work late for full credit.

Dave is a great teacher and very fun guy. I really wasn't looking forward to taking first year writing, but have Dave made it so much better. Work was usually read this article and write a discussion post. Had one essay and one research project which he didn't make us do an essay for. Shows videos in class and let us leave early on nice days!
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Hilarious']

comment: Professor Dave is one of the best professors I've ever had. The course was mandatory and no one really wants to take first year writing seminar, but he makes the class so much better. He is super down to earth with his students, really easy to talk to, and is lenient when it comes to assignments. I can't praise this man enough!

He's the best! Very funny guy, there was not a lot of reading for the class, but some texts were long. He made me love writing as I hated it before. I took his class with Phil Shaw in the DDI summer program. You should DEFINITELY take both of their classes if you get the chance to. He made the class fun and cares a lot about his students.

It's very easy to become teachers pet in this class. He goes easy in general, but ask good questions, participate in conversation, and joke around a bit, and you'll have a good time. However there are many course texts that are provided, and some can be long. It's very easy to bs writing assignments in this class, but still put some thought into it

He's a super personable guy, and very down to earth. Definitely cares about his students, don't hesitate to talk to him about anything. If you put thought and effort into the class, it should be an easy pass. Also, Dave is super accessible and friendly so getting help outside of class isn't an issue.

Dave's a really great professor. He actually cares about helping you grow as a writer, and even if you are just taking this class as a prereq or whatever, it breezes by as long as you put effort into the class. Dave is funny and helpful, you don't need textbooks and most work is done online. The work is very easy you just have to read short essays.

I don't like writing or English classes at all but Dave was a great teacher. He is super chill and funny. The workload was very little and he was lenient with due dates. He gives good feedback on writings and wants to help you succeed and get a good grade. If you have the chance to take him then do it.

Favorite professor I've had so far. Very laid back. First day of class told us to just call him Dave. Very friendly, will make you laugh. If you put in decent effort it is very easy to get an A. He gives good feedback on papers, and I actually learned useful writing tips in this class.

Dave is literally the best professor ever. Because of him, I truly have started to like writing. He is so nice and makes lectures entertaining to the very end. Really chill guy and as long as you give him the respect he deserves, you're semester will be a breeze. He respects your opinions and helps you whenever you need. There's no better teacher.
Amazing.

It really couldn't be more cliche, it's the first college class I've ever taken, and I walk in and the professor says to call him "Dave". Seriously though, he's a nice and funny guy who just happens to teach a boring subject. An easy A if you can write decently, and might actually be a pretty good time if your class isn't at 9am like mine was.

Dave creates a really positive environment in the class, is very down to earth, and cares about students. His class was fun and easy to get a good grade if you complete the assignments. He doesn't make you buy the text book and there are three main assignments which are short papers. I would recommend him to anyone.
He's ultra-cool and grades real good. I'd like to give him a 10/5.
I love Dave. He made this otherwise boring class so much fun. I am so glad that he is now a full time professor, and I hope to stay in contact with him. If you can, DEFINITELY take him!

Really funny guy. Relaxed class. I hated the topic of writing, but he made the class possible to sit through. He wants you to do well and learn something and will meet you outside of class as much as possible. Not a lot of writing to do for a writing intensive course. 5 discussion posts, 3 papers, and a daily journal. Wanted to be called Dave too.

Really chill guy and connects with his students. He works with you one on one with your papers. There wasn't much homework except for the discussion posts once or twice a week, or all 15 at the end of the semester. There is a textbook but its online for free. Overall really nice guy. Would take again. (PS Mention you're a Mets fan bonus points 3)

Dave is a bro. He is hilarious, his classes are so open, anyone can talk and it's a really free environment. He really wants you to learn something from his class. He will do everything to support you if you ask for it. He's an amazing teacher and I would say he's the best writing teacher on campus. He also gives you a free pdf of the textbook.
Prefers to be called Dave. Great guy, really funny. Always enjoyed his class, never really a dull moment. Gives good feedback on your papers and responds to emails pretty quickly.

Prefers you call him Dave, had him at 8AM great way to start the day. Really funny guy and gives good feedback on his assignments. Very clear on what is expected on his assignments. Not a lot of papers, instead you write discussion posts two maybe three times a week. overall great class.
greatest science teacher ever.
Great Professor! enjoyed taking microeconomics with him. Explains the subject matter very clearly.

One of the best economics professors I've had. Very scholarly (and grandfatherly, lol). Class (benefit-cost analysis) was very interesting, and Dr. Hopkins presented the material in a very effective manner.

I had Professor Hopkins for Honors Economics this quarter. His class was challenging, but I enjoyed it. He's a great teacher and very concerned that his students understand the material. 3 papers, midterm, final, and online homeworks. Tests are hard, so study hard. Overall, a great teacher.

The best economics professor in my opinion. Took him for micro and benefit-cost analysis. Grades are usually a few large assignments and the two exams. He knows his stuff and if you follow along in the textbook you will do fine.

She was very helpful answering questions during and after class. She tried to engage all students, and used simulation websites and games to makes microeconomic theory more applied and appealing to us. Good professor overall.

not helpful at all, and gets offended sometimes when students ask questions during class(no idea why). huge textbook using, she expects you to do ALL the readings so that she doesn't have to go over everything during class. DISLIKE her class, worst class I've taken so far

Easy going and approachable professor. Heavy use of textbook and online program (MyEconLab) which helps reinforce skills. Most exams are open-note/book and some are done through the online program. Easy A or B depending if you put in the required effort. Gives lots of extra credit.
Very easy teacher. All her tests are open book / open notes. You don't have to study to get an A.

Very heavy use of book and online sites, basically an online class. Teacher knew the material she was lecturing about but didn't convey it an an understandable manner. Not always clear in assignments, and in answering questions. Not recommended
Heavy usage of MyEconLab, which basically means you should be getting 100s on any quiz / homework because you get multiple attempts.  Everything was open-notes too.

Insanely easy for a 500 lvl class. Two 1-page essays as well as a midterm + final. His lectures are long and rambly, but also really funny at points, and we had a lot of thoughtful discussions throughout. He's very passionate about art history and it shows. If you even gloss over the required readings then you'll be more than set.

comment: Not even a month and a half into the semester and I've done more work and reading for this 201 class than the other 4 classes I'm taking COMBINED with no exaggeration. Readings are long and tedious, lectures are rambling and pointless, tests and essays are huge sprung on you with little warning. Absolutely avoid if possible.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'So many papers']

comment: Chip is a really wonderful professor. He is insanely passionate about image and is very knowledgable about art history. The image class is somewhat difficult though. It is based mostly in long lectures with some critical response papers throughout the course. As long as you pay attention and take notes, then you should be set.
tags: ['So many papers', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: I have so much respect and admiration for Chip. I spent a whole academic year taking 2 classes from him. He's so rich, and he speaks very clearly. As long as you want to improve, he will help you as much as he can. He came to class even right after his surgery. No matter how bad the weather was, he always came on time.

Chip is really passionate about art which translates so well in how he delivers his lectures. I had very little interest in Contemporary Art, but after his class walked away with such an appreciation and new found respect for the subject. Highly, highly recommended!
Chip is AWESOME. What a boss. So passionate about what he teaches and really willing to help if you need it. Definitely my favorite prof so far at RIT!
Chip brought us donuts and made sure we understood everything. He never condescended, and was pleasant to be around.
Chip is enlightening, invigorating, and extraordinary! Highly recommended.

Took him for 20th Century Art 1900-1950. Chip is a great guy & definitely knows his stuff. He is passionate about what he teaches and loves to answer questions & help students. Two 1-page papers are the only assignments but the tests can are kind of hard if youre bad with dates and names. He has a slight but charming southern accent & loves Norway.
Hardworking passionate professor.  Makes sure to but detailed comments when returning all essays.  Friendly, kind, and understanding.
Extremely dedicated to his job and the information he teaches.  Plus, he buys the class coffee and doughnuts sometimes!

Sheffield really steps up his classes to a whole new level Ive never experienced.  He really gave me a drive to want to succeed in his class, even though it was really challenging and time consuming.  Thumbs up!
awesome. knows his stuff. wears a hilarious looking bowtie and calls everyone mr. or miss. has a iphone which is a little bizarre.

Definitely knows his stuff, but often can't convey the material in a clear and interesting way. Lectures are extremely dry and repetitive. Tests on material not covered in class. Approachable, though has a tendency to condescend and is somewhat pretentious. Yes, you will learn in his class, but it is often excruciatingly slow and painful

He really likes the sound of his own voice. He jumps all over the place and loves to repeat himself. Absent minded and doesn't seem very interested in the student, you can approach him and he will talk about himself, but will never ask or become interested in the student themself. He is a nice guy, but not my choice for a professor.
No Comments

I dreaded going to this class.I have never been so bored in a lecture class in my life.I found his accent hard to listen to, and I missed words b/c of it.If you enjoy slide after slide, this is the class for you. Papers were extremely easy, and the tests were mainly memorization with a few essays that he allowed you to prepare for ahead of time.
No Comments
best teacher i've ever had at RIT. take one of his classes, he has so much insight into art history and contemporary art.  he really makes you think and keeps you interested in the subject!

He's an adjunct and teaches CCNA classes at Monroe, so very qualified. Cuts out all the fluff from the curriculum and really gets the core points across. Friendly and hilarious, but lectures very quickly and with boring slides. Lots of labs, 2 practical and written exams, but he's very available and stays after class. Study and you'll do great!
An incredible professor who is caring for his students.

comment: easy B

He's an adjunct professor at the moment, but I hope he stays. The guy knows his stuff and it's rare to have a professor who knows what he is doing inside and out. I did poorly in the class and wish I invested more time in the class because he invested a lot in his students
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Prof. Ziarnowski is knowledgable and professional. He's quite detached from the students, however. I don't think I spoke a word to him all semester, and I got an A. Grades are based on a 20-question test every class about the previous lecture. Though there is a required textbook, only a few test questions refer to it, and I never once opened it.

The entire class was all lectures with 10 weekly chapter quizzes that made up your entire grade (no final). I never even got the textbook, the lectures contain everything you need to know for the quizzes as long as you pay attention and take notes. He seems like an interesting person, but his lectures can get pretty boring.

Alright professor, though decently old fashioned in lecture style. Every class, you're given a 20 question quiz on last week's topic, then a lecture, and then you're expected to read the textbook chapter. His teaching style might work better for some than others.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Test heavy']

comment: The class is only graded on 10 quizzes, which is mostly things you learn out of the textbook. It's best to pay attention during lectures, because there are little bits of info that might be on the quiz that aren't in the textbook. He's actually a pretty nice professor. The lectures can get a bit boring, but it is what it is as a pretty easy class.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Great class for anyone looking to get into Psychology. There are 10- 20 multiple choice question quizzes but no unit tests or final exam. He is very accessible outside of class and was a very fun teacher to learn from.

I like Professor Ziarnowski, but not his style of teaching. He's a very interesting guy with lots of real world experience, but gives long lectures and difficult quizzes. You won't fail any quizzes, but there are some questions that I swear I hadn't seen in the book or lecture, and they are 100% of the grade, leading to an undeserved B-.

The class is what you make of it. Its very self-taught, and the quizzes arent hard if you study. I dont think he is a bad guy, but it can be difficult to approach him outside of class and it can be hard to really express your perspective, especially if its different. I wish the class was more open to new ideas and discussion.

His lectures are taken directly from the textbook and it feels like a waste of time. He gives an easy quiz (if you read the book) on each chapter at the start of the class. It's the only grade. An easy class to pass, but not one where you can express your ideas - since he tries to shoot down anything that disagrees with what he thinks.

A very nice well-educated man who lectures well. There are 10 quizzes that you absolutely must read/study the textbook for to pass; this is very time consuming. One paper is optional to replace lowest quiz grade. If you don't read textbooks/study for quizzes you better avoid this class. Honestly, with time spent it's likely a B for me.
tags: ['Respected', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: Professor Ziarnowski gives good lectures using lots of examples. DO NOT take this class if you don't test well! The /entire/ grade is based on 10 quizzes which are based on the reading. I barely slid into an A. Be prepared to really study the assigned chapter in the textbook.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: He is a practicing clinical psychologist with a great memory. His lectures are like Morgan Freeman's through the wormhole--with many anecdotes that explain individual concepts well. He can be intimidating but if any information is missed, it can 100% be found in the chapter. He does not take attendance--going to class saves you from doing any RTNs.

The guy might be knowledgeable but the guy isn't much help outside of class. He doesn't have office hours, he is rude when talking to students and not what you exactly call "humble". Weekly quizzes are average and all multiple choice which were direct and not very hard. Quizzes were from book not the lecture but the lecture helps you understand it.

Took 6-10 PM class, never went past 8:30 except for the first class.  He make everything clear and follows the textbook more or less.  Easy class to pass, all you need to do is take notes in class and use the textbook to review before each quiz (20 questions taken directly from lecture & reading)

Extremely boring class, with long, confusing examples. Doesn't teach from the book, but material on weekly quizzes is often not covered in lectures so you have to read your notes AND the whole chapter (20-30 pages) each week. Prof is knowledgable but not very approachable. Grade is determined SOLELY on quiz scores so it is hard to get B or higher

A great professor, wish I'd taken more time to get to know him outside of class.  He's a clinical psychologist so he is very knowledgeable and has a lot of real-world examples.  Often lets class out early with the longer sections (mine was 4 hours, we rarely stayed all 4), and if you take good notes you'll do fine.

Dr. Ziarnowski is a clinical psychologist, so he knows the field very well and is able to give relevant examples in class. His quizzes were fair; if you took notes well and read the book, you could get at least a B. We frequently got out of class half an hour to an hour early because of his good lecturing ability. I highly recommend him.

I wish all liberal art classes were like his!  When explaining concepts, he would give really good examples that stuck with me.  Weekly quizzes were easy if you paid attention in class and read over the chapter.  No midterm or final.  I found it really easy to pay attention even though its was a long night class.

It's an interesting class, but it can get trying to pay attention for the full four hours. If you aren't a good test taker, avoid, as your entire grade is based on a weekly exam of moderate difficulty. If you don't put in the study time and PAY ATTENTION, you will not do well in this class.

By far my favorite class since coming to RIT! He makes all of the topics you learn relatable by telling you interesting stories and facts. 4 hour lecture flew by, often you get out early. 1 quiz per week and an easy paper. GREAT teacher, highly recommended. I wish he taught more courses than just Intro to Psych!

This guy is awesome. He makes class so interesting and connects what you learn in class to life. His four hour class went by faster than one of my one hour classes, and usually we got out early anyways. If you review beforehand, his weekly quizzes aren't bad. Take good notes. He bases them directly on what's said in class. I highly recommend him!

He is a nice guy and can be kind of funny but he only teaches 4 hour lectures and at night. so its kinda intense. tests are EXTREMLY HARD!! hes not helpful at all. i asked to do extra credit, review with him, email. he said keep doing what your doing basically and i was FAILING!

Incredible professor. I loved every minute of his classes. 4 hours means nothing, you can feel like 20 min have gone by til the end of his lecture. Incredibly interesting, great stories relevant to material. Quizes every class, but if you take notes then you'll ace them, all multiple choice. I highly recommend this prof!

There is a quiz every week covering the stuff he goe sover in class and the rest from the text; all worth 20 points that are just 20 minute multiple choices. He drops the worst quiz grade by asking you to write an essay at the end of the quarter. I would defenitely recommend his class!!

Dont let the four hour lecture period scare you, because he makes the class so interesting that it wont bore you.There is a quiz every week covering the stuff he goe sover in class and the rest from the text; all worth 20 points that are just 20 minute multiple choices. If you pay attention in class and take notes and yeah go through the text; the

Very interesting class. Don't let the 4 hour period scare you, there is a reason he only teaches one 4 hour block. Relates concepts to real life very well, and keeps you interested the whole time. Weekly quizzes can be tricky, be sure to review a few times before taking them. One grade is dropped and replaced with an essay. Definately take him.

Good teacher, great clarity, easy class (provided you study!). Weekly quiz, no comprehensive tests or finals. One  bad score can be made up via an easy essay near week 9. Keeps you the whole class, but makes it interesting. Do read the book as some questions come from the chapter. Would recommend for anyone to take for a GPA booster or for fun. :)
very clear, stays on course schedule.  gives a ton of helpful information that you need to pass the tests.  very knowledgable about the field, very good teacher.

Worse teacher ever. We had a quiz every week, no cheat sheets or study guides were allowed. NOT open book too. Quizes were material he barely went over in class. Boring four hours... you stay the whole time.
Awesome teacher! His examples are directly related and applicable! Learned so much!

excellent. no tests or midterm or final. just 20 point quizzes each week on the context of the week before. very good at making explanations and relating things to your own life so you can understand it better.
Amazing teacher, made a four hour class seem not that long, always held my attention, really easy to get an A in his class, too.
Good professor, material is covered well. It was easy to follow along and learn.
Good Professor

Wonderful Professor.  He is helpful during in-class exercises and office hours if you need help with projects and other exercises.  The exams should be easy.  Very fair graders on projects.  I recommend to take this professor!

Great professor. Teaches off the slides for the lectures, but is very helpful during in-class exercises. Good guy, interesting class. Always felt prepared for the exams. The exam practicals are easy, but you should study the slides for the multiple choice. Fair grader on tests and projects.
nice class
tags: ['BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'SO MANY PAPERS', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: One of the funniest and most laid-back, effective teachers and friends I've ever had. Sign up today for the Zachary Dietl experience! You won't regret it! Unless you're lazy and hate work. Cuz he does give work. That will make you amazing.

His tests weren't too hard by the standards of RIT; however, I gave him a lower rating because of his attitude. He seemed friendly at first, but there was a major error in one of the labs which he refused to fix for two months, despite my constant insistence. He finally fixed it, but was very defensive about it.

Relies and grades heavily on Calculus and tricky trig problems. Chip has very little or is unable to teach practical radiometry - take the Other professors, they are solid. This joker thinks that tricking you on test questions is a great way to test your knowledge rather than testing you on radiometry. Find someone else to take this with.

For a 200 level class, this is one of the worst lectures I've ever had, and I actively take 300+ level courses easier than this course. Work can never be late, his critique is unhelpful and sometimes sarcastic/condescending, and good luck with reaching him outside of class. He reads directly from a docx file and doesn't leave room for questions.
Did not provide useful feedback, and graded a 100's level course like a 500's level course. Only focused on western music for the majority of class which was incredibly boring.

The professor's lectures are devoid of student well-being. Gets side tracked often and doesn't repeat anything. His email responses are unhelpful, and he always replies with “it's in the syllabus.” His teaching methods are absolutely terrible. There are no slideshows; he just talks for an hour and fifteen minutes. I wouldn't recommend this class.

Dr. Ruhling completely changed my perspective on music. Not difficult at all. I don't understand what these ratings are about. Dr. Ruhling loves what he teaches and teaches it well. The man's teaching will make you love music. It will open your eyes to music in a way that doesn't leave you, even after you graduate.

Professor Ruhling was very nice and understanding, but he is definitely "by the book" about grading and the workload given to students. If you participate in class, you will pass very easily, but if not, then it will be very dependent on your homework, tests, and understanding of the material. It was a Zoom class, but it made him a bit lenient.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Professor is pretentious, using excessive technical vocabulary. Dismissive of valid questions, making students feel unwelcome. Teaching style lacks clarity and structure. Would not recommend for those seeking a supportive learning environment.

Ruhling is a decent person but an awful professor, solely because he teaches as if we're music students. I took Music History 1 with him, and my grade was determined by 2 assessments, and essay, and attendance. There is no room to improve in a class with so few assessments. He forgets that this isn't Eastman, this is an Institute of Technology.

I took two course with Dr. Ruhling. The second course was a Master's-level course I took for my B.A. degree simply because I WANTED to take another Ruhling class. He's tough, but he's also fair. I earned my A grades in his classes, but I was eager to learn and really apply myself. If you're don't want to work hard, then take a different class.

He is a really tough grader. Professor Ruhling doesn't let us use electronics to take notes during classes and the class is very lecture based. He talks a lot and then you take notes off what he says. Some of it is important and some of it is not really. Additionally, his grading criteria on essays are so harsh.
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']

comment: Ruhling will be a fine professor if you are a passionate student. I wouldn't recommend taking a class with him if you just want an easy A. Participation matters a lot grade-wise. He really is passionate and loves class discussions, but will not tolerate slackers. If you care about the topic and are willing to work, you and him should get along fine

I don't mind a tough professor but this man has such unrealistic expectations for his students it's ridiculous. The only reason I got by in this class was because of my background knowledge with music. If you don't have intermediate-advanced knowledge of music theory and histroy, his class is going to be your hardest class I promise.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Claimed that he saw me smile during his lecture, stopped the entire class to belittle me and accuse me of laughing at him. He made the rest of the term miserable for me. Never had any other issues like this during my time at RIT. My attempts to discuss the misunderstanding went ignored. #1 Worst professor after 6 years of higher ed.

Showed up to the first class and already got a bad vibe from him. He is extremely strict. No electronics to take notes even when you have a disability. He is very passionate about music and shows it. He's a one way street. If you know music you can do well but if you don't good luck.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: He is an awful person. I went to ask him if I could be late to a dress rehearsal one semester because I had a concert for band. He told me flat out he was disappointed in my lack of dedication and directly told me to drop, because someone did a poor job planning concerts.
Took him 590 class at Eastman Summer Courses.  Extremely knowledgeable and very helpful on the subject (Viennese Opera Buffa)

Hardest music class I've taken by far. Lots of work outside of class that you're expected to do beforehand so you can participate in discussions. 4 credit class so you're expected to put hours outside of class into the online listening and visual assignments. Tests were hard but if you basically copy your notes word for word, you'll probably be ok.

Had him orchestra. He really cares about music, he is a great conductor. But I don't like his attitude. I've had  tough conductors, and I'm ok with that. The problem was that he would claim to say some things when he really didn't. I've gotten yelled at multiple times for things he supposedly said. A great professor, just needs an attitude check.

Ruhling really is a great professor, but you have to understand going in that his courses aren't the GPA-padding liberal arts you may be used to - they're hard, and you have to put in real work. That said, if you put the work in, you should come out immensely knowledgeable about whatever subject you're taking.

I had Ruhling for orchestra and even though he may get angry easily, it just shows that he is really passionate about music and really cares about it. He just doesn't want people to slack off and not try at all, he can tell when someone is trying and just doesnt understand. He is an amazing teacher who cares a lot about what he does.
Good orchestra instructor. Expects a lot from students and gets stressed easily when things aren't right- but it's for the orchestra's own good. Kinda funny and a nice person.

Horrible horrible horrible........ bad teaching style, ridiculously hard tests for no particular reason.  Makes music history boring.... the only interesting part was towards the end when he talks about film music.

Absolutely the worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life -- not exaggerating in the least. He has a very poor teaching style, very rude, and makes tests unreasonably difficult. AVOID AT ALL COST!

I had many personal issues happening to me and she noticed that. She was very laid back with me and made sure I was doing well in class, despite what was going on. Her tests are well written and there is only one homework once a week. She is very outgoing and has a sense of humor. The whole class loves her. I would definitely take her again.

She doesn't know how to code or really anything related to it or even tech. If you ask her a question she will first run it through ChatGPT then ask the TA (don't be surprised if she gives word for word answers from it). Easy grade if you do the work, allows extensions if you ask. The whole class is a coding project but no coding on the. exams

It isn't Professor Delaus' fault as much as it is the fault of the SWEN-261 class in general. The class is incredibly unorganized, and both assignment information as well as due dates are not communicated clearly. This is not helped by Delaus' lack of knowledge in the subject, and you'll have to ask the TA's if you have questions about anything.

Caring for students and gives lots of wiggle room in an otherwise very strict class. She makes the project much less stressful than other teachers but is not very technically skilled. She just reads off the slides in class and doesn't provide much useful information. You will not learn much from her, but the term project will be less stressful.

Like what everyone else said, she has no clue how to code. She just reads off a slide, but it is an easy grade. All the programming assignments and phases of the project are graded by the TA. Find a good group for the project, and you should be fine. Take this if you need a GPA boost, and learn on your own.

While she is fairly clueless on actual coding for a SWEN professor, this does mean that she has the easiest midterm/most flexible deadlines/gives the most project time. The course itself is painful no matter who you take, but being in a good group/joining the class with friends does make it slightly better.

I'm not sure if she understands what she's teaching because she's mainly reading off of the slides all of the lecture. This course is just poorly managed and you basically have to learn everything on your own with your group members.

Sandra is a really nice person, but should not be teaching the class. She does not understand code and relies on the TA to help. The course itself is horribly constructed and is a living hell. I had it good because the group I got was good, but if you get a bad group its not good. There was actually a fight once because group members didn't agree.

Professor DeLaus's lecture consists of her very fastly going through material dense slides, vaugly explaining the material and assignments. The Quizzes felt rushed to do in class as well. And you have to dig into the slides to find the answer as she doesn't go through it. But a huge part of your grade is project, so having a good team helps a lot!

The most improtant part of this class is your group and not the professor but she makes the tests super easy. There is review with all the questions and answers before all the tests and you can bring a full sheet of notes for the tests with these written on it. This makes them so easy. If you get a good team and makes a notes sheet you'll get an A.
She has little to zero knowledge of software engineering but the class in general is very easy as long as you get a decent group. Ask TA if you have any questions.

The prerequisites to this class are CSCI 141 and CSCI 142. I genuinely from the bottom of my heart do not believe Sandra Cirel Delaus would not pass either of these classes with a C-. I have no clue how people like her  end up in teaching positions such as SWEN 261. In a class that is already structured poorly Sandra makes it worth.
Yeah this professor was terrible

Going to this class was an absolute drag, but what made my Tuesday's and Thursday's even worst was seeing Sandra Cirel Deleaus sit up there and pretend that she knows what she is doing. Imagine taking a SOFTWARE ENGINEERING class and your professor is genuinely a vegetable sitting up front. She has no knowledge of any programming and has to be ai.

SWEN261 is one of the worst CS classes at RIT but Sandra makes it bearable. Project requirements and deadlines are unclear but that is no fault of hers: just ask her about them and she's more than willing to clear things up. She was quick to grade and provide feedback. She was flexible and understanding for issues I faced especially with teammates.

The complaints about Sandra are mostly not her fault. This class is structured horribly, and it's completely out of her control. She is very nice, caring, and understanding, even though she doesn't know the most about the subject. If you have to take this class, I recommend taking it with Sandra.

When I emailed her asking for clarification on slides I didn't understand, she sent me a copy of the slides.  When one of my group members kept asking her for help, she kept saying "I'll get to it" and never did.  She even admitted she didn't know what an interface is in Java.  Even though the course was poorly structured, she made it much worse.

She can't help you with the group project as she reads off all the material given to her. Yet she grades you like she knows what she's doing. Very hard to get a hold of outside of class. Didn't have office hours for 3/4 of the semester, but claimed emails were harassment when asked for clarification about unclear feedback on assignments.

I think people get the wrong idea about this class. It's meant for you to learn groupwork and plan your projects in the real world. It's not just a programming course. It'd be easier if Sandra knew how to code, but that's what the TA is for.
One big group project is your entire grade for this class, you just have to hope you get a good group.

The class is structured horribly, but Sandra doesn't help that at all. She doesn't know anything about coding, deferring to the TA whenever a question comes up, and pretty much just grades on what the rubric says. She is at least kind about late work and mistakes, but don't expect to learn anything at all beyond how to write BS about SWEN terms.

She does not know what she's talking as she just reads over the slides almost verbatim. Whenever I had a clarifying question, she would either ask the TA or say to read the slides again. It takes forever for her to get back to emails in which she can be condescending/rude. The class is already disorganized, but having her definitely made it worse.

Lectures were really confusing she was just reading off slides that were given to her by the department.She often allows late submissions and would give you full credit. Really nice professor BUT if you need help just ask the TA, she doesn't know how to code. Stay on top of your work and you should be fine.
She is amazing! She is super kind and nice, especially if you participate a lot. As long as you get your work done, she will grade you well.

In my opinion, Sandra has been a good professor because she cares for her students but the class itself is the problem for all the pain. She is a very lenient grader as long as you show effort and communicate with her about assignments like if the submission is unclear. Participate in class ask questions to get on her good side. Class was rushed.

This class is bad, but Sandra does nothing to make it better. Many times asking her questions about the term project gets you nowhere, she doesn't know how to actually do the project. Sandra also has a habit of extending deadlines at the time of the deadline, meaning that if you're a good student and get it done, you feel bad for cramming to do it

Her lectures are pretty bad, she reads directly from the slides, pretty much skimming them, which are made for her, not by her. There's a lot of busy work outside of class, but that's not her fault, it's just the class. She is a very kind and understanding teacher. She often gave 100s for assignments we turned in late or didn't even complete.

comment: She's okay, sometimes I got the feeling that she didn't really know everything that we were talking about in class and was kind of winging it, especially with programming stuff.

all material given to her, she didnt look at it. the few times she opened a powerpoint, she scrolled to a picture and stopped. doesnt look at the quizzes until we complain something was wrong. didnt grade assignments until last 2 weeks of semester. if assignment isnt perfect or she doesnt understand it(happens a lot), she drops it a letter grade

Took her SWEN 261 class, which was based around a Web Checkers team project in Java. Not only did she not know Java, she couldn't explain how the starter code worked, and when asked questions would defer us to the TA 100% of the time. She doesn't know anything about code, which is saying a lot considering that a majority of the class is based on a coding project that we had no experience with beforehand. comment: Fun class, not too much work, but the professor was ready to help with anything you needed along the way. Highly recommend the class and professor.

comment: I think the other review is a little too critical given the context. I was able to meet with the professor regarding some concerns I had regarding my group members and class content and was met with empathy. She helped me develop a plan to save my grade. Would take this class again.

Takes points off if you don't code in the EXACT way she says. Tests are 30% concepts and the rest is making you fill out code snippets. A 700 level course that takes 20min to talk about "diversification" is ridiculous. She said "I will not be teaching you how to code in this class," then takes points off for not coding her way. 0/100.

I absolutely love Professor Ancilliotti. She made learning new concepts really easy, gave so much extra credit, and the class Discord made getting clarification on things so quick. She also graded and responded to emails with insane speed. Our final grades for this class were given back the day of the final.

Professor Ancillotti is literally the best. She gives you extra credit just for showing up and participating in the lectures, + extra credit on the tests. She also has class discords where she's super accessible and will answer all of your less specific questions there. Also, she gives out candy sometimes too! 10/10
Besides the slightly boring lectures, this was an amazing class. The labs were engaging, the environment was generally very fun, and there was even a class discord where wordle was played!

If you have years of programming experience going into intro cs like I did, and had to choose a professor to make an otherwise boring class feel worth it, I would 100% take prof Ancillotti. She has engaging lectures, very amiable, and has a class discord which makes the class feel way more alive. Hope she'll eventually teach higher level courses :3

Professor Ancilotti is super nice and you can tell she's very excited about CS. The labs and homework get pretty hard as the semester goes on but she has lots of office hours and is also available on discord ti help out. Lots of slides that get kinda boring but the code examples later are pretty fun.

She is easy to contact and responds pretty quickly, really liked the use of the discord to get help. Uses a lot of slides but as the semester went on there was more coding activities that helped a lot. There is a graded part every class but she did allow makeups for missed work.

Very accessible outside of class and wasn't judgmental when answering questions. Love how we did examples in class! Her handwriting wasn't great but she posted better copies of the work. Homework was hard but if you go to office hours she helps get you in the right direction.

Homework's were harder than the quizzes and exams but I liked that. Her office hours were super helpful and she really makes sure you understand before leaving. She made me actually enjoy learning theory!

If you enjoy reading words upon words of slides for concepts this is the teacher 100%. If you enjoy actual live coding sessions during full on lecture than reconsider. A lot of her material is in slide forms and continues into CS2 shes currently teaching. Its Boring. She's sweet and is a kind grader but needs a new form of teaching material.
Always had office hours to help explain the lectures, even if you don't have time for office hours, she is willing to do it another time.
Great professor has a great and inclusive teaching style. Almost always available and willing to help if there are questions about the material.

Ancillotti is an excellent professor! She is very helpful during her office hours. If you cannot reach her during office hours, she has a Discord where you can ask questions to her, other students, the TAs, or the SLIs. Her lectures are straightforward, she is fun, and she clearly wants to see her students succeed.

A really friendly professor who explains all concepts very clearly. She uses plenty of code examples to demonstrate each concept and often includes live coding sessions during lectures so students can see the implementation. She is also very helpful during lab hours and effectively clarifies doubts, whether related to labs or homework.
Great prof. with a good teaching style and projects that actually help you learn the material.

I had Foundations of Public Policy with Professor Keefe. He's a really kind hearted guy, but he is a terrible professor  of the class that I took. He did not know the right answ

Genuinely cares about his students and goes out of his way to make sure the course is well fitted to them.
Quizzes every week, very easy grader. Has a heart of gold and felt a sense of friendship with him and the classmates there. Very positive learning environment.

During my time in this course, my interest and understanding in the content of the course grew tenfold. He inhertied this course from a previous professor and has continuosly worked to improve upon it. He understands how difficult the content is, and prioritizes student understanding over anything else. Overall great professor and great guy.

Good instructor who genuinely tries to supports his students. Most of the lectures occur between weeks 2 and 6, rest includes a ton of in-class lab time and time for project work, the second half of the semester is more relaxed and easy going no heavy lectures. His exams are easy and straightforward, making the course manageable and enjoyable.

The professor talks too fast and does not check if students understand. He is very strict and gets angry quickly, especially about phones. The class feels stressful, and students are treated like high school kids. I think he should focus more on explaining clearly and showing more patience and respect.

A total of 5 missing homework or percentage three exams is below 75% is considered failing this course in Syllabus. The prof is strong with lectures, and homework assigned on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Very independent on activity homework individually.

Carlos is a great professor and is very knowledgeable about packaging. He does his best to make sure that every student understands the material. Also, he is quite lenient with grading. Glad that I was able to take metals with Carlos.
Very kind and fun. He's very compassionate and cooperative with students. Sometimes goes really quickly with material, but slows down if you let him know.

Professor Diaz seems very passionate about what he is teaching. He takes the time to better explain some of the more confusing packaging topics. As long as you pay attention and study the powerpoints, you should be fine.

This is my second semester taking a class with Carlos and he's a really great guy. The lectures are easy to follow and keep me focused. Very understanding and you know he cares, especially during COVID-19.
Want a passionate professor who cares about the subject, and your understanding of it?

Carlos is a really great guy and loves to chat in and outside of class. He is really knowledgeable about packaging, just not very good at lecturing. He sometimes confuses himself or gets lost in his own lecture. Metals & Plastics is easy if you study the ppts. He does take attendance for minor grade points.
Very nice professor. Although tough to understand at times, he is very eager to help you learn

Carlos knows his stuff but doesn't seem like it. Will constantly stop during lectures because of lost train of thought or simply doesn't know whats going on. Likes to asks questions, especially if you are not paying attention. Sometimes he doesn't even know the answer. Does attendance points. Reads off ppts. Hw is in textbook. Class isn't too hard.

Funny teacher but Carlos just sits there and reds what you need to do out of the book and demonstrates it on the computer. He sometimes doesn't know what he is doing and needs to sit there and think. Being that is a night class it feels long but it is easy. Final project is 50% of your grade so be on top of it!
Good teacher. Very nice and helpful. Tests covered material well. If you put the effort in he'll meet you halfway.

This teacher was honestly the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. He taught his lectures through skype from New Mexico, and the internet connection was awful. Most of the lecture was spent trying to get a connection with him. His online texbook (that he makes you buy) has many errors in it, and the online material does not help. AVOID HIM!!!!
Very nice guy. Class was boring, but he seems an ok teacher.

Great guy as long as if you put in the effort. His homework are difficult and assigned and due before he teaches it in the class so make sure to read the book otherwise you won't know how to do them. Quizzes and exams are very straightforward and much easier than the homework. Do the work then you will get what you want out of the class.
he is the most useless thing that i've seen in my entire life

He wrote his own textbook. Which he copy-pasted from to create the slides he teaches from. Lectures are a waste of time as he posts videos of how to do the lab each week. The textbook is frequently not clear on the expectations of the lab and often things that should be explained are not.
Simple course but his teaching style is a bit different, goes off on tangents and explains theory much more in depth than you need to know for the labs.

Professor Howland is a very engaging lecturer and presents complex topics in an easily understandable way. He is willing to field any question, even silly hypotheticals. His classroom environment is very positive and contributes to lots of cohesion among classmates. I would highly recommend Professor Howland.
Male Karen vibes and could be very uptight but was also chill like that at times. Midterm and final were online iykyk.
GET A GOOD GROUP. homeworks and quizzes are fairly easy but remember the brunt of your grade is the semester-long project. great lectures and he's a nice guy!

You absolutely do not need to read the textbook to do the homeworks. The TA's go over them before they're due. Most of your grade in this class comes from attendance and the large group project. Make sure to do your project well and come to class and you'll get a good grade.

a lot of your grade in this class comes from one paper and one group project. Make sure you get a good group or it will be difficult. Also, he has a dog that he brings to class if everyone wants him to. Overall, great professor and you'll learn a lot

I loved Professor Zoyhofski's class, he cared more about us learning and understanding the material than harshly grading us on it. Homework was gone over before handed in and tests were simple and happened every other week. Lectures were full of information and there were 3 pop quizzes, all of which were very easy, one question.

comment: He is the best professor I ever had. No question is stupid, everything you ask he will explain no questions asked. Goes through the PowerPoints and clearly explains everything. Uses real world examples, makes it better for you to understand. Very reasonable with tests, he has graders who grade them and if you like the grade you can talk to him.

He is not a bad professor; he teaches you the basics and let you try what you learned with the projects. The midterms are fine, just harder than the practice exams that he gives you. The final, he made it difficult for no reason, not only me that said that but his TA said that also. But it does not weight that much then the projects so that is fine

I went into this class with zero coding knowledge and feel like I learned a lot. I cannot say what your experience will be if you already know C or another language. Barrios was a great professor; lectures were interesting and went pretty in depth into how the C language works. Tests and projects make up most of the great. Good luck on the final.

Exams are a decent chunk of your grade and he tests you on super obscure c knowledge, oftentimes not covered in the lectures. As for the lectures, he is very monotone and you dont really learn much from them. Attendance is not mandatory per se but there are participation quizzes that you can get the questions from in the slides.

Carlos is a wonderful professor and person. His classes are always very casual and fun to be in. The labs can take a little bit of time to figure out sometimes, but are never unreasonably difficult. I loved being in this class and would take it again if I could.

Carlos is more interested in being liked than being an effective professor. He comes across as insecure, and his knowledge feels surface-level at best. If you're looking for genuine guidance or technical expertise, you won't find it here.

Carlos is an great professor and great person, always willing to help students at any time. The class is well set up for you to learn C coding to a fairly high level for 1 semester's worth of work. The final exam is dogshit, and tests you on super obscure C knowledge and error finding. Great lesson in accepting so-so results, but fix the final pls

He cares a lot about the course and student success. I feel that the lectures are hard to learn from though as it doesn't really make sense hearing about code more often than seeing it. Exams are very tedious and worth so much of your grade, so hard to pass them.

Respects his students and does a good job guiding them to completing their projects without straight up giving away the answer (i.e. teaching a man to fish). Classes are hands on and you will learn a lot from the projects.

Class is structured with 2 classes and 1 recitation a week. The lectures have a lot of content but start very simple as is explained well. He reads off slides but still adds more information to them. You do not need to pay too much attention if you are at all familiar with coding. Great guy, fun class which wasn't too hard.

Lectures are good and the lab reinforces what is learned in the lectures. The labs feel like digital systems 2 labs because they were written by Patru, they are a lot of work but its very satisfying to take all the labs and turn them into 1 final project. Go to lecture, do the homework to understand the lab. Keep up with the labs!

Carlos is a cool dude, he answers emails very quickly and will help you if you ask. His lectures are pretty good if not a little boring if you already have some coding experience. Carlos does a good job of introducing C programming in CMPR.
Good professor, but class had lots of work.

Professor Barrios is one of the best professors in the Electrical Engineering department. His lectures are easy to follow along with and engaging. What sets him apart from others is his availability and true desire for students to learn. If you put the effort forth in his class, you will succeed. It's not easy material, but it is very rewarding.

For CMPR you NEED to have previous experience in programming. Otherwise, make sure to study Java or C prior to taking the course, it will be overwhelming. Prof. Barrios is easily accessible outside of class and provides good feedback. The exams were fairly straightforward, but require a lot of review at home. He is solid with this material.

Carlos is one of the best and most caring professors at RIT. Yes his class can be hard, but Carlos is easily the easiest professor to get ahold of outside of class and will guide you through any questions until you understand. He understands that students are juggling 5+ classes and are just trying to do their best and tries his best to help you.
don't slack off on the labs. Do them well and on time and you'll be in a good place

Lectures contain lots of material, but are presented in a manner that is easy to understand. Many examples are used and make it far easier to follow. Homeworks and exams are reasonable and plenty of time is given for projects. Office hours are plentiful and extremely helpful.

He provides very dense lectures, but takes the time to explain tough concepts (through example) so you understand. Helpful outside class. Tough grader, though, and exams are quite tricky. If you study enough, you should do well. Practice exams are key. Much HW but they help reinforce topics. Overall, gives a good foundation of C language.

comment: He is a really good professor and very helpful outside the class. He prepares you well for the work field and he makes sure that you understand the theory behind it. Would love to take more courses with him.

Barrios is an abrasive guy. Makes brash judgments and gave a lot of attitude whenever asking for help. While he is not an alright teacher, his lack of patience holds him back from being a better professor.

comment: Barrios will take off points for things that are unspecified and don't matter. Getting the right answer doesn't mean you will get a good grade. Class is pointless and could be replaced by the handout

Extremely helpful professor. Goes rather fast so you may struggle to keep up. He seems super strict in class but outside, he's a pretty chill guy. comment: Hard class, but amazing professor. Very organized and in-depth lectures, a topic is introduced, and then example problems are walked through in class. Super helpful and kind, wonderful to talk to outside of class, and always willing to help. Plenty of office hours to help with the weekly homework and quizzes.

I took fluids and contemporary issues with Prof. Landschoot. The lectures were clear and very easy to follow along. I felt fully prepared for all exams and the review problems were well prepared to go over each topic through multi-step problems. Overall, a great person and professor.

He is a very nice guy and fairly good at explaining the material. However, compared to the other strengths professors, I found his explanations and pacing a little more rushed. He is more specialized in the thermo, fluids, and heat class sequence though. Still, overall, I would highly recommend him for most classes.

Professor Landschoot is easily my favorite professor. This class was a breeze, but he kept students engaged all semester. The criteria for assignments was clear, and he is very accessible by email or in-person if there is any confusion. 'Schoot really cares about his students, often asking them about co-ops, their other classes, or life in general.
Most wholesome professor in the department. Introduce yourself once and he will address you by your name for the rest of the year. Great professor, better human.

Landschoot's lectures are clear and easy to follow, which makes him the preferred choice over other professors no matter what he's teaching. However, he doesn't have the final say over exam material or homework which are determined by the department, so his classes can still be difficult with a heavy workload.
Best professor I have ever had. Very engaging and fun. Loves to teach and talk with students. Actually cares about his students. Truly amazing.

Like everyone else says, Prof Landschoot is one of the best in MECE. Lectures are clear and exactly what you need to learn. Always has interesting engineering news articles to share. Truly cares about each student, and wants to see you succeed. IMO, the definition of what an engineering professor should be. I wish more profs were like him.
Very nice, definitely worth trying to get into his section(s)

Professor Landschoot is just great.  I am overall not the biggest fan of fluids as a subject, but he made the class enjoyable to attend.  Also incredibly helpful during office hours, and cares about his students as individuals. I wish he still taught thermo; he would've made that class a lot more enjoyable. 10/10 professor, take him if you can.

Probably the best professor I've had at RIT. He makes a difficult subject so easy to learn. He is kind and outgoing, and class is very pleasant. Homework is straightforward and understandable, and the exams are similar to it so you are always well prepared. And, if you're fresh out of thermo, don't worry this class is WAY better!
One of the best lecturer in the entire MECE department. Makes difficult classes easy if you pay attention in class.

Landschoot is the best in the ME department. If you can take him for any class, you take him, simple as that. Fluids is a tough class, but he does a good job explaining things and wants his students to do well. Awesome guy!

Timothy Landschoot is by far the best professor I've had at RIT. Not only is he incredibly supportive and helpful, he turned a difficult class like Thermodynamics into something easily understandable. If you are struggling do not hesitate to visit him during his office hours.

comment: Professor Landschoot is a great professor. He's fun and engaging and he's always very helpful during his office hours. Landschoot makes difficult thermo concepts very clear and does a great job teaching.

I had Professor Landschoot for Thermodynamics and Fluid Mechanics, and he was excellent for both. He explains concepts very clearly and gives lots of in-class examples. Exams are not a breeze, but if you study his notes you'll be in good shape for them. He is really welcoming in office hours and will work through problems as much as you need.

I've had Landschoot twice now and he remains one of my favorite professors of all time! Hilarious yet informative lectures, helpful in-class examples, fair exams and an overall really nice guy. He brings in content from the news that relates to what is covered in class, and it manages to keep you engaged in the material. Can't recommend enough!!!!
Best professor in the mechanical engineering department. Clear lectures and helpful in office hours. Exams are challenging because class is not easy but he teaches the material perfectly.

One of my favorite professors in the MECE department! Lectures and interesting and informative, material is presented in a way that is clear, several examples are done in class and homework/quizzes are a good reinforcement of content and serve as preparation for the exams, which are quite fair. I'd take Landschoot again anytime, all day long!

He is the best teacher in the mechanical engineering department and should be awarded most reasonable teacher award. A reasonable and understanding professor that was great to have for a change. I often feel like a burden for a lot of teachers but I felt like he actually genuinely cares. RIT is lucky to have Landschoot as a professor.

Prof. Landschoot is great! Very clear lectures with many example problems. Also ties in topics from his other class, contemporary issues, into the beginnings of his thermo class, which is always interesting and fun. He is very accessible outside of class and is always willing to help and provide feedback
not so impressed, should have tried another section.
Tim is always a pleasure to have as a professor. Highly recommend taking his section of contemporary issues if you have the choice

Landschoot is a great guy! Fun and energetic professor who takes a boring class and does his best to make it interesting. This course does involve a lot of reading and writing so be prepared for some long assignments, regardless of the professor.

comment: Great professor; clear, concise, and very willing to help with HW or anything that you don't understand
Very clear and precise.

Thermo was fairly difficult for me but his lectures and style of teaching was very effective and clear. I would recommend taking him. Schertzer also seems like a great teacher

His lectures are super organized and easy to follow. He is incredibly helpful. He always has another way to explain things so that everyone gets what's going on.

102 was a pretty tough class. I had a lot of physics experience in high school so I was ok but with people who don't you will have to get help. Landschoot was pretty good. Fast passed lecture and he didn't show to many example problems. He was a nice guy though

Fantastic teacher. Always helpful.

Scooter is by far the best MECE teacher I've had at RIT. Best teacher ever!

This guy is not all he is trumped up to be.  Nice guy, but just an average teacher.
He IS the best MECE102 teacher  that a freshman could get!

By far the best professor I have ever had

Landschoot is one of the best teachers that I have ever had!  He is very clear in what he expects of you and is very open to questions.  He really cares about your understanding of the material and will do his best to make sure that you learn.

Best Prof EVAR

Landschoot is one of the best. He know his stuff, presents it very clear, and encourages questions. Definitely take a class from him if you get the chance!

Best professor in the thermo sequence, and arguably in the whole engineering science sequence.  Very clear, perfect balance of examples and theory, energetic, answered questions well, pointed out common mistakes to avoid when solving problems.

Great professor. Extremely helpful and explains everything clearly with examples sometimes. Not required to come to class. Hw comes straight from problems at the end of the chapters in the book. Quizzes are same as these hw problems.

The best thermo/fluids techer in the ME department. If you can get into his class before it fills up TAKE HIM! He explains the material really well, so not only will you be able to do the problems and do well on the common test, you will actually understand the material!
Amazing prof. Explains things really well. Homeworks are pretty easy. I would recommend him to anyone
Great professor, loves what he does and is willing to help you whenever you ask for it. Although he likes to talk about fuel injectors a lot

Excellent professor. He explains everything completely and thoroughly. He is a very fair grader. He also made class very interesting and I enjoyed it. If you have to take Materials Processing, take it with Landschoot!

Awesome teacher, very helpful and very clear. Tests and quizzes are graded fairly. He is young, and has experience in industry. Highly reccomended.
Easiest four credits in the world.
What a guy.

The course materials for this course cost near 200 dollars. The professor himself is fine but just be warned that you will spend a lot of money that he does not make clear and the fees hit you from left field

Not many professors are more passionate about their material and teaching than Professor Spadafora. Made a 3 hour class feel like 1. Very insightful, interesting class and always inspiring to see a prof that brings out enthusiasm in even the most jaded students.

Ettore is literally amazing. He is super easy to get along with and so passionate about what he teaches. He made our 3 hours class feel like an hour and gave multiple opportunities for extra credit. I would 100% take him again.

Amazing professor. Very enthusiast and cares about his students. Makes a 3-hour class as less boring as possible. Lots of work outside of class, but he is a fair grader. As long as you do the work, you will pass the class. Rare to find a professor like this at RIT.
Easy to follow, very enthusiastic, and somehow makes a 3 hour online course fun. Any other professor for a 3 hour class and I'd be sleeping, but this guy? Never even thought of it.

Awesome human being and professor. really enthusiastic about his subject and topics provides feedback and help student always both inside and outside the class. very nice if any taking INTB225 must take his class. just have to purchase some case studies for the class and home assignments, with 2 presentations and final exam cumulative but very easy

One of the best in this department!

It's not that difficult of a class, it's just time-consuming because that's how lab courses go. All things considered, McGowan is a great professor. In the first class, Dr.McGowan created a Discord and told us to communicate through that for any questions. Only good things to say about this guy. He was available at almost all times and extremely helpful, was always very clear with grading requirements, and is lenient when a student is struggling. Dr. McGowan raises the standard of a good professor.  Highly recommend taking his classes, it might be tough but he'll always be there to help you.
Had him for ad lab, McGowan is the absolute best, grades labs fairly and is super useful during class time! Answers Slack messages ungodly fast. Wish I had more classes left to take with him :(

McGowan is very good teacher. Physics is hard to make lively, and he does his best to keep the class awake. He has very clear expectations for the test and gives similar practice tests. I would recommend him as professor.

Dr. McGowan is a tough grader, but so is the entire physics department.  He's fair though.  He's very good at explaining things.  I enjoyed the nerdy references he makes a couple times each class. Even though the class was hard, Dr. McGowan made it more understandable.  The LA sessions are super helpful in my opinion. He is a guy who is willing to help you do good in his class if you put effort in it.

McGowan is easily one of the most underated physics 2 professors. For one, he's always available if you need help, and organizes several TA sessions a week. Lectures are dry but he is very good at teaching concepts and reinforcing them.  Is very nice and helpful if you have questions.  Tests were difficult and confusing.

Dr. McGowan is a bit of a nerd and will frequently reference sci-fi movies. As a teacher he's pretty good, but he's only been teaching for a few year and teaches a lot out of the activities manual. All in all, he wasn't a bad professor, better than many of the ones in the RIT physics department. I say he used a textbook because he teaches almost directly out of the activities manual (which is not necessarily a bad thing). Decent professor.

Lectures are clear. No quizzes. Homework weekly and it's a group thing. Very nice guy and helpful in class and office hour. Make sure to do the problems in the lab manual! TAKE HIM, the others are referring to aron Mcgowan (with one a)thats his cousin. This is the legit Mcgowan and he's amazing!

He is a nice professor and is extremely helpful in office hours. His lectures can be pretty monotonous, but he throws in some corny jokes once in a while. He has several conceptual iClicker questions every class that serve as attendance and participation. Good professor, but difficult class.

He is a very smart guy, a bit corny at times, and he does a fairly decent job of introducing new topics. sadly, he does boring and drawn out reinforcement of topic and he seems to have a minor understanding that his coursework isn't the only work students have to deal with. he give frequent and significant work, even if there is a test

He tends to get the material across in lecture but he has a very dull speaking voice and puts little to no emphasis in presentation. He is a new teacher but he is very helpful and the tests relates to what he teaches and assigns for mastering physics.  highly recommended
