Prof. Richmond is a saint. He is the nicest professor I have and he is hilarious. I don't know if all of his classes are like Special Relativity, but that class is very hard for some and not bad for others

Respects his students. ASK QUESTIONS! He's more than happy to explain concepts and why things are. Funny. Make sure you study ahead so that you don't have to jam last minute studying in. It much easier that way. Since there aren't many tests, is crucial that you score well on them.
His class is funny. You have to put effort in to understand it though.

nice Professor, very helpful, his class is not that easy but he let you learn a lot of stuff.

One of those professors you can establish a good rapport with. He's fairly laid back, although sometimes his teaching style can be confusing. As long as you ask questions when you're lost you'll be fine.

Homework is worth 20% of the grade and only assigns maybe one per week, eight questions long. Very easy to get an A if you come to class and do a little studying outside of class.
I don't see why people don't like him. He gives hw once a week for two weeks then a test. Tests have three questions and are not that hard. Overall, better than i expected

This is the worst teacher I have had since I've been in RIT. His tests have 3 questions, and he is very vague on what will be on them. STAY AWAY!!!!!
Had him for year one, great guy. Made the class actually very tolerable and sort of interesting. He promotes group discussions and tries to be as relatable as possible. I'd recommend him to anyone.

He is a chill, nice guy. Is not strict or unreasonable. Treats class as a constructive discussion.
He gave less homework than the other discovery teachers but attendence is manditory.
Good educator, but the mandatory nature of the coursework makes the class ultimately unsatisfying.

Took Electronic Devices Spring 2022. Good lectures but doesn't use slides and everything is written on the whiteboard. DO NOT SKIP CLASS OR YOU WILL MISS SOMETHING. Otherwise he's a great professor and is very thorough in explaining the concepts.

He is a great professor! He has many years of experience and knows what he is talking about! He has no slides so you will need to pay attention when he writes, but he explains concepts well and gives the solutions simply.

i strongly appreciated her teaching methodology and the layout of her course. the readings are dense but are genuinely very important concepts to learn imo. also just one of the most caring and considerate professors i've ever had, and provides immense amount of feedback/room for dialogue when working on projects.
Had her for an 8am. What a terrible way to start the day. This class was boring. I got bad grades on my papers after her giving me advice. Would not recommend even though the class is really easy.

comment: A great instructor who provides lectures that are understandable to students. Someday, she gives half of class time to students to break up in groups and discuss about the materials presented in class. The exams and quizzes consisting multiple choices can be tricky so make you read the questions carefully before deciding the correct answer.
great class
Provides class notes, teaches practical side of topic, hates the Yankees.  Don't fall asleep in class!!!
Easy professor. Teaches an upper level process engineering class. No math only concepts! Tests are short answer questions. Notes are online.
tough class if you are not good
Generally easy, remembers most students.  Ungraded homework, all test allowed 1/4 page of notes.  No final in the course.
Great teacher. Definitely recommend taking her if you don't mind actually doing work and learning.  One of few you want to take whenever you can.

I had her for solid modeling and DDT. She is probably the best professor in the MET department. She will take the time to guide you and assist you if you go to her office hours and ask for help. Really hot teacher also :) YOU MUST HAVE HER AS A PROFESSOR DO NOT GET MARIO CASTRO!!!
Good looking, well actually HOT! She seems to be very compassionate, considerate and above all helpful. I wish I met her in person to tell her all the above! Thank You Dianne!
This is a great professor and she is just a very helpful lady. Kind, generous and just down to earth. I recommend her for any classes because you will enjoy her company and value her information.

Great teacher and a sweet lady. she gives lots of second chances for homework and projects her grading is not tough so if you can draw it is okay. Alot of homework but she dropped two of them if you do the in class assignments she is very helpful when ask questions
Good looking and teaching professor. Her experience in industry is evident as she explains things. Very helpful in answering questions.

Felt real anger during lectures, which was basically every class. They were incredibly boring and I can still hear her voice. Sometimes did not fully open submitted work and incorrectly graded based on that. Gave empty or open-ended responses to emails concerning incorrect grades and questions.
great writing class
Amazing

Professor was really cool. No tests, quizzes or finals. Small homework assignments. 3 essays through out the quarter, and you could rewrite them to get a better grade. Writing class on animals...he took us to the zoo!

The class is very boring. Goodwin is long winded and generally drones on but he's not terrible. Tests were super easy but he grades labs poorly. He starts you out at 80 and then gives you an arbitrary # of pts back if he likes it.
Tough class, but Goodwin worked hard to help me
No UP2 professor is going to make sure you learn like this one. Put in the work, and he will make sure you come out the other end ok.

UP2 is hands down the hardest class I've ever taken (only non A or B grade I've received in my life), but Professor Lusignan does everything he can to help you. He is a thorough and funny lecturer, and very kind. He's extremely lenient with due dates, and gives a good amount of extra credit. This class is hard, but he wants you to succeed.

His lectures are incredible, but attendance is absolutely mandatory and there is a lot of homework. This class is extremely difficult but that is in no way professor Lusignan's fault. Be ready to study outside of class and keep up with a large worload.

Lusignan is one of the better physics professors and does his best to make the class interesting and fun. UP2 is incredibly difficult and tedious, however, and the flipped-classroom layout makes an already complicated subject even worse. Much of the class time feels wasted on super-specific examples which are far more complex than the exams.

The class is tough but Dr. L prepares you well. He assigns 2 homeworks weekly with one being for correctness and one for effort. He posts up an insane amount of practice and he uses iClicker with questions ripped straight from previous tests. He is a great guy and is very knowledgeable and quite entertaining.

He had us do the lectures and notes at home with videos, which actually was pretty cool because then it gave us time to work on the challenging stuff and ask questions in class. He REALLY knows what he's talking about. He also always starts class off with some quotes and small stories, which was always cool. Would take again

Lusignan's lectures are amazing, hilarious, and inspirational, and he is always actively engaging in conversations with students. Be prepared to do a LOT of homework, he's not an easy professor at all but you WILL come out of his class knowing physics. Exams are a cakewalk in comparison to his homeworks, so think about it as cramming ahead of time.

Dr. L is great for teaching physics. Definitely one of the best at RIT for the subject. Be warned, however, that this man gives a ton of homework. There are weekly online and written homeworks that sometimes take many hours each. Especially true in the week before an exam. You WILL know physics by the end of the semester. Best of luck out there!

Lusignan is the best professor I've had at RIT thus far. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He wants to support you in any way he can whether that be regarding physics or literally anything else. He has lots of stories to tell and will keep you entertained. If you need help he will ACTUALLY help you understand material

Lusignan does have lots of work, with clickers, spotchecks, and problem sets, but you will learn physics. It feels awful in the first week or two, but you get used to it, and if you pay attention in class and put some time in and do all of the assignments, the exams will be fairly easy and require minimal studying. Overall would recommend this prof
Pretty good all around.

Dr. L is one of the best UP2 teachers at RIT. You have to be willing to work hard, complete all prac problems, go to recitations, & office hours > pays off & well worth it, became my fav class of the sem. Lots of hw but if you take the time to learn it you will do better on the tests. Reversed learning approach >hard stuff in class, easier-ish hw

comment: UP2 is a very difficult class to teach and learn, but I would say Dr. Lusignan does a pretty good job of teaching the concepts. I'd say take him if you can.

Dr. L is fantastic. He made understanding UP2 a whole lot simpler, and was always excited to answer any questions I had. Seemed like a fairly generous grader. He was also great to just chat with before and after class about news, science, or personal stuff!

Dr. L is amazing and I would definitely recommend him to anyone taking university physics. UP is really tough in general, but Dr. L puts in so much effort and you can tell he wants his students to succeed. His class is very well organized and he is great at conveying the important material. He's very approachable and helpful.

Really cares about students and wants you to succeed. Did his best to accommodate for us having extra stress from the pandemic, and adapted to improve the course as went along. Great help in office hours.
Lusignan is a true gem. He really cares about the success of his students.

Dr. L has to be one of the most passionate professors I've ever had. comment: UP II is hard, regardless of who is teaching the class. Lusignan is probably the best professor you can have if you want a good grade. Lots of extra credit, he teaches well, and really wants to help, but exams are standardized by the department, so be prepared for that.

comment: The most passionate professor I've had at RIT. This dude sincerely cares about the students he teaches and how effectively he's teaching. I am astounded every class at how much he would like the students to be successful. Tons of work but it's manageable.

comment: I really liked the guy but he simply did not teach. He did not lecture at all. The material we learned from is usually considered supplemental material. I don't know if he can even write on a whiteboard.

I love Dr. Lusignan. It was not an easy-class but he is very encouraging and helpful. He gives a lot of advice and extra-credit assignments. He is funny and try to make us less stressed. The labs were great and he is a very good chatter. I loved it. Just study, ask a lot of question, do not be afraid to. And attend classes, it really helps!

A great professor who genuinely wants all his students to succeed. Physics is a lot of work, but he helps by not taking much off for late HW and giving lots of extra credit. Gives clicker quizzes during class so attendance is mandatory, but he gives you the about half the answers. I got an A- with a B test average curved. Makes lectures pretty fun.

He was available out of class all the time even though I never went to office hours. Great professor, really wants everyone to pass and gives a lot of extra credit. Had a horrible experience with Physics 1, he turned my perspective of physics around and actually enjoyed coming to class, even if it was 8am.

Charlie is an amazing professor, he communicates material extremely well. If you care enough about the class to listen to him, you'll understand the material. He gives out a lot of extra credit opportunities and wants to see everyone pass. He also curves tests which is nice to see.
He is very boring but also really easy. Labs were fun and he always tried helping out with whatever he could.

If you go to his office hours his explanation for concepts are way more straightforward than presented in his lectures. During his lectures he tends to over simplify simple concepts. I would not blame him, if I had a PHD in physics I would have trouble dumbing down from polymer physics  to alberga physics. Overall nice guy well respected.

Always available to help whenever you need, even late at night through email. If you go to office hours and put in genuine effort, you will get all the help you need. Trys to put humor into what many people find to be a dry, boring , difficult class and I would highly recommend him for Physics 111. There is a lot of HW but it is helpful .

Boring lectures, has a tendency to over explain simple concepts and make them seem more confusing than they actually are. Tough grader too; he doesn't mind taking off lots of points for trivial or careless mistakes on exams.

Lectures are very, very boring and he has a tendency to make simple concepts seem more complicated than they actually are by overexplaining them. Tough grader too;  he has no problem taking off lots of points for careless or trivial mistakes on tests.

I have taken him for several classes and he is amazing. I did some undergrad research with him a few summers ago and I didn't get much help from him when I encountered a problem but every class with him has been a treat, I try to take a class with him every quarter. Definitely take him if you can!
I don't know how anyone could not like him. Real good teacher, real cool guy. Definitely take his class if you can.
Best teacher ever, if you listen and do the work you'll get a good grade, not hard at all.

This man is not just smart but he understands more than just his field. He seems to enjoy teaching but likes to force students to come to realizations on there own. I think that makes a better teacher rather than having you regurgitate lectures. Funny accent but you can understand him. I would  recommend if you like to class topic.
Great guy in and out of the classroom. He is there for you when you need help. He tries to make learning as fun as possible and in college you can't ask for much more.
Jake was a difficult professor in that he wouldn't give me straight answers for things, but i learned a lot by working through problems by myself with his guidance.

I'd be willing to bet the negative comments were from the same person... probably a disgruntled arrogant physics type who got a C... he's a pretty good teacher and his classes are comparatively interesting. Maybe not my favorite ever, but one of the better professors I've had.
Jake is the best professor i have ever had.  He has an amazing set of values in edifying his students and making them more intellectual as a whole. Not one minute of is feckless.

Dr. Noel-Storr is a wonderful, insightful and challenging teacher for COLLEGE STUDENTS. His level of interaction is stimulating and thought provoking for those with a post- high school mindset. Jake is very helpful. He is passionate about what he does. He is fun and makes class fun. He is always available for help.  Pretty much... Jake is awesome.

I don't think he's cut out to be a teacher since he can't make up a decent lesson, not to mention he just copy-and-pastes the instructions/grading for each project he's assigned us. When I wake up in the morning, I DREAD going to this class. I stare at the clock, wondering when it will all end. OMG, he holds us late when we have other plans, really IMPORTANT plans. What a dork! This guy has the best British accent, but he's so boring it cancels himself out! He's also extremely biased on how you treat him. Which is funny.
One of the most useful and reliable guys to work with in senior design. Will go out of his way to help you.

This guy is the worst professor at RIT. He doesn't have a PHD yet he is teaching classes! He is useless both in and outside the classroom. He doesn't care whether you learn the material or not. Read the textbook that's the only way you are going to pass the class. I swear this guy should be straight up fired.
He's a good guy and the class didn't require much teaching, but he relied heavily on his teaching assistant and all we really did was come in, sit down, read the lab, do the lab, and leave.
He is bad

He a nice guy, but his analogies and teaching method leaves you confused a lot on what he is talking about. He he famous for the saying "It's really easy." When slack says this most of the time people in the class were lost on what was actually happening
No Comments

Quizzes, daily homework assignments, ear training, compositions, and musicianship final make up the grade so don't worry if you bomb one thing. In-class exams were too long so you have to rush to finish. Would recommend.

Ms. Toca is always clear about what she expects from her students and lets you know if you need to work on something outside of RIT Singers. Class was really easy, barely took any effort to get an A, but we learned just about nothing. She's a new professor but she basically just reads off her notes for an hour and plays some music. Really easy artistic perspective, but don't expect to get anything out of it.

Had him for 20th c. art since 1950. 66% of the grade: take-home essays for the midterm & final. The other 33% a museum paper and "discussion" index cards that we submit at the end of every class. At first he always spent the full 3 hours lecturing, which put me to sleep, but then he brought in films. Allows rewrites and is very understanding. :)
I think that Alan Singer is such a great man. He gives great feedback and is so inspiring. The assignments aren't that special but he gives you every chance to try new things and grow.

I am not sure why students don't like him. He is a very helpful professor, although his grasp of IT in an IT based course is beneath that of most of the students. Thanks to him I learned about a new subject and my work has improved. He tries to be supportive and i appreciate his effort.
He was not clear on some of the projects he had us complete

Disorganized curriculum  (unplanned). I majority of class stopped showing up within weeks of this class due to his teaching. Please do not take this class.

Gets a worse rep than he deserves. When not overloaded with a ridiculous amount of classes, he was way more organized and had time to dedicate to us. Gives great individual feedback & professional help. Will repeat things when asked. Still a little messy & hard to reach outside class. Understanding about absences as long as you do the work.
Completely disorganized and extremely vague in his instructions. Takes FOREVER to post grades. Do NOT recommend this professor at all.

Chris was one of the best professors I've had for a class. He'll grade his exams on a curve if too many people get questions wrong and is always open to feedback.

Does a phenomenal job of teaching and grades in a way that makes you feel like learning the material matters instead of just trying to get an A. One of my favorite classes this semester. Super receptive to feedback at all times and actually cares.

The only reason he taught here is because he took this class when he went here and he didn't like it, so he came back to make it better (and succeeded). Funny and practical career advice and he's clearly very knowledgeable in computing security. An adjunct who actually cares is hard to come by, but he's one of them.
Great prof. He was super transparent and was extremely accessible for students. Also really funny, and the lectures are not boring at all! By far my best prof experience at RIT!
He is very friendly and a good lecturer. The course itself has a good amount of homework, but he makes the course material easy to understand and he has a food sense of humor.
He is very resonable if you need help

Homeworks take an hour at most if you payed attention in lecture and can usually be finished in 2-3 short methods. There is also a test and final, but they review concepts learned for through the project.

Bruce Herring was a decent professor, although he could use some improvements. He could slow down the pace. Put Woolie lore on an exam for extra credit. Lectures were really engaging and aided by a clear interest in the subject. Awesome class for some random elective.
Great professor who has a deep interest in the content he teaches and is always happy to share that interest with you. Also, the first professor ever to put Woolie lore on an exam.
A lot better towards his students than the Woolies. Made some random elective I decided to take last minute a really enjoyable, engaging experience.

He has a bit of an ego, and he would look down on those who were struggling, especially at the beginning (telling them they will "find out how to fix it later" and/or telling them to "figure it out outside of class"). 
People quickly stopped asking for help and were hesitant to respond to in-class questions. 
I do not recommend professor Herring.

The teacher is fine. He is very informed on the stuff that he teaches and is pretty social. GCIS-124(JAVA) the teacher isn't super important because the lectures are the same for all of them. The class has 12 main units. Normally 2 homeworks per unit, one quiz at the end of a unit, and an exam every 3 or 4 units. Learn a lot in the class

Bruce is the best professor for 124 hands down. He is funny, actually answers questions, makes the lectures interesting. Use the tutoring center!!

Great guy, better teacher. 

Herring's lecture style may seem dry to some, but if you pay attention, his way of explaining subjects makes things very simple; instead of diving head-first into complex topics, he first describes how to approach them, and once you are familiar, you learn about the underlying concepts behind. 

Must take professor!

comment: Professor Herring speaks pretty quickly, which was really good for focusing with ADHD. Every section of GCIS-123 is taught using the same slides and same homework, so he is not the reason why this class is hard. Herring wants his students to succeed and is good at handling students with all levels of experience going into this class. Very approachable and worth taking.
Herring was a chill and good professor, definitely need to pay attention during class because all class work is a grade. Make sure to use the tutoring center to your advantage!

Great professor. I feel like he made himself more available than he should have. Students were reaching out online at 10pm and he would respond promptly even on weekends and holidays. Great guy, great at conveying information, and very tolerant of rude students.

He's a great professor when you ask lots of questions, but most of the material you are expected to basically learn on your own. Great professor, take him if you can. Tries to make lectures fun and engaging by telling some jokes. Makes it easy to ask questions without you feeling dumb. It is clear he wants you to succeed and is accessible outside of class.

Bruce is a kind, caring, and funny instructor. His lecture is not clear at all. He does not really know how to explain things. He also ignores me and my questions which is unacceptable. Cannot understand why people like him

Bruce is a great professor. People complain a lot about this course, as well as GCIS123, but the complaints are not his fault. Can't take it? Change majors.

Professor Herring was a very good teacher, but one of the flaws he had was "freestyling" his code at times, and taking a long amount of time to figure out what was wrong, since he was trying to make the code more efficient. While learning python, He explains the materials well. and is easy for you to stay on track. If I have to complain, I would say the SE department lecture slides are sometimes too long for the class.
This professor goes way too fast, classes are boring an monotonous. I won't recommend this professor at all

Bruce is a terrible teacher, his lessons are just as awful as his usage of parenthesis. comment: Super nice guy. Strongly recommend taking a course with him if you have the option. He goes out of his way to make sure everyone succeeds. He understands the material super well and uses his real world experience to enhance the lectures and keep them interesting. Great prof.
Gives great examples of when we would use certain topics in the real world. Love Professor Herring and how he presented the work that the SE department wanted us to learn.

Herring has very, very good lectures/slides and can explain things well. His exams aren't pushovers nor are they unfair. That being said, CS2 will make you cry. No professor can save you from that. If you want to do well and get your work turned days (not at the last hour) before its due, go to Prof. Herring's office and ask questions if there are any concepts you are confused about. comment: Bruce Herring is a great professor because he is fair and easy to talk to. Prof. Herring is a great resource for understanding concepts and he will work with you during office hours to ensure you have the right idea. Lecture attendance is basically mandatory as you will not understand the material without it. If you put in effort, he will notice.

Herring is a pretty decent teacher. Although his lectures could be boring he gets his point across.

comment: Herring was a great Computer Science I teacher, and I'm disappointed I won't have him for CS 2. His lectures were very helpful and clear. He's also very approachable and accessible. He didn't create the curriculum for the class, so I can't accurate judge his personal standards for how much homework he assigns.

This class is definitely challenging but prof. Herring's packets and lectures helped break the information down so that it was more manageable and easy to understand. He was always very helpful during lab sessions and office hours and I never felt like I got stuck on any one thing for too long.

I really enjoyed having Bruce Herring as a professor. He's very knowledgable, approachable and always willing to help both in and out of class. He's willing to meet outside of his office hours as long as you give him some prior notice. I'd be happy to have him as a professor again in the future.

Professor Herring was amazing. I had him for CS1 and immediately knew I wanted him for CSII as well and it worked out great. Awesome funny guy with clear and concise notes and a very experienced individual in his field. Highly recommend his class.

Absolutely loved his class. All lectures were based off of easy to follow handouts/packets. Exams were straight forward and he was willing to give partial credit everywhere. Watch out, his lectures were pretty dry and easy to fall asleep in.

Herring is a solid teacher that lays out his lectures clearly. Regardless of what professor you have you will get a homework and lab each week as well as a final project. comment: Bruce is amazing, if you have an option on getting him please do. Super nice person and genuinely cares about you if you put forth the effort to build a relationship. He also gives packets that are pretty much study guides for exams. I am taking him for CS142.

comment: His approach to teaching is a bit aloof. He won't go out of his way to help you; you have to come to him. When you do ask for help, he'll answer quickly and clearly. I do prefer this for a project-oriented class, though I'm not sure others would agree.

Lectures tend to be a bit boring but he gets key points across fairly well. Easy grader, accessible outside of class and willing to help whenever you're stuck on an assignment. Class is an easy A if you pay attention and do the homeworks.
Lectures can be a bit dry, but he is always available outside of class and willing to help.
Great professor that makes class and lab more enjoyable!

Bruce is a fun and great guy, but his lectures can be dull. I still took him because I had him for CS 1 and enjoyed his class. Missing lectures will leave you confused but he is always available for one-on-one. He is very helpful when you go to him outside of class time. Overall a good professor

Herring is actually fantastic. He is very good keeping the class on track and relaying the concepts in clear and understandable ways. Labs are especially good because Herring will take time out of his day to sit down and help you with any problem you're having. The class was reasonably challenging, but more because of the department, not Herring.
Herring is a good professor. He knew what he was talking about and could explain things clearly. The class was hard but nothing unreasonable.

Herring is awesome guy! He's willing to help if you need it and his lectures are very clear. He might not know everything about python but he is humble about what he doesn't know and will find an answer for you. I really enjoyed his class.

Herring is a great professor for anyone that has little to no experience with programming. He provides in-class examples using Python for each lecture, while posting the slides each week. Some of the assignments may be challenging, however you can always reach out to Herring outside of class during office hours or email for help.
Professor Herring is a great professor. He is able to teach effectively and tries to make the class as fun as possible. I had no prior coding experience, and I would still recommend him!

I came to RIT not knowing any programming whatsoever, and I feel like Prof Herring made it incredibly easy to understand the material. I was able to get the hang of Python through the lectures and homework, and when I didn't understand something, he was extremely accessible outside of class and during office hours. He's chill and easy to talk to.

Bruce is a great professor. Little jumbled on slides sometimes but he conveys the topics clear for student and is always willing to help when needed. Not only is he a good teacher but he is easy to talk with and if you get to know him class becomes very enjoyable with light jokes to break up the heavy work load that CS requires of students.

I can't blame Prof Herring for not knowing some unique RIT CS things since it was his first semester here. But I can blame him for not knowing how to teach Python to freshmen, since he did not know Python himself! He openly admitted to it in class! I would not choose Herring again, he was chill tho.

Out of all the professors in the building, Bruce Harris certainly isn't the best. I would definitely recommend against him as a teacher, as his lectures are awful!!!! You will struggle if you have no prior knowledge with him as a teacher, as his lectures have almost no content.

Spring 2017 was his second semester teaching ever, so if you've never done any programming you might want to pick someone else for CS 1- sometimes during lecture he'd say something backward and he's not always on the ball with Python. HOWEVER- he's really great one-on-one, and if you couldn't make his office hours he'd find another time that works.
Fantastic professor!
Bruce is the best, that's all anyone needs to know. Truly.

Although Professor Herring is a great person, having someone try to teach you intense programming while he's learning it himself at the same time is not a good combination. Although I'm sure he'll get better as time goes on, I would advise to either know a lot of coding beforehand or take another professor.

comment: Great professor. Was thrown into teaching straight from industry and he handled it well. He's the type of professor that is very practical and reasonable about the way he handles teaching.
He is a great professor. By making the class interesting, I was inspired to change my major to Computer Science.
He makes the course interesting and helps all of his students to the best of his ability.

Brucie is the man. Lectures can be boring but if you ask him for help outside of class he will take the time to help you. Show up to his review sessions because sometimes he gives extra credit for just showing up.

Honestly loved Bruce, he's a good character and even though he had some difficulty teaching python, he really did want to make sure everyone succeeded. I'm taking him for his CS 2 course next semester, and I honestly can't wait. He's always accessible and very responsive to emails, love this guys.
Very helpful outside of class. He is willing to meet with students outside of office hours.
One of the best CS professors out there. I would take this guy again in a heartbeat. He is very helpful during and outside of class.

comment: The structure of the class is forced by the department and should not be  factor while rating this professor. comment: sure, Almost impossible not to get an A
Almost impossible not to get an A. I did almost nothing and managed an A.
Great person. Just attend her sessions, do the work get an A at the end. Fun & enjoyable

Pathways Service: Easy in-class projects. No homework, quizzes, or exams.  Meet with her once to talk about life, and go to class = 100%.  She is very very kind and caring, and she tries to make class fun.  She is a very genuine person.  Best professor for the class.
Asbestos a professor as you could ask for.
Amazingly helpful and super nice.  Super nice with side of nice....oh...and google her...she's awesome.
Great Teacher. Always there to help out in any situation. Ran a really fun class. If you can get in her class take it.

What a great person! Her class was the highlight of my week--I wished it was more often than 1 hour/week. She really cares about making your time at RIT what you want it to be. She connected me to a community service group and sends out personal emails to check up on you if you seem to need it.  I'll be staying in contact with her for a long time!

she is amazing!!! Will help you out in any situation at any time.  Easy to talk to and relate to.  Her class was the highlight of my day!  She wrote an amazing book too and met the band kiss!! She is kick ass haha and she is a lot of fun.  She does really fun class activities.  Also, very understandable and it is an easy A.

She is such a nice and helpful person - I don't think I could have asked for a better FYE instructor. She just wants to help you with whatever you need and to make FYE as fun as possible. When you meet her, you immediately start to like her. If you have a choice for which FYE teacher you want, pick this one.
She is one of the greatest professors you can take at Rit! She is fun to work with, sweet, and she assigns hw to you that are easy to complete and also fun to do in the meanwhile!
She is extremely nice and helpful. Once you first meet her, you feel very comfortable around her. If you ever need to talk to someone, she's the one - she wants to help.
He's a new professor though I claimed to be a jedi master... He still has much to learn with the force
one of worst professor i ever experience

Aaron is an amazing professor. Aaron gives amazing critique, he's very fair and kind, his lectures and lab activities are very well thought up and planned. I can't speak enough praise of his class, DDDD 101 was an amazing introduction to the 3D major. Lots of work in this class, so do your best and put in as much effort as you can.

Aaron Powell is a great professor. He knows the material well, explains everything clearly, and is always willing to help. Labs are fun and engaging. He is not a tough grader, but if you do not put effort into your projects he will notice during critique.

comment: Aaron is an awesome, practical, and thoughtful professor! He helped me become a much better 3D artist by providing honest, and helpful critiques which ultimately has made my work quality better overall. The workload is not bad as long as you don't try to do it all last minute and communicate with him. Overall do your work, and you'll get an A.

I learned a lot in his class, but Powell creates a learning environment that is unnecessarily stressful. Is constantly yelling, cursing, and disrespecting people that aren't in the room. The final critique consisted of the entire class (professor and TA included) shouting out things they thought were bad. I always left class on edge.
Great professor. Always willing to help and solve any problems or questions you have. Great at critiquing works and helping you improve. Always enjoyed going to his class.
He is the best teach I've ever had, and one of the most kind and caring mathematics teacher! Love you professor kifle!!

I love math, but learning from him was difficult. We had an amazing substitute teacher one day that really put into perspective how bad he is.  He's a nice enough guy, but maybe not cut out for teaching. Is confusing and makes errors, only to correct them days later. Only passed because I had already taken AP Calc.

one of my favorite professors. his lectures are helpful when doing the homework and studying for exams. exam topics are clearly covered in class. his tests are hard, but always generously curved. he's also very helpful in office hours, and will spend as much time with you going over examples as it takes for you to understand the material.
One of the worst professors I have ever had. Coming from an engineering student

Professor Kifle is a good guy who knows his stuff,  but is not good at teaching. His accent makes it difficult to understand him in lecture. He gives almost no partial credit, and his quizzes and tests are short, meaning if you get one question wrong you are going to get a poor grade. Really have to work to get a good grade.

Mr. Kifle is a very nice guy once you get to know him, and he is very willing to help you as long as you ask him. Although sometimes it can be difficult to understand him because of his accent, but he is very patient and humorous. Tests are harder than average, but he will let you know what type of questions will be on the test in advance.

Does not really convey the material very clearly but will do his best to help you if you go and see him. Not an awful teacher but certainly not the best. Does curve the class at the end (very largely I might add). Light homework load, explains specifically what will be on tests, but you do have to put in work and effort or you will struggle.

Gives almost no partial credit, grades very hard, gives many examples but doesn't necessarily explain how to apply the concept to other types of problems.  Definitely would not take him again, although there was a curve of almost a full letter grade at the end of the course.

He very often tests you on topics you never covered in class or in the text book. Generally, he the problem is he treats you like you already know half the stuff you came to his class to learn. If you're really good at math, you'll be fine. If you're iffy (if you just stopped to think about it) I would encourage you to find a different professor.

Prof. Kifle is amazing! He is super clear about what he wants to convey and he knows his subject well. His lectures are always lively.  He always makes us think about things rather than accept them blindly. Great teacher :)

Spends a lot of time in class going through the proofs of certain theorems and goes over many examples. He's very enthusiastic about the subject and if you're ever stuck on something he's more than happy to help you out. Tells you what to expect on every test, and lets you use formula sheet.

He's such a nice guy and is really there for you if you need any help at all. You get a cheat sheet for your exams but most people still did really poorly for some reason. 4 tests and quizzes make up your entire grade. Really enthusiastic but teaches right out of the book. Curves the class and lets you know that. Definitely take him if you can!

Hagos is my boy! He's a jolly man with a fun accent and somehow inspires a positive environment in a calculus class. His tests can get difficult but he is willing to curve them to help his students out.    "Christmas starts with C, so does curved!" - Dr. Kifle

Prof. Hagos essentially writes on the white board what is written in the textbook. In class, there is very little interaction between student and professor. The tests are not difficult, however they are graded strictly and very little partial credit is given.

I had him for Diff Eq. I like math, but he made it miserable. He read from the book, copied it straight (even then would still mess up the equations). Zero partial credit on any problems, so drop one negative and you are done. Very disorganized and condescending. He messed up almost every example done in class. Average final exam grade was a 50.

He expects you to know the information as you go. However he is always in his office if you ever need help. If you struggle in math I highly recommend another teacher, well me and the 4 people who doped his class this semester. Lastly, he grades randomly, not even the TA knows how he grades.

Very unorganized and hard to follow. Tests and quizzes are only a few questions, ergo if make any simple mistake, poof! There goes half your grade. I'm a math major and had to withdraw from his class. Avoid at all costs.
Horrible Teacher, Very Inconsistent Grading, Messes up his own examples in class. Avoid

Professor Kifle is an extremely helpful teacher. He effectively communicates the course material to the students. He does give a lot of homework but it helps you understand the material and prepare for quizzes and the exams. A majority of the exams consist of homework, workshop, and quiz problems. If you do the homework you should have an A.

This guy gives absurd amounts of homework when each problem takes a page or more to complete.  He reads the textbook verbatim in class as a method of teaching which is supremely unhelpful.  Avoid at all costs.

Professor Kifle is very pleasant if you are willing to put in the effort to learn the material. He has a fairly heavy Caribbean accent but I don't find it too difficult to understand. You can tell that he likes to teach and is very intelligent, he will help you to help yourself. One of my favorites so far at RIT.

Not a good teacher. He tries to help, but just confuses everyone even more. He will refuse to help on certain problems as well. I got an A in the class, not sure how, because he never posts anything online and doesn't give back all of your work. I don't think I have learned any Calculus.

I had him for PB Calc 1.  He is a nice person and will go out of his way to help you if you ask.  He gives challenging problems for classwork, but tests and quizzes are easy -or- are the exact same problems (so you should know how to do them).  Very lenient in his grading.  South American accent, I like it. 1 Homework assignment a week. I got an A!

He's an absolutely useless teacher. He spends the majority of class just writing examples with no explanation, he's hard to understand, he has even been unable to solve some of the questions he assigns. His grading is inconsistent, sometimes he gives partial credit while other times he takes off lots of points for tiny mistakes. Avoid if possible.

Terrible Teacher. He is hard to understand, give little to no help with anything, assigns only the hardest projects and problems to do. Worst math teacher I have ever had. Only up side of this class is that if you get an A on the final he will give you an A for the class. If not he averages everything.

Spends the majority of the class writing equations on the board. When a question is asked he doesn't really get to the point. His accent is hard to understand. He only assigns the hardest problems for HW and labs. If you study his equations well, his tests and quizzes are easy.
tests are tough

I have had 3 classes with Royka now and during scheduling everybody tries to get into his classes. He is really one of the best teachers CIAS has! If you follow his advice to boost your portfolio and get an internship or job, you will have a lot of success. His projects are always current, clear, creative and make great portfolio pieces.

Awesome professor. He has been in the real design world so he knows what people want.  Lots of work, which is great and all of his projects are real projects that are going to boost your portfolio.  If you care about school and want to earn your grade, I HIGHLY recommend him for he is da bomb.

Royka is definitely the best professor at RIT in regards to his passion for design and love of teaching. I give him my highest recommendation- take every class he teaches! His courses are challenging, but the work pays off when your stellar portfolio lands you the job you have had your eyes on. He will truly help you succeed as a designer.

If you want to succeed as a designer take as many classes with Royka as possible.  He's one of the most respected professors in the graphic design department at RIT right now. He's extremely helpful, and will push you to reach your potential. His projects are thorough and concise & will overall benefit you as a student/professional.

Royka is one of the most amazing professors I have had. I have learned so much from him, and by the end of every class I know that it was worth my time. He isn't an easy grader, but he is fair, and will only give you the grade you deserve. He is the most helpful professor I've ever worked with, and really defines and refines students as designers.

Royka is an incredibly dedicated professor. He's genuine and is passionate about design, which is clear in the classroom. His teaching method is different in that he gives his students a real life perspective of design and how it will be applied. I will continue to take his courses and strongly recommend him.

Highly recommend to take all his classes!!!He is one of the best professors of Graphic Design program and always willing to help students with school projects and portfolio reviews. If you really care about your portfolio, his class will definitely help you to gain some great pieces.

Royka is by the far the best professor I've ever had! He is very understanding and truly cares for his students success. He has met with me outside of his office hours to help me when I really needed it. He will go out of his way for his students which you don't find in other professors. He even brings in candy and pop tarts! He's just wonderful :)

Royka is by far one of the best professors currently at RIT. He goes out of his way to help his students succeed. I have had 3 classes with him in the past, and he customizes each one to get the best out of the students. Every class was unique and challenging in its own way. He will push you to do your best. He genuinely cares about his students.

Royka sends clear emails informing students everything they need for each project. He is interested in your portfolio and happy to give advice. His projects are designed to make your book as complete as possible, ranging from print to web projects.

Graphic design students at RIT: I highly suggest taking at least one class with Royka. He was my instructor for Symbol & Icon. He's very clear about what was expected in his class. He goes above and beyond to make himself available to students. He lays the groundwork for anyone to design amazing logos & icons, which can be used in your portfolio.

Royka is a great professor and really knows what he is talking about. He is serious about attendance, if you miss one class you will get an early warning. He takes the time to meet with students outside of class, to make sure you're on track and providing help. He is willing to help any student prepare a portfolio and work on getting an internship.

Overall a Great professor! He legitimately cares about his students & wants everybody to succeed. He even goes out of his way to meet with students to make sure they are on track. If you have the chance to take him, I definitely would! :)  (He does expect you to go to EVERY class though, so if you like to skip a lot i'd go with another professor)

Entirely unqualified to teach the subject, frequently would use AI to supplement his own knowledge of the subject matter even if it directly contradicted the up to date documentation on the software we were using. Impossible to communicate with in a timely manner, failed to update my final grade in the course until 3 months after the expected date

Super reliant on AI. Every single assignment was generated by Claude. I saw him use Claude Code to generate the next semester's assignment one time.  Makes the class seem super difficult while also not caring about the subject. He barely knows what he talks about and can only recite what's on the slides.

The class is pretty fun if you are into a class with projects and no exams, but they are pretty big and time consuming. If you ask for extensions he was pretty lenient. He is new to the department so a little confused about the material at times but I honestly learned a ton about app development from him.

Horribly reliant on ai, to the point where I feel like I am collaterally being dumbed down by it. He was not knowledgeable enough to teach this course, so he used ai for making notes, feedback, and code, including 'vibe coding' some examples which didn't work. Said to ask ai questions if you didn't understand his notes or to fix your code.

Professor Takats was a great professor and someone I'm really glad I had. His class provided me a lot of  useful experience that I've actually used since (including a good project to put on my resume), and he was always easy to reach if I had questions or needed help outside of class.

Professor Takats would usually show up late to lecture, often frazzled and unprepared for teaching the material. The lectures were often boring and a little difficult to follow at times due to his frequent rabbit-holes. But overall, he was a kind person, fair grader, and very available and willing to help outside of class.

Good person, bad professor. Every lecture he forgets about something, and gets passive-aggressive when you ask questions despite the lectures being extremely bare-bones and giving a lot of assignments that require knowledge he barely provides.
Class is pretty good, do a group project for a non-profit. Sometimes a little unclear in expectations, but was a really good experience and learned lots.

pretty good professor! he sometimes seems to not know the details of what he's teaching, but regardless he gets the material across in an effective way. extensive office hours if you need help with anything. there is a group project in this class, which i don't love but i understand why he does it. homework is not often, and is very doable.

JP is a good dude, but man does he suck at teaching. He has no idea how to code and has to constantly google if he's doing things right (but doesn't allow students to look up anything). The rubrics are unclear, and you can get points off for random things that aren't on the rubric or even stated in class. Most boring lectures in the IST department

Takats is quite a funny guy and says a lot of very funny and random things during class, but his lectures can be a bit dull. Extremely easy class as long as you do the homework and put in some effort. He is hard to reach outside of class. No tests, just the midterm and final which were both practicals that if you follow along, are cake.

He was a great professor and throughout the course, he was pretty funny which lead to the classes being a lot easier to follow. The homework is not bad at all, Zybooks is what the textbook is on and there was a unit due at the end of each week, then the occasional quick lab, or towards the end we had a larger project. Overall very manageable.

Takats is seriously funny, but sometimes he's so quiet you can't hear the jokes. Struggles to gain respect from his class. It's okay to look at documentation, but he looks at it so often that it's hard to tell if he even knows what he's talking about. Very bad at communicating outside of class. Class is really easy, though.

John Paul's lectures and coursework are really helpful for learning HTML, JScript, and PHP. He is really flexible and understanding with deadlines if you are transparent and open with him. His lectures are really thorough and he makes sure that everyone is on the same page. I really enjoyed his classes and wish that he taught more courses!

He has been meeting with outside of class times to get caught up in the course and genuinely wants to help it seems. Although the class is pretty basic and topics can be boring I think he does a good job of explaining it and he got me interested in the web development field.

John manages to make this class a disorganized mess. The assignment instructions are never correct, and he constantly forgets to either assign them altogether, or throws things on at the last minute. His communication skills are virtually non-existent, and never responds to questions via email. Lectures are nap inducing.
Good and easy to learn under!

Takats can be a little dull sometimes, other times he has a pretty subtle sense of humor. Classes are mostly just lecture notes with some demonstrations, homework assignments are pretty easy with clear rubrics. He is very good on giving feedback if students have issues. Overall a nice but pretty average professor.

Gets easier as the semester goes on, because there's less homework. Otherwise, Takats is the pinnacle of default teacher. Boring and inflectionless. I'm learning, but only as much as I need to pass the tests and do the homework.

Although many might say that his lectures were boring, I found them to be quite amusing. Prof. Takats has a very low-key humor that you will be able to catch if you are paying close attention. Regarding his ISTE-140 course, although he gives quizes at the start of class, they really help in keeping your mind fresh on the content.

Lectures are usually dry since it's primarily him talking to the class with little interaction. Homework assignments are frequent but easy to complete. If you take him as a professor you will get feedback usually within a day or two of submitting an assignment and he will be very communicative on what can be improved. Overall a good professor.

comment: Takats is a very nice man and is understanding if you have to hand in an assignment late but man are his lectures boring. He reads the slides for the entire time. Once I realized this, I stopped paying attention. I would take the quiz at the start of every class, then play games for the rest. Very easy grader and the exams/practicals are easy.
Good class but lots of assignments so it is easy to fall behind. He is lenient with due dates most of the time.
He's spacy and rushes through the lectures. It takes him a while to turn back assignments. The class is easy.

This professor is new. However he practically rushes through the material and example codes basically making you rely on the TA for a reasonable explanation or help. He's an adjunct so don't expect much availability. The course is easy overall. If you want the better experience, Get Jim Lenone or someone else who can actually TEACH.

comment: Heavy Russian accent, difficult lectures. Feel free to take the class, but be prepared to go to office hours for either of the other (very god) thermo teachers. We were best bros though because I took Russian as a foreign language. Good Luck.

His accent is tough to understand, and his diagrams are awful, but Comrade is a great guy, I would take him again for other classes.  He is very helpful with in class quizzes and is great in office hours as well.

There were very few times when I walked out of class feeling like I knew more than when I walked in. I felt discouraged to go to class after both midterms after he essentially yelled at students for not performing well. My experience was one that was not particularly pleasant and when I went to sign up for my next classes, I made sure to avoid him.

He's a clear professor; has clear guidelines, expects you to ask questions if you don't understand something, and loves answering them. Very reasonable in grading-strict, but fair. He has industry experience and cares about his students. I would highly recommend taking his class. He also has a great sense of humor!

He has a thick accent, so sit near the front if you want a chance to hear him. He also writes small and badly. Taking notes is kind of hard, a TA suggested to close your eyes and write what he says, not what's on the board. He's a nice guy and quizzes are partner quizzes with help from him. Tests are brutal. Go to class! Trust me.
thick accent makes him impossible to understand. class wasn't too hard, though the final is worth 50% of the grade so its hard to know how you're doing in the class

He's very helpful and willing to help students.Class is fast paced and can become difficult if you miss a day of class. Do your homework and in class assignments and you will get a good grade. I would recommend him.
Political Science Professor Sarah Burns is the daughter of the CIA Director. You should bring her flowers and candy everyday and be very nice to her.

I found her class both interesting and easy. Idk what the person below was going on about. There's a weekly reading quiz consisting of 3 questions, a 3 page midterm essay and 2 essays written at finals week. Certainly not the "hardest level 100 class". Personally I was engrossed in the material, she kept lectures informative and interactive.

Ive never worked so hard before for a level 100 class. Participation is 30% of your grade so definitely dont miss a class. There are weekly reading quizzes that she grades like its a graduate level class and same goes for the midterm essay. The final is two essays written on the spot at finals week about the entire class material.

comment: The class is interesting, makes you think but other wise isn't hard, quizzes are weekly and easy if you do the reading.  There is a group presentation and a final essay to write, certainly not hard but the group work depending on your group can be challenging. Classroom participation is a must, again, easy if you do the readings.

She took what sounded like a fun class and killed it pointless lectures. She is constantly proved wrong by her students and either try to refute their argument with nonsense or just doesn't say anything and moves on to the next slide. But you better be there in class because attendance is a huge part of your grade.

For Science, Technology, and Values, this teacher makes you read for every class. Groups of students are expected to teach the class, and the professor only speaks for a few minutes at the end of class. What she talks about rarely connects to the reading we did, and she doesn't know much about what she talks about either.

Definitely not the best professor, but also not the worst. She is very boring and makes students pretty much teach each other the class, instead of teaching herself. She is a nice lady, but bad professor. The class overall was not extremely difficult as long as you followed directions. There was limited mandatory work outside of class.
She is the worst teacher ever!!!I failed this class because of the plagiarism,when I was just describing facts for the discussion leading. Argh

Don't ever take her class. She's incredibly egotistic and accepts no views other than her own. If you are not willing to agree with her on everything, you won't get an A. She also gave me an attitude when I came to class sick to hand in a paper, so she doesn't seem to understand that sometimes people can't be in class.

Course is very boring. First hour of every class is wasted with student presentations, followed by an hour of ranting against technology. Textbooks are hundreds of pages that say absolutely nothing of value. Unfair grading of papers. Attendance enforced by five pop quizzes. Course caused lots of stress and sleep loss. Verdict: Avoid at all costs!

I haven't been here for long but she is by far the worst teacher OR professor I've ever had. Boring, loves being right, unusual class structure, and not to mention the class kinda sucks.  Don't take, avoid, or drop.  It's worth it I wish I did.
terrible teacher, all of these comments are 100% true. I would never take one of her classes again. She grades very hard and expects students to do much of the teacher by presentations
