Very knowledgeable in what he talks about. Be prepared to know TCP alot, and all of it's functions.  Lots of written content by him that you can reference, so if you dont know something in the class, reference them.

Long, dense lectures. Full of important content though. Prof is an expert who is currently working in industry, he has a lot of knowledge you won't get elsewhere. Not the most outgoing, but is still friendly. Labs can be challenging, ask questions and don't attempt them solo. Expect to spend time outside of class working on them.

Professor Kuliner has the best explanations of low level networking, and guides you through what actually matters. There is a lot of notes (hundreds of pages total) across each section that you should read if you want to genuinely understand the content. The TA can sometimes be a miss because he does not put much effort into finding one.

Mitel is very caring and EXTREMELY knowledgeable. He really wants his students to learn and be prepared. Unlike some networking professors at RIT, he did an amazing job tailoring so security students could enjoy it. While he does have a tendency to go on tangents, all of the class material is laid out clearly in the lecture notes he provides.

His grading is awful and he'll just throw in rude comments in your homework. He was never helpful whenever you try to ask him about a concept you don't understand. A lot of homework and 10 labs minimum. His lab instructions and lab reports are not in sync because he does not do his lab instructions.

He does not teach very well, often rambling off about the glory days of his work experiences in the 80s or about the nitty-gritty details, while missing the overarching points. He also is not very nice, often making degrading jokes about students and misgendering them.

Lectures were consistently unhelpful and full of tangential wisdom that could be important at some point down the road, but definitely not for first-year students. Has plenty of experience in the industry, but teaching skills are seriously lacking. Also, quite rude to a few students. Deviates from the curriculum.

Mitel is very caring and EXTREMELY knowledgeable. He really wants his students to learn and be prepared. However, he is very bad at lecturing. He CONSTANTLY goes off on tangents. Even when on topic, he struggles to explain the information effectively and reads right off of the documents he makes. You can still get an A, but you'll hate his lectures

Quizzes are somewhat hard, horrible with instructions, writes everything himself and barely knows how to do the labs. Says slides say how to do everything... not true. Agree with Feb 3rd post. Funny guy so try to get on his good side and he may be more nice and lenient towards you. Wouldn't take him again, but don't stress if you have to take him

Not much good to say about him. Funny but doesn't answer questions, tells you to just look at the slides, and writes terrible instructions. You will be very confused no matter how hard you try. He also writes all his own stuff and does believe in the internet at all.

Don't take him for an 8AM, his lectures can be boring. However he is super knowledgeable and nice. Also no text book is a massive plus in my book. He also changed some of the course material to be a bit higher level, there were times when I was confused but mostly I think the changes were good.
Honestly, extremely knowledgeable in the field but lectures can be boring. I had him in the evening, so I was already tired as is. He kept the class very simple but could sometimes be disorganized.

I've had Kuliner for two semesters in a row now. I've given the benefit of the doubt. He is nice, and wants you to succeed, but by god he cannot write clear instructions to save his life. The entire semester he constantly needed to make clarifications for his own poor wording again and again. You're not screwed if you get him, but it's a pain.

I really like this guy, he is very kind, outgoing, and funny. Always said hi to me whenever he saw me even a full semester later. Tells stories during class, always tries his best to be helpful, very easy to talk to, hands down one of the nicest professors I had this whole year. Not the best lecturer, but will always be there to help you.

Mitel Kuliner is a great person. As a professor, he is not so great. Since he works in the security field, he teaches at a very high level. This was a 101 class and I felt like I was taking a third or fourth year class. I came into this class with no prior knowledge about the security field and I was not able to learn much in the class.

Mitel is a very caring man and he's very respectful of students' time. Labs are easier because he gets rid of parts that he feels are no longer relevant. However, it can be hard to understand the wording on his assignment sometimes, and his lectures are pretty boring.

Coming into this class, I knew absolutely nothing about CSEC, and after taking the class, I can't say I learned much more. Mitel Kuliner teaches at a very high level and his lectures are very difficult to decipher. For students who want to take CSEC-101 and are in the CSEC major, I highly recommend going with another professor.

My biggest issues are his lectures. They are very informative, but so, so boring. If you already know your stuff, you're golden, otherwise write as much as you can, at least to abate the boredom. Other than that, he's a great prof with tons of industry experience if you have any questions about what it's really like to work in csec. Labs are easy.

Adjunct professor with no set office hours so good luck catching up with him if you need extra help or have a question. Labs are time consuming and difficult. Lectures - boring. Sent an email the evening before the final, (20 minutes before to be exact), indicating he would be in the network lab if anyone had questions. His idea of test prep.

Really enjoyable professor. He has a lot of useful anecdotes due to industry experience, and keeps the class interesting-enough despite it being mostly just talking at you. Some of the written assignments felt like they could have been worded a little better, though. Sit up front and take good notes and you'll do just fine.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Hilarious', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: Overall, he is a very caring guy. The class itself was nothing special, a typical 101 class. He put a lot of effort into making sure we understood the labs and even tried his best to give us more than we needed in order to gain understanding. Tried to make a fairly boring class as interesting as possible. Overall, nothing amazing but nothing bad.
Love class! Networking great! Why he like red so much?
Mitel knows his networks!!!

Mitel is a caring guy and extremely knowledgeable. He is hilarious in class and tells it like it is from someone who is currently in the industry. He really really cares about the class and wants us to be excited. Does things for the class other professors won't.
Great professor, he knows that our other classes have a lot of workload so he would be fine extending deadlines and what not. Doesn't curve grades though.

Kuliner is a great professor, has an extreme amount of knowledge in his field and is currently associated in the field for security and networking. He is caring and knows that classes should be balanced and will work out extending deadlines or work and what not. Overall the subject for networking is hard but he does a great job of teaching it.

Mitel is an interesting guy and certainly has a ton of relevant experience from the industry. He can be pretty funny too. However, he usually isn't very helpful in labs (which can be brutal), doesn't seem to look at slides before he's teaching and sometimes just glazes over slides and tells us to read it on our own.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Hilarious']

comment: Demarco makes this course bearable. The original course is boring and dry but the professor knows that so he tries his best to get through everything and teach a bit of life lesson on the side. He is willing to sit outside of class time and talk to you about what ever. In conclusion, Awful course-Awesome Professor.

This class is extremely boring and the teacher knows it which makes it a little easier to deal with. The content of the class is useless which can be self taught on a coop. The midterm and final are simple and the group projects are a joke. Teacher doesnt mind laptops which makes the 4 hours pass by quicker. All notes are posted on mycourses.

Incredibly boring class, but he knows it and will tell you exactly that on the first day.  Seriously, prepare to be bored every class. Projects are straightforward and easy, midterm and final are short and simple. It's a very easy A. The class is horrible, but he's a real nice guy with plenty of stories and experience.

He tells you up front that the class is boring.  But if you come to class, kind of listen, and do the 4 very easy group projects, you will almost definitely get an A.  Bring a laptop to class to keep entertained, and pay minor attention to the lecture and you will be fine.

Get this guy for Needs Assessment if you can. He has a ton of experience in the field and will give you great advice on everything. He also acknowledges that the class is boring and will give you an A as long as your group finishes the (easy) projects. Midterm/Final are very easy too.

I've had him for 3 online classes. He's nice and easy to contact if you need help but you won't receive a single grade from him. His online lectures and exercise instructions are also very outdated (i.e. deprecated functions) as if he wrote them several years ago and recycles them each semester without checking to make sure they're still relevant.

Don't waste your time and money. The instructor is very poor, online lectures are 15-45 minutes per week (for a 3 credit hour semester) and lack adequate baby-steps for the target students, the whole course is presented via copy-paste code, many students couldn't even complete mid-semester projects due to all of these issues. It's bad.

This professor seemed like a helpful teacher at the beginning, but slowly became worse overtime. I wasn't able to fully undertand php and javascript like i was suppose to. And, his final group project was ridiculous. Really bad, please avoid.

Dr. Vullo is a great teacher, Web and Mobile I isn't exactly a hard class, so you might have trouble taking him in a different course. One of the problems I have with him is that he doesn't give enough detail in some of the projects and tests. For example on the final I completely misunderstood what he required for a certain part.

First half of the course had in class exercises which were just tutorials from the internet. Second half of the course was doing work that you didn't have to attend class for. Rarely explained anything. Easy grader, but terrible class.

Very disorganized. Didn't provide a syllabus or clear project guidelines. An easy grader though and extremely helpful if you ask. Just not your cup of tea if like to know what you're supposed to be doing.

I took the class having no experience whatsoever with HTML or CSS. That being said, I got an A just by showing up for class and trying. If you ever get stuck, you can always ask him for help during his office hours. There were no quizzes or tests, just projects. Just go to class and you will get an A and learn something too.

Nice guy and is sure to give you a good grade if you show up to class and try. He isn't always clear in his lectures, but if you ask him for help, he will help you. He doesn't use a textbook for this class either, which is nice.

Nice professor but never available when you need help.  Assumes everyone knows basic html so he moves really fast when showing how to do something.  His midterm and final exams are hard even if they are open notes.

Not a bad guy. Busy work every day, but nothing terrible. Teaches the basics pretty well and is very open to questions. Pretty relaxed and easy class if you have any past experience with HTML or Photoshop. Posts notes and presentations online, as well.

Nice guy. He made this freshman level class interesting, even though I was only re-taking it because prior credits did not transfer from my old school & I knew most of the material already. He is very clear about what you need to do for projects, & if you know the material & finish lab early, you can leave, which is nice when you have a night class

The subject matter was relatively easy but he was very approachable when you had a problem. He explains things rather clearly and makes sure to give you back your results on time. He gives you a list of exactly what he wants in the projects. If you follow the guidelines, you'll do really well. He also bought us breakfast for our last class.

Great professor. He is amazingly clear what he wants and he really teaches you what you need to know. The class actually is not boring and he mixes in a lot of visuals to make the class more at ease like watching videos and playing music during class.
Vullo is a nice and easy professor for anyone.  Classes aren't long and boring, teaches the material well. Good guy, good course
Very easy class and interesting too. He is more than willing to help you learn what you need to know. A fun professor to have.

Dr. Pough is a great professor! He posts all sorts of review material online and you can e-mail him responses to sample test questions, and the prepared question is posted online and is 1/2 of the testt grade. If you really love biology you can easily get an A. work in groups for the online quizzes and it's easy to get a 100 every time.

nice person and knows a lot but his tests are really confusing... you'll never know whats going to be on the test no matter how hard you study. I'll take him and just make sure you do all the HW and the Quizzes...you won't learn a lot but you'll pass the course with a decent grade

I do believe that the professor do try his best to explain, but Intro to Biology was just too hard for me and I didn't understand a single thing. Take the class only if you can truly understand the very very IN-depth information about biology.

i dont know where the material from the exams comes from, his lectures & the book don't really pertain to each other.  exams are impossible to score well on--but if you take the time to review every review asgn. he puts on mycourses, youll at least come across the vast majority of questions on the test.the correct answers will remain mystery though

This professor is very helpful, but the class is really hard. You better have a love for biology and reading because you'll have to stay in the book for this class, the lectures are boring and doesn't pertain to anything your supposed to be studying about. Just try and make sure your on top of the daily quizzes and the hw, because you'll need to!
Excellent teacher! Really smart
Great professor.  Very difficult class, but it's one of the few thats worth the amount of time put in.  If you go to him before assignments are due it will be a HUGE help.

Interesting teacher. Make sure to go to class as to not miss the activities that count as points toward your grade (they really boost it to counter the uh, 60% avg for the tests) Tests are really difficult. Memorize the material and try to guess what goofy questions he'll have on. The pre test sessions online REALLY help. WRITE YOUR ESSAYS BEFORE!!

Great professor...gently eases students into topics that are not very easy to grasp. Also gives great recommendation letters. If you have a problem he's always around to help out AND he's got a great tutoring program set up including tutoring at home from your computer and the tutors are really nice too =)

Wonderful professor, skilled teacher, smart man. His lectures are sometimes interesting, but you can get away with not going if you read the book. Heavily weighted in-class activities are not good to miss. Live by the book...test questions transcend simple fact retention. Lab component is 50% of lecture grade, usually taught by a different PhD.

I have seen people not touch the book, and score well on his exams. He takes his questions for tests primarily from his lecture materials, which are well-supplemented by the book. If you want to do well in this course, READ the book. He gives bonus points for Clicker responses. He takes plenty of grades, so midterm and fnl don't completely kill you

Excellent teacher.  Explains concepts very well and is a fair grader.  He trys very hard to make sure that we succeed and is very interesting.  Take his Intro Bio class!!  His tests are difficult for people because they are not used to thinking about stuff instead of memorizing.

Excellent teacher.  He is hard, and will make you work, but if you put the time in, you will get a lot out of the class.  His midterm and final exams are hard, but much of your grade is based on other things.  He is interesting and brilliant.  He's definitely one of my all time favorite teachers.

There are a million ways in Dr. Pough's class to ask a question and get it answered. If you come out of this class and still have questions, it's because you never asked them. His tests are tough because he's asking you to think more deeply than your used to, but it's a good thing! You can get a 60 on his exam and still get an A in the class.

Dr. Pough will probably be one of the most interesting people you will ever meet. Getting a B is easy, as long as you do the weekly readings and come to class. Getting an A can be tricky. Going to his study sessions before exams is key to getting good grades on the exams. His lectures are always entertaining, and he will keep you interested.
Clear, very helpful, but alot of reading required
What is he talking about????

His lectures is pretty clear but you have to live and breathe with your Bio textbook in order to understand everything he has to teach... His quizzes is pretty easy but Midterm is really challenging so you will have to commit a large amount of time to read through the assigned reading and flash cards is pretty helpful with the facts and etc.
Pough's lectures are completely supplementary, read the book, kick back in lecture and get an A. He is a very nice guy and wants to help you, just don't get freaked out in lecture.
Lectures are boring as hell.  If you want to get an A, you have to suck up and live by the book.
great class if your willing to get off your ass and read the book and pay attention during the lecture.
His lectures are damn blur~ confusing!!! but we r gonna stucked with him for one yesr! god help me!

Extremely confusing ppt presentations... test(open notebook) average is around 68% but only worth 30% of your grade. 15% of the class will get A's. Doesn't seem like you have a choice though - he's the only intro bio prof.

As the course progresses, the content may become a bit abstract (cs theory), but you can combine her quizzes and assignments to practice understanding what she is saying, connect it together as a whole, and explain office hours very patiently. She is a great teacher! I hope to be able to choose more of her courses in the future.

Ting is super nice and knowledgeable about the topic but does not respond to emails EVER and also takes forever to grade. The final is in a week and over half of the assignments aren't graded (day of final and the midterm is not graded). Overall, easy class with a nice professor but she's a terrible grader.
She does a good job of explaining things and she is a very nice lady. Sometimes the grades would come in quite late but I feel like that is a trend with any prof.

Ting was a fantastic professor, very engaging and extremely helpful. Class was hard, but she made it more manageable to understand. Her tests were brutal though. Stay on top of the homework as they are the majority of the grade, though whoever our TA was would not read our writeups (only grade on completion) so that made it better.

The class itself is incredibly difficult, all 261 courses are like that, but Ting makes it as easy as possible to do well. The homework grading was lenient, she answered all my questions really well, and flat out told us the layout to every exam(and the questions). Lecture notes are in person only, if you go to the lectures you will do well!

Great professor, very kind and knows what she's talking about. Assigns about 1 homework assignments every few weeks. In-person quizzes every few weeks as well, but she gives you a warning about when they will be. Tests were very difficult and aren't like the homework. There are online quizzes too but she doesn't remind you when they are due.

GO TO LECTURE. Pay attention & take notes. Had a morning class and many people stopped coming/clocked out when they came, then complained when it got hard. Homeworks are difficult, utilize your resources (make friends). She is helpful at office hours if you go with specific questions. Wont give you the answer but points you in the right direction.
Great professor however impossible to ever reach over email. Quite horrible in that regards, if you need something GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS.

Lovely professor with good lecture slides. Her lectures can get a bit boring at times, but it's easy to catch up if you miss a class or two. Homeworks can take A LOT of your time but are graded somewhat easy and really do help you learn the material. Go to her office hours, she doesn't respond to emails.

Clearly brilliant and very passionate. Great professor, but can sometimes talk a little fast. The homeworks are very challenging, but the exams are way easier. Algo is a notoriously difficult class, but if you actively attend lectures you will not have any problems.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Algo with Ting is not too hard, although the homeworks are really tough. They take the full 2 weeks to complete, if you procrastinate on them you will not do well in the class. If you're stuck, she's very helpful and communicative during her office hours. I find it hard personally to listen to her lectures, but her office hours help so much.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Ting is a great professor. I took her for CS Theory and am taking her for Algo now. For CS Theory, there wasn't much that we were graded on, just weekly homeworks, sometimes a weekly quiz, and the exams. The class isn't too hard if you pay attention to her lectures or use EasyTheory on youtube, and the homeworks aren't too hard.
Good lectures, although often slow and boring. Overall good professor.

Ting does a great job conveying information during her accessible office hours. She should be more abstract and talk about major concepts instead of specific code scenarios and edge cases. The tests are very silly, instead of "analyzing algorithms", the entire midterm and final are completely composed of handwritten leetcode questions.

Lectures can get boring, but she posts her slides and they are very detailed so it is easy to kinda catch up on your own. Tests and homework are more difficult than the work shown in class, but it is do-able. Definitely seems to care about what she is teaching so that's a plus.

She is very unresponsive to emails and does not post lectures online. If you miss class you'll fall behind and it's impossible to catch up as she moves at lightning speed. She doesn't give partial credit on homework or exams and doesn't post homework answers to study. Her feedback is minimal and does not work to help student improvement.

Very fast paced lectures and hard grader. Textbook was not required but definitely recommend it since it's hard to keep up in her lectures. Also a very hard homework grader and has office hours at the worst possible times when like every other class is taking place.

I thought this would be a difficult class given popular lore but she made some otherwise tough material interesting and easy to understand through extensive worked examples. That kind of rigor on her part really helped me understand the concepts clearly. She is also accessible outside class, very caring and considerate.

This class wasn't particularly hard or notable for anything. If you go to class, somewhat pay attention, and do the homework, you'll be fine. Cao is clear and concise about what you're learning, organized with her homework, and makes the class run smoothly. Tests are like the homework but easier, and homework is half the grade. Solid teacher.

Ting was a great professor to have, honestly one of my favorite lectures to go to every time. She has a slight accent but never struggled to understand her. For this class we had supplementary videos outside of the class which she edited down for the students so that they take up as little time of the day while also giving you all the material.

Explains topics well, even if they are at a fast pace. Did not record her lectures so if you miss class you are toast. Exams were the most difficult of all Algo professors. Homeworks took the entire 2 weeks they were allotted for. Would take if she's your only option but otherwise I'd look elsewhere.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Lectures at a fast pace, but at the same time speaking clearly and explaining things well. If you miss something, she will be happy to repeat it. I didn't find myself getting bored during her lectures because of this.

Not sure how she has over a 2 rating. Obviously she knows the material well, but she can't teach it. Lectures are recaps on what you learn yourself, which is pretty pointless because you need to take a hw assignment and quiz before the lecture about it. She talks faster than Sonic can run, miss one thing and you'll be lost the whole lecture.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Tough grader']

comment: Professor Cao speaks quite quickly, but sure won't mind repeating it if you did not understand. She taught at a pace faster than I could manage, but she teaches well. She knows the material well but does not explain it as best as she could. Not a bad choice, but would not enthusiastically recommend either.
She talks like she is on x1.75 speed which is nice if you like to blitz lectures. The material is interesting and having the book helps. (Can be found as a pdf online easily.) Definitely recommend.

Lectures at a great pace for me, fast enough that I don't get bored but not so fast I get lost. Homeworks are challenging, but they were the most fun assignments I've had at RIT since I enjoyed the types of problems. She cares about the students. She dropped the lowest homework and lowest question on each exam.

Ting has a very thick accent and speaks quickly, but really does understand the material and does a good job of conveying it. The homework is difficult but interesting. Her class is challenging, but not in any way that felt unfair.

It was her first semester when I had class with her, but it was clear she didn't have a good understanding of the material. If I asked questions in office hours she often didn't know the answer and I could figure it out much quicker than she could explain. But she's very kind and definitely wants to help; I'm sure she'll improve over time.

She is a pretty solid choice overall, as she explains the material pretty clearly and is willing to help if you need it. The tests and homework are a very reasonable level of difficulty, with the homework being challenging but doable and the tests being a bit easier. She does have an accent but it isn't too bad, you'll learn the content if you try.
Good professor. The material is difficult but she makes it easy. Fair grader. I would take again.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Very good professor. I like the examples. She take care of students.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Good professor. She explains everything very well. Extremely happy with the courses.
Excellent professor. Knows her stuff. Very approachable. Yes she speaks fast but people here over exaggerate. One of the better professors in cs department.

I've never felt so lost in a lecture. Her accent is not the problem; it's how fast she talks.. It's almost unintelligible. She does not pause between concepts, and there is no spacing. She scribbles annotations on the slides rapidly, without explaining or slowing anything down, or metering whether anyone in the class understands. Disgusting.

She has an extremely thick accent, so maybe not the best choice if you're hearing impaired. That being said, she knows what she's talking about and the subject material isn't super difficult. Homework is kinda easy, makes up a large portion of the grade, and you're allowed to work with other people on it, so you really have no reason to do badly.

Was a new professor when I had her. She definitely knew her stuff and could teach it well. I went to many office hours with her and it definitely paid off. Just do your homework and take advantage of her extra help.

Her homework assignments were very difficult, but tests were comparatively easy. She sometimes moved too quickly in lectures, but being a new teacher she may improve in the future. She's very receptive to student feedback. When the semester moved online, she posted lecture videos, and being able to rewind was helpful with comprehending material.

She's a new professor this year, so I guess it's expected that she's a bit awkward. She definitely knows her stuff and is able to teach it, albeit with very boring lectures. She wouldn't be my first choice for a future class, but I would take her again if I needed to. Hopefully she gets better with experience.

Asked way too much of his students for a L.A. class. Each missed class is 5% off your final grade. Each HW was to read 1-2 published journals and be prepared to talk about them. Not to mention the 8 page group paper, 4 page final paper, plus 2 other papers, AND midterm essay. He also has an accent, but it was generally understandable. BE CAUTIOUS!!

Professor Stackpole is a nice guy but a terrible professor, at least for this class. He gives detailed feedback mostly but takes forever to grade stuff and his assignments are all over the place. Nobody in the class even knew when the final was going to take place... for an online class... Overall a good guy but a terrible professor.

Prof. Stackpole is a super motivated and caring professor. He's constantly trying out new and novel ways of teaching his classes, which is admirable although I think it can be a bit overwhelming for students at times. Regardless, you learn a LOT from his classes if you do the work. He's always there to help if needed.

A lecture from Bill Stackpole isn't just a lecture, its a storybook of life lessons within the security field relating to whatever that weeks topic may be. Of course he explains all the technical aspects, but it is far more valuable to hear specific cases that show why each topic is important, and how it comes into play in industry.

he gives really good in class feedback on group presentations. however he does not puts a lot of effort into giving feedback on the assignments, and grades them very leniently. he also goes off tangents way too much in lectures.

I have now taken 3 classes with Professor Stackpole. He does a great job teaching the material when he does not go off on tangents. Granted some of his stories do have a good lesson to learn. He is not very organized and with a lot of assignments he leaves most of the class confused. All in all a decent Professor with normal assignments.

What can I say about Professor Stackpole? He is the one of most interesting and valuable Professors I have ever had. He loves what he teaches. He is not always the the most clear or organized and The Coke Head analogy is spot on for him. He goes off on a lot of tangents. But pay attention to him cause you will learn.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tests are tough', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: Fairly easy professor with easy assignments but isn't always the most clear or organized. Often all over the place and often provides no clear instructions leaving the entire class being confused.

The coke head analogy is on point for this guy in a great way.  One of, if not the best professor in the CSEC department.  He knows his stuff and will always do some outside research to provide you with the correct answer if he is stumped in class.

Having Stackpole is kind of like having a coke-head for a professor. He's super excited/bouncy and always fascinated about what he's teaching; He's interesting to hear lecture. Labs for the course are easy to follow/understand. If you have any problems, emailing him usually resolves questions and issues in < 2 hours. Great guy, and a great class.

Bill's one of my favorite professors to take classes from - he always has entertaining (and relevant) stories, gets excited by just about everything he teaches, and relays material in a clear, concise, and easy to understand manner. His labs and projects are usually a lot of fun, too! :)

Bill is the man! He makes classes very interesting and make sure you understand the subject. He explains things extremely clearly. Probably the best professor at RIT. Take any class you possibly can with him. Do your work, attend lecture, do good on labs, and take notes. You will get an A.

"that class" the one that most students fail out of the program on.  The one with 100+ page labs.  Doesn't sound like fun, especially winter quarter at 6pm.  Billie Stacks makes it not only fun, but a class that I desired to go to every time.  Don't get me wrong, it's a hard class, he just makes it.

Excellent lecturer. Easy to understand, covers the material well. He does post his lectures online but attendance is still recommended. Offers plenty of feedback and grades fairly. I would recommend taking him for any NSSA class, especially 516.
Always fun to have a Stackpole class. I loved lecture for Net Services with him. Lab is different; randomly walks out, is always late and theres no accountability with the TAs.

One of the best professors in the department. Kind of spacey on occasions, but he really does know his stuff and his excitement to teach the material is infectious- regardless of your feelings upon entry, you'll WANT to learn the material when he teaches it. A Stackpole class is an interesting, fun class. :)
He is def one of the best at RIT. I am pretty sure I would've hated the class if he didn't teach it. Highly recommended.

I've had many classes with Bill.  The content in his class is rough, but you would never learn more from another teacher in NSSA, making it well worth it to take a class with him.  He is extremely fair and can be flexible, his brain is also a never ending plethora of knowledge.  All of this said makes Bill Stackpole the "Chuck Norris of GCCIS".

Best/smartest professor in the NSSA department, having him as a professor is like having a stand up comic teach you.  Really knows his stuff.  Class work is hard but you will learn way more than any other teacher.  I have taken 3 classes with him so far, and am looking forward to taking another course or two with him next trimester. He is the man.

Great Professor had him for Network Fundamentals and he really knows his stuff. The amount of work he gives is a lot, but if you need help with something, he will take the time to explain it until you fully understand... he could make anyone able to understand networking

Bill will make you work for your grade. He is a very very smart individual. He takes slide shows to new height and will make boring items fun. He makes confusing material not so confusing. I would highly recommend Professor Stackpole to anyone.Don't expect A's unless you honestly earned it as he will not curve grades. Highly recommended.

Took crypto with him and it was great. It was a new class and we were allowed to take the class where we wanted to because the curriculum wasn't set in stone. Very fair and will always get back to you with an answer if he doesn't know. Knowledgeable in all areas. Lecture material can be boring but his personality makes up for it.

AMAZING professor. Do not underestimate the work he will have you do, but he is very fair, VERY knowlageable about the subject, and knows when he doesn't know something, and reseaches the answer for next class. Read the texts, pass in all assignments on time, and if you want some brownie points, buy some honey off of him!
Fun stories, interesting content, and a bit of a hottie (blush).

This teacher is probably the most enjoyable teacher to listen to at RIT. Can take boring and confusing material and make it fun and clear. Definitely will take him again next quarter. Be sure to do assignments on time and to do the readings.  All quizzes were straight from the textbook.

This teacher is probably the most enjoyable teacher to listen at RIT. Can take boring and confusing material and make it fun and clear. Definitely will take him again next quarter. Be sure to do assignments on time and to do the readings.  All quizzes were straight from the textbook.

Awesome teacher. He will go out of his way to help you out. He REALLY knows the material. Presentations can get a little slow, but he will start telling an interesting story, and it will become fun again. 516 takes  A LOT of work, but is worth it once you have finished the class. He is a great guy out of class as well.
Holds you to high standards but keeps your attention - One of the best and most interesting teachers I've EVER had. TAKE HIS CLASSES!
Probably one of the best teachers in all of building 70. Boom shacka lacka.
Lots of energy. Exciting classes that keep you interested in the content. You WON'T be sorry for taking his classes (but be SURE to submit assm'ts on time.)
Willing to help...if you can catch him. Makes something boring very entertaining.
Really know his stuff. Tough class and lab but he made it enjoyable.
Probably the best professor I've ever had a class with at RIT, bar-none. I never thought I'd be as attentive in an 8:30 class as I was in this.
Awesome.  Fun, interesting.
One of the few lecturers I didn't mind listening to.

LOTS of reading and long written reports required. GREAT professor - goes out of his way to help. Keeps class interesting and fun (even when topics are not so fun). Won't give you a **** answer - instead will research unanswered questions and address them next class. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
If he is a good teacher there would not be OVERT discontent among ALL students. Class expressions contort and turn to frowns when he enters the classroom.

He knows what he is talking about. He WILL MAKE YOU WORK. But if you can keep up with reading and pay attention in class then you are fine. He will help you outside of class too. Very friendly. You should take him.

Obviously the people above have never taken Prof. Stackpole.  He's easily the best teacher I've ever had and I'd take his classes again in a hearbeat.  All his classes will fill within a few hours of registration opens while others do not.  He makes you work, but makes it easy and interesting.
if you don't like real geeks, this guy will make you homicidal

He will be the biggest mistake of your college career. Unreasonable doesn't even begin to describe. Knowledge that belongs in a reference dictionary he will make you memorize. Doesn't know two bits what's important in the real world.

Knows his limitations , gives it his all
Intelligent, clear, very helpful. A bit too fast, but will wait if asked. GREAT!

Dr. Jayathilaka is one of the best professors I have had. He explains difficult physics concepts in a clear and simple way and makes sure everyone understands. Very helpful and always available outside class. He genuinely cares about students and wants everyone to succeed. His passion and effort set him apart. Highly recommend. Truly exceptional!

Professor P is clearly very passionate about what he teaches. He takes students feedback and experiences from previous years (via survey) and uses it to tailor the class to the best of his ability. Although he is great, beware of his slight accent as that could affect some students. Besides that, you can tell he wants all his students to excel.

The goat. Very accesible outside of class, If you ask him for office hours he will make time whenever in his day to accomidate you. Lectures are decently clear, but he provides more then enough resources to do well in UP1.

Dr. J uses a more standard classroom format of half the class being lecture and problem solving, half being mini labs and time to work on daily checks instead of the videos outside class time. He has regular office hours to help students, and is very available during the class time for questions about the problem sets or labs. Very friendly!

One of the best professors I have ever had! He really loves what he is doing and tries to explain all the hard topics in the easiest way possible. Always willing to help and has extra office hours if you have any questions. Wish there was more professors like him.

This professor is one of the best that I have had. He holds really good review sessions outside of class before tests and if you do not understand a concept, he will take the time to help you and answer all of your questions. He is super kind and very helpful. He is also super understanding for extraneous circumstances. Would take again.
Great professor, made it very easy to succeed with assignments and extra credit. Always available for extra help.

Dr. J explains concepts clearly and shows genuine care for student learning. Physics is a challenging subject, but he provides support through regular office hours and is approachable when students need help.

The assignments aren't too bad because most of the time you have a partner. There are no tests. However she's never on time to class, doesn't put any grades on mycourses so good luck on keeping track of your grade. You will rarely speak English in this class so be prepared

comment: Bad professor. Never showed up to class on time. Doesn't have an organized teaching method. Teaches straight from the textbook. Assigns massive amounts of homework due the next day, but doesn't put it online and tell you about it until after you go to bed. Nobody respects her, and class is never full. She also won't tell you what your grade is.
Great Professor!!! Took two courses. Would take another one
Great professor.  Very helpful.  Lots of online homework, but it's bearable.  Very generous grading.  Would definitely take her again.

A great language teacher! Cares and wants to make sure you get the material. Mixes french w/ english so you can grasp the content more. Also, she stresses the importance of studying the book by asking questions in class. Easy grade if your interested in the language, TAKE HER CLASS!

hilarious guy, very engaging and inspiring. lectures are pretty nice and he's pretty good at getting everyone (and i mean everyone) to participate. assignments were also very manageable and great resources for hands on learning.

The best professor I've had, HANDS DOWN. Not sure why Hartpence's rating isn't higher. He CARES about his students, and is accessible after class and through email. He is extremely knowledgeable for everything networks, and supplies you more than enough resources. His lectures are engaging and encompass everything you need to know on homeworks.
Dr. Hartpence has a lot of energy which he brings to lectures, very encouraging of class participation. I cannot say how he is in labs, but he is very knowledgeable with networks

Bruce is hands down one of my favorite professors at RIT.  He's relatable, easily approachable, and actually helps you learn with whatever questions you ask.  He responds to emails extremely fast and makes sure to update students on any assignment changes.  Overall, I highly recommend any student who can take a class with Bruce to take it.

This is for *CSCI 351*. I wouldn't say he's an outstanding teacher, but if you're just looking for someone to get the job done, this is your man. His lectures albeit boring at times are very informative, he gives an adequate amount of work, uses online materials to his advantage, and he grades fairly. Basically what you'd hope for in a professor.

Professor Hartpence may seem intimidating in his form of helping with labs, but he truly does care about his students and shows it. He assigns quizzes for each lab with content that is not really taught and can be difficult to find the answers. There are not written exams but he does add two extra labs and a practical at the end. A difficult prof.

Professor Hartpence is passionate and knowledgeable in this subject. He creates his own presentations for the lectures, but opts to not follow them. Hartpence falls short for me when it comes to his assignments. It is hard, without immense effort, to find out assignment details with his MyCourses setup. Good luck eye-balling your final grade.

If you want a professor with no respect for you, then Bruce is your guy. Whenever I asked a question in lab, his typical response was to belittle me, tell me to do something I had already done, and ultimately not answer my question. One of the least pleasant people I've encountered. Would not recommend.
Great professor and really knows his stuff, he's really fun, passionate, and willing to help you. Highly recommend you take this prof.

Prof Hartpence clearly knows his stuff. I wouldn't say to be scared of having him, but definitely find someone in the class and try to work together on assignments when you can. Lectures are fine not too boring and if you need help he tries to work with you to get the answer. Quizzes and Tests are the hardest part of his class and there are few
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Caring']

comment: Professor Hartpence is an amazing professor! His lectures are hardly ever boring and he has a whole lot of energy and that makes learning a lot easier. The only difficult thing about his class is his quizzes and test. They are very challenging and you have to study and know your stuff. But if you read his books they help tremendously.

Hartpence knows what he's doing, and his lectures benefit from it. Warning: He's very much a morning person; if you get him for an 8 am, be aware he will be WAY more chipper than the time of day merits. He CLEARLY loves both teaching and his subject, so his courses are of unparalleled quality, even if he expects a bit much at times.

Previously, I was a 4.0 student coming into this class. I had heard both posi/neg things about him but took the course anyway. First week in and none of us knew what was going on. It seemed as though he expected you had outside knowledge. 2 students dropped NSA as their minor and myself and 1 other are no longer 4.0 students post this class.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tests are tough']

comment: Prof. Hartpence definitely knows his networking stuff, he's a nice guy, and his lectures are rarely boring. But, his quizzes and labs are way too hard. When you take his quizzes, you get the sense you're going to get a 100%, but then you get  a 40.  His labs are not straight forward. It's almost impossible to do them outside of lab time in class.

Re-wrote advanced routing & switching for the class so he's pretty awesome. Can be tough sometimes, but it is often worth the knowledge you get out of it. Can be pretty funny & casual guy too. He is the god of networking and it's worth taking a class with him.

While he might not have the highest ratings from me or others in terms of easiness, he is by far one of the most knowledgeable professors RIT has. He knows what he's talking about and loves it. Can be a little difficult to get help out of him for labs, but you just have to push a little. Will be taking him again!

Hartpence is awesome. He is VoIP. Legend has it if you call his number from ANY VoIP phone the call will go through. In all seriousness, he's a great guy and a great professor. Take him for every class you can.
Excellent knowledge of subject. Although he is not structured but who needs spoon feeding at this level? Very flexible with deadlines and makes the course interesting. Really helpful too.

Telephony and networking are really his passion, and he has a ridiculous amount of knowledge that he wants to impart on his students.  Class is not incredibly challenging if you attend class and pay attention... TAKE NOTES, lots of important details. Workload is average for ANSA advanced courses - labs, online quizzes, and a project.

The man knows his stuff; his classes will make you work, but if you do the work, you'll do fine. Show up to class and take notes on what he says, not just what he writes. Quizzes are ridiculously tricky. He'll help you if you are struggling and ask. His classes are notorious for being a lot of work but he makes sure you learn.
Tough but fair. Makes you think but you learn a lot. Dude knows networking.
550 Tough but fair. Advanced class so we had to think a bit but we learned a lot.
The only professor I have ever met to take points off for citing sources in a formal paper.

Extremely unorganized and expects you to live of to standards he himself doesn't.  For our first project, which took half of the quarter, he didn't even give us the rubric until a week before the project was do.  He refused to write anything in stone about the project because he had no clue about it himself.  AVOID if at all possible!  Never again.
Bruce is an excellent professor.  He knows networks.  Telephony is one of his easier classes but you learn a lot in the labs.  I always enjoy a class with the colonel.
Bruce will make you work for your grade. Very knowledgeable of the material. He doesn't curve grades and will make you work for the answers. One of the best professors I had. pjb
Miserable professor - I wish I could sum him up without foul language. I would have been better off using the tuition money to heat my apartment last winter
Very smart professor, great teacher. Tough and expects a lot.  Highly recommended but be prepared to do the work - and have some fun!
Not easy but definately worth the work.
not so easy
No Comments

No Comments
Excellent teacher, cares about students, very informative

Dr. Asllani isn't the most traditional prof but I really enjoyed her class. She does a good job teaching basic content but her real strong suit is getting her students to interact with the class and learn without having boatloads of work. Go to office hours! One of the only profs I have had that taught me lessons and skills outside of just content

This class is graded primarily on the 3 exams and 2 pop quizzes. It is important to go in to office hours and get help. Showing that you understand what you did wrong and reviewed the material is really important and can earn you points back on your exams and quizzes. Dedication to fixing mistakes and get help when needed can get you an A.

comment: It's true, she preaches and is very much aware of it. She is not a conventional professor especially when it comes to her grading, but she does care about her students. She does pick her favorites but if you go to office hours and put in the effort, you will be fine. She also gives pop quizzes and takes examples from the textbook.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: The worst professor I have ever had in my life. She does not teach, she preaches. She never finishes problems and always goes off topic. She makes it clear that she is always right, and you will always be wrong. She belittles her students with harsh comments and tells students they are failures. I retook the class with another professor & got an A.

Iris is a fantastic person. Shes caring, funny, and an all around great person. Dont let that confuse you though. She is a terrible professor. Iris doesnt teach biomechanics. She preaches. You dont learn physics in her class, you learn how to play to what she wants and how to take her tests. No other teacher is as grossly finicky as she is.

Professor Asllani values learning above all. She really wants you to succeed and get something out of her class. Grading is very subjective, so make sure that she knows who you are and that you are trying to learn. Go to her office hours, she will help you with anything you need and she is fun to talk to. Lectures can be disorganized sometimes.

She cares more about the thought process than what your answer is, which can be a blessing and a curse.  Her exam are also a lot harder than what was gone over in class. But it is so evident that she cares about her students and is such a unique, kind person.
educator. I wish she taught more classes.  should get a chance to take a class
Great educator. I wish she taught more classes. Everyone should get a chance to take a class with Iris.

Professor Chavasse expected far too much from his students in this class. This is a 100-level elective course, and it seems unfair to me that it would take up more of my time than my major classes. Many of the videos we were required to watch were AI-generated. This class consisted purely of busy work that required tons of time and energy.

Chavasse is a very understanding and respectful teacher who will work with you along the way. There is a lot of HW, but it ties in to the learning well and makes sense for a language course. He is easily accessible, understanding, and can very clearly teach the content. Chavasse is also incredible at boosting confidence, especially in speaking.

M. Chavasse is amazing and very patient w/ those learning French and advocates for language at RIT. He is an easy grader but this class had lots of work. I took this class for my second major and while I can speak, read, and write French well enough, this class was just so. much. work. My reading/writing skills did greatly improve though.

comment: Such a sweet guy. He would usually lecture and then do mini assignments during class that we'd then go over, very productive way of teaching. If you show up and pay attention you'll do fine!
Great prof and class, no complaints!
Prof. Chavasse is an awesome, supportive professor and a great teacher! He puts in tremendous effort in his lessons. You will learn a lot if you take his class seriously.

As this was asynchronous, I didn't interact with Chavasse often. That being said, it was okay. There's SO much homework, and due dates were odd at times; and were put into the titles of the assignment and not the due date spot, which had me lose track and forget them often. Feedback was great and he seems passionate about French film and culture.

comment: Very knowledgable teacher, and you can tell that he cares about what he's teaching. However for an online asynchronous class there was a lot of work to do, and the discussion posts had specific days and times in which they were supposed to be done. Quizzes require a very good understanding. This class is hard to take if you have a busy schedule/job

comment: I took Intermediate French 1 with Chavasse and I really enjoyed it. He is a really nice professor and cares about his students. However, I would say that there is a lot of homework and outside work but if you do it you can get a pretty good grade on it. The tests were online and open notes and the final exam was cumulative of everything.

Very interesting class if you love film and/or French culture. Grading criteria is very clear with every assignment and due date outlined before the class begins. A fair amount of lecture and reading assignments but no more than a standard in-person class would have. Highly recommend!
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Would take again']

comment: He's not easy, but he's reasonable and helpful.

He is a great teacher. His accent is not hard to understand and most of the time he will just speak french to you which is great for practice. Take this class only if you care about seriously learning the french language and about french culture.  He will help you out if you try! Also a very funny man!

Amazing teacher. Lots of work but in order to learn a language you must practice it regardless. He cares about his students and if you show interest and try in his class, he recognizes that and will do the same for you. You won't regret taking him.

Great great teacher! So knowledgeable. If you're interested in french culture or cinema he is the go-to guy. Very knowledgeable and engaging in lectures. Great sense of humor. Very understanding and flexible with grades and tests. Requires some work but only enough to keep you involved and participating. Must have!

Soooo, the class wasn't awful, but don't go if you're sleepy... he talks for huge blocks and it can be very difficult to understand what he's saying because his accent is so thick.  We watched really terrible movies and for the final project we had to make our own movies... way too much expected for a liberal arts class.

I've taken Advanced French III and French Cinemas with Chavasse. Be prepared for a ton of work. If you stay on top of the work load and get everything in on time, he's a great professor. He tries to keep things interesting, and he knows what he's talking about.

Greatest French teacher I have ever had. Extremely helpful, nice, clear, and concise. I took both French Film and Hollywood and Intermediate French with him and never once was class dull. He tends to give a lot of homework for French but in the long run it's for the students benefit. His tests are fair. Hand in work=good grade.
Just take his class

He is one of the best calculus professors. His slides are some of the most informative and helpful. I don't have this professor for 182, I wish I did because just his slides for 182 are helping me so much in my current 182 class, even though I have a different professor. Clear, straightforward, and very approachable.

Great professor who is super lax and makes multivariable feel easy to understand. Tests are formatted exactly like the worksheets he posts, so if you go through those and write down the equations you need on the notecard he offers you will be just fine despite the high grade %. Attendance is also not mandatory at all.

Dr. Jones is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is passionate about teaching and helping students. You can tell he loves what he does and is great at getting his point across clearly. As long as you show up to class and pay attention, you're going to be guaranteed to do good in his class. His office hours are very effective as well.

Mostly lectures the whole time, solves examples, and follows a pre-made slideshow. Everything is posted online, and he does not care about attendance. Easy to understand and really cares about helping students understand.
Great professor, material can be hard to digest at times but if you ask questions he will help make sure you understand it.

I transferred into this class from another calculus 1 class at the start of the year, and Dr. Jones was amazing. It's very clear that he cares about his students and was available outside of class if students needed help. Not the most difficult class, but Dr. Jones makes sure you're on track.

Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. He would post the entire chapter slides, as well as the annotated slides to view and he knows his stuffs, especially when people asks him questions. He made math not as scary and broke down the topics well and overall the best professors. One homework after each topic covered 3 exams 1 final.

Jones is amazing. Doing homework will make or break your grade. He is super easy to talk to and willing to work with students to help them understand the material. Equation sheets are provided for exams.

Prof. Jones explains things clearly, gives helpful exam advice, and allows calculators and formula sheets for mid-terms. Pay attention to lectures, do the HW, and you're set for the final. Slide-decks are long and annoying to sift through. Dry humor and gives interesting tidbits for optional further reading. Overall, definitely worth the 8 am.

Prof. Jones is definitely a good professor to take if you'd like to increase your GPA. His grading scheme and exams are far more lenient than other professors. He's a bit too dependent on his lecture slides in my opinion and frequently makes calculation errors during class, but he answers questions well and attendance isn't particularly mandatory.

Just a really amazing professor, makes a pretty tough class feel really easy. He does a good mix of talking about the actual material and going over examples in class, and adjusts his pace really well to how well everybody seems to be understanding things. Also a great help during his office hours.
I took discrete math with him and he was a super good lecturer and really cared about our success. Definitely a great teacher.
All i can say is, G.O.A.T

HE IS WORTH THE HYPE - Hands down best math professor I have ever had. Highly recommend for anyone who wants a professor to explain the derivations and logic behind theorems, lots of examples in class, in-class slides and notes are always accessible, and homework and tests are consistent and fair. Class is all lecture so beware if thats not for you
Great professor. clearly understands what he is teaching and will slow down if someone in class needs something reexplained. also a friendly person

I took Jones during the summer and he made the course easy to follow. He uploads not only lecture videos but annotated slides with detailed examples and explanations. Homeworks were assigned but optional and 100% of our grade came from Quizzes and Exams. Exams are usually 5 questions with multiple parts. He also rounded grades to the nearest .1%.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Large portion of grade is not tests which is helpful. The tests are made by him so that they are easy to do if you understand the concepts (doesn't just test mental math and algebra). Very enjoyable teacher and very accessible outside of class, went to some office hours at times as was very useful.

Dr. Jones is a great teacher and always makes himself available and helpful if you need help. The class is very faced paced which can make it very challenging at times. The help I got in office hours was essential to my performance on tests. I would definitely recommend his class to others.

Professor Jones is very professional and careing, his exam is fairly easy, you will do great if you understand lecture and do your homework. He provides formula sheets for his own exams, so you don't have to rememeber formulas. And by the final exam, you should have all the formulas memerized. And if you missed class, he usually allow make up quizs

Went through his slides and had many examples. would go over anything people would ask very well. Some homework but gave a lot of time. Grade split was very easy, with most consisting of homework. would recommend.

He always gives a 5-10 minute break in between his long lectures. Also during lecture he would often pause and let students ask questions. He is willing to repeat or explain again until everyone understands (even 2-3 times). The only downside is that he doesn't teach how to stick with one notation (leibniz or newton) which is crucial in calculus.

Class was sort of hard, but he made it easy. Lectures are very good, he answers all questions, explains things thoroughly, AND he posts ALL of it online. He provides more than enough resources to get an A in the class, no matter how difficult. Best math professor at RIT. I wish he could teach all my classes he is so good at being a teacher.

Very difficult class but Dr. Jones made it a lot easier. He handwrote practice problems during lecture which made it really easy to follow along. He was also freely available outside of class for one-on-one help which was really great. Weekly quizzes on Wed. but was very clear on what mattered for those (as well as 3 exams plus final).
tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: He does a great job with his notes; he takes digital notes online and posts all his notes in a clear format. A quiz every Wednesday after class which is fairly easy. He is very approachable and takes his time explaining things one-on-one if needed. Homework is light; however, calc II is a difficult class so don't underestimate it.

Professor Jones is one of the best math professors/teachers I have ever had in my lifetime.  Something about his teaching style just sticks with me.  He is very accessible after class if you have any questions, and gives really great partial credit opportunities on tests.

I did not like his teaching style at all. It didn't help me learn and so I stopped attending very early on. I did better on both tests that I didn't show up to class for than the one that I did go to class for. Ended the class with an A and taught myself the entire thing. Fair grader.

The class was difficult, but I feel Dr. Jones did everything he could to help us succeed. He was available outside of class, answered questions on tests, and worked with students to solve grading disputes. The combination of lectures and workshops gave us a good balance of being able to learn and practice.

Raymond is a really chill dude who watches Hassan. He's super forgiving on quizzes and exams and always informs you what is most important to understand. If you do all of the weekly worksheets and understand those questions, you will get an A in the class. When you get past the infinite typos -corrected now, I've never had a better math professor.

This professor is one of the best math professors I've had at RIT. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. He communicates the course material in an effective, yet approachable manner. His tests are fair, and he is extremely reasonable in what he includes on his formula sheets. Overall, I had a great time taking this class.

No quizzes, he does not give out exam reviews to use for studying. But I always used textbook questions to practice for the exams and it always worked out in the end. There is homework but usually he tries to minimize the amount of questions per homework assignment because he does not want us to spend a lot of time on homework.

Lectures are long and not very informative to the material on the quizzes. Many tangents that don't help much, and absolutely no online content posted. Get ready to read if you want to feel secure during tests.
Godawful teacher. try not to take him, if at all possible. He grades very fairly though. You won't learn in his class, though.
All oral lecture, barely no class participation. Quizzes every week. Questions are wordy, exams not too hard.

His course is 100% oral lecture.  There are no visual aids/slides/etc... You have the option to either be very good at taking notes, or to read the books.  The exams may contain things not covered in lecture.  The final requires 3 essays.  He will require book research for the med-long term paper.
Man this class bad! It isn't that hard, but i would take another Liberal arts class over this! Oh don't even bother reading the books. Just write your book reviews off his summary or find one online.

He should have retired a while ago. Consistently rambles. Textbooks are two books for book reviews, which he goes over in class. Some of the stuff he teaches is wrong(perhaps he misunderstood) or dated, so be careful.

Should have retired long ago.  Very boring.  I read the textbook during class to study for the weekly quizzes.  If you study for the quizzes and midterm/final and read the textbook,  you will do fine.  Entertaining when he laughs at his own jokes.

Professor loves to teach modern history, you get the feeling he could continue speaking about certain individuals continuously. He tries to spark the interest of students with cartoons, though his humor can be a bit dry. It's a fairly decent class though some might complain about the amount of reading required and the rather long paper you'll need.
He's a pretty good teacher, he talks a lot and shows pictures and maps.  Quizzes weren't too hard, you only have to answer 10 of 12 questions and he drops the two lowest quiz grades.

Man is this guy dry! If you know what he is talking about you'll pick up on his witticisms. Regardless, you'll probably have a hard time paying attention. You read two books and write a review on each in addition to a paper. There is a quiz at random times each week. His style is to give you a summary of a book then quiz you as if you read it.
